Who Is Sun City Center Best For?

Sun City Center is best for: active retirees 60-80 years old who want a social community with built-in activities; buyers who are downsizing from a larger home and want lower maintenance (villa sections have exterior maintenance included in some HOA fees); buyers who split time between Florida and a northern state and want a low-maintenance Florida base; retirees who want affordability relative to the Tampa Bay market overall; and buyers who value proximity to both Tampa and Sarasota for medical, cultural, and travel access.

Who Should Look Elsewhere?

Sun City Center is not the right choice for: families with children (age restriction prohibits children under 19 as permanent residents); buyers who need a daily commute to Tampa or MacDill AFB (55-75 min rush hour commute is significant); buyers who want diverse retail, restaurant, and entertainment options close by; buyers who value intergenerational neighborhoods; or buyers who want beachfront or waterfront access (Sun City Center is inland, Tampa Bay coastal access requires driving).

Yes, for active retirees who want a built-in social community with golf, pools, clubs, and activities. It is affordable relative to other Florida 55+ communities, well-organized, and has strong I-75 access to Tampa and Sarasota. The trade-off is that it is somewhat isolated from urban amenities. If you want a quiet, low-maintenance retirement community with a rich social calendar, Sun City Center delivers that well.

Can my grandchildren visit me in Sun City Center?

Yes, grandchildren can visit as guests. The 55+ restriction prohibits permanent residency for those under 19, not visits. The specific guest policies vary by section (SCCA vs Kings Point) and individual community rules, but extended visits are generally permitted for 30-60 days per year or longer depending on the specific community's policies. Verify the guest rules for the specific community you are buying in before purchase.

What is the crime rate in Sun City Center FL?

Sun City Center generally has low crime rates, particularly for property crime and violent crime, compared to the Hillsborough County average. The age-restricted community nature, along with gated sections in Kings Point, contributes to security. The surrounding Ruskin area has higher crime rates, so the distinction between Sun City Center proper and surrounding communities matters when reviewing area crime statistics.

What are HOA fees like in Sun City Center?

HOA fees in Sun City Center vary significantly by section. SCCA community fees are modest, typically $300-$600 per year for basic community association dues. If your home is in a specific sub-association (villa community, patio home neighborhood), additional neighborhood HOA fees apply, often $200-$600/month covering exterior maintenance, landscaping, and sometimes amenity access. Kings Point has its own HOA structure with fees that can run $300-$700/month covering more comprehensive amenities and services. Always review HOA documents in full before making an offer.

For retired buyers, yes, the trade-off in commute for the price advantage and lifestyle often makes sense. Quick Answer

Sun City Center FL real estate in 2026 has median prices ranging from roughly $230K for smaller SCCA villas to $420K+ in Kings Point gated sections. The market is active with steady turnover driven by the large 55+ resident base. No new construction exists within Sun City Center proper, so all purchases are resale. Sun City Center FL Real Estate Market Overview

Sun City Center is a mature, fully-built active adult community with no new construction available. Every purchase is a resale. The market has consistent turnover driven by the natural life cycle of a 55+ community: residents who need to move closer to family, transition to assisted living, or have passed. This steady inventory is a buyer advantage compared to tighter markets in newer communities.

As of mid-2026, the Sun City Center resale market leans buyer-favorable. Higher interest rates have cooled demand from some buyers, and the wide price range (under $200K for small villas to $480K+ for large updated detached homes) means there is inventory at most price points. Days on market for the area generally runs 45-90 days, longer than in more competitive Hillsborough County markets. See current Sun City Center homes for sale.

Sun City Center Neighborhoods and Price Ranges

Sun City Center Community Association (SCCA) Areas

The SCCA sections are the older, original portions of Sun City Center developed from the 1960s through the 1980s. Homes here tend to be smaller (1,000-1,800 sq ft), on modest lots, and in need of updating in many cases. Prices range from approximately $175K-$325K depending on size, condition, and specific location. These sections have the most affordable entry points in Sun City Center and appeal to buyers focused on value over newer construction. The SCCA master association fee is modest, but individual neighborhood HOA fees may apply.

Kings Point

Kings Point is a gated 55+ community within Sun City Center with its own amenities center, pools, golf courses, and transportation system. Homes in Kings Point were developed primarily from the 1990s through the 2000s and tend to be newer and better-appointed than the original SCCA sections. Prices run from approximately $250K for smaller 2BR/2BA villas to $480K+ for larger detached 3BR homes with updated finishes. Kings Point has its own HOA fees ($300-$700/month) on top of the SCCA master fees. The Kings Point transportation system (electric shuttle vehicles) provides internal community mobility.

Newer Sections and Semi-Custom Homes

Some Sun City Center sections developed in the late 1990s and early 2000s have more contemporary home designs with higher ceilings, open floor plans, and larger garages. These homes tend to sell in the $280K-$420K range depending on lot size and updates. Buyers who want a more modern layout without the price premium of a fully renovated home often find good value in these sections.

What to Know When Buying in Sun City Center

Understand the Age Verification Process

Sun City Center is a federally-recognized 55+ community under the Housing for Older Persons Act (HOPA). To purchase, at least one buyer must be 55 or older and provide documentation. The community maintains age-verification records. If you plan to rent the property after purchase, the same age verification applies to tenants: at least one resident must be 55+, and no one under 19 may reside permanently.

4-Point Insurance Inspection

Florida insurance companies require a 4-point inspection (roof, electrical, plumbing, HVAC) for homes typically 25+ years old. Given that much of Sun City Center was built in the 1960s-1980s, virtually every purchase will require a 4-point. This can affect insurability and insurance cost. Older electrical panels (Federal Pacific, Zinsco, and aluminum wiring) and aging roofs are the most common obstacles. Budget $5,000-$20,000 for needed updates if inspections reveal issues.

HOA Document Review

Sun City Center has multiple layers of association governance: the SCCA master association, Kings Point association (if applicable), and individual neighborhood sub-associations. Each has its own rules, restrictions, and fees. Before closing, review all HOA documents (Declaration, Rules and Regulations, Budget, and Reserve Study) to understand what is allowed (pets, rentals, modifications), what fees are required, and whether reserves are adequately funded. Under-funded reserves can mean special assessments in your future.

Property Taxes in Sun City Center

Sun City Center is in Hillsborough County. The effective property tax rate after homestead exemption typically runs 1.0-1.3% of assessed value. On a $290K home with homestead exemption, expect annual taxes of approximately $2,800-$4,000. Florida's homestead exemption saves buyers $500/year at minimum and provides the Save Our Homes cap limiting annual assessment increases to 3% or CPI (whichever is lower) after the first year. Apply for homestead by March 1 of the year after purchase.

As of mid-2026, the Sun City Center market leans buyer-favorable with more inventory and longer days on market compared to the 2021-2022 peak. Buyers have more time to negotiate and more choices. Are there any new construction homes in Sun City Center?

No. Sun City Center is a fully-built community with no undeveloped land remaining for new construction. All purchases are resale. If new construction is important to you, Wimauma (15-20 min away) has active builder communities, some with 55+ sections. The Valencia Lakes community in Wimauma, developed by GL Homes, is one 55+ option with newer construction in the area.

What are the biggest red flags when buying in Sun City Center?

The four biggest red flags: (1) older roofs that insurers will not cover, (2) outdated electrical panels (Federal Pacific, Zinsco) that are difficult to insure, (3) under-funded HOA reserves that signal potential special assessments, and (4) undisclosed rental restrictions that may affect your plans. A thorough home inspection, 4-point insurance inspection, and full HOA document review before closing address most of these risks.

Can I rent out my Sun City Center home?

Yes, with restrictions. Rentals must comply with the 55+ age restriction: at least one tenant must be 55+ and no permanent residents under 19 are permitted. No Short-Term Rental Market

Insurance and Maintenance on Older Homes

Sun City Center's older housing stock (1960s-1980s for SCCA sections) can carry higher maintenance and insurance costs than newer construction. Florida insurance companies scrutinize older roofs, electrical panels, and plumbing systems. Hillsborough River Frontage

Temple Terrace has genuine Hillsborough River frontage, with riverfront lots on the north side of the city. Riverfront homes command a significant premium and are rarely available. When they do come to market they typically list in the $550K-$900K+ range depending on lot size, riparian rights, and dock feasibility. The river in this section is upstream of tidal influence and generally freshwater.

East and South Temple Terrace (Newer Development)

South and east of the original platted area, Temple Terrace expanded in the 1960s-1980s with more conventional subdivisions. These areas offer 3-4 bedroom homes with more standard street layouts, typically $300K-$430K. Less character than the original sections but more inventory and competitive pricing.

University Area Proximity

Temple Terrace borders the USF campus on its western edge. title: Is Temple Terrace FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Pros and Cons
excerpt: Honest assessment of living in Temple Terrace, FL, the good, the not-so-good, and what you need to know before moving.
content:
Quick Answer

Temple Terrace FL is a good place to live for buyers who value proximity to USF, a shorter Tampa commute than most suburbs, mature established neighborhoods with tree canopy, no HOA in most sections, and lower prices than South Tampa. The primary trade-offs are below-average schools, older housing stock that needs more careful inspection, and limited upscale retail and dining locally. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 for honest guidance.

What Is Temple Terrace FL?

Temple Terrace is an incorporated city in Hillsborough County, established in 1925 and developed as a planned community centered around the Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club (founded 1921). The city borders Tampa on the north and northeast, sits adjacent to the University of South Florida (USF) on its western edge, and covers ZIP codes 33617 and 33637. Population is approximately 26,000 residents.

Temple Terrace has its own city government, city services, and parks department, which distinguishes it from unincorporated Hillsborough County communities like Brandon or Riverview. The city has a distinct identity, mature tree canopy, and a relatively compact footprint compared to larger suburban developments. For current available homes, see Temple Terrace homes for sale.

Pros of Living in Temple Terrace FL

USF and Northeast Tampa Employment

Temple Terrace is the closest residential community to the University of South Florida's main Tampa campus. USF is one of Hillsborough County's largest employers, with faculty, staff, hospital (USF Health/Moffitt Cancer Center), and research positions representing thousands of jobs. For anyone who works at USF, Moffitt Cancer Center, or the broader USF campus medical and research complex, Temple Terrace eliminates long commutes that employees in Brandon, Riverview, or Wesley Chapel face. The 5-12 minute drive or even bike-ride distance to USF is genuinely valuable for these buyers.

Close-In Tampa Location

Temple Terrace's position 8-12 miles northeast of downtown Tampa puts it significantly closer to the city center than Brandon, Riverview, New Tampa, or Wesley Chapel. Off-peak commutes to downtown Tampa run 18-28 minutes. This short baseline commute means less time driving and more flexibility for jobs throughout the greater Tampa corridor. For buyers who work in downtown Tampa, Ybor City, or East Tampa, Temple Terrace offers a meaningfully shorter commute than most comparably-priced alternatives.

Mature Neighborhood Character and Tree Canopy

Temple Terrace has been developed since the 1920s and has mature oak trees, established landscaping, and neighborhood character that newer master-planned communities in Wesley Chapel or Riverview simply cannot replicate. Many streets in Temple Terrace have canopy coverage, sidewalks connecting to parks, and a neighborhood feel that appeals to buyers looking for character over uniformity. The city's own parks department maintains several parks along the Hillsborough River and throughout the city.

Hillsborough River Access

The Hillsborough River runs along portions of Temple Terrace, creating riverside park access for kayaking, canoeing, fishing, and nature walks. Riverhills Park, within Temple Terrace city limits, provides direct river access. For outdoor enthusiasts who want to live near water without paying waterfront property prices, Temple Terrace's city parks provide accessible river amenities. This is a differentiator that suburban communities farther from Tampa cannot offer.

No HOA in Most Sections

Most of Temple Terrace's established residential neighborhoods are not part of an HOA, and the city's own ordinances govern standards. This means buyers have more freedom for landscaping choices, vehicle storage, and minor modifications without seeking HOA approval. It also means lower carrying costs compared to communities with HOA fees. For buyers who dislike HOA oversight or want the flexibility of no deed restrictions, Temple Terrace's no-HOA character is appealing.

Pricing Advantage vs South Tampa

Temple Terrace offers similar neighborhood character to some South Tampa neighborhoods (tree-lined streets, walkable areas, city amenities) at significantly lower prices. A home that would cost $650K-$900K in Hyde Park or Palma Ceia might run $320K-$480K in Temple Terrace. For buyers who like the close-in, established neighborhood feel but cannot afford South Tampa pricing, Temple Terrace is a legitimate alternative.

Trade-Offs of Living in Temple Terrace FL

Below-Average Schools

Temple Terrace's assigned public schools, including King High School, rank below the Hillsborough County average on statewide academic metrics. For families who prioritize the public school zone as the primary real estate driver, Temple Terrace is not the right market. Buyers seeking strong public schools in the broader northeast Tampa area should look at New Tampa (Freedom HS zone), Carrollwood (Sickles HS), or Lutz (Steinbrenner HS), all of which carry school zone premiums.

Older Housing Stock Needs Inspection

Temple Terrace homes were built primarily from the 1950s through the 1980s. At 40-70+ years of age, roofs (15-25 year lifespan), HVAC systems (12-18 years), electrical panels, and plumbing can all require attention or replacement. Florida insurance companies require a 4-point inspection on homes typically 25+ years old, and insurability issues with older roofs and panels can complicate purchases. Budget for inspection costs, and anticipate that the purchase price may need to account for deferred maintenance. I identify these issues during the inspection period and use them to negotiate fair pricing or seller credits.

Limited Local Upscale Retail and Dining

Temple Terrace's commercial areas are not upscale. Fowler Avenue has chain restaurants, fast food, and basic retail. The lack of walkable dining, specialty grocery stores, or boutique retail in the immediate area is a trade-off for buyers who enjoy those amenities. Tampa's Westshore area, Hyde Park, and South Howard offer upscale dining and shopping, but they require a 20-35 minute drive from Temple Terrace.

Flooding Risk in River-Adjacent Sections

Portions of Temple Terrace near the Hillsborough River carry flood zone designations. Homes in FEMA Zone AE (100-year floodplain) require flood insurance, which adds $1,500-$5,000+ to annual carrying costs. The flooding risk is highly specific to address and elevation: some Temple Terrace homes are at no flood risk while others near the river have significant exposure. I always pull the FEMA flood map and recommend an elevation certificate for any property near the Hillsborough River in Temple Terrace.

Who Is Temple Terrace Best For?

Temple Terrace works best for: USF faculty, staff, researchers, and graduate students who want to own near campus; professionals with jobs in downtown Tampa or northeast Tampa who want a shorter commute than Brandon or Riverview offer; buyers who value established neighborhood character and mature trees over new construction; budget-conscious buyers who want a closer-in Tampa location at a lower price point than South Tampa; outdoor enthusiasts who want Hillsborough River park access; and buyers who prefer no-HOA freedom.

Who Should Look Elsewhere?

Temple Terrace is less suitable for: families who prioritize strong public schools (look at New Tampa, Carrollwood, Lutz, or Riverview); buyers who want new construction (very limited in Temple Terrace); buyers who want upscale walkable retail and dining immediately available; buyers who want a low-maintenance home (older homes need more care); and buyers seeking the largest possible lot sizes or rural feel (Temple Terrace is urban suburban with modest lot sizes).

Yes, for the right buyer. Temple Terrace has genuine appeal: mature neighborhoods, close Tampa access, no HOA in most areas, and USF proximity. The trade-off is older housing that needs care and schools that rank below the county average. For buyers whose priorities align with Temple Terrace's strengths, it is a well-regarded close-in community with good value relative to South Tampa pricing.

Is Temple Terrace safe?

Temple Terrace's crime rates are generally moderate. As an incorporated city, Temple Terrace has its own police department (City of Temple Terrace Police), which provides dedicated local policing rather than relying on the Hillsborough County Sheriff. Crime varies significantly by neighborhood within Temple Terrace. The western portions near USF are generally safer than some areas closer to the city's southern boundaries. What is the Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club?

The Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club is a private 18-hole golf course founded in 1921, making it one of Tampa Bay's oldest golf clubs. It is located within the city and is members-only. The club features the golf course, dining, and social membership options. Living near the club adds to the neighborhood character of the surrounding streets, though membership is separate from home purchase and has its own dues and application process.

How do Temple Terrace home prices compare to South Tampa?

Temple Terrace median home prices typically run $300K-$420K, compared to $650K-$1.5M+ for similar character neighborhoods in South Tampa (Hyde Park, Palma Ceia). The price gap reflects school zone differences, South Tampa's water/bay access, and South Tampa's social cachet. For buyers who want the established neighborhood feel without the South Tampa price premium, Temple Terrace offers meaningful value.

Temple Terrace has a moderate resale market with steady inventory and balanced buyer-seller conditions as of mid-2026. title: Town 'n' Country FL Schools Guide: Ratings & School Zones
excerpt: Complete guide to schools serving Town 'n' Country, FL, elementary through high school ratings, zoning, and how school choice affects home values.
content:
Quick Answer

Town 'n' Country is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools (HCPS). The two primary high school zones are Alonso High School (IB World School, arts magnet) and Sickles High School (JROTC, growing academic reputation). Middle school feeder is Sergeant Paul R. Smith Middle. Elementary options include Town 'n' Country Elementary and several nearby schools. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to verify zoning for any specific address before you buy.

What High Schools Serve Town 'n' Country FL?

Town 'n' Country sits within two high school attendance zones depending on the exact address. Alonso High School serves the eastern portions of Town 'n' Country near the Westshore corridor, while Sickles High School serves sections further north and west. Both are Hillsborough County public schools with distinct strengths. Verify your specific address at HCPSS.net before finalizing any home purchase.

Alonso High School (IB World School)

Alonso High School is the academic anchor for eastern Town 'n' Country. It carries International Baccalaureate (IB) World School designation, making it one of a small number of public high schools in Hillsborough County offering the full IB diploma program. The IB pathway gives motivated students access to college-level coursework, recognized by universities worldwide. Alonso also hosts an arts magnet with programs in visual arts, theater, and performing arts. For families who prioritize academic rigor, the IB designation is a meaningful differentiator.

Beyond IB, Alonso offers AP courses, dual enrollment through Hillsborough Community College, CTE pathways, and competitive athletics. The school draws students from outside its attendance zone through the magnet program, adding diversity of academic focus to the student body.

Sickles High School

Sickles High School serves the northern and western sections of Town 'n' Country. The school has a strong JROTC program and arts curriculum, along with AP and dual enrollment pathways. Sickles has built a growing reputation in extracurricular activities and competitive sports. Families in the Countryway area and sections along Sheldon Road are typically zoned for Sickles.

What Middle School Serves Town 'n' Country?

Sergeant Paul R. Smith Middle School is the primary middle school feeder for most of Town 'n' Country. The school serves grades 6-8 and feeds into both Alonso and Sickles depending on the student's residential zone. Hillsborough County also operates an open enrollment magnet program at the middle school level that allows families to apply for schools outside their assigned zone.

Middle School Magnet Options

Hillsborough County's Choice and Magnet Office manages open enrollment applications for specialty programs at middle and high school levels. Town 'n' Country families can apply for magnet programs at schools across the county. Transportation to magnet schools outside the attendance zone is the family's responsibility. Applications for the following school year typically open in January and close in February. Check the HCPSS Choice and Magnet Office website for current application windows.

What Elementary Schools Serve Town 'n' Country?

Town 'n' Country Elementary School is the neighborhood school for much of the community. Elementary zone assignments in this area depend on the specific address, and the boundaries shift over time as enrollment changes. Use the HCPSS school locator (hcpss.net) with the exact street address to confirm your current-year assignment before purchasing.

Other Elementary Options Near Town 'n' Country

Depending on the section of Town 'n' Country, some addresses feed to adjacent elementary schools including Lowry Elementary and Dickenson Elementary. Families with strong preferences for a specific elementary school should verify zoning for their target address and use the school choice program if the assigned school does not meet their needs.

How Do School Zones Affect Home Values in Town 'n' Country?

The Alonso IB zone is a meaningful driver of demand in the eastern sections of Town 'n' Country. Homes in the Alonso attendance zone, particularly near the Westshore corridor, attract families specifically for the IB pathway. This concentrated demand supports pricing in those sections relative to the broader Town 'n' Country market.

Town 'n' Country as a whole does not command the school-driven premium you see in the Steinbrenner zone (Lutz/Westchase) or the Plant zone (South Tampa). The honest assessment: buyers who place schools as their top priority and have flexibility in budget often look at Westchase or Carrollwood for stronger overall school performance. Town 'n' Country's competitive advantage is location and price, not school ratings.

The IB Exception

For families specifically seeking the IB diploma pathway, Alonso is one of the few public school options in Hillsborough County. Families from outside the attendance zone can apply for the IB magnet, subject to space availability. Living within the zone removes the uncertainty of magnet acceptance and gives guaranteed access. This is a niche but real value driver for Alonso-zoned properties.

Private School Options Near Town 'n' Country

Town 'n' Country's proximity to central Tampa puts several private schools within reasonable drive times. Families considering private education should factor in commute time along Dale Mabry Highway and the Veterans Expressway during school hours.

School Choice and Florida Scholarship Programs

Florida offers several scholarship programs that can expand educational options for Town 'n' Country families beyond their assigned public school:

Step Up For Students (Family Empowerment Scholarship)

The Family Empowerment Scholarship provides funding for eligible families to apply toward private school tuition. Income-based eligibility applies. Families can use the scholarship at participating private schools in the Tampa area. Check the Step Up For Students website (stepupforstudents.org) for current eligibility thresholds and participating schools.

Hillsborough County Magnet and Choice Programs

Beyond the IB program at Alonso, Hillsborough County operates magnet programs at multiple schools across the district covering performing arts, STEM, language immersion, and other academic focuses. Town 'n' Country families can apply for any magnet program. Transportation is not provided for magnet placements outside the home zone. Contact the HCPSS Choice and Magnet Office for the current application calendar.

title: Town 'n' Country FL Commute Guide: Drive Times & Commutes
excerpt: Real commute times from Town 'n' Country, FL to downtown Tampa, Brandon, MacDill AFB, and other Tampa Bay employment centers.
content:
Quick Answer

Town 'n' Country offers one of the shortest commutes to Tampa International Airport and the Westshore Business District of any affordable Tampa suburb. TPA is 4-7 miles away (8-12 min off-peak). Downtown Tampa is 10-14 miles (15-25 min off-peak). Clearwater Beach is roughly 18-22 miles (25-35 min off-peak). Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 if location is your top priority in your home search.

Why Is Town 'n' Country's Location a Competitive Advantage?

Town 'n' Country sits in the geographic sweet spot of west Tampa. It is close enough to Tampa International Airport to feel like an airport neighborhood, yet priced at $330K-$420K for a median single-family home rather than the $700K-$2M+ you would pay in South Tampa or Hyde Park. For buyers whose work keeps them in the Westshore or airport corridor, no comparably priced Tampa community saves more commute time.

The community is unincorporated Hillsborough County, which means you are not paying a city of Tampa millage on top of county taxes. The tradeoff is that you lose easy walkability and some city services in exchange for location value and price. For car-dependent commuters who need to be near the airport corridor, that is a rational trade.

What Are the Main Routes Out of Town 'n' Country?

Hillsborough Avenue (SR-580)

Hillsborough Avenue is Town 'n' Country's main east-west surface corridor. It connects directly to the heart of Tampa to the east and provides access to Veterans Expressway on-ramps heading north toward Citrus Park, Lutz, and I-275. The stretch between the Veterans Expressway and Memorial Highway (SR-580) can get congested between 4:30-6:30 PM on weekdays. If your work hours are flexible, a 7:00 AM departure from Town 'n' Country to Westshore or downtown Tampa typically runs under 15 minutes.

Veterans Expressway (FL-589)

The Veterans Expressway is the toll-road spine for northern and western Town 'n' Country. It runs north from the airport area and connects to I-275, providing direct access to downtown Tampa and Westshore. The expressway also reaches Lutz and the I-75 interchange further north. Tolls run approximately $2-$4 for a typical Town 'n' Country to downtown Tampa trip. SUNPASS or TOLL-BY-PLATE users pay at the posted rate. Budget roughly $60-$100/month if you use the Veterans Expressway daily.

Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR-60)

The Courtney Campbell Causeway runs west from Rocky Point at the edge of Town 'n' Country directly to Clearwater. It is a free route (no toll) and one of the most efficient paths to the Clearwater area and Pinellas beaches. Rush-hour inbound traffic on the causeway (heading east toward Tampa in the AM) can back up near the Rocky Point end, but the 25-35 minute Clearwater Beach drive is one of Town 'n' Country's most underrated features.

Memorial Highway / Westshore Blvd

For airport access and International Plaza, Memorial Highway (SR-580) and Westshore Boulevard provide direct surface routes from Town 'n' Country without requiring the expressway. These are the go-to routes for airport runs and Westshore retail. Expect 8-12 minutes off-peak and 15-22 minutes during rush hour.

What About MacDill AFB Commuters?

Town 'n' Country is a reasonable choice for MacDill Air Force Base personnel. The commute runs south on Dale Mabry Highway or through the Selmon Expressway extension from downtown Tampa. The typical trip is 20-28 minutes off-peak and 32-48 minutes during peak hours. This is a meaningful improvement over Brandon (35-50 min), Riverview (45-65 min), or Wesley Chapel (60-80 min) for MacDill commuters. Many active-duty families choose Town 'n' Country specifically for this combination of price, location, and reasonable MacDill drive time.

Is There Public Transit From Town 'n' Country?

HART (Hillsborough Area Regional Transit) operates bus routes along Hillsborough Avenue and the Westshore corridor that pass through and near Town 'n' Country. The HART MetroRapid service on Hillsborough Avenue provides faster bus service toward downtown Tampa. For most commuters in Town 'n' Country, a car remains necessary given the dispersed destinations across the metro, but the Hillsborough Avenue bus corridor is functional for those with downtown Tampa employment.

The commute from Town 'n' Country to downtown Tampa runs 15-25 minutes off-peak via the Veterans Expressway or I-275. During rush hour, add 15-20 minutes. Most routes avoid the worst of I-275's congestion because you are entering from the west rather than the north or south.

Yes. Town 'n' Country is a reasonable MacDill AFB commute at 20-28 minutes off-peak and 32-48 minutes during rush. It outperforms Brandon, Riverview, and eastern Tampa suburbs for MacDill commute time and offers prices comparable to or below those alternatives.

Yes. The Courtney Campbell Causeway (free, no toll) leaves from Rocky Point at the western edge of Town 'n' Country and runs directly to Clearwater. Beach drive time is 25-35 minutes off-peak. This is one of the most direct beach routes of any affordable Tampa suburb.

The worst congestion is on Hillsborough Avenue between the Veterans Expressway and Memorial Highway during the 7:30-9:00 AM inbound and 4:30-6:30 PM outbound windows. The Veterans Expressway itself moves well in both directions. Countryway Blvd and Sheldon Road see local congestion near school zones during dismissal hours (2:30-3:30 PM).

title: Is Town 'n' Country FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Pros and Cons
excerpt: Honest assessment of living in Town 'n' Country, FL, the good, the not-so-good, and what you need to know before moving.
content:
Quick Answer

Town 'n' Country is a practical, affordable choice for buyers who need fast access to Tampa International Airport and the Westshore Business District. Homes run $330K-$420K (median), significantly below Westchase and South Tampa. The tradeoff: schools are average, the neighborhood aesthetic is older (1960s-1990s housing), and there is no walkable town center. Best for: working professionals, MacDill commuters, first-time buyers, and anyone who values location over amenities. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 for a straight answer on whether it fits your situation.

What Is Town 'n' Country FL?

Town 'n' Country is an unincorporated community in western Hillsborough County, bounded roughly by Tampa International Airport to the east, the Courtney Campbell Causeway to the south, Veterans Expressway to the west, and Hillsborough Avenue to the north. ZIP codes 33615, 33616, 33634, and 33635 cover different sections. Being unincorporated means no city of Tampa municipal government, no city income tax, and lower property tax millage than homes inside Tampa city limits.

The community developed primarily in the 1960s through 1980s, creating a stock of concrete block construction homes on modest lots. There is no new construction to speak of; it is a fully built-out resale market. Countryway, built in the 1980s-1990s, is the newest and most polished section. Canal-front homes along waterways connected to Old Tampa Bay represent the premium tier.

What Are the Pros of Living in Town 'n' Country?

1. Unbeatable Location for Airport and Westshore Access

Tampa International Airport is 4-7 miles away. The Westshore Business District, Tampa's largest employment center outside downtown, is 4-6 miles away. These drive times are 8-12 minutes off-peak. No comparably priced Tampa community delivers this airport and employment proximity. Frequent travelers who hate long airport runs find Town 'n' Country genuinely convenient in a way that is hard to replicate elsewhere at this price point.

2. Affordability Relative to Location

The median single-family home runs $330K-$420K in mid-2026, versus $500K-$900K+ in adjacent Westchase and $700K+ in South Tampa. You are buying real location at a fraction of the price. Many Town 'n' Country sections have no HOA or low HOA, keeping monthly carrying costs manageable. Canal-front homes with Old Tampa Bay boat access can reach $550K-$850K+, still well below waterfront pricing in South Tampa or the Westshore islands.

3. Unincorporated Status Means Lower Property Taxes

Town 'n' Country is unincorporated Hillsborough County, not within Tampa city limits. This means buyers do not pay the City of Tampa municipal millage rate (approximately 5-6 mills). The savings are meaningful: on a $400,000 home, not paying city millage saves approximately $2,000-$2,400 per year compared to an identical home inside Tampa. This is a structural tax advantage that compounds over time.

4. Direct Clearwater Beach Access

The Courtney Campbell Causeway leaves from Rocky Point at the western edge of Town 'n' Country and runs directly to Clearwater with no toll. Clearwater Beach is 25-35 minutes away on a typical weekend morning. Indian Rocks Beach and other Pinellas beaches are similarly accessible. This beach proximity at an affordable price point is a quality-of-life advantage over most Tampa suburbs at comparable or higher prices.

5. Canal Homes With Old Tampa Bay Access

Town 'n' Country's western edge fronts a canal system with access to Old Tampa Bay. Canal-front homes with boat docks exist in the Waterford and Rocky Point areas at $550K-$850K, offering boating, kayaking, and waterfront living at prices that would be $1M+ in South Tampa or Davis Islands. For buyers who want water access without paying South Tampa waterfront prices, these sections are a legitimate alternative.

What Are the Cons of Living in Town 'n' Country?

1. Older Housing Stock Requires More Due Diligence

The bulk of Town 'n' Country's housing was built from the 1960s through 1980s. This means buyers will frequently encounter older roofs, aging plumbing, original HVAC systems, and kitchens and bathrooms that need updates. A thorough inspection is not optional here. Homes in original condition can be an investment opportunity for buyers willing to renovate, but buyers who want move-in ready should expect to pay a premium for updated properties or look at Countryway's newer housing stock.

2. Schools Are Average, Not a Selling Point

Town 'n' Country's public schools are functional but not the premium that drives Westchase or Lutz home values. Alonso High School offers the IB program, which is a real academic asset. But elementary and middle schools in Town 'n' Country are rated below Westchase, Lutz, and Land O Lakes options. Families for whom school ratings are the primary criterion should compare Westchase (Steinbrenner HS, Westchase Elementary, Farnell Middle, all A-rated) before committing to Town 'n' Country.

3. No Walkable Town Center

Unlike Westchase's West Park Village or South Tampa's Hyde Park area, Town 'n' Country has no walkable mixed-use core. Retail and restaurants are available in strip centers along Hillsborough Avenue and Memorial Highway, plus the nearby WestShore Plaza and International Plaza malls, but you will drive everywhere. This is typical for Tampa suburbs but worth noting for buyers who value walkable neighborhoods.

4. Flood Zone Risk in Western Sections

Properties near the canal network and Old Tampa Bay in the western sections of Town 'n' Country fall in FEMA flood zones. Flood insurance adds $1,500-$4,500 per year to annual housing costs depending on the property's specific zone and elevation. Non-canal properties further inland are typically in lower-risk zones but buyers should pull the FEMA Flood Map for any specific address. After Hurricane Helene (2024), flood zone awareness has increased significantly among Tampa Bay buyers.

Who Is Town 'n' Country the Right Fit For?

Good fit: Working professionals commuting to TPA, Westshore, or downtown Tampa who want to maximize location at a reasonable price. MacDill AFB personnel. Buyers who want a walkable neighborhood with restaurants and shops within walking distance. Buyers who want newer construction built after 2000 as the norm (look at Westchase or Wesley Chapel). Buyers who need the Steinbrenner HS zone specifically.

Is Town 'n' Country a safe area?

Town 'n' Country is a mixed community. Crime rates vary significantly by section. The Countryway area and sections near Westchase on the northern edge tend to have lower crime. As with any purchase in this market, review Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office crime data for the specific address before buying.

Is Town 'n' Country in Tampa FL?

Technically no. Town 'n' Country is unincorporated Hillsborough County, not within Tampa city limits. It uses Tampa mailing addresses and ZIP codes (33615, 33616, 33634, 33635), which is why it is commonly referred to as a Tampa community. The unincorporated status means lower property taxes (no city millage) and county-level services rather than city services.

Does Town 'n' Country have HOA fees?

Many sections of Town 'n' Country have no HOA at all, which is relatively rare for communities this close to Tampa. Countryway has HOA sections with modest annual fees, typically in the $300-$800/year range. Canal-front sections may have small community associations. What are property taxes like in Town 'n' Country?

Town 'n' Country is unincorporated Hillsborough County, so the total millage rate is approximately 19-21 mills depending on your specific location. On a $400,000 home with homestead exemption, estimated annual property taxes run $6,650-$7,350. This is meaningfully lower than inside Tampa city limits, where the city millage adds another $2,000-$2,400/year on a $400K home.

How close is Town 'n' Country to the beach?

Clearwater Beach is approximately 25-35 minutes via the Courtney Campbell Causeway (free, no toll) from the western edge of Town 'n' Country. Indian Rocks Beach and other Pinellas beaches are similarly accessible. This is one of the shortest beach commutes among affordable Tampa suburban communities.

Town 'n' Country is a fully built-out resale market. There is essentially no new construction within the community boundaries. Every home for sale is a resale from the original 1960s-1990s development period, except for rare custom infill teardown-rebuilds. This means buyers are choosing between condition levels of existing homes rather than comparing new builds to resale.

The 2026 market reflects elevated mortgage rates keeping some buyers on the sidelines. Inventory is higher than the 2021-2022 peak frenzy. What Are the Neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country?

Countryway ($370K-$600K)

Countryway is the newest and most organized section of Town 'n' Country, developed primarily in the 1980s-1990s. Countryway has the highest home values in Town 'n' Country proper. Buyers seeking a more polished version of Town 'n' Country affordability start here.

Town 'n' Country Park ($290K-$390K)

The original development from the 1960s, Town 'n' Country Park features the most affordable homes in the area. Concrete block construction, 1,000-1,600 sq ft, generous lots by Tampa standards, many with no HOA. The Town 'n' Country Regional Park anchors this section with ball fields and a community center. This section appeals to investors, first-time buyers, and renters who want to become owners without leaving the airport corridor.

Rocky Point / Canal Front ($450K-$850K+)

The western edge of Town 'n' Country fronts a canal system with access to Old Tampa Bay. Rocky Point Drive and the waterfront sections in Waterford offer homes with private boat docks and bay breezes. These are the premium properties in the area. Flood insurance is required and adds $1,500-$4,500/year. Ben T. Davis Beach on the Courtney Campbell Causeway provides public waterfront access nearby.

Bay Crest Park ($280K-$420K)

Bay Crest Park offers a quieter residential feel south of Hillsborough Avenue. The streets here are less traffic-exposed than the sections near the main commercial corridor. Homes are primarily 1970s-1980s construction, and the section draws buyers who want a calmer location at an accessible price. Some streets in Bay Crest Park have water views at non-waterfront prices.

What Should Buyers Know in 2026?

Roof Age Is the Single Biggest Variable

In Florida, homeowners insurance carriers require a roof under 15-20 years old (carrier-dependent) to offer or renew coverage at reasonable rates. Town 'n' Country's 1960s-1980s housing stock means many roofs are approaching or past this threshold. Before writing an offer, ask about the roof age. A home with a 5-year-old roof has meaningfully better insurance cost certainty than one with an 18-year-old roof. Factor $15,000-$22,000 for a tile or shingle re-roof on a typical TnC home if the current roof is near end of life.

Flood Zone Check for Western Properties

Pull the FEMA Flood Map for any Town 'n' Country property near the canal system or within a few blocks of Old Tampa Bay. Flood zones AE and AH require mandatory flood insurance if there is a mortgage. Get a flood insurance quote before finalizing your offer, not after. The difference between Zone X (no requirement) and Zone AE can be $1,500-$4,000/year in added annual cost.

Verify School Zone for the Specific Address

Town 'n' Country spans multiple high school zones (Alonso and Sickles). For families where the Alonso IB program is the goal, confirm the specific address is in the Alonso zone at HCPSS.net before signing a contract. Zone boundaries are not always intuitive from a map view.

What Should Sellers Know in 2026?

Pricing Accuracy Matters More in a Balanced Market

Town 'n' Country buyers in 2026 are more patient than 2021-2022 buyers. Overpriced listings sit, and days on market accumulates, which leads to price reductions and signals distress to future buyers. A well-prepared seller who prices accurately, discloses the roof age upfront, and does basic cosmetic preparation (fresh paint, cleaned up yard, minor repairs) closes faster and at better net proceeds than sellers who test the top of the market.

Roof Age Disclosure Builds Trust

Sellers with newer roofs should lead with that information in marketing. A 2020 or newer roof is a legitimate selling point that reduces buyer concern about insurance and lender conditions. Sellers with older roofs may consider getting a roof condition report to proactively address buyer concerns rather than letting it become a surprise in inspection.

title: Investing in Town 'n' Country FL Real Estate: Rentals & ROI

content:
Quick Answer

Town 'n' Country is a solid long-term rental market driven by airport corridor employment, airport hotel workers, Westshore business district employees, and MacDill AFB families. Typical 3BR/2BA rents run $1,800-$2,400/month. Gross yields on entry-level properties ($290K-$380K range) run 6.2-8.0% before expenses. The key advantages: no HOA rental restrictions in most sections, no CDD fees, and strong tenant demand near TPA. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 for investor-specific guidance.

Why Do Investors Buy in Town 'n' Country?

Town 'n' Country offers a combination of tenant demand drivers that many suburban markets cannot match. Tampa International Airport is 4-7 miles away, creating consistent demand from airline employees, airport contractors, hospitality workers at the Rocky Point hotel strip, and corporate travelers who need furnished month-to-month housing near TPA. The Westshore Business District, Tampa's largest employment center outside downtown, adds thousands of office workers and corporate travelers who need housing close to work. MacDill AFB families also represent stable, consistent rental demand.

The other investor-friendly factor: most Town 'n' Country sections have no HOA or a minimal HOA that places no restrictions on rentals. This is increasingly rare as HOA communities implement rental caps and owner-occupancy requirements. Town 'n' Country's older, less-organized sections are largely free of these restrictions.

What Are the Investor Advantages in Town 'n' Country?

No HOA Rental Restrictions in Most Sections

A growing number of HOA communities across Tampa Bay have implemented minimum lease terms (often 12 months), caps on total rental units (25-30% of homes), or owner-occupancy requirements that block investor purchases entirely. Most of Town 'n' Country's older sections have either no HOA or minimal HOAs that impose no such restrictions. This is increasingly valuable as HOA restrictions continue to expand across newer Florida communities.

No CDD Fees

Community Development Districts (CDDs) are common in newer Florida communities and add $1,000-$4,500+ per year in additional property tax-line fees. Town 'n' Country has no CDDs. This reduces annual holding costs compared to investing in CDD-heavy markets like Wesley Chapel, Riverview, or Wimauma, where CDD fees can significantly compress net yields.

Airport Corridor Demand Is Durable

Tampa International Airport ranked among the busiest airports in Florida and continues to expand service. Airport employment, including airlines, cargo, ground handling, catering, and retail, generates consistent housing demand from workers who want short commutes. This type of tenant is durable across economic cycles in ways that downtown-dependent demand is not.

What Are the Investor Risks and Limitations?

Older Housing Means Higher Maintenance

1960s-1980s homes require a larger capital expenditure reserve than 2000s construction. Roofs, HVAC systems, plumbing stacks, and electrical panels (some still have original breaker boxes) need more frequent attention. Budget for a CapEx reserve of $200-$400/month depending on property age and condition. Investors who buy an older TnC home and do no inspection due diligence often encounter expensive surprises in the first year.

No Short-Term Rental Market

Town 'n' Country is not a short-term rental (STR) or vacation rental market. Proximity to TPA creates some corporate housing demand, but the tourist and vacation driver is not present here (unlike Tampa's Ybor City or St. Pete Beach). Investors should underwrite for long-term tenants, not STR income. Hillsborough County also has regulations governing short-term rental activity.

Insurance Costs Have Risen

Homeowners insurance in Florida has increased significantly since 2020, and older homes face higher premiums or eligibility challenges. A 20-year-old roof may be uninsurable through standard carriers. Investors buying Town 'n' Country properties should get insurance quotes before closing, not after. Budget $2,500-$5,000/year for homeowners insurance on a non-waterfront property; add flood insurance on top for waterfront or canal-adjacent homes.

title: New Construction Homes in Town 'n' Country FL: Builders & Communities

content:
Quick Answer

There is essentially no new construction available in Town 'n' Country FL. The community is fully built out, developed between the 1960s and 1990s, with no active builder communities. If you want new construction near the airport corridor and Westshore, your best options are the Airport South area, or nearby communities in Odessa, Lutz, and Wesley Chapel. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to discuss your options.

Why Is There No New Construction in Town 'n' Country?

Town 'n' Country is a mature, built-out suburb. The land was developed in the 1960s through 1990s and is essentially 100% occupied by existing homes, businesses, and infrastructure. There are no remaining vacant parcels large enough for a builder community, no undeveloped land to assemble, and no feasible path for a homebuilder to enter the market with a tract development.

This is common for close-in Tampa communities. Carrollwood has the same constraint. South Tampa is built out. The new construction opportunity in this part of Tampa Bay is in communities further out: Odessa, Lutz, Wesley Chapel north of SR-54, and the Land O Lakes corridor. Buyers willing to accept a longer commute can get a new-construction home; buyers who must be in the Town 'n' Country location are in the resale market only.

Are There Any Infill or Teardown Options?

Occasionally, individual lots with older structures become available for teardown and custom rebuilds. These are rare, site-specific opportunities rather than a systematic new construction option. A custom infill rebuild in Town 'n' Country would typically cost $175-$280 per square foot for the build (land purchased separately), plus demolition and permitting. The land cost plus construction cost often approaches the same price as buying a finished updated home in the area, so infill custom builds require careful financial analysis.

If you are specifically interested in a custom build within Town 'n' Country, Barrett can help identify any lots that become available and connect you with builders who specialize in infill construction in west Tampa.

What If You Want New Construction and a Short Airport Commute?

Odessa offers the best combination of new construction availability and proximity to the airport corridor. The price premium over Town 'n' Country resale is real ($420K-$800K+ vs. $330K-$420K), but you get a new home, modern construction, and no deferred maintenance concerns for 10-15 years.

Sickles High School serves parts of Odessa, which ties that school zone to both communities. If your household includes high-schoolers and Sickles is acceptable, Odessa becomes a natural step up from Town 'n' Country when budget allows.

Builder Incentives to Know Before You Shop

When shopping new construction in communities near Town 'n' Country (Odessa, Wesley Chapel, Land O Lakes), understand these negotiation points:

  • Closing cost credits: Most national builders offer $5,000-$20,000 in closing cost assistance when you use their preferred lender. The trade-off is that preferred lender rates may not be competitive. Compare offers from outside lenders before committing.
  • Rate buydowns: Builders with affiliated mortgage companies frequently offer temporary or permanent interest rate buydowns as an alternative to price reductions. A 2-1 buydown can lower your first-year payment meaningfully.
  • Design center credits: Some builders allow you to redirect closing cost credits toward design center upgrades. Upgraded flooring, cabinetry, and countertops through the builder are often overpriced, so cash credits are usually the better value.
  • Use your own agent: Having your own buyer's agent in a new construction transaction costs you nothing (the builder pays the commission) and gives you someone whose job is to protect your interests, not the builder's sales numbers.

What High School Serves Westchase FL?

Its modern facilities, comprehensive AP and honors program, competitive athletics, and wide extracurricular offerings have made it one of the most sought-after high school zones in west Tampa Bay. Some addresses in the southern portions of the 33626 ZIP code may be zoned for Sickles High School rather than Steinbrenner. Always verify your specific address at HCPSS.net before purchasing a home if school zone is a priority.

Steinbrenner High School: Key Details

Steinbrenner High School opened in 2009 as one of the newest large high schools in Hillsborough County. The school consistently earns a state A rating and ranks among the top-performing high schools in the county. Academic programs include a robust AP curriculum across multiple departments, dual enrollment through Hillsborough Community College, honors tracks, and career-technical education pathways. The school's comparatively recent construction means modern labs, classrooms, and athletic facilities.

Steinbrenner HS is shared by Lutz and portions of Westchase, which means families in both communities compete for the same top-rated zone. Research has documented that homes in the Steinbrenner zone command an 8-15% premium over comparable homes outside the zone in the same general area. This school-driven value increase is real and measurable in Hillsborough County market data.

What Middle School Serves Westchase?

Farnell Middle School serves most of Westchase and is another A-rated school. Parents consistently rate Farnell for strong academics, a well-organized administration, and a positive school environment. Farnell's location within reasonable proximity to Westchase makes it a manageable drive for most families.

Farnell offers advanced academic tracks, competitive sports, and extracurricular programs. As with the elementary and high school, verify the specific zone assignment for your address at HCPSS.net, as boundary lines can shift between school years.

What Elementary School Serves Westchase?

Westchase Elementary School is located within the Westchase community itself and consistently earns an A rating. Its in-community location means many students can walk or bike to school from their homes, which is a meaningful quality-of-life advantage in Florida where most families drive everywhere. The school's performance on state assessments places it among the stronger elementary schools in Hillsborough County.

Some addresses in Westchase, particularly in the southern sections of 33626, may be zoned for Bryant Elementary rather than Westchase Elementary. title: Is Westchase FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Pros and Cons
excerpt: Honest assessment of living in Westchase, FL, the good, the not-so-good, and what you need to know before moving.
content:
Quick Answer

Westchase is one of the best-planned communities in Tampa Bay and consistently ranks as a top place to live in the region. It delivers A-rated schools (Steinbrenner HS, Farnell Middle, Westchase Elementary), a walkable town center with restaurants and a Publix, an 18-hole golf course, swim and tennis centers, miles of trails, and a genuine neighborhood identity. The tradeoff: homes start at $450K-$500K and the mandatory two-tier HOA adds real cost. This is a premium product at a premium price. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 for an honest assessment of whether Westchase fits your situation.

What Is Westchase FL?

Westchase is a master-planned community in northwest Hillsborough County, developed by Westchase Associates beginning in the early 1990s. The community spans roughly 2,000 acres and encompasses over a dozen distinct villages, each with its own character but sharing access to community amenities. By 2016, Westchase was largely built out, and it now functions as an established, in-demand community rather than an active development. ZIP code 33626.

The community centers on West Park Village, a walkable town center with restaurants, shops, a Publix grocery, a wine bar, and community gathering spaces. The Westchase Golf Club (public, 18-hole, designed by Lloyd Clifton) winds through the heart of the community. Multiple swim and tennis centers operate under the Westchase Community Association (WCA). Miles of greenway trails connect the villages. It is the most comprehensively amenitized master-planned community at this price point in west Tampa Bay.

What Are the Pros of Living in Westchase?

1. Top-Rated Public Schools (A-Rated Across All Three Levels)

Westchase feeds into Westchase Elementary (A-rated, within the community), Farnell Middle School (A-rated), and Steinbrenner High School (A-rated, opened 2009). This is one of a small number of communities in Hillsborough County where you get top-rated public schools from kindergarten through 12th grade without any breaks in the chain. For families paying $500K-$900K for a home, the school quality often justifies a significant portion of the price premium over Town 'n' Country or Carrollwood alternatives.

2. Walkable Town Center (Rare in Tampa Bay)

West Park Village is one of the few genuinely walkable neighborhoods in the entire Tampa Bay area. Residents can walk to dinner, grab morning coffee, run to Publix, and attend community events without getting in a car. This traditional neighborhood design with front porches, alleys, and tree-lined sidewalks creates a community character that is unusual for Florida suburban development. Buyers who have lived in walkable urban neighborhoods and are not ready to give that up entirely often find West Park Village the most palatable suburban option in Tampa Bay.

3. Short Commute to TPA, Westshore, and Downtown Tampa

Tampa International Airport is 8 miles and 12-15 minutes away. The Westshore Business District is 8 miles and 15-20 minutes away. The Veterans Expressway entrance is 2 miles from the community. This proximity gives Westchase one of the best commute profiles of any Tampa planned community with A-rated schools. Lutz, New Tampa, and FishHawk have comparable school quality but significantly longer airport and Westshore drives.

4. Comprehensive Master-Planned Amenities

The Westchase Golf Club (18-hole public course designed by Lloyd Clifton), multiple swim and tennis centers, miles of greenway trails, community parks and playgrounds, and the West Park Village town center are all included in community life. The Westchase Community Association (WCA) manages common areas and enforces community standards that maintain neighborhood quality. Residents consistently cite the amenity package and community involvement as the top reasons they would not leave Westchase.

5. Strong Long-Term Property Values

Westchase has demonstrated strong price stability through multiple market cycles because it delivers a combination of factors (schools, amenities, location, community identity) that are difficult to replicate elsewhere in Tampa Bay. The supply of homes within Westchase is fixed (built out), while demand from families targeting the Steinbrenner school zone remains consistent. This supply-demand dynamic supports values in downturns and drives appreciation in upturns.

What Are the Cons of Living in Westchase?

1. High Entry Price ($450K-$1.5M+)

Townhomes start at $380K-$550K. Single-family homes in the smaller-lot sections start at $500K. Larger-lot single family runs $700K-$1.2M, and luxury custom homes can exceed $1.5M. This is a significant price premium over comparable suburban Tampa communities. Buyers who want Steinbrenner HS at a lower entry point often look at Lutz, where Steinbrenner-zone homes can be found starting around $430K, though Westchase's full amenity package and walkable town center are not replicated in Lutz.

2. Mandatory Two-Tier HOA Fees

Westchase has a two-tier HOA structure. The Westchase Community Association (WCA) master HOA charges approximately $280-$400 per quarter, covering community pools, parks, trails, and common areas. On top of the WCA fee, most villages have a sub-association with additional monthly fees ranging from $50-$200+ depending on the village and what it maintains (exterior landscaping, additional amenities, gated entrances). Total HOA costs of $1,500-$3,600/year are common, and some village sub-associations run higher for townhomes. These fees are real and must be budgeted alongside the mortgage.

3. Limited Entry-Level Inventory

First-time buyers with budgets under $500K will find very limited options in Westchase proper. Townhomes and villas in the $380K-$550K range exist but move quickly. Single-family homes in the true $380K-$450K range in Westchase are essentially non-existent in the current market. Buyers who want into Westchase at a lower price point often need to wait for a townhome or accept a smaller footprint.

4. Rush Hour Traffic on Sheldon Road

The Sheldon Road corridor between Hillsborough Avenue and the Westchase community entrances gets congested during the 5:00-6:30 PM window. This is the one consistent complaint from Westchase residents about the commute home. Expressway users are largely insulated from this congestion, but surface-street commuters heading home on Sheldon Road experience daily delays. The issue is somewhat self-contained to that specific stretch and time window.

Who Is Westchase the Right Fit For?

Good fit: Families who place school quality as the top priority and need A-rated public schools from elementary through high school. Professionals who work in the Westshore corridor or at TPA and want a premium community within a short commute. Buyers who value walkability, community events, and neighborhood identity in a way most Tampa suburbs cannot deliver. Move-up buyers who want the best-amenitized west Tampa community and can afford the premium.

Not the right fit: Buyers with budgets under $450K (limited inventory; look at Town 'n' Country or Carrollwood). Buyers who want no HOA or low HOA costs. Buyers whose primary commute destination is South Tampa, Brandon, or east/south Hillsborough (the location advantage is less compelling). Investors looking for yield (HOA fees and prices compress rental returns relative to eastern Hillsborough County markets).

Yes, Westchase is widely regarded as one of the best neighborhoods in the Tampa Bay area. It consistently ranks highly for school quality, amenities, community organization, and quality of life. It is not the most affordable option in west Tampa, but buyers who can afford it tend to stay long-term and express high satisfaction with the decision.

What is the HOA fee in Westchase?

Westchase has a two-tier HOA structure. The WCA master HOA charges approximately $280-$400 per quarter for most homeowners. Sub-associations within individual villages add $50-$200+/month depending on the village. Total annual HOA costs commonly run $1,500-$3,600+. Verify both the WCA fee and the sub-association fee for any specific property during due diligence.

What is the Westchase Golf Club?

The Westchase Golf Club is an 18-hole championship course designed by Lloyd Clifton that runs through the heart of the Westchase community. It is open to the public (not a private member-only club). The course features a pro shop, practice range, putting greens, and a clubhouse with dining options. Some villages within Westchase (particularly Harbor Links) offer homes with direct golf course frontage.

Does Westchase have a grocery store?

Yes. A Publix grocery is located within West Park Village town center, walkable from most homes in the central Westchase villages. This is a genuine convenience that most Tampa suburbs cannot offer. Additional grocery options (Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, other Publix locations) are accessible within a 10-15 minute drive.

How does Westchase compare to Lutz for families?

Both Westchase and Lutz feed into Steinbrenner High School, making the high school zone comparable. Westchase adds the Westchase Elementary and Farnell Middle advantage, a walkable town center, the Westchase Golf Club, swim and tennis centers, and trail connectivity. Lutz offers more land, more diverse price points (starting around $430K for Steinbrenner-zone homes), and a more rural feel in some sections. Westchase is the premium community; Lutz is the value alternative for families who primarily want the Steinbrenner HS zone.

Village Sub-Associations

Most Westchase villages have their own sub-association with additional fees ranging from $50-$200+/month. The WCA enforces architectural standards covering exterior paint colors, landscaping, fences, additions, and visible improvements. Elementary and middle school quality is mixed, newer schools built to serve growing communities have outperformed older schools in annual state assessments. Families who prioritize top-rated public schools should verify zones carefully and consider charter and school choice options before buying.

School zone verification is one of the most important steps in buying a home in Wimauma. High Schools

It is not in the same tier as A-rated schools like Steinbrenner, Newsome, or Plant City High. Families who are prioritizing highly rated public high schools should research this carefully before committing to a Wimauma address.

East Bay High School serves northern Wimauma sections. East Bay's ratings have similarly been below county average in recent years. The school offers vocational and technical programs and serves a large, diverse student population from Gibsonton and southeast Hillsborough.

Middle Schools

Shields Middle School and Eisenhower Middle School both serve Wimauma addresses. State assessment scores for these schools are mixed, not among the top-rated middle schools in Hillsborough County but with dedicated staff and improving programs. The rapid growth in the area has added significant new enrollment in recent years.

Elementary Schools

Elementary school quality in Wimauma varies by school and recent year. Newer construction in the master-planned communities has brought more families with different demographic profiles into the school zones, and some elementary schools in the area have shown improvement in state grades. Florida offers several scholarship programs that allow families to use state funds for private school tuition. content:
Quick Answer

From most Wimauma neighborhoods, downtown Tampa is 40-50 minutes off-peak and 55-70 minutes during morning rush via I-75 north. MacDill AFB runs 40-55 minutes. Brandon is 25-35 minutes via US-301 north. Wimauma works for hybrid and south Hillsborough commuters. Daily Tampa office commuters should budget 80-110 minutes round trip in normal traffic.

Wimauma (ZIP 33598) sits at the southern edge of Hillsborough County, which makes it one of the most affordable new construction markets in the Tampa Bay area, and one of the longer commutes to Tampa's employment centers. Understanding actual drive times before you buy is the most important pre-purchase research you can do.

What Are the Best Routes from Wimauma?

Route 1: US-301 North to I-75 North (Primary Tampa Route)

Most Wimauma neighborhoods are east of US-301 or directly on the US-301 corridor. Heading north on US-301 to the I-75 interchange at Big Bend Road (Exit 246) is the most direct path to Tampa. From Big Bend, I-75 north runs to downtown Tampa exits at I-4 (Exit 260A) or Ybor/downtown exits. This route is free, no tolls. Morning rush congestion builds on I-75 northbound between Gibsonton and downtown starting around 7:00-7:30 AM.

Route 2: CR-672 West to US-41 North (Alternative for MacDill or Ruskin Destinations)

County Road 672 (Balm Wimauma Road / Boyette Road connector west) provides a cross-county route from Wimauma toward Ruskin and the US-41 corridor. This is the best route for residents commuting to Apollo Beach employers, Ruskin businesses, or MacDill AFB via US-41 south through the Gandy Bridge approach. This route avoids I-75 entirely and is often faster for south and west destinations during peak I-75 congestion.

Route 3: US-301 South to I-75 South (Sarasota and Bradenton)

Wimauma's position at the county line makes it surprisingly convenient for Sarasota and Manatee County employment. US-301 south connects to I-75 south at the Hillsborough/Manatee county line, reaching Sarasota in roughly 45-55 minutes off-peak. This equidistant positioning, Tampa roughly the same drive time as Sarasota, is a lifestyle feature some buyers value for weekend access to the Sarasota arts scene and Gulf Coast beaches.

Are There Tolls on Wimauma Commutes?

The primary I-75 corridor is free. If you use the Selmon Expressway (Lee Roy Selmon Crosstown) to reach downtown Tampa from I-75, toll costs run approximately $1.00-$3.00 per trip depending on entry and exit points, adding $40-$120/month for daily commuters using SunPass. The Veterans Expressway (SR-589) is not in the typical Wimauma commute path.

Is Public Transit an Option from Wimauma?

No practical public transit connects Wimauma to Tampa. HART (Hillsborough Area Regional Transit) does not serve Wimauma directly. Wimauma is a car-dependent community, every household should budget for reliable vehicle transportation. Rideshare surge pricing can be unpredictable in this far-south location during peak hours.

  • Leave by 6:45 AM to avoid the worst of the I-75 northbound backup at Big Bend and Gibsonton. After 7:15 AM, add 15-25 minutes.
  • Use Waze or Google Maps live US-301 surface congestion from Riverview south to Sun City Center can vary significantly on school days vs. holidays.
  • CR-672 is your friend for west-bound trips If heading toward Apollo Beach, Ruskin, or Gibsonton, use CR-672 west instead of backtracking north on US-301.
  • MacDill commuters: US-41 north through Ruskin to Gandy is often comparable to or faster than the I-75 route during peak hours, test both in your first month.
  • Hybrid schedules change the math: A 3-day-per-week Tampa commuter spends roughly the same transit time as a 5-day Brandon commuter. Run the numbers for your specific schedule.

title: Is Wimauma FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Pros and Cons
excerpt: Honest assessment of living in Wimauma, FL, the good, the not-so-good, and what you need to know before moving.
content:
Quick Answer

Wimauma, FL is a good choice for buyers who prioritize affordability, new construction, and south Hillsborough's lower cost base. Trade-offs include a 40-55 minute commute to Tampa, below-average legacy schools, and CDD fees layered on top of HOA costs in most new communities. It is not the right fit for everyone, but for buyers who do the math, it delivers more house per dollar than most Tampa Bay zip codes.

Wimauma (ZIP 33598) sits in south Hillsborough County, roughly 30 miles south of downtown Tampa along the US-301 corridor. The area has transformed over the past decade from a rural agricultural community into one of Hillsborough's fastest-growing new-construction markets. Understanding what that growth means for daily life takes more than reading a builder's brochure.

What Are the Pros of Living in Wimauma?

1. More House for the Money

New construction in Wimauma runs from the low $290Ks for smaller DR Horton and LGI entry-level plans to the mid-$400Ks for Lennar's larger designs. For that same budget in Brandon or Riverview, buyers are often competing for older resale homes with deferred maintenance and no builder warranty. Wimauma delivers fresh construction, modern floor plans, and smart home features at a price point those closer-in markets cannot match.

2. New Master-Planned Communities

Communities like Berry Bay (Lennar), Ayersworth Glen (DR Horton), Sundance (Lennar), and Cedarbrook (Ryan Homes) include resort-style amenity centers, pools, playgrounds, and walking trails built into the community cost. These are not bolt-on amenities added years later, they are part of the original development plan. Residents get lifestyle infrastructure that comparable-price resale neighborhoods in Brandon or Seffner do not offer.

3. Hillsborough County Services Without City Taxes

Wimauma is unincorporated Hillsborough County, meaning residents pay no city taxes. You receive county services, fire, sheriff, road maintenance, without the additional municipal tax layer that incorporated cities like Plant City or Temple Terrace carry. The total millage rate in Hillsborough County runs approximately 19-20 mills, and CDD assessments vary by community (see the trade-offs section below).

4. Proximity to Sun City Center and Ruskin

Sun City Center is 10-15 minutes north on US-301 or US-41, giving Wimauma residents access to additional retail, the Sun City Center medical corridor (South Bay Hospital), and the recreational amenities of that community (though 55+ membership rules apply there). Ruskin's waterfront dining and marina area is 15-20 minutes west via CR-672. These nearby communities add lifestyle options that a purely rural zip code would not provide.

5. Growing Retail and Commercial Base

The growth of master-planned communities along US-301 south has attracted commercial development. Walmart Supercenter on US-301, a Publix-anchored center, and expanding fast-casual dining options have come to the corridor within the past few years. The retail base is still developing relative to Brandon or Riverview, but it is meaningfully better than it was five years ago.

What Are the Trade-Offs of Living in Wimauma?

1. The Tampa Commute Is Real

From most Wimauma neighborhoods, reaching downtown Tampa takes 40-50 minutes off-peak via I-75 north, and 55-70 minutes during morning rush hour. MacDill AFB runs 40-55 minutes depending on base gate and Wimauma origin. This is not a deal-breaker for hybrid workers or those employed in south Hillsborough, but buyers who commute daily to Tampa should budget this time honestly. See the Wimauma commute guide for specific route breakdowns.

2. CDD Fees on Top of HOA Fees

Most of Wimauma's new construction communities are built within Community Development Districts. CDD assessments typically run $1,500-$3,500 per year on top of HOA fees of $200-$600 per year. These fees appear on your property tax bill as a separate line item, not in the mortgage payment some buyers budget from the builder's worksheet. On a $340K purchase, a $2,500 CDD assessment adds roughly $208/month to your true housing cost. Always request the CDD bond balance and annual assessment before writing an offer.

3. Schools in Transition

The legacy schools serving older parts of Wimauma have historically rated below the Hillsborough County average. Lennard High School and East Bay High School, the two high schools serving most Wimauma addresses, both have room to improve relative to top-rated Hillsborough campuses like Steinbrenner or Plant City. Elementary school options include Wimauma Community School and several newer schools built to serve the growing population. Families who prioritize highly rated schools may find Lithia or Wesley Chapel more satisfying. See the Wimauma schools guide for a full breakdown.

4. Limited Established Neighborhood Character

Wimauma's rapid growth means most of the housing stock is very new, many communities are still actively under construction. Mature trees, established sidewalks, and walkable neighborhood character take years to develop. Buyers who want a neighborhood that feels settled and lived-in should look at Brandon, Riverview, or Valrico for resale inventory in established subdivisions.

5. Flood Zone Considerations in Some Sections

Some sections of Wimauma near the Bullfrog Creek drainage basin and low-lying areas on the east side carry FEMA flood zone designations. Always check the specific parcel on msc.fema.gov before purchase. Flood zone AE designation requires flood insurance in addition to standard homeowners coverage, that can add $800-$2,500/year to carrying costs depending on elevation and structure. The newer master-planned communities are typically graded to minimize flood exposure, but individual parcels vary.

Wimauma works well for:

  • First-time buyers stretching their budget as far as possible

  • Investors targeting new construction with builder warranties for long-term hold

  • Commute daily to Tampa or MacDill and are not willing to spend 80-110 minutes per day in the car

Wimauma is one of the most active new construction markets in Hillsborough County. Lennar, DR Horton, Ryan Homes, and LGI are the primary builders. Prices start in the low $290Ks and run to the mid-$400Ks and above. Every community carries CDD fees of $1,500-$3,500 per year on top of HOA, understand this cost before comparing Wimauma to older areas with no CDD.

Wimauma's transformation from agricultural land into one of Tampa Bay's primary new construction corridors has happened rapidly. The US-301 corridor through south Hillsborough County now hosts multiple active builder communities targeting entry-level and move-up buyers priced out of Brandon, Riverview, and Apollo Beach. If you are buying new construction in Wimauma, understanding how the builder sales process works, and what the real all-in cost looks like, is more important than touring model homes.
