  3. Real Estate Market Overview
  4. Waterfront and Beach Real Estate
  5. Best Neighborhoods for Families
  6. Best Areas for Retirees
  7. Best Areas for Investors
  8. Downtown St. Petersburg
  9. Schools and Education
  10. Property Taxes
  11. Transportation and Commutes
  12. Lifestyle, Beaches, and Culture
  13. Tips for Buying in Pinellas County
  14. Frequently Asked Questions
Talk to a Tampa Bay ExpertSearch All Homes

Pinellas County Overview

Pinellas County occupies a peninsula on Florida's central Gulf Coast, bordered by Tampa Bay to the east and the Gulf of Mexico to the west. Despite being the smallest county by area in Florida (just 280 square miles), it's the most densely populated with nearly one million residents packed into a narrow strip of land that averages only 10 miles wide.

This geographic constraint is the defining feature of Pinellas County real estate. Unlike Hillsborough County, which can expand into rural land to the east, Pinellas is essentially built out. There is very little vacant land left for new development, which means supply is permanently constrained while demand continues to grow. For buyers and investors, this translates to strong long-term appreciation and a market that tends to hold value better during downturns.

The county includes the cities of St. Petersburg (population ~265,000), Clearwater (~117,000), Largo (~85,000), and dozens of smaller municipalities and beach communities. It's connected to Hillsborough County by four bridges: the Howard Frankland (I-275), Gandy Bridge, Courtney Campbell Causeway, and the Bayside Bridge.

Major Cities and Beach Towns

St. Petersburg

St. Pete is the largest city in Pinellas County and has experienced a remarkable transformation over the past decade. Downtown St. Petersburg is now one of the most desirable urban neighborhoods in Florida, with a thriving arts scene, nationally recognized restaurants, craft breweries, and a waterfront that rivals any in the state. Neighborhoods like Snell Isle, Old Northeast, and Historic Kenwood attract buyers seeking walkability and character.

Clearwater

Clearwater anchors the northern end of the county. Clearwater Beach consistently ranks among the best beaches in America, driving strong tourism and vacation-rental demand. The mainland side of Clearwater offers more affordable options, while the beach and nearby Belleair command premium waterfront prices.

Dunedin

Dunedin is a charming small city north of Clearwater with a walkable downtown, craft breweries, the Pinellas Trail running through its center, and access to Honeymoon Island and Caladesi Island State Parks. It's become increasingly popular with younger buyers and transplants drawn to its village-like atmosphere.

Safety Harbor and Tarpon Springs

Safety Harbor sits on Tampa Bay's western shore with a quaint downtown and the historic Safety Harbor Resort and Spa. Tarpon Springs, at the county's northern tip, is known for its Greek heritage, sponge docks, and a growing arts community. Both offer a quieter lifestyle with lower price points than the beach communities.

Beach Communities

Pinellas County's barrier islands host a string of beach towns, each with its own character:

  • Indian Rocks Beach Low-key, family-friendly beach town with a mix of condos and single-family homes
  • Treasure Island and Pass-a-Grille Relaxed Gulf-front communities with wide beaches and strong vacation-rental markets
  • Madeira Beach Home to John's Pass Village, a popular tourist destination with waterfront dining and shops
  • Sand Key and Tierra Verde Upscale waterfront communities with luxury condos and island living
  • Redington Shores / North Redington Beach Quieter beach communities popular with retirees and seasonal residents

Inland Communities

Largo, Seminole, and Pinellas Park form the county's inland core and offer the most affordable housing options in Pinellas. These communities provide practical, everyday living with shopping, dining, and services, without the beach premium. Median prices in these areas typically run $300K to $400K, significantly below the waterfront communities.

Real Estate Market Overview

Pinellas County's real estate market is driven by its geographic constraints and desirability. Here's a snapshot of current pricing:

Area Median Home Price Typical Buyer
Downtown St. Pete / Old Northeast$500K to $900KUrban professionals, walkability seekers
Snell Isle$800K to $3M+Luxury waterfront buyers
Clearwater Beach$500K to $2M+ (condos)Vacation, investment, seasonal
Dunedin$400K to $650KLifestyle buyers, young professionals
Safety Harbor$380K to $550KFamilies, quiet lifestyle
Largo / Seminole / Pinellas Park$300K to $400KBudget-conscious, first-time buyers
Treasure Island / Pass-a-Grille$500K to $1.5MBeach lifestyle, vacation rental
Tarpon Springs$320K to $480KValue buyers, cultural community

Because Pinellas is nearly built out, the market is dominated by resale properties rather than new construction. Buyers willing to renovate older homes can find significant value, and programs like the FHA 203(k) renovation loan make this feasible for many purchasers.

Waterfront and Beach Real Estate

Waterfront property is what defines Pinellas County's luxury real estate market. With over 580 miles of shoreline between the Gulf, Tampa Bay, and the Intracoastal Waterway, water access is abundant but premium-priced.

Gulf-front condos are the most common waterfront property type, ranging from $400K studios to $3M+ penthouse units on Clearwater Beach and Sand Key. Single-family waterfront homes on Tampa Bay or the Intracoastal are rarer and command $800K to well over $2M depending on location and water access.

Key considerations for waterfront buyers include flood insurance requirements, wind mitigation credits, condo association special assessments (especially post-Surfside legislation), and seawall condition on bayside properties.

Best Neighborhoods for Families

  • Safety Harbor Excellent schools, a family-oriented downtown, parks, and reasonable prices make this one of Pinellas's best family values
  • Seminole Strong schools (Seminole High), established neighborhoods with larger lots, and a suburban feel
  • Dunedin Walkable downtown, great parks, Pinellas Trail access, and a tight-knit community feel
  • Palm Harbor (unincorporated) Just north of the county line in the Pinellas school district, Palm Harbor offers newer subdivisions and top-rated schools
  • Clearwater (mainland) More affordable than the beach with good school access and family-friendly neighborhoods in the Countryside area

Best Areas for Retirees

  • Clearwater Beach / Sand Key Low-maintenance condo living with beach access, restaurants, and healthcare nearby
  • Indian Rocks Beach / Redington Quieter beach communities with a laid-back pace and manageable condo options
  • Largo Affordable, central location with excellent medical facilities (Largo Medical Center) and 55+ communities
  • St. Pete Beach / Tierra Verde Upscale island living with boating access and Gulf views
  • Downtown St. Pete For active retirees who want walkable culture, dining, arts, and a vibrant social scene

Best Areas for Real Estate Investors

Pinellas County offers strong investment opportunities across multiple strategies:

  • Short-term vacation rentals Beach communities like Clearwater Beach, Indian Rocks Beach, and Treasure Island generate strong Airbnb/VRBO income (check local STR regulations)
  • Long-term rentals Inland communities like Largo, Pinellas Park, and Lealman offer affordable entry points with steady tenant demand
  • Value-add renovation Older homes in St. Pete neighborhoods (Kenwood, Coquina Key, Shore Acres) can be purchased below market, renovated, and either flipped or rented at a premium
  • Condo investment Waterfront condos in well-managed buildings offer appreciation plus rental income, but carefully evaluate reserves, special assessments, and insurance costs post-Senate Bill 4D

Downtown St. Petersburg: A Market Within a Market

Downtown St. Pete deserves special attention because its transformation over the past decade has been remarkable. What was once a sleepy retiree town has become one of the most vibrant urban districts in the Southeast, with nationally recognized restaurants, the Dali Museum, a thriving mural arts scene, weekly markets, and a waterfront park system that rivals much larger cities.

Real estate in downtown St. Pete ranges from $300K condos in older mid-rises to $2M+ luxury units in newer towers. Single-family homes in adjacent neighborhoods like Old Northeast, Snell Isle, and Historic Kenwood range from $500K for bungalows to several million for waterfront estates. The walkability factor, unusual for Florida, commands a significant premium.

Schools and Education

Pinellas County Schools serves approximately 96,000 students across 130+ schools. The district offers:

  • Fundamental schools A unique Pinellas County program emphasizing discipline, homework, and parental involvement; highly sought-after and admission-based
  • Magnet programs in arts, STEM, IB, and gifted education
  • Top-rated schools concentrated in Seminole, Safety Harbor, Palm Harbor, and north Pinellas
  • School choice allowing open enrollment across the county

Higher education options include St. Petersburg College (one of the largest community colleges in the state), Eckerd College, and the University of South Florida St. Petersburg campus.

Property Taxes in Pinellas County

Pinellas County's property tax rates are comparable to Hillsborough County, with combined millage rates of approximately 19 to 22 mills depending on the municipality. The effective rate works out to roughly 0.9 to 1.2% of assessed value after exemptions.

Florida's $50,000 Homestead Exemption and Save Our Homes 3% annual cap apply here as well. For investors and non-homesteaded properties, taxes will be higher since these exemptions don't apply. Condo owners should also factor in association fees, which can range from $300 to $1,500+ per month in waterfront buildings.

Transportation and Commutes

Pinellas County's biggest transportation challenge is the bridge commute to Hillsborough County. If you work in Tampa, expect:

From To Downtown Tampa Route
Downtown St. Pete25 to 45 minI-275 (Howard Frankland)
Clearwater30 to 50 minCourtney Campbell / SR 60
Largo / Seminole30 to 50 minI-275 or Gandy Bridge
Dunedin / Palm Harbor40 to 60 minCourtney Campbell / US 19

Bridge traffic is the primary bottleneck, particularly during rush hours. Remote workers and those who work within Pinellas County benefit from avoiding this altogether. PSTA (Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority) operates bus routes throughout the county, and the Su Runner BRT line now connects downtown St. Pete to St. Pete Beach. St. Pete, Clearwater International Airport (PIE) handles domestic flights and is a low-cost alternative to Tampa International.

Lifestyle, Beaches, and Culture

Pinellas County's lifestyle is defined by water, weather, and culture:

  • Beaches: 35 miles of Gulf beaches including Clearwater Beach (#1 in USA multiple years), St. Pete Beach, and Caladesi Island (accessible only by boat or ferry)
  • Arts and culture: The Dali Museum, Chihuly Collection, Museum of Fine Arts, Imagine Museum, and a nationally recognized mural arts district in St. Pete
  • Outdoor recreation: The Pinellas Trail (a 75-mile paved bike/walk trail spanning the county), Fort De Soto Park, Honeymoon Island, and Weedon Island Preserve
  • Dining: St. Petersburg has emerged as a nationally recognized food city with James Beard-nominated restaurants, craft breweries, and a vibrant culinary scene
  • Sports: Tampa Bay Rays (Tropicana Field in St. Pete), spring training for the Phillies (Clearwater) and Blue Jays (Dunedin)

Tips for Buying in Pinellas County

  1. Get flood insurance quotes early Much of Pinellas is in FEMA flood zones. Flood insurance can add $1,000 to $5,000+ annually depending on zone and elevation
  2. Scrutinize condo financials Florida's new reserve requirements (Senate Bill 4D) mean older condo buildings may face special assessments. Review reserve studies carefully
  3. Factor in wind and flood insurance Barrier island properties face higher insurance costs; get quotes before making an offer
  4. Understand STR regulations Short-term rental rules vary by municipality. Some beach towns have strict regulations or bans on vacation rentals
  5. Consider renovation opportunities With limited new construction, buying an older home and renovating can provide significant equity
  6. Plan your commute If you work in Tampa, drive the bridge route during rush hour before committing to a Pinellas purchase

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average home price in Pinellas County?

The countywide median home price in Pinellas County is approximately $380,000 to $430,000. However, prices vary widely: inland areas like Largo and Pinellas Park average $300K to $400K, while waterfront and beach properties range from $500K to well over $1 million. Downtown St. Pete and luxury waterfront homes in Snell Isle can exceed $2M+.

Is Pinellas County a good place to buy a home?

Yes, particularly for long-term appreciation. Pinellas County's constrained land supply means new inventory is limited, supporting property values even during market corrections. The county offers beach lifestyle, walkable urban neighborhoods in St. Pete, strong cultural amenities, and no state income tax. The trade-off is higher insurance costs and bridge commute times to Tampa.

What are the best beach towns in Pinellas County?

Clearwater Beach is the most famous and highest-priced. Indian Rocks Beach offers a more laid-back, less touristy atmosphere. Treasure Island and Pass-a-Grille provide wide beaches with strong vacation-rental potential. St. Pete Beach is popular for both full-time residents and seasonal visitors. Dunedin provides nearby beach access (Honeymoon Island) with a walkable downtown.

How are the schools in Pinellas County?

Pinellas County Schools serves about 96,000 students. The district's unique Fundamental School program is highly sought-after. Top-performing schools are concentrated in Seminole, Safety Harbor, and Palm Harbor. The district offers magnet programs, IB, and open school choice that allows families to apply outside their zoned area.

What is the property tax rate in Pinellas County?

Pinellas County's combined millage rate is approximately 19 to 22 mills, resulting in an effective tax rate of about 0.9 to 1.2% of assessed value. Florida's $50,000 Homestead Exemption and Save Our Homes 3% annual cap reduce taxes for primary residents. Condo owners should also budget for association fees, which can be substantial in waterfront buildings.

Is Pinellas County good for real estate investors?

Yes, with the right strategy. Beach properties can generate strong short-term vacation rental income (verify local STR regulations). Inland areas like Largo and Pinellas Park offer affordable long-term rental properties with steady tenant demand. Value-add renovation projects in St. Pete neighborhoods provide equity upside. The constrained land supply supports long-term appreciation across the county.

What is the cost of living in Pinellas County?

Pinellas County's cost of living is approximately 5 to 10% above the national average, driven primarily by housing costs and insurance. Waterfront and beach areas are significantly more expensive than inland communities. Florida has no state income tax, which helps offset the higher cost of living. Compared to Hillsborough County, Pinellas generally runs 10 to 20% higher for similar property types due to the beach premium and limited supply.

How does Pinellas County compare to Hillsborough County for real estate?

Pinellas County offers beach access, walkable urban neighborhoods (St. Pete), and constrained supply that supports appreciation. Hillsborough County offers more affordable housing, abundant new construction, and larger lots. Pinellas prices run 10 to 20% higher for comparable properties. Hillsborough has better highway access and more room to grow. The choice typically comes down to lifestyle preference: beach and urban walkability (Pinellas) versus space, affordability, and newer construction (Hillsborough).

Best Neighborhoods in Dover: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Dover offers agricultural character and affordable acreage east of Brandon, with homes from $280K to $500K+. Strawberry farms, large lots, and proximity to I-4 make it ideal for buyers who want land without leaving Hillsborough County.

Top picks: Sydney/Dover area ($300K-$500K+) for established homesteads, Plant City border ($280K-$420K) for small-town charm, rural Dover ($280K-$450K) for maximum acreage and agricultural freedom.

Dover sits in eastern Hillsborough County where the suburban development of Brandon and Valrico gives way to strawberry fields, cattle ranches, and oak-canopied country roads. This agricultural community straddles the line between Brandon's convenience and Plant City's small-town character, offering buyers something increasingly rare in the Tampa Bay metro: real land at a reasonable price.

With 23 years of experience selling homes, I point buyers toward Dover when they want acreage, agricultural zoning, and the ability to actually use their land, all while staying within 30 minutes of Tampa's urban core via I-4 or the Selmon Expressway.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Dover?

Sydney/Dover Area

Price range: $300K-$500K+

The Sydney Road and Dover Road intersection is the hub of the Dover community. Properties here tend to be well-established homesteads on 1-5+ acre parcels, many with mature fruit trees, outbuildings, and the kind of old-Florida character that new construction cannot replicate. You will find a mix of updated ranch homes, newer custom builds, and older properties with renovation potential. The area has a strong sense of community, with longtime families and newcomers coexisting along its rural roads.

  • Known for: Established homesteads, community character, and central Dover location
  • Best for: Families who want space and a small-community atmosphere
  • Standout features: Multi-acre lots, agricultural zoning, proximity to Dover Elementary, quick access to SR-60 for Brandon and Tampa commutes

Plant City Border

Price range: $280K-$420K

The eastern edge of Dover blends into the Plant City area, and this border zone offers some of the best value in eastern Hillsborough County. Properties here combine Dover's agricultural zoning and larger lot sizes with proximity to Plant City's charming downtown, restaurants, and the annual Florida Strawberry Festival. You get the rural Dover lifestyle with small-town amenities just a short drive away.

  • Known for: Proximity to Plant City's downtown, strawberry farms, and agricultural heritage
  • Best for: Buyers who want rural living with nearby small-town charm
  • Standout features: Close to Plant City restaurants and shops, Florida Strawberry Festival access, I-4 interchange nearby for Tampa commuting, lower price points than inner Dover

Rural Dover

Price range: $280K-$450K

South and east of the Dover core, the roads get quieter and the lots get bigger. This is where you will find 5-20+ acre parcels with active agricultural use, strawberry fields, cattle grazing, plant nurseries, and hobby farms. Homes here range from modest older houses to newer custom builds that take advantage of the space and privacy. If your goal is maximum land for the dollar in Hillsborough County, rural Dover delivers.

  • Known for: Large-acreage parcels, working farms, and wide-open space
  • Best for: Hobby farmers, equestrian buyers, and anyone who wants maximum land
  • Standout features: 5-20+ acre parcels available, active agricultural community, agricultural tax exemptions for qualifying properties, no HOA restrictions

Turkey Creek Road Area

Price range: $300K-$480K

Turkey Creek Road runs through the northern portion of Dover, connecting to SR-60 (Brandon's main east-west artery) and providing quick access to Brandon's shopping, dining, and healthcare. Properties along Turkey Creek tend to be on 1-3 acre lots with a mix of older ranch homes and newer construction. This is the sweet spot for buyers who want Dover's space and agricultural character with the shortest possible commute to suburban conveniences.

  • Known for: Convenient access to Brandon while maintaining rural character
  • Best for: Commuters who work in Brandon or western Hillsborough County
  • Standout features: Fastest route to Brandon shopping and SR-60, 1-3 acre lots at moderate prices, balance of rural and suburban accessibility

Dover Market Context for 2026

Dover's real estate market is driven by a simple supply-and-demand reality: they are not making more agricultural land this close to Tampa. As suburban development continues to push east from Brandon and Valrico, Dover's large-lot properties become more scarce and more valuable. Buyers who purchase acreage here in 2026 are buying something that cannot be replicated once the surrounding area develops further.

The area benefits from I-4 access for Tampa commuters and from Plant City's growing appeal as a dining and entertainment destination. Dover itself remains unincorporated and agricultural, which keeps property taxes reasonable and gives homeowners the freedom to use their land without HOA or municipal restrictions.

View current listings in the Dover area or browse Dover homes for sale.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Dover FL a good place to live?

Dover is an excellent choice if you want acreage and agricultural freedom within commuting distance of Tampa and Brandon. The tradeoff is that Dover has limited commercial development, you will drive to Brandon or Plant City for most shopping and dining. For buyers who prioritize land and privacy over walkable retail, Dover is hard to beat in Hillsborough County.

How far is Dover from Tampa?

Dover is approximately 25-30 minutes from downtown Tampa via I-4 or SR-60. Brandon's major shopping areas are 10-15 minutes west, and Plant City's downtown is 10 minutes east. Most Dover residents commute westbound for work and appreciate the reverse-commute advantage of living east of the metro core.

Can you keep horses in Dover?

Yes. Most of Dover is zoned for agricultural use, which permits horses, livestock, and farming operations. Dover is one of the most horse-friendly areas in Hillsborough County, with properties that include barns, paddocks, and fenced pasture. Verify the specific zoning on any property you are considering.

What school district serves Dover?

Dover is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools. Dover Elementary is the local elementary school, and students typically feed into middle and high schools in the Brandon or Plant City area. Several private and charter school options are available in nearby Brandon.

Best Neighborhoods in Thonotosassa: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Thonotosassa offers rural acreage and large-lot living just 15-20 minutes from Tampa, with homes ranging from $300K to $600K+. It is the best option in Hillsborough County for buyers who want land, horses, or privacy without a long commute.

Top picks: Hillsborough River area ($350K-$600K+) for waterfront acreage, Morris Bridge corridor ($320K-$500K) for nature access, rural Thonotosassa ($300K-$450K) for affordable land and agricultural freedom.

Thonotosassa is where Tampa Bay's suburban sprawl gives way to open pastures, oak-lined dirt roads, and properties measured in acres rather than square feet. This unincorporated Hillsborough County community sits northeast of Tampa, roughly 15-20 minutes from I-75 and I-4, yet feels like a completely different world from the subdivisions and strip malls that define most of the metro area.

In 23 years of selling real estate, I consistently recommend Thonotosassa to buyers who want land, privacy, and room for horses or hobby farms without sacrificing access to Tampa's job market. Here is a breakdown of the area's best neighborhoods and pockets.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Thonotosassa?

Hillsborough River Area

Price range: $350K-$600K+

Properties along the Hillsborough River in Thonotosassa represent some of the most unique real estate in all of Hillsborough County. You are talking about multi-acre parcels with direct river frontage, mature hardwood canopy, and wildlife (including manatees in the cooler months). Homes range from updated Florida ranch houses to custom-built retreats. River-front lots command a premium, but the lifestyle is unlike anything you will find elsewhere this close to Tampa.

  • Known for: River frontage, kayaking, fishing, and natural beauty
  • Best for: Buyers who want a retreat-like setting with Tampa access
  • Standout features: Direct Hillsborough River access, multi-acre lots, wildlife viewing, proximity to Hillsborough River State Park

Morris Bridge Corridor

Price range: $320K-$500K

The Morris Bridge Road corridor runs north-south through Thonotosassa and connects to the Hillsborough River, Flatwoods Park, and the Trout Creek and Morris Bridge nature areas. This is outdoor recreation central for northeast Hillsborough County. Properties along this corridor sit on generous lots, typically 1-5 acres, and many are zoned for agricultural use, meaning you can keep livestock, build outbuildings, and use the land as you see fit.

  • Known for: Nature preserves, hiking and biking trails, and agricultural zoning
  • Best for: Outdoor enthusiasts, hobby farmers, and equestrian buyers
  • Standout features: Adjacent to Flatwoods Park (over 5,000 acres of trails), agricultural zoning for horses and livestock, peaceful rural setting minutes from New Tampa and I-75

Rural Thonotosassa

Price range: $300K-$450K

The broader rural areas of Thonotosassa, along McIntosh Road, Thonotosassa Road, and the smaller side roads, offer the most affordable path to acreage in northeast Hillsborough County. Properties here are typically 1-10+ acres with older homes, and many buyers purchase with plans to renovate or build new. The agricultural zoning and lack of HOA restrictions give homeowners freedom that is nearly impossible to find closer to Tampa.

  • Known for: Affordable acreage, agricultural properties, and small-town character
  • Best for: Buyers who want land and freedom at a reasonable price point
  • Standout features: No HOA, agricultural zoning, large lots at the lowest price per acre in the Tampa area, room for workshops, barns, and outbuildings

Equestrian Properties

Price range: $400K-$600K+

Thonotosassa is Hillsborough County's primary equestrian community. Several properties feature barns, paddocks, riding arenas, and fenced pasture on 5-20+ acre parcels. The area's agricultural zoning supports horse keeping without the deed restrictions you will encounter in most suburban communities. If you are looking for a horse property within commuting distance of Tampa, Thonotosassa is your starting point.

  • Known for: Horse properties, barns, and riding trails
  • Best for: Equestrian families and hobby farmers
  • Standout features: Purpose-built equestrian facilities, trail riding access, agricultural tax exemptions available for qualifying properties, 20 minutes to I-75

Thonotosassa Market Context for 2026

Thonotosassa occupies a unique niche in the Tampa Bay market. While most of Hillsborough County trends toward higher density and smaller lots, Thonotosassa has maintained its rural character thanks to agricultural zoning and the Hillsborough River corridor's environmental protections. This means supply stays limited, when a well-maintained acreage property hits the market, it does not last long.

The area benefits from its proximity to the booming New Tampa and Wesley Chapel corridors without absorbing their development pressure. For buyers who value land and privacy, Thonotosassa delivers something that simply does not exist elsewhere this close to a major metro area.

View current listings in the Thonotosassa area or browse Thonotosassa homes for sale.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Thonotosassa a good place to live?

Thonotosassa is an excellent choice for buyers who want rural living with Tampa access. The area is quiet, properties are spacious, and the Hillsborough River and surrounding nature preserves provide outstanding outdoor recreation. It is not the right fit if you want walkable retail or suburban amenities, the tradeoff for acreage is that you will drive for groceries and restaurants.

How far is Thonotosassa from Tampa?

Most Thonotosassa properties are 15-20 minutes from I-75 at the Morris Bridge Road exit, putting downtown Tampa about 30 minutes away in normal traffic. The New Tampa area with major shopping and dining is roughly 10-15 minutes north.

Can you have horses in Thonotosassa?

Yes. Much of Thonotosassa is zoned for agricultural use, which permits horses, livestock, and other farm animals. This is one of the primary reasons equestrian buyers gravitate to the area. Check the specific zoning for any property you are considering, as some parcels may have different designations.

Are there flood concerns in Thonotosassa?

Properties along the Hillsborough River and its tributaries may fall within FEMA flood zones. River-front parcels in particular should be evaluated carefully for flood insurance requirements. Properties on higher ground away from waterways are generally outside high-risk flood zones, but always verify the specific flood zone for any property before making an offer.

Best Neighborhoods in Gibsonton: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Gibsonton is the most affordable community in south Hillsborough County, with homes ranging from $250K to $400K. Rapid development and I-75 access make it a strong pick for buyers priced out of Riverview and Brandon.

Top picks: Riverview/Gibsonton border ($300K-$400K) for newer construction, Gibsonton proper ($250K-$340K) for value buyers, Alafia area ($280K-$380K) for river access, Symmes Road corridor ($260K-$360K) for commuters.

Gibsonton, locals call it "Gibtown", has been one of the fastest-improving areas in south Hillsborough County over the past several years. Sitting along U.S. 41 between Riverview and Apollo Beach, Gibsonton offers the lowest entry price in the southern Tampa Bay corridor while benefiting from the same infrastructure investments and commercial growth that have transformed neighboring Riverview.

After 23 years selling real estate, I tell buyers that Gibsonton in 2026 looks a lot like Riverview did 10 years ago: affordable, improving rapidly, and positioned for strong appreciation as development pushes south along the I-75 corridor. Here is where to focus your search.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Gibsonton?

Riverview/Gibsonton Border

Price range: $300K-$400K

The northern edge of Gibsonton blends seamlessly into the Riverview community, and this border zone offers the best of both worlds, Gibsonton pricing with Riverview-quality newer construction. Several subdivisions built in the 2010s and 2020s feature modern floor plans, community amenities, and easy access to Big Bend Road and I-75. If you have been shopping in Riverview and finding prices above your budget, look at communities just south of the Riverview line.

  • Known for: Newer subdivisions, community pools, and sidewalk-lined streets
  • Best for: Families and commuters who want newer homes at below-Riverview prices
  • Standout features: Quick I-75 access, proximity to Riverview shopping and dining, newer construction with modern layouts and energy efficiency

Gibsonton Proper

Price range: $250K-$340K

The core of Gibsonton along U.S. 41 (Tamiami Trail) is where you will find the area's most affordable single-family homes. Properties here tend to be older construction on larger lots, and many come without HOA restrictions. This is prime territory for buyers who want space and value. The area has a distinct small-town character despite its proximity to Tampa, and longtime residents take pride in the community's unique history and identity.

  • Known for: Rock-bottom pricing for south Hillsborough County, large lots, and no-HOA freedom
  • Best for: First-time buyers, investors, and anyone who prioritizes value over polish
  • Standout features: Lowest entry price in the I-75 south corridor, generous lot sizes, proximity to Alafia River State Park

Alafia Area

Price range: $280K-$380K

The Alafia River runs through the eastern portion of Gibsonton, and properties near the river offer a more natural setting with kayaking, fishing, and wildlife access. Alafia River State Park provides over 6,000 acres of trails, mountain biking, and camping just minutes away. Homes in this pocket tend to sit on larger lots with mature tree canopy, giving the area a rural feel that contrasts with the newer subdivisions to the north.

  • Known for: River access, natural setting, and outdoor recreation
  • Best for: Outdoor enthusiasts, nature lovers, and buyers seeking privacy
  • Standout features: Kayak and fishing access on the Alafia River, proximity to Alafia River State Park, larger lot sizes with established landscaping

Symmes Road Corridor

Price range: $260K-$360K

The Symmes Road area in western Gibsonton connects to U.S. 41 and provides an alternative route to I-75 via Gibsonton Drive. This corridor has seen steady residential development and offers a mix of established homes and newer pockets. Grocery stores, restaurants, and services have followed the residential growth, making this a more self-sufficient part of Gibsonton where daily errands do not require a long drive.

  • Known for: Growing commercial services, mixed housing stock, and improving infrastructure
  • Best for: Commuters heading north on I-75 or south toward Sun City Center and Ruskin
  • Standout features: Dual access to U.S. 41 and I-75, growing retail and restaurant options, mid-range pricing with room for appreciation

Gibsonton Market Context for 2026

Gibsonton is in the middle of a transformation. Commercial development along U.S. 41 has accelerated, new residential construction continues to push south from Riverview, and the area's proximity to both I-75 and the bay gives it infrastructure advantages that support long-term growth. Median home prices remain 15-25% below neighboring Riverview, creating an opportunity for buyers and investors who can see where the trend line is heading.

For investors specifically, Gibsonton's low entry price and strong rental demand from the nearby Amazon and FedEx distribution centers make it one of the better cash-flow markets in Hillsborough County.

View current listings in the Gibsonton area or browse Gibsonton homes for sale.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Gibsonton a good place to live?

Gibsonton has improved significantly over the past decade and continues to see new investment in housing and commercial services. It offers the most affordable single-family homes in south Hillsborough County with direct I-75 access. Buyers who prioritize value and are comfortable with an area still in transition will find strong opportunities here.

Is Gibsonton safe?

Like any large unincorporated area, safety varies by neighborhood. The newer subdivisions near the Riverview border have the suburban infrastructure, streetlights, sidewalks, community management, that many buyers associate with safety. As with any purchase, drive the specific streets at different times of day before making a decision.

How far is Gibsonton from Tampa?

Downtown Tampa is approximately 20-25 minutes north via I-75 or U.S. 41, depending on traffic. The Westshore business district is about the same distance. MacDill Air Force Base is roughly 20 minutes west.

Is Gibsonton good for investment property?

Gibsonton is one of the stronger investment markets in Hillsborough County right now. Low purchase prices combined with solid rental demand from nearby distribution centers and the growing south county job base create favorable cash-flow numbers. Many investors priced out of Riverview and Brandon are finding better returns in Gibsonton.

Belmont - $300K-$400K - Affordable new construction

Best Neighborhoods in Wimauma: Where to Live in 2026

Wimauma has transformed from a quiet agricultural community into one of the fastest-growing areas in south Hillsborough County. New master-planned communities have brought modern amenities, resort-style pools, and well-designed floor plans to an area where prices still undercut Brandon and Valrico by $50K-$100K or more. The trade-off: longer commutes to Tampa and CDD fees that add $150-$300/month on top of your mortgage. For buyers who prioritize new construction, square footage, and community amenities over proximity to downtown, Wimauma delivers serious value.

After 23 years selling real estate, I have watched Wimauma evolve from "too far south" to "why didn't I buy there sooner." Here is my honest breakdown of the best neighborhoods. Learn more about Wimauma real estate.

Sereno

Sereno is the standout master-planned community in the Wimauma area. Built by Mattamy Homes and other national builders, it features a massive clubhouse, resort-style pool complex, fitness center, sports courts, and miles of walking trails. Homes range from $350K to $500K depending on size and lot. Most homes have 3-5 bedrooms, open floor plans, and modern finishes. CDD fees apply but the amenity package rivals communities priced $100K higher in FishHawk or Wesley Chapel.

  • Price range: $350K-$500K
  • Best for: Families wanting resort-style amenities at below-market prices
  • Schools: Zoned for Hillsborough County schools; some improvement in recent years as population has grown
  • Standout: One of the best amenity packages per dollar in all of Hillsborough County

South Fork

South Fork is a well-established master-planned community straddling the Riverview/Wimauma border. It offers a strong mix of single-family homes with community pools, playgrounds, and sports facilities. The community has been building out for over a decade, so you can find both newer construction and resale homes with mature landscaping. Prices typically run $320K-$450K.

  • Price range: $320K-$450K
  • Best for: Families and first-time buyers looking for established community feel
  • Schools: Eisenhower MS and Lennard HS zone
  • Standout: More mature trees and landscaping than newer Wimauma communities; slightly better commute position

Belmont

Belmont offers new construction at some of the most competitive prices in the area. National builders like Lennar and DR Horton deliver move-in-ready homes with modern floor plans, granite counters, and stainless appliances in the $300K-$400K range. Community amenities include a pool and playground. CDD fees are typical for the area.

  • Price range: $300K-$400K
  • Best for: First-time buyers and young families wanting new construction without the $400K+ price tag
  • Schools: Improving Hillsborough County schools in the south county corridor
  • Standout: Some of the lowest per-square-foot pricing for new homes in Hillsborough County

Ayersworth Glen

Ayersworth Glen sits on the northern edge of the Wimauma area, closer to Riverview. It is one of the more affordable master-planned options with homes in the $280K-$370K range. The community has a pool, clubhouse, and playground. Homes are mostly 3-4 bedroom single-family with attached 2-car garages. For buyers stretching to get into homeownership, this is a solid entry point.

  • Price range: $280K-$370K
  • Best for: Budget-conscious first-time buyers, investors looking for rental properties
  • Schools: Zoned for Hillsborough County south corridor schools
  • Standout: Lowest entry price among Wimauma's master-planned communities

Balm Area / Rural Acreage

If you want land, privacy, and no HOA, the rural pockets around Balm and eastern Wimauma still offer 1-5+ acre parcels. You will find older ranch-style homes, hobby farms, and equestrian properties alongside newer custom builds. Prices vary widely: $300K for a modest home on an acre up to $500K+ for newer construction on multiple acres. This is the anti-subdivision option for buyers who want space over amenities.

  • Price range: $300K-$500K+
  • Best for: Buyers wanting land, agricultural use, or complete privacy
  • Schools: Varies by exact location
  • Standout: No HOA, no CDD; some properties allow horses, livestock, and agricultural activity

Waterset (Apollo Beach/Wimauma Border)

Waterset straddles the Apollo Beach and Wimauma border. Technically it carries an Apollo Beach address, but it draws from the same buyer pool. This master-planned community by Newland features excellent amenities including a Crystal Lagoon-style pool, fitness center, dog parks, and event spaces. Homes range from $380K-$500K+. The community feels more upscale than most Wimauma options.

  • Price range: $380K-$500K+
  • Best for: Buyers wanting a premium community feel with new construction
  • Schools: Apollo Beach/Wimauma border school zones
  • Standout: Crystal Lagoon amenity and higher-end finishes set it apart from neighboring communities

Wimauma Housing Market Context (2026)

Wimauma's median home price sits around $350K in early 2026, well below the Hillsborough County median. Inventory has increased as builders delivered new phases, giving buyers more negotiating power than in 2021-2022. CDD fees remain the biggest surprise for newcomers; budget an extra $150-$300/month beyond your standard property taxes and insurance. Despite slower appreciation than the pandemic peak, Wimauma's growth trajectory remains strong as infrastructure improvements and commercial development continue pushing south along the US-301 corridor. See current Wimauma market data.

Find the Right Wimauma Realtor

Looking for a realtor who actually knows Wimauma? Read why Barrett Henry is the top-rated realtor in Wimauma -- 23+ years of experience, 5.0-star Google rating, and deep neighborhood knowledge.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are CDD fees in Wimauma and how much do they cost?

Community Development District (CDD) fees fund the infrastructure that builders needed to create these communities: roads, water management, parks, and amenities. In Wimauma, CDD fees typically run $150-$300/month and appear on your annual tax bill. They are not optional and do not go away, though they can decrease slightly over time as bonds are paid off. Always factor CDD fees into your monthly budget before committing to a purchase.

Are Wimauma schools good?

Wimauma schools have historically scored below county averages, but that is changing as the population grows and the county invests in the area. Families who prioritize top-rated schools may want to look at nearby Valrico or FishHawk. That said, several Wimauma schools have shown measurable improvement, and school choice options are available through Hillsborough County.

Is Wimauma a good investment in 2026?

Wimauma offers strong long-term investment potential due to below-market entry prices, continued population growth, and infrastructure development. Rental demand is solid as the area attracts workers priced out of Tampa and Brandon. The key risk is oversupply from builders delivering too many homes at once, which can soften prices short-term. For buy-and-hold investors, Wimauma's fundamentals are strong.

How far is Wimauma from Tampa?

Wimauma is roughly 30-40 minutes from downtown Tampa depending on traffic and your exact location. During rush hour, the commute via US-301 or I-75 can stretch to 45-60 minutes. This is the primary trade-off for Wimauma's lower prices. Remote workers and hybrid employees get the best of both worlds here.

Best Neighborhoods in Westchase: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Westchase's top neighborhoods include West Park Village ($500K-$800K), The Bridges ($550K-$900K+), and Glencliff ($450K-$700K). This master-planned community in west Tampa offers a walkable town center, top-rated schools (Alonso High School zone), and a true neighborhood feel.

Best for walkability: West Park Village | Best for families: Glencliff, Baybridge | Best for luxury: The Bridges

Westchase is consistently ranked among the best places to live in the Tampa Bay area, and it earns that ranking. This master-planned community in unincorporated west Hillsborough County delivers something rare in Florida: a walkable town center, excellent schools, and a genuine sense of community identity. When families tell me they want "the total package," Westchase is often the first neighborhood I show them.

Developed starting in the early 1990s, Westchase encompasses multiple distinct villages, each with its own character but sharing community amenities, a swim and tennis center, and the walkable West Park Village town center. For a broader look at the area, visit the Westchase city page.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Westchase?

West Park Village

Price range: $500K-$800K | Best for: Walkability seekers, empty nesters, professionals

West Park Village is the heart of Westchase and one of the most walkable neighborhoods in the entire Tampa Bay area. The village features a town center with restaurants, shops, a wine bar, a yoga studio, and a Publix. Residents can walk to dinner, grab coffee, and run errands without getting in a car. In Florida, that is genuinely rare.

Housing in West Park Village includes townhomes, courtyard homes, and single-family detached homes. The architecture has a traditional neighborhood design (TND) feel with front porches, alleys, and tree-lined sidewalks. The owners suite in most homes is on the second floor in the townhome models, while single-family homes offer first-floor primary options.

  • Walkable town center with restaurants and shops
  • Traditional neighborhood design with front porches
  • Mix of townhomes, courtyard homes, and single-family
  • Community events and farmers market

The Bridges

Price range: $550K-$900K+ | Best for: Luxury buyers, families wanting premium finishes

The Bridges is the premium village within Westchase, featuring larger homesites, higher-end finishes, and some of the most desirable floor plans in the community. Homes here range from 2,500 to over 4,000 square feet, many with expansive owners suites, three-car garages, and outdoor living spaces designed for Florida's climate.

The neighborhood has a quieter, more exclusive feel compared to the busier West Park Village, while still being a short drive or bike ride to the town center. The Bridges is particularly popular with move-up buyers who have outgrown their first Westchase home and want to stay in the community.

  • Larger homesites and premium construction
  • Homes from 2,500 to 4,000+ square feet
  • Quiet, established neighborhood feel
  • Popular with move-up buyers staying in Westchase

Glencliff

Price range: $450K-$700K | Best for: Families with school-age children, community-oriented buyers

Glencliff is one of Westchase's most popular family villages. The neighborhood features single-family homes on moderate-sized lots with sidewalks, mature trees, and a family-friendly feel. Many homes have been updated over the years, with renovated kitchens and expanded living spaces being common.

The village is well-positioned within Westchase for access to the community swim and tennis center, playgrounds, and the trail system. School zoning includes some of the most sought-after assignments in the Westchase area, making Glencliff particularly competitive among families with school-age children.

  • Prime family village within Westchase
  • Single-family homes with sidewalks and mature trees
  • Close to swim and tennis center
  • Sought-after school zone assignments

Baybridge

Price range: $400K-$650K | Best for: Families, first-time Westchase buyers, value seekers

Baybridge offers a more accessible entry point into Westchase while still delivering the community's signature amenities and school access. Homes here tend to be slightly smaller than in Glencliff or The Bridges, making this village popular with younger families and first-time buyers who are stretching to get into the Westchase school zone.

The neighborhood has a friendly, active feel with families using the sidewalks and community spaces regularly. Proximity to Citrus Park Mall and the Westchase commercial corridor along Linebaugh Avenue provides convenient retail and dining options beyond the town center.

  • More accessible Westchase price point
  • Full access to all Westchase community amenities
  • Same top school zoning as other villages
  • Close to Citrus Park Mall and Linebaugh retail

Additional Westchase Villages

Price range: $400K-$750K | Best for: Varies by village

Westchase includes over a dozen distinct villages beyond the ones highlighted above. Communities like Stamford, Keswick, and Harbor Links each have their own character, lot sizes, and price ranges. Some villages back up to the Westchase Golf Club, while others are tucked into quieter, more secluded sections of the master plan.

The advantage of Westchase's village structure is that nearly every buyer can find a fit somewhere in the community. Whether you want a golf course view, a larger lot, a smaller maintenance-free home, or a specific school assignment, there is likely a Westchase village that matches. Working with an agent who knows the individual villages is key to finding the right one.

  • Over a dozen distinct villages to choose from
  • Golf course, preserve, and pond-view options
  • All villages share Westchase community amenities
  • Each village has unique character and pricing

Westchase Real Estate Market Context for 2026

Westchase is one of the most competitive real estate markets in Tampa Bay in 2026. The combination of top schools (Alonso High School zone is a major driver), walkability, and community amenities creates consistent demand that keeps inventory low and prices firm. Homes in the $450K-$700K range typically receive multiple offers when priced correctly.

Because Westchase is fully built out with no new construction available, all transactions are resale. This scarcity factor supports values but also means buyers need to be ready to move quickly when the right home hits the market. For current market data, visit the Westchase housing market page.

Find the Right Westchase Realtor

Looking for a realtor who actually knows Westchase? Read why Barrett Henry is the top-rated realtor in Westchase -- 23+ years of experience, 5.0-star Google rating, and deep neighborhood knowledge.

Frequently Asked Questions

What schools serve Westchase?

Westchase is zoned for Hillsborough County Public Schools, with Alonso High School being the primary high school. Alonso is consistently rated among the top public high schools in the Tampa Bay area. Elementary and middle school assignments vary by village, so check the specific address. The school zoning is one of the top reasons families choose Westchase.

Is Westchase walkable?

West Park Village is genuinely walkable with a town center featuring restaurants, shops, and a grocery store. The broader Westchase community has an extensive sidewalk and trail network connecting villages. Compared to most Florida suburbs, Westchase offers significantly above-average walkability, particularly within West Park Village.

Are there HOA fees in Westchase?

Yes. All Westchase homes pay into the Westchase Community Development District (CDD) and most villages have an additional HOA fee. Combined, these typically range from $200-$500/month depending on the village. The fees cover community maintenance, the swim and tennis center, landscaping of common areas, and security patrols.

How far is Westchase from the beach?

Westchase is approximately 20-25 minutes from Clearwater Beach via the Courtney Campbell Causeway. Tampa International Airport is about 15 minutes away. Downtown Tampa is roughly 20 minutes east. The location provides balanced access to beaches, the airport, and the city center.

Best Neighborhoods in Town n Country: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

The best neighborhoods in Town n Country offer affordable west Tampa living from $250K to $500K, with easy access to Tampa International Airport and the Westshore business district.

Top picks: Westshore area ($350K-$500K) for professionals, Town n Country Park ($250K-$380K) for families, Bay Crest Park ($280K-$400K) for quiet suburban living, Rocky Point ($300K-$450K) for waterfront proximity.

Town n Country is one of the Tampa Bay area's best-kept secrets for affordable homeownership west of downtown Tampa. This unincorporated Hillsborough County community sits between Tampa International Airport to the east and the Veterans Expressway to the west, giving residents fast access to jobs, shopping, and the beaches without the price tag that comes with South Tampa or Westchase.

With 23 years selling real estate, I've watched Town n Country evolve from a sleepy suburb into a diverse, well-connected community that draws first-time buyers, investors, and families alike. Homes here typically range from $250K to $500K, and many neighborhoods have no HOA fees, a rarity this close to Tampa's urban core.

Here is a closer look at the neighborhoods worth your attention.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Town n Country?

Westshore Area

Price range: $350K-$500K

The Westshore corridor is Town n Country's most professionally oriented neighborhood. Proximity to the Westshore business district, Tampa's largest employment center outside downtown, makes this area popular with professionals who want a short commute. You will find updated ranch-style homes from the 1960s and 70s alongside newer infill construction. Many properties here have been renovated with modern kitchens, updated owners suites, and screened lanais.

  • Known for: Walkability to Westshore Plaza, International Plaza, and major employers
  • Best for: Working professionals and dual-income households
  • Standout features: Short commute to airport and downtown, restaurant and retail density, no HOA in many sections

Town n Country Park

Price range: $250K-$380K

This is the heart of Town n Country and one of the most affordable neighborhoods this close to Tampa's core. Homes are predominantly concrete block construction from the 1960s through 1980s, sitting on generous lots by Tampa standards. The Town n Country Regional Park anchors the area with ball fields, a community center, and green space that gives the neighborhood a small-town feel.

  • Known for: Affordability, large lots, and established tree canopy
  • Best for: First-time buyers, families on a budget, and investors
  • Standout features: No HOA options, large backyards, proximity to Town n Country Regional Park, access to Hillsborough County magnet schools

Rocky Point

Price range: $300K-$450K

Rocky Point sits along the Courtney Campbell Causeway corridor, offering some of the closest bay views you will find at this price point. The area has seen steady investment as Tampa's waterfront appeal continues to grow. While Rocky Point itself is partly commercial (hotels, restaurants along the causeway), the surrounding residential pockets offer bay breezes and sunset views that punch well above their price range.

  • Known for: Bay proximity, causeway access, waterfront dining
  • Best for: Buyers who want waterfront character without waterfront prices
  • Standout features: Minutes from Clearwater beaches via the causeway, Ben T. Davis Beach access, bay views from select properties

Bay Crest Park

Price range: $280K-$400K

Bay Crest Park is a well-established residential pocket south of Hillsborough Avenue, offering a quieter suburban feel compared to the busier Westshore corridor to the east. Streets are lined with mature oaks and homes sit on comfortable lots. This neighborhood attracts buyers who want the location advantages of Town n Country, airport access, Westshore jobs, Veterans Expressway, without living on a main artery.

  • Known for: Quiet streets, mature landscaping, and solid mid-range values
  • Best for: Families, retirees, and anyone who values a low-key neighborhood atmosphere
  • Standout features: Easy access to both Veterans Expressway and Dale Mabry, no HOA in most sections, well-maintained homes with Florida-friendly landscaping

Town n Country Market Context for 2026

Town n Country remains one of the most competitively priced communities within a 15-minute drive of downtown Tampa. While areas like Westchase and Carrollwood have climbed into the $400K-$600K+ range, Town n Country still delivers solid homes in the $250K-$500K window. Inventory has loosened slightly from the tight pandemic years, giving buyers more options and negotiating room.

The area benefits from ongoing investment in the Westshore district and continued growth around Tampa International Airport. For investors, Town n Country's rental demand stays strong due to the nearby employment base and relatively low entry price compared to surrounding communities.

View current listings in the Town n Country area or browse Town n Country homes for sale.

Find the Right Town 'n' Country Realtor

Looking for a realtor who actually knows Town 'n' Country? Read why Barrett Henry is the top-rated realtor in Town 'n' Country -- 23+ years of experience, 5.0-star Google rating, and deep neighborhood knowledge.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Town n Country a good area to buy a home?

Yes. Town n Country offers some of the most affordable housing within a 15-minute drive of Tampa's Westshore business district and the airport. Many neighborhoods have no HOA, and the area has good access to major highways including the Veterans Expressway and I-275. It is a strong pick for first-time buyers and investors.

What are property taxes like in Town n Country?

As an unincorporated Hillsborough County area, Town n Country residents pay county taxes but no city taxes. This typically results in lower overall property tax bills compared to homes within Tampa city limits, though Hillsborough County's millage rate is still one of the higher rates in Florida.

How far is Town n Country from the beach?

Clearwater Beach is roughly 25-30 minutes via the Courtney Campbell Causeway. Ben T. Davis Beach, a popular local spot on the causeway, is less than 10 minutes from most Town n Country neighborhoods.

Does Town n Country flood?

Some low-lying areas near the bay and along drainage channels do carry flood risk. Always check the FEMA flood zone map for any specific property you are considering. Many homes in Town n Country sit outside high-risk flood zones, but flood insurance is worth discussing with your insurance agent regardless of zone designation.

Best Neighborhoods in Temple Terrace: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Temple Terrace's top neighborhoods include Historic Temple Terrace ($350K-$550K), Temple Crest ($275K-$425K), and Terrace Park ($250K-$400K). This small city within Tampa offers Hillsborough River access, a historic golf course, USF proximity, and prices well below comparable Tampa neighborhoods.

Best for character: Historic Temple Terrace | Best for value: Temple Crest, Terrace Park | Best for river access: Hillsborough River corridor

Temple Terrace is one of Tampa Bay's best-kept secrets. This small incorporated city (population around 26,000) sits between the University of South Florida and the Hillsborough River, offering a unique combination of riverfront living, historic charm, and affordability that is hard to find elsewhere in the Tampa metro.

The city has its own government, police force, and parks system separate from Tampa, which gives it a small-town identity despite being surrounded by the larger city. The Temple Terrace Golf & Country Club, founded in 1921, anchors the historic core. Buyers who discover Temple Terrace often wonder why it is not more widely known. For a broader look, visit the Temple Terrace city page.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Temple Terrace?

Historic Temple Terrace

Price range: $350K-$550K | Best for: History lovers, character-home buyers, golf enthusiasts

Historic Temple Terrace is the original heart of the city, developed in the 1920s as a Mediterranean Revival golf course community. The neighborhood features winding streets, mature oak and citrus trees, and homes with architectural details you will not find in modern construction. Many homes have been lovingly restored while others present renovation opportunities.

The Temple Terrace Golf & Country Club sits at the center, offering golf, tennis, swimming, and dining. Homes along the Hillsborough River in this section offer private river access for kayaking and canoeing. The historic district has its own preservation guidelines that protect the neighborhood's character.

  • 1920s Mediterranean Revival architecture
  • Temple Terrace Golf & Country Club access
  • Hillsborough River frontage on select homes
  • Historic preservation protections maintain character

Temple Crest

Price range: $275K-$425K | Best for: First-time buyers, young families, USF employees

Temple Crest is a residential neighborhood on the eastern side of Temple Terrace, offering solid mid-century homes at prices that make it one of the best values in the Tampa metro. Homes here were built primarily in the 1960s through 1980s, featuring concrete block construction, mature landscaping, and generous lot sizes compared to newer communities.

The neighborhood's proximity to USF makes it popular with university faculty and staff. Riverhills Park provides a neighborhood gathering spot with a playground and open space. This is a practical, no-frills neighborhood that delivers square footage and location at an accessible price.

  • Affordable entry to the Temple Terrace market
  • Close proximity to USF campus
  • Solid concrete block construction
  • Generous lot sizes with mature landscaping

Terrace Park

Price range: $250K-$400K | Best for: Budget buyers, investors, renovation seekers

Terrace Park covers the southern section of Temple Terrace, offering the most affordable homes in the city. The neighborhood includes a mix of single-family homes and some townhome or condo options. Prices here represent strong value relative to the location, which is minutes from I-75, I-4, and the USF area.

Some homes in Terrace Park need updating, which creates opportunity for buyers willing to renovate. The area has seen gradual improvement as the broader Temple Terrace market has gained recognition. For investors, rental demand from USF students and hospital workers at nearby Moffitt Cancer Center and AdventHealth provides a reliable tenant pool.

  • Most affordable homes in Temple Terrace
  • Strong rental demand from USF and hospital workers
  • Minutes from I-75 and I-4 interchange
  • Renovation opportunities at entry-level prices

Along the Hillsborough River

Price range: $400K-$550K+ | Best for: Nature lovers, kayakers, privacy seekers

Homes along the Hillsborough River corridor in Temple Terrace offer a lifestyle that feels worlds away from suburban Florida. The river is navigable by kayak and canoe, and the tree canopy along its banks creates a shaded, natural environment. Riverfront lots in Temple Terrace are significantly more affordable than comparable waterfront properties in other Tampa neighborhoods.

Properties vary from historic homes with long river frontage to more modest homes that back up to the river. Lettuce Lake Park and Riverhills Park provide public river access and nature trails. The combination of river living, wildlife viewing, and a 15-minute drive to downtown Tampa is genuinely unique.

  • Hillsborough River frontage at below-market waterfront prices
  • Kayaking, canoeing, and wildlife viewing
  • Mature tree canopy and natural setting
  • Lettuce Lake Park and Riverhills Park nearby

Temple Terrace Real Estate Market Context for 2026

Temple Terrace remains undervalued relative to comparable Tampa neighborhoods in 2026. The city's median home price sits well below the Tampa metro average, yet it offers amenities, river access, and a historic core that many pricier areas lack. The USF area continues to drive demand from academic professionals and medical workers at nearby hospitals.

The city has invested in infrastructure improvements and streetscaping along its main corridors, signaling continued revitalization. Buyers who get in now are likely to see solid appreciation as more people discover what Temple Terrace offers. Inventory is moderate, with the best deals typically found in Temple Crest and Terrace Park. For current numbers, visit the Temple Terrace housing market page.

Find the Right Temple Terrace Realtor

Looking for a realtor who actually knows Temple Terrace? Read why Barrett Henry is the top-rated realtor in Temple Terrace -- 23+ years of experience, 5.0-star Google rating, and deep neighborhood knowledge.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Temple Terrace part of Tampa?

No. Temple Terrace is its own incorporated city with its own mayor, city council, police department, and parks system. It is completely surrounded by the City of Tampa and uses Hillsborough County services for schools and some utilities, but it maintains independent governance. This distinction gives it a small-town feel within the metro area.

What is the Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club?

The Temple Terrace Golf & Country Club was founded in 1921 and is one of the oldest golf courses in the Tampa Bay area. The club offers golf, tennis, swimming, and dining. Membership is available to area residents. The course is the centerpiece of the Historic Temple Terrace neighborhood.

How close is Temple Terrace to USF?

Temple Terrace borders the University of South Florida campus. Some parts of Temple Terrace are a 5-minute drive or bike ride to USF. This proximity makes it popular with faculty, staff, graduate students, and employees at the adjacent Moffitt Cancer Center and AdventHealth Tampa hospital.

Is Temple Terrace safe?

Temple Terrace has its own police department and generally reports lower crime rates than surrounding unincorporated areas. The Historic Temple Terrace section and river-adjacent neighborhoods are particularly quiet. As with any area, conditions vary by street, so drive the specific neighborhood at different times of day before buying.

Best Neighborhoods in Sun City Center: Where to Live in 2026

QUICK ANSWER

Sun City Center's top neighborhoods include Kings Point ($180K-$350K), Sun City Center proper ($200K-$400K), and Renaissance ($250K-$500K). This premier 55+ community offers a golf cart lifestyle, 200+ clubs, and some of the most affordable active-adult living in Florida.

Best for budget: Kings Point condos | Best for single-family: SCC proper | Best for newer construction: Renaissance

Sun City Center is one of Florida's largest and most established 55+ communities, home to over 20,000 residents. Located about 30 minutes south of Tampa off I-75, this community runs on golf carts. Residents drive them to the grocery store, restaurants, medical offices, and the community's extensive recreation facilities. It is a self-contained lifestyle that appeals to active retirees who want amenities, social connection, and affordability.

I work with buyers relocating to Sun City Center from across the country, and the most common reaction on their first visit is surprise at how much is here. Multiple golf courses, hundreds of clubs and activities, a performing arts theater, fitness centers, and indoor pools. All at prices that make coastal Florida retirement communities look expensive. For more on the area, visit the Sun City Center city page.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Sun City Center?

Kings Point

Price range: $180K-$350K | Best for: Budget-conscious retirees, snowbirds, condo buyers

Kings Point is a gated 55+ community within Sun City Center, offering some of the most affordable retirement housing in the Tampa Bay area. The community features condos, villas, and single-family homes. Kings Point has its own clubhouse, pools, fitness center, and a full calendar of social events separate from the main Sun City Center amenities.

Condos in Kings Point start as low as $180K for updated 2-bedroom units, making this one of the most accessible entry points into the Sun City Center lifestyle. The gated access, maintained grounds, and included amenities provide a secure, low-maintenance living experience. Monthly HOA fees cover exterior maintenance, lawn care, and community facilities.

  • Most affordable entry to Sun City Center lifestyle
  • Gated with its own clubhouse and pools
  • Condos, villas, and single-family options
  • HOA covers exterior maintenance and lawn care

Sun City Center Proper

Price range: $200K-$400K | Best for: Active retirees, golfers, social butterflies

The main Sun City Center community offers single-family homes, duplexes, and some condos across a sprawling campus of neighborhoods. Residents have access to multiple golf courses, the Community Association's fitness and recreation facilities, indoor and outdoor pools, woodworking shops, art studios, and over 200 clubs and organizations.

Homes range from 1,200 to over 2,500 square feet. Many feature updated kitchens, enclosed lanais, and golf cart garages. The community is deed-restricted to 55+ (at least one resident must be 55 or older). Annual Community Association fees provide access to all recreational facilities and common areas.

  • Access to multiple golf courses
  • 200+ clubs and organizations
  • Indoor and outdoor pools, fitness centers
  • Golf cart lifestyle throughout the community

Freedom Plaza

Price range: $250K-$450K (entrance fees vary) | Best for: Seniors wanting continuing care, peace of mind

Freedom Plaza is a continuing care retirement community (CCRC) within Sun City Center that offers independent living, assisted living, and skilled nursing all on one campus. Residents typically pay an entrance fee plus monthly fees that cover housing, dining, housekeeping, and access to higher levels of care if needed.

This is the option for buyers who want the security of knowing their care needs are covered as they age. The campus includes restaurants, a fitness center, swimming pool, and a full activities calendar. Freedom Plaza appeals to retirees who want a single move that covers them through all stages of retirement.

  • Continuing care with independent, assisted, and skilled nursing
  • On-campus dining, fitness, and activities
  • Peace of mind with guaranteed care access
  • Located within the Sun City Center community

Renaissance

Price range: $250K-$500K | Best for: Buyers wanting newer construction, upgraded finishes

Renaissance is a newer section of Sun City Center featuring homes built in the 2010s and later. These homes offer modern floor plans, impact-resistant windows, updated building codes, and contemporary finishes that older SCC homes may lack. The community has its own amenities including a clubhouse and pool.

This is the choice for buyers who want the Sun City Center lifestyle and social infrastructure but prefer a newer home without the renovation projects that come with 1970s-1990s construction. Prices are higher than the older sections, but you get move-in-ready condition with modern energy efficiency.

  • Newest construction in the Sun City Center area
  • Modern floor plans with impact windows
  • Move-in ready with contemporary finishes
  • Own clubhouse and pool amenities

Aston Gardens Area

Price range: Rental and buy-in options vary | Best for: Seniors wanting luxury independent living with services

The Aston Gardens area near Sun City Center offers luxury senior living with services like dining, housekeeping, transportation, and planned activities included. While not a traditional home purchase, it represents an important option in the Sun City Center ecosystem for seniors who want a full-service living experience.

The surrounding area also includes several independent senior communities and newer developments that benefit from proximity to Sun City Center's commercial infrastructure, including the medical offices, shopping, and restaurants along SR-674.

  • Full-service luxury senior living
  • Dining, housekeeping, and transportation included
  • Proximity to SCC medical and retail infrastructure
  • Social programming and planned activities

Sun City Center Real Estate Market Context for 2026

Sun City Center's market in 2026 continues to attract retirees from the Northeast, Midwest, and other high-cost states seeking affordable Florida living. The community's all-inclusive amenity model at relatively low annual fees remains a strong value proposition. Median prices in SCC are well below the Tampa Bay metro average, which is a key draw for fixed-income buyers.

The 55+ age restriction limits the buyer pool but also maintains the community's character and keeps demand stable among its target demographic. Properties in Kings Point and the older sections of SCC proper may need roof or HVAC updates. Newer sections like Renaissance trade at a premium but require less immediate maintenance. For current market data, visit the Sun City Center housing market page.

Looking for a realtor who actually knows Sun City Center? Read why Barrett Henry is the top-rated realtor in Sun City Center -- 23+ years of experience, 5.0-star Google rating, and deep neighborhood knowledge.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the age requirement for Sun City Center?

Sun City Center is a 55+ deed-restricted community. At least one person in each household must be 55 or older. There are no children under 16 permitted as permanent residents. The age restriction is enforced through the Community Association and deed covenants.

Can you use golf carts in Sun City Center?

Yes. Golf carts are a primary mode of transportation in Sun City Center. The community has designated golf cart paths and most commercial areas along SR-674 are golf cart accessible. Many homes include golf cart garages. This is one of the defining lifestyle features of the community.

How much are HOA fees in Sun City Center?

Fees vary by neighborhood. Kings Point condos include exterior maintenance and lawn care in their HOA fees, which typically run $300-$600/month. Sun City Center proper charges an annual Community Association fee (typically $400-$600/year) that covers access to recreation facilities. Individual HOA fees for specific neighborhoods are additional.

Is Sun City Center a good investment?

Sun City Center offers strong value for owner-occupants seeking an affordable retirement lifestyle. Appreciation has been steady but typically trails the broader Tampa Bay market due to the 55+ restriction and age of many homes. The best investment play here is buying in newer sections like Renaissance that attract a wider range of 55+ buyers at resale. Contact Barrett for specific investment analysis.
