Diamond Hill sits in the sweet spot for families who want strong schools, reasonable lot sizes, and minimal monthly fees.

Who Is Diamond Hill Best For?

After years of selling homes in this area, I can tell you exactly which buyers tend to be the best fit for Diamond Hill:

Families with School-Age Children

This is Diamond Hill's primary audience. The strong school zones, family-friendly atmosphere, and spacious lots make it an ideal landing spot for families who prioritize education and outdoor space. You're getting the Valrico school advantage without the premium pricing of FishHawk or the heavy fees of newer developments.

First-Time Home Buyers Looking for Value

If you're a first-time home buyer in the Brandon/Valrico area, Diamond Hill offers a path into an established Valrico neighborhood at a more accessible price point than many alternatives. The lower entry price combined with minimal monthly fees means your total housing cost stays manageable - and you're not sacrificing school quality or neighborhood safety to get there.

Buyers Who Want Lower Monthly Fees

Diamond Hill has both an HOA and a CDD, but the combined costs are lower than what you'll find in newer master-planned communities. When you compare Diamond Hill's total fees against $300-$500/month in combined HOA and CDD at places like FishHawk, the savings add up significantly over a 30-year mortgage.

Move-Up Buyers from Brandon or Riverview

Many of my Diamond Hill buyers are families who started in Brandon or Riverview and are ready to upgrade - whether that means more space, better schools, or a quieter neighborhood. Diamond Hill delivers the upgrade without a dramatic jump in price or monthly costs.

Retirees and Empty Nesters

Diamond Hill isn't exclusively for families. The low monthly fees, manageable home sizes, and established neighborhood character also appeal to retirees and empty nesters who want a well-maintained home in a safe, quiet community without the overhead of a master-planned community's amenity fees.

Frequently Asked Questions About Diamond Hill Valrico FL

Is Diamond Hill Valrico a good neighborhood?

Yes. Diamond Hill is a well-established residential neighborhood in Valrico, FL with strong school zoning, generous lot sizes, mature landscaping, and a quiet family-friendly atmosphere. It offers lower total monthly carrying costs than most newer subdivisions in the area thanks to minimal HOA fees and a CDD with maturing bonds. The neighborhood is popular with families who want access to top-rated Hillsborough County schools, including the possibility of the Newsome High School zone, without paying the premium prices and monthly fees associated with communities like FishHawk Ranch. For buyers who value space, established character, and affordability, Diamond Hill consistently checks the right boxes.

What school zone is Diamond Hill Valrico in?

Diamond Hill is part of the Hillsborough County School District. Depending on the specific address within the neighborhood, homes may be zoned for Bloomingdale High School or Newsome High School - both are strong public high schools. Middle school assignments include Randall Middle School and Burns Middle School, and elementary assignments include several well-regarded Valrico-area elementary schools. School zones in Hillsborough County are determined by exact home address, so I always verify the specific school assignment for every property my clients consider. This is especially important in Valrico, where school zone boundaries can vary within the same neighborhood.

What are homes like in Diamond Hill Valrico FL?

Homes in Diamond Hill are predominantly single-family residences built from the late 1980s through the early 2000s. Most are concrete block construction with stucco exteriors, tile or shingle roofs, and 2-car garages. Floor plans typically range from 1,400 to 2,800 square feet with 3 to 5 bedrooms. You'll find a mix of single-story and two-story homes. Interior features vary widely based on whether the home has been updated - renovated homes may feature modern kitchens, updated bathrooms, and new flooring, while original-condition homes may need cosmetic or functional updates. Lots range from about a quarter-acre to over a half-acre, giving homeowners meaningful outdoor space.

Does Diamond Hill have an HOA?

Diamond Hill does have a homeowners association, but the fees are minimal compared to most newer communities in the area. HOA assessments are generally in the range of $100 to $300 per year - not per month. The HOA covers basic community standards, deed restriction enforcement, and common area maintenance. There are no resort-style amenities bundled into the fee. Diamond Hill does have a CDD (Community Development District), but the assessments are lower than what you'll find in newer subdivisions in the Valrico, Riverview, and Lithia areas where combined HOA and CDD fees can reach $250 to $500 per month.

How much do homes cost in Diamond Hill Valrico?

Home prices in Diamond Hill generally range from the low $300s to the mid-$500s, depending on square footage, lot size, number of bedrooms, and the extent of updates and renovations. A typical 3-bedroom/2-bathroom home in the 1,400-1,800 square foot range might sell in the $310,000-$375,000 range, while larger 4-5 bedroom homes with 2,200+ square feet and modern updates can reach $475,000-$550,000. Updated homes with newer roofs, modern kitchens, and contemporary flooring command the highest prices. For the most current pricing in Diamond Hill, contact me directly at (813) 733-7907.

Is Diamond Hill in a flood zone?

Most of Diamond Hill sits on higher ground and is not within a FEMA-designated Special Flood Hazard Area. However, specific parcels near any low-lying areas or drainage features may have different flood zone designations. Flood zone status is determined on a property-by-property basis, and I always verify the flood zone designation for my clients before they make an offer. Even if a property is outside a flood zone, you may still want to consider flood insurance - Florida weather can surprise you. For more on flood considerations in this area, check out the Hillsborough County flood zone maps or ask me for a property-specific assessment.

How far is Diamond Hill from downtown Tampa?

Diamond Hill is approximately 18-22 miles east of downtown Tampa. During off-peak hours, you can expect a drive time of roughly 25-35 minutes. During rush hour (7-9 AM and 4-6:30 PM), that extends to 40-55 minutes depending on traffic conditions. The Selmon Expressway (toll road) is the most efficient route and can save you 10-15 minutes compared to surface streets during peak times. Tampa International Airport is roughly 35-45 minutes from Diamond Hill. If you work in the Westshore business district or at MacDill Air Force Base, the Selmon is your best friend for the daily commute.

Is Diamond Hill Valrico safe?

Diamond Hill is located in an area of Valrico that is generally considered safe and family-friendly. The neighborhood falls under the jurisdiction of the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, and the Valrico ZIP code (33594) consistently reports crime rates below the Hillsborough County average. Diamond Hill is a quiet, residential neighborhood with low through-traffic, which contributes to its safe, family-oriented atmosphere. As with any home purchase, I recommend checking the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office crime mapping tool for the most current data specific to any address you're considering. For more information on safety in the broader area, read my guide on whether Brandon FL is safe.

Ready to See Homes in Diamond Hill Valrico FL?

If Diamond Hill sounds like the right fit for your family, I'd love to help you take the next step. Whether you're ready to schedule showings, need to sell your current home first, or just want to ask a few more questions about the neighborhood, I'm here to help - with the same honest, no-pressure approach you've been reading in this guide.

I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've been helping buyers and sellers throughout Valrico, Brandon, Lithia, and the greater Tampa Bay area. I know this market, I know these neighborhoods, and I'll give you the straight answers you need to make a confident decision.

Here's how to reach me:

  • Phone/Text: (813) 733-7907
  • Email: barrett@nowtb.com
  • Website: nowtb.com

No pressure, no obligation - just honest answers about Diamond Hill and the Valrico real estate market from someone who knows this area better than anyone. Let's find the home that fits your family.

title: Living in Valrico FL: The Complete Guide to Schools, Neighborhoods & Lifestyle
excerpt: Thinking about moving to Valrico FL? Get the full guide to schools, neighborhoods, cost of living, and why families love this Tampa Bay suburb.
content:
Quick Answer

What is it like living in Valrico FL?

Valrico FL offers top-rated Hillsborough County schools, a semi-rural atmosphere, and median home prices around $350K-$425K - making it one of Tampa Bay's most desirable family-friendly suburbs. Valrico is just 20 minutes east of Tampa with excellent dining and parks. Compare in our Brandon vs Riverview vs Valrico guide, explore Diamond Hill, and search Valrico homes for sale.

What's in This Guide ▼
  1. Where Exactly Is Valrico FL?
  2. What Makes Valrico Different from Brandon?
  3. What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Valrico FL?
  4. How Much Do Homes Cost in Valrico FL?
  5. What Are the Schools Like in Valrico FL?
  6. What Is the Lifestyle Like in Valrico FL?
  7. What About Dining, Shopping, and Everyday Conveniences?
  8. What Is the Commute Like from Valrico FL?
  9. How Does Valrico Compare to Brandon, FishHawk, and Lithia?
  10. What Are the Pros and Cons of Living in Valrico FL?
  11. Frequently Asked Questions About Living in Valrico FL
  12. Ready to Explore Homes in Valrico FL?

Living in Valrico FL means settling into one of the most sought-after suburban pockets in the Tampa Bay area - an unincorporated community in eastern Hillsborough County known for larger homesites, top-rated schools (including the highly coveted Newsome High School zone), a quieter semi-rural atmosphere, and home prices that reflect the premium quality of life here. Valrico sits just east of Brandon along the SR-60 corridor, bordering Lithia and the FishHawk Ranch area, and offers something you won't easily find closer to Tampa: space, privacy, and elbow room without sacrificing access to shopping, dining, and major highways. I sell homes in Valrico regularly, and the buyers who land here tend to stay - it's the kind of place where families put down roots and don't look back.

In this guide, I'll cover everything you need to know about living in Valrico, Florida - from neighborhoods and home prices to schools, commute times, lifestyle, and the honest pros and cons. Whether you're relocating from out of state or comparing Valrico to nearby communities like Brandon and Riverview, this breakdown will give you the full picture.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Homes

Where Exactly Is Valrico FL?

Valrico is an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County, which means it's not a city with its own government - it falls under the jurisdiction of Hillsborough County and the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. Geographically, Valrico sits directly east of Brandon along State Road 60 (Brandon Boulevard) and extends south toward Lithia and the FishHawk Ranch area.

Here's how Valrico relates to its neighbors:

  • West: Brandon proper - the more commercial, densely developed suburb with malls, restaurants, and a more urban feel
  • South/Southeast: Lithia and FishHawk Ranch - the master-planned community with resort-style amenities
  • East: Plant City - Florida's strawberry capital, about 15 minutes further east on SR-60
  • North: Thonotosassa and the I-4 corridor

Valrico's primary ZIP codes are 33594 and 33596, though some Valrico addresses also carry 33547 (Lithia). The area is roughly 15-20 miles east of downtown Tampa and sits at the crossroads of SR-60, Lithia Pinecrest Road, Bloomingdale Avenue, and Buckhorn Road - all corridors that connect you to the rest of the Tampa Bay metro.

What Makes Valrico Different from Brandon?

This is the question I get from almost every buyer who starts their search in Brandon and then discovers Valrico. On paper, they're neighbors. In practice, they feel like different worlds. Here's how they actually compare in day-to-day living:

Lot Sizes and Space

Brandon proper is a mature suburb with typical subdivision lots - most homes sit on a quarter-acre or less. Valrico is where you start finding half-acre, one-acre, and even multi-acre properties. If you want a big backyard, room for a pool and a detached workshop, or the ability to keep horses, Valrico delivers options that Brandon simply doesn't have.

Feel and Atmosphere

Brandon feels suburban - strip malls, traffic on SR-60, chain restaurants, busy intersections. Valrico feels more like a small town transitioning from rural roots. You'll see horse farms, oak-lined roads, produce stands, and properties with no HOA and no neighbors peering into your windows. Clients love the Valrico vibe because it feels like you're out in the country, but you're still 10 minutes from a Publix and 20 minutes from a Target.

Schools

This is Valrico's trump card. A significant portion of Valrico falls within the Newsome High School attendance zone, which is consistently rated one of the top public high schools in Hillsborough County. Brandon has strong schools too (Bloomingdale High, for example), but the Newsome zone is the single biggest reason many families specifically target Valrico. More on schools in a dedicated section below.

Home Prices

Valrico generally trends higher than Brandon proper because of the larger lots, the Newsome school zone, and the overall desirability of the area. You're looking at a median home price in the $400,000-$475,000 range in Valrico compared to $300,000-$370,000 in central Brandon. That said, Valrico offers a wide range - you can still find homes in the mid-$300s, and custom estate properties on acreage can exceed $800K. For a broader cost comparison, check out my cost of living guide for the Brandon area.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Valrico FL?

Valrico isn't one large master-planned community - it's a collection of subdivisions, established neighborhoods, and pockets of acreage properties. Here are the main areas I steer buyers toward, depending on what they're looking for. For more detail on any of these, see my guide to the best neighborhoods in the greater Brandon area.

Bloomingdale

Bloomingdale stretches along Bloomingdale Avenue and technically straddles the Brandon-Valrico border. It's one of the most established master-planned communities in the area, with mature trees, community pools, and excellent schools. Homes here range from $350,000 to $550,000 and typically sit on lots of a quarter-acre to a third-acre. Bloomingdale offers a great middle ground between Brandon's convenience and Valrico's quality of life - you get strong schools and community infrastructure without the CDD fees that come with newer developments.

FishHawk Ranch (Lithia/Valrico Border)

FishHawk Ranch technically carries a Lithia mailing address, but it borders Valrico directly and shares many of the same school zones. This master-planned community is the premium option in the area - expect $400,000 to $750,000+ for homes with resort-style amenities, 40+ miles of trails, and all A-rated schools including Newsome High. The trade-off is higher monthly carrying costs: combined HOA and CDD fees typically run $250-$500 per month. If you're interested in new construction in the area, my new construction guide covers the latest developments.

Buckhorn Area

The Buckhorn Road corridor running through Valrico offers a mix of newer subdivisions and older homes on larger lots. This area feeds into some of the best school zones in the county, and you can find homes from the mid-$300s to the mid-$500s. The Buckhorn area is popular with families who want newer construction without the premium price tag of FishHawk, and several subdivisions here were built in the 2010s with modern floor plans and impact-rated windows.

Lithia Pinecrest / Valrico Corridor

This is the stretch along Lithia Pinecrest Road between SR-60 and the Lithia area. It's where you'll find some of the most desirable acreage properties in Valrico - homes on one to five acres with no HOA, room for horses, and that true semi-rural Florida lifestyle. Prices here vary widely based on lot size and home condition, ranging from $375,000 for a modest home on an acre to well over $700,000 for updated properties on multiple acres. Many of these are custom-built homes, so you'll see a lot of variety in architectural style.

SR-60 / Valrico Proper

The area directly along and just off State Road 60 in Valrico includes a mix of older established homes from the 1970s-1990s and some newer infill construction. This is where you'll find Valrico's most affordable options - homes in the $300,000-$400,000 range - while still being in the Valrico ZIP code and benefiting from the area's school zones. Lots are typically a quarter-acre to a half-acre, and many properties here have no HOA.

How Much Do Homes Cost in Valrico FL?

Home prices in Valrico reflect the area's quality schools, larger lot sizes, and overall desirability. Here's a breakdown by area so you can see where different budgets land. Prices reflect typical single-family home sales as of early 2026 - call me at (813) 733-7907 for the most current numbers, as inventory moves quickly in this market.

Note: Prices based on Stellar MLS data and Hillsborough County Property Appraiser records. Individual home prices vary based on condition, updates, and specific location. For homes with CDD fees, review my Florida Homestead Exemption guide to understand how to reduce your annual property tax burden.

What Are the Schools Like in Valrico FL?

Schools are the number-one reason families choose Valrico over other Tampa Bay suburbs. Period. I cannot overstate how much the school zoning drives demand in this area. Here's the full picture.

Newsome High School - The Selling Point

Newsome High School is consistently rated among the top public high schools in Hillsborough County, earning an A rating from the Florida Department of Education. It offers strong AP and honors programs, competitive athletics, and active extracurricular clubs. The Newsome zone is THE reason many families specifically target Valrico and the Lithia/FishHawk corridor. When a home is listed in the Newsome zone, it sells faster and commands a premium - that's just the reality of this market. For a deeper dive into area schools, check out my guide to the best schools in the Brandon/Valrico area.

Top Middle Schools

Randall Middle School feeds into Newsome High and carries a strong reputation among Valrico families. Barrington Middle School is another A-rated option that primarily serves the FishHawk Ranch area. Burns Middle School serves parts of the Bloomingdale corridor and also earns consistently high marks.

Top Elementary Schools

Valrico is served by several strong elementary schools, including:

  • Alafia Elementary - A-rated, serves parts of Bloomingdale and Valrico
  • FishHawk Creek Elementary - A-rated, serves FishHawk Ranch and surrounding areas
  • Buckhorn Elementary - Serves the Buckhorn Road corridor
  • Valrico Elementary - Serves Valrico proper along the SR-60 corridor
  • Stowers Elementary - Serves parts of the Lithia Pinecrest corridor

Important: School zones are tied to your specific home address, not your ZIP code or neighborhood name. I always verify the exact school zone for my clients before they make an offer - it's one of the most critical steps in the buying process in this area. Hillsborough County provides an online school zone locator tool, and I recommend double-checking directly with the school district.

What Is the Lifestyle Like in Valrico FL?

Valrico's lifestyle is what I'd describe as suburban with a semi-rural edge. It's not the manicured, master-planned uniformity of a FishHawk Ranch (although FishHawk is right next door if that's your preference). Valrico has more character, more variety, and more breathing room. Here's what daily life actually looks like:

Space and Privacy

This is Valrico's defining characteristic. You can actually have a meaningful backyard here. Families with kids, dogs, or just a desire for outdoor space gravitate to Valrico because the lot sizes are genuinely larger than what you'll find in Brandon or Riverview. If you want acreage - a full acre, two acres, five acres - Valrico and the adjacent Lithia corridor are where you look.

Equestrian and Agricultural Properties

Valrico and Lithia are two of the few areas in the Tampa Bay metro where you can realistically own horses or have a small hobby farm while still being within a reasonable commute of Tampa. Equestrian properties on three to ten acres are available in the $500K-$1M+ range, and the agricultural zoning in parts of unincorporated Hillsborough County supports this lifestyle. You'll see horse trailers, feed stores, and riding trails mixed in with newer subdivisions - that's the Valrico character.

Outdoor Recreation

Living in Valrico puts you close to some of the best outdoor recreation in Hillsborough County. Alafia River State Park is a favorite for mountain biking, hiking, and horseback riding. Lithia Springs Park offers natural spring swimming and is packed on weekends. Alderman's Ford Conservation Park provides trails along the Alafia River. FishHawk Ranch's 40+ miles of multi-use trails are also accessible to surrounding neighborhoods.

Community Pace

Valrico moves at a slower pace than Brandon. There's no mall, no major commercial strip (that's all in Brandon, minutes away). People know their neighbors. Kids ride bikes in the street. It's the kind of community where you'll see a bald eagle overhead and a gopher tortoise in your yard. If you're moving from a dense urban area, the transition to Valrico's pace feels like exhaling for the first time.

What About Dining, Shopping, and Everyday Conveniences?

This is where I give you the honest assessment: Valrico itself is not a dining and shopping destination. But Brandon is right next door, and that's the key. You're never more than 10-15 minutes from everything you need.

Grocery and Everyday Shopping

  • Publix - Multiple locations along SR-60 and Bloomingdale Avenue, all within 5-10 minutes of most Valrico homes
  • Walmart Supercenter - Located on SR-60 at the Brandon/Valrico border
  • Wi -Dixie and ALDI - Additional grocery options along the SR-60 corridor
  • Westfield Brandon Mall - Full-service shopping mall about 10-15 minutes west on SR-60
  • Brandon Town Center area - Big-box retailers including Target, Home Depot, Lowe's, Best Buy, and more

Dining

Valrico has a handful of local restaurants and fast-casual spots, but the bulk of dining options are concentrated along Brandon's SR-60 corridor. You'll find everything from national chains to local favorites within a 10-minute drive. The FishHawk area has also developed its own small restaurant scene along FishHawk Boulevard. For the best local spots, check my area comparison guide which includes dining highlights for each community.

Healthcare

Brandon Regional Hospital is approximately 10-15 minutes from most Valrico addresses. Multiple urgent care centers, pediatric offices, and dental practices are scattered along the SR-60 and Bloomingdale corridors. For specialized medical care, Tampa General Hospital and the USF Health campus are about 25-35 minutes away.

What Is the Commute Like from Valrico FL?

Commute times are one of the most common questions I get from buyers considering Valrico, especially those who work in downtown Tampa, MacDill Air Force Base, or the Westshore business district. Here's the realistic picture:

The Selmon Expressway (toll road) is your best friend for commuting from Valrico to Tampa. It bypasses the worst of the surface-street congestion and can shave 10-15 minutes off a downtown commute during rush hour. The toll runs roughly $3-$5 each way depending on your entry and exit points. Most commuters I work with use a Su Pass for automatic toll payments.

If you work remotely - and many of my Valrico buyers do - the commute conversation is less relevant. But even for remote workers, knowing you can reach Tampa International Airport in about 35-45 minutes is important for business travel.

How Does Valrico Compare to Brandon, FishHawk, and Lithia?

Buyers in this part of Hillsborough County almost always compare these four communities before deciding. Here's how they stack up across the factors that matter most. For an even more detailed side-by-side, read my Brandon vs. Riverview vs. Valrico comparison.

The bottom line: Valrico sits in the sweet spot between Brandon's convenience and Lithia's full rural experience. If FishHawk's amenities appeal to you but the HOA/CDD fees don't, Valrico gives you a strong alternative with better lot sizes and lower monthly costs.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Living in Valrico FL?

I believe in giving you the complete picture - not just the highlights. Here's my honest assessment after years of selling homes in Valrico:

Pros

  • ✅ Top school zones - Newsome High School and strong feeder schools are a major draw
  • ✅ Larger lot sizes - Half-acre to multi-acre properties are common, giving you space you won't find closer to Tampa
  • ✅ Lower monthly costs - Many Valrico homes have no HOA and no CDD, keeping your monthly carrying costs down
  • ✅ Semi-rural atmosphere - Quiet streets, mature oak trees, and a slower pace of life
  • ✅ Proximity to Brandon - All of Brandon's shopping, dining, and services are 10-15 minutes away
  • ✅ Equestrian and acreage options - One of the few Tampa Bay areas where you can keep horses and still commute to work
  • ✅ Strong home values - Valrico properties hold their value well due to consistent demand, especially in the Newsome zone
  • ✅ No state income tax - Florida's tax advantage applies to every resident

Cons

  • ❌ Limited walkability - Valrico is car-dependent; there's no downtown, no walkable village center
  • ❌ Longer commute to Tampa - Expect 30-55 minutes to downtown Tampa depending on traffic and your specific location
  • ❌ Limited local dining and nightlife - You'll need to drive to Brandon or Tampa for restaurant variety and entertainment
  • ❌ Higher home prices than Brandon - The school zones and lot sizes come at a premium over Brandon proper
  • ❌ Older housing stock in some areas - Parts of Valrico have homes from the 1970s-1990s that may need significant updates (roof, HVAC, electrical)
  • ❌ Limited public transit - HART bus service is minimal in Valrico; you need a car
  • ❌ Florida heat and humidity - Summers are hot (June through September averages in the 90s), and afternoon thunderstorms are a daily occurrence
  • ❌ Flood zone considerations - Some properties near the Alafia River may fall in flood zones; always check before buying

Frequently Asked Questions About Living in Valrico FL

Is Valrico FL a good place to live?

Yes. Valrico consistently ranks as one of the most desirable communities in the Tampa Bay area for families, offering top-rated schools (especially the Newsome High School zone), larger lot sizes than neighboring Brandon, a quieter semi-rural atmosphere, and strong home values. It's particularly well-suited for families who want space and excellent public schools without moving deep into rural Hillsborough County. The main trade-offs are a longer commute to Tampa and limited local shopping and dining compared to Brandon.

What is the average home price in Valrico FL?

The median home price in Valrico ranges from approximately $400,000 to $475,000 for single-family homes, though prices vary significantly by neighborhood and lot size. Homes in the Bloomingdale and Buckhorn areas start in the mid-$300s, while acreage properties along the Lithia Pinecrest corridor and custom estate homes can exceed $700,000 to $1 million. Valrico generally trends 15-25% higher than central Brandon due to larger lot sizes and the Newsome High School zone premium.

What school district is Valrico FL in?

Valrico is part of the Hillsborough County School District, one of the largest school districts in the United States. The most notable school serving Valrico is Newsome High School, which is consistently A-rated by the Florida Department of Education. Feeder schools include Randall Middle School, Barrington Middle School, and several A-rated elementary schools. School zones are determined by your specific home address, so it's essential to verify the zone before purchasing. I confirm school zoning for every client I work with in this area.

How far is Valrico from Tampa?

Valrico is approximately 18-22 miles east of downtown Tampa. In practical terms, that means a 25-30 minute drive during off-peak hours and 40-55 minutes during rush hour. The Selmon Expressway (toll road) is the most efficient route for commuting to downtown Tampa, the Westshore business district, or MacDill Air Force Base. Tampa International Airport is roughly 35-45 minutes from most Valrico addresses.

Is Valrico FL safe?

Valrico is generally considered a safe community. It falls under the jurisdiction of the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, and the Valrico ZIP codes (33594 and 33596) consistently report crime rates below the Hillsborough County average. Master-planned communities like Bloomingdale and FishHawk Ranch (on the Valrico border) have particularly low crime rates. As with any area, safety varies by specific neighborhood, and I always recommend checking the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office crime mapping tool for the most current data on any address you're considering.

Does Valrico FL flood?

Most of Valrico sits on higher ground and is not in a FEMA-designated flood zone. However, properties near the Alafia River and certain low-lying areas may fall within flood zones and require flood insurance. This is something I check for every client before they make an offer. Newer subdivisions in the area are typically engineered with modern stormwater management systems that mitigate flooding risk. If flood zones are a concern, read my guide on what to know before buying in this area.

What is there to do in Valrico FL?

Valrico's recreation leans heavily toward outdoor activities. Alafia River State Park offers mountain biking, hiking, and horseback riding trails. Lithia Springs Park is a popular spot for swimming in natural spring water. Alderman's Ford Conservation Park provides scenic trails along the Alafia River. FishHawk Ranch's trail system is accessible for walking and biking. For shopping, dining, entertainment, and nightlife, Brandon's SR-60 corridor is 10-15 minutes away, and downtown Tampa's Riverwalk, Sparkman Wharf, and Ybor City are within a 30-40 minute drive.

Is Valrico better than Brandon?

It depends on your priorities. Valrico is better for families who prioritize top school zones (especially Newsome High), larger lot sizes, a quieter atmosphere, and lower monthly carrying costs (no HOA/CDD in many areas). Brandon is better for buyers who want a shorter commute to Tampa, walkable access to shopping and dining, lower home prices, and more housing inventory to choose from. Many of my clients start searching in Brandon and end up in Valrico once they see the difference in lot sizes and school quality. For a detailed comparison, check out my Brandon vs. Riverview vs. Valrico guide.

Ready to Explore Homes in Valrico FL?

If you've read this far, you're serious about Valrico - and I'd love to help you take the next step. Whether you're relocating from out of state, moving up from a starter home in Brandon, or looking for that perfect acreage property with room for your family to spread out, I know this market inside and out.

I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've been helping buyers and sellers in the Valrico, Brandon, Lithia, and FishHawk areas for years. I live and work in this community, and I'll give you the same honest, no-pressure guidance you've been reading in this article.

Here's how to reach me:

No pressure, no obligation - just honest answers about the Valrico real estate market from someone who knows this area better than anyone. Let's find the home that fits your family.

title: Moving to Plant City FL: Small-Town Charm with Big-City Access
excerpt: Moving to Plant City FL? Discover this charming small town near Tampa  -  affordable homes, top schools, strawberry festivals, and a tight-knit community feel.
content:
Quick Answer

What is it like living in Plant City FL?

Plant City FL offers small-town charm, a median home sale price of $350,000, the famous Florida Strawberry Festival, and a growing downtown - all just 30 minutes east of Tampa. It's popular with families and retirees seeking space and value. Explore Plant City, compare nearby Brandon, Riverview, and Valrico, and search Plant City homes for sale.

What's in This Guide ▼
  1. Where Exactly Is Plant City FL?
  2. What Makes Plant City Different from Brandon and Tampa?
  3. What's the Strawberry Festival All About?
  4. What Are the Best Neighborhoods and Areas in Plant City?
  5. How Affordable Is Plant City Compared to Brandon and Tampa?
  6. How Are the Schools in Plant City FL?
  7. What's the Commute Like from Plant City?
  8. What New Development and Growth Is Coming to Plant City?
  9. What Is There to Do in Plant City FL?
  10. What Are the Honest Pros and Cons of Living in Plant City FL?
  11. Frequently Asked Questions About Moving to Plant City FL
  12. Ready to Explore Plant City FL?

Moving to Plant City FL means settling into a charming, agricultural small town in eastern Hillsborough County that offers affordable housing, a tight-knit community, and surprisingly easy access to Tampa, Brandon, and Lakeland along the I-4 corridor. Plant City is known worldwide for the Florida Strawberry Festival, its historic downtown, and a pace of life that feels refreshingly slower than the surrounding metro - all while being just 25 minutes from downtown Tampa and 20 minutes from Lakeland. If you're looking for a place where you can buy more home for your money, enjoy genuine small-town character, and still commute to a major metro, Plant City deserves a serious look. As someone who works in eastern Hillsborough County, I've helped families find homes in Plant City for years, and this guide covers everything you need to know before making the move.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Homes

Where Exactly Is Plant City FL?

Plant City is an incorporated city in eastern Hillsborough County, Florida, situated directly along the Interstate 4 corridor between Tampa to the west and Lakeland to the east. Unlike neighboring Brandon and Riverview - which are unincorporated communities governed by Hillsborough County - Plant City is its own city with its own mayor, city commission, police department, and municipal services.

Geographically, Plant City sits about 25 miles east of downtown Tampa and about 20 miles west of Lakeland. It's surrounded by farmland, strawberry fields, and open space - giving it a distinctly different feel from the suburban sprawl that defines much of the rest of western Hillsborough County. If you're coming from Brandon, Plant City is roughly 15 minutes further east along I-4.

Here's how Plant City connects to the surrounding area:

DestinationDistance from Plant CityDrive Time (approx.)
Downtown Tampa25 miles25-35 minutes
Brandon14 miles15-20 minutes
Lakeland20 miles20-25 minutes
Tampa International Airport (TPA)30 miles30-40 minutes
Orlando (theme parks)55 miles50-60 minutes
Clearwater Beach50 miles50-60 minutes
MacDill Air Force Base30 miles30-40 minutes

Major highways serving Plant City include:

  • Interstate 4 - The primary east-west artery connecting Plant City to Tampa (west) and Orlando (east). This is the main commuter route for most residents.
  • State Road 39 - Runs north-south through Plant City connecting to Zephyrhills to the north and the rural southern portions of Hillsborough County.
  • US Highway 92 (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd) - An alternative east-west route that runs through the heart of Plant City's commercial corridor.
  • State Road 574 (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd / Park Road) - Connects Plant City to Brandon and western Hillsborough County.

What Makes Plant City Different from Brandon and Tampa?

This is the single most important thing to understand about Plant City: it's a real small town with big-city access. That combination is what makes it special - and it's exactly why more people are discovering it every year.

Brandon and the rest of suburban Tampa have grown rapidly, and while those communities offer excellent amenities and convenience, they feel like suburbs - strip malls, chain restaurants, and subdivisions that look similar to those in any growing metro. Plant City has a completely different character. You'll find a walkable historic downtown with locally owned shops and restaurants, agricultural land surrounding the city, and a community where people actually know their neighbors. There's a Friday night football feel here that you won't find in more developed suburbs.

But here's the thing - you're not giving up access to the city. Jump on I-4 and you're in Brandon in 15 minutes, downtown Tampa in 30, and Lakeland in 20. You get the small-town lifestyle without being isolated. That's Plant City's secret weapon, and it's driving a lot of the interest from buyers who've been priced out of, or just grown tired of, the suburban sprawl closer to Tampa.

What's the Strawberry Festival All About?

You can't talk about Plant City without talking about strawberries. The Florida Strawberry Festival is one of the largest and most beloved events in the state, drawing over 500,000 visitors annually over 11 days each February and March. It features live concerts with major national acts, agricultural exhibits, carnival rides, livestock shows, and more strawberry shortcake than you can imagine.

But the agricultural heritage goes far beyond one festival. Plant City has been called the "Winter Strawberry Capital of the World," and the surrounding farmland has been producing strawberries, blueberries, and other crops for well over a century. You'll see farm stands along the roads, tractors on the highways, and the Parkesdale Farm Market bustling with visitors year-round. That agricultural identity gives Plant City a sense of place and pride that newer suburban communities simply don't have.

For residents, the Strawberry Festival is a point of community pride. School groups participate, local businesses sponsor events, and the whole town comes alive. It's the kind of annual tradition that makes you feel like you're part of something - not just living in a zip code.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods and Areas in Plant City?

Plant City offers a wide range of housing options - from historic homes near downtown to newer master-planned developments on the outskirts. Here's a breakdown of the key areas I recommend to my clients:

Walden Lake

Walden Lake is one of Plant City's most established and well-known neighborhoods. It's a large, master-planned community with mature trees, a golf course, community pools, tennis courts, and a clubhouse. Homes here range from the mid-$200s to $400K+ depending on size and lot. It's a popular choice for families who want a suburban feel within Plant City - good school zones, well-maintained common areas, and an active HOA. If you're coming from a suburban community in another state and want something familiar but affordable, Walden Lake checks a lot of boxes.

Historic Downtown

If character is what you're after, downtown Plant City delivers. You'll find craftsman-style bungalows, renovated historic homes, and tree-lined streets with sidewalks. Homes in the historic core generally range from $180K to $350K depending on condition and size. You can walk to restaurants, coffee shops, and the train depot. It's an area that appeals to buyers who value charm and walkability over cookie-cutter construction. Be aware that some older homes may need updates - plumbing, electrical, and roof upgrades are common in homes built before 1960.

Coronet Area

The Coronet area, located on the north side of Plant City, offers a mix of established homes and some newer construction. It's a bit more rural-feeling than Walden Lake or downtown, with larger lots and more space between homes. Prices here tend to be very affordable - you can find homes in the $200K-$350K range with generous lot sizes. If you want land, privacy, and a quieter setting while still being within city limits, Coronet is worth exploring.

Newer Developments

Plant City has seen a wave of new residential development in recent years, particularly along the southern and eastern edges of the city. National builders have moved in with new subdivisions featuring modern floor plans, energy-efficient construction, and community amenities. Prices for new construction generally start in the low $300s and go up from there depending on the builder and lot. These developments appeal to buyers who want a move-in-ready home with warranties and modern features - but keep in mind that many of them come with CDD fees on top of HOA fees, so factor that into your monthly budget.

AreaTypical Price RangeStyleBest For
Walden Lake$250K - $400K+Established master-plannedFamilies wanting community amenities
Historic Downtown$180K - $350KHistoric bungalows, renovated homesBuyers wanting character and walkability
Coronet Area$200K - $350KEstablished, larger lotsBuyers wanting space and privacy
Newer Developments$300K - $450K+New construction, modern amenitiesMove-in-ready buyers, young families

How Affordable Is Plant City Compared to Brandon and Tampa?

This is where Plant City really shines. If you've been looking at home prices in Brandon, Riverview, or Tampa and feeling priced out, Plant City offers a significant affordability advantage - often 15-30% lower for comparable square footage. And because it's an incorporated city with its own services, property tax structures can be slightly different than unincorporated Hillsborough County communities.

Here's a rough comparison of median home prices and key cost factors:

Cost CategoryPlant CityBrandonTampa
Median Home Price$290K - $320K$350K - $400K$400K - $475K
Price Per Sq Ft (avg.)$175 - $200$210 - $240$250 - $300+
Property Tax Rate (approx.)~1.1% - 1.3%~1.1% - 1.2%~1.0% - 1.2%
State Income TaxNoneNoneNone
GroceriesBelow averageAverageSlightly above average
Utilities (electric/water)AverageAverageAverage
Gas PricesSlightly below avg.AverageAverage

The bottom line: your dollar goes further in Plant City than in almost any other part of the Tampa Bay metro. For families or first-time buyers who want to get into homeownership without stretching their budget to the breaking point, Plant City is one of the best-value markets in the region. If you're exploring your options as a first-time home buyer, the affordability here is hard to beat.

For a deeper look at how living costs compare across the eastern Hillsborough County area, check out my cost of living in Brandon FL guide - much of that data applies to the Plant City corridor as well.

How Are the Schools in Plant City FL?

Plant City is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools - the same district that serves Brandon, Tampa, and the rest of the county. The school system is the seventh-largest in the United States, and Plant City has its own cluster of schools that serve the local community.

Here are the main schools serving Plant City families:

High Schools

SchoolGradesNotable
Plant City High School9-12One of the oldest high schools in Hillsborough County; strong athletics, JROTC, and career/technical programs
Durant High School9-12Located just south of Plant City; Cambridge AICE program, strong academic reputation, competitive athletics
Strawberry Crest High School9-12Newer school on the east side; growing reputation, modern facilities, active extracurricular programs

Middle and Elementary Schools

Plant City has several middle and elementary schools, including Marshall Middle School, Tomlin Middle School, Springhead Elementary, Burney Elementary, and Cork Elementary, among others. School assignments are based on your home address, so the neighborhood you choose directly impacts your child's school zone. This is something I always map out with relocating families before they narrow down their home search.

One important note: Plant City's schools don't always get the same high ratings you'll see for some of the Brandon-area schools like Newsome or Bloomingdale. But there are strong programs at Durant and Strawberry Crest in particular, and the district has been investing in improvements across the Plant City cluster. Many families find that the combination of solid school options, smaller class sizes, and a more close-knit community experience more than makes up for what the ratings might suggest on paper.

Private and Charter School Options

Plant City also has private and charter school options, including Resurrection Catholic School and several charter schools in the area. For families willing to drive, the Brandon and Tampa areas offer additional private school choices within a 20-30 minute commute.

What's the Commute Like from Plant City?

Commute time is one of the most common questions I get from buyers considering Plant City. The answer depends on where you're going and when you're driving.

DestinationOff-Peak Drive TimeRush Hour Drive TimeRoute
Downtown Tampa25-30 minutes40-55 minutesI-4 West
Brandon / Westfield Mall area15-20 minutes20-30 minutesI-4 West or SR-574
Lakeland20-25 minutes25-30 minutesI-4 East
USF / North Tampa30-35 minutes45-60 minutesI-4 West to I-275 North
MacDill AFB30-35 minutes45-55 minutesI-4 West to Selmon Expressway
Tampa International Airport30-35 minutes40-50 minutesI-4 West

The I-4 commute is the reality check for Plant City. During morning and evening rush hours, westbound I-4 into Tampa can get congested, particularly through the I-4/I-75 interchange near Brandon. That said, many Plant City commuters find that the commute is manageable - especially compared to what they were dealing with in their previous city. And if you work in Lakeland or eastern Hillsborough County, the commute is actually shorter than it would be from Brandon or Tampa.

Remote and hybrid workers are finding Plant City especially attractive. If you only need to commute into Tampa two or three days a week, the trade-off of a slightly longer drive for significantly lower housing costs and a better quality of life is well worth it.

What New Development and Growth Is Coming to Plant City?

Plant City is in the early stages of a growth wave, and it's worth paying attention to. As housing prices in Tampa, Brandon, and Riverview have climbed, buyers and builders have pushed east - and Plant City is directly in that path of growth.

Here's what's happening:

  • New residential developments - Multiple national and regional builders have active subdivisions in and around Plant City, adding hundreds of new homes to the market. This is bringing new rooftops, which in turn attracts commercial development.
  • Commercial and retail growth - New restaurants, shops, and services are opening to serve the growing population. The areas along US-92 and near I-4 interchanges are seeing the most commercial activity.
  • Infrastructure improvements - The city and county have been investing in road improvements, utilities expansion, and public facilities to accommodate growth.
  • Downtown revitalization - There's been a steady push to revitalize Plant City's historic downtown with new restaurants, small businesses, and community events. The downtown area is becoming a destination, not just a pass-through.
  • I-4 corridor development - As the I-4 corridor between Tampa and Orlando continues to develop, Plant City's position along that route makes it a natural beneficiary of regional economic growth.

For buyers, this growth means opportunity. Buying in Plant City now - before prices fully catch up to Brandon and western Hillsborough County - could mean strong appreciation over the next 5-10 years. That said, growth also brings change, so if the quiet, rural character of Plant City is what attracts you, keep an eye on which areas are developing and choose your location accordingly.

What Is There to Do in Plant City FL?

Plant City may be a small town, but there's more to do here than most people expect - and you're always a short drive from the full range of Tampa Bay attractions.

In Plant City

  • Florida Strawberry Festival - The marquee event. Eleven days of concerts, rides, exhibits, and strawberry shortcake every February/March. Over 500,000 attendees annually.
  • Dinosaur World - A unique outdoor museum with over 200 life-size dinosaur sculptures set in a lush, natural landscape. Great for kids and families. It's one of only three Dinosaur World locations in the country.
  • Parkesdale Farm Market - A Plant City institution. Fresh strawberries, strawberry milkshakes, produce, and baked goods. If you live in Plant City, you'll become a regular.
  • Historic Downtown Plant City - Walkable downtown with local restaurants, antique shops, boutiques, and the beautifully restored train depot. Regular community events, farmers markets, and seasonal celebrations.
  • Edward Medard Conservation Park - Over 1,200 acres of green space with a reservoir, fishing, hiking, biking, and camping. A hidden gem that rivals any state park in the area.
  • Plant City Stadium - Home to community events, youth sports, and occasional professional exhibitions. A gathering spot for the community.
  • Krazy Kup, 1916 Irish Pub, and local eateries - Plant City's dining scene is small but authentic. You'll find Southern comfort food, barbecue, and locally owned cafes that feel like home.

Nearby Attractions (Within 30-45 Minutes)

  • Busch Gardens Tampa Bay - World-class theme park and zoo, about 30 minutes west.
  • Bok Tower Gardens - A stunning 250-acre garden and bird sanctuary near Lake Wales, about 35 minutes southeast.
  • LEGOLAND Florida - Located in Winter Haven, about 30 minutes east. Perfect for families with kids ages 2-12.
  • Hillsborough River State Park - Kayaking, hiking, and camping, about 20 minutes north.
  • Tampa Riverwalk, Channelside, and downtown Tampa - Dining, nightlife, museums, and waterfront activities, about 30 minutes west.
  • Alafia River State Park - Mountain biking and trail hiking, about 20 minutes south.

What Are the Honest Pros and Cons of Living in Plant City FL?

I believe in giving my clients the complete picture. Plant City is a great fit for a lot of people - but it's not for everyone. Here's an honest breakdown:

Pros of Living in Plant City

  • Significantly more affordable housing - Your dollar goes 15-30% further than in Brandon or Tampa for comparable square footage
  • Genuine small-town community - Neighbors know each other, local businesses thrive, and the pace of life is slower and more relaxed
  • No state income tax - Same Florida tax advantage as the rest of the state
  • Agricultural heritage and character - Strawberry Festival, farm stands, historic downtown - Plant City has an identity that newer suburbs lack
  • Easy I-4 access - Direct highway connection to Tampa, Brandon, Lakeland, and Orlando
  • Growth potential - Buying now before prices catch up to western Hillsborough could mean strong appreciation
  • Larger lots and more space - Many Plant City properties offer lot sizes that are rare in closer-in suburbs
  • Florida homestead exemption - Same property tax savings available to all Florida primary residents
  • Lower overall cost of living - Groceries, gas, and daily expenses trend below Brandon and Tampa averages

Cons of Living in Plant City

  • Longer commute to Tampa - Rush-hour drives to downtown Tampa can reach 45-55 minutes via I-4
  • Fewer dining and shopping options - Plant City has local favorites, but you'll head to Brandon or Tampa for big retail and upscale dining
  • School ratings are mixed - While there are strong individual programs, Plant City schools don't always carry the same ratings as top-tier Brandon schools
  • Limited nightlife and entertainment - This is a quiet town. If you want a vibrant nightlife scene, you'll need to drive to Tampa or Ybor City
  • Humidity and heat - Same Florida summer as everywhere else - hot, humid, and stormy from June through September
  • Car-dependent - Public transit is virtually nonexistent. You need a vehicle for everything
  • Flood zones in some areas - Parts of Plant City, especially near the Hillsborough River and low-lying agricultural land, can be in FEMA flood zones. Always check before buying
  • Growth is changing the character - New developments are coming, which means Plant City's small-town feel may evolve over the next decade

Frequently Asked Questions About Moving to Plant City FL

Is Plant City FL a good place to live?

Yes, Plant City is a good place to live - especially if you value affordability, community, and small-town character with access to a major metro. It's one of the most affordable communities in Hillsborough County, and its location along I-4 puts Tampa, Brandon, and Lakeland within easy reach. Families, retirees, and remote workers in particular find that Plant City offers a quality of life that's hard to match at this price point.

How far is Plant City from Tampa?

Plant City is approximately 25 miles east of downtown Tampa via Interstate 4. The drive takes about 25-30 minutes without traffic and 40-55 minutes during peak rush hours. Brandon, which sits between Plant City and Tampa, is about 14 miles west and takes roughly 15-20 minutes to reach.

What is the average home price in Plant City FL?

As of early 2026, the median home price in Plant City ranges from approximately $290,000 to $320,000, depending on the neighborhood, condition, and whether the home is new construction. This is significantly lower than Brandon (median around $350K-$400K) and Tampa (median around $400K-$475K). New construction in Plant City typically starts in the low $300s, while older and historic homes can be found in the $180K-$280K range.

Are there good schools in Plant City FL?

Plant City is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools and has three main high schools: Plant City High School, Durant High School, and Strawberry Crest High School. Durant's Cambridge AICE program is particularly well-regarded. While Plant City's schools may not all carry the same top-tier ratings as some Brandon schools, there are strong programs available, and the district continues to invest in improvements. Private and charter school options are also available locally and in nearby Brandon.

What is the Florida Strawberry Festival?

The Florida Strawberry Festival is an annual 11-day event held in Plant City every February and March. It's one of the most popular festivals in the state, drawing over 500,000 visitors with live concerts featuring major national acts, carnival rides, agricultural exhibits, livestock shows, contests, and of course, mountains of fresh strawberry shortcake. It's a point of community pride and one of the things that makes Plant City unique in the Tampa Bay area.

Is Plant City FL safe?

Plant City is generally a safe community. Like any city, crime rates vary by neighborhood, and it's important to research specific areas before buying. The city has its own police department (unlike unincorporated areas that rely on the county sheriff), which provides dedicated local law enforcement. Overall, the community has a small-town feel where neighbors look out for each other, and many residents cite safety and the close-knit atmosphere as key reasons they love living here.

Does Plant City have a homestead exemption?

Yes. Plant City residents benefit from the same Florida homestead exemption as all Florida primary residents. This allows you to exempt up to $50,000 of your home's assessed value from property taxes, which can save you hundreds to thousands of dollars per year. You must file with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year following your purchase. The exemption also caps annual assessment increases at 3% and provides asset protection from creditors.

Is Plant City a good place to invest in real estate?

Plant City is increasingly attractive for real estate investment. Its affordability relative to the rest of the Tampa Bay metro, combined with the growth trajectory (new developments, commercial expansion, I-4 corridor growth), suggests strong appreciation potential over the next 5-10 years. Home prices are still well below Brandon, Riverview, and Valrico, which means there's room for values to rise as the area continues to develop. As with any investment, it's important to understand the local market, pick the right neighborhoods, and factor in all carrying costs including insurance, taxes, and potential CDD or HOA fees.

Ready to Explore Plant City FL?

If you're considering a move to Plant City, I'd love to help you explore the area and find the right home for your situation. I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I specialize in eastern Hillsborough County - including Plant City, Brandon, Valrico, and the surrounding communities. I've helped families relocate from across the country, and I know this market inside and out.

Here's what I can help with:

  • Personalized neighborhood recommendations based on your budget, lifestyle, commute, and school preferences
  • Virtual and in-person home tours - including driving tours of Plant City's different areas
  • School zone mapping so you know exactly which schools your kids will attend
