Where Can You Find the Best Pizza in Brandon FL?

Pizza is one of those foods where everyone has an opinion, and Brandon gives you enough options to have a strong one. Here's where to look.

Cappy's Pizzeria

Cappy's has been a Tampa Bay favorite for years, and their Brandon-area location delivers the same quality that earned them their reputation. The dough is made fresh daily, the sauce has a nice balance of sweet and tangy, and the specialty pies are creative without being gimmicky. If you like a thicker, chewier crust with quality toppings, Cappy's is your spot. They also have a solid beer selection, making it a good casual dinner option.

Eddie & Sam's NY Pizza

If you're a New York transplant - and let's be honest, there are a lot of you in the Tampa Bay area - Eddie & Sam's is going to feel like a slice of home. Thin crust, foldable slices, and that specific NY-style cheese pull that chain pizza can never replicate. Their plain cheese slice is the litmus test, and it passes with flying colors. It's quick, it's affordable, and it scratches the itch that Domino's never will.

Local vs. Chain Pizza in Brandon

Brandon has all the major chains - Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's, Marco's - plus a healthy number of local and regional pizzerias. The local spots generally offer better quality at a slightly higher price point. For delivery convenience, the chains are hard to beat. For a sit-down pizza dinner or a genuinely great slice, go local. You can also find some excellent pizza at unexpected places like gas station delis and small Italian markets in the area - a very Florida thing.

What About BBQ and Southern Food in Brandon FL?

Florida sits at an interesting crossroads when it comes to barbecue - you'll find influences from Carolina, Texas, Memphis, and a distinctly Florida style that leans heavy on smoked pork and a tangy vinegar-tomato hybrid sauce. Brandon's BBQ scene is modest but satisfying.

Local BBQ spots in the Brandon area tend to run the gamut from roadside smokers and food trucks to small counter-service restaurants with plastic trays and butcher paper. The quality of the smoked meats is generally good - pulled pork, brisket, and smoked ribs are the staples, often served with coleslaw, baked beans, and cornbread. Look for places that smoke on-site with real wood - you can usually smell them before you see them.

For Southern comfort food beyond BBQ, Brandon offers several options for fried chicken, collard greens, mac and cheese, and other soul food staples. The area's proximity to Tampa also means that restaurants like Datz, Ella's Americana Folk Art Cafe, and other Tampa-based Southern food destinations are only a 15-20 minute drive away.

If BBQ is a top priority in your dining life, you're also within easy reach of some of Tampa Bay's best pitmasters. The drive is short, and the payoff is significant.

Where Are the Best Coffee Shops and Cafes in Brandon FL?

Whether you need a morning caffeine fix or a quiet place to work remotely, Brandon has options ranging from familiar chains to local coffee spots.

  • Starbucks (multiple locations): Brandon has several Starbucks locations spread throughout the area, including drive-throughs along SR-60, near Westfield Brandon mall, and in various shopping plazas. Consistent, convenient, and open early - you know what you're getting.
  • Local coffee shops: Brandon has a growing number of independent coffee shops and cafes that offer specialty roasts, unique drink menus, and a more relaxed atmosphere than the chain options. These are great spots for remote work or a casual meeting over a pour-over or cold brew.
  • Buddy Brew Coffee (Tampa): While not technically in Brandon, Buddy Brew in Tampa is worth the 20-minute drive if you're serious about coffee. They roast their own beans locally, the cafe vibe is excellent, and they've become one of Tampa Bay's most respected coffee brands. Many Brandon residents make the trip regularly.

The coffee scene in Brandon is still developing compared to Tampa's Hyde Park or Seminole Heights neighborhoods, but what's here is solid and growing. If you're moving to Brandon and coffee culture is important to you, you'll be pleasantly surprised by what's available - and Tampa's world-class coffee scene is always a short drive away.

What About Craft Beer and Breweries Near Brandon FL?

Tampa Bay has one of the best craft beer scenes in the Southeast, and while Brandon itself doesn't have a major brewery within its borders, some of the region's best are a short drive away.

  • Coppertail Brewing Co. (Tampa, ~20 min): Located in Tampa's Ybor City area, Coppertail produces some of the most creative beers in the region. Their taproom is spacious, dog-friendly, and features rotating food trucks. The Unholy (Belgian-style tripel) and Free Dive IPA are flagship favorites.
  • Cigar City Brewing (Tampa, ~20 min): The flagship of Tampa Bay's craft beer movement. Jai Alai IPA is nationally distributed and nationally acclaimed, and visiting the taproom gives you access to limited releases and taproom-only pours you can't get anywhere else. If you only visit one Tampa Bay brewery, make it this one.
  • Local taprooms and craft beer bars: Brandon has several bars and restaurants with strong craft beer selections on tap, giving you access to local and regional brews without having to drive into Tampa. These spots typically rotate their tap lists and feature Florida breweries prominently.

For beer enthusiasts looking for things to do in Brandon, the proximity to Tampa's brewery district is a major plus. You can hit 3-4 world-class breweries in a single afternoon and be back in Brandon by dinner.

What Is Brandon's "Restaurant Row" on SR-60?

If you've driven down Brandon Boulevard (State Road 60) at any point, you've experienced what locals casually refer to as "Restaurant Row." This corridor, stretching roughly from the Selmon Expressway interchange on the west to Valrico on the east, packs an extraordinary density of dining options into a relatively short stretch of road.

Here's what makes SR-60 such a unique dining destination:

  • Variety: Within a 4-5 mile stretch, you'll find Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Colombian, Peruvian, Mediterranean, Indian, Cuban, American, Italian, and seafood restaurants - all alongside every major national chain
  • Density: At certain intersections, you can see 8-10 restaurants without turning your head. The competition keeps quality high and prices reasonable
  • Accessibility: SR-60 connects directly to I-75 and the Selmon Expressway, making it easy to reach from any part of Brandon, Riverview, Valrico, or even Tampa
  • Price range: From $5 banh mi sandwiches to $40 seafood dinners, the corridor covers every budget

Key restaurant clusters along SR-60 include:

  • West Brandon (near I-75/Selmon): Koizi, Yummy House, Bonefish Grill, Outback Steakhouse, and numerous chains
  • Central Brandon (near Westfield Brandon mall): The highest concentration of dining, with both chains and independents packed into shopping plazas on both sides of SR-60
  • East Brandon / Valrico: More independent restaurants, ethnic eateries, and a slightly less congested dining experience

For people considering which Brandon neighborhood to live in, proximity to the SR-60 restaurant corridor is a genuine lifestyle consideration. Living in Bloomingdale, Brandon Proper, or along the Lithia Pinecrest corridor puts you within 5-10 minutes of dozens of dining options. That matters on a Tuesday night when nobody wants to cook.

How Does Brandon's Food Scene Compare to Tampa's?

This is a question I get from a lot of people who are weighing the pros and cons of living in Brandon versus Tampa proper. Here's my honest take:

Tampa has more high-end dining, more trendy/Instagram-worthy restaurants, and a more developed nightlife-meets-dining culture. If you want James Beard-nominated chefs, rooftop bars with skyline views, and the latest food trends, Tampa wins.

But Brandon beats Tampa in a few key areas:

  • Value: You'll consistently pay less for comparable quality at Brandon restaurants versus their Tampa counterparts
  • International food diversity per square mile: Brandon's SR-60 corridor packs more cuisines into a smaller area than almost anywhere in Tampa
  • Convenience: Easier parking, shorter waits, and less traffic to deal with
  • Family-friendliness: More restaurants are geared toward families and casual dining, with less emphasis on the bar/nightlife scene

The best part? Living in Brandon means Tampa's dining scene is only 15-25 minutes away. You get the everyday convenience of Brandon's restaurant density plus easy access to Tampa's top-tier dining whenever you want it. That's a pretty strong position to be in. For more on the lifestyle advantages, check out my cost of living breakdown for Brandon FL.

Tips for Getting the Most Out of Brandon's Restaurant Scene

After years of eating my way through Brandon, here are a few practical tips:

  • Avoid SR-60 between 5:30-7:00 PM on weekdays. Traffic is brutal during the dinner rush. Either eat early, eat late, or take side streets to your restaurant of choice.
  • Try the strip mall restaurants. Some of Brandon's best food comes from unassuming storefronts in small shopping plazas. Don't judge by the exterior.
  • Go for lunch specials. Many of the international restaurants offer deeply discounted lunch combos and buffets. Indian lunch buffets, Vietnamese lunch combos, and Chinese lunch specials can save you 30-40% compared to dinner pricing.
  • Download the apps. Restaurants like First Watch, Chick-fil-A, and PDQ have apps with rewards programs that save you real money if you're a regular.
  • Explore east of Kingsway. Many people stick to the western half of SR-60 near the mall, but the eastern stretch toward Valrico has excellent restaurants with fewer crowds.
  • Ask locals. The Brandon community is friendly, and people love sharing their favorite spots. Neighborhood Facebook groups are goldmines for restaurant recommendations.

Frequently Asked Questions About Restaurants in Brandon FL

What is the best restaurant in Brandon FL?

The best overall restaurant in Brandon FL depends on what you're looking for, but locals consistently recommend Skupos Seafood for fresh Gulf seafood, Pho Quyen for Vietnamese, Petra Mediterranean for Mediterranean cuisine, and Koizi for all-you-can-eat sushi and hibachi. For waterfront dining, Tarpon Turtle Grill & Marina in nearby Gibsonton is the top pick.

Where can I find the best seafood in Brandon FL?

Skupos Seafood on Brandon Blvd is widely considered the best seafood restaurant in Brandon for its fresh catch and no-frills preparation. For a waterfront experience, Tarpon Turtle Grill & Marina is about 10-15 minutes south in Gibsonton. Miguel's Mexican Seafood & Grill is another excellent option if you want Mexican-style seafood preparations like ceviche and camarones a la diabla.

Is Brandon FL a good place to eat?

Yes. Brandon FL has one of the most diverse and affordable restaurant scenes in the Tampa Bay area. The SR-60 corridor alone features dozens of independent restaurants spanning Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, Mexican, Colombian, Peruvian, Mediterranean, Indian, and American cuisines, plus a strong selection of national chains. The combination of quality, variety, and value is hard to beat in any Tampa Bay suburb.

What restaurants are on Brandon Boulevard (SR-60)?

Brandon Boulevard (SR-60) is the area's primary dining corridor and features restaurants including Koizi Endless Hibachi & Sushi, Yummy House China Bistro, Pho Quyen, La Terraza, First Watch, Bonefish Grill, Outback Steakhouse, PDQ, Culver's, and dozens more. The corridor stretches from the Selmon Expressway to Valrico and offers virtually every cuisine and price point.

Are there good breakfast restaurants in Brandon FL?

Yes. First Watch is the top breakfast and brunch spot in Brandon, with fresh seasonal menus and multiple locations. Another Broken Egg Cafe offers a more upscale brunch experience with craft cocktails. For a budget-friendly breakfast, IHOP and Denny's have multiple Brandon locations, and several local diners serve classic American breakfast plates at fair prices.

What international food can I find in Brandon FL?

Brandon FL has an exceptionally diverse international food scene. You can find authentic Vietnamese (Pho Quyen, Viet-Nomz), Thai (Thai Ruby, Thai Island), Chinese and dim sum (Yummy House), Japanese (Koizi), Indian (Curry Leaves, India's Grill), Mexican (Miguel's, El Patron), Colombian (La Terraza), Peruvian (Green Lemon), Mediterranean (Petra), Cuban, and Middle Eastern (Pita & Kabob) restaurants throughout the area - most concentrated along the SR-60 corridor.

Brandon's Food Scene Is One More Reason People Love Living Here

When people think about relocating to the Tampa Bay area, they think about the weather, the beaches, the lack of state income tax, and the job market. The restaurant scene doesn't always make the top of the list - but it should. The ability to eat well, affordably, and diversely on a random Tuesday night without leaving your neighborhood is a quality-of-life factor that adds up over time.

Brandon delivers on that front. Between the independent local gems, the international food options, and yes, even the well-placed chains, you're never stuck wondering "where should we eat tonight?" There's always somewhere good, and there's always something new to try.

If you're considering moving to Brandon FL, the dining scene is just one piece of a larger lifestyle picture that includes excellent neighborhoods, a reasonable cost of living, and plenty of things to do. I'd love to help you see the full picture.

I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've been helping people buy and sell homes in Brandon, Valrico, Riverview, and the greater Tampa Bay area for years. One of the first things I do with new clients who are relocating is drive them through the neighborhoods and show them the everyday stuff - the restaurants, the grocery stores, the parks, the school drop-off routes. Because buying a home isn't just about the house; it's about the life you build around it.

If you're thinking about making Brandon home, or if you're already here and looking to buy, sell, or invest, I'm happy to help. No pressure, no obligation - just honest, local expertise.

Quick Answer

How much are property taxes in Brandon FL?

Property taxes in Brandon FL are levied at a combined millage rate of roughly 20-22 mills by Hillsborough County, meaning a $300K home pays approximately $5,500-$7,500/year before homestead exemption. Filing for homestead can save you $500-$1,500 annually. Learn about the homestead exemption, understand tax portability if moving within Florida, and search Brandon homes for sale.

Property taxes in Brandon FL are levied by Hillsborough County at an effective rate of roughly 1.1%-1.3% of your home's assessed value, depending on which taxing districts apply to your parcel. On a median-priced home around $350,000 with a Florida Homestead Exemption, you can expect to pay approximately $5,400-$5,900 per year in property taxes - or around $450-$490 per month tucked into your escrow payment. Florida has no state income tax, so property taxes and sales taxes are the primary ways the state and local governments fund services. That trade-off works in your favor if you earn a decent income, but it means your property tax bill deserves real attention.

I walk every buyer through their property tax estimates before we write an offer - because in my experience, taxes are the line item that surprises people most often after closing. This guide breaks down exactly how property taxes work in Brandon, what you'll pay at every price point, how to reduce your bill, and the deadlines you cannot afford to miss.

Talk to a Tampa Bay ExpertSearch All Homes

How Do Property Taxes Work in Florida?

Florida's property tax system has a few moving parts that are worth understanding before you look at any specific numbers. Once you grasp the basics, everything else in this guide will click into place.

Assessed Value vs. Market Value

Your property's market value (also called "just value") is what the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser determines your home would sell for on the open market. Your assessed value is the number your taxes are actually calculated on - and it can be significantly lower than market value if you have a Homestead Exemption with a Save Our Homes cap in place.

For a brand-new purchase or a home without homestead, assessed value typically equals market value. But for homesteaded properties you've owned for several years, the Save Our Homes cap limits annual assessment increases to the lesser of 3% or the Consumer Price Index. Over time, this creates a growing gap between what your home is worth and what you're taxed on - which is one of the most powerful tax benefits in the state.

Millage Rates Explained

Florida property taxes are expressed in millage rates. One mill equals $1 in tax for every $1,000 of taxable value. So if your taxable value is $300,000 and the total millage rate is 19.0 mills, your annual tax would be $300,000 / $1,000 x 19.0 = $5,700.

Multiple taxing authorities set their own millage rates each year, and they all get added together to form your total combined millage rate. The major authorities that show up on a Brandon property tax bill include Hillsborough County government, the School Board, the Southwest Florida Water Management District, the Children's Board, and several other special districts.

Hillsborough County Millage Rate Breakdown

Brandon is an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County, which means you do not pay city taxes - there is no municipal millage. However, you do pay the full slate of county and special district millages. Here is an approximate breakdown of the millage rates that apply to a typical Brandon property:

Taxing AuthorityApproximate Millage Rate
Hillsborough County Operating5.5 mills
Hillsborough County School Board7.4 mills
City of Tampa (N/A - Brandon is unincorporated)0.0 mills
Southwest FL Water Management District (SWFWMD)0.3 mills
Hillsborough County Library / Transportation2.0 mills
Children's Board of Hillsborough County0.5 mills
Hospital Authority / Other Special Districts1.8 mills
Total Combined Millage (approximate)~17.5-19.5 mills

Note: Millage rates are set annually and can change. The figures above are approximate and intended for estimation purposes. Your actual combined millage rate depends on the specific taxing districts that apply to your parcel. Always verify current rates on the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser website or the Hillsborough County Tax Collector website.

The fact that Brandon doesn't carry city millage is one of its cost advantages. If you buy within the City of Tampa limits, you'll pick up an additional 6+ mills on top of the county rate, pushing your effective tax rate significantly higher.

How Do You Calculate Property Taxes on a Brandon FL Home?

Let me walk you through a step-by-step calculation using a $350,000 home - right around the median price for the Brandon area. I'll show you the numbers with and without the Florida Homestead Exemption so you can see exactly how much it matters.

With Homestead Exemption ($350,000 Home)

For this example, I'm using a combined non-school millage of approximately 10.1 mills and a school millage of approximately 7.4 mills (total ~17.5 mills). Your specific parcel may differ slightly.

Line ItemAmount
Market / Assessed Value (first year of ownership)$350,000
Homestead Exemption - first $25,000 (applies to all taxes)-$25,000
Additional Homestead - $50,001 to $75,000 (applies to non-school taxes only)-$25,000
Taxable Value for Non-School Taxes (~10.1 mills)$300,000
Taxable Value for School Taxes (~7.4 mills)$325,000
Estimated Non-School Taxes ($300,000 x 10.1 / 1,000)~$3,030
Estimated School Taxes ($325,000 x 7.4 / 1,000)~$2,405
Total Estimated Annual Property Tax~$5,435
Monthly Equivalent (in escrow)~$453

Without Homestead Exemption ($350,000 Home)

Line ItemAmount
Market / Assessed Value$350,000
Homestead Exemption$0
Taxable Value (all taxes, ~17.5 mills combined)$350,000
Estimated Total Taxes ($350,000 x 17.5 / 1,000)~$6,125
Monthly Equivalent~$510

That's a difference of roughly $690 per year just from the homestead exemption. And it gets better over time - once the Save Our Homes cap kicks in, your assessed value grows slower than the market, widening the gap between your tax bill and what it would be without homestead. I've seen long-term Brandon homeowners saving $2,000-$4,000 per year compared to what a new buyer would pay on the same house.

If you haven't filed yours yet, stop reading this and go handle that first. Here's my complete Florida Homestead Exemption guide.

What Are Property Taxes at Different Home Prices in Brandon?

Here's a quick reference table showing estimated annual property taxes at common Brandon-area home prices. These assume homestead exemption is in place, the home was recently purchased (assessed value equals market value), and a combined millage rate of approximately 17.5 mills.

Home PriceEst. Annual Tax (With Homestead)Monthly Equivalent
$250,000~$3,690~$308
$300,000~$4,565~$380
$350,000~$5,435~$453
$400,000~$6,310~$526
$500,000~$8,060~$672
$600,000~$9,810~$818

Note: These are estimates. Your actual taxes depend on your specific millage rate, any additional exemptions you qualify for, and your property's assessed value. Non-ad valorem assessments (CDD fees, solid waste, stormwater, lighting) are not included above and will add to your total tax bill.

When I run numbers for buyers, I always calculate the full picture - not just the ad valorem taxes, but also CDD fees, HOA, insurance, and any special assessments. If you want that level of detail for a specific property you're considering, give me a call and I'll pull the actual tax records.

What Are CDD Fees and How Do They Show Up on Your Tax Bill?

If you're buying in a newer community in Brandon, Riverview, or Valrico, there's a very good chance you'll encounter CDD fees - Community Development District assessments. These are not technically "property taxes" in the traditional sense, but they appear on your annual property tax bill as a non-ad valorem assessment, and they function the same way from your wallet's perspective.

CDDs are special-purpose government districts created to finance the infrastructure of new communities - roads, water/sewer systems, parks, pools, playgrounds, stormwater management, and sometimes even school contributions. The developer creates the CDD, issues bonds to build the infrastructure, and then homeowners pay off those bonds through annual assessments on their tax bills.

Here's what CDD fees typically look like in Brandon-area communities:

Community TypeTypical Annual CDD FeeMonthly Equivalent
Newer subdivisions (Riverview, South Brandon)$1,500-$2,500$125-$210
Master-planned communities (FishHawk, Waterset)$2,000-$3,500$167-$292
Luxury / resort-style communities$2,500-$4,000+$210-$335+
Established Brandon neighborhoods (no CDD)$0$0

The critical thing to understand is that CDD fees are in addition to your property taxes. A $350,000 home in a CDD community could have a total annual tax-and-fee bill of $7,000-$9,000+ once you combine ad valorem taxes and CDD assessments. That's a meaningful difference compared to the same-priced home in an established Brandon neighborhood without a CDD.

I always pull the actual CDD schedule for any new construction or newer-community listing my buyers are considering. For a deep dive into how CDDs work, what they fund, and which communities have them, read my full CDD Fee Florida Guide.

How Can You Reduce Your Property Taxes in Brandon FL?

You have more control over your property tax bill than you probably think. Here are the most impactful strategies available to Brandon homeowners, ranked roughly by how much they can save you.

1. File Your Homestead Exemption

This is the single most important thing you can do. The Florida Homestead Exemption removes up to $50,000 from your assessed value, saving you roughly $690-$975 per year depending on your millage rate. It also activates the Save Our Homes cap, which limits future assessment increases to 3% per year - a benefit that compounds dramatically over time.

You must own the property and make it your primary residence by January 1, then file by March 1. If you haven't done this yet, here's my step-by-step Homestead Exemption Florida Guide.

2. Use Portability When You Move

If you already own a homesteaded property in Florida and you're buying a new home, you can transfer your Save Our Homes benefit (up to $500,000 of accumulated differential) to your new property. This is called portability, and it can save you thousands of dollars per year on your new home. You must establish homestead on the new property within three tax years of leaving the old one.

I've worked with buyers who ported over $100,000 in Save Our Homes benefit to their new Brandon home - that's over $1,750 in annual tax savings that would have vanished if they hadn't filed. It's one of the first things I discuss with anyone selling a homesteaded property in Florida.

3. Check Your Assessment for Errors

The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office assesses hundreds of thousands of properties. Mistakes happen. I recommend every homeowner review their property record on the HCPA website at least once a year. Look for:

  • Incorrect square footage or lot size
  • Wrong number of bedrooms, bathrooms, or garage bays
  • Features listed that don't exist (pool, fireplace, extra buildings)
  • Assessed value that seems significantly higher than comparable sales

If you find an error, contact the Property Appraiser's office. Many corrections can be made informally without needing a formal appeal.

4. File a Value Adjustment Board (VAB) Petition

If you believe your property has been overassessed and the Property Appraiser won't adjust it informally, you have the right to file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board. The filing fee is $15, and hearings are held between August and December. You'll need to present evidence - comparable sales, condition issues, or other factors - showing that the assessed value exceeds market value.

VAB petitions are particularly worth considering if your home has condition issues that the mass-appraisal model doesn't capture, if the market has softened since your last assessment, or if you purchased the home for significantly less than the assessed value.

5. Claim Additional Exemptions

Beyond the standard homestead exemption, Florida offers additional exemptions that can stack on top of your base $50,000. These include:

  • Senior Exemption (Age 65+): An additional exemption of up to $50,000 on the county portion of taxes for qualifying seniors who meet household income limits. Income thresholds are adjusted annually.
  • Disabled Veteran Exemption: An additional $5,000 exemption for veterans with a 10%+ service-connected disability. Veterans who are totally and permanently disabled may receive a full exemption.
  • Total and Permanent Disability Exemption: A full exemption from property taxes for homeowners certified as totally and permanently disabled.
  • Surviving Spouse of First Responder / Military: Additional exemptions and full exemptions are available depending on circumstances.
  • Widow/Widower Exemption: An additional $500 exemption for surviving spouses who have not remarried.

If any of these apply to you, contact the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser to apply. These exemptions don't apply automatically - you have to file for them.

6. Pay Early for the Discount

This one is easy money if you pay your taxes directly (not through escrow). Florida offers discounts for early payment - up to 4% off if you pay in November. I'll cover the full discount schedule in the next section.

When Are Property Taxes Due in Brandon FL?

The Hillsborough County Tax Collector mails property tax bills on or around November 1 each year. The bill covers the tax year from January 1 through December 31. Here's the payment schedule and the discount structure Florida uses to incentivize early payment:

Payment MonthDiscountEffective Cost
November4% discount96% of the total bill
December3% discount97% of the total bill
January2% discount98% of the total bill
February1% discount99% of the total bill
March (due date)No discount - full amount due100% of the total bill
April 1 and afterDELINQUENT - interest and penalties begin100% + penalties

On a $5,400 tax bill, that November discount saves you $216 - basically free money for paying a few months early. If you have the cash available and you're paying directly, there's no reason not to pay in November.

Escrow vs. Direct Pay

Most homeowners with a mortgage have their property taxes escrowed - meaning your lender collects a monthly portion as part of your mortgage payment and pays the tax bill on your behalf. If your taxes are escrowed, your lender typically pays in November or December to capture the discount. You won't see a separate tax bill, but you should still verify that your lender is paying on time and claiming the discount.

If you own your home outright or your lender doesn't require escrow, you'll pay directly to the Hillsborough County Tax Collector. You can pay online, by mail, or in person. Set a calendar reminder for early November so you don't miss the maximum discount.

What happens if you don't pay? Taxes become delinquent on April 1. Starting June 1, the Tax Collector sells tax certificates on unpaid amounts, and the property begins accruing interest at up to 18% annually. Continued non-payment can eventually lead to a tax deed sale - which means losing the property. Don't let it get there.

What Should New Homeowners Expect for Property Taxes in Brandon?

If you just bought a home - or you're about to - pay close attention to this section. Your first-year property tax bill will almost certainly be higher than what the previous owner was paying, and the difference can be significant enough to throw off your budget if you're not prepared.

The "Assessment Reset" When a Property Sells

When a homesteaded property changes hands, two things happen that increase the tax bill:

  • The Save Our Homes cap is removed. The previous owner may have had their assessed value capped well below market value - sometimes $50,000 to $150,000+ below, depending on how long they lived there. When you buy the property, the assessed value resets to current market value (your purchase price, essentially).
  • The homestead exemption is removed. The seller's homestead exemption doesn't transfer to you. You'll need to file your own, and it won't take effect until the tax year after you close (assuming you close after January 1).

This means your first full year of property taxes could be 30-50% higher (sometimes more) than what the seller was paying. I see this surprise buyers regularly. The tax amount shown on a listing is based on the previous owner's assessed value and exemptions - not what the new buyer will owe.

First-Year Tax Timeline Example

Let's say you close on a $350,000 home in Brandon on June 15:

  • Year of purchase: You'll receive a prorated tax bill at closing. The seller pays taxes through the closing date, and you cover the remainder of the year. Since you don't yet have homestead exemption, this will be at the full (non-exempt) rate based on the county's current assessed value.
  • January 1 of the following year: If you've made the home your primary residence, this is when you must own and occupy it to qualify for homestead. File your application as soon as possible - the deadline is March 1.
  • November of the following year: Your first full tax bill arrives with homestead exemption applied (assuming you filed on time). This bill reflects your purchase price as the assessed value, minus the $50,000 homestead exemption.

Budgeting Tips for Your First Year

  • Don't rely on the listing's tax amount. Always calculate your expected taxes based on your purchase price, without Save Our Homes cap, with or without homestead depending on timing.
  • Expect an escrow adjustment. If your lender initially estimated taxes based on the seller's old tax bill, they'll adjust your escrow once the higher bill comes in. This can increase your monthly mortgage payment by $100-$300+. It's not a surprise if you plan for it.
  • File homestead immediately. The sooner your homestead exemption is in place, the sooner you start getting the $50,000 reduction and the Save Our Homes cap starts building.

This first-year tax adjustment is one of the most common things I walk my first-time home buyers in Brandon through. It's completely normal - it just needs to be in your budget from day one.

How Does Brandon Compare to Other Areas for Property Taxes?

Property tax rates vary across Central Florida depending on county, city, and special district millage rates. Here's how Brandon stacks up against other popular areas, assuming a $350,000 home with homestead exemption in each location:

LocationCountyApprox. Effective Tax RateEst. Annual Tax ($350K Home w/ Homestead)Notes
Brandon (unincorporated)Hillsborough~1.1%-1.3%~$5,200-$5,700No city millage; may have CDD
Tampa (City of)Hillsborough~1.3%-1.5%~$6,000-$6,800City millage adds ~6+ mills
St. PetersburgPinellas~1.1%-1.3%~$5,100-$5,600Different county/city millage structure
Riverview (unincorporated)Hillsborough~1.1%-1.3%~$5,200-$5,700Similar to Brandon; higher CDD likelihood
LakelandPolk~1.0%-1.2%~$4,500-$5,200Lower county rates; city millage applies
OrlandoOrange~1.1%-1.3%~$5,000-$5,500Comparable effective rate

Note: These are approximate estimates based on publicly available millage rate data for each jurisdiction. Actual taxes depend on specific parcel location, exemptions, and current-year millage rates. Non-ad valorem assessments are not included.

Brandon and Riverview tend to have very similar tax rates since they're both unincorporated Hillsborough County. The key differentiator is often the CDD - newer Riverview communities tend to carry higher CDD assessments due to more recent infrastructure bonds. Tampa's city millage makes it notably more expensive on the tax front, which is one reason Brandon's cost of living comes in lower than Tampa proper even though the areas are adjacent.

Frequently Asked Questions About Property Taxes in Brandon FL

How much are property taxes in Brandon FL?

On a median-priced home of around $350,000 with homestead exemption, you can expect to pay approximately $5,200-$5,700 per year in ad valorem property taxes. Without homestead, that same home would owe closer to $6,100. If the home is in a CDD community, add $1,500-$3,500 per year in non-ad valorem assessments on top of that.

What is the property tax rate in Hillsborough County?

The combined millage rate for unincorporated Hillsborough County (which includes Brandon) is approximately 17.5-19.5 mills, translating to an effective tax rate of roughly 1.1%-1.3% of assessed value. The exact rate depends on which special taxing districts apply to your specific parcel. Properties within the City of Tampa carry additional city millage.

Why is my tax bill different from the previous owner's?

When a property sells, the assessed value resets to current market value and the previous owner's homestead exemption and Save Our Homes cap are removed. If the prior owner had lived there for many years, their assessed value could have been tens of thousands of dollars below market - meaning their tax bill was significantly lower than what a new buyer will pay on the same property.

Can I appeal my property tax assessment in Hillsborough County?

Yes. You can first contact the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office to discuss your assessment informally. If that doesn't resolve it, you can file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board (VAB) for a formal hearing. The filing fee is $15 and the petition deadline is typically 25 days after the TRIM (Truth in Millage) notice is mailed, usually in August.

Do Brandon FL homeowners pay city taxes?

No. Brandon is an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County, which means there is no city government and no city millage rate. This is one of the advantages of Brandon from a property tax standpoint - you avoid the additional 6+ mills that Tampa residents pay to the City of Tampa.

What is the early payment discount for Hillsborough County property taxes?

Florida offers a sliding discount for early payment: 4% off if paid in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, and 1% in February. The full amount is due in March with no discount. Taxes become delinquent on April 1. If your taxes are escrowed through your mortgage lender, they typically pay in November or December to capture the discount on your behalf.

Are CDD fees included in property taxes?

CDD fees appear on your annual property tax bill as a non-ad valorem assessment, so they're collected alongside your property taxes by the Hillsborough County Tax Collector. However, they are technically separate from ad valorem property taxes - they're a special district assessment that funds community infrastructure. Not all Brandon homes are in a CDD; it depends on the community. For details, see my CDD Fee Florida Guide.

How do I find my property's current assessed value and tax amount?

Visit the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's website (hcpafl.org) and search by your property address or folio number. You'll find your assessed value, market value, exemptions, and a detailed breakdown of your tax bill by taxing authority. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector website shows your actual tax bill and payment status.

Sources

Data referenced in this guide comes from the following sources:

  • Hillsborough County Property Appraiser - Assessed Values, Exemptions, and Millage Rates
  • Hillsborough County Tax Collector - Tax Bills, Payment Schedules, and Delinquency Information
  • Florida Department of Revenue - Property Tax Exemptions and Millage Rate Information
  • Florida Constitution, Article VII - Homestead Exemptions and Save Our Homes Provisions
  • Florida Statutes, Chapter 193 & 197 - Assessment and Collection of Taxes

Need Help Understanding Property Taxes on a Specific Brandon Home?

Property taxes are one of those things that look straightforward on paper but get complicated fast once you're looking at a real home in a real neighborhood with real CDD fees, special assessments, and Save Our Homes resets. The tax amount on a listing is almost never the amount you'll actually pay as the new owner - and I've seen that disconnect catch too many buyers off guard.

When you work with me, I pull the actual tax records, calculate your expected first-year taxes, factor in homestead timing, CDD assessments, and non-ad valorem charges, and build out a true monthly payment estimate before we ever write an offer. No surprises after closing.

Whether you're a first-time buyer trying to understand what you can afford, you're comparing new construction communities with different CDD structures, or you just want someone to double-check your current tax bill - I'm here to help.

Quick Answer

What are the best things to do in Brandon FL?

Top things to do in Brandon FL include visiting Westfield Brandon mall, kayaking the Alafia River, exploring the local restaurant scene, and enjoying 20+ parks and recreation areas. Brandon's central location also gives you easy access to Tampa's attractions and Gulf beaches. Check out the best restaurants in Brandon, explore Brandon's top parks, and browse homes for sale in Brandon.

What's in This Guide ▼
  1. What Are the Best Shopping & Entertainment Options in Brandon FL?
  2. What Parks and Outdoor Activities Are Near Brandon FL?
  3. What Day Trips Can You Take From Brandon FL?
  4. How Close Is Brandon FL to Professional Sports?
  5. What's the Dining Scene Like in Brandon FL?
  6. Where Can You Work Out and Stay Active in Brandon FL?
  7. What Family Activities Are Available in and Around Brandon FL?
  8. What Arts and Cultural Attractions Are Near Brandon FL?
  9. What Seasonal Events and Festivals Happen Near Brandon FL?
  10. Is Brandon FL a Good Place to Live?
  11. Frequently Asked Questions About Things to Do in Brandon FL
  12. Ready to Make Brandon FL Home?

Brandon, Florida, is one of Tampa Bay's most active and well-rounded communities - and if you're wondering what there is to do here, the short answer is a lot. From world-class mountain biking trails and natural spring swimming to professional sports, major shopping destinations, and a dining scene that punches well above its weight, Brandon FL activities cover every interest, age group, and energy level. Whether you're a long-time resident looking for something new, a newcomer scoping out the lifestyle, or a visitor passing through, this guide breaks down everything worth your time in and around Brandon.

I'm Barrett Henry, a REMAX Collective real estate agent who helps people buy and sell homes across the Tampa Bay area every day. A huge part of what I do is helping clients understand what life actually feels like in a neighborhood - not just the square footage and the school ratings, but the weekend plans, the Tuesday-night dinner spots, and the trails you'll hit on a Saturday morning. This guide is built from that perspective.

If you're also researching the area for a potential move, you'll want to pair this with our complete Brandon FL relocation guide and our breakdown of the cost of living in Brandon FL.

Talk to a Tampa Bay ExpertSearch All Homes

What Are the Best Shopping & Entertainment Options in Brandon FL?

Brandon has quietly become one of the strongest retail and entertainment corridors in Hillsborough County. You don't have to drive into Tampa for a full day of shopping and fun - most of it is right here.

Westfield Brandon Mall

Westfield Brandon is the largest mall in the Tampa Bay area, anchored by Macy's, Dillard's, and JCPenney with over 150 stores and restaurants under one roof. It's a legitimate regional draw. Beyond the standard retail, you'll find a food court, specialty shops, and seasonal events that keep the space active year-round. For families relocating to the area, this is one of those everyday conveniences that makes life here feel complete - you're never far from what you need.

Topgolf Tampa

Located about 10 minutes from Brandon, Topgolf Tampa is one of my favorite spots to recommend for a casual night out. It's part driving range, part sports bar, part social experience - and you don't need to be a golfer to enjoy it. Climate-controlled hitting bays, a full menu, and a rooftop terrace make this a go-to for date nights, birthday parties, corporate outings, and groups of friends who want something more interactive than sitting at a restaurant.

Dave & Buster's

Dave & Buster's sits right in the Brandon entertainment corridor and delivers exactly what you'd expect - arcade games, a full bar, big-screen sports viewing, and a menu that works for families and adults alike. It's a reliable option when you need to entertain a group with mixed ages and interests.

Main Event Entertainment

Main Event brings bowling, laser tag, gravity ropes, billiards, and arcade games into one venue. It skews a bit more family-friendly than Dave & Buster's and tends to be a hit for birthday parties and weekend outings with kids. The value is solid - especially during their weekday specials.

Brandon Town Center Area & Shopping Plazas

Beyond the mall, Brandon's retail footprint is impressive. Regency Square and Brandon Crossing are two major shopping plazas that house big-box retailers, grocery stores, specialty shops, and restaurants. The Brandon Town Center corridor along SR-60 (Brandon Boulevard) essentially functions as the commercial spine of the community - you'll find everything from Target and Best Buy to local boutiques and service providers.

What Parks and Outdoor Activities Are Near Brandon FL?

This is where Brandon really separates itself from a lot of other suburbs. The outdoor recreation access here is genuinely excellent. You've got state parks, county parks, river systems, and natural springs all within a short drive - and that's a major quality-of-life factor that people often underestimate until they've lived here for a while.

Hillsborough River State Park

Hillsborough River State Park is one of the oldest state parks in Florida and a true gem just northeast of Brandon. You can canoe or kayak the river, hike several miles of trails through hardwood hammocks and wetlands, camp overnight, and even take a dip in the park's swimming area. It's a full-day outdoor experience without leaving the county. One of my favorite spots to send clients who want to understand what "Florida nature" really looks like beyond the beaches.

Lettuce Lake Park

Lettuce Lake Park sits along the Hillsborough River and features elevated boardwalks that wind through cypress swamps and hardwood forests. There's a nature center, a playground, picnic pavilions, and an observation tower. It's an accessible, family-friendly way to experience Florida's natural landscape - and you'll regularly spot river otters, turtles, herons, and the occasional alligator from the boardwalk.

Alafia River State Park

If you mountain bike - or want to start - Alafia River State Park is a destination. The trail system here is considered world-class, built on reclaimed phosphate mining land that created an unusually hilly terrain for Florida. Riders come from across the Southeast to tackle these trails. Beyond biking, the park offers hiking, horseback riding, and camping. It's located in Lithia, just minutes south of Brandon.

Lithia Springs Park

Lithia Springs is a natural spring-fed swimming area along the Alafia River. The water stays cool year-round (around 72°F), which makes it an incredible escape during Florida's long summers. The park includes picnic areas, a playground, and canoe/kayak launches. On weekends and holidays, it fills up fast - plan to arrive early. This is the kind of spot that makes people fall in love with living in this part of Florida.

Edward Medard Conservation Park

Edward Medard Conservation Park is a 1,284-acre park centered around a 770-acre reservoir - making it one of the best freshwater fishing spots in the area. Bass, bream, and catfish are all on the menu. Beyond fishing, there are hiking and biking trails, a boat ramp, picnic shelters, and a campground. It's peaceful, spacious, and rarely overcrowded.

Neighborhood Parks & the Brandon Regional Library

For everyday recreation, Brandon's network of neighborhood parks is solid. Riverhills Park and Bloomingdale Park both offer playgrounds, sports fields, walking paths, and pavilions - the kinds of green spaces that anchor a community and give families a reason to get outside on a Tuesday evening. The Brandon Regional Library also deserves a mention here: it's a well-maintained, active branch of the Hillsborough County Public Library system with programming for all ages, meeting rooms, and a solid children's section.

Curious about which neighborhoods put you closest to these parks? Check out our guide to the best neighborhoods in Brandon FL for families.

What Day Trips Can You Take From Brandon FL?

One of Brandon's biggest lifestyle advantages is its central positioning in the Tampa Bay region. You're close enough to major attractions that day trips are genuinely easy - not the kind of "day trip" that eats your whole day in the car. Here's a breakdown of the most popular destinations and how long it actually takes to get there.

DestinationDrive Time from BrandonHighlights
Busch Gardens Tampa Bay~20 minutesWorld-class roller coasters, African wildlife, live entertainment
Tampa Riverwalk & Downtown Tampa~20 minutesWaterfront dining, museums, nightlife, events
Ybor City~20 minutesHistoric district, Cuban culture, restaurants, nightlife
The Florida Aquarium~25 minutesMarine exhibits, shark swim programs, wildlife cruises
Clearwater Beach~40 minutesConsistently top-rated U.S. beach, white sand, Pier 60 sunset celebrations
St. Pete Beach~45 minutesAward-winning beach, historic Don CeSar hotel, laid-back vibe
Legoland Winter Haven~45 minutesTheme park built for kids ages 2-12, water park, hotel
Walt Disney World (Orlando)~60 minutesFour theme parks, two water parks, Disney Springs

That table is a big reason people choose Brandon over more isolated suburbs. You're not sacrificing access to anything - you're just getting more house for the money while staying connected to all of it. That's a point I make constantly when working with buyers who are comparing communities. If you're weighing your options, our Brandon vs. Riverview vs. Valrico comparison digs deeper into how these areas stack up.

How Close Is Brandon FL to Professional Sports?

Tampa Bay is a legitimate four-sport metro, and Brandon puts you right in the middle of it. If you're a sports fan, this is one of the best suburbs in the region for easy access to games.

  • Tampa Bay Buccaneers (NFL) - Raymond James Stadium is about 20 minutes from Brandon. Tom Brady may have moved on, but the fan culture here is electric, and tailgating at Raymond James is a rite of passage.
  • Tampa Bay Lightning (NHL) - Amalie Arena, right on the downtown Tampa waterfront, is roughly 20 minutes away. The Lightning have built one of the most passionate fanbases in hockey, and Amalie Arena is considered one of the best venues in the NHL.
  • Tampa Bay Rays (MLB) - The Rays currently play in St. Petersburg, about 40 minutes from Brandon. The franchise has been exploring stadium options, so this may shift in the coming years - but for now, catching a game is still a reasonable weeknight outing.
  • Tampa Bay Rowdies (USL Championship Soccer) - Also based in St. Pete at Al Lang Stadium, the Rowdies offer an affordable, energetic game-day experience right on the waterfront.
  • USF Bulls (NCAA) - The University of South Florida campus is about 25 minutes north of Brandon and fields competitive Division I programs in football, basketball, baseball, and more.

Between NFL Sundays, Lightning playoffs, Rays summer games, and college athletics, there's virtually no off-season for sports fans living in Brandon.

What's the Dining Scene Like in Brandon FL?

Brandon's food scene is deeper than most people expect from a suburb. The restaurant row along SR-60 (Brandon Boulevard) is packed with options - but what really sets this area apart is the international variety.

You'll find a strong Vietnamese food corridor, authentic Cuban spots, Indian restaurants, Thai kitchens, and a growing number of Latin American eateries alongside the usual American chains. Brandon's demographic diversity drives this, and it's one of the things long-time residents appreciate most about everyday life here.

The craft brewery scene is also picking up steam in the greater Brandon and Riverview area, with several taprooms offering local brews, food trucks, and live music on weekends.

A full restaurant guide for Brandon is in the works - but if you're moving to the area and want specific recommendations based on the neighborhood you're looking at, that's the kind of local insight I share with every client. Don't hesitate to reach out.

Where Can You Work Out and Stay Active in Brandon FL?

Fitness infrastructure in Brandon is comprehensive. You won't struggle to find a gym, a class, or a community that fits your routine - which matters more than people think when choosing where to live.

  • Major gym chains: LA Fitness, Planet Fitness, and Anytime Fitness all have locations in the Brandon area, giving you options at every price point and schedule.
  • CrossFit boxes: Several CrossFit-affiliated gyms operate in and around Brandon for those who prefer high-intensity functional training with a tight-knit community feel.
  • Yoga studios: Multiple yoga studios offer everything from hot yoga to restorative and prenatal classes.
  • Recreation & active entertainment: Topgolf, bowling alleys, and the trail systems at Alafia River State Park and Hillsborough River State Park give you ways to stay active that don't feel like "working out."

Add in the parks, river trails, and year-round outdoor weather, and staying active in Brandon is more about choosing which option than finding any option.

What Family Activities Are Available in and Around Brandon FL?

Families are a huge part of Brandon's identity - and the area delivers on activities that keep kids engaged, entertained, and active. Here's what's in easy reach.

Kid-Friendly Attractions Nearby

  • Glazer Children's Museum (Tampa) - An interactive, hands-on museum in downtown Tampa designed for kids ages 0-10. About 20 minutes from Brandon.
  • MOSI - Museum of Science & Industry (Tampa) - Science exhibits, a planetarium, a ropes course, and rotating hands-on displays. One of the better STEM-focused attractions in the region, roughly 20 minutes north of Brandon.
  • ZooTampa at Lowry Park - Consistently ranked among the top zoos in the country. It features Florida wildlife, African exhibits, a manatee viewing center, rides, and splash areas. About 25 minutes from Brandon.
  • Splash pads and water parks - Several Hillsborough County parks feature free or low-cost splash pads, and Adventure Island (Busch Gardens' water park) is a short drive for full-day water park fun.

Youth Sports & Leagues

Brandon has a strong youth sports infrastructure. Little League baseball, soccer leagues, competitive swim teams, flag football, basketball - the community invests in organized youth athletics, and you'll find leagues for virtually every age group and skill level. This is one of the things that makes Brandon such a popular landing spot for families with school-age kids. If that's your situation, our guide to the best Brandon neighborhoods for families covers which areas put you closest to the best parks, schools, and youth programs.

What Arts and Cultural Attractions Are Near Brandon FL?

Brandon itself is more of a residential community than a cultural hub - but you're a short drive from some of the best arts and cultural institutions on Florida's Gulf Coast.

  • Straz Center for the Performing Arts (Tampa) - The largest performing arts center in the Southeast. Broadway touring shows, ballet, opera, concerts, comedy - the programming is year-round and genuinely world-class. About 20 minutes from Brandon.
  • Tampa Museum of Art - Located along the Tampa Riverwalk, the museum features contemporary and classical exhibitions. Free admission on select days.
  • The Salvador Dalí Museum (St. Petersburg) - One of the most visited museums in the Tampa Bay area and home to the largest collection of Dalí works outside of Spain. About 40 minutes from Brandon and worth the trip.
  • Local community theater - Several community theater groups in the greater Brandon and Tampa area produce regular seasons of plays and musicals, offering both entertainment and opportunities for residents who want to get involved on stage or behind the scenes.

Living in Brandon means you can catch a Broadway show, visit a world-renowned museum, and be home in time for dinner - without the hassle or expense of living in a downtown core.

What Seasonal Events and Festivals Happen Near Brandon FL?

The Tampa Bay area has a packed event calendar, and Brandon residents are well-positioned to take advantage of all of it. Here are the highlights by season.

Winter & Early Spring (January-March)

  • Gasparilla Pirate Festival (Tampa, late January) - Tampa's signature event. A massive pirate-themed parade and invasion along Bayshore Boulevard, followed by a day-long street festival. It's one of the largest parades in the country, and Brandon residents pour into Tampa for it every year.
  • Florida State Fair (Tampa, February) - Rides, livestock shows, concerts, fried everything. The Florida State Fairgrounds are actually located in the Brandon/Tampa border area, making this practically a neighborhood event.
  • Plant City Strawberry Festival (February/March) - One of the most beloved festivals in the region, held in Plant City (about 15 minutes east of Brandon). Live concerts from major country and classic rock acts, strawberry shortcake, agricultural exhibits, and carnival rides.

Summer & Fall

  • Brandon Fourth of July Celebration - The community hosts its own Independence Day festivities with fireworks, food, and family activities.
  • Brandon Holiday Parade (December) - A hometown holiday parade that draws residents from across the community. It's the kind of event that gives Brandon its small-town-within-a-big-metro feel.

Between Gasparilla, the Strawberry Festival, the State Fair, and local Brandon events, there's something on the calendar almost every month - and most of it is within a 20-minute drive.

Is Brandon FL a Good Place to Live?

Everything in this guide points to the same conclusion: Brandon is a community where you can live a full, active, well-connected life without the costs and congestion of downtown Tampa. You've got nature, entertainment, professional sports, top-tier dining, strong schools, and a central location that keeps the entire Tampa Bay region within easy reach.

For a deeper look at safety data and livability metrics, read our guide on whether Brandon FL is safe. And if you're seriously considering a move, our Brandon FL relocation guide walks you through everything from school zones to commute times to housing costs.

Frequently Asked Questions About Things to Do in Brandon FL

What is there to do in Brandon FL for families?

Brandon is loaded with family-friendly options. Locally, you have parks like Lithia Springs and Lettuce Lake, entertainment venues like Main Event and Dave & Buster's, and strong youth sports leagues. Within a short drive, families can access ZooTampa at Lowry Park, the Glazer Children's Museum, MOSI, Busch Gardens, and Legoland in Winter Haven. It's one of the most family-oriented communities in the Tampa Bay area.

How far is Brandon FL from the beach?

Clearwater Beach is approximately 40 minutes from Brandon, and St. Pete Beach is about 45 minutes away. Both are consistently ranked among the best beaches in the United States. Beach trips from Brandon are easily doable as a half-day or full-day outing.

Are there good hiking and biking trails near Brandon FL?

Yes - and some of them are exceptional. Alafia River State Park features world-class mountain biking trails. Hillsborough River State Park offers miles of hiking through diverse Florida ecosystems. Edward Medard Conservation Park and Lettuce Lake Park provide additional trail options for all skill levels.

What professional sports teams are near Brandon FL?

Brandon residents have easy access to four professional sports teams: the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (NFL), Tampa Bay Lightning (NHL), Tampa Bay Rays (MLB), and Tampa Bay Rowdies (USL soccer). Raymond James Stadium and Amalie Arena are both about 20 minutes from Brandon. USF Bulls NCAA athletics are also nearby.

Is Brandon FL a good place for outdoor recreation?

Brandon is one of the best suburbs in the Tampa Bay area for outdoor recreation. Between Hillsborough River State Park, Alafia River State Park, Lithia Springs Park, Lettuce Lake Park, and Edward Medard Conservation Park, residents have access to canoeing, kayaking, swimming, fishing, mountain biking, hiking, and camping - all within a short drive.

What is the biggest mall near Brandon FL?

Westfield Brandon is the largest mall in the Tampa Bay area, located right in Brandon. It features over 150 stores and restaurants, including anchors like Macy's, Dillard's, and JCPenney.

How far is Brandon FL from Disney World?

Walt Disney World in Orlando is approximately 60 minutes from Brandon via I-4. It's a manageable day trip, and many Brandon residents hold annual passes for regular visits. Legoland in Winter Haven is even closer at about 45 minutes.

What are the best seasonal events near Brandon FL?

The top seasonal events include the Gasparilla Pirate Festival in Tampa (January), the Florida State Fair (February), the Plant City Strawberry Festival (February/March), Brandon's own Fourth of July celebration, and the Brandon Holiday Parade in December. Most are within a 20-minute drive.

Ready to Make Brandon FL Home?

If this guide has you thinking seriously about living in Brandon - or if you're already here and ready to find a home that puts you closer to the things you love - I'd be glad to help. I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I specialize in helping people buy and sell homes across the Brandon, Riverview, Valrico, and greater Tampa Bay area.

I don't just help you find a house. I help you find the right neighborhood, the right commute, the right parks, and the right lifestyle fit. That's what this guide is all about - and it's how I approach every client relationship.

Whether you're browsing from out of state or driving around Brandon this weekend, reach out anytime. No pressure, no obligation - just honest, local insight from someone who knows this area inside and out.

title: New Construction Homes in Brandon FL: Builder Guide & What to Know

content:
Quick Answer

Where can you buy new construction homes in Brandon FL?

New construction in Brandon FL is available in communities like La Collina, Rivercrest, and several infill developments, with prices starting in the mid-0Ks from builders like Lennar, DR Horton, and Taylor Morrison. Expect CDD fees in most new communities. Learn about CDD fees in Florida, browse new construction across Tampa Bay, and search Brandon homes for sale.

What's in This Guide ▼

  2. Which Builders Are Active in the Brandon and Tampa Bay Area?

  10. Sources and References
  11. Ready to Tour New Construction Homes in Brandon FL?

New construction homes in Brandon FL are available across dozens of communities in the greater Brandon, Riverview, Valrico, and Lithia areas, with prices ranging from the low $280s to over $800K depending on the builder and community. Major national builders like Lennar, D.R. Horton, Ryan Homes, Taylor Morrison, Meritage Homes, M/I Homes, Pulte Homes, and Toll Brothers all have active communities within a short drive of Brandon - giving you more options than almost any other suburb in the Tampa Bay metro. I've walked hundreds of new construction sites with buyers throughout this area, and I can tell you firsthand: buying new construction is a completely different process than buying a resale home, and most buyers don't realize that until they're already in over their heads.

This guide covers everything you need to know about buying a new construction home in the Brandon FL area: which builders are active, what communities are available, the true cost beyond the base price, common mistakes to avoid, and why having your own real estate agent - one who represents you, not the builder - is one of the smartest decisions you'll make. Whether you're a first-time home buyer in Brandon or upgrading to a larger home for your growing family, this is the guide I wish every buyer had before walking into a model home.

Get New Construction GuidanceSee New Builds

Why Is New Construction So Popular in Brandon FL?

Brandon and the surrounding communities have experienced a surge in new construction over the past decade, and the demand shows no signs of slowing. Here's why more and more buyers are choosing to build rather than buy resale:

  • Limited resale inventory: The greater Brandon area continues to deal with tight resale inventory. When there aren't enough existing homes to go around, new construction fills the gap - and builders have responded by developing communities in every direction around Brandon.
  • Modern floor plans: Today's new construction homes feature open-concept layouts, larger owner's suites, bigger pantries, home offices, flex rooms, and multi-slide glass doors that just weren't standard 10-15 years ago. If you've been touring older homes and feeling like the layouts are dated, new construction solves that immediately.
  • Energy efficiency: New homes are built to the latest Florida energy codes, which means better insulation, impact-rated windows, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and in many cases solar panel packages. That translates to lower TECO bills - something every Brandon homeowner cares about during a Florida summer.
  • Builder warranties: Most national builders offer a 1-year bumper-to-bumper warranty, a 2-year systems warranty (plumbing, electrical, HVAC), and a 10-year structural warranty. That's peace of mind you simply don't get with a resale home.
  • Customization: Depending on when you buy during the construction process, you may get to choose your lot, floor plan, exterior elevation, interior finishes, cabinet styles, countertop materials, flooring, and more. There's something genuinely exciting about designing your home from the ground up.
  • No renovation needed: Everything is brand new. No worrying about a 15-year-old roof, aging water heater, or outdated electrical panel. You move in and everything works - and it's all under warranty.

The greater Brandon area - including Riverview, Valrico, Lithia, and the Boyette corridor - has become one of the most active new construction markets in all of Tampa Bay. Between the school quality, the commute access, and the cost of living in Brandon, it's easy to see why builders keep buying land here.

Which Builders Are Active in the Brandon and Tampa Bay Area?

One of the biggest advantages of buying new construction near Brandon is the sheer number of builders competing for your business. Competition means better pricing, more incentives, and more floor plan options. Here's a breakdown of the major builders you'll encounter in the greater Brandon area:

Note: Price ranges are approximate and change frequently based on incentives, lot availability, and market conditions. For up-to-date pricing on any builder or community, call or text me at (813) 733-7907.

Quick Builder-by-Builder Breakdown

Lennar is one of the most active builders in the Brandon/Riverview area. Their "Everything's Included" (EI) model bundles upgrades like quartz countertops, stainless steel appliances, and smart home features into the base price. This makes comparing prices easier - what you see is generally close to what you'll pay. Lennar tends to build in larger master-planned communities with resort-style amenities.

D.R. Horton is the nation's largest homebuilder by volume, and their presence near Brandon is massive. They offer everything from their Express Series (entry-level, smaller footprints) to their Emerald Series (higher-end finishes). D.R. Horton is often the most aggressive with closing cost incentives when you use their preferred lender.

Ryan Homes typically offers some of the most competitive base pricing in the area. They're a good option for first-time buyers who want a single-family home without stretching their budget. Just keep in mind that the base models are fairly basic - upgrades at the design center add up quickly.

Taylor Morrison targets the move-up buyer who wants a step above entry-level. Their standard finishes tend to be higher quality than what you'd get from budget-focused builders, and their communities often feature premium amenity packages. They've been active in the Waterset and Lithia-area communities.

Meritage Homes has built their brand around energy efficiency. Many of their homes come with solar panels, spray foam insulation, and ENERGY STAR certifications as standard features. If keeping your utility bills low is a priority - and it should be in Florida - Meritage is worth a close look.

M/I Homes falls in the mid-range and offers solid design flexibility. They've been active in the Boyette corridor and in Waterset. Their communities tend to be well-located with good school zones.

Pulte Homes / Del Webb covers two demographics: Pulte builds family-oriented communities, while Del Webb focuses on 55+ active adult living. Both brands are under the PulteGroup umbrella. If you're an active adult looking for a low-maintenance lifestyle with clubhouse amenities, golf, and social clubs, Del Webb communities in the area are worth touring.

Toll Brothers is the luxury play. If your budget is $500K+ and you want premium finishes, larger homesites, and architectural details that stand out from the production-builder look, Toll Brothers delivers. Their communities in the Lithia and South Hillsborough area offer some of the most upscale new construction near Brandon.

What New Construction Communities Are Available Near Brandon?

The greater Brandon area is surrounded by new construction communities in virtually every direction. Here's how the landscape breaks down by area, followed by a reference table:

Explore Tampa Bay Communities

The Boyette corridor, running along Boyette Road south and east of Brandon, has exploded with new development. Multiple builders are active here, and the area benefits from strong school zones and proximity to both Brandon and Riverview shopping. Communities here tend to be newer master-planned neighborhoods with CDD fees, amenity centers, and community pools. This is one of the most popular areas I take buyers who want new construction with top-rated schools.

Riverview / South Brandon Overlap

The line between "South Brandon" and "Riverview" is blurry - many communities that feel like Brandon are technically in Riverview's ZIP codes. This area along US-301 and the I-75 corridor is where you'll find the highest concentration of new construction, with communities from nearly every major builder. Price points here tend to be the most accessible in the area, making it a prime target for first-time buyers.

FishHawk Newer Phases

FishHawk Ranch is a well-established master-planned community that many families already know for its A-rated schools and resort-style amenities. While much of FishHawk is built out, newer phases and adjacent communities continue to offer new construction options. Prices here tend to be higher than entry-level Riverview communities, but you're paying for the FishHawk school zone, trail system, and community infrastructure. For more on this area, see my guide to the best neighborhoods in Brandon for families.

Lithia Area

Lithia sits southeast of Brandon and offers a more spacious, semi-rural feel with larger lots and higher price points. Builders like Toll Brothers and Taylor Morrison have targeted this area for their move-up and luxury lines. If you want new construction but also want acreage and a less "subdivision" feel, Lithia delivers.

Valrico New Developments

Valrico, directly east of Brandon, has seen pockets of new development - though less large-scale than Riverview. Smaller infill communities and custom builders are more common here. Valrico's appeal is its established neighborhoods, larger lots, and strong school zones without the CDD fees that come with the big master-planned communities.

New Construction Community Reference Table

Below is a snapshot of some of the active new construction communities in the greater Brandon area. Community availability and pricing change frequently - call me at (813) 733-7907 for the latest inventory and incentives.
