title: Is Largo FL a Good Place to Live? What Buyers Should Know in 2026
excerpt: Quick Answer Is Largo FL a good place to live? Yes - Largo is one of the best value picks in Pinellas County for 2026.
content:
Quick Answer

Is Largo FL a good place to live?

Yes - Largo is one of the best value picks in Pinellas County for 2026. Sitting in central Pinellas, Largo puts you 15-25 minutes from Clearwater Beach and Indian Rocks Beach while keeping home prices well below Clearwater and St. Petersburg. Add in no state income tax, 150+ acres of parks, the Florida Botanical Gardens, and the Pinellas Trail right through town, and you get a lifestyle that punches above its price point. Explore Largo homes for sale, check out the best neighborhoods in Largo, and review the Largo housing market.

What's in This Guide ▼
  1. Key Takeaways
  2. Where Is Largo FL?
  3. What Are the Pros of Living in Largo?
  4. What Are the Cons and Trade-Offs?
  5. How Much Does It Cost to Live in Largo?
  6. How Are the Schools in Largo?
  7. Is Largo FL Safe?
  8. What Is There to Do in Largo?
  9. Who Is Largo Best For?
  10. Largo vs Clearwater vs St. Pete vs Seminole
  11. Frequently Asked Questions

Largo FL flies under the radar compared to its flashier neighbors, and that's exactly why smart buyers are paying attention to it in 2026. With a population of roughly 84,000, Largo is the fourth-largest city in Pinellas County and sits in a geographic sweet spot - close enough to the Gulf beaches and downtown St. Petersburg to enjoy both, but priced significantly lower than either. I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've been helping buyers navigate the market for over 23 years. This guide gives you the honest breakdown on what it's actually like to live in Largo - the good, the trade-offs, and who this city is the best fit for.

Quick FactsLargo Details
Population~84,000 (2024 estimate)
CountyPinellas County
Median Home Price~$340,000-$370,000 (2026)
Distance to Beach15-25 minutes to Clearwater Beach and Indian Rocks Beach
State Income TaxNone - Florida has no state income tax
Key EmployersLargo Medical Center, Pinellas County government, retail and healthcare sectors
School DistrictPinellas County Schools (choice/magnet program)
Parks150+ acres including Largo Central Park, Botanical Gardens, Pinellas Trail

Key Takeaways - Is Largo FL a Good Place to Live?

Key Takeaways

  • Largo sits in the center of Pinellas County, giving you quick access to beaches, St. Pete, and Tampa without paying premium prices
  • Median home prices in Largo run $50,000-$100,000+ less than Clearwater and St. Petersburg for comparable properties
  • The Pinellas Trail, Florida Botanical Gardens, and Largo Central Park make this one of the best park systems in the county
  • Pinellas County Schools runs an open-choice program, letting families apply to magnet and specialty schools countywide
  • No state income tax in Florida means more take-home pay, which is a major draw for people relocating from the Northeast and Midwest
  • Flood zones and insurance costs are real factors - some parts of Largo sit in FEMA flood zones that require separate flood insurance
  • Largo is car-dependent with limited public transit, so plan on driving for most errands and commuting

Where Is Largo FL?

Largo occupies a central position in Pinellas County, the densely populated peninsula that forms the western edge of the Tampa Bay area. The city is bordered by Clearwater to the north, Seminole to the east, Pinellas Park to the south, and Belleair/Belleair Bluffs to the west. That central location is one of Largo's biggest selling points.

From most parts of Largo, you're 15-25 minutes from the Gulf beaches (Clearwater Beach, Indian Rocks Beach, Redington Beach), 20-30 minutes from downtown St. Petersburg, and about 35-45 minutes from downtown Tampa via the Courtney Campbell Causeway or Howard Frankland Bridge. US-19 runs along the western edge of the city, and East Bay Drive/Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard provide major east-west access. I-275 is accessible within about 10-15 minutes from most Largo neighborhoods.

Pinellas County is the most densely populated county in Florida, and Largo reflects that - this is suburban living, not rural acreage. Lots tend to be compact, neighborhoods are established, and you're never far from commercial corridors. That density also means you have grocery stores, medical facilities, and restaurants within a short drive from anywhere in the city.

What Are the Pros of Living in Largo?

Beach Proximity Without Beach Prices

This is the number-one reason buyers choose Largo over the coastal cities. Living in Clearwater Beach or Redington Shores means paying a premium - often $200,000-$500,000+ more for comparable square footage. Largo gives you a 15-25 minute drive to some of the best Gulf beaches in Florida while keeping your housing costs manageable. You get the beach lifestyle without the beach mortgage.

Affordability Compared to Neighbors

Largo's median home price sits well below Clearwater, St. Petersburg, and Seminole. In 2026, you can still find solid 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom single-family homes in the $300,000-$400,000 range in Largo. That same home in St. Pete or Clearwater would likely run $400,000-$550,000 or more. For a detailed cost analysis, check out my cost of living in Largo FL guide.

Outstanding Parks and Green Space

Largo has one of the strongest park systems in Pinellas County. Largo Central Park is a 70-acre recreation complex with athletic fields, a performing arts center, playgrounds, walking trails, and a disc golf course. The Florida Botanical Gardens (also in Largo) covers 182 acres and features themed gardens, nature trails, and free admission. The Pinellas Trail - a 75-mile paved recreational trail stretching from Tarpon Springs to St. Petersburg - runs directly through Largo, making it ideal for cyclists, runners, and walkers.

Downtown Redevelopment

Largo has been investing in its downtown core around the Largo Central Park area. The city has added mixed-use developments, improved streetscaping, and attracted new restaurants and small businesses. It's not downtown St. Pete - and it's not trying to be - but the trajectory is positive. For buyers looking at long-term appreciation, neighborhoods near downtown Largo could benefit as redevelopment continues.

No State Income Tax

Florida has no state income tax, which is a significant financial advantage - especially for people relocating from states like New York, New Jersey, Illinois, or California. Depending on your income, this can mean $5,000-$20,000+ in annual savings. That extra money can go directly toward your mortgage, savings, or enjoying the Florida lifestyle.

What Are the Cons and Trade-Offs?

Car-Dependent Living

Like most of the Tampa Bay metro, Largo requires a car for daily life. PSTA (Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority) runs bus routes through the area, but service is limited and slow compared to driving. If you're coming from a city with robust public transit, this is an adjustment. Plan on driving to the grocery store, to work, and to the beach.

Flood Zones and Insurance Costs

Parts of Largo - particularly areas near Allen's Creek, Cross Bayou Canal, and the western portions closer to the Intracoastal - sit in FEMA-designated flood zones. Properties in AE or VE flood zones require separate flood insurance, which can add $1,500-$5,000+ per year to your housing costs depending on the zone and elevation. Homeowners insurance in Florida is already expensive, and adding flood insurance compounds that. I strongly recommend checking flood zone status before making an offer on any Largo property. My Pinellas County flood zone guide covers this in detail.

No Waterfront Downtown

Largo is an inland city. Unlike St. Petersburg with its waterfront parks or Clearwater with its beach boardwalk, Largo's downtown doesn't have a water feature as a focal point. The Largo Central Park area is attractive and growing, but if a waterfront lifestyle is a priority, you'll be driving to the coast for that experience.

Aging Housing Stock

Many homes in Largo were built in the 1960s-1980s. That means concrete block construction (which is good for hurricanes) but also older roofs, older plumbing, older electrical systems, and potentially outdated floor plans. Budget for updates and inspections. Newer construction exists but is limited compared to areas like Wesley Chapel or Riverview where builders have more land to develop.

How Much Does It Cost to Live in Largo?

Largo's cost of living runs slightly below the national average and noticeably below the coastal Pinellas cities. Housing is the biggest factor - you'll save meaningfully on purchase price compared to Clearwater, St. Pete, and Dunedin while still being within 15-30 minutes of all the same amenities and employers.

Expense CategoryLargo Estimate
Median Home Price$340,000-$370,000
Property Tax Rate~1.0-1.1% of assessed value (with homestead)
Homeowners Insurance$3,000-$6,000+/year depending on age, roof, and location
Flood Insurance (if required)$1,500-$5,000+/year in flood zones
Utilities$250-$400/month (electric, water, sewer, trash)
State Income Tax$0 - Florida has none

For the full breakdown including groceries, transportation, healthcare, and how Largo compares to other Pinellas County cities, read my cost of living in Largo FL guide.

How Are the Schools in Largo?

Largo is served by Pinellas County Schools, which is one of the largest school districts in Florida. The district operates an open-choice program that allows families to apply to any school in the county - not just the one in their neighborhood zone. This is a major advantage for families with school-age children, because it means your home address doesn't lock you into a single school.

Schools zoned within the Largo area include Largo Middle School, Largo High School, Mildred Helms Elementary, Ridgecrest Elementary, and several others. Ratings vary by campus. Pinellas County also offers highly rated magnet programs - including STEM academies, International Baccalaureate (IB), and performing arts programs - that Largo residents can apply to regardless of zone.

Private school options in the area include Blessed Sacrament Catholic School, Indian Rocks Christian School, and several others within a short drive. If school quality is a top priority, I recommend touring specific campuses and checking current ratings on the Pinellas County Schools website before buying.

Is Largo FL Safe?

Largo's overall crime rate is comparable to other mid-size Florida cities in the Tampa Bay metro. Like any city of 84,000 people, crime rates vary significantly by neighborhood. The northern and eastern sections of Largo - closer to Belleair and Seminole - tend to have lower crime rates, while areas along the US-19 corridor see more property crime and incidents typical of commercial corridors.

The Largo Police Department is responsive and well-staffed relative to the city's size. Residential neighborhoods - particularly established subdivisions away from major commercial strips - are generally safe and quiet. When I work with buyers in Largo, I always recommend driving the specific neighborhood at different times of day (morning, evening, weekend) to get a firsthand feel for the area before committing.

What Is There to Do in Largo?

Largo has more to offer than most people expect. Here are the highlights.

  • Largo Central Park - 70 acres of recreation including athletic fields, walking trails, playgrounds, a disc golf course, and the Largo Central Park Performing Arts Center, which hosts concerts, movies, and community events year-round.
  • Florida Botanical Gardens - 182 acres of themed gardens, nature trails, butterfly gardens, and seasonal displays including the Holiday Lights event every winter. Free admission makes this a regular stop for residents.
  • Pinellas Trail - This 75-mile paved trail runs right through Largo and connects to Clearwater, Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, St. Petersburg, and beyond. Cyclists, joggers, and dog walkers use it daily.
  • Heritage Village - A 21-acre living history museum in Largo with 30+ preserved historic structures and exhibits documenting Pinellas County's history. Free admission.
  • Beach Access - Indian Rocks Beach, Indian Shores, and Clearwater Beach are all 15-25 minutes away. Sand Key Park and Fred Howard Park offer additional options.
  • Restaurants and Breweries - Largo's food scene includes everything from local seafood spots to craft breweries. The area around West Bay Drive and Indian Rocks Road has a growing selection of independent restaurants.
  • Golf - Largo has multiple golf courses including Largo Golf Course (public, 18-hole) and several private and semi-private options nearby.

Who Is Largo Best For?

Based on the buyers I work with in Pinellas County, Largo tends to be the best fit for these groups.

  • Retirees - The combination of no state income tax, affordable housing, excellent parks, mild winters, and close beach access makes Largo a strong retirement destination. Many retirees from the Northeast and Midwest settle in Largo specifically because they get the Florida beach lifestyle without paying Clearwater or Naples prices.
  • Families - Pinellas County's school choice program gives families flexibility. Largo's parks and recreation programs for kids are excellent. The Botanical Gardens and Heritage Village are free, and there's always something happening at Largo Central Park. The lower home prices mean more square footage for the same budget compared to neighboring cities.
  • First-Time Buyers - If you want to buy in Pinellas County but can't stomach $450,000+ for a starter home in St. Pete or Clearwater, Largo is where you should be looking. You can find move-in ready 3-bedroom homes in the low $300Ks here. Search Largo homes for sale to see current inventory.
  • Beach Lovers on a Budget - If Gulf beach access is non-negotiable but your budget can't handle beachfront prices, Largo gives you the closest thing to it. A 15-minute drive to Indian Rocks Beach is close enough to make evening sunsets a weeknight activity instead of a weekend event.
  • Remote Workers - If your office is your home, Largo's lower housing costs let you get more space for the same money. You still have easy access to Tampa, St. Pete, and the beaches for entertainment and dining when you're off the clock.

Largo is not the best fit if you want walkable urban living (look at downtown St. Pete), waterfront property (look at Gulfport, Indian Rocks, or Clearwater Beach), or brand-new construction neighborhoods with modern amenities (look at Wesley Chapel or Riverview). For more neighborhood-specific guidance, see my best neighborhoods in Largo guide.

Largo vs Clearwater vs St. Pete vs Seminole

How does Largo stack up against its closest competitors in Pinellas County? Here's a side-by-side comparison of the livability factors that matter most to buyers.

FactorLargoClearwaterSt. PetersburgSeminole
Median Home Price$340K-$370K$400K-$475K$420K-$500K$380K-$430K
Beach Distance15-25 min5-15 min15-30 min10-20 min
WalkabilityLow - car neededLow-MediumMedium-High (downtown)Low - car needed
Nightlife/DiningGrowing - casual diningGood - beach/downtown sceneExcellent - best in countyLimited - mostly residential
Parks/RecreationExcellent - Botanical Gardens, Pinellas TrailGood - beach parksExcellent - waterfront, trailsGood - park system
Flood RiskMixed - check by propertyHigher - coastal exposureHigher - peninsulaMixed - check by property
Best ForBudget-conscious, families, retireesBeach lovers, tourists-turned-residentsYoung professionals, culture seekersQuiet suburban families

Largo wins on affordability and parks. St. Pete wins on walkability and culture. Clearwater wins on beach proximity. Seminole wins on quiet residential neighborhoods. The right choice depends entirely on your priorities and budget. For current listings in any of these areas, visit REMAX Largo or browse Pinellas County homes for sale.

Largo FL - Frequently Asked Questions

Is Largo FL a good place to retire?

Yes. Largo is one of the better retirement destinations in Pinellas County. No state income tax keeps more of your pension and Social Security in your pocket. Home prices are lower than Clearwater and St. Pete, the parks system is outstanding, healthcare access is strong (Largo Medical Center and multiple clinics nearby), and the beaches are 15-25 minutes away. Many retirees relocate from the Northeast and Midwest to Largo specifically for this combination of factors.

What is the average home price in Largo FL in 2026?

The median home price in Largo in 2026 is approximately $340,000-$370,000 for single-family homes. Condos and townhomes start lower, typically in the $180,000-$280,000 range. Prices vary significantly by neighborhood, home size, age, and proximity to flood zones. For the latest market data, check the Largo housing market report.

How far is Largo from the beach?

Most parts of Largo are 15-25 minutes from the nearest Gulf beach. Indian Rocks Beach and Indian Shores are the closest beach communities to western Largo. Clearwater Beach is about 20-30 minutes from central Largo. The drive time depends on traffic and which part of Largo you're in - neighborhoods on the western side of the city are closer to the coast.

Is Largo FL in a flood zone?

Some parts of Largo are in FEMA-designated flood zones, but not all. Flood risk varies property by property. Areas near Allen's Creek, Cross Bayou Canal, and the western portions of the city closer to the Intracoastal Waterway tend to have higher flood risk. Many Largo neighborhoods are in Zone X (minimal flood risk) and do not require flood insurance. Always check the specific FEMA flood zone for any property before making an offer. See my Pinellas County flood zone guide for maps and details.

What are the best neighborhoods in Largo FL?

The most popular neighborhoods in Largo include Bardmoor (upscale, gated, golf course), Belcher Road area (central, convenient), West Bay Drive corridor (near restaurants and parks), and the neighborhoods bordering Seminole and Belleair (quieter, higher-end). Each neighborhood has a different feel and price point. My best neighborhoods in Largo guide breaks them down in detail.

Does Largo have good schools?

Largo schools range from average to above-average within Pinellas County. The biggest advantage is the county's open-choice enrollment program, which lets families apply to any public school in the district - including highly rated magnet programs for STEM, IB, and performing arts. This means your address doesn't limit your school options the way it does in most Florida counties.

Is Largo FL safe to live in?

Largo's crime rates are comparable to other mid-size Florida cities. Residential neighborhoods away from the US-19 commercial corridor are generally safe and quiet. The Largo Police Department maintains a visible presence. As with any city, safety varies by neighborhood - I always recommend visiting a neighborhood at multiple times of day before buying.

How does Largo compare to St. Petersburg for buyers?

Largo is more affordable - expect to save $50,000-$150,000+ on comparable homes. St. Pete offers better walkability, a stronger dining and nightlife scene, and waterfront parks. Largo offers better parks and recreation (Botanical Gardens, Pinellas Trail access), lower insurance costs (fewer flood zone properties), and more square footage per dollar. Both are excellent choices in Pinellas County - it comes down to lifestyle priorities and budget.

title: Schools in Carrollwood FL: Complete Guide for Families (2025-2026)
excerpt: QUICK ANSWER What are the best schools in Carrollwood FL? Carrollwood is zoned for some of the top-rated public schools in Hillsborough County, including...
content:
QUICK ANSWER

What are the best schools in Carrollwood FL?

Carrollwood is zoned for some of the top-rated public schools in Hillsborough County, including Steinbrenner High School (A-rated), Sickles High School (A-rated with IB program), and several strong elementary and middle schools. The area also has excellent private options like Carrollwood Day School (Pre-K through 12th grade). Schools are a major reason families choose to buy in Carrollwood, making it one of the best Tampa suburbs for families. Read the full Carrollwood community guide for more on what makes this area ideal for families with children.

What's in This Guide ▼

Key Takeaways

  • Steinbrenner High School is the crown jewel - consistently A-rated and one of the best public high schools in Hillsborough County
  • Sickles High School offers an International Baccalaureate (IB) program and is also A-rated
  • Gaither High School serves parts of northwest Carrollwood with strong academics and athletics
  • Elementary options include Carrollwood Elementary, Essrig Elementary, and several other well-rated schools
  • Adams Middle and Martinez Middle are the primary middle school options for the area
  • Carrollwood Day School is the top private option - Pre-K through 12th grade, located in the Village
  • School zoning depends on your specific street address, not just ZIP code - always verify before buying

Jump To

  1. Why Schools Drive Home Values in Carrollwood
  2. High Schools Serving Carrollwood
  3. Middle Schools Serving Carrollwood
  4. Elementary Schools Serving Carrollwood
  5. Carrollwood School Ratings at a Glance
  6. Private and Charter School Options
  7. How to Verify School Zoning Before You Buy
  8. How School Zones Affect Home Prices
  9. Frequently Asked Questions

Why Schools Drive Home Values in Carrollwood

In my 23 years of selling real estate, I have seen one factor consistently outweigh almost everything else in a buyer's decision: school quality. Carrollwood is a prime example. Families routinely target this area specifically because of its school zones, and that sustained demand is one of the key reasons property values here have remained strong even during market corrections.

Hillsborough County is the 7th largest school district in the United States, with more than 230,000 students. Within that enormous system, the schools serving Carrollwood consistently rank among the top performers. This is not a coincidence - it is the result of strong community involvement, experienced faculty, and a tax base that supports school programs and facilities.

For families considering a home purchase in the Tampa Bay area, understanding the school landscape is critical. This guide covers every school zoned for Carrollwood neighborhoods across ZIP codes 33618, 33624, and 33625.

High Schools Serving Carrollwood

Steinbrenner High School

Grade: A | Enrollment: ~2,700 | Opened: 2009 | Location: 5575 W Lutz Lake Fern Rd

Steinbrenner High School is the marquee school for the Carrollwood area and one of the highest-performing public high schools in all of Hillsborough County. Named after the late George Steinbrenner (longtime New York Yankees owner who lived in Tampa), the school opened in 2009 and has earned an A rating from the Florida Department of Education in nearly every year since.

Steinbrenner serves students from Carrollwood Village, portions of Northdale, parts of Westchase, and sections of Lutz. The school offers a comprehensive curriculum including:

  • Advanced Placement (AP) courses - 25+ AP classes across all disciplines
  • AICE (Cambridge) program - An accelerated international curriculum offering college credit
  • STEM programs - Robotics, engineering, and computer science tracks
  • Athletics - Competitive programs in baseball, football, swimming, soccer, and more
  • Fine Arts - Award-winning band, chorus, theater, and visual arts programs

The Steinbrenner zone is the single most requested school zone by buyers I work with. Homes zoned for Steinbrenner typically sell faster and at a premium compared to homes zoned for other high schools in the area.

Sickles High School

Grade: A | Enrollment: ~2,400 | Opened: 2004 | Location: 7950 Gu Hwy

Sickles High School is another outstanding option serving the Carrollwood area, particularly the eastern portions of Carrollwood Village, the Lake Magdalene neighborhood, and parts of the 33618 ZIP code. Sickles has earned consistent A ratings and is known for its strong academic rigor.

The standout program at Sickles is the International Baccalaureate (IB) program. The IB diploma is recognized worldwide and is considered one of the most challenging and respected pre-college programs available. Students who complete the full IB diploma often enter college with significant credit and a competitive advantage in admissions.

Sickles also offers strong AP courses, career and technical education (CTE) programs, and competitive athletics. The school has produced notable alumni in academics, athletics, and the arts. For families who specifically want the IB program, being zoned for Sickles can be a decisive factor in their home search.

Gaither High School

Grade: B | Enrollment: ~2,200 | Opened: 1970 | Location: 16200 N Dale Mabry Hwy

Gaither High School serves portions of northwest Carrollwood, primarily in the 33625 ZIP code and parts of Northdale. While Gaither does not carry the same cachet as Steinbrenner or Sickles, it is a solid school with a long history in the community. The school has undergone significant renovations and improvements in recent years.

Gaither offers AP courses, a strong JROTC program, and competitive athletic teams. The school also has career-focused academies that prepare students for specific industries. For buyers on a tighter budget, the Gaither zone often offers the most affordable home prices in the Carrollwood area - making it an excellent entry point for first-time home buyers.

Middle Schools Serving Carrollwood

Adams Middle School

Grade: B | Enrollment: ~1,200 | Location: 10201 N Boulevard

Adams Middle School serves much of the core Carrollwood area, including portions of Carrollwood Village and surrounding neighborhoods. The school offers gifted programs, advanced math tracks, and a variety of electives including band, chorus, art, and technology. Adams feeds into both Steinbrenner and Sickles high schools depending on the student's address, making it a strong feeder school for two of the area's best high schools.

Martinez Middle School

Grade: B | Enrollment: ~1,400 | Location: 5515 W Lutz Lake Fern Rd

Martinez Middle School primarily serves the northern portions of Carrollwood, Northdale, and adjacent areas. The school offers Cambridge AICE courses at the middle school level, which provides an accelerated pathway for students heading to Steinbrenner's Cambridge program. Martinez also has strong STEM offerings and active extracurricular programs. It is one of the larger middle schools in the area and feeds primarily into Steinbrenner High School.

Elementary Schools Serving Carrollwood

Several elementary schools serve the Carrollwood area, each with its own strengths and character. Here are the primary options:

Carrollwood Elementary School

Grade: B | Enrollment: ~650 | Location: 12505 N Dale Mabry Hwy

The namesake elementary school of the community, Carrollwood Elementary has been serving families since the 1970s. The school offers gifted programs, ESE services, and a strong reading curriculum. Its central location within Carrollwood makes it walkable for many families in the Village and surrounding neighborhoods.

Essrig Elementary School

Grade: A | Enrollment: ~750 | Location: 11515 Carrollwood Dr

Essrig Elementary consistently earns A ratings and is one of the most sought-after elementary schools in the Carrollwood area. The school is located within Carrollwood Village and benefits from high levels of parent involvement and community support. Essrig has a strong gifted program and is known for its reading and math achievement scores.

Deer Park Elementary School

Grade: B | Enrollment: ~600 | Location: 8440 N Ola Ave

Deer Park Elementary serves the eastern edges of the Carrollwood area near Lake Magdalene. The school offers a well-rounded curriculum with active extracurricular activities. Deer Park feeds into Adams Middle School and subsequently into Sickles High School.

Northdale Middle Magnet School (K-8)

Hillsborough County offers several magnet school options that Carrollwood families can apply to. These include choice programs in STEM, performing arts, and accelerated academics. While magnet schools do not guarantee admission (they use a lottery system), they provide additional educational pathways beyond zoned schools.

Carrollwood School Ratings at a Glance

School Level FL Grade Notable Programs
Steinbrenner HS High (9-12) A 25+ AP, Cambridge AICE, STEM
Sickles HS High (9-12) A IB Diploma, AP, CTE
Gaither HS High (9-12) B AP, JROTC, Career Academies
Adams MS Middle (6-8) B Gifted, Advanced Math
Martinez MS Middle (6-8) B Cambridge AICE, STEM
Essrig Elementary Elementary (K-5) A Gifted, Strong Reading
Carrollwood Elementary Elementary (K-5) B Gifted, ESE
Deer Park Elementary Elementary (K-5) B Balanced Curriculum

Private and Charter School Options

Carrollwood Day School

Grades: Pre-K through 12 | Location: 1515 W Bearss Ave | Type: Private, College-Preparatory

Carrollwood Day School (CDS) is the premier private school in the Carrollwood area and one of the most respected private schools in the Tampa Bay region. Founded in 1981, CDS offers a rigorous college-preparatory curriculum from Pre-K through 12th grade. The school sits on a spacious campus within Carrollwood Village, featuring modern facilities including science labs, athletic fields, a performing arts center, and an aquatics center.

CDS has small class sizes (typically 15-18 students), a strong faculty-to-student ration, and a 100% college acceptance rate. The school offers AP courses, honors tracks, and a robust arts and athletics program. Annual tuition ranges from approximately $12,000-$22,000 depending on grade level. For families who prioritize private education, having CDS within the community is a significant draw.

Bell Shoals Baptist Academy

Grades: Pre-K through 8 | Type: Private, Faith-Based

Bell Shoals Baptist Academy offers a faith-based education with small class sizes and a focus on character development alongside academics. While not located directly in Carrollwood, it serves many families from the area and offers a lower-cost alternative to Carrollwood Day School. The school is known for its nurturing environment and strong sense of community.

Other Private and Charter Options

Several other options serve Carrollwood families, including Montessori schools, charter schools, and faith-based institutions within a short drive. Tampa also has county-wide magnet and choice programs that Carrollwood students can apply to, including the highly regarded Plant High School IB program (which accepts students from across the county through its magnet application).

How to Verify School Zoning Before You Buy

This is critically important and a step that too many buyers skip. In Carrollwood, school zone boundaries do not follow simple geographic lines. Two homes on the same street can be zoned for different high schools. Here is how to verify:

  1. Use the Hillsborough County School District's official school finder tool - Enter the exact street address of any home you are considering to see which schools it is zoned for at every grade level.
  2. Call the school directly - If you have any doubt, call the school's front office and give them the address. They can confirm enrollment eligibility.
  3. Check with your real estate agent - An experienced Tampa Bay real estate agent will verify school zoning as part of the home evaluation process. This is standard practice for any agent who knows the local market.
  4. Do not rely on MLS listings alone - While MLS data usually includes school information, it can occasionally be outdated or incorrect, especially after zone boundary changes.

Zone boundaries can change. The Hillsborough County School Board periodically reviews and adjusts boundaries based on enrollment patterns and new school construction. While major changes are rare in established areas like Carrollwood, it is always worth confirming with the district directly.

How School Zones Affect Home Prices

The impact of school zoning on home values in Carrollwood is measurable and significant. Based on my experience selling in this market:

  • Steinbrenner zone premium: Homes zoned for Steinbrenner High School typically sell for 5-8% more than comparable homes zoned for Gaither, even when located in similar neighborhoods.
  • Sickles IB effect: Families specifically seeking the IB program create additional demand for Sickles-zoned properties, supporting values in Lake Magdalene and eastern Carrollwood Village.
  • Elementary school impact: Homes zoned for A-rated Essrig Elementary sell faster and at higher prices than those zoned for B-rated elementary schools in the area.
  • Resale advantage: When you sell a home in a top school zone, you will always have a deeper pool of interested buyers - families will pay more to avoid private school tuition.

For perspective on the broader market dynamics, see our Florida housing market forecast. And if you are ready to start your search in a specific school zone, browse available Carrollwood homes and filter by location to find homes in your preferred zone.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best high school in Carrollwood FL?

Steinbrenner High School is generally considered the best high school serving Carrollwood. It consistently earns an A rating from the Florida DOE, offers 25+ AP courses and a Cambridge AICE program, and has strong athletics and fine arts. Sickles High School is a very close second, with the added advantage of an International Baccalaureate (IB) program that attracts families seeking globally recognized academic credentials.

Does Carrollwood have good elementary schools?

Yes. Essrig Elementary is the standout, earning consistent A ratings. Carrollwood Elementary and Deer Park Elementary are both B-rated and provide solid educational foundations with gifted programs and strong community involvement. The elementary school options in Carrollwood are among the reasons it is consistently rated one of the best Tampa suburbs for families.

How much does Carrollwood Day School cost?

Annual tuition at Carrollwood Day School ranges from approximately $12,000 for lower grades to $22,000 for upper school (grades 9-12). Financial aid and merit scholarships are available. The school has a 100% college acceptance rate and small class sizes of 15-18 students, making it a strong option for families willing to invest in private education.

Can I choose which school my child attends in Carrollwood?

Your child is assigned to schools based on your home address. However, Hillsborough County offers a magnet and choice school program that allows families to apply for admission to schools outside their zone. Acceptance is not guaranteed and is typically by lottery. If attending a specific school is essential for your family, the most reliable approach is to buy a home within that school's zone. Use the mortgage calculator to see what you can afford in your target zone.

Do school zones change in Carrollwood?

School zone boundaries are reviewed periodically by the Hillsborough County School Board. While changes in established areas like Carrollwood are uncommon, they can happen when new schools open or enrollment imbalances arise. Always verify current zoning with the district before making a purchase decision based on school assignments.

content:
Is Brandon FL a good market for rental property investors? Yes. Brandon offers a strong combination of affordable purchase prices, solid rental demand, and competitive returns. The average rent for a 3-bedroom home in Brandon ranges from $1,800 to $2,400 per month, and vacancy rates remain low due to steady population growth and proximity to Tampa employment centers. Here is what investors need to know.

3 BR / 2 BA home$1,800-$2,400Families, military

Rents in Brandon have increased approximately 30-50% over the past 5 years, driven by population growth, limited rental inventory, and rising home prices pushing more buyers into renting.

Here is a realistic investment scenario for a Brandon rental property:

Brandon's cap rates are competitive for the Tampa Bay market. When you factor in appreciation (historically 7-10% annually), total returns are strong.

High Demand, Moderate Price

  • Central Brandon (no HOA) $250K-$340K purchase, $1,800-$2,200 rent. No HOA means no rental restrictions or fees. Strong demand from families.
  • Four Winds Estates no HOA, larger lots, $280K-$345K. Rents $1,900-$2,300.
  • Alafia Estates no HOA, $275K-$350K. Popular with families wanting space.

What Are Florida Landlord-Tenant Laws?

Key Florida landlord-tenant regulations that Brandon investors should know:

  • Security deposits no statutory limit, but must be held in a separate account. Return within 15-30 days depending on claims.
  • Lease terms no minimum required by state law (HOAs may require 12-month minimum)
  • Eviction process 3-day notice for nonpayment, 7-day notice for lease violations. Court-ordered eviction typically takes 3-6 weeks.
  • Rent control Florida prohibits local rent control ordinances. Landlords can set market rates.
  • Required disclosures radon, lead paint (pre-1978), and security deposit holding method

Should I Self-Manage or Hire a Property Manager?

Brandon landlords have both options:

  • Self-management saves 8-10% of rent but requires handling tenant screening, maintenance, and legal compliance
  • Property management costs 8-10% of monthly rent plus a tenant placement fee (typically one month's rent). Handles everything from tenant screening to maintenance to evictions.

For out-of-area investors or those with multiple properties, professional management is usually worth the cost.

HOA Rental Restrictions to Watch For

Before buying a Brandon investment property in an HOA community, verify:

  • Rental caps some HOAs limit the percentage of rentals allowed
  • Minimum lease terms typically 12 months (no short-term/Airbnb)
  • Tenant approval HOA may require background checks and approval
  • Application fees $100-$250 per tenant application charged by the HOA

No-HOA properties give you maximum rental flexibility with no restrictions on tenants, lease terms, or short-term rentals.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Brandon FL a good place to invest in rental property?

Yes. Brandon offers strong fundamentals: affordable purchase prices relative to rents, low vacancy rates, steady population growth, and proximity to Tampa employment. Cap rates of 4-5% plus annual appreciation make it a solid long-term investment.

Can I do Airbnb in Brandon?

Hillsborough County allows short-term rentals but requires registration and tax collection. However, most Brandon HOAs prohibit short-term rentals. No-HOA properties offer the best opportunity for Airbnb if you choose that strategy.

What is the vacancy rate in Brandon?

Brandon's rental vacancy rate has been consistently low at 3-5%, well below the national average. Strong demand from families, military personnel, and professionals relocating to Tampa Bay keeps vacancies minimal.

What repairs should I budget for on a Brandon rental?

Budget 1-2% of the property value annually for maintenance and repairs. Common Brandon-specific items include roof maintenance (Florida weather), HVAC service (heavy use year-round), and pest control.

Do I need a real estate license to manage my own rental in Florida?

No. Florida property owners can manage their own rental properties without a license. A license is only required if you manage properties for other owners.

title: Apollo Beach vs Riverview FL: Which Community Should You Choose?
excerpt: Apollo Beach vs Riverview FL comparison covering prices, lifestyle, schools, commute, and home types. Barrett Henry, REALTOR with 23+ years of experience.
content:
Apollo Beach and Riverview are neighboring South Hillsborough County communities that attract very different buyers. Apollo Beach is defined by its waterfront canal system and bay access, while Riverview is one of Tampa Bay's largest suburban communities with extensive new construction and family amenities. Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience and helps buyers decide which community aligns with their priorities.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Factor Apollo Beach Riverview
Median Home Price$430K$390K
Waterfront AccessDeep-water canals, bayAlafia River (limited)
New ConstructionLimitedExtensive
Tampa Commute25-40 min20-35 min
School OptionsGoodExtensive
Shopping & DiningGrowingEstablished
LifestyleWaterfront / boatingSuburban / family

Which Is More Affordable?

Riverview offers lower entry prices, especially for new construction. First-time buyers and families on a budget get more house per dollar in Riverview. Apollo Beach commands a premium, especially for waterfront, but non-waterfront Apollo Beach homes are competitively priced against Riverview equivalents.

Which Has Better Schools?

Riverview has more school options simply due to its larger geographic footprint. Newsome High School in nearby Lithia is one of the highest-rated high schools in Hillsborough County and serves parts of Riverview. Apollo Beach schools are solid but the community has fewer campuses to choose from. Both areas benefit from Hillsborough County school choice programs.

Need Help Deciding Between Apollo Beach and Riverview?

Barrett Henry is a licensed Broker Associate with REMAX Collective and has 23+ years of real estate experience. Whether you are buying, selling, or investing in South Hillsborough County, get straight talk and real data.

Schedule a Free Consultation Call (813) 733-7907

Which Is Better for Families?

Riverview is the stronger pick for families who prioritize schools, nearby retail, and community size. Riverview has more parks, more restaurants, more shopping, and more kid-friendly activities. Apollo Beach is better for families who want a waterfront lifestyle, boating, fishing, and bay access are part of daily life.

Which Is Better for Commuters?

Riverview has a slight edge on commute times to downtown Tampa and Brandon, primarily due to more I-75 access points. Apollo Beach residents can use US-41 as an alternate route to South Tampa and MacDill. For MacDill AFB specifically, Apollo Beach is closer.

Which Is the Better Investment?

Both areas are solid investments. Apollo Beach waterfront properties have stronger long-term appreciation potential due to supply constraints. Riverview offers more inventory at lower entry prices, which can mean better cash-on-cash returns for rental investors. Use the mortgage calculator to compare scenarios.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Apollo Beach nicer than Riverview?

Apollo Beach and Riverview offer different lifestyles. Apollo Beach is a waterfront community with a boating culture. Riverview is a larger suburban community with more retail and schools. Neither is objectively nicer, it depends on your priorities.

Which is closer to Tampa, Apollo Beach or Riverview?

Riverview is slightly closer to downtown Tampa by approximately 5-10 minutes. Apollo Beach is closer to MacDill AFB and South Tampa via US-41.

Can you boat from Riverview?

Riverview has limited boat access through the Alafia River. Apollo Beach offers far superior boating with deep-water canals and direct Tampa Bay access.

Which has more new construction?

Riverview has significantly more new construction than Apollo Beach. Apollo Beach is largely built out while Riverview continues adding thousands of new homes annually across multiple communities.

title: Tampa Waterfront Condos for Sale 2026, Bayshore, Channelside, Harbour Island
excerpt: Browse waterfront condos in Tampa FL, Bayshore Boulevard, Channelside, Harbour Island, Davis Islands. Pricing, buildings, and what to know before buying.
content:
Quick Answer

Tampa waterfront condos range from $300K studios near Channelside to $5M+ penthouses on Bayshore Boulevard. The most active condo submarkets are Water Street Tampa, Harbour Island, Davis Islands, and downtown towers along the Hillsborough River. Flood insurance, milestone inspections, and HOA financial health are the three biggest due-diligence items for any waterfront condo purchase in Tampa Bay.

Tampa's waterfront condo market spans several distinct submarkets, each with its own character, price range, and ownership profile. Whether you want direct bay views from a high-rise, a boat slip in your building, or walking access to Water Street's restaurants and entertainment, there is a waterfront condo product for most budgets above $300K. I have helped buyers navigate this market for over two decades, and the due-diligence questions are more complex here than in any other property type.

Tampa Waterfront Condo Submarkets: What to Expect by Area

Water Street Tampa and Channelside

Water Street Tampa is Tampa's most ambitious urban development, a 50-block mixed-use district along the eastern waterfront. Buildings like The Heron and the Ritz-Carlton Residences at Water Street deliver brand-new construction with high-speed elevators, EV charging in parking garages, rooftop amenities, and concierge services. Prices in this submarket start around $600K for one-bedroom units and escalate quickly past $2M for two-bedroom and three-bedroom units with direct views of Tampa Bay and the Convention Center waterfront. HOA fees in Water Street buildings typically run $900 to $2,000 per month and include services like valet parking, fitness centers, resort-style pools, and doorman service.

Channelside proper, the neighborhood immediately adjacent, includes older towers like The Place at Channelside (built 2007), Towers of Channelside (2007), and 1000 Water Street. These offer more affordable entry points, often $350K to $700K, but carry the usual caution flags for mid-2000s construction: deferred maintenance, higher special assessment risk, and HOA financials that need careful review under Florida's condo laws.

Harbour Island

Harbour Island sits between downtown Tampa and Davis Islands, connected by a causeway. It offers a mix of single-family homes and condo buildings with protected marina access. Condo buildings like Harbour Place, Harbour House, and several mid-rise towers give buyers bay and skyline views, with prices typically ranging from $450K to $1.5M. The island's walkability, private-community feel, and proximity to Water Street make it one of the more desirable urban waterfront addresses in Tampa. HOA fees range from $600 to $1,400 per month depending on the building and amenities.

Davis Islands

Davis Islands is primarily a single-family neighborhood with some waterfront condos. The island's condo inventory is limited but includes buildings with boat slip options and direct bay access. Prices for Davis Islands condos typically start around $500K and go well into the $1M+ range. The island's character is decidedly residential, not urban, so buyers who want walkable urban amenities should look at Water Street or Harbour Island instead.

Bayshore Boulevard Towers

Bayshore Boulevard is lined with high-rise towers that offer panoramic views of Hillsborough Bay and Tampa's skyline. Buildings like The Virage Bayshore, Vue at Bayshore, and older towers like Harbour House sit along the world's longest continuous sidewalk and deliver views that justify premium pricing. Prices range from $400K for older one-bedroom units to $5M+ for large penthouse floors in newer builds. HOA fees in Bayshore towers vary widely, from $600 to over $2,500 per month, depending on building age and amenities.

Downtown Tampa and the Riverwalk

Downtown Tampa condos along the Hillsborough River include buildings like SkyPoint Tampa, Skyhouse Tampa, and Element Tampa. These are not technically bay-front but are waterfront along the River, with Riverwalk access and views of the downtown skyline. Entry prices start around $300K for studios and one-bedrooms. This submarket appeals to urban professionals and investors looking for rental income from downtown Tampa's growing tenant base.

Tampa Waterfront Condo Price Guide by Submarket (2026)

Area Entry Price Mid-Range Luxury/Penthouse HOA/Month
Water Street Tampa$600K$900K-$1.5M$2M+$900-$2,000
Channelside (older)$320K$450K-$700K$800K+$550-$1,100
Harbour Island$450K$600K-$1M$1.5M+$600-$1,400
Davis Islands$500K$700K-$1.2M$1.5M+$500-$900
Bayshore Boulevard$400K$700K-$2M$2M-$5M+$600-$2,500
Downtown Riverwalk$300K$400K-$650K$800K+$400-$900

Florida SB 4D and Milestone Inspections: What Condo Buyers Must Know

Florida Senate Bill 4D, passed after the Champlain Towers South collapse in Surfside (2021), created mandatory milestone inspection requirements for all condominium buildings three stories or taller. According to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation, buildings that are 30 years old (or 25 years if within three miles of a coastline) must complete Phase 1 milestone inspections by December 31, 2024, with Phase 2 structural integrity reserve studies required by December 31, 2024 as well. Buildings that fail Phase 1 must complete Phase 2 structural assessments and then address any life-safety deficiencies on an accelerated timeline.

This law directly affects many Channelside, Bayshore, and downtown Tampa buildings built in the 1990s and 2000s. Before purchasing any resale condo in a building over 25 years old, request the building's milestone inspection report, the structural integrity reserve study, and the most recent reserve funding disclosure. Special assessments tied to milestone compliance can run $20,000 to $100,000+ per unit in older buildings with deferred maintenance. I strongly recommend buyers review these documents before writing an offer, not after inspection.

How Is Flood Insurance Handled for Tampa Waterfront Condos?

Flood insurance for condos works differently than for single-family homes. The building's HOA typically carries a master flood insurance policy under FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) that covers the building structure and common areas up to $500,000. Individual unit owners need a separate "walls-in" or unit-owner flood policy to cover their personal property, interior improvements, and any loss assessment from the building's policy deductible.

For waterfront buildings in designated flood zones (AE or VE on FEMA's maps), the master policy premium is often substantial and built into HOA fees. When shopping for waterfront condos in Tampa, ask the HOA for a disclosure of insurance costs and whether the building has had any flood claims. Buildings along Bayshore Boulevard and Harbour Island are in Hillsborough County Flood Zone AE, meaning flood insurance is mandatory for any federally backed mortgage. Private flood insurance markets have also expanded in Florida, sometimes offering lower premiums than NFIP for newer buildings with favorable elevation certificates.

Condo Financing in Tampa Bay: Loans, Warrantability, and Jumbo Thresholds

Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable Condos

Not every Tampa condo qualifies for conventional Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac financing. A "non-warrantable" condo fails one or more agency guidelines, such as having more than 35% of units owned by a single investor, more than 35% commercial use in the building, active litigation, or inadequate reserve funding. Non-warrantable condos typically require portfolio loans or hard money, with higher down payments (20-25%+) and rates that are 0.50 to 1.25% above market. Some newer Water Street buildings have had temporary non-warrantable designations as occupancy ramps up. Always verify warrantability before assuming standard financing is available.

Jumbo Loans for Luxury Condos

For 2026, the conforming loan limit in Hillsborough County is $806,500. Condos priced above that threshold require jumbo loan financing. Jumbo loans for condos carry additional underwriting scrutiny: lenders review the building's HOA financials, pending litigation, insurance adequacy, and occupancy ratios alongside the borrower's credit and assets. Down payment minimums on jumbo condo loans are typically 20% to 25%. Use the mortgage calculator to estimate payments, and call me to connect with lenders who specialize in Tampa Bay condo financing.

FHA Condo Loans

FHA loans are available for condos in FHA-approved condo projects only. HUD maintains a searchable database of approved developments. Many Tampa waterfront condo buildings, especially in Water Street and Channelside, are not currently FHA-approved, which eliminates 3.5% down financing as an option. Buildings can apply for FHA approval or single-unit approval (for specific units in an unapproved project) if certain criteria are met. This is worth exploring for buyers with limited down payments considering lower-priced Channelside or downtown Riverwalk units.

What to Inspect in a Tampa Waterfront Condo

Balcony and Railing Condition

Salt air and humidity accelerate corrosion on concrete balconies and metal railings in Tampa's coastal environment. For buildings over 20 years old, request the milestone inspection report and any engineering assessments of balcony structural integrity. Spalling concrete and corroding rebar are red flags that can indicate expensive future assessments.

HVAC and Plumbing Inside the Unit

Individual unit HVAC systems and plumbing are typically the unit owner's responsibility, not the HOA's. Older buildings may have original plumbing and HVAC equipment that is at or past end-of-life. Budget for HVAC replacement ($4,000-$8,000 for a typical condo unit) and ask about the age of water heaters. Buildings with chilled-water central HVAC systems (where the HOA runs central cooling) eliminate some of this risk but add to HOA costs.

HOA Reserve Fund Adequacy

Florida law now requires structural integrity reserve studies for buildings three stories or taller. Beyond structure, review the full reserve study to see how funded the building is for roofing, elevators, pool resurfacing, and common-area updates. A building funded below 70% of its recommended reserve level is a caution flag. Some buildings in the 25-40% range face near-term special assessments to comply with new reserve requirements.

Tampa Waterfront Condo vs. Waterfront Single-Family: Key Trade-offs

Factor Waterfront Condo Waterfront Single-Family
Maintenance burdenLow (HOA handles exterior)High (owner responsible)
Monthly cost predictabilityLow (special assessments)Higher
Boat accessLimited (some buildings)Yes (private dock option)
Urban walkabilityHighLow to moderate
PrivacyLower (shared spaces)Higher
SecurityHigh (doorman, fob access)Depends on neighborhood
Entry price$300K-$600K$700K-$3M+

Frequently Asked Questions About Tampa Waterfront Condos

What is the cheapest waterfront condo in Tampa?

The most affordable Tampa waterfront condos are typically found in older Channelside or downtown Riverwalk buildings, with units starting around $300K to $350K for studios and one-bedrooms. These buildings carry higher due-diligence requirements: request milestone inspection reports, the reserve study, and HOA meeting minutes for the past two years before proceeding.

Do Tampa waterfront condos allow short-term rentals?

This varies entirely by building. Most residential condo buildings in Tampa prohibit short-term rentals (Airbnb, VRBO) and require minimum lease terms of 6 or 12 months. Some buildings in Channelside and downtown were built with hotel-condo hybrid structures that do allow short-term rentals under specific programs. Always verify the rental restriction language in the condo declaration before purchasing with investment intent.

How much are HOA fees for Tampa waterfront condos?

HOA fees for Tampa waterfront condos range from about $400 per month for smaller buildings with limited amenities to over $2,500 per month in full-service luxury towers with valet, concierge, pool, gym, and 24-hour security. The average for a mid-range Channelside or Harbour Island building is $600 to $1,100 per month. Also factor in any special assessment history and funded reserve percentages, which affect future assessment risk.

Is flood insurance required for Tampa waterfront condos?

If you finance the purchase with a federally backed mortgage (FHA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac) and the building is in a designated Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA), flood insurance is required. Most waterfront buildings in Tampa are in Flood Zone AE. The building's HOA policy covers the structure; you need a separate unit-owner policy for your interior and personal property. Flood insurance costs vary by building elevation and flood zone designation.

What is a milestone inspection and does it affect my condo purchase?

A milestone inspection is a mandatory structural assessment for Florida condo buildings three stories or taller, required under SB 4D (2022). Phase 1 is a visual assessment; Phase 2 (if deficiencies are found) is a more detailed engineering analysis. For buyers, the key question is: has the building completed its required inspections, and if Phase 2 was triggered, have deficiencies been remediated? Any open deficiencies or pending remediation can affect financing and create future special assessment risk. Always request these reports from the HOA before closing.

title: FishHawk FL Commute Guide: Drive Times, Routes & Tips
excerpt: FishHawk Ranch to Tampa is 30-45 min off-peak via the Selmon Expressway. MacDill AFB is 40-55 min. Brandon is 15-20 min. No public transit exists. Complete drive times table, route options (Selmon vs Lithia Pinecrest vs US-301), and MacDill commute tips for FishHawk Ranch buyers.
content:
Quick Answer

From FishHawk Ranch in Lithia FL (ZIP 33547), downtown Tampa is approximately 30 to 45 minutes off-peak via the Selmon Expressway (FL-618 Toll). MacDill AFB is 40 to 55 minutes. Brandon is 15 to 20 minutes. Rush hour adds 15 to 30 minutes to any Tampa destination. There is no public transit from FishHawk Ranch. A personal vehicle is required for all commuting.

The commute is the most common question I get from buyers considering FishHawk Ranch. The community sits in Lithia, in southeastern Hillsborough County, far enough from Tampa to feel suburban and rural, close enough to make a daily commute workable. Whether it is workable for your specific situation depends on your destination and how much commute time you can accept. Here is the honest breakdown.

FishHawk Ranch FL Drive Times to Key Destinations

According to Google Maps routing under typical off-peak conditions, here are estimated drive times from FishHawk Ranch (ZIP 33547, Lithia FL):

Best Routes from FishHawk Ranch to Tampa

Route 1: Selmon Expressway (FL-618 Toll), Fastest to Downtown

The Selmon Expressway (FL-618) is the fastest route from southeastern Hillsborough County into downtown Tampa for most FishHawk Ranch residents. The typical path is: FishHawk Blvd to US-301 North, then west on FL-618 Selmon to downtown. The Selmon has electronic tolls (E-Pass or SunPass required, cash tolls are not available). The toll cost is modest and the time savings versus I-75 or US-301 into Tampa are significant during rush hour. I always tell FishHawk Ranch buyers heading to Tampa to budget for a SunPass transponder.

Route 2: Lithia Pinecrest Road to I-75 North

Lithia Pinecrest Road runs north from FishHawk Ranch through Riverview and connects to I-75. From I-75, you can head north toward Tampa or south toward Sarasota. This route is useful for destinations on the west side of Tampa (like TPA airport via I-75 to I-275) and for destinations in the I-75 corridor. However, Lithia Pinecrest itself is a two-lane road with traffic signals and school zone slowdowns during peak hours, it is not as fast as it looks on the map during morning rush.

Route 3: US-301 North to Brandon and I-75

US-301 provides a direct route north into Brandon and then to I-75. For MacDill AFB, downtown Tampa, or South Tampa destinations, US-301 to the Selmon Expressway entry is typically the most reliable all-weather route. US-301 through Riverview has significant commercial development that creates signal delays, avoid it during peak hours if you can use Boyette Road or other parallel routes.

Is There Public Transit from FishHawk Ranch?

There is no Hillsborough Area Regional Transit (HART) bus service that provides practical commuting from FishHawk Ranch to Tampa. HART routes in Hillsborough County (gohart.org) focus on urban and suburban corridors in central and north Tampa. FishHawk Ranch in southeastern Hillsborough County is outside practical transit reach. According to HART's route maps, no direct bus service connects FishHawk Ranch addresses to Tampa destinations. A personal vehicle is required. This is a car-essential community.

MacDill AFB Commute from FishHawk Ranch

FishHawk Ranch is a popular choice for military families assigned to MacDill AFB, and for good reason. The commute is manageable and the community offers excellent schools, amenities, and a family-friendly environment. I work with many MacDill families and here is what I tell them:

Gate Routing Matters

MacDill AFB has multiple gate access points. The Dale Mabry gate versus the Gandy Blvd or other entrance options affects which approach from Tampa is most efficient from FishHawk Ranch. The Selmon Expressway to Dale Mabry South is typically the fastest route to the base's main gate. Allow 40 to 55 minutes off-peak, 55 to 70 minutes during peak morning hours, from most FishHawk Ranch addresses.

Remote Work and Hybrid Schedules

Many FishHawk Ranch residents, whether working at MacDill, downtown Tampa, or elsewhere, use hybrid work schedules that reduce the number of daily commute days. FishHawk Ranch has Spectrum and WideOpenWest (WOW) internet service available in most areas, making remote work from home fully viable. Even for non-remote workers, a 3-day office / 2-day home schedule dramatically changes the commute calculus from FishHawk Ranch.

title: FHA Homes in Valrico FL: Loan Limits, Neighborhoods, and Buyer Guide 2026
excerpt: FHA loan homes in Valrico FL: 2026 loan limit of $524,225, 3.5% down payment, neighborhoods priced under the limit, and what buyers need to know.
content:
Most homes in Valrico FL qualify for FHA financing. The 2026 FHA loan limit for Hillsborough County is $524,225 for a single-family home, and Valrico's median home price of approximately $410K-$430K sits well within that ceiling. FHA's 3.5% down payment requirement makes it one of the most accessible paths to homeownership in the area for buyers with credit scores of 580 or higher. This guide covers the loan limit, qualifying neighborhoods, MIP costs, and what FHA buyers need to know in the current Valrico market.

What Is the FHA Loan Limit in Valrico FL for 2026?

The FHA loan limit for Hillsborough County, Florida (which includes Valrico, Brandon, and Tampa) is $524,225 for a single-family home in 2026. This means FHA can finance homes up to that purchase price with 3.5% down (for borrowers with 580+ credit) or 10% down (for borrowers with 500-579 credit). The majority of Valrico's housing inventory falls within this limit, making FHA one of the most applicable financing programs in the market.

Factor FHA Details (2026)
Loan Limit (Hillsborough County)$524,225
Minimum Down Payment (580+ credit)3.5%
Minimum Down Payment (500-579 credit)10%
Upfront MIP1.75% of loan amount (financed)
Annual MIP (loan to value over 90%)0.55% annually (on 30-yr fixed)
MIP Duration (under 10% down)Life of loan
Valrico Median Home Price~$410K-$430K (2026)

Which Valrico Neighborhoods Work Well for FHA Buyers?

Valrico Forest and Valrico Groves (Under $350K)

Older sections of Valrico in the 33594 ZIP code, including Valrico Forest and similar established neighborhoods from the 1980s and 1990s, regularly have listings in the $280K-$350K range. These entry-level homes work perfectly for FHA financing. The lower price point means a smaller down payment and lower MIP costs. These neighborhoods have no HOA (or minimal HOA), which also reduces carrying costs for buyers on a budget.

Arbor Oaks, Brandon Traces, and Mid-Priced Valrico ($350K-$480K)

The broad mid-range of Valrico (most of the 33596 ZIP code) falls comfortably within FHA limits. Neighborhoods like Arbor Oaks, Brandon Traces, Copper Ridge's lower-priced sections, and similar communities offer 3-4 bedroom homes in this range. FHA 3.5% down on a $420K purchase equals $14,700 down, which is substantially less than a conventional 5% or 10% down payment.

Bloomingdale Area ($380K-$600K)

Bloomingdale (technically Brandon but closely associated with Valrico in 33596) has a wide price range. Homes in Bloomingdale's lower tier ($380K-$500K) fall within FHA limits. Upper-end Bloomingdale homes above $524,225 would require conventional financing or a larger down payment to keep the loan balance within FHA limits.

Diamond Hill and Arista (Some Units Within FHA Limits)

Diamond Hill's base-priced townhomes and smaller single-family homes can fall within the $420K-$524K range, making FHA an option for entry-level buyers in this resort-amenity community. The upper-end homes in Diamond Hill ($600K+) require conventional financing.

FHA vs. Conventional: What Makes Sense in Valrico?

When FHA Makes Sense

FHA is the right choice for Valrico buyers who have a credit score in the 580-679 range (where FHA rates are more competitive than conventional), have limited down payment funds (3.5% vs. conventional 5-20%), or have had past credit events (bankruptcy discharged 2 years ago, foreclosure 3 years ago) that would disqualify them from conventional financing. First-time buyers using Florida Housing Finance Corporation (HFA) down payment assistance programs typically pair those grants with FHA financing.

When Conventional Makes More Sense

If your credit score is 740 or above and you can put 20% down, conventional financing typically outperforms FHA in Valrico. Conventional loans with 20% down have no PMI (private mortgage insurance equivalent), while FHA MIP on a sub-10%-down loan lasts the life of the loan. Buyers who plan to stay 10+ years in a Valrico home often find conventional is cheaper over the long term despite higher upfront credit requirements.

Factor FHA Conventional (5% down) Conventional (20% down)
Minimum Credit Score580 (3.5% down)620620
Down Payment on $420K$14,700$21,000$84,000
Mortgage InsuranceMIP (life of loan if under 10% down)PMI until 80% LTVNone
Best For580-679 credit, low down payment680+ credit, moderate savings740+ credit, strong savings

What Do FHA Buyers Need to Know in the Valrico Market?

FHA Property Condition Requirements

FHA appraisals include a health and safety check that conventional appraisals do not. The FHA appraiser will note issues like peeling paint, exposed electrical wiring, missing handrails, non-functioning HVAC, or major roof damage. Sellers of older Valrico homes (1970s-1990s construction) sometimes resist FHA offers because of the additional repair requirements. Budget for potential FHA repair requests and be transparent with your agent about financing type when making offers.

FHA and Florida Down Payment Assistance

Florida Housing Finance Corporation's HFA Preferred and HFA Preferred Plus programs can be paired with FHA loans. The Florida Hometown Heroes program offers up to 5% of the loan amount (max $35,000) for first-responders, educators, healthcare workers, and others in qualifying professions. These assistance funds are structured as a 0% interest second mortgage, not a grant, but they require no monthly payment and are forgiven after 10 years for HFA Plus. Applying through an approved lender is required.

Competing Against Conventional and Cash Buyers

In the current Valrico market, FHA buyers compete with conventional buyers and occasional cash buyers. FHA is not a dealbreaker for most Valrico sellers, but it can affect seller perception for competitively-priced homes. Working with an agent who can present your FHA offer professionally, demonstrating pre-approval strength and flexibility on other terms, levels the playing field.

Buying a Valrico Home With FHA Financing?

Frequently Asked Questions About FHA Homes in Valrico FL

What is the FHA loan limit in Hillsborough County for 2026?

The 2026 FHA loan limit for Hillsborough County is $524,225 for a single-family home. This covers the vast majority of Valrico's housing inventory, since the Valrico median is approximately $410K-$430K.

Can I use FHA financing to buy a home in Bloomingdale or Diamond Hill?

Yes, for homes priced under $524,225. Bloomingdale and Diamond Hill both have inventory in the FHA-eligible range. Diamond Hill's higher-end homes above the loan limit require conventional financing or a down payment to reduce the financed amount below the FHA ceiling.

Will Valrico sellers accept FHA offers?

Most Valrico sellers will consider FHA offers. In a balanced or buyer-friendly market, FHA financing is competitive. Sellers of older homes may have concerns about FHA repair requirements, but many Valrico homes built after 1990 have no significant FHA property condition issues. Working with an experienced agent who frames FHA offers professionally helps.

What down payment assistance programs work with FHA in Valrico?

Florida Housing Finance Corporation programs including HFA Preferred, HFA Preferred Plus, and the Florida Hometown Heroes program all work with FHA financing. Hometown Heroes provides up to 5% of the loan amount (max $35,000) for qualifying professions including first responders, teachers, healthcare workers, and military. Contact an approved Florida Housing lender for current eligibility and income limits.

Does FHA work for Valrico condos or townhomes?

FHA financing for condos requires the condo project to be FHA-approved. Not all condo associations maintain FHA approval. Townhomes structured as fee-simple properties (you own the land under the unit) are generally easier to finance with FHA than traditional condos. Ask your agent to confirm FHA eligibility before going under contract on any Valrico attached home.
