title: Riverview FL Flood Zones: What Every Buyer Needs to Know
excerpt: Which parts of Riverview FL are in flood zones? FEMA flood maps, flood insurance costs, and how to check any property's flood risk before buying in 33569, 33578, or 33579.
content:
Flood risk is one of the most important, and most overlooked, factors when buying a home in Florida. Riverview, FL sits along the Alafia River in Hillsborough County, and while most of the community's master-planned neighborhoods are well-engineered for stormwater management, certain areas carry real flood risk that affects insurance costs, resale value, and peace of mind. Here is what every buyer needs to know about flood zones in Riverview's three ZIP codes: 33569, 33578, and 33579.

What Are FEMA Flood Zones and Why Do They Matter?

FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) designates flood zones based on historical flood data, topography, and proximity to waterways. The zones that matter most for Riverview homebuyers:

  • Zone X (unshaded): Minimal flood risk. No federal flood insurance requirement. Most of Riverview's residential neighborhoods fall in this zone
  • Zone X (shaded): Moderate flood risk (0.2% annual chance). Not required to carry flood insurance, but it is recommended
  • Zone AE: High-risk flood zone (1% annual chance of flooding). Flood insurance is required if you have a federally backed mortgage. Premiums can be significant
  • Zone AH: High-risk zone with shallow flooding. Similar insurance requirements to Zone AE

The designation on your specific lot determines whether flood insurance is mandatory and how much it costs. Even within the same neighborhood, one lot may be in Zone X while an adjacent lot falls in Zone AE.

Which Parts of Riverview Are in Flood Zones?

Flood risk in Riverview is primarily concentrated along waterways:

  • Alafia River corridor: Properties along the Alafia River and its tributaries have the highest flood risk. The river runs east-west through Riverview and has a well-documented flood history, including significant flooding events during major hurricanes
  • Bullfrog Creek area: Properties near Bullfrog Creek in western Riverview carry elevated flood risk
  • Low-lying areas near US-301: Some commercial and residential areas along the US-301 corridor sit in moderate flood zones
  • Waterfront properties: Any home marketed as "riverfront" or "waterfront" on the Alafia River almost certainly falls in a high-risk flood zone

Most master-planned communities, including Waterset, Triple Creek, Panther Trace, and Summerfield, were engineered with retention ponds, grading, and stormwater systems designed to keep residential lots out of high-risk flood zones. However, always verify the flood zone for the specific lot, not just the neighborhood.

How Do I Check a Property's Flood Zone?

Before making an offer on any Riverview property, check the flood zone designation:

  • FEMA Flood Map Service Center: The official source at msc.fema.gov. Enter the property address to see the current flood map panel and zone designation
  • Hillsborough County Property Appraiser: The county GIS system includes flood zone overlays on property maps
  • Elevation certificate: For properties near flood zone boundaries, an elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor can determine whether the structure's lowest floor is above the base flood elevation. This directly affects insurance pricing
  • Ask your REALTOR: An experienced Riverview agent should pull flood zone data as part of the property analysis before you make an offer

FEMA updates flood maps periodically, and the most recent updates for Hillsborough County have shifted some boundaries. A property that was previously in Zone X may now be in Zone AE, or vice versa. Always check the current effective map, not outdated information.

Not Sure About Flood Risk? Ask Before You Buy.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective, checks flood zone designations, insurance requirements, and elevation data on every property. 23+ years of real estate experience protecting buyers from costly surprises.

(813) 733-7907  |  Get a Property Flood Analysis

How Much Does Flood Insurance Cost in Riverview?

Flood insurance costs in Riverview vary dramatically based on zone designation, property elevation, and coverage amount:

  • Zone X (no requirement): Preferred risk policies are available for $400-$700/year if you choose to carry coverage voluntarily. This is smart even in low-risk zones, about 25% of flood claims nationally come from outside high-risk areas
  • Zone AE (required): Premiums typically range from $1,500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the property's elevation relative to the base flood elevation, construction type, and coverage limits
  • FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0: The updated pricing methodology now factors in property-specific characteristics like distance to water, flood frequency, and building attributes. Some properties saw premiums decrease while others increased significantly

Flood insurance is separate from your homeowner's insurance policy. Standard homeowner's insurance does not cover flood damage. Even if flood insurance is not required for your zone, consider carrying it, Florida's hurricane season creates flooding risks even in areas that are not near rivers.

What Happens If My Property Floods?

Understanding the claims process before you need it:

  • Document everything: Photos and video of damage before cleanup begins
  • Contact your insurance company immediately: Most policies require prompt notification
  • Separate flood damage from wind damage: Flood insurance covers rising water. Homeowner's insurance covers wind and rain intrusion through the roof. Hurricane damage often involves both
  • FEMA assistance: If a disaster is federally declared, FEMA may provide additional assistance, but this is typically loans, not grants, and should not be relied on as a substitute for insurance

Should Flood Risk Stop You from Buying in Riverview?

Not necessarily, but it should inform your decision:

  • Most Riverview homes are in Zone X minimal flood risk, no insurance requirement, though voluntary coverage is affordable and recommended
  • Waterfront and river-adjacent properties carry real risk and meaningful insurance costs. Factor $2,000-$5,000+ annually into your housing budget
  • New construction communities are typically engineered to avoid high-risk flood zones. The stormwater management systems in communities like Waterset and Triple Creek are designed for Florida's heavy rainfall
  • Older properties near the Alafia River require the most careful flood zone analysis. Some have flood history that should be disclosed during the transaction

Use the mortgage calculator to factor flood insurance premiums into your monthly payment estimate.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Riverview FL in a flood zone?

Parts of Riverview are in FEMA-designated flood zones, primarily along the Alafia River and its tributaries. However, the majority of Riverview's residential neighborhoods, especially newer master-planned communities like Waterset, Triple Creek, and Panther Trace, are in Zone X (minimal flood risk). Always check the specific lot's flood designation before purchasing.

Do I need flood insurance in Riverview FL?

If your property is in a FEMA high-risk flood zone (Zone AE or AH) and you have a federally backed mortgage, flood insurance is required. If your property is in Zone X, flood insurance is not required but is strongly recommended. Voluntary policies in low-risk zones are affordable at $400-$700/year and provide valuable protection.

How much is flood insurance in Riverview FL?

Flood insurance in Riverview ranges from $400-$700/year for voluntary policies in Zone X to $1,500-$5,000+ per year for properties in high-risk Zone AE. Premiums depend on the property's elevation, distance to water, construction type, and coverage limits under FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 methodology.

Does Riverview flood during hurricanes?

The Alafia River has flooded during major hurricanes, affecting properties in its floodplain. Master-planned communities with engineered stormwater systems have generally fared well during recent storms. Properties on higher ground and away from waterways face minimal flooding risk even during hurricanes, though localized street flooding can occur anywhere during heavy rain events.

How do I find the flood zone for a specific Riverview address?

Check the FEMA Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov by entering the property address. You can also use the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's GIS system, which overlays flood zone data on property maps. For properties near flood zone boundaries, an elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor provides the most precise determination.

title: Tampa Bay Quarterly Market Report: Q1 2024
excerpt: Q1 2024 brought cautious optimism to the Tampa Bay housing market. Mortgage rates hovered around 7% but showed signs of easing. Inventory continued bu
content:
Quick Answer: Q1 2024 brought cautious optimism to Tampa Bay. Mortgage rates hovered around 7% with signs of potential easing. Inventory reached approximately 3 months of supply, more buyer-friendly than any quarter since 2019. Sale-to-list ratios averaged 97-98%, meaning buyers could negotiate 2-3% off list. About 40% of transactions included seller concessions.

I walked into Q1 2024 telling buyers: "This is your best opportunity since 2019." Not because prices had crashed, they hadn't. Not because rates were low, they weren't. But because the combination of more inventory, seller flexibility, inspection contingencies, and reduced competition created genuinely better buying conditions than we had seen in four years. Buyers who acted in Q1 2024 positioned themselves well ahead of rate improvements that came later in 2024.

What Were Median Prices Across Tampa Bay in Q1 2024?

Hillsborough County

Hillsborough County median reached $390,000, up 1.3% year-over-year. The Valrico-Lithia corridor in the Fishhawk/Newsome school zone outperformed at $425K+. Brandon volume remained strong as the most active established community in the county. Riverview continued absorbing steady demand from families prioritizing school access. The Ruskin and South Shore corridor offered the best Hillsborough values below $380K.

Pinellas County: Beach Holds, Condos Soft

Pinellas County median: $380,000, up 2.7%. Waterfront and beach-adjacent properties held firm, demand for Clearwater Beach, Dunedin, and St. Pete Beach single-family homes stayed consistent from buyers relocating from the Northeast and Midwest. Inland condos softened, particularly in older buildings where reserve funding shortfalls had become a material issue following Florida's new condo reserve laws enacted after the Champlain Towers collapse.

High-Growth Corridors: Pasco and Manatee

Pasco County: $350,000 median, with Wesley Chapel new construction maintaining strong absorption at $390K-$500K+. The Epperson and Mirada communities continued drawing buyers who wanted master-planned amenities at Hillsborough-adjacent prices. Manatee County: $430,000. Parrish and Bradenton new construction from multiple national builders remained the most active segment. Sarasota County: $460,000. Luxury above $1M stayed competitive. Polk County: $315,000, the best value in the region for Tampa commuters and remote workers prioritizing space over commute.

How Did Inventory and Buyer Leverage Look in Q1 2024?

Three Months of Supply, A Meaningful Shift

Active listings across the six-county region reached approximately 3 months of supply, up from 2 months a year earlier but still below the 4-6 month balanced threshold. The biggest inventory gains came in new construction, particularly in Pasco and Manatee counties. Resale inventory remained tighter in established neighborhoods with top-rated schools.

The Lock-In Effect Easing

Through 2022-2023, many homeowners with sub-3% mortgages refused to sell because they would be trading a $1,500/month payment for a $2,800/month payment on their next home. By Q1 2024, life circumstances, job changes, divorces, growing families, retirements, had started overcoming that reluctance for more sellers. New listing volume grew modestly, and sellers who entered the market were generally more realistic about pricing than those who had listed speculatively in 2022-2023.

Were Sellers Still Getting Full Price in Q1 2024?

Sale-to-List Ratios Shift

Sale-to-list price ratios averaged 97-98% across the region, a significant shift from the 100-103% ratios of 2021-2022. Buyers were routinely paying 2-3% below list on most transactions. This meant a $400,000 listed home typically sold for $388,000-$394,000. For a seller, that math required accurate pricing, a seller who listed at $420,000 hoping to accept $400,000 found the market often settled at $390,000 after longer days on market and a price reduction.

Seller Concessions Became Standard

Roughly 40% of transactions included seller concessions, closing cost credits, 2-1 rate buydowns, and home warranty inclusions. For first-time homebuyers with limited cash reserves, negotiating a $10,000-$15,000 seller credit toward closing costs made a material difference in ability to close. Sellers who refused concessions in Q1 2024 typically sat longer and still made the concession, just later, after more days on market.

Q1 2024 County-by-County Comparison Table

County Q1 2024 Median YoY Change Sale-to-List Concession Rate
Hillsborough$390,000+1.3%97-98%~40% of deals
Pinellas$380,000+2.7%97-99%~35% of deals
Pasco$350,000+3.0%97-98%~45% of deals
Manatee$430,000+1.2%97-98%~40% of deals
Sarasota$460,000+2.2%96-98%~40% of deals
Polk$315,000+1.6%97-99%~42% of deals

What Buyer and Seller Strategies Worked Best in Q1 2024?

Buyer Strategies That Won

The best-positioned buyers in Q1 2024 came pre-approved, had clarity on their must-have criteria, and did not over-negotiate. Asking for seller concessions was reasonable and expected, but lowballing on price AND demanding maximum concessions consistently killed deals. The winning formula was fair price negotiation (2-3% off list) combined with reasonable concession request ($5,000-$10,000 closing credit or rate buydown). Learn more about the buyer process.

Seller Strategies That Worked

Sellers who priced accurately based on actual recent comparable sales, not 2022 peak prices, sold in 28-42 days. Those who priced aspirationally (5%+ above comps) sat 60-90 days and typically took price reductions that netted less than accurate pricing from day one would have achieved. I worked with sellers throughout Q1 2024 to deliver honest pricing guidance that maximized net proceeds, not list price.

Frequently Asked Questions: Q1 2024 Tampa Bay Market

Was Tampa Bay in a buyer's market in Q1 2024?

Technically still a seller's market (3 months vs. balanced 4-6 months). Practically, conditions were the most buyer-friendly since 2019: inspection contingencies were standard, concessions were common, and buyers had time to make thoughtful decisions rather than 48-hour offers.

How did the NAR settlement affect the Q1 2024 market?

The NAR settlement was announced in March 2024, changing how buyer agent compensation is structured. Buyers began signing buyer broker agreements before touring homes. The practical impact on Q1 2024 transactions was minimal, the market continued operating normally, and both buyers and sellers adapted to the new documentation requirements. Ask me how this affects your transaction.

title: Dover FL Homes with Acreage: Land and Horse Properties
excerpt: Find homes with acreage in Dover FL, horse properties, farmland, and large-lot rural homes in Hillsborough County. What to know about well water, septic, ag zoning, and buying land near Tampa.
content:
Why Do Buyers Look for Acreage in Dover FL?

Dover, Florida (33527) is one of the last remaining pockets of rural, large-lot properties in Hillsborough County that's still within a reasonable commute to Tampa Bay. While communities just a few miles west, like Brandon, Riverview, and FishHawk, have been developed into dense suburban neighborhoods, Dover has maintained its agricultural character with properties sitting on 1 to 10+ acres of land.

Buyers looking for acreage near Tampa typically find their way to Dover for several reasons: the ability to keep horses and livestock, space for workshops and outbuildings, agricultural zoning that allows small farming operations, and the simple desire for privacy and open space. Dover delivers all of this while keeping you within 25 miles of downtown Tampa.

What Types of Acreage Properties Are Available in Dover?

Dover's real estate market includes several categories of acreage properties:

Horse properties. Dover is one of the most popular areas in Hillsborough County for equestrian buyers. Many properties include fenced pastures, barns, riding arenas, and tack rooms. Properties set up for horses typically range from 2 to 10+ acres and are priced from $400,000 to $800,000+ depending on the home, structures, and total acreage.

Small farms and hobby farms. Dover's agricultural heritage means many properties are zoned for farming. Buyers use these properties for produce gardens, small nursery operations, poultry, goats, and other small-scale agricultural activities. The area's proximity to the Plant City Farmers Market and local produce distribution makes it practical for small agricultural businesses.

Large-lot single-family homes. Not everyone buying in Dover wants to farm or ride horses. Many buyers simply want a large lot (1-3 acres) with a single-family home, a private yard, and space between neighbors. These properties offer a lifestyle that's increasingly rare in the Tampa Bay suburbs.

Vacant land. Buyers looking to build their dream home on acreage can find vacant parcels in Dover ranging from 1 acre to 20+ acres. Prices depend on location, road access, and whether utilities are available. Expect to budget for well drilling, septic installation, and potentially bringing power to the property.

Have Questions About Dover FL Acreage Real Estate?

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience and knows the Tampa Bay market inside and out.

(813) 733-7907

Get Expert Help Today

What Should Buyers Know About Well Water and Septic Systems?

Most acreage properties in Dover are on well water and septic systems rather than municipal water and sewer. This is standard for rural properties in Hillsborough County, but buyers coming from suburban or urban settings should understand the implications:

  • Well water you'll need a well inspection before purchasing to test water quality and flow rate. Wells require periodic maintenance and occasional pump replacement. Water quality in the Dover area is generally good, but some wells may need treatment for iron or sulfur content.
  • Septic systems a septic inspection is essential before buying. Septic systems need to be pumped every 3-5 years and properly maintained. Failing septic systems can be expensive to replace ($10,000-$25,000+). Hillsborough County requires septic inspections at the time of sale.
  • Impact fees if you're building on vacant land, be aware of Hillsborough County impact fees for water and sewer connections (if available) or well and septic permitting.

What About Flood Zones and Insurance on Acreage Properties?

Some Dover properties sit within or adjacent to flood zones, particularly those near the Alafia River or Hillsborough River. Flood zone designation can significantly impact your insurance costs and may require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Always check FEMA flood maps for any property you're considering and factor insurance costs into your budget.

The good news is that many Dover properties, especially those on higher ground away from rivers and drainage corridors, are in Flood Zone X, which means they're outside the 100-year floodplain and don't require flood insurance. Your insurance agent can provide exact flood zone information for any specific address.

How Does Agricultural Zoning Work in Dover?

Many Dover properties carry an agricultural zoning designation from Hillsborough County, which provides several advantages:

  • Agricultural tax exemption qualifying properties can receive a significant reduction in property taxes through the agricultural classification. This can save thousands of dollars per year compared to residential-only tax assessments.
  • Permitted uses agricultural zoning allows farming, livestock, nurseries, and related activities that wouldn't be permitted in residentially zoned areas
  • Fewer restrictions agricultural properties generally have fewer restrictions on outbuildings, fencing, and property use compared to HOA-governed communities

If you're buying acreage in Dover with plans to use the agricultural exemption, consult with a local tax advisor to understand the qualification requirements and application process.

Ready to find your acreage property in Dover? I'm Barrett Henry with 23+ years of real estate experience. I help buyers find land and rural properties throughout Hillsborough County. Browse Dover homes and land for sale or call me at (813) 733-7907. Use our mortgage calculator and explore your FHA loan options yes, FHA loans can be used on properties with acreage in many cases.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I get a mortgage on a property with acreage in Dover FL?

Yes, most conventional and FHA lenders will finance properties with acreage, though some lenders limit the total acreage they'll include in the appraisal. Properties over 10 acres or those with heavy agricultural use may require specialized agricultural or portfolio lending. I can connect you with lenders experienced in financing rural properties.

What is the agricultural tax exemption in Florida?

Florida's agricultural tax exemption allows qualifying properties used for bona fide agricultural purposes to be assessed at a lower value for property tax purposes. This can significantly reduce your annual tax bill. Properties must demonstrate active agricultural use, simply owning acreage isn't enough to qualify. Hillsborough County's Property Appraiser determines eligibility.

Are there HOA restrictions on Dover FL acreage properties?

Most acreage properties in Dover are not within HOA-governed communities. This is one of Dover's key appeals, property owners have significantly more freedom regarding land use, structures, and property appearance compared to HOA neighborhoods. However, all properties must still comply with Hillsborough County codes and zoning regulations.

How much does it cost to drill a well in Dover FL?

Well drilling costs in the Dover/Hillsborough County area typically range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on depth, diameter, pump type, and any water treatment equipment needed. Permit fees are additional. If you're buying vacant land, factor well drilling into your total budget along with septic installation and any utility connections.

Can I subdivide acreage in Dover FL?

Subdivision of land in Dover is subject to Hillsborough County zoning and platting regulations. Whether you can subdivide depends on the current zoning designation, minimum lot size requirements, road access, and utility availability. Contact Hillsborough County's Development Services department for guidance on a specific parcel.

content:
FHA Homes in Riverview FL: Loan Limits, Requirements & Listings

FHA loans remain one of the most accessible paths to homeownership for first-time buyers and those with limited down payment savings. In Riverview, Florida, FHA financing opens the door to a wide range of homes across ZIP codes 33569, 33578, and 33579. This guide covers FHA loan limits, requirements, property standards, and how to find FHA-eligible homes in Riverview.

Quick Answer

Can you buy a home in Riverview with an FHA loan?

Yes. FHA loans work for most Riverview homes under the Hillsborough County loan limit. Requirements include a minimum 3.5% down payment, 580+ credit score, and a property that meets FHA minimum standards. Most Riverview single-family homes and select condos qualify.

What Are FHA Loan Limits for Riverview?

FHA loan limits are set by county and updated annually by HUD. Hillsborough County's single-family FHA loan limit has been in the $472,000 to $498,000+ range in recent years, which covers the majority of Riverview starter homes and many mid-range properties. Only homes priced above the limit would require a different loan program.

For the current year's exact FHA loan limit in Hillsborough County, check HUD's Mortgage Limits page or contact a local FHA-approved lender. Barrett Henry works with several lenders who specialize in FHA loans and can connect you with the right loan officer.

What Are FHA Loan Requirements?

Credit score580+ preferredMost lenders require 580-620+

First-Time Buyer? FHA Could Be Your Path In.

Barrett Henry connects buyers with trusted FHA lenders and finds homes that meet FHA property requirements. Let's get you into your first Riverview home.

Schedule a Free Consultation Call (813) 733-7907

What Properties Qualify for FHA in Riverview?

Most Riverview single-family homes built in the 2000s or later meet FHA property requirements without issues. The FHA appraiser will check for:

  • Functional heating, cooling, and ventilation systems
  • Roof in serviceable condition with at least 2 years of remaining life
  • Safe electrical wiring and plumbing
  • No major structural defects or safety hazards
  • Adequate access (ingress/egress)
  • No peeling or chipping paint on pre-1978 construction

Older homes or properties that need significant repairs may not pass FHA appraisal. Homes with roof issues, major water damage, or safety concerns could require seller repairs before closing. Barrett Henry identifies potential FHA issues during property tours so you do not waste time on homes that will not qualify.

FHA vs. Conventional vs. VA: Which Is Right for You?

FHA is not the only option. Here is how it compares to other common loan programs:

  • FHA: Best for buyers with limited down payment and lower credit scores. Trade-off is lifetime mortgage insurance.
  • Conventional: Better for buyers with 5-20% down and 680+ credit. No mortgage insurance with 20% down, or removable PMI with less.
  • VA: Best for eligible veterans and active military. Zero down, no mortgage insurance, competitive rates. The best loan program available if you qualify.

Barrett Henry does not push any particular loan program. The right choice depends on your credit, savings, and long-term plans. Getting pre-approved with a lender who understands FHA guidelines is the first step. Use our mortgage calculator to estimate monthly payments.

Ready to explore FHA options in Riverview? Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the FHA loan limit in Riverview FL?

The FHA loan limit for Hillsborough County is updated annually by HUD. As of recent years, the limit for a single-family home has been in the $472,000 to $498,000+ range, which covers the vast majority of Riverview homes. Check HUD's website for the current year's exact limit.

What are FHA loan requirements in Florida?

FHA loans require a minimum 3.5% down payment with a 580+ credit score (10% down for scores 500-579), mortgage insurance premium (MIP) for the life of the loan, property must meet FHA minimum property standards, and the home must be your primary residence. Gift funds are allowed for the down payment.

Can I buy a condo with FHA in Riverview?

Only condos in FHA-approved condominium projects are eligible for FHA financing. Not all Riverview condo communities are FHA-approved. Barrett Henry can identify which communities have FHA approval and help you target your search accordingly.

What are FHA property requirements?

FHA requires the property to meet Minimum Property Requirements (MPRs): functional heating and cooling, adequate roofing, safe electrical and plumbing, no peeling paint on pre-1978 homes, and generally habitable condition. Homes that need significant repairs may not qualify for FHA financing.

Is FHA a good option for Riverview first-time buyers?

FHA is one of the most popular loan programs for first-time Riverview buyers because of the low 3.5% down payment requirement and flexible credit guidelines. The trade-off is mortgage insurance that lasts the life of the loan. For buyers who plan to build equity and refinance later, FHA provides an accessible entry point.

content:

La Collina is Brandon's premier luxury community, featuring a championship golf course, gated sections, resort-style amenities, club dining, and homes from $400K to $600K+. It offers a country club lifestyle without the South Tampa price tag. Browse the Brandon neighborhoods map and search Brandon homes for sale.

When people think of luxury living in Brandon, La Collina is the name that comes up first - and for good reason. This golf course community off Lumsden Road offers something you won't find anywhere else in the Brandon/Valrico corridor: a genuine country club lifestyle with resort-style amenities, gated privacy, and homes that rival anything in South Tampa at a fraction of the price. I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've helped buyers navigate La Collina's multiple sections, membership options, and pricing tiers. This is the guide that cuts through the brochure language and gives you the real story.

What Is the History of La Collina?

La Collina - Italian for "the hill" - was developed in the early 2000s on a large parcel of former agricultural land off Lumsden Road. The vision from the start was to create Brandon's answer to the exclusive golf communities that had been thriving in South Tampa, Westchase, and Lakewood Ranch. The developers invested heavily in the golf course design, bringing in architects who crafted an 18-hole championship layout that winds through the residential sections and creates natural buffers between neighborhoods.

The community was built out over roughly 15 years, with different builders handling different sections. This phased approach means you'll find a range of home styles - from the early Mediterranean-influenced designs of the first phases to more contemporary Florida architecture in later additions. The golf course and club facilities were among the first amenities completed, which helped establish La Collina's reputation as a premium community before most of the homes were even built.

What Makes La Collina Brandon's Luxury Option?

It's the combination of amenities, home quality, and privacy that sets La Collina apart. The community features a championship golf course, a resort-style swimming pool, tennis and pickleball courts, a fitness center, and a clubhouse with dining facilities. You can have dinner at the club, play a round of golf, swim laps, and never leave the neighborhood. That kind of self-contained lifestyle is what draws executives, retirees, and families who value convenience and community.

The homes themselves are a step above standard Brandon construction. You'll find upgraded finishes - granite and quartz countertops, hardwood and porcelain tile flooring, crown molding, tray ceilings, and owners suites with spa-style bathrooms. Many homes have three-car garages, summer kitchens, and screened pool enclosures that overlook the golf course. The lot sizes in the gated sections tend to be generous by Brandon standards, giving you the kind of breathing room that's increasingly hard to find in newer developments.

Interested in La Collina's Country Club Lifestyle?

Barrett Henry knows every section, every price tier, and every membership option. Get the insider perspective before you tour.

Call (813) 733-7907 Schedule a Consultation

How Does the Golf Club Membership Work?

La Collina Golf & Country Club operates as a semi-private facility, meaning you don't have to be a resident to join, and not all residents are required to join. However, living in certain sections may include mandatory club membership as part of your HOA. Membership tiers typically include full golf membership (with unlimited course access, dining, and facility use), social membership (dining and amenities without golf), and fitness-only options.

Initiation fees and monthly dues vary by tier and have changed over the years as the club's ownership has evolved. Current full golf membership dues typically run $200-$400/month on top of any initiation fee. Social memberships are more affordable but still add to your monthly housing cost. I always tell buyers: factor the club costs into your total budget before falling in love with a golf course view. That view comes with a bill.

Gated Sections and Home Styles

La Collina has both gated and non-gated sections. The gated enclaves tend to have larger homes, higher HOA fees, and more exclusive access to specific amenity areas. Non-gated sections still benefit from the golf course views and community amenities but at a lower price point and with lower monthly fees. Architecturally, you'll find everything from 2,000 sq ft three-bedroom homes in the non-gated sections to 4,500+ sq ft estates in the premier gated areas.

What Do Homes Cost in La Collina?

The range is wide because the community serves multiple buyer profiles. Entry-level homes in non-gated sections start around $400K for 2,000-2,500 sq ft. Mid-range golf-view homes in gated sections run $450K-$550K. Premium estate lots with expansive golf course views and upgraded everything push into the $600K+ range. When you compare this to comparable golf communities in South Tampa or Westchase where you'd pay $800K-$1.2M for similar amenities, La Collina's value proposition becomes clear.

Schools Near La Collina

La Collina is zoned for Limona Elementary, McLane Middle School, and Bloomingdale High School. Bloomingdale High consistently ranks among the better public high schools in Hillsborough County. Private school families have access to Bell Shoals Baptist Academy, Foundation Christian Academy, and several other options in the Brandon/Valrico corridor. Tampa Catholic and Jesuit High School are also within commuting distance for high school students.

Daily Life and Amenities

Life in La Collina revolves around the club and the course. Morning golfers hit the first tee at sunrise. The pool area fills up on weekend afternoons. Tennis and pickleball leagues run year-round. The clubhouse restaurant offers dining options that residents actually use - it's not just a banquet facility that sits empty during the week. Grocery runs are easy - Publix and several shopping plazas are within five minutes on Lumsden Road.

The community has a distinct personality compared to other Brandon neighborhoods. It's quieter, more manicured, and more intentionally social. If you're the type of person who wants to know your neighbors through club events and golf scrambles rather than just waving from the driveway, La Collina delivers that experience.

Who Should Buy in La Collina?

  • Golf enthusiasts who want to live on a championship course without paying Avila or Palma Ceia prices
  • Executives and professionals who value resort-style amenities and community dining
  • Active retirees looking for a social community with fitness, tennis, and pool facilities
  • Families who want Brandon schools with a more upscale living environment

Barrett's Take on La Collina

La Collina is the community I show buyers who tell me they want a country club lifestyle but can't justify spending $800K+ in South Tampa or Westchase. The homes are well-built, the course is in good condition, and the amenities are real - not a clubhouse that doubles as a storage facility. The thing I always caution buyers about is the total monthly cost. Between HOA fees, potential CDD assessments, and club membership dues, your non-mortgage housing costs can easily hit $500-$700/month. That's manageable for many buyers, but you need to budget for it honestly. When the total cost works, La Collina is genuinely one of the best lifestyle values in all of Hillsborough County.

La Collina - Frequently Asked Questions

Is golf membership required in La Collina?

It depends on which section you live in. Some gated sections require mandatory club membership as part of the HOA. Non-gated sections generally do not require membership, though you can join voluntarily. Always verify the specific requirements for the section you're considering.

Can non-residents play golf at La Collina?

Yes, the club operates as semi-private, meaning public tee times are available when the course isn't reserved for member play. This also means you can test the course experience before committing to a home purchase in the community.

How do La Collina's prices compare to other golf communities?

La Collina offers significant value compared to golf communities in South Tampa, Westchase, and Lakewood Ranch. You'll find comparable homes and amenities at 40-60% less than what you'd pay in those areas, making it one of the best golf community values in the Tampa Bay market.

What are the HOA fees in La Collina?

HOA fees range from $150 to $350 per month depending on the section. Gated sections with additional amenity access tend to have higher fees. These fees are separate from any club membership dues, which are optional in most sections.

Is La Collina a good investment?

Golf course communities in established areas tend to hold value well, and La Collina benefits from Brandon's steady demand and limited luxury inventory. The key risk is that golf course communities depend on the club's financial health - a well-managed course supports property values, while a struggling one can hurt them.

title: Best Restaurants and Things to Do in Riverview FL
excerpt: Looking for things to do in Riverview FL? Local restaurants, parks, outdoor recreation, family activities, and nightlife, a local's guide to living in Riverview.
content:
One of the most common questions from people considering a move to Riverview, FL is whether there is enough to do. The honest answer: Riverview is not a nightlife destination, but it offers a strong mix of outdoor recreation, family-friendly activities, and an improving restaurant and dining scene that keeps residents happy without driving 30 minutes for dinner. Here is what daily life looks like beyond the subdivision gates.

What Are the Best Restaurants in Riverview FL?

Riverview's dining scene has grown significantly as the population has boomed. While you will find the usual chain restaurants along US-301, the area also has standout local spots:

  • Riverview staples: Local favorites include casual American dining, barbecue joints, and family-owned Mexican restaurants scattered along Boyette Road and Big Bend Road corridors
  • Seafood: Fresh Gulf seafood restaurants serve grouper, shrimp, and stone crab in season. Several casual waterfront-adjacent spots near the Alafia River offer a Florida fish camp vibe
  • International cuisine: Riverview's growing diversity has brought Vietnamese, Indian, Colombian, and Thai restaurants to the area. The US-301 corridor between Boyette and Big Bend has the highest concentration
  • Coffee and brunch: Local coffee shops and brunch spots have popped up in newer shopping centers, giving residents alternatives to Starbucks and Dunkin
  • Fast-casual and chains: Every major chain is represented, Chick-fil-A, Chipotle, Outback, Longhorn, Olive Garden, and more line the US-301 and Big Bend corridors

For fine dining and upscale restaurants, most Riverview residents head to nearby Brandon, South Tampa, or the Riverwalk area downtown, a 20-30 minute drive.

What Outdoor Activities Are Available in Riverview?

Outdoor recreation is where Riverview truly shines:

  • Alafia River State Park: Over 6,000 acres of trails for mountain biking (some of the best in Florida), hiking, horseback riding, and camping. The park's elevation changes are unusual for Florida and make the mountain bike trails genuinely challenging
  • Alafia River: Kayaking, canoeing, and fishing on the Alafia River. Launch points are accessible from several public parks. The river is tidal in its lower stretches, so you can catch both freshwater and saltwater species
  • Lettuce Lake Park: A 240-acre Hillsborough County park with a boardwalk through cypress swamp, a nature center, and excellent bird watching. Just north of Riverview along the Hillsborough River
  • Community parks and trails: Master-planned communities like Waterset, Triple Creek, and Summerfield have extensive walking and biking trail networks, splash pads, and playgrounds
  • Riverview Civic Center and pool: The community's public recreation center offers a pool, sports fields, and community programs
  • Fishing: Beyond the Alafia River, nearby Tampa Bay, Hillsborough Bay, and dozens of retention ponds throughout the community offer bass, tilapia, and panfish opportunities

What Family Activities Does Riverview Offer?

Riverview is built for families, and the activity options reflect that:

  • Sports leagues: Youth baseball, soccer, football, and basketball leagues run year-round through the Greater Riverview Little League and community sports organizations
  • Swimming: Nearly every master-planned community has at least one pool and splash pad. Some communities like Waterset have resort-style pool complexes
  • Library: The Riverview branch of the Hillsborough County Public Library system offers children's programs, summer reading, and community events
  • Farmers markets: Weekend farmers markets operate seasonally, offering local produce, crafts, and food vendors
  • Nearby attractions: Tampa's major attractions are a short drive, Florida Aquarium, ZooTampa at Lowry Park, Busch Gardens, MOSI (Museum of Science and Industry), and the Tampa Riverwalk

Want the Inside Scoop on Riverview?

Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective, lives and works in the Tampa Bay area and knows which Riverview neighborhoods offer the best lifestyle match. 23+ years of real estate experience.

(813) 733-7907  |  Find Your Riverview Home

What About Shopping in Riverview?

Riverview's commercial growth has kept pace with residential development:

  • Riverview Village: Shopping centers along US-301 provide most daily needs, groceries (Publix, Walmart Supercenter, Aldi), pharmacies, banks, and services
  • Big Bend Road corridor: Newer retail development along Big Bend Road has brought more restaurants, services, and retail options to the southern part of Riverview
  • Boyette Road corridor: Additional shopping centers and restaurants serve the eastern Riverview communities
  • Nearby Brandon: Westfield Brandon mall and the extensive retail along SR-60 in Brandon are 10-15 minutes from most Riverview neighborhoods. This is where Riverview residents go for major shopping trips
  • Tampa Premium Outlets: Located nearby on I-75 at the Grand Regency interchange

Is There Nightlife in Riverview FL?

Riverview is not a nightlife destination, and that is by design, most residents chose it specifically for its family-oriented character. For evening entertainment:

  • Local bars and sports bars: Several sports bars and casual pubs along US-301 offer game-day watching and casual evenings out
  • Breweries: The Tampa Bay craft beer scene has expanded into the Riverview/Brandon area with several taprooms
  • Movie theaters: Multiple cinema options including nearby AMC and Regal locations
  • Ybor City and SoHo: For real nightlife, clubs, live music, and late-night dining, residents head to Ybor City or SoHo in Tampa, about 25-35 minutes away

How Does Riverview Compare for Lifestyle?

Compared to other Tampa Bay suburbs:

  • Riverview vs Valrico: Valrico has a more established feel with slightly more restaurant diversity. Riverview has more new construction and community amenities
  • Riverview vs Wesley Chapel: Wesley Chapel has more upscale retail (The Shops at Wiregrass) and newer commercial development. Riverview has better outdoor recreation with the Alafia River corridor
  • Riverview vs Brandon: Brandon has significantly more retail, dining, and entertainment options. Riverview offers newer homes and more community amenities at lower prices

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there anything to do in Riverview FL?

Yes. Riverview offers strong outdoor recreation including Alafia River State Park (mountain biking, hiking, camping), kayaking and fishing on the Alafia River, community parks with pools and splash pads, youth sports leagues, and a growing restaurant scene. For major entertainment, attractions in Tampa proper are 20-30 minutes away.

What are the best parks in Riverview FL?

Alafia River State Park is the standout, over 6,000 acres with nationally recognized mountain bike trails, hiking, and camping. Lettuce Lake Park offers a boardwalk through cypress swamp. Community parks within Waterset, Triple Creek, and Panther Trace provide pools, playgrounds, and walking trails for residents.

Does Riverview FL have good restaurants?

Riverview's restaurant scene has improved significantly with the area's growth. You will find quality local restaurants for seafood, barbecue, Mexican, Vietnamese, and other cuisines, particularly along the US-301 and Boyette Road corridors. For fine dining, most residents drive to nearby Brandon or downtown Tampa.

How far is Riverview from the beach?

The nearest Gulf beaches (Apollo Beach, Bahia Beach) are about 20-30 minutes from Riverview. The popular Clearwater Beach and St. Pete Beach areas are 45-60 minutes depending on traffic. Riverview is an inland community, so beach proximity is a trade-off compared to coastal Tampa Bay cities.

Is Riverview FL boring?

That depends on your lifestyle priorities. Riverview is a family-oriented suburb, not a nightlife or entertainment district. Residents who value outdoor recreation, community amenities, good schools, and affordable housing find it engaging. Those who prioritize walkable urban neighborhoods, nightlife, or beach access will likely want to live closer to Tampa or the coast.

title: Is Plant City FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Guide
excerpt: Honest review of living in Plant City FL, the small-town charm, the commute, the strawberry festival, home values, and whether Plant City is the right fit for your family.
content:
What's It Really Like to Live in Plant City FL?

Plant City, Florida is one of those communities that people either love immediately or overlook entirely. If you're coming from a big city or a trendy suburb, Plant City's pace and character might seem like a step backward. But if you're looking for genuine small-town living, the kind where your waitress knows your name, your kids can ride bikes to their friends' houses, and the annual festival shuts down the whole town for 11 days, Plant City delivers something that most Tampa Bay communities can't replicate.

With 23+ years of real estate experience, I've helped dozens of families move to Plant City. Here's an honest assessment of what you'll love and what might give you pause.

What Do Residents Love About Plant City?

Real community identity. Plant City isn't a collection of subdivisions, it's a city with history, traditions, and a genuine downtown. The Strawberry Festival, high school football games, downtown events, and local businesses create a community fabric that newer suburbs simply don't have. Residents feel like they're part of something, not just living in a house near Tampa.

Affordability. Your dollar stretches further in Plant City than in almost any other Hillsborough County community. First-time buyers can find homes in the low $200s, and families looking for 4-bedroom homes with a yard have options under $400K. Compared to FishHawk ($475K+ median) or even Brandon ($400K+ median), Plant City's pricing gives buyers room to breathe.

Space and land. Plant City and its surrounding area offer properties with real acreage, something that's nearly impossible to find at comparable prices closer to Tampa. Horse properties, hobby farms, and large-lot homes are common on Plant City's outskirts. See our Plant City homes with land guide for details.

Self-contained services. As an incorporated city, Plant City has its own police department, fire department, utility services, parks, and recreation programs. You don't need to drive to Tampa or Brandon for everyday needs, Plant City has grocery stores, healthcare facilities, restaurants, and retail within the city.

The Strawberry Festival. It's more than a festival, it's a cultural institution. For 11 days every February/March, Plant City hosts one of the largest community events in Florida, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors. Major concert acts, agricultural exhibits, and strawberry everything make it a uniquely Plant City experience. Learn more in our Plant City things to do guide.

Have Questions About Plant City FL Real Estate?

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience and knows the Tampa Bay market inside and out.

(813) 733-7907

Get Expert Help Today

What Are the Downsides of Living in Plant City?

The commute to Tampa. At 25+ miles from downtown Tampa, the commute can stretch to 40-50+ minutes during rush hour on I-4. If you work in downtown Tampa, South Tampa, or Westshore, this is a daily reality. Remote workers and those employed in eastern Hillsborough or Lakeland won't have this issue.

Limited nightlife and entertainment. Plant City is a small town. The dining options, while charming and locally owned, aren't as diverse as Tampa's or even Brandon's. For concerts (outside the Strawberry Festival), cultural events, professional sports, and nightlife, you'll need to drive to Tampa, 30+ minutes each way.

Summer heat and humidity. Like all inland Florida communities, Plant City gets genuinely hot from June through September. Without coastal breezes, the heat can be intense. Most residents plan outdoor activities for early morning or evening during summer months.

City taxes. Unlike unincorporated communities such as Dover or Seffner, Plant City is an incorporated city. This means residents pay city millage taxes in addition to county taxes, which adds to the total tax burden. The tradeoff is city services, your own police force, utility services, and parks department.

Fewer high-end amenities. Plant City doesn't have the resort-style pools, fitness centers, and trail systems found in master-planned communities like FishHawk Ranch. If those amenities are important to you, Plant City's more traditional neighborhood structure won't deliver them.

Who Is Plant City Best For?

  • Families who value small-town community and don't need urban entertainment
  • First-time buyers who need affordable entry into homeownership
  • Rural/agricultural buyers who want land within driving distance of Tampa
  • Remote workers who don't need a short commute
  • Retirees looking for a quiet, affordable community with local services
  • Workers in eastern Hillsborough County or Lakeland

If Plant City sounds like your kind of community, browse Plant City homes for sale or call me at (813) 733-7907. I'm Barrett Henry with 23+ years of real estate experience, and I know Plant City well. Use our mortgage calculator and explore the Florida Homestead Exemption to maximize your investment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Plant City FL a safe place to live?

Plant City has its own police department which provides dedicated law enforcement for the city. Overall, the city is comparable in safety to other small cities in the Tampa Bay area. Like any community, safety varies by neighborhood. Residential areas away from the main commercial corridors tend to be quieter. Visit specific neighborhoods at different times of day before purchasing.

What is Plant City FL famous for?

Plant City is best known as the 'Winter Strawberry Capital of the World' and home to the annual Florida Strawberry Festival. The city's agricultural heritage, particularly strawberry farming, defines its identity. The Strawberry Festival draws hundreds of thousands of visitors each year and features major concert performances.

Is Plant City growing?

Yes, Plant City has experienced steady growth with new subdivisions under development and downtown revitalization efforts attracting new businesses. The city has managed to grow while maintaining its small-town character. New construction ranges from affordable single-family homes to homes on larger lots on the city's outskirts.

How are the hospitals near Plant City?

AdventHealth Plant City (formerly South Florida Baptist Hospital) is located in the city and provides emergency, surgical, and inpatient services. For specialized care, Tampa General Hospital and other major medical centers in Tampa are within 30-40 minutes. Lakeland Regional Health is also accessible within 20-25 minutes to the east.

Does Plant City have public water and sewer?

Within the city limits, Plant City provides municipal water and sewer services through its own utility department. Properties outside the city limits in the Plant City area may be on well water and septic systems. City water and sewer is an advantage over rural properties that rely on wells and septic.

title: Tampa Bay Home Values 2026: What Your Home Is Worth
excerpt: Tampa Bay home values range from $280K in Plant City to $600K+ in South Tampa and Lithia. Learn what actually drives value: school zones, flood status, pool, lot type, and kitchen/bath updates.
content:
Your Tampa Bay home's value depends on recent comparable sales within a half-mile, your school zone, lot size, condition, flood zone status, and key upgrades like a pool or updated kitchen. Online estimates from Zillow and Redfin can be off by 5-15% in Tampa Bay because algorithms cannot account for school zone boundaries, flood zone differences, or renovation quality. A comparative market analysis from a local agent who works your neighborhood is the most accurate tool available for determining current value.

How Accurate Are Zillow Zestimates for Tampa Bay Homes?

Zillow's own published data shows their Zestimate has a median error rate of approximately 6-7% for on-market homes and higher for off-market homes. In Tampa Bay, the practical error is often greater because of specific local factors:

  • School zone boundaries: Two homes on the same street in the same subdivision can differ by $20K-$40K in value depending on which school feeds which, and Zillow does not capture this.
  • Flood zone differences: Two identical homes one block apart can have dramatically different insurance costs and values if one is in FEMA flood zone X and the other is in zone AE.
  • Individual renovation quality: A $40K kitchen renovation in a Valrico home adds value, but only if it was done well and matches the price point of the neighborhood. Zillow cannot assess renovation quality.
  • Seller concessions in recent sales: When a seller paid $10K toward buyer closing costs, the recorded sale price may be inflated. Comps using that sale without adjusting for concessions overestimate value.

The Zestimate is a useful starting point for getting a ballpark, nothing more. Do not list or make an offer based solely on an online estimate.

What Factors Drive Home Values Most in Tampa Bay?

School Zone

In Hillsborough County's eastern suburbs, school zone is arguably the single most powerful value driver. The premium for A-rated high school zones is quantifiable and consistent:

  • Homes in the Newsome HS zone (33596 in Valrico) sell for $25K-$50K more than identical homes in adjacent zones
  • Homes in the Bloomingdale HS zone command similar premiums over lower-rated alternatives
  • Homes in the Plant HS zone in South Tampa carry significant school premiums
  • In Wesley Chapel, homes in the Wiregrass Ranch High zone can sell for more than adjacent homes feeding other schools

This matters most for families. Buyers without school-age children or investors are less affected by school zone premiums and sometimes find better value in non-premium zones.

Flood Zone Status

Florida's flood insurance costs are a material factor in home value. A home in FEMA flood zone X (minimal risk, no flood insurance required by lenders) is worth more than an equivalent home in zone AE (high risk, flood insurance required). The insurance cost difference can be $2,000-$8,000+ per year. Buyers model this into their monthly payment. The value differential between an X-zone and AE-zone home in the same neighborhood routinely runs $15K-$40K.

Pool

In Tampa Bay's climate, a pool adds genuine value. The increment depends on neighborhood price range:

  • $280K-$380K neighborhoods: pool adds $12K-$22K
  • $380K-$500K neighborhoods: pool adds $18K-$35K
  • $500K+ neighborhoods: pool adds $25K-$55K depending on features (heated, salt system, screen enclosure, outdoor kitchen)

A basic above-ground pool adds minimal value. An in-ground pool with screen enclosure and salt system adds meaningfully. A new pool with outdoor kitchen and summer kitchen can add $50K+ in value in the right neighborhood.

Kitchen and Bathroom Updates

Modern finishes add verifiable value at resale. Quartz or granite counters, soft-close cabinets, and stainless appliances in the kitchen typically add $10K-$20K over original builder-grade finishes in the $350K-$500K price range. Updated primary and secondary bathrooms add $5K-$15K each. The key caveat: updates must match the neighborhood. A $40K kitchen in a $300K neighborhood will not return full value. Updates shine when the rest of the neighborhood supports that price point.

Lot Type and Premium

Standard interior lots are the baseline. Premium lots add:

  • Conservation/preserve backing: $10K-$30K (no rear neighbors, natural view)
  • Cul-de-sac: $5K-$15K (more usable yard, less traffic)
  • Corner lot: Can be positive (more yard) or negative (more traffic exposure) depending on configuration
  • Pond/lake frontage: $15K-$60K depending on water body size and view
  • Oversized/irregular lot: Varies; large lots in an area of standard lots add value, but only up to a point

Roof Age

Florida's insurance market makes roof age a significant value factor. A home with a roof over 20 years old is harder and more expensive to insure. Some carriers will not write a policy on a 20+ year roof. Buyers know this and discount their offers accordingly. A roof replacement ($12,000-$22,000 in Tampa Bay) on a home with an aging roof often returns close to its cost in sale price because it removes an insurance objection.

Current Home Value Ranges by Tampa Bay Area (2026)

Area Typical Range Premium Zip/Zone Entry Point
Valrico $350K-$560K 33596 (Newsome HS) $340K
Brandon $310K-$460K Near Bloomingdale HS $295K
Riverview $325K-$500K Newsome/Bloomingdale zones $315K
Lithia $430K-$850K+ FishHawk / Newsome HS $425K
Wesley Chapel $340K-$600K Epperson, Bexley $330K
Lutz $370K-$650K Cheval gated areas $360K
Plant City $285K-$420K Walden Lake area $270K
Land O'Lakes $355K-$580K Concord Station, Wilderness Lake $345K
Parrish $330K-$550K Watercolor, newer communities $315K

What Is a CMA and Why Is It Better Than Zillow?

A Comparative Market Analysis (CMA) is a professional analysis of your home's likely market value based on 3-6 recent sales of comparable homes, adjusted for differences in size, condition, upgrades, and location. A good CMA accounts for what algorithms miss:

  • Does the home back to a power line or a busy road?
  • Is the roof 3 years old or 20 years old?
  • Was the kitchen renovation done professionally or by a homeowner doing their own work?
  • Is the garage converted to living space (which many buyers dislike)?
  • Were there seller concessions in the comparable sales?

These details swing value by $15K-$50K and no algorithm captures them. A CMA from an agent who knows the neighborhood does.

How to Prepare for a Listing CMA

When Barrett (or any agent) comes to evaluate your home before listing, gather:

  • Date and cost of any major improvements (roof, HVAC, kitchen remodel, bathroom remodel, pool installation)
  • Your property's square footage (verify against tax records, which sometimes differ from actual finished area)
  • HOA documents and monthly fee
  • Flood zone determination if available
  • Any notable lot features: backing to conservation, pond, etc.

This information helps an agent provide a more accurate valuation and a stronger listing narrative for buyers.

Want to Know What Your Tampa Bay Home Is Worth?

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience. I provide free, no-obligation CMAs for Tampa Bay homeowners. No Zillow estimate needed.

Contact Barrett Call (813) 733-7907

Frequently Asked Questions: Tampa Bay Home Values 2026

What is the average home price in Tampa Bay in 2026?

The median home price in the Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater metro area runs approximately $370K-$420K as of 2026, but this varies enormously by specific location. Hillsborough County suburban neighborhoods range from $285K (Plant City entry-level) to $850K+ (Lithia luxury). Coastal Pinellas properties are often $450K-$1M+. The metro-wide average obscures dramatic local variation.

Are Tampa Bay home prices dropping in 2026?

Tampa Bay home prices have moderated from their 2022 peak but have not declined broadly. Most submarkets show values 3-8% below the 2022-2023 peak with modest appreciation since. The market is segmented: entry-level homes under $350K face strong demand from first-time buyers. Move-up homes $350K-$500K have more inventory. Luxury above $700K has the most supply relative to demand. Conditions vary significantly by neighborhood.

Does a pool add value in Tampa Bay?

Yes. A well-maintained in-ground pool with screen enclosure typically adds $15K-$40K in value in Tampa Bay depending on the neighborhood price range and pool condition. Buyers at the $350K-$500K price range particularly value pools in Florida's climate. A neglected pool, or one that is old and requires significant work, can actually reduce value or complicate the sale if the buyer has to budget for pool remediation.

How do school zones affect home values in Tampa Bay?

A-rated school zones in Hillsborough County's eastern suburbs add a measurable premium of $20K-$50K over comparable homes in adjacent lower-rated zones. The Newsome HS and Bloomingdale HS zones in Valrico and south Brandon are the clearest examples. Buyers with school-age children are willing to pay significant premiums to secure the A-rated zone. Investors and buyers without children are less influenced by school zones.

How long does it take to sell a home in Tampa Bay?

In 2026, well-priced Tampa Bay homes in desirable areas typically sell within 15-35 days. Overpriced homes sit 60-90+ days and often require price reductions. The days-on-market target has increased from the 2021-2022 frenzy (3-7 days) to a more normalized market. Pricing accurately from day one is critical, as homes that linger develop a stigma that makes buyers wonder what is wrong with them.

title: Berry Bay and Wimauma FL New Construction 2026: Affordable Homes Guide
excerpt: Berry Bay in Wimauma offers D.R. Horton homes starting under $320K, making it one of Hillsborough County's most affordable new construction options. Southshore Bay adds a 7-acre crystal lagoon nearby. Here is the complete guide.
content:
Wimauma in southern Hillsborough County has two distinct new construction markets: Berry Bay, D.R. Horton's affordable community with homes starting under $320,000, and Southshore Bay, a Metro Development Group crystal lagoon community with homes starting in the low $310Ks. Both offer new construction with builder warranties in Hillsborough County at prices significantly below the county median. Here is what buyers need to know about both communities and the broader Wimauma market in 2026.

What Is Berry Bay and Who Is It Best For?

Community Overview

Berry Bay is a D.R. Horton community located off US-301 in Wimauma, surrounded by conservation land and wetlands in southern Hillsborough County. The community offers D.R. Horton's Express series (entry-level), Tradition series (mid-range), and Emerald series (upper-mid) homes. Floor plans range from 1,400 to 2,600 square feet with 3-5 bedrooms. All D.R. Horton homes feature concrete block construction, the D.R. Horton Smart Home technology package, and stainless steel appliances as standard.

The community includes a neighborhood pool, open green space, and basic amenities typical of D.R. Horton's lower-CDD-cost product. Berry Bay is not an amenity-heavy resort community. It is a well-located, new construction neighborhood for buyers whose primary priorities are price, builder warranty, and Hillsborough County location.

Who Berry Bay Is Best For

Berry Bay fits a specific buyer profile. First-time buyers who cannot compete in Brandon or Riverview pricing. VA and FHA buyers who benefit from D.R. Horton's experience with government-backed financing. Investors looking for affordable rental inventory in a growing south Hillsborough corridor, where 3-bedroom single-family homes can rent for $1,800-$2,200/month. Buyers who work in the south Hillsborough employment corridor, near Sun City Center, or at MacDill AFB.

Berry Bay is not for buyers who want walkable shopping and dining or a resort amenity package. Wimauma's commercial development is still limited. Nearby Apollo Beach and Sun City Center provide more established retail options, but both require 10-15 minutes of driving. If proximity to US-301 commercial development is acceptable and affordability is the primary driver, Berry Bay delivers.

Berry Bay Pricing in 2026

As of mid-2026, D.R. Horton's Express series homes at Berry Bay start approximately $309,000-$330,000 for 1,400-1,600 sq ft floor plans. Tradition series runs $340,000-$420,000 for 1,700-2,200 sq ft. Emerald series with premium finishes runs $400,000-$500,000 for 2,200-2,600 sq ft. Lot premiums for conservation or pond views add $8,000-$20,000 to base prices. HOA fees run approximately $80-$120/month. CDD fees at Berry Bay are modest compared to resort communities: $500-$1,500/year depending on phase.

Southshore Bay: The Lagoon Alternative Next Door

What Is Southshore Bay

Southshore Bay is a Metro Development Group community approximately 5 miles from Berry Bay along US-301 in Wimauma, featuring a 7-acre MetroLagoons crystal lagoon (the same technology as Epperson in Wesley Chapel and Mirada in San Antonio). Multiple builders are active including D.R. Horton, Lennar, and Ryan Homes. The lagoon, beach entry, water sports, and resort-style amenity center differentiate Southshore Bay from Berry Bay as a product type, at a higher total monthly cost.

Southshore Bay Pricing and Total Cost

New construction homes at Southshore Bay run $310,000-$520,000 depending on builder, series, and lot. The apparent base price is similar to Berry Bay. However, CDD fees at Southshore Bay run $2,000-$3,500/year, and HOA fees add $150-$250/month. On a $380,000 home, the monthly cost comparison looks like this:

  • Berry Bay: $1,900/month mortgage + $100 HOA + $100 CDD = approximately $2,100/month (plus taxes/insurance)
  • Southshore Bay: $1,900/month mortgage + $200 HOA + $250 CDD = approximately $2,350/month (plus taxes/insurance)

The $250/month premium for Southshore Bay versus Berry Bay at the same base price buys the lagoon amenity. Whether that is worth it depends on how often you would use the lagoon and how much the resort lifestyle matters to your household.

Wimauma Schools: What Families Need to Know

Hillsborough County School Zone

Wimauma communities are served by Hillsborough County Public Schools. As of 2026, the primary schools serving Berry Bay and Southshore Bay residents include Sumner High School (opened 2021, serving south Hillsborough growth communities), Shields Middle School, and Cypress Creek Elementary. Sumner High School is a newer facility with strong initial reviews but does not yet have the established academic track record of Hillsborough's top-rated schools like Bloomingdale or Newsome.

For buyers where school zone prestige is a primary decision factor, Wimauma's schools are a trade-off versus communities in the Bloomingdale or Newsome attendance zones in Brandon or Valrico. Buyers who prioritize affordability and are comfortable with a developing school record at Sumner High will find the trade-off acceptable. The school facilities themselves are modern and well-equipped.

Commute From Wimauma: The Real Numbers

Destination Distance Non-Peak Time Peak Time
Downtown Tampa30-35 miles35-45 min50-75 min
Brandon/Riverview12-18 miles15-22 min25-35 min
MacDill AFB28-32 miles30-40 min45-60 min
Sun City Center8-10 miles10-15 min15-20 min
Tampa Int'l Airport35-38 miles40-50 min55-75 min
Sarasota45-50 miles50-60 min65-85 min

The US-301 corridor is Wimauma's primary commute artery. Traffic on US-301 north toward the I-75 interchange has grown significantly as Wimauma's population expanded. The I-75 junction at Gibsonton Drive can back up substantially during peak hours. Buyers who commute to Tampa should plan on 50-75 minutes in peak traffic, which is manageable but not close-in suburban commute territory.

Berry Bay vs. Southshore Bay: Which Should You Choose?

Factor Berry Bay Southshore Bay
Base home price$309K-$500K$310K-$520K
Lagoon amenityNoYes (7 acres)
CDD fees/yr$500-$1,500$2,000-$3,500
