What Are Total Monthly Costs in 55+ Communities?

The monthly HOA number is only the starting point. Here is the full picture for a $450K home in a typical 55+ community:

  • Mortgage (30-yr at 6.5%, 20% down): ~$2,275/month
  • Property taxes (est.): ~$450/month ($5,400/yr with homestead)
  • Homeowner's insurance: ~$250/month ($3,000/yr for newer construction)
  • HOA: $300-$500/month
  • Total: $3,275-$3,475/month before utilities, golf fees, or CDD

Many buyers moving from northern states where property taxes are high are surprised that Florida's insurance costs offset some of the tax savings. Budget honestly for the full monthly cost before committing to a 55+ community.

Should You Buy or Rent First When Retiring to Tampa Bay?

If you are relocating from out of state, I strongly recommend renting for 6-12 months before buying. Tampa Bay's communities vary dramatically in character, and the difference between Sun City Center and Valencia Lakes or between the Wesley Chapel market and the Venice market matters enormously for daily lifestyle. Seasonal rentals (January through April) let you experience the community during peak season. Many 55+ communities have rental units available for seasonal stays, which is the best market research you can do.

Planning your Tampa Bay retirement? I am Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective with 23+ years of real estate experience. I work with relocating retirees regularly and can help you compare all the 55+ options honestly. Call (813) 733-7907 or email barrett@nowtb.com.

Frequently Asked Questions: Tampa Bay 55+ Retirement Communities

What is the best 55+ community in Tampa Bay?

The best 55+ community depends entirely on your priorities. For best value and golf, Sun City Center or Kings Point. For resort amenities and newer construction, Valencia Lakes or Esplanade communities. For Tampa proximity and modern homes, Del Webb South Fork or Del Webb Wesley Chapel. For Southwest Florida lifestyle, Del Webb Lakewood Ranch or Esplanade Lakewood Ranch. There is no single best option without knowing what matters most to you.

How much does it cost to live in Sun City Center, FL?

Sun City Center single-family homes start around $250K and range to $650K+ for golf-front properties. HOA fees vary by section: $150-$400/month for single-family, plus a community amenity fee of approximately $200/month. Kings Point condos start around $150K with HOA fees of $600-$900/month that typically include some utilities and golf access. Total monthly costs for a $350K home with typical fees run $2,500-$3,500/month including mortgage, taxes, insurance, and HOA.

What is the difference between Sun City Center and Valencia Lakes?

Sun City Center is an established large-scale community (16,000+ homes, 200+ clubs, golf included, homes from $150K-$650K+) built primarily from the 1960s-1990s. Valencia Lakes is a newer GL Homes resort community (2010s-2020s construction, $400K-$700K homes, $350-$500/month HOA, no golf but resort-quality amenities). Sun City Center offers more value and community scale; Valencia Lakes offers newer construction and more upscale finishes at a higher price point.

Is Tampa Bay a good place to retire?

Yes. Tampa Bay offers no state income tax, a large selection of 55+ communities at multiple price points, excellent healthcare infrastructure including Moffitt Cancer Center and Tampa General Hospital, warm year-round weather, Gulf beaches within 45-90 minutes depending on location, and a growing arts and dining scene. The main trade-offs are increasing homeowner's insurance costs, hurricane risk requiring preparedness, and summer heat and humidity from June through September.

Should I rent before buying in a Tampa Bay 55+ community?

Yes, if you are relocating from out of state. Renting for 6-12 months before buying lets you experience different communities, understand seasonal versus year-round dynamics, and confirm the lifestyle fits before committing. Many 55+ communities have rental units available. The cost of renting for a year is modest compared to the risk of buying in the wrong community for your lifestyle.

title: Arbor Oaks Brandon FL: New Construction Deep Dive (Prices, CDD, Schools)
excerpt: Arbor Oaks is a Taylor Morrison new construction community off Lumsden Rd in Brandon FL, featuring modern floorplans from $350K-$500K, CDD fees, and builder warranties. Complete guide by Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

What is Arbor Oaks in Brandon FL like?

Arbor Oaks is a newer Taylor Morrison community off Lumsden Road in Brandon, featuring modern floorplans from $350K to $500K, CDD fees, and builder warranties - making it one of the most popular new construction options for relocating families in the 33510 zip code. Browse the Brandon neighborhoods map and search Brandon homes for sale.

  2. What Was Here Before Arbor Oaks?

  6. What Schools Serve Arbor Oaks?
  7. What Is Daily Life Like in Arbor Oaks?
  8. Who Should Buy in Arbor Oaks?
  9. Barrett's Take on Arbor Oaks
  10. Arbor Oaks FAQs
Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Homes

Arbor Oaks Quick Facts

CategoryDetails
Zip Code33510
LocationOff Lumsden Rd, eastern Brandon - Hillsborough County
BuilderTaylor Morrison
Year Built Range2018-Present
Price Range$350K-$500K
Home Sizes1,600-3,000+ sq ft
Lot Sizes0.12-0.22 acres
HOA Fees~$50-$80/month
CDD FeesYes - ~$1,800-$2,400/year (on tax bill)
SchoolsLimona Elementary, McLane Middle, Bloomingdale High
Community AmenitiesPlayground, walking trails, dog park
Commute to Downtown Tampa25-35 minutes via I-75 or Selmon Expressway

There are plenty of new construction communities popping up across Brandon and eastern Hillsborough County, but Arbor Oaks stands out for a specific reason: it gives relocating families a turnkey, modern home in a location that actually makes sense for daily life. Sitting right off Lumsden Road in the 33510 zip code, this Taylor Morrison community has been one of the steadiest-selling new builds in Brandon since the first models opened. I'm Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective, and I've walked buyers through this community dozens of times. Here's what you actually need to know before buying here.

What Was Here Before Arbor Oaks?

Before the first shovel hit the ground, the Arbor Oaks parcel was agricultural land - mostly cattle pasture and a handful of citrus groves that had been thinning out since the freezes of the 1980s and the arrival of citrus greening in the 2000s. If you talked to old-timers in the Lumsden Road corridor, they'd remember this stretch as wide-open ranchland with a few horse farms scattered between the subdivisions. Hillsborough County's eastward growth pattern had been creeping this direction for years, and when the land was rezoned for residential planned development, Taylor Morrison moved quickly to secure the parcel.

The site was attractive to developers because it had decent elevation for Florida - sitting above the 100-year flood zone on most lots - and direct frontage on Lumsden Road, which connects to both Providence Road and Lithia-Pinecrest. Unlike some of the infill projects squeezed into existing Brandon neighborhoods, Arbor Oaks had enough acreage to create proper stormwater retention ponds and community green space. That planning matters when you're living through a Florida summer and watching drainage do its job.

Who Built Arbor Oaks and What Are the Floorplans?

Taylor Morrison is a national builder with a strong Florida presence, headquartered right here in the Tampa Bay area. They're known for energy-efficient construction, open-concept designs, and a design center process that lets buyers customize finishes before the home is complete. In Arbor Oaks, they've offered a rotation of floorplans ranging from roughly 1,600 to over 3,000 square feet - typically three to five bedrooms, two to three bathrooms, and two-car garages.

The architectural style leans contemporary Florida - concrete block construction, tile roofs, impact-rated windows in most models, and open kitchens with oversized islands. The owners suites feature walk-in closets and dual vanities as standard. One thing I point out to buyers: Taylor Morrison includes their TM LiveSmart program, which bundles energy-efficient HVAC systems, tankless water heaters, and smart home wiring into the base price. That's not always the case with national builders - some charge premiums for those upgrades.

Builder warranties typically include a 1-year bumper-to-bumper warranty, a 2-year mechanical systems warranty (plumbing, electrical, HVAC), and a 10-year structural warranty. I always tell buyers to document everything during their first year - settlement cracks, minor cosmetic issues, anything - and submit warranty claims before that first anniversary hits. The builder is generally responsive, but you need to be proactive.

Looking at New Construction in Brandon?

Barrett Henry has walked buyers through Arbor Oaks and every new construction community in the area. Get honest comparisons before you sign with a builder.

Call (813) 733-7907 Schedule a Consultation

What Does It Cost to Live in Arbor Oaks?

Base prices have ranged from the low $350s to just over $500K depending on the floorplan, lot premium, and structural options selected at the design center. Lot premiums for conservation or pond-view lots can add $10K-$25K to the base price. Interior upgrades - extended tile, quartz countertops, upgraded cabinets - can easily add another $15K-$40K depending on how far you go in the design center.

Resale values have held steady as the community has matured. Homes that closed in the low $400s during the early phases have generally maintained or increased in value, which is a positive sign for long-term equity. Brandon's overall market has been resilient compared to some of the more speculative markets in Pasco and northern Hillsborough County.

How Do CDD Fees Work in Arbor Oaks?

This is the question every buyer asks, and it's the one where I spend the most time in new construction communities. CDD stands for Community Development District. When a developer builds infrastructure - roads, sidewalks, stormwater systems, community amenities - they can finance those costs through municipal bonds. Those bonds get repaid by homeowners through an annual CDD assessment that appears on your property tax bill. In Arbor Oaks, that assessment typically runs $1,800-$2,400 per year depending on your lot.

CDD fees are separate from your HOA dues. The HOA covers community maintenance, common area landscaping, and amenity upkeep. The CDD pays off the infrastructure bonds. CDD bonds typically have a 20-30 year term, so you'll be paying them for the life of the bond unless you prepay (which some communities allow). When comparing Arbor Oaks to an older community like Bloomingdale that has no CDD, you need to factor that $150-$200/month CDD into your total housing cost. It changes the math.

What Schools Serve Arbor Oaks?

Arbor Oaks is zoned for Limona Elementary, McLane Middle School, and Bloomingdale High School - all part of the Hillsborough County Public Schools system. Bloomingdale High has consistently been one of the higher-performing high schools in the Brandon/Valrico area, which is a major draw for families relocating from out of state. McLane Middle is centrally located and feeds directly into Bloomingdale High. Limona Elementary serves the younger grades and has a solid community reputation.

Private school options nearby include Bell Shoals Baptist Academy, Foundation Christian Academy, and several Montessori programs in the Brandon corridor. For families considering magnet programs, Hillsborough County offers some of the best magnet school options in Florida, with application-based admission.

What Is Daily Life Like in Arbor Oaks?

The Lumsden Road corridor gives Arbor Oaks residents easy access to everyday conveniences without the Brandon Boulevard traffic congestion. Publix, Winn-Dixie, CVS, and a mix of restaurants are all within a five-minute drive. The Westfield Brandon mall and the restaurant cluster at I-75 and SR-60 are about 10-15 minutes west. Brandon Regional Hospital is a straight shot down Lumsden to Brandon Boulevard.

Inside the community, the vibe is young families and working professionals. You'll see strollers on the walking trails in the evening, kids at the playground after school, and neighbors walking dogs past the retention ponds. The community is still new enough that the landscaping hasn't fully matured - you won't find the canopy oaks of older Brandon neighborhoods yet - but the community spaces are well-maintained and the HOA keeps standards consistent.

Commute-wise, I-75 is accessible via Lumsden to Providence Road, and the Selmon Expressway is reachable through Riverview or via Brandon Boulevard. Most residents report 25-35 minute commutes to downtown Tampa during peak hours, which is competitive with anything in this part of Hillsborough County.

Who Should Buy in Arbor Oaks?

  • Relocating families who want a move-in ready, modern home without the hassle of renovating an older property
  • First-time buyers who can stretch into the mid-$300s and want builder warranty protection
  • Remote workers who need dedicated home office space - several floorplans include flex rooms or lofts
  • Buyers who value energy efficiency - newer construction means lower utility bills and modern insulation standards

If you want mature trees, large lots, and established character, Arbor Oaks isn't the right fit. Look at Brandon Lakes or Four Winds Estates instead. If you want modern construction with warranty coverage and a predictable HOA environment, this community delivers.

Barrett's Take on Arbor Oaks

I've shown Arbor Oaks to a lot of out-of-state buyers, and it consistently makes the short list for families moving from the Northeast or Midwest. The homes are well-built, the floorplans make sense for modern life, and the location on Lumsden gives you access to everything without sitting in Brandon Boulevard traffic. The CDD fees are the one thing I always flag - they're not a deal-breaker, but you need to understand them before you commit. When I run the numbers with buyers, I compare total monthly cost (mortgage + taxes + insurance + HOA + CDD) against an older home in a no-CDD community. Sometimes the newer home wins on energy savings and lower maintenance. Sometimes it doesn't. That's the conversation you need to have with a REALTOR who knows the numbers, not just the sales pitch.

Arbor Oaks - Frequently Asked Questions

Are Arbor Oaks CDD fees permanent?

CDD bonds typically have a 20-30 year term. Once the bonds are fully paid off, the CDD assessment drops significantly, though a small operations and maintenance fee may remain for ongoing infrastructure upkeep.

Can I negotiate the price on a Taylor Morrison home?

National builders rarely discount the base price, but they frequently offer incentives on closing costs, design center upgrades, or preferred lender credits. Having your own REALTOR represent you (at no cost to you) gives you an advocate who can negotiate these incentives on your behalf.

Is Arbor Oaks in a flood zone?

Most lots in Arbor Oaks sit in FEMA Flood Zone X (minimal risk), meaning flood insurance is not required by most lenders. However, all Florida homeowners should consider flood coverage - it's relatively inexpensive in Zone X and protects against unexpected events.

What's the resale outlook for new construction in Brandon?

Brandon's resale market for newer construction has been stable. Homes purchased in early phases of communities like Arbor Oaks have generally held or appreciated in value. The key factor is location - Lumsden Road access and proximity to Brandon's job centers support long-term demand.

Do I need a REALTOR when buying new construction?

Absolutely. The builder's sales agent represents the builder, not you. Your REALTOR can review the purchase agreement, negotiate incentives, attend inspections, and ensure your interests are protected throughout the process. There's no additional cost to you - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Why Do Families Move to FishHawk Ranch for the Schools?

FishHawk Ranch in Lithia, FL (zip code 33547) is one of the most school-driven real estate markets in the Tampa Bay area. Families relocating to Hillsborough County consistently rank FishHawk among their top choices specifically because of the school zones serving the community. The combination of top-rated elementary, middle, and high schools within a master-planned community makes FishHawk a standout for families with children at any grade level.

Unlike many communities where school quality varies, FishHawk's assigned schools, FishHawk Creek Elementary, Barrington Middle School, and Newsome High School, are all well-regarded by parents and consistently receive strong performance ratings from the state of Florida. This K-12 pipeline of quality education is a major driver of property values in the community.

What Schools Are Zoned for FishHawk Ranch?

FishHawk Creek Elementary

FishHawk Creek Elementary is located within the FishHawk Ranch community itself, making it incredibly convenient for families. The school serves students in grades K-5 and is known for strong academic performance, dedicated teachers, and active parent involvement through its PTA. The school offers gifted programs and has consistently received high marks on Florida state assessments.

Having an elementary school inside the community means many students can walk or bike to school, reducing commute stress and creating a true neighborhood school atmosphere.

Barrington Middle School

Located near the community, Barrington offers a range of academic programs including advanced coursework that prepares students for Newsome High School's rigorous programs. The school emphasizes STEM education and has active extracurricular programs including sports, arts, and academic clubs.

Newsome High School

Newsome High School is the crown jewel of the FishHawk school zone and arguably the biggest driver of real estate demand in the area. Newsome consistently ranks among the top public high schools in Hillsborough County and is well-known across the Tampa Bay region for:

  • International Baccalaureate (IB) Program one of the most rigorous academic programs available in public schools, preparing students for college-level work
  • Advanced Placement (AP) courses a wide selection of AP classes across multiple subjects
  • Athletic programs competitive sports including football, basketball, swimming, cross country, and more

  • College readiness high graduation rates and strong college acceptance records

The Newsome High School zone is a premium factor in FishHawk real estate. Homes zoned for Newsome typically command higher prices than comparable homes in other Hillsborough County school zones.

In FishHawk's case, the premium may be even higher because the community combines top schools with resort-level amenities and a desirable location.

For homebuyers, this means that while you may pay more upfront for a home in FishHawk, the investment is supported by strong and consistent demand. Homes in the Newsome High School zone tend to sell faster and hold their value better than the broader Hillsborough County market.

What Should Buyers Know About School Zoning Before Purchasing?

It's important to verify current school zoning before making a purchase decision. School zone boundaries can change, and Hillsborough County Public Schools periodically reviews and adjusts zone lines. Here are some tips:

  • Always verify the exact school zone for a specific address through the Hillsborough County Public Schools website, don't rely solely on community marketing materials
  • If you're buying in a newer section of FishHawk or a bordering community, double-check that the address is within the Newsome High zone
  • Ask your REALTOR® about any pending zone changes that might affect the property
  • Consider both current zoning and the age of your children, a zone change five years from now could matter

Yes, FishHawk Creek Elementary is located within the FishHawk Ranch community. Many families can walk or bike to school, which is a major convenience and one of the reasons families choose FishHawk.

Does the Newsome High School zone include areas outside FishHawk?

Yes, the Newsome High School attendance zone includes FishHawk Ranch as well as some surrounding areas in Lithia and parts of nearby communities. However, zone boundaries can change, so always verify the zoning for a specific address before purchasing.

title: Is FishHawk Ranch a Good Place to Live? Honest Review
excerpt: An honest review of living in FishHawk Ranch, the pros, the cons, the fees, the schools, and what real residents say about this popular Lithia FL community.
content:
What's It Really Like to Live in FishHawk Ranch?

FishHawk Ranch in Lithia, FL (33547) consistently ranks among the most desirable communities in the Tampa Bay area. But is it actually a good place to live, or is the hype overblown? After helping buyers purchase homes in FishHawk for years, I can give you an honest assessment of the pros and cons. This isn't a marketing brochure, it's a real look at what living in FishHawk Ranch is actually like.

The short answer: FishHawk Ranch is an excellent community for families, outdoor enthusiasts, and anyone who values a well-maintained, amenity-rich neighborhood. But it's not perfect for everyone. The fees add up, the commute to Tampa can be long, and the HOA rules are strictly enforced. Let's break it all down.

What Are the Best Things About Living in FishHawk?

Here's what residents consistently praise about the community:

Top-rated schools. This is the number one reason families move to FishHawk. The Newsome High School zone, combined with FishHawk Creek Elementary and Barrington Middle, gives families a K-12 pipeline of quality public education. Read more in our FishHawk schools guide.

Unmatched amenities. 32+ miles of trails, the FishHawk Sporting Club, multiple pools, splash parks, dog parks, sports courts, a skate park, and community gardens. Very few communities in Florida can match this amenity package. Residents genuinely use these facilities, they're not decorative.

Strong sense of community. FishHawk has an active social calendar with regular events, food truck nights, holiday celebrations, and fitness classes. The community Facebook groups are active, and neighbors tend to know each other. For families with children, the built-in social network is a significant benefit.

Safety. FishHawk is a well-maintained community with security patrols and well-lit streets. Crime rates in the Lithia/33547 zip code are lower than the Hillsborough County average. Families regularly cite safety as a top reason for choosing FishHawk.

Nature and outdoor access. Beyond the community trails, residents are close to Alafia River State Park (mountain biking), Lithia Springs (swimming), and numerous parks. The preserved wetlands within FishHawk itself provide a natural setting that's unusual for a suburban community.

Have Questions About FishHawk Ranch Real Estate?

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience and knows the Tampa Bay market inside and out.

(813) 733-7907

Get Expert Help Today

What Are the Downsides of Living in FishHawk?

No community is perfect. Here are the common complaints and things to consider:

The commute. FishHawk is about 25 miles from downtown Tampa and 20 miles from Brandon. During rush hour, the drive to Tampa can take 40-50 minutes or more. If you work in downtown Tampa, South Tampa, or Westshore, the daily commute is real. Residents who work remotely or in the Brandon/Riverview/Plant City corridor tend to be happier with the location.

HOA and CDD fees. Combined, these can add $400-500+ per month to your housing costs beyond your mortgage and taxes. That's significant. Some buyers are caught off guard by the total when they see the full picture. Read our FishHawk HOA and CDD fee guide for exact numbers.

HOA enforcement. The FishHawk Ranch HOA is known for strict enforcement of community standards, lawn maintenance, exterior paint colors, parking regulations, and holiday decorations all have rules. If you value a well-maintained appearance, this is a positive. If you prefer more freedom with your property, the rules may feel restrictive.

Limited nightlife and dining. FishHawk has local restaurants and shops in the Village center, but it's not a walkable urban area. For nightlife, diverse dining, or cultural events, you'll need to drive to Brandon, Riverview, or Tampa. The community is suburban by design.

Summer heat. This isn't unique to FishHawk, it's a Florida reality. But the lack of coastal breezes means inland communities like FishHawk can feel hotter during peak summer months. The pools and splash parks help, but July through September is genuinely hot.

Who Is FishHawk Ranch Best For?

Based on years of helping buyers in this community, FishHawk Ranch is the best fit for:

  • Families with school-age children who prioritize the Newsome High School zone
  • Active adults who want trails, fitness facilities, and outdoor amenities
  • Remote workers or people who work in the eastern Hillsborough corridor
  • Buyers who value community and want an active neighborhood social scene
  • 55+ buyers looking at the Encore at FishHawk active adult section

Who Might Want to Look Elsewhere?

  • Buyers who commute to downtown Tampa daily and want a shorter drive
  • People who want large acreage or agricultural zoning (look at Dover or rural Lithia)
  • Buyers on a tight budget who can't absorb the combined HOA/CDD fees
  • People who want walkable urban living with restaurants and nightlife nearby

Want to see FishHawk Ranch in person? I'm Barrett Henry with 23+ years of real estate experience, and I'd love to tour the community with you. Browse FishHawk homes for sale or call me at (813) 733-7907. You can also check out the complete FishHawk community guide or compare FishHawk vs Waterset to explore your options.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is FishHawk Ranch safe?

Yes, FishHawk Ranch is considered a safe community. The Lithia/33547 zip code has lower crime rates than the Hillsborough County average. The community has security patrols, well-maintained common areas, and well-lit streets. Like any area, it's not crime-free, but residents consistently cite safety as one of FishHawk's strengths.

What is the average home price in FishHawk Ranch?

As of mid-2026, the median home price in FishHawk Ranch is approximately $475,000 to $525,000. Prices range from the mid-$300s for older townhomes and villas to over $900,000 for newer construction on larger lots. The price you pay depends on the village, home size, lot size, and age of the home.

Is FishHawk Ranch good for retirees?

FishHawk Ranch offers the Encore section, a 55+ active adult community with its own clubhouse and amenities. For active retirees who want trail access, fitness facilities, and a social community, it's an excellent option. However, if you prefer a quieter, less family-oriented atmosphere, a dedicated 55+ community might be a better fit.

How far is FishHawk Ranch from the beach?

FishHawk Ranch is approximately 45-60 minutes from the nearest Gulf coast beaches (St. Pete Beach, Clearwater Beach) depending on traffic. It's an inland community, so beach access requires a drive. Some residents consider this a drawback, while others appreciate the lower insurance costs that come with being away from the coast.

Does FishHawk Ranch flood?

FishHawk Ranch was designed with extensive water management systems including retention ponds, drainage infrastructure, and preserved wetlands that help manage stormwater. While no area is completely flood-proof, the community's engineering significantly reduces flood risk. Individual flood zone status varies by lot, always check FEMA flood maps for a specific address before purchasing.

title: Is Brandon FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Guide
excerpt: Is Brandon FL a good place to live? Honest pros and cons covering cost of living, schools, safety, commute times, neighborhoods, and what daily life really looks like in 2026.
content:
Brandon FL is one of the best suburbs in the Tampa Bay area for families, commuters, and anyone who wants affordable living with big-city access. Located in eastern Hillsborough County with ZIP codes 33510 and 33511, Brandon offers a median home price below the Tampa Bay average, solid schools, tons of shopping and dining, and a 20-minute commute to downtown Tampa. It is not perfect -- traffic on SR-60 can be brutal and flooding risk is real in some areas -- but for overall value, Brandon consistently ranks among Tampa Bay's top suburbs.

What Is the Cost of Living in Brandon FL?

Brandon's cost of living runs about 3-5% below the Tampa metro average and well below national coastal city averages. The median home price in 2026 sits around $340,000-$380,000, which buys a 3-bedroom, 2-bath home with a garage in a decent neighborhood. Compare that to South Tampa at $600K+ or even Riverview at $350K-$400K, and Brandon stands out for value.

Groceries, utilities, and everyday expenses are close to national average. Florida has no state income tax, which effectively gives you a 5-10% raise compared to moving from states like California, New York, or Illinois. Property taxes in Hillsborough County run 1.9-2.2% of assessed value, but the homestead exemption saves homeowners roughly $800-$1,100 annually.

Monthly housing costs for a typical Brandon family: mortgage payment around $2,000-$2,400 (with taxes and insurance), utilities $200-$300 (summer AC drives the high end), and groceries similar to national average. Use the mortgage calculator to estimate your specific numbers.

How Are the Schools in Brandon FL?

Brandon is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools, the 7th largest district in the nation. School quality varies significantly by zone, so the specific address you buy at matters more than the city name.

The top-rated school zones feeding through Brandon include:

  • Bloomingdale High School zone -- covers Bloomingdale, parts of Heather Lakes, and surrounding neighborhoods. Consistently rated B or higher.
  • Brandon High School zone -- covers central Brandon neighborhoods and several established communities.
  • Riverview High School zone -- covers southern Brandon and into Riverview.

Families specifically targeting the Bloomingdale High zone should look at neighborhoods south of Bloomingdale Avenue. Several private school options are also available, including Bell Shoals Baptist Academy and Nativity Catholic School. Check the Brandon FL school zones guide for detailed boundary maps.

What Are the Best Neighborhoods in Brandon FL?

Brandon has dozens of distinct neighborhoods, each with a different personality and price point:

  • Arbor Oaks -- Established, tree-lined streets, no CDD, close to everything. Popular with families wanting a classic Florida neighborhood feel.
  • Providence Lakes -- Gated community with lakes, pool, and playground. Well-maintained with active HOA. Prices from mid-$300s to $500s.
  • Heather Lakes -- Lakefront living with larger lots, Bloomingdale school zone, and a quiet residential feel.
  • Sterling Ranch -- Newer construction with modern floorplans and community amenities.
  • La Collina -- Golf course community with upscale homes, resort-style pool, and Brandon's most exclusive address.
  • Bloomingdale -- Large neighborhood with its own commercial district, schools, and parks.

Browse all available homes on the Brandon homes for sale page.

What Is the Commute Like from Brandon?

Brandon's location along the I-75 corridor and Selmon Expressway makes commuting manageable but not painless. Here are realistic drive times during rush hour:

DestinationOff-PeakRush Hour
Downtown Tampa18-22 min30-45 min
Westshore / Airport20-25 min35-50 min
MacDill AFB25-30 min40-55 min
St. Petersburg35-40 min50-70 min
Lakeland30-35 min35-45 min

The Selmon Expressway toll lanes shave 10-15 minutes off the westbound commute during peak hours. Many Brandon residents who work in Tampa use the Selmon daily -- budget $3-$5 per day in tolls. Remote workers love Brandon because you get suburban space and quiet without paying Tampa prices.

What Are the Downsides of Living in Brandon FL?

No honest guide would skip the drawbacks:

  • Traffic on SR-60 (Brandon Boulevard) -- The main east-west corridor through Brandon gets congested during rush hour and weekends near Westfield Brandon mall.
  • Flooding in some areas -- Parts of Brandon sit in FEMA flood zones, particularly near the Alafia River and low-lying areas. Always check flood maps before buying. Read the Brandon FL flood zones guide for details.
  • Summer heat and humidity -- June through September is hot. AC bills can hit $250-$350/month for larger homes.
  • Limited nightlife -- Brandon is a family suburb. For nightlife, you are heading to Tampa's SoHo or Ybor districts.
  • Hurricane exposure -- Like all of Tampa Bay, Brandon faces hurricane season June-November. Inland location reduces storm surge risk, but wind damage and flooding remain concerns.

Is Brandon FL Safe?

Brandon's crime rates are below the Tampa city average and comparable to other established Hillsborough County suburbs. As an unincorporated community, Brandon is patrolled by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office (HCSO), which maintains a strong presence in the area.

Like any suburb, safety varies by specific neighborhood. Gated communities like Providence Lakes have lower crime rates than some areas near the commercial corridors. Barrett can pull crime data for any specific neighborhood you are considering.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Brandon FL a good place to raise a family?

Brandon is one of the top family suburbs in Tampa Bay. Strong school options including the Bloomingdale High zone, dozens of parks and youth sports leagues, family-friendly restaurants, and affordable housing make it a popular choice. Most neighborhoods have sidewalks, community pools, and playground access.

Is Brandon FL expensive to live in?

Brandon is more affordable than most Tampa Bay suburbs. The median home price of $340K-$380K is below the metro average, and Florida's lack of state income tax further reduces living costs. Monthly expenses for a family of four typically run $4,500-$6,000 including housing, which is competitive for a major metro area.

What is Brandon FL known for?

Brandon is known for Westfield Brandon mall (one of Tampa Bay's largest), its central location between Tampa and Lakeland, strong community parks and youth sports programs, and diverse dining options along Causeway Boulevard and Brandon Boulevard. It is also one of the most ethnically diverse suburbs in Hillsborough County.

How far is Brandon from the beach?

Brandon is approximately 45-60 minutes from Gulf beaches like Clearwater Beach and St. Pete Beach, depending on traffic. Ben T. Davis Beach on the Courtney Campbell Causeway is about 30 minutes away. While not beachfront, Brandon's inland location provides better protection from storm surge during hurricane season.

Is Brandon FL growing?

Brandon is largely built out, but infill development and redevelopment continue. New construction communities in surrounding areas like Riverview and Valrico absorb much of the growth. Brandon's population remains stable with steady demand driven by location, schools, and affordability. Contact Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for the latest market data.

title: Riverview FL vs Wesley Chapel: Which Is Better?
excerpt: Riverview or Wesley Chapel, which Tampa Bay suburb is better for your family? Schools, home prices, taxes, commute, lifestyle, and an honest side-by-side comparison.
content:
Riverview and Wesley Chapel are two of the fastest-growing suburbs in the Tampa Bay metro area, and they compete directly for the same buyer: families and professionals relocating to Florida who want newer homes, good schools, and reasonable commute times. Both communities have exploded in population over the past decade. But they are different in ways that matter. This comparison breaks down the key factors so you can decide which one fits your family better.

How Do Home Prices Compare?

Both communities offer new and resale homes across a wide price range, but Riverview generally has the lower entry point:

  • Riverview median home price: $350,000-$425,000 across ZIP codes 33569, 33578, and 33579. New construction starts in the low $300s for townhomes and mid-$300s for single-family homes
  • Wesley Chapel median home price: $400,000-$500,000 across ZIP codes 33543, 33544, and 33545. New construction starts in the mid-$300s but skews higher overall due to more upscale communities
  • Price per square foot: Riverview averages $190-$220/sq ft while Wesley Chapel averages $210-$250/sq ft, reflecting Wesley Chapel's newer inventory mix and higher-end communities
  • Bottom line: Riverview gives you more house for less money. Wesley Chapel offers newer, more upscale communities but at a premium

How Do Property Taxes Compare?

This is one of the biggest differences between the two communities and it is often overlooked:

  • Riverview (Hillsborough County): Combined millage rates of 19-22 mills. Hillsborough County has some of the highest property tax rates in the Tampa Bay metro area
  • Wesley Chapel (Pasco County): Combined millage rates of 17-20 mills. Pasco County's lower base millage means lower property taxes on comparable homes
  • Annual difference: On a $400,000 home with homestead exemption, the difference can be $800-$1,500/year in favor of Wesley Chapel. Over a 10-year hold, that adds up significantly
  • CDD fees: Both communities have widespread CDD assessments in newer neighborhoods. Riverview CDDs range from $1,500-$3,500/year; Wesley Chapel CDDs are similar

How Do the Schools Compare?

Both communities offer strong public schools, but the districts operate differently:

  • Riverview schools (Hillsborough County): Riverview High School, Sumner High School, and Spoto High School. Hillsborough is the eighth-largest school district in the nation, a large district with extensive resources but also bureaucratic complexity. School zones vary significantly by neighborhood
  • Wesley Chapel schools (Pasco County): Wiregrass Ranch High School, Wesley Chapel High School, and newer additions. Pasco is a smaller district that has invested heavily in new school construction to keep pace with growth. Some Wesley Chapel schools are very new with modern facilities
  • Bottom line: Both areas have schools that attract families. Wesley Chapel's newer schools have more modern facilities. Riverview's established schools have longer track records and more developed programs. Research specific schools rather than comparing districts broadly

How Do the Commutes Compare?

Your commute destination determines which community works better:

  • To downtown Tampa: Riverview wins, 25-40 minutes via Selmon Expressway vs 35-50 minutes from Wesley Chapel via I-75 to I-275
  • To MacDill Air Force Base: Riverview wins clearly, 25-35 minutes vs 45-60 minutes from Wesley Chapel
  • To USF/Temple Terrace: Wesley Chapel wins, 20-30 minutes via I-75 vs 30-40 minutes from Riverview
  • To Westshore business district: Similar, both 25-40 minutes depending on traffic
  • To St. Petersburg: Riverview has a slight edge, 35-50 minutes vs 40-55 minutes from Wesley Chapel
  • To New Tampa/Bruce B. Downs corridor: Wesley Chapel wins, 10-20 minutes vs 25-35 minutes from Riverview

Riverview or Wesley Chapel? Let's Find Your Best Fit.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective, works across Tampa Bay and can show you homes in both communities. 23+ years of real estate experience helping families compare suburbs and find their match.

(813) 733-7907  |  Compare Your Options

How Does the Lifestyle Compare?

Daily life in these two suburbs feels different:

  • Shopping and retail: Wesley Chapel has a clear advantage with The Shops at Wiregrass (upscale outdoor mall), Tampa Premium Outlets, and more developed retail corridors. Riverview's shopping is functional (strip centers, big box stores) but less destination-oriented
  • Dining: Wesley Chapel has a wider restaurant selection, including more upscale and chain options around the Wiregrass area. Riverview's restaurant scene is growing but is more casual and locally driven
  • Outdoor recreation: Riverview wins with Alafia River State Park (6,000+ acres, mountain biking, kayaking) and the Alafia River corridor. Wesley Chapel has Flatwoods Park and the Upper Tampa Bay Trail but less dramatic natural features
  • Community feel: Both are suburban and car-dependent. Neither has a walkable town center. Wesley Chapel feels more polished and planned; Riverview feels more diverse and organic
  • Nightlife: Neither is a nightlife destination. Both communities' residents drive to Tampa for evening entertainment

Which Is Better for Investors?

Both communities attract real estate investors, but the profiles differ:

  • Riverview for investors: Lower entry prices, higher rental yields on paper, more inventory to choose from, and strong school-zone-driven tenant demand. Higher property taxes in Hillsborough County reduce cash flow
  • Wesley Chapel for investors: Higher entry prices but lower property taxes, strong appreciation due to continued growth and development, and premium rents from tenants attracted to newer communities and schools. Lower yields but potentially stronger appreciation
  • Both: CDD fees are common in both communities and reduce cash flow equally. Tenant quality in school-zone-driven neighborhoods is similar in both areas

The Verdict: Which Should You Choose?

Choose Riverview if you:

  • Want the most house for your money
  • Work in downtown Tampa, MacDill AFB, or South Tampa
  • Value outdoor recreation (Alafia River, state park)
  • Are a first-time buyer looking for affordable new construction
  • Want a more diverse, organic community character

Choose Wesley Chapel if you:

  • Work in New Tampa, USF, or the Bruce B. Downs corridor
  • Value upscale retail and dining (The Shops at Wiregrass)
  • Prioritize lower property taxes
  • Want the most modern schools and infrastructure
  • Are willing to pay more for a more polished suburban environment

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Riverview cheaper than Wesley Chapel?

Yes. Riverview's median home prices are 10-20% lower than Wesley Chapel's on comparable properties. Entry-level new construction starts lower in Riverview. However, Riverview's higher Hillsborough County property taxes partially offset the lower purchase price. Over a long hold, the total cost difference is narrower than the sticker price suggests.

Which has better schools, Riverview or Wesley Chapel?

Both communities have strong public schools that attract families. Wesley Chapel's schools tend to be newer with more modern facilities due to Pasco County's rapid construction of new schools. Riverview's established schools (particularly Riverview High) have longer track records and more developed extracurricular programs. The best approach is to research the specific schools that serve your target neighborhoods.

Is Wesley Chapel safer than Riverview?

Crime statistics show both communities are relatively safe suburban areas. Wesley Chapel's newer development and smaller geographic footprint contribute to slightly lower per-capita crime rates. Riverview's larger size and more diverse mix of neighborhoods produce more variation in safety metrics. Both communities' master-planned neighborhoods with active HOAs are consistently safe.

Which is closer to Tampa, Riverview or Wesley Chapel?

Riverview is closer to downtown Tampa and South Tampa. Riverview to downtown Tampa is 25-40 minutes. Wesley Chapel to downtown Tampa is 35-50 minutes. However, Wesley Chapel is closer to New Tampa, USF, and the I-75 north corridor. The better commute depends entirely on where you work.

Can I find waterfront homes in Riverview or Wesley Chapel?

Riverview has more waterfront options along the Alafia River and retention pond/lake lots in master-planned communities. Wesley Chapel has pond and lake-front lots within planned communities but no significant river frontage. True waterfront living with river access is a Riverview advantage.

title: Homeowners Insurance in Brandon FL: Costs, Coverage, and How to Save
excerpt: What does homeowners insurance cost in Brandon FL? Average premiums, coverage requirements, wind mitigation discounts, and tips to lower your insurance costs.
content:
How much does homeowners insurance cost in Brandon FL? The average annual premium ranges from $2,400 to $4,800 depending on your home's age, construction type, roof condition, and coverage limits. Florida has some of the highest insurance costs in the nation, but Brandon buyers can take specific steps to reduce premiums significantly. Here is what you need to know.

What Is the Average Cost in Brandon?

Home Value Est. Annual Premium Monthly Cost
$250,000$2,000-$3,200$167-$267
$350,000$2,800-$4,200$233-$350
$500,000$3,600-$5,400$300-$450
$750,000$5,000-$7,500$417-$625

Brandon homes tend to fall slightly below the Florida state average because the area is inland (lower hurricane surge risk) and most homes are in favorable flood zones.

What Factors Affect Insurance Costs?

Roof Age and Material

Your roof is the single biggest factor. A roof over 15 years old will dramatically increase costs, and some insurers will not cover homes with roofs over 20 years old. Metal and concrete tile roofs get better rates than shingle.

Construction Year and Type

Homes built to current Florida Building Code (2002+) receive significantly lower premiums. Concrete block construction (CBS) is cheaper to insure than wood-frame.

Wind Mitigation Features

A wind mitigation inspection ($75-$150) can document features that earn major discounts:

  • Hurricane shutters or impact windows 5-15% discount
  • Hip roof design 3-8% discount
  • Secondary water resistance (SWR) 15-35% discount
  • Roof-to-wall connections clips vs. straps vs. toe nails affect pricing
  • Opening protection all openings protected earns the biggest discount

How Can I Lower My Insurance?

  1. Get a wind mitigation inspection can save $500-$2,000/year
  2. Upgrade your roof a new roof meeting current code can cut premiums 20-40%
  3. Install impact windows or hurricane shutters
  4. Increase your deductible 2% to 5% hurricane deductible lowers annual premium
  5. Bundle with auto insurance 10-15% multi-policy discounts
  6. Install a security system 3-5% discounts
  7. Shop multiple carriers get at least 3-5 quotes
  8. Consider Citizens Insurance Florida's state-backed insurer, sometimes competitive

What Does Standard Coverage Include?

  • Dwelling coverage structure of your home
  • Other structures fences, sheds, detached garages
  • Personal property furniture, electronics, clothing
  • Liability if someone is injured on your property
  • Loss of use living expenses if home is uninhabitable
  • Wind/hurricane damage included (separate deductible)

What Is NOT Covered?

  • Flood damage requires separate policy. See Brandon flood zone guide.
  • Sinkholes optional coverage
  • Mold limited in most policies
  • Normal wear and tear

Do I Need Flood Insurance in Brandon?

If your home is in a FEMA flood zone (Zone A or AE), your lender will require it. Even in low-risk Zone X, flood insurance is recommended, roughly 25% of flood claims come from low-risk areas. Costs range from $400-$1,200/year for low-risk to $1,200-$3,000+ for high-risk zones. Check our Brandon flood zone guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is insurance so expensive in Florida?

Hurricane exposure, litigation costs (Florida has more insurance lawsuits than any other state), and reinsurance costs. The state has passed reforms to stabilize the market, but costs remain high.

Can I get insurance with an old roof?

Increasingly difficult. Many insurers will not write policies on roofs over 15-20 years old. Citizens Insurance is more lenient. Barrett recommends budgeting for a roof replacement if buying an older home.

What is the hurricane deductible?

A separate deductible, typically 2%, 5%, or 10% of dwelling coverage. On a $350,000 home with a 2% deductible, you pay the first $7,000 of hurricane damage. Higher deductibles lower your premium.

Should I get sinkhole coverage in Brandon?

Sinkhole activity in Brandon is relatively low compared to Pasco or Hernando counties. However, the coverage provides peace of mind. Discuss with your insurance agent.

When should I start shopping for insurance?

As soon as you have an accepted offer. You need proof of insurance before closing, and some carriers take 2-3 weeks to issue a policy. Barrett's team provides insurance agent referrals at contract time.

title: Seffner FL Parks & Recreation: Outdoor Spaces and What to Do in 33584
excerpt: Guide to parks, sports fields, playgrounds, and outdoor recreation in Seffner FL including county parks, nature areas, and nearby attractions.
content:
Quick Answer

Seffner has several Hillsborough County parks within the community and immediate access to major regional parks and recreation facilities within a 10-20 minute drive. While Seffner does not have master-planned private amenities, residents have access to sports fields, lakes, playgrounds, trails, and the full Brandon Sports and Aquatic Complex nearby. It offers more outdoor options than many buyers initially expect.

What County Parks Are in or Near Seffner FL?

Seffner (33584) is an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County, which means parks are managed by Hillsborough County Parks and Recreation. The county system is extensive and includes neighborhood parks, regional parks, and nature preserves within reasonable driving distance of Seffner.

Seffner Community Park

The primary community park serving the Seffner area. Features sports fields suitable for baseball, softball, and multipurpose use, a playground area, picnic facilities with covered pavilions, and open green space. Youth sports leagues use the park during spring and fall seasons. It serves as a gathering point for the community and is maintained by Hillsborough County Parks.

Lake Weeks Park

Lake Weeks provides waterfront access in the broader Seffner/Mango area. The park includes fishing access, open green space along the shoreline, and picnic areas. For families and fishing enthusiasts, lakefront parks like this are one of the underappreciated outdoor amenities in the eastern Hillsborough area. No formal boat ramp, but bank fishing is available.

Seffner-Mango Park Area

The Seffner-Mango area (the name references the historic Mango community adjacent to Seffner along US-92) has additional Hillsborough County park space. This is a quieter area with a residential character, and the parks serve the local neighborhood population. Good for walking, casual recreation, and kids' outdoor play.

What Major Parks Are Within 15 Minutes of Seffner?

Seffner's location at the intersection of I-4 and SR-60 puts residents within easy reach of several significant Hillsborough County parks and recreation destinations that serve as extensions of what the immediate area offers.

Eureka Springs Regional Park (Temple Terrace, ~15 min)

One of Hillsborough County's largest public parks, located near Temple Terrace on US-92. Eureka Springs features multiple sports fields, a butterfly garden, picnic pavilions, nature trails, and open space. The park hosts organized sporting events and community gatherings throughout the year. For Seffner residents, it is the most significant regional park within easy reach via US-92 West.

Brandon Sports and Aquatic Complex (~10-12 min via SR-60 W)

The Brandon Sports and Aquatic Complex is a major Hillsborough County recreation facility with an indoor aquatic center (competition and recreation pools), sports courts, and organized programming. For swimming lessons, lap swim, youth sports registration, and fitness programming, this facility is essentially Seffner residents' closest major recreation center. The drive from most Seffner locations is 10-12 minutes west on SR-60.

Turkey Creek (Lithia/Alafia River Area, ~20-25 min via SR-60 E)

For outdoor enthusiasts, the Alafia River State Trail and related recreation areas along SR-60 East are accessible within 20-25 minutes. The Alafia area offers multi-use trails, mountain biking, kayak access to the river, and natural Florida scenery. More active outdoor recreation than what the immediate Seffner area provides.

What Sports and Recreation Activities Are Available to Seffner Residents?

Youth Sports Leagues

Seffner is served by the East Hillsborough Youth Athletic League, which organizes baseball, softball, football, and soccer programs for youth. Games and practices use parks in the Seffner and Brandon areas. Registration typically opens several months before each season. Hillsborough County Parks and Recreation also runs programs through Brandon Parks for Seffner-area youth.

Fishing

Eastern Hillsborough County has extensive freshwater fishing opportunities. Lake Weeks, the Alafia River corridor, and multiple smaller lakes within 15-20 minutes of Seffner offer largemouth bass, bluegill, and catfish fishing. A Florida freshwater fishing license is required for adults. The combination of no-HOA properties and fishing access nearby makes Seffner attractive to outdoor-oriented buyers.

Cycling and Walking

Seffner's residential streets and the broader Mango/Seffner area offer neighborhood walking routes. The area is not as bike-infrastructure-rich as planned communities, but many residents walk the neighborhood streets and access nearby parks by bicycle. The Alafia River State Trail, 20-25 minutes east, is the region's primary dedicated multi-use trail for cycling enthusiasts.

Private Fitness and Recreation

Multiple private gym and fitness options are within 10-15 minutes of Seffner in the Brandon area, including major chain fitness centers on SR-60 and Brandon Boulevard. For Seffner residents who want fitness amenities comparable to what HOA communities offer, these options fill the gap effectively.

The public recreation options within 10-20 minutes, particularly the Brandon Sports Complex, provide meaningful recreation access without the ongoing costs.

Does Seffner FL have a community pool?

Seffner does not have a community-wide public pool, as it is an unincorporated area without HOA amenities. Many Seffner residents install private pools on their properties, which is feasible given the larger lots.

Are there youth sports leagues in Seffner FL?

Yes. Youth sports leagues serving Seffner operate through Hillsborough County Parks and Recreation and local youth athletic associations. Baseball, softball, football, basketball, and soccer programs serve the Seffner/eastern Hillsborough community. Seffner Community Park hosts practices and games.

Is there fishing near Seffner FL?

Yes. Lake Weeks in the Seffner/Mango area provides freshwater fishing access. The Alafia River is approximately 20-25 minutes east, offering river fishing and kayaking access. A Florida freshwater fishing license is required for adults age 16 and older.

title: Moving to Brandon FL from Out of State: Relocation Guide
excerpt: Moving to Brandon FL from out of state? Complete 2026 relocation guide covering cost of living, neighborhoods, schools, jobs, taxes, and what to do before and after you arrive.
content:
Thousands of people relocate to Brandon FL every year, and most of them come from states with higher taxes, higher home prices, and worse weather. Brandon sits in eastern Hillsborough County -- ZIP codes 33510 and 33511 -- about 20 minutes east of downtown Tampa. It offers affordable housing, no state income tax, solid schools, and year-round warm weather. This guide covers everything you need to know before and after your move.

Why Are So Many People Moving to Brandon FL?

Brandon attracts relocators for practical, financial reasons:

  • No state income tax -- Florida does not tax personal income. If you earn $100,000 and move from a state with 5% income tax, you keep an extra $5,000 per year.
  • Affordable housing -- Brandon's median home price of $340K-$380K buys a 3-bed, 2-bath home with a garage and yard. That same money gets you a studio apartment in many coastal cities.
  • Job growth -- Tampa Bay's economy is diversifying beyond tourism into tech, healthcare, finance, and defense. Major employers include USAA, Citibank, Moffitt Cancer Center, James A. Haley VA Hospital, and MacDill AFB.
  • Location -- 20 minutes to Tampa, 30 minutes to the airport, 45 minutes to Gulf beaches. Central enough to reach anything without living in urban density.
  • Schools -- Multiple high school zones including Bloomingdale High, Brandon High, and Riverview High. Quality varies by zone -- Barrett matches families to the right school zone during the home search.

What Should Out-of-State Buyers Do Before Moving to Brandon?

Here is your pre-move checklist, in order:

  1. Visit first -- Fly down for 3-4 days. Drive neighborhoods at different times (morning commute, evening, weekend). Barrett offers relocation tours that cover multiple neighborhoods in a day.
  2. Get pre-approved by a Florida lender -- Use a lender licensed in Florida. Out-of-state lenders sometimes cause delays with Florida-specific title requirements. Ask Barrett for lender recommendations.
  3. Research school zones -- If you have kids, the school zone determines where you buy. Check the Brandon FL school zones guide before falling in love with a house in the wrong zone.
  4. Check flood zones -- Some Brandon areas carry flood insurance requirements that add $1,200-$8,000 annually. Read the Brandon FL flood zones guide.
  5. Understand homestead exemption timing -- You must file by March 1 of the year after purchase. Miss it and you lose a year of tax savings. See the homestead exemption guide.
  6. Budget for insurance -- Florida homeowner's insurance is higher than national averages. Budget $2,500-$5,000+ annually depending on home value and age. Get quotes before closing.

Which Brandon Neighborhoods Are Best for Relocators?

Relocators tend to gravitate toward neighborhoods with community amenities, newer homes, and easy highway access:

  • Providence Lakes -- Gated, community pool, playground, well-maintained. Mid-$300s to $500s. Popular with families relocating from the Northeast.
  • La Collina -- Golf course community with upscale homes from $400K-$700K+. Resort-style amenities. Great for empty nesters and move-up buyers.
  • Arbor Oaks -- Established neighborhood with mature trees, no CDD, walkable to shopping. Mid-$300s. Good for buyers who want character over newness.
  • Bloomingdale -- Large community with its own schools, parks, and commercial area. Prices from $300K-$500K+. Feels like its own small town within Brandon.
  • Sterling Ranch -- Newer construction, modern floorplans, community amenities. Great for buyers wanting move-in-ready without the maintenance of an older home.

Browse everything available on the Brandon homes for sale page. Barrett can filter by school zone, flood zone, price range, and commute distance to your workplace.

Have Questions About Brandon Real Estate?

Barrett Henry specializes in relocations to Tampa Bay with 23+ years of real estate experience. One call gets your entire move organized.

📞 (813) 733-7907 Send a Message

What Is the Job Market Like in Brandon FL?

Brandon itself is primarily residential and retail, but its location puts you within commuting distance of Tampa Bay's major employment centers:

Employment HubDrive from BrandonMajor Employers
Downtown Tampa20-35 minBanking, law, government
Westshore Business District20-40 minUSAA, corporate offices, tech
MacDill AFB25-40 minMilitary, defense contractors
USF / Moffitt Area25-35 minHealthcare, education, research
Brandon / Local5-10 minRetail, healthcare, services

Remote workers represent a growing percentage of Brandon buyers. The suburb offers home office space at a fraction of Tampa prices, reliable internet infrastructure, and plenty of coffee shops and co-working spaces for when you need to get out of the house.

What Do Relocators Get Wrong About Moving to Florida?

Common mistakes Barrett sees from out-of-state buyers:

  • Underestimating insurance costs -- Florida homeowner's insurance has increased significantly since 2022. Budget $2,500-$5,000+ annually and get quotes before you close.
  • Ignoring flood zones -- "It doesn't flood here" is something you will hear from sellers. Trust FEMA maps, not neighbors.
  • Buying in the wrong school zone -- Hillsborough County does not allow school choice transfers easily. Your address determines your school. Verify before purchasing.
  • Not filing homestead exemption -- This is free money. File by March 1 or lose a year of savings.
  • Skipping the visit -- Photos and Google Street View do not show you traffic patterns, neighborhood noise, or the feel of daily life. Visit before you buy.
  • Assuming all of Florida is flat and boring -- Brandon and surrounding areas have rolling terrain, old-growth oaks, rivers, and springs. It is not the pancake-flat stereotype.

What Should You Do in Your First 30 Days After Moving to Brandon?

  1. Update your driver's license -- Florida requires a new license within 30 days of establishing residency. Visit your local tax collector's office.
  2. Register your vehicle -- Florida vehicle registration is due within 10 days of employment or enrollment in school. Annual registration fees vary by vehicle weight.
  3. File for homestead exemption -- If you purchased before January 1, file by March 1 for that tax year. If you purchased after January 1, you will file the following year.
  4. Register to vote -- Available at the driver's license office or online at registertovoteflorida.gov.
  5. Set up utilities -- TECO Energy (electric), Hillsborough County water, Spectrum or Frontier (internet).
  6. Find a primary care doctor -- Healthcare demand in Tampa Bay is high. Get on a patient list early. BayCare and AdventHealth have locations near Brandon.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to move to Brandon FL?

Moving costs from out of state to Brandon range from $3,000-$8,000 for a full-service move depending on distance and volume. Add first-month expenses: security deposits, utility setup fees, and temporary housing if needed. Home purchase closing costs in Florida run 2-3% of the purchase price. An FHA loan can reduce your down payment to 3.5%.

Is Brandon FL good for remote workers?

Brandon is excellent for remote workers. Affordable homes with dedicated office space, no state income tax (keep more of your salary), reliable high-speed internet from Spectrum and Frontier, and plenty of coffee shops and co-working spaces. You get suburban quiet for focused work and Tampa access when you want to socialize.

What is the best time of year to move to Brandon FL?

October through April offers the best weather and the most inventory on the market. Summer (June-September) is hot and humid, making moving physically uncomfortable, but you may find better deals as the market slows slightly. Avoid hurricane season peak (August-October) for scheduling flexibility.

Do I need a car in Brandon FL?

Yes, a car is essential. Brandon has limited public transit (HART bus routes exist but service is infrequent). Everything from grocery shopping to commuting requires a vehicle. Most households have two cars. The upside: no paid parking almost anywhere in Brandon, and gas prices track national averages.

How do I find a good REALTOR in Brandon FL?

Look for an agent with deep local knowledge of Brandon neighborhoods, school zones, flood zones, and market conditions. Barrett Henry at REMAX Collective has 23+ years of real estate experience and specializes in relocations to Tampa Bay. Call (813) 733-7907 to start your relocation plan.

title: Durant Area Valrico FL: Subdivisions, Acreage, and Everything Between
content:
Quick Answer

What defines the Durant Road corridor in Valrico FL?

The Durant Road corridor encompasses multiple communities near Durant High School, featuring everything from 1970s ranch homes on multi-acre parcels to 2020s new construction. Prices range from $320K to $500K+ depending on acreage and updates. See our Valrico community guide for a broader overview.

What Makes the Durant Corridor Unique in Valrico?

The Durant Road corridor is where Valrico's suburban development meets its rural roots, and the result is a housing landscape unlike anything else in eastern Hillsborough County. Within a few miles of Durant High School, you can find a brand-new four-bedroom home on a quarter-acre lot in a planned subdivision, a 1970s ranch house on three acres with a barn and pasture, and a custom-built estate on five acres with a pond and horse facilities. This range of options exists because the Durant corridor developed in fits and starts over five decades rather than being master-planned by a single developer.

Durant Road itself is one of Hillsborough County's historic rural roads, running east from the Valrico core toward the Plant City corridor. The road has been widened and improved multiple times over the decades, but its character remains distinctly different from the commercial corridors of SR-60 or Bloomingdale Avenue. Commercial development along Durant Road is limited, which preserves the residential and semi-rural feel but means residents drive to Brandon or the SR-60 corridor for major shopping.

What Was the Durant Area Before Residential Development?

The Durant corridor was agricultural land for the entirety of its recorded history until residential development began encroaching in the 1960s and 1970s. Citrus groves, strawberry farms, and cattle ranches occupied the landscape in a patchwork pattern that reflected the diverse agricultural economy of eastern Hillsborough County.

Strawberry farming was particularly significant in this corridor. The sandy, acidic soil and the mild winter temperatures created ideal growing conditions, and small strawberry operations dotted the landscape alongside the larger citrus groves and cattle ranches. During the strawberry season (December through March), the area's farm stands would draw customers from Brandon and Tampa. While the large-scale strawberry farming has largely moved to the Plant City corridor to the east, a few small operations still exist in the Durant area, connecting the present to this agricultural heritage.

The cattle ranching history is still visible in the Durant corridor. Several properties along the road maintain their agricultural exemptions, with small herds grazing on acreage that has been in the same families for generations. These ranch properties are becoming increasingly rare as land values make residential development more economically attractive to landowners, but they contribute to the rural character that distinguishes the Durant corridor from more developed areas of Valrico.

How Did the Durant Area Develop Over 50 Years?

The 1970s-1980s: Homesteads and Ranchettes

The earliest residential development along the Durant corridor consisted of individual homes built on large parcels, typically one to five acres. These were not subdivision homes but rather custom builds on agricultural parcels, often constructed by the landowners themselves or by small local builders. The homes from this era are modest in size (1,200-2,000 square feet) but sit on lots that are enormous by today's standards. Many have outbuildings, workshops, barns, and the infrastructure of small agricultural operations.

The 1990s-2000s: Subdivisions Arrive

As Hillsborough County's population pushed eastward, developers began purchasing agricultural parcels along the Durant corridor and platting them for conventional subdivisions. Communities like Durant Oaks, Durant Woods, and Durant Trails were developed during this period, offering three-to-five-bedroom homes on quarter-acre lots with community amenities. These subdivisions brought sidewalks, streetlights, and HOA management to a corridor that had been defined by gravel driveways and fence lines.

The 2010s-2020s: New Construction and Infill

The most recent wave of development has filled in remaining parcels with new construction communities featuring modern floor plans, energy-efficient construction, and the amenity packages that today's buyers expect. These newer communities sit alongside the older ranch properties and the 1990s-2000s subdivisions, creating the eclectic housing mix that defines the Durant corridor today.

Comparing Durant Oaks, Durant Woods, and Durant Trails

Durant Oaks was among the first formal subdivisions in the corridor, with homes built primarily in the late 1990s through the mid-2000s. The community features mature landscaping, a community pool, and homes in the 1,800-2,600 square foot range. Prices typically fall between $360K and $460K. The "Oaks" name is earned: the community preserved many of the live oaks from the original property, giving it a canopy that newer developments lack.

Durant Woods developed slightly later, with most homes dating from the early to mid-2000s. The community has a more conventional subdivision layout with slightly smaller lots than Durant Oaks but comparable home sizes. Pricing runs $340K-$440K. The community amenities include a playground and common areas maintained by the HOA.

Durant Trails is the newest of the three named communities, with homes built from the mid-2000s through the early 2010s. The community features walking trails that connect to common areas and green spaces. Homes are 1,600-2,400 square feet with prices in the $330K-$430K range. The trail system provides walking and jogging routes that residents use heavily, particularly in the cooler months.

The Acreage Properties: What Buyers Need to Know

The large-acreage properties along the Durant corridor are a distinct market segment that requires different evaluation criteria than conventional subdivision homes. Properties on one to five-plus acres are available in the $400K-$600K+ range, with pricing driven as much by land value and agricultural potential as by the home itself.

Buyers considering acreage properties should evaluate well and septic systems (many are not on county water and sewer), agricultural exemptions (which can significantly reduce property taxes but come with usage requirements), outbuilding condition, fencing, and road access. These are not the same purchase considerations as a subdivision home, and working with an agent who understands rural property is essential.

The potential upside of acreage properties in the Durant corridor is substantial. As Hillsborough County continues to grow eastward, large parcels in the Valrico area become increasingly valuable. Buyers who purchase three to five acres today are acquiring land that developers will want in 10-20 years, and the agricultural exemption provides favorable tax treatment in the meantime.

Schools in the Durant Corridor

Durant High School is the anchor institution for this corridor, and its presence is a significant factor in the area's residential demand. The school has built a strong reputation for academics and athletics within the Hillsborough County School District, and the Durant zone is actively sought by families relocating to eastern Hillsborough County.

Elementary and middle school options in the corridor include multiple schools with strong performance ratings. School zoning in the Durant area can be complex due to the corridor's length and the presence of multiple elementary zones. Always verify specific assignments through the school district before purchasing.

Exploring the Durant Corridor?

Barrett Henry can help you navigate the differences between subdivision homes and acreage properties in the Durant area. From starter homes to estate parcels, the Durant corridor has options.

Call (813) 733-7907  |  Send a Message

Current Market in the Durant Corridor

The Durant corridor's pricing reflects its extreme variety. Subdivision homes in communities like Durant Oaks, Durant Woods, and Durant Trails trade in the $320K-$460K range. Acreage properties with homes run $400K-$600K+, with pricing heavily influenced by lot size, improvements, and agricultural exemption status. New construction in the corridor's newest communities starts in the $380K-$450K range and can exceed $500K for premium lots and upgraded floor plans.

Days on market vary significantly by property type. Well-priced subdivision homes in the named communities typically sell within 20-35 days. Acreage properties take longer, often 45-90 days, because the buyer pool for rural properties is smaller and more specialized. New construction absorption depends on builder pricing and the overall market tempo.

Who Should Buy in the Durant Area

The Durant corridor appeals to diverse buyers. Families seeking Durant High School zoning in a conventional subdivision find excellent options in the named communities. Buyers who want space, privacy, and the ability to keep animals or pursue hobby farming target the acreage properties. New construction buyers who want to be in the Durant zone without the renovation needs of older homes find options in the corridor's newest developments.

Barrett's Take on the Durant Corridor

The Durant corridor is the part of Valrico where I most enjoy working with buyers because the range of options is unlike anywhere else in eastern Hillsborough County. Within a 10-minute drive, I can show you a $340K three-bedroom in a planned subdivision, a $480K five-bedroom on two acres with a workshop and room for horses, and a brand-new four-bedroom with a pool for $440K. Try that in any other part of the county.

The acreage properties are the hidden gems of this corridor. Land in established Valrico is not being made anymore, and the properties with one to five acres along the Durant corridor represent a finite and diminishing supply. Buyers who secure acreage here are buying something that genuinely cannot be replicated, and the long-term value reflects that scarcity.
