title: Gibsonton FL Property Taxes: Rates, Exemptions & How to Pay
excerpt: Gibsonton FL property taxes follow Hillsborough County millage rates (19-21 mills total). Most Gibsonton neighborhoods have no CDD fees. Here is what to budget for a primary home purchase and how the homestead exemption saves you money.
content:
Quick Answer: Gibsonton FL Property Tax Rate

Gibsonton FL (unincorporated Hillsborough County, ZIP 33534) has a combined millage rate of approximately 18-22 mills depending on the specific taxing districts that apply to your address. There is no incorporated municipal millage. A $320,000 home without homestead pays roughly $6,400-$7,040/year. With the $50,000 homestead exemption (apply by March 1), the annual bill drops to approximately $5,400-$5,940. The Save Our Homes cap then limits assessment increases to 3% per year regardless of market value growth.

Property taxes are a recurring cost that affect your monthly budget and return on investment for years after purchase. Gibsonton FL (ZIP 33534) is unincorporated Hillsborough County, which means your property tax bill includes county, school board, and special district levies, but no municipal city tax. Here is everything you need to know about how property taxes work in Gibsonton.

What Is the Gibsonton FL Property Tax Rate?

Millage Rate Breakdown for Unincorporated Hillsborough County

Property taxes in Florida are expressed in mills. One mill equals $1 in tax per $1,000 of taxable assessed value. The total millage rate for a Gibsonton (33534) property is the sum of all applicable taxing authorities. Typical components include:

Taxing AuthorityApprox. Millage RateNotes
Hillsborough County BOCC (General)~5.5-6.2 millsCounty services, roads, parks
Hillsborough County School Board~6.5-7.5 millsK-12 public education funding
SW Florida Water Mgmt. District (SWFWMD)~0.25-0.35 millsRegional water management
Fire/EMS District (varies by address)~2.0-4.0 millsSeveral fire districts serve 33534
Hillsborough County Library~0.5-0.6 millsPublic library system
Children's Board~0.5 millsChildren's services
Municipal (City)0 millsNone, Gibsonton is unincorporated
Approximate Total~18-22 millsVaries by address and year

Because Gibsonton is unincorporated, there is no municipal city millage. This is an advantage compared to incorporated cities like Tampa, Riverview (if annexed), or Plant City, which layer a city millage on top of county levies. The exact millage rate for your specific address can be verified with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser at hcpafl.org or by calling (813) 272-6100.

How Is Property Tax Calculated in Gibsonton FL?

Step-by-Step Calculation

Florida uses assessed value (not market value) as the tax base. The calculation:

  1. Just (Market) Value: The Property Appraiser's estimate of market value as of January 1.
  2. Assessed Value: May differ from just value due to Save Our Homes cap (for homesteaded properties) or agricultural or other exemptions.
  3. Exemptions: Subtract applicable exemptions (homestead, disability, veteran, senior). Most homeowners use the $50,000 homestead exemption.
  4. Taxable Value: Assessed value minus exemptions.
  5. Tax Due: Taxable value ÷ 1,000 × total millage rate.

Sample Tax Calculation for a $320,000 Gibsonton Home

ScenarioAmount
Just (market) value$320,000
Minus homestead exemption-$50,000
Taxable value$270,000
Estimated total millage rate~20.0 mills
Estimated annual tax~$5,400
Without homestead: $320,000 × 20 mills = ~$6,400/yr. Actual rate varies by address; verify at hcpafl.org.

What Is the Florida Homestead Exemption and How Do I Get It?

The Standard $50,000 Homestead Exemption

Florida's homestead exemption reduces the taxable value of a primary residence by $50,000:

  • The first $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities, including schools.
  • The second $25,000 applies only to non-school tax levies (the school portion of your bill is calculated on a larger taxable value).

Net effect for a $320,000 home at 20 mills: roughly $700-$1,000 per year in tax savings versus no exemption. The savings compound over time as market values rise, because Save Our Homes protects your assessed value from increasing faster than 3% per year.

How to Apply for Homestead in Gibsonton FL

  • Deadline: March 1 of the tax year. Miss it and you pay a full year without the exemption.
  • Online: Apply at hcpafl.org (Hillsborough County Property Appraiser).
  • In person: 601 E. Kennedy Blvd., Tampa FL 33602. Phone: (813) 272-6100.
  • Required documentation: Florida driver's license or ID with the property address, vehicle registration showing the property address, and Social Security numbers for all owners.
  • Eligibility: Must own and occupy the property as your permanent primary residence as of January 1 of the year you are applying for the exemption.

How Does Save Our Homes Protect Gibsonton Homeowners?

The 3% Annual Cap

Florida's Save Our Homes (SOH) amendment limits the annual increase in the assessed value of a homesteaded property to 3% or the Consumer Price Index (CPI), whichever is lower. The cap applies starting in the year after you first receive the homestead exemption.

Example: You buy a Gibsonton home for $320,000 in 2026 and receive homestead. The market value increases to $350,000 in 2027 (a 9.4% increase). With SOH, your assessed value for 2027 can only increase by 3% (or CPI if lower), to approximately $329,600. You pay taxes on $329,600 minus exemptions, not on $350,000 minus exemptions. Over time, the "SOH difference" (market value minus assessed value) compounds and can produce significant tax savings.

SOH Resets When You Sell

The SOH benefit does not transfer to a new owner. When a Gibsonton home is sold, the Property Appraiser resets the assessed value to market value for the new owner. This means buyers of homes that have been owned for many years may see a significantly higher tax bill than what the current owner is paying. Always look up the current assessed value at hcpafl.org and calculate what your tax bill will be as the new owner, not what the current owner pays.

What Is Florida Portability and Does It Apply in Gibsonton?

Portability allows Florida homesteaded property owners to transfer up to $500,000 of their accumulated SOH benefit to a new homesteaded property anywhere in Florida. If you are selling a home in another Florida county or city where you have a large SOH difference, you can carry that benefit to your Gibsonton purchase and have your new assessed value set below market value from day one. To claim portability:

  • File form DR-501T (Portability Application) with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser when applying for homestead on your new Gibsonton property.
  • The deadline is March 1, same as the homestead application.
  • You have up to 3 years to transfer portability after selling your previous homesteaded property.

Portability is one of the most underused tax benefits in Florida real estate. Buyers moving from high-value markets (South Tampa, Pinellas County, Sarasota) can bring significant SOH carry-over to their Gibsonton purchase.

How to Look Up and Appeal Your Gibsonton Property Taxes

Looking Up Your Assessment

Search any Gibsonton property's assessed value, taxable value, and tax history at:
Hillsborough County Property Appraiser: hcpafl.org | (813) 272-6100 | 601 E. Kennedy Blvd., Tampa FL 33602
Hillsborough County Tax Collector: hillstax.org | (813) 635-5200

Filing a Value Adjustment Board Petition

If you believe your property's assessed value is higher than its market value, you can petition the Hillsborough County Value Adjustment Board (VAB). The petition must be filed by September of the tax year (deadline is typically the 25th day after the TRIM Notice mailing). File at hcpafl.org. The TRIM (Truth in Millage) Notice is mailed in August each year and shows your proposed assessed value, exemptions, and estimated tax before the bills are finalized.

Frequently Asked Questions: Gibsonton FL Property Taxes

What is the property tax rate in Gibsonton FL?

The combined millage rate for most Gibsonton (33534) properties is approximately 18-22 mills, including county, school board, SWFWMD, and fire/EMS district levies. There is no municipal city millage since Gibsonton is unincorporated. The exact rate depends on which fire district and other special districts apply to your specific address; verify at hcpafl.org.

How much are property taxes on a $320,000 home in Gibsonton FL?

Without homestead: approximately $6,400/year at 20 mills. With the $50,000 homestead exemption: approximately $5,400/year. After Save Our Homes kicks in, annual increases are capped at 3% regardless of market appreciation.

How does the Florida homestead exemption work in Gibsonton?

The $50,000 homestead exemption reduces the taxable assessed value of your primary residence by $50,000. Apply by March 1 at hcpafl.org or in person at 601 E. Kennedy Blvd., Tampa. You must own and occupy the home as your primary residence as of January 1 of the application year.

What is the Save Our Homes cap in Florida?

Save Our Homes caps annual increases in the assessed value of a homesteaded Florida property at 3% or CPI, whichever is lower. This means your tax bill grows slowly even if your home's market value rises rapidly. The cap resets when the property is sold.

Can I transfer my Save Our Homes benefit when I move within Florida?

Yes. Florida's portability provision allows you to transfer up to $500,000 of your accumulated SOH difference to a new homesteaded Florida property. File form DR-501T with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser by March 1 along with your homestead application.

Housing Costs: What Does Gibsonton Offer?

The Purchase Price Advantage

Gibsonton's primary cost advantage is its lower purchase price. At $295,000-$345,000 for a standard 3-bedroom home, Gibsonton prices are:

  • $75,000-$175,000 less than comparable homes in Apollo Beach (33572)
  • $50,000-$100,000 less than comparable homes in Riverview (33578)
  • $20,000-$60,000 less than comparable homes in Ruskin (33570) for newer construction

On a 30-year mortgage at 7%, every $50,000 less in purchase price saves approximately $280 per month in principal and interest payments. Over 30 years, a $125,000 purchase price difference translates to roughly $700/month in lower mortgage payments, or approximately $252,000 in total mortgage payments saved.

No CDD Fees: A Meaningful Advantage

Gibsonton's unincorporated, older-neighborhood character means no Community Development District (CDD) fees. Many comparable homes in Apollo Beach's Waterset community carry CDD assessments of $1,500-$3,000 per year ($125-$250/month). Over a 10-year ownership horizon, that is $15,000-$30,000 in additional costs that Gibsonton buyers avoid.

Insurance Costs in Gibsonton FL

Homeowner's Insurance

Homeowner's insurance costs in Gibsonton are a function of the home's age, construction type, roof age, roof shape, and wind mitigation features. CBS (concrete block structure) construction with a hip roof and recent wind mitigation report are the key variables that reduce premiums:

  • Best-case scenario (2015+ roof, hip shape, CBS, wind mitigation report): $3,200-$4,500/yr
  • Typical scenario (2005-2015 roof, mixed construction, some wind mitigation): $3,800-$5,500/yr
  • Higher-risk scenario (pre-2001 construction, gable roof, no wind mitigation): $5,000-$7,500+/yr

Get 2-3 insurance quotes before going under contract. Florida's insurance market has tightened significantly since 2022, and some insurers have exited the market entirely. Citizens Property Insurance Corporation is the state-backed insurer of last resort available when private market coverage is unavailable, but Citizens has its own limitations and rate schedule.

Flood Insurance

Not all Gibsonton homes require flood insurance. Properties in FEMA Zone X (most interior Gibsonton addresses) have no lender-required flood insurance. Properties in Zone AE (areas near Tampa Bay and lower-elevation zones) require flood insurance if there is a mortgage on the property. NFIP (National Flood Insurance Program) annual premiums for Zone AE properties in Gibsonton typically range from $1,200 to $4,000+ depending on elevation relative to Base Flood Elevation. Verify the flood zone at msc.fema.gov using the specific property address.

Utilities in Gibsonton FL

Electricity: Duke Energy Florida

Duke Energy Florida is the electric utility serving Gibsonton. Monthly electricity costs for a 1,500-2,200 sq ft home in Gibsonton:

  • Winter months (December-February): $90-$140/month
  • Spring/fall (March-May, October-November): $110-$170/month
  • Summer peak (June-September): $160-$240/month
  • Annual average: $120-$220/month

Florida homes run air conditioning almost year-round, with the peak July-September period driving the highest bills. Energy-efficient construction with newer HVAC systems and good insulation can reduce cooling costs by 20-30%. Contact Duke Energy at duke-energy.com or (800) 700-8744 for new service connections.

Water and Sewer: Hillsborough County Utilities

Most Gibsonton (33534) addresses are served by Hillsborough County Utilities (HCU) for water and sewer. Monthly HCU bills for average usage (2-3 person household) are typically $65-$100/month. Bills increase with lawn irrigation, pools, and larger households. Contact HCU at hcflgov.net/utilities or (813) 272-5977.

Internet: Spectrum and Frontier

Spectrum (Charter) and Frontier (fiber in some areas) are the primary internet providers in Gibsonton. Monthly costs:

  • Spectrum standard cable: $60-$80/month for 400-500 Mbps
  • Frontier fiber (where available): $65-$90/month for gigabit speeds

Fiber internet availability in 33534 varies by specific address. Verify provider availability at the property address before purchasing if high-speed internet is critical for your work-from-home situation.

How Does Gibsonton Compare to Nearby Communities for Total Monthly Cost?

Gibsonton consistently shows the lowest estimated total monthly cost in this comparison. The caveat: older Gibsonton homes may have higher insurance costs and maintenance costs than newer builds in Waterset or Riverview communities. A home inspection and insurance quotes are essential to get an accurate picture for any specific property.

Transportation Costs in Gibsonton

Gibsonton is car-dependent. There are no practical alternatives to owning a vehicle for daily errands, grocery shopping, or commuting. Estimated monthly transportation costs for Gibsonton residents:

  • One-car household: $500-$750/month (insurance, gas at current prices, maintenance/repair reserves)
  • Two-car household: $900-$1,400/month
  • Selmon Expressway tolls (if commuting to Tampa daily): approximately $2-$4 each way, or $80-$160/month for daily Tampa commuters

Frequently Asked Questions: Cost of Living in Gibsonton FL

Is Gibsonton FL affordable?

Yes. Gibsonton is one of the most affordable communities in Hillsborough County for homeowners. Median home prices of $295K-$345K are below the county median. Most neighborhoods have no HOA, no CDD fees, and property taxes benefit from the homestead exemption and Save Our Homes cap. The trade-offs are older housing stock and a car-dependent lifestyle.

How much does homeowner's insurance cost in Gibsonton FL?

Annual homeowner's insurance in Gibsonton ranges from approximately $3,200-$5,000 for well-maintained homes with newer roofs and wind mitigation, to $5,000-$7,500+ for older homes with gable roofs and no wind mitigation documentation. Get multiple quotes from Citizens and private insurers before going under contract.

Are there HOA fees in Gibsonton FL?

Many Gibsonton neighborhoods have no HOA or minimal HOA fees ($50-$150/month). There are no CDD communities within Gibsonton proper, which is a significant monthly savings compared to master-planned new construction communities in Apollo Beach and Riverview.

What are utility costs in Gibsonton FL?

Typical monthly utilities: electricity (Duke Energy) $120-$220; water/sewer (HCU) $65-$100; internet (Spectrum or Frontier) $60-$90. Total utility costs of $250-$410 per month for an average 1,500-2,200 sq ft home.

How does Gibsonton compare to Apollo Beach for cost of living?

Gibsonton is significantly less expensive monthly. A $320K Gibsonton home with no CDD or HOA compares to a $460K Apollo Beach/Waterset home with $300-$450/month in CDD and HOA fees. The monthly difference is approximately $900-$1,400 in favor of Gibsonton, before factoring in differences in insurance costs between older Gibsonton homes and newer Apollo Beach builds.

title: Lutz FL Property Taxes 2026: Rates, CDD Fees, and Exemptions
excerpt: Lutz FL property taxes run $5,500-$9,500/year depending on your community and CDD status. Learn about Hillsborough County millage, homestead exemption, and how CDD fees add to your annual cost.
content:
Property taxes in Lutz, Florida run approximately 1.8-2.2% of assessed value before exemptions. On a $450K home with homestead exemption, expect to pay $5,800-$7,500/year in property taxes, plus CDD fees if your community has them. Understanding these costs before you buy can save you from budget surprises on what is often a significant expense.

What Is the Property Tax Rate in Lutz FL?

Lutz is unincorporated Hillsborough County, so Hillsborough County's millage rates apply. The combined millage rate in unincorporated Hillsborough County runs approximately 19-21 mills depending on which fire district and other taxing authorities cover your specific property. One mill equals $1 per $1,000 of taxable value.

How the Millage Rate Breaks Down

Hillsborough County's millage is composed of multiple overlapping taxing authorities. The general breakdown for unincorporated Hillsborough County:

  • Hillsborough County general fund: approximately 5.5-6.0 mills
  • School district (Hillsborough County Public Schools): approximately 6.0-7.0 mills
  • Fire district: approximately 2.0-3.0 mills (varies by district)
  • Water management, mosquito control, and other special districts: approximately 1.5-2.5 mills

Total combined millage for most Lutz addresses: 19-21 mills. This is similar to Brandon, Riverview, and Valrico, which are all unincorporated Hillsborough County.

What Does That Mean for a Specific Lutz Home?

Home Value After Homestead ($50K off) At 20 Mills Typical Annual Tax
$350,000 $300,000 taxable $6,000 $5,500-$6,500
$450,000 $400,000 taxable $8,000 $7,200-$8,500
$550,000 $500,000 taxable $10,000 $8,800-$10,500
$650,000 $600,000 taxable $12,000 $10,500-$12,500

Note: These are estimates using homestead exemption. Investors (no homestead) pay on full assessed value without the $50K reduction. Actual bills vary by your specific taxing authorities.

What About CDD Fees in Lutz Communities?

Community Development Districts (CDDs) are a significant additional cost in many newer Lutz communities. CDDs are special taxing districts formed to finance the infrastructure of new developments. When you live in a CDD community, you pay an annual CDD assessment on your property tax bill in addition to regular county taxes.

CDD Fees by Lutz Community

  • Cheval: Older gated golf community with lower or no CDD fees; HOA fees are the primary community cost. Annual HOA varies by section ($1,200-$3,600/year).
  • Stonebrier: Newer community. CDD fees approximately $800-$1,400/year depending on lot size and phase.
  • Heritage Harbor: CDD fees approximately $700-$1,100/year. Golf community with pool, tennis, fitness center.
  • Long Lake Ranch: CDD fees approximately $1,500-$2,500/year for larger homes. Newer community with lake amenities.
  • Older Lutz (no CDD): Pre-2000 neighborhoods along Van Dyke Road and US-41 generally have no CDD fees, making them attractive for buyers who want lower carrying costs.

Always ask your real estate agent to pull the exact CDD assessment amount before making an offer. CDD fees are non-negotiable and run with the land until the CDD bond is retired, which can take 20-30 years.

How Does Florida's Homestead Exemption Work in Lutz?

Florida's Homestead Exemption reduces your taxable value by $50,000 if the property is your primary residence as of January 1. The first $25,000 exemption applies to all taxes. The second $25,000 applies to non-school taxes only (so school taxes are calculated on a slightly higher taxable value).

On a $450K assessed home: taxable value drops to approximately $400K for non-school taxes and $425K for school taxes. The blended savings is roughly $800-$1,200/year depending on the applicable millage.

To qualify: file at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office by March 1 of the year you are claiming. You can file online at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser website. You need proof of Florida residency (driver's license, voter registration, vehicle registration) and the property address. It is free.

What Is the Save Our Homes Cap?

Once you have homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes amendment caps your assessed value increase at 3% per year or the Consumer Price Index (whichever is lower), regardless of what the market does. This is one of the most powerful long-term tax benefits in Florida homeownership.

Example: You buy a Lutz home for $450K in 2026. Your assessed value is $450K. By 2031, the market value might be $530K, but your assessed value can only be $450K x (1.03)^5 = approximately $521K. In reality, with CPI running below 3%, your assessed value might only grow to $490K-$500K by 2031. The longer you own, the greater the tax advantage.

This is also why buying a resale home from a long-term owner can mean a significant tax jump for the new buyer. The seller's assessed value may be far below market value due to years of Save Our Homes protection, but the new buyer's assessed value resets to the purchase price.

How Do Lutz Property Taxes Compare to Nearby Areas?

Area Effective Tax Rate CDD Common? $450K Home Est. Tax
Lutz 1.8-2.0% Yes (newer areas) $7,200-$8,500
Land O'Lakes 1.9-2.1% Yes (many) $7,500-$9,000
Wesley Chapel 1.9-2.2% Very common $7,800-$10,000+
Valrico 1.8-2.0% Rare $7,200-$8,400
Riverview 1.9-2.1% Common (newer) $7,500-$9,500
Pasco County (Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel) 1.8-2.1% Very common $7,500-$9,000+

Additional Exemptions Available to Lutz Homeowners

Beyond the standard homestead exemption, Florida law provides additional property tax relief for qualifying residents:

  • Senior exemption (age 65+): Additional exemption of up to $50,000 for seniors with income below a threshold (approximately $35,167/year in 2025). Apply at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office.
  • Widowed persons: $500 additional exemption.
  • Disabled veterans: Partial to full exemption depending on disability rating. 100% disabled veterans may receive a full exemption.
  • First responders: Disabled first responders may qualify for additional exemptions.
  • Total disability: Permanently and totally disabled persons meeting income limits may qualify for additional exemptions.

How to Appeal Your Lutz Property Tax Assessment

If your Hillsborough County assessed value appears higher than market value, you can file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board (VAB). The process:

  1. Wait for your TRIM notice (mails in August/September)
  2. Review: does the assessed value seem higher than what you paid or what nearby homes are selling for?
  3. File a VAB petition within 25 days of the TRIM notice mailing
  4. Prepare comparable sales data showing your home's market value is lower than assessed value
  5. Attend your hearing (can be done virtually)

Barrett Henry provides comparable sales data to homeowners considering appeals. Call (813) 733-7907 or visit the contact page for help with property valuation data.

How to Look Up Your Actual Lutz Property Tax Bill

For the most accurate tax information on any specific Lutz property:

  • Visit the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser website and search by address or parcel ID to see the current assessed value, exemptions, and millage rates applied
  • Visit the Hillsborough County Tax Collector website to see prior year bills and payment history
  • Always ask for the current year's tax bill when making an offer on a home, and verify the CDD amount if applicable

Frequently Asked Questions: Lutz FL Property Taxes

What are property taxes in Lutz FL?

Property taxes in Lutz FL run approximately 1.8-2.0% of assessed value. On a $450K home with homestead exemption, expect to pay $7,200-$8,500/year. If your community also has CDD fees, add $700-$2,500/year on top of that base tax bill.

Does Lutz FL have CDD fees?

Some Lutz communities have CDD fees; others do not. Newer communities like Long Lake Ranch, Stonebrier, and Heritage Harbor have CDDs. Older neighborhoods along Van Dyke Road and US-41 generally do not. Always confirm the CDD status of any property before making an offer, as CDD fees are non-negotiable and can add $1,000-$2,500/year to your annual costs.

How do I apply for homestead exemption in Lutz FL?

File with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year you are claiming. You need a Florida driver's license, voter registration or vehicle registration showing your property address, and the property's parcel ID. Filing is free and can be done online or in person at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office.

How much will property taxes increase each year in Lutz?

Once you have homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes amendment caps your assessed value increase at 3% per year or CPI (whichever is lower). On a $450K homesteaded home, your taxes cannot increase more than roughly $150-$160/year even if the market jumps significantly. Without homestead exemption (investment properties), there is no cap.

Are Lutz property taxes higher than Wesley Chapel?

Lutz (Hillsborough County) and Wesley Chapel (Pasco County) have similar effective tax rates, both in the 1.8-2.1% range. However, Wesley Chapel new construction more frequently has CDD fees that push total annual costs higher. Older Lutz neighborhoods without CDDs often have lower total tax burdens than equivalent new Wesley Chapel communities with CDDs.

title: Sun City Center FL Activities: Clubs, Golf, and Social Life for Active Adults
excerpt: Sun City Center FL Activities: Clubs, Golf, and Social Life for Active Adults, practical guide from Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Sun City Center FL offers more than 200 clubs and organizations through the Sun City Center Community Association, covering everything from golf and pickleball to pottery, chorus, theater, and travel. The community is legally a golf cart community with more than 100 miles of golf cart paths connecting homes, clubhouses, restaurants, and services. For active adults 55 and older, Sun City Center provides a level of social and recreational activity that is difficult to match outside of larger retirement communities like The Villages. Here is a complete breakdown of what is available and what to expect before you buy.

What Golf Courses Are Available in Sun City Center?

Golf is central to the Sun City Center lifestyle, and residents have access to multiple courses without needing to travel far.

Scepter Golf Club

Scepter Golf Club is the primary course serving Sun City Center Community Association members. The 18-hole course is maintained for year-round play and is accessible to all SCCCA members. Green fees for members are significantly discounted versus public rates. The clubhouse includes a restaurant and pro shop. Scepter is a more casual, community-oriented course designed for the full range of golfers from beginners to experienced players.

Caloosa Golf and Country Club

Caloosa Golf and Country Club is a semi-private club within the Sun City Center area, operated somewhat independently from the main SCCCA structure. Caloosa offers 27 holes of golf spread across three nine-hole combinations, making it one of the larger golf complexes in the area. The club has its own restaurant and social calendar. Membership at Caloosa is separate from the SCCCA fee and costs additional annually. The course is known for its mature tree lines and water features typical of 1980s Florida golf course design.

Kings Point Golf Courses

Kings Point, the separate 55-plus community adjacent to Sun City Center, operates its own private golf facilities exclusively for Kings Point residents. The complex includes multiple nine-hole courses that can be combined for 18-hole rounds. Kings Point golf is included in the monthly HOA fee for Kings Point residents. Sun City Center Community Association members do not have automatic access to Kings Point's golf facilities without Kings Point residency.

What Sports and Recreation Facilities Does SCC Offer?

Pickleball and Tennis

Sun City Center has embraced pickleball enthusiastically, with dozens of outdoor courts maintained across the community. The sport's popularity among active adults has driven significant court expansion over the past decade. Tennis courts are also available, and the community supports active tennis leagues and round-robins. Both sports have organized leagues, drop-in play sessions, and instruction programs through the SCCCA.

Aquatics

Multiple pools serve the SCCCA community, including both indoor heated pools and outdoor pools. Lap swimming, water aerobics classes, and recreational swimming are available throughout the week. The indoor pools allow year-round aquatic programming even on cooler winter days. Swimming instruction and water fitness classes draw consistent participation from residents.

Lawn Sports: Shuffleboard, Bocce, Lawn Bowling

Shuffleboard courts are plentiful across Sun City Center, a nod to the community's history as a shuffleboard destination. Bocce ball courts serve the Italian-American community members who helped build SCC's social character. Lawn bowling, played on a flat grass green with heavy balls, has a dedicated following with regular league play. These sports may seem dated to outside observers, but they have active participant bases with competitive leagues and social events.

Softball, Baseball, and Field Sports

Adult softball leagues play on lighted fields within Sun City Center. The leagues accommodate players from casual recreational levels to competitive seniors. Baseball and similar field sports round out the outdoor athletic programming. The flat terrain of central Hillsborough County makes outdoor field sports practical year-round for Florida's mild winters, and the summer heat thins participation from June through September.

Fitness Centers

Multiple fitness centers with cardiovascular equipment, weight machines, and free weights operate across Sun City Center's clubhouse facilities. Fitness classes including aerobics, yoga, Pilates, Zumba, and strength training run on regular schedules. Personal training is available at additional cost. The fitness facilities are well-maintained and comparable to mid-tier commercial gym offerings.

What Arts and Social Clubs Are Available?

Performing Arts

The Sun City Center's Nanci Danison Performing Arts Center hosts theatrical productions, musical performances, and community events throughout the year. The resident theater group produces multiple shows annually, with auditions open to community members. Chorus groups, handbell choirs, and musical ensembles perform regularly. Dance clubs covering styles from ballroom to line dancing have active memberships.

Visual Arts and Crafts

Pottery, painting, stained glass, woodworking, and fiber arts clubs operate out of dedicated studio spaces. The pottery studio has wheels and kilns. The woodworking shop has equipment for both hand and power tool projects. These facilities would cost thousands per year to access commercially; they are included in or accessible through the SCCCA membership.

Educational and Intellectual Clubs

Book clubs, investment clubs, bridge and card clubs, discussion groups, and computer assistance programs cater to intellectually active residents. The Osher Lifelong Learning Institute (OLLI) affiliated programs offer structured learning opportunities. Computer clubs help residents stay current with technology. The breadth of intellectual programming attracts buyers who want an active mind, not just an active body.

Travel Clubs and Special Interest Groups

Multiple travel clubs organize group trips domestically and internationally. Specialty clubs cover everything from amateur radio to photography, astronomy, genealogy, and coin collecting. Veterans' organizations, civic groups, and faith-based social clubs operate within the community. The sheer number of clubs means most residents find multiple groups that match their interests within the first few months of moving in.

How Does Sun City Center Compare to Kings Point for Activities?

Feature SCC Community Association Kings Point
Monthly Fee $350-$500 (varies by sub-community) $700-$950
Golf Courses Scepter GC (additional fees); Caloosa (separate membership) Multiple 9-hole courses included in HOA
Number of Pools 6+ pools across three clubhouses 6 pools (indoor and outdoor)
Number of Clubs 200+ clubs and organizations 200+ clubs (similar breadth)
Cable/Internet Included No (pay separately) Yes (included in HOA)
Water/Sewer Included No Yes (in some sections)
Gated Entry No (open community) Yes (guarded gates)
Home Price Range $250K-$500K (SFH); some villa options lower $150K-$350K (condos and villas)

What Is Daily Life Like in Sun City Center?

Sun City Center operates on a schedule driven by the social calendar, not work obligations. Mornings fill with fitness classes, golf tee times, and pool sessions. Afternoons bring club meetings, hobby workshops, and card games. Evenings feature theater productions, dinner clubs, and community events. The golf cart is not optional for serious engagement with the community: it is the primary mode of local transportation, and the network of cart paths connects everything from grocery stores to medical offices to the golf course.

Shopping and Dining Without Leaving

Sun City Center has an embedded commercial strip along SR-674 that includes a Walmart Supercenter, Publix, multiple medical offices, restaurants, and essential services. Most daily needs can be met without leaving the area. For broader dining and shopping, Brandon's retail corridor (US-60) is about 20 minutes north, and I-75 access is straightforward.

Thinking About Sun City Center?

Frequently Asked Questions About Sun City Center Activities

How many clubs and activities does Sun City Center have?

Sun City Center Community Association (SCCCA) supports more than 200 clubs and organizations covering sports, arts, crafts, intellectual pursuits, travel, civic groups, and social activities. Kings Point, the adjacent community, has a similar breadth of programming for its residents. The depth of programming is one of Sun City Center's primary competitive advantages over smaller 55-plus communities in the Tampa Bay area.

Do you have to be 55 to live in Sun City Center?

Yes. Sun City Center and Kings Point are both age-restricted communities under the Housing for Older Persons Act (HOPA), requiring that at least one occupant of each home be 55 or older and that 80% of occupied units be occupied by at least one person 55 or older. A 35-year-old married to a 56-year-old may qualify, but the 56-year-old must be on title and occupy the home. Children under 18 cannot be permanent residents.

Is Sun City Center or Kings Point better for activities?

Both offer comparable breadth of programming. The primary differences: Kings Point is gated and all-inclusive (cable, water, and golf included in a higher monthly fee), while SCCCA is open and individually priced with a lower base fee but additional costs for utilities and golf. Buyers who want the premium, everything-included resort experience tend to prefer Kings Point. Buyers who want lower base costs and more flexibility tend to prefer SCCCA.

Can you walk everywhere in Sun City Center?

Sun City Center was designed as a golf cart community. While some areas are walkable to immediate neighbors, the full community is more accessible by golf cart than on foot. Golf carts are licensed for use on designated SCC paths and certain local roads (SR-674 corridor). Most residents own one or two golf carts as their primary local transportation. Bringing or buying a golf cart is effectively necessary for full community participation.

What are the medical facilities near Sun City Center?

South Bay Hospital in Sun City Center provides emergency care and inpatient services within the community. Brandon Regional Hospital (Level II Trauma Center) is approximately 20 minutes north via I-75. Numerous specialist offices are embedded within the SCC commercial corridor for cardiology, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and general medicine. The high concentration of medical services within or near the community is a significant draw for buyers with ongoing health needs.

title: Temple Terrace FL Property Taxes: City vs County Rates Explained
excerpt: Temple Terrace FL Property Taxes: City vs County Rates Explained, practical guide from Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Property taxes in Temple Terrace FL are higher than in unincorporated Hillsborough County because Temple Terrace is an incorporated city and charges its own city millage on top of county and school levies. The combined total runs approximately 25-27 mills, adding roughly $1,500-$2,000/year to your tax bill compared to an equivalent home in unincorporated Hillsborough County. Here is the complete breakdown and what to budget before buying in Temple Terrace.

What Makes Temple Terrace Taxes Different from Surrounding Areas?

The critical distinction: Temple Terrace is one of Hillsborough County's incorporated cities, alongside Tampa, Plant City, and Temple Terrace itself. Incorporated city residents pay both county millage and city millage. Unincorporated Hillsborough County areas like Brandon, Valrico, Town 'n' Country, and Riverview pay only the county millage.

Temple Terrace City Millage

The City of Temple Terrace levies its own millage rate, which has historically run approximately 5.87 mills. This city millage funds Temple Terrace's own police department, parks, public works, and city administration. It is separate from and in addition to the Hillsborough County general fund millage. Temple Terrace residents benefit from a dedicated city police department (distinct from the Hillsborough County Sheriff), well-maintained city parks, and direct city services as a return on this additional tax.

Full Millage Stack for Temple Terrace

City of Temple Terrace ~5.87
Hillsborough County General Fund ~5.25
Hillsborough County School Board ~6.50
Hillsborough County Schools Local Discretionary ~0.748
Children's Board of Hillsborough County ~0.50
Southwest Florida Water Management District ~0.28
Other County Levies (Mosquito, Port, Hospital) ~0.50-1.00
Total Approximate ~25-27 mills

Actual millage rates are set each September when taxing authorities certify their final rates. The figures above are approximations based on recent years. For the exact current millage, check HCPAFL.gov or request a tax estimate from the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser.

title: Town 'n' Country FL Property Taxes and Cost of Living
excerpt: Town 'n' Country FL Property Taxes and Cost of Living, practical guide from Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Property taxes in Town 'n' Country FL run approximately $3,500-$6,000 per year on a $400,000-$600,000 home, based on Hillsborough County's millage rate of approximately 19-21 mills total depending on your specific location within the unincorporated area. Town 'n' Country is unincorporated Hillsborough County, which means you do NOT pay a city millage tax, making your tax burden lower than comparable homes inside the City of Tampa city limits. Here is the complete breakdown of how property taxes work and what to budget.

How Are Property Taxes Calculated in Town 'n' Country?

Florida property taxes are calculated as: Taxable Value multiplied by the millage rate, expressed as dollars per $1,000 of value. The taxable value starts with the assessed value (set by the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser each January 1) and is reduced by applicable exemptions.

Step 1: Assessed Value vs Market Value

The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser assesses your home at what they determine to be its market value as of January 1 each year. For recently sold homes, this is usually close to the purchase price. For homes held longer than one year, Florida's Save Our Homes cap limits annual assessment increases to 3% or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower.

Step 2: Homestead Exemption

Florida's homestead exemption reduces your assessed value by $25,000 for all tax purposes, and an additional $25,000 for all purposes except school taxes. Combined, most primary residence owners in Town 'n' Country receive a $50,000 effective reduction on most of their tax bill, though the second $25,000 exemption does not apply to the school district levy. On a $400,000 home, the exemption saves approximately $800-$1,000 per year compared to paying taxes on the full value.

Step 3: Millage Rate Components

Hillsborough County's total millage rate for unincorporated areas (where Town 'n' Country is located) includes multiple components:

Note: Town 'n' Country does NOT pay a City of Tampa millage (approximately 5-6 mills) because it is unincorporated Hillsborough County, not within city limits. This is a meaningful savings compared to homes inside Tampa city boundaries.

Town 'n' Country includes a range of communities from no-HOA older sections to master-planned HOA communities. Countryway, one of TNC's larger planned communities, has HOA fees in the $60-$120/month range covering common area maintenance and community access to the Countryway Golf Club (semi-private). No CDD Fees

Town 'n' Country communities generally do not have Community Development District (CDD) fees, which is a meaningful cost advantage over newer communities in Riverview, Wimauma, Apollo Beach, and Wesley Chapel where CDD fees commonly run $1,500-$4,000/year. Insurance

Homeowners insurance in Town 'n' Country runs $2,500-$5,000/year for typical homes, depending on age, roof condition, and proximity to Tampa Bay. Homes near Old Tampa Bay have flood zone exposure that adds $2,000-$8,000/year for flood insurance if required. This is one of its financial advantages: TNC residents pay county millage rates only and do not pay the City of Tampa millage (approximately 5-6 mills), saving $1,000-$2,000/year in property taxes compared to an equivalent home inside Tampa city limits.

What is the homestead exemption and how does it work in TNC?

Florida's homestead exemption reduces your assessed value by $25,000 for all levies and an additional $25,000 for levies other than school district. The combined effect saves most homeowners $800-$1,200/year in property taxes. You must apply by March 1 of the year following your purchase date. File online through HCPAFL.gov or in person at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office. The exemption also activates the Save Our Homes cap, which limits annual assessment increases to 3% or CPI, whichever is less.

What is the Save Our Homes cap and how does it help long-term residents?

The Save Our Homes cap (SOH) limits the annual increase in the assessed value of a homesteaded property to 3% or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. This means long-term TNC homeowners pay taxes on a frozen assessed value well below current market value. A homeowner who bought in 2015 for $250,000 might have an assessed value of $310,000 today even if the market value is $450,000 or more. When you sell, however, the SOH cap resets to zero. The new buyer pays taxes on the full market value from day one.

Are there any CDD fees in Town 'n' Country?

Town 'n' Country communities generally do not have CDD fees. This is a significant financial advantage over newer communities in Riverview, Wimauma, and Wesley Chapel where CDD fees commonly run $1,500-$4,000/year in addition to HOA fees. The absence of CDD fees makes TNC's total monthly carrying cost lower than many comparably priced newer communities.

How do I dispute my property tax assessment in Hillsborough County?

If you believe your assessed value is too high, you can file an informal appeal with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office or a formal petition with the Value Adjustment Board (VAB). The deadline to file a VAB petition is 25 days after the TRIM (Truth in Millage) notice is mailed in August. You must provide evidence that the assessed value exceeds the market value, typically using recent comparable sales. The property appraiser's office will sometimes reduce an assessment informally before a formal hearing is necessary.

Living in Westchase FL costs more than comparable Tampa Bay suburbs. Home prices run $450K-$1.5M+. The Westchase Community Association (WCA) charges quarterly dues. Property taxes follow Hillsborough County millage rates. Insurance runs higher for newer, larger homes. But Westchase buyers are getting something specific: top-rated public schools (Sickles High School, Farnell Middle, Bryant Elementary), maintained common areas with pools and parks, and one of northwest Hillsborough County's most established neighborhoods. Here is what it actually costs to live here.

Westchase Home Prices: What You Can Buy at Each Budget

Westchase is a master-planned community in the 33626 ZIP code of northwest Hillsborough County. Westchase has a two-tier HOA structure. The master HOA, the Westchase Community Association (WCA), charges dues that cover common areas, pools, sports courts, parks, and community management. Many Westchase villages have their own sub-association with additional fees ranging from $50-$200 per month. Villages with maintained landscaping, private pools, or gated entrances typically have higher sub-association fees. Townhome and villa sections have higher sub-association fees because exterior maintenance is included. When evaluating any Westchase property, always ask for both the WCA fee and the sub-association fee to understand the full HOA obligation.

The WCA maintains the Westchase swim and tennis centers (multiple locations), extensive trail network connecting the community, community parks, Westchase Recreation Center, and the neighborhood's landscaped corridors and signage. title: Wimauma FL Property Taxes: CDD Fees, Millage Rates, and What to Budget
excerpt: Wimauma property taxes include Hillsborough County millage plus CDD fees that add $1,500-$3,000/year in newer communities. Here is exactly what to budget for Berry Bay, Sereno, Lake Toscana, and other Wimauma neighborhoods.
content:
Property taxes in Wimauma FL combine Hillsborough County millage (approximately 19-21 mills total depending on your location) with Community Development District (CDD) fees that run $1,500-$3,000 or more per year in most new construction communities. The total tax and assessment burden in Wimauma can be $500-$1,000 per month higher than the sticker price on your home suggests. Here is what to budget across each major community.

How Are Hillsborough County Property Taxes Calculated in Wimauma?

Hillsborough County uses a millage rate system. One mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. The total millage rate for unincorporated Hillsborough County (where Wimauma sits) is typically 19-21 mills combined across all taxing authorities. This includes the county general fund, the school district (the largest component at roughly 8 mills), the SWFWMD water management district, fire/EMS, and library.

The Homestead Exemption Reduces Your Assessed Value

Florida's homestead exemption reduces your taxable assessed value by $50,000 for your primary residence. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities. The second $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities except the school board. In practice, on a $400,000 home with full homestead exemption, you are taxed as though the home is worth $350,000 for the school board portion and $375,000 for county purposes. This saves most Wimauma homeowners $900-$1,200 per year compared to non-homesteaded properties.

Save Our Homes Cap Limits Annual Increases

Once you have a homestead exemption, the assessed value of your home can only increase 3% or the Consumer Price Index (whichever is less) each year, regardless of how much the market value increases. This means long-term Wimauma homeowners pay taxes on assessed values that may be significantly below market value. New buyers, however, receive a new tax assessment at close to purchase price in the year following sale. Budget based on the full purchase price, not the prior owner's assessment.

Estimates based on approximately 20 mills and homestead exemption on primary residence. Actual bills vary. Verify at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser website.

CDD Fees in Wimauma Communities

Community Development Districts (CDDs) are independent special-purpose government units that finance infrastructure construction (roads, utilities, amenity centers, ponds) in new communities. They issue bonds and collect annual assessments from homeowners to repay those bonds over 20-30 years. CDDs are separate from property taxes and show up as a line item on your property tax bill. They do not disappear when the community is built out, they wind down as the bonds are paid off.

Why Wimauma Has So Many CDD Communities

Wimauma (ZIP 33598) has been one of Hillsborough County's primary growth areas for the past decade. The land was affordable, allowed large-scale master-planned community development, and builders used CDD financing extensively to fund infrastructure. Berry Bay, Sereno, Lake Toscana, Harvest Cay, Vista Palms, and Legacy Park all have CDD structures. Buyers should ask for the CDD amount in any new or recent construction community in Wimauma before making an offer.

CDD Fee Ranges in Major Wimauma Communities

CDD fees vary by community and can change year to year as bonds are paid down or refinanced. The ranges below reflect typical fee levels but should be verified directly with the community HOA or through the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser's office. CDD fees are included in your annual tax bill, not billed separately.

Total Monthly Cost: Property Tax Plus CDD in Wimauma

Buyers comparing Wimauma to older communities without CDDs should calculate the total monthly obligation. Florida Property Tax Exemptions That Apply in Wimauma

Standard Homestead Exemption ($50,000)

Available to any Florida resident using the property as their primary residence as of January 1. You must apply with the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the tax year. Apply at hcpafl.org or in person at one of their offices.

Senior Citizen Additional Exemption

Hillsborough County residents 65 and older with household income below the threshold set by the Florida Legislature (adjusted annually) may qualify for an additional $25,000 exemption. Low-income senior households may qualify for exemption from the county portion of their tax bill entirely.

Disabled Veteran Exemption

Veterans with a service-connected total and permanent disability may qualify for a full exemption from property taxes. Surviving spouses of qualifying veterans may also qualify. Documentation from the VA is required.

Widow or Widower Exemption

Florida provides a $5,000 reduction in assessed value for widows and widowers who have not remarried. This is a modest benefit but worth claiming if applicable.

Understanding Your Wimauma TRIM Notice

Each August, Hillsborough County mails a Truth in Millage (TRIM) notice to all property owners. This is not a bill, it is a proposed tax notice showing the proposed assessed value, proposed millage rates from each taxing authority, and calculated proposed taxes. If you believe your assessed value is too high, the TRIM notice period (typically 25 days from mailing) is when you file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board. Missing this window means waiting another year to challenge your assessment.

How to Appeal Your Wimauma Property Assessment

If comparable Wimauma homes are selling for less than your assessed value, you have grounds to appeal. Gather three recent comparable sales (similar size, location, condition) where sale prices are below your assessed value. File a petition with the Hillsborough County Value Adjustment Board during the TRIM notice period. The filing fee is modest and hearings are conducted with a special magistrate. New buyers who purchased at market value sometimes find their assessed value is already reasonable, but it is worth checking.

Resources for Wimauma Property Tax Information

Hillsborough County Property Appraiser (hcpafl.org) is the primary source for current assessed values, exemption applications, and sales history. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector (hillstax.org) handles bill payment, due dates, and early payment discounts. Florida property taxes are paid in arrears: the November 30 bill covers the prior calendar year. Early payment discounts apply: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February, face value in March.

The combined millage rate for unincorporated Hillsborough County, which includes Wimauma, is approximately 19-21 mills depending on the specific taxing districts in your location. This translates to roughly $1,900-$2,100 in annual property taxes per $100,000 of assessed value before exemptions. With the homestead exemption, most Wimauma homeowners pay $4,500-$9,000+ per year depending on home value.

Are CDD fees included in the property tax bill in Wimauma?

Yes. CDD assessments are billed through the Hillsborough County annual property tax notice and are paid at the same time as property taxes. They are shown as a separate line item on the bill. CDD fees are not part of the millage rate but are collected alongside property taxes for administrative convenience.

Do CDD fees ever go away in Wimauma communities?

CDD fees are tied to bonds that typically mature over 20-30 years. The fees should decrease as bonds are paid down and eventually disappear when the bonds are retired. However, some CDDs issue new bonds for additional improvements, which can extend the fee period. Ask specifically whether new bonds are planned and when the current bonds mature when evaluating any CDD community.

How do I apply for homestead exemption in Wimauma?

Apply online at hcpafl.org or in person at the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser office. You must apply by March 1 of the first full tax year you occupy the property as your primary residence. You will need your deed, proof of Florida residency (driver's license), and Social Security number. Once established, the exemption renews automatically as long as you remain in the home.

How does the Save Our Homes cap benefit Wimauma homeowners?

Save Our Homes limits your assessed value increase to 3% or CPI per year once homestead exemption is in place. Over time, this creates a growing gap between market value and assessed value. After 10 years in a home that appreciated at 5%/year, your assessed value might be 25-30% below market. This is a significant tax benefit for long-term owners but resets to near market value when the home sells.

content:
Quick Answer: Clearwater FL Homes for Sale in 2026

Clearwater FL has active listings ranging from under $250,000 for entry-level condos to over $3 million for waterfront estates on Clearwater Beach. The city sits in Pinellas County on Florida's Gulf Coast, with Clearwater Beach consistently ranked among the top beaches in the United States. Buyers get beach proximity, established neighborhoods, and a Gulf Coast lifestyle. Median price in 2026 is approximately $395,000.

About Clearwater, Florida

Clearwater is a Gulf Coast city in Pinellas County, Florida, with a population of approximately 117,000. It is best known for Clearwater Beach, which has been ranked the #1 beach in the United States by TripAdvisor multiple times. The city spans roughly 28 square miles across barrier islands, peninsulas, and mainland neighborhoods, giving buyers a wide variety of property types and price points.

The city covers ZIP codes 33755, 33756, 33759, 33760, 33761, 33762, 33763, 33764, 33765, and 33767 (Clearwater Beach). Neighboring communities include Largo, Dunedin, Safety Harbor, and Belleair. For current listings, browse Clearwater homes for sale or review the Clearwater housing market for recent sales data.

Pinellas County is the most densely populated county in Florida, which means land is scarce and new construction is limited. This structural constraint supports home values over time. The trade-off is that prices per square foot are generally higher here than in comparable communities in Hillsborough or Pasco counties.

Clearwater Home Prices by Neighborhood and Type (2026)

Clearwater's price range is wide because the city contains everything from entry-level condos near US-19 to multi-million-dollar Gulf-front estates. Here is a breakdown by property type and location.

What Neighborhoods Should I Consider in Clearwater?

Clearwater Beach

Clearwater Beach is the barrier island west of downtown. It is famous for the white-sand beach, Pier 60, Caladesi Island State Park, and the vibrant dining and entertainment strip on Mandalay Avenue. Most housing here is condos and townhomes. Gulf-front units carry the highest prices and the highest insurance costs. FEMA Zone VE designation along the Gulf-front means open-pile construction is required for new builds and insurance costs are steep, often $8,000 to $20,000 or more per year.

Countryside and East Lake

Countryside (ZIP 33761) and East Lake (ZIP 33765) are northern Clearwater's suburban communities with larger lots, newer construction (1980s-2000s), good schools including Countryside High School and East Lake High School, and lower flood risk. These areas draw families who want suburban lifestyle with Gulf Coast proximity. Most homes fall between $380,000 and $600,000.

North Clearwater and East Clearwater

The areas directly north and east of downtown Clearwater offer more affordable entry points, generally $290,000 to $420,000 for single-family homes. These neighborhoods are older (1960s-1980s construction) with smaller lots. They are car-dependent but provide reasonable access to US-19 and US-60.

Harbor Oaks and Del Oro Groves

Harbor Oaks and Del Oro Groves are established waterfront neighborhoods along the Intracoastal Waterway south of downtown. Homes here offer boat access to Tampa Bay and the Gulf via Clearwater Pass or Dunedin Pass. Prices range from $600,000 to $1.5 million or more for direct Intracoastal frontage.

Belleair and Belleair Bluffs

The Belleair communities just south of Clearwater proper offer some of the area's most prestigious addresses. The Belleair Country Club anchors the neighborhood. Prices range from $450,000 for inland homes to $2 million or more for waterfront estates. See the Clearwater Beach and Belleair luxury guide for detail.

The Buying Process in Clearwater FL

Step 1: Get pre-approved

Pinellas County is a competitive market. Sellers expect pre-approval letters, not just pre-qualification. Get a full underwritten pre-approval if possible. Include flood insurance quotes in your budget, this is non-negotiable for Zone AE or VE properties.

Step 2: Identify your neighborhood criteria

Decide upfront whether flood zone exposure is acceptable, whether you need top-rated schools (Countryside/East Lake), whether condo vs single-family matters, and what your maximum HOA tolerance is. These filters narrow the search significantly.

Step 3: Write an offer with due diligence period

Florida contracts include an inspection period (typically 10-15 days). Use this time to order a home inspection, wind mitigation report, four-point inspection (required by most insurers for homes 20+ years old), flood zone determination, and elevation certificate if applicable.

Step 4: Close with a Florida real estate attorney or title company

Florida is a title company state. Clearwater closings are handled by title companies. The title search confirms no liens or ownership disputes. Title insurance protects the buyer and lender. Closing costs for buyers typically run 2-3% of the purchase price.

Investment Property Considerations in Clearwater

Clearwater is one of the top short-term rental markets in the Tampa Bay area because of Clearwater Beach tourism. However, condo declarations vary widely in what rentals they allow. Some buildings prohibit rentals under 30 days. Others allow weekly rentals. Always verify the condo documents before buying for STR purposes.

Long-term rental demand is strong across all neighborhoods. The ViVi Property Management team handles long-term rentals throughout Pinellas County. See the investment property analysis in the Clearwater real estate guide for cap rate estimates.

Schools in Clearwater FL

Clearwater is served by Pinellas County Schools (pcsb.org). School assignment depends on your specific address. Notable high schools include Clearwater High School (540 S Hercules Ave), Countryside High School (3000 SR-580 W), and East Lake High School (1300 Silver Eagle Dr). See the Clearwater schools guide for full detail.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average home price in Clearwater FL?

In 2026 the median home price in Clearwater FL is approximately $395,000. The range runs from under $250,000 for entry-level condos to $3 million or more for waterfront homes on Clearwater Beach or the Intracoastal Waterway.

Is Clearwater FL a good place to buy a home?

Clearwater offers strong lifestyle value with world-class beaches, an established downtown, and steady long-term demand. Pinellas County is the most densely populated county in Florida, which limits new supply and supports home values over time.

What neighborhoods are popular in Clearwater FL?

Popular neighborhoods include Clearwater Beach for Gulf-front living, Countryside and East Lake for suburban families, North Clearwater for value buyers, and Del Oro Groves and Harbor Oaks for waterfront access on the Intracoastal.

Is Clearwater FL in a flood zone?

Parts of Clearwater are in FEMA flood zones, especially Clearwater Beach (Zone VE), waterfront areas along the Intracoastal, and low-lying inland areas. Interior neighborhoods in Countryside and East Lake are mostly Zone X with no mandatory flood insurance. Always verify via the FEMA Flood Map Service Center before making an offer.

How long do homes sit on the market in Clearwater?

In 2026 homes in Clearwater average around 45 to 65 days on market, depending on price point and condition. Well-priced move-in-ready homes in desirable neighborhoods still attract multiple offers. Overpriced listings sit significantly longer.

Does Clearwater FL have HOA communities?

Clearwater has both HOA and non-HOA communities. Clearwater Beach condos almost always have HOA fees ranging from $400 to $1,500 per month or more. Many Countryside and East Lake subdivisions have HOA fees between $100 and $400 per quarter. Always request the HOA documents and financials during due diligence.

title: Clearwater FL Commute Guide: Drive Times, Transit & Hybrid Work (2026)
excerpt: Drive times from Clearwater FL to Tampa, St. Pete, and other destinations. PSTA transit coverage and hybrid work analysis for Pinellas County buyers.
content:
Quick Answer: Clearwater FL Commute (2026)

From most Clearwater neighborhoods, the commute to downtown Tampa takes 35 to 55 minutes via the Courtney Campbell Causeway under normal conditions, with peak-hour times reaching 60 to 75 minutes. St. Petersburg is 30 to 50 minutes via US-19 and I-275. Tampa International Airport is 25 to 40 minutes away. PSTA bus service exists but is not practical for most suburban commute patterns. Clearwater is well-suited for hybrid workers.

Primary Routes Out of Clearwater FL

SR-60 / Courtney Campbell Causeway (to Tampa)

SR-60 (Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard) runs east-west through central Clearwater and crosses Tampa Bay via the Courtney Campbell Causeway. This is the primary route for Clearwater residents commuting to Tampa, Westshore, or Tampa International Airport. The causeway is a non-toll bridge with two lanes each direction. It narrows at the bay crossing and backs up during rush hour, particularly eastbound in the morning (7-9 am) and westbound in the evening (4-7 pm).

US-19 (North-South Pinellas Corridor)

US-19 runs north-south through Clearwater, connecting the city to Dunedin, Palm Harbor, and Tarpon Springs to the north, and Largo and St. Petersburg to the south. It is a high-traffic, high-signal arterial with significant congestion through central Clearwater. FDOT has grade-separated US-19 in some segments to reduce signal stops. Plan for 30 to 50 minutes to reach central St. Petersburg via US-19 south to I-275.

SR-580 (to Oldsmar and I-275)

SR-580 is the main route for Countryside and East Lake residents heading east toward Tampa. It connects to SR-55 (McMullen-Booth Road) and eventually to I-275 near Tampa's Westshore Business District. This route avoids the Courtney Campbell congestion point for north Clearwater commuters.

Buying Near Your Clearwater Commute Route?

Contact BarrettCall (813) 733-7907

Clearwater Beach Commute Specifics

Clearwater Beach is accessed exclusively via the Memorial Causeway from downtown Clearwater. During tourist season (November through April) and summer weekends, traffic on the causeway and Beach Drive backs up significantly. If you live on Clearwater Beach and commute to Tampa or St. Pete on weekdays during peak season, add 10 to 20 extra minutes versus off-season times.

Clearwater Beach does not have a direct road connection to the Howard Frankland Bridge or Gandy Bridge. Every route from Clearwater Beach to Tampa crosses mainland Clearwater first, then proceeds east via SR-60 or SR-580.

PSTA Bus Service in Clearwater

Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority (psta.net) operates bus routes throughout Clearwater and Pinellas County. Key routes for Clearwater commuters include:

According to PSTA, most Pinellas County commuters drive. Bus routes exist but are not practical for most suburban-to-suburban commutes. The lack of a cross-bay bus service to Tampa means driving is the default for Tampa-bound workers. Visit psta.net for current schedules and trip planning.

Bicycle Commuting and the Pinellas Trail

The Pinellas Trail is a 70-mile paved multi-use trail running north-south through Pinellas County. It passes through Clearwater, connecting to Dunedin, Palm Harbor, and Tarpon Springs to the north and Largo and St. Petersburg to the south. For residents who work in Clearwater or in the immediate trail corridor, bicycle commuting is a realistic option.

Cross-bay bicycle commuting to Tampa is not practical. The Courtney Campbell Causeway has a dedicated bicycle and pedestrian path, but the trip to Tampa is 18+ miles from central Clearwater. It is used for recreation, not daily commuting.

Airport Access from Clearwater FL

Tampa International Airport (TPA)

TPA is the primary international airport for the region. From central Clearwater it is approximately 18-28 miles via SR-60 east to the Veterans Expressway or directly on SR-60 past the Courtney Campbell to the TPA exit. Drive time is typically 25 to 40 minutes. Plan for 50+ minutes during peak traffic or when driving from Clearwater Beach.

St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport (PIE)

PIE is a smaller airport serving Allegiant, Sun Country, and a handful of other carriers with seasonal service. It is 10 to 20 minutes south of Clearwater via US-19. If your travel patterns match PIE's routes, it is a convenient alternative to TPA with free parking and shorter security lines.

Hybrid Work and Remote Work in Clearwater

Clearwater is well-positioned for hybrid workers who commute 2-3 days per week. The drive to Tampa or St. Petersburg is manageable when you can choose off-peak departure times. Several coworking spaces operate in and near downtown Clearwater, including options in the Clearwater Beach tourism corridor.

If you work fully remote, Clearwater's lifestyle advantages, beach access, and relatively lower cost compared to Naples or Sarasota make it compelling. The combination of Gulf Coast lifestyle and Gulf-to-bay geography is a draw for remote workers relocating from higher-cost metros.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long is the commute from Clearwater to Tampa?

The commute from Clearwater to downtown Tampa via the Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR-60) takes 35 to 55 minutes under normal conditions and 50 to 75 minutes or more during peak hours. The Howard Frankland Bridge (I-275) is an alternative but adds distance for most Clearwater ZIP codes.

How far is Clearwater from Tampa Airport?

Tampa International Airport (TPA) is approximately 18 to 28 miles from most Clearwater ZIP codes, with a typical drive of 25 to 40 minutes under normal conditions. Peak traffic on SR-60 and the Courtney Campbell Causeway can push this to 50 minutes or more.

Does Clearwater have public transit?

Clearwater is served by PSTA (Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority). PSTA routes connect Clearwater to St. Petersburg, Largo, Dunedin, and Clearwater Beach. However, bus service frequency and coverage are limited compared to major urban systems, making it impractical for most suburban commutes. Visit psta.net for routes and schedules.

Is Clearwater Beach easy to commute from?

Clearwater Beach is a barrier island accessed by Memorial Causeway from downtown Clearwater. Traffic during tourist season (November through April) and summer weekends can make the causeway significantly congested. Commuting from Clearwater Beach to Tampa during peak hours typically runs 55 to 80 minutes.

Is Clearwater FL good for remote workers?

Yes. Clearwater has several coworking spaces and coffee shops with good wifi, and many residents work fully remote. The lifestyle benefits (beach proximity, outdoor activities, lower cost vs. South Florida) make it attractive for remote workers. Hybrid schedules with 2-3 office days per week are very manageable from most Clearwater neighborhoods.

title: Is Clearwater FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Pros and Cons (2026)
excerpt: Honest pros and cons of living in Clearwater FL. Beach access, flood risk, cost, schools, commute, and how Clearwater compares to Largo, Dunedin, and Safety Harbor.
content:
Quick Answer: Is Clearwater FL a Good Place to Live?

Clearwater FL is a good place to live for people who prioritize beach proximity, outdoor lifestyle, and Gulf Coast weather. It is one of the few places in the country where you can own a home within 15 minutes of a world-class beach and still have access to a major metro area. The trade-offs are real: traffic on US-19 is frustrating, flood insurance on coastal properties is expensive, and hurricane risk requires preparation. For the right buyer, the lifestyle value is significant.

What Makes Clearwater FL a Good Place to Live

Clearwater Beach access

Clearwater Beach is consistently ranked among the top beaches in the United States. The combination of white quartz sand, calm Gulf water, and a walkable pier and entertainment district is genuinely difficult to replicate. Residents of mainland Clearwater can reach the beach in 10 to 20 minutes, which is a real lifestyle benefit that appreciates over time.

Gulf Coast weather

Clearwater averages more than 360 days of sunshine per year, with low humidity from October through May and warm Gulf water from roughly May through November. The outdoor recreation calendar is year-round. Winters are mild, with overnight lows rarely dropping below 45 degrees Fahrenheit.

Outdoor recreation options

Beyond the beach, Clearwater residents have access to the 70-mile Pinellas Trail (cycling, walking, running), kayak and paddleboard access from multiple waterfront parks, boating via Clearwater Pass and the Intracoastal Waterway, Caladesi Island State Park (accessible by ferry from Dunedin), and a network of city parks and nature preserves.

Proximity to Tampa Bay metro amenities

Clearwater is 35 to 50 minutes from downtown Tampa and 30 to 45 minutes from downtown St. Petersburg, giving residents access to two major metros. This means major medical centers, professional sports (Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Rays, Lightning), international airports, concert venues, and a broad employment base are all within practical reach.

No state income tax

Florida has no state income tax. For high-income earners relocating from California, New York, or other high-tax states, the savings can be substantial. This factor directly affects affordability calculations and is a recurring reason buyers choose Florida over other coastal states.

Clearwater Beach is a high-tourism area with its own crime profile distinct from residential neighborhoods.

Does Clearwater flood during hurricanes?

Clearwater Beach Condo Market and SB 4-D (2026)

Florida's Condominium Safety Law (SB 4-D, effective December 2022) requires condominium buildings three stories or taller to complete a Milestone Structural Inspection by December 31, 2024 (for buildings 30 years or older by July 2022) and fund a fully-funded reserve account by December 31, 2024 and all subsequent years.

For buyers, this means: older Clearwater Beach condo buildings may have passed their inspection (good) or may have identified deficiencies requiring expensive repairs (risk). Buildings that are not fully-funded on reserves will charge current owners and new buyers through special assessments or sharply higher monthly HOA fees. According to Pinellas County real estate data, some Clearwater Beach buildings have seen monthly fees increase by $300 to $900 or more per month since 2023.

Due diligence checklist for Clearwater Beach condos

1. Request the most recent Milestone Structural Inspection report. 2. Request the most recent reserve study and confirm the percent-funded status. 3. Review board meeting minutes for the past 24 months for discussion of special assessments or repair plans. 4. Confirm whether the building has pending special assessments and the amount. 5. Verify the building's flood insurance policy and coverage limits (separate from unit owner's HO6 policy). 6. Check whether the condo documents permit short-term rentals if investment is the intent.

Insurance is now a negotiating factor. Buyers who can quantify insurance costs before making an offer, and who can negotiate seller contributions to cover insurance escrow shortfalls or known issues, have a real financial advantage. Barrett recommends getting homeowners insurance quotes on any property before making an offer, not after.

Seller Strategy for Clearwater FL in 2026

Sellers in 2026 need accurate pricing. Overpriced listings sit for 60-120+ days, accumulate market stigma, and typically sell below where they would have if priced correctly from the start. The most effective approach is to price at current market value (not 2022 peak value), complete minor repairs and cosmetic improvements before listing, and have documentation ready: HOA financials, recent inspection reports, wind mitigation and four-point inspection.

Sellers of Clearwater Beach condos with known SB 4-D assessments or compliance issues should disclose them upfront. Buyers who discover these in due diligence will either renegotiate significantly or terminate. Full disclosure early builds trust and prevents failed transactions.

Quick Answer: Clearwater FL Property Taxes in 2026

Clearwater FL property taxes combine Pinellas County millage, City of Clearwater municipal millage, and special district levies. The total combined millage is approximately 19 to 22 mills for most City of Clearwater addresses. On a $395,000 home with homestead exemption, annual property taxes run approximately $6,000 to $7,500. Florida's homestead exemption reduces assessed value by $50,000 and must be applied for at pcpao.gov by March 1.

How Clearwater FL Property Taxes Work

Florida property taxes are ad valorem taxes based on the assessed value of real property. The Pinellas County Property Appraiser (pcpao.gov) sets annual assessed values. The Pinellas County Tax Collector (taxcollect.com) bills and collects taxes. Multiple taxing authorities set their own millage rates, and your total bill is the sum of all applicable millage rates applied to your assessed value.

Property taxes are paid in arrears in Florida. The tax year runs January 1 through December 31. Bills are issued in November and are due by March 31 of the following year. Florida offers a 4% discount for paying in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, and 1% in February. After March 31, penalties and interest apply.
