Trinity is predominantly a resale market. Unlike Wesley Chapel or Land O' Lakes, there is limited new construction within Trinity proper, most new building has moved further north and east. This means buyers are looking at homes that are 10-25 years old with the typical maintenance profile of that age range.

What Are the Neighborhoods in Trinity, FL?

Trinity Oaks

One of Trinity's largest and most established neighborhoods. Trinity Oaks features deed-restricted single-family homes built from the mid-1990s through mid-2000s. Community amenities include a pool, park, and trail connections. HOA fees are moderate. Homes typically range from $400,000 to $600,000+ depending on size and condition, with larger lots on the western sections of the community.

Champions Club

A golf community centered around the Fox Hollow Golf Club, a public 18-hole course. Champions Club homes tend to be larger and priced above Trinity's overall median, many 3,000+ square foot homes in the $550,000-$900,000 range. The neighborhood attracts buyers who want the golf lifestyle within Trinity's school district without the extreme prices of communities further south in Hillsborough County.

Fox Wood

A newer section of Trinity (early 2000s through 2010s construction) with a more suburban feel and generally lower HOA fees. Fox Wood is popular with first-time buyers in the $380,000-$480,000 range who want Trinity's school district but are working with a tighter budget.

Heritage Springs

An active adult (55+) community within Trinity. Heritage Springs has its own clubhouse, golf course, and amenities, with HOA fees that include more services than typical family communities. Buyers under 55 are generally not eligible to purchase here. Prices typically run $300,000-$500,000 depending on size and golf course position.

Thousand Oaks

Positioned along Mitchell Boulevard, Thousand Oaks is a deed-restricted community with established tree canopy and a quieter feel. Homes here are generally mid-sized single-family residences built in the late 1990s through early 2000s. Proximity to J.W. Mitchell High School makes this neighborhood popular with families.

Schools in Trinity, FL: What Buyers Need to Know

J.W. Mitchell High School is the primary driver of Trinity's price premium. It is ranked #131 in Florida by U.S. News and World Report, holds an A rating from the Florida Department of Education, and earns a 7 out of 10 on GreatSchools. The school serves approximately 2,201 students with a 22:1 student-to-teacher ratio and offers IB (International Baccalaureate) coursework alongside AP classes and dual enrollment options at Pasco-Hernando State College.

For context: J.W. Mitchell HS is ranked meaningfully above Pasco County's overall average and consistently outperforms most Pasco County high schools. Buyers specifically targeting this school zone should verify their home's attendance boundaries with Pasco County Schools before closing, boundaries can shift with new development.

Buyer Guide: Buying a Home in Trinity, FL

What Price Range Should Trinity Buyers Expect?

The Trinity market segments roughly as follows in 2026:

  • $350,000-$430,000: Older townhomes, smaller single-family in Fox Wood or outer Trinity areas. May need updates.
  • $430,000-$550,000: Mid-size single-family in Trinity Oaks, Thousand Oaks, Fox Wood. The core of the market.
  • $550,000-$750,000: Larger homes, golf course positions, updated kitchens and baths. Champions Club and Trinity Oaks west sections.
  • $750,000+: Top-tier Trinity. Larger lots, fully renovated, golf frontage, or estate section positions.

Do Trinity Homes Have CDD Fees?

CDD (Community Development District) fees exist in some Trinity communities but are generally lower than in newer Wesley Chapel developments because Trinity's CDDs have had more time to pay down their bond obligations. Many established Trinity neighborhoods carry $0-$800/year in CDD fees, compared to $1,500-$4,000 in recent Wesley Chapel new construction. However, HOA fees in Trinity can be substantial, Champions Club buyers should request the full fee disclosure before submitting an offer.

What Should Trinity Buyers Look for in Inspections?

Trinity homes are 15-30 years old in most neighborhoods. Key inspection items:

  • Roofs: Tile roofs common in this vintage can last 40+ years but underlayment often needs replacement at 20-25 years. Ask for roof age and underlayment inspection.
  • HVAC: Systems 12-15 years old are at end-of-life in Florida. Budget $8,000-$15,000 for replacement if the system is original.
  • Electrical: Some homes from this era have aluminum wiring in branch circuits, verify this with your inspector.
  • Plumbing: Polybutylene (gray plastic) pipes were used in some 1990s builds, if present, this is a significant remediation item.
  • Pool condition: Many Trinity homes have screened pools. Inspect pool finish, equipment, and cage condition carefully.

How Competitive Is the Trinity Market for Buyers?

At 39 days on market, Trinity moves faster than most of Pasco County. Well-priced, move-in-ready homes in the $430,000-$550,000 range attract multiple offers. Buyers should be pre-approved (not just pre-qualified) before touring, have earnest money ready, and use an agent familiar with Trinity's neighborhood-specific pricing, a home in Trinity Oaks and a home in Fox Wood at the same square footage can have meaningfully different values based on neighborhood, lot, and condition.

Seller Guide: Selling a Home in Trinity, FL

What Is My Trinity Home Worth?

Online estimates (Zestimate, etc.) consistently underperform in Trinity because they cannot account for neighborhood-specific premiums, lot position, pool presence, and renovation quality. A Champions Club golf-frontage home and a Fox Wood corner lot with original kitchen are not comparable on a price-per-square-foot basis, yet automated tools often treat them similarly. A proper CMA (comparative market analysis) using sold data within 0.5 miles and 90 days is required for accurate pricing.

When Is the Best Time to Sell in Trinity?

February through May is Trinity's peak listing season. Families with school-age children want to close before summer and be settled before the next school year. Listings that hit the market in late January or early February with updated photos and competitive pricing attract the largest buyer pool. June through August sees reduced buyer activity as families with children have settled their plans. Sellers listing in summer should price slightly more aggressively to compensate for the smaller buyer pool.

What Repairs and Updates Maximize Trinity Sale Price?

In Trinity's price range, buyers expect move-in-ready condition. Updates with the highest ROI in this market:

  • New interior paint (neutral): High ROI, low cost. Required if original or dated colors are present.
  • Updated kitchen: Counters, hardware, and appliances if original. Full gut renovations rarely recover cost in this price range, targeted updates work better.
  • Flooring: Replace worn carpet in main living areas with LVP or hardwood. Buyers in this price range expect hard surface or tile in main areas.
  • Landscaping: First impressions matter. Fresh mulch, trimmed shrubs, and a clean driveway add perceived value at low cost.
  • Roof certification or replacement: A roof in questionable condition either kills deals or results in price concessions larger than replacement cost. Know your roof's status before listing.

How Does Trinity Compare to Nearby Markets?

Trinity's premium relative to Land O' Lakes and Wesley Chapel reflects the combination of established neighborhoods, lower CDD burdens, and the J.W. Mitchell school zone. Buyers who need to be on the western side of Tampa Bay, near Clearwater, Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, or the beaches, will find Trinity's position on Veterans Expressway more advantageous than Land O' Lakes or Wesley Chapel, which require longer drives to reach the Pinellas side.

Is Trinity FL a Good Real Estate Investment?

Trinity is a hold-value market, not a speculative appreciation market. Home values in Trinity have been relatively stable and have held up better than some surrounding Pasco County markets during correction cycles. The combination of deed restrictions, an active HOA culture, and a dominant school zone creates durable demand. That said, Trinity is not a high-cap-rate rental market, the buy price is too high relative to rents to generate strong cash flow for investors. Buyers purchasing for primary residence or long-term equity building are the natural fit here.

If you are specifically an investor, Land O' Lakes or Zephyrhills offer lower entry prices with improving fundamentals. Trinity makes the most sense for owner-occupants who will benefit from the school zone and appreciate the established neighborhood character.

For rental property in the broader area, ViVi Property Management handles full-service leasing, tenant placement, and maintenance coordination across Pasco County.

Approximately 39 days on average in 2026. Move-in-ready homes in the $430,000-$550,000 range in the J.W. Mitchell school zone tend to sell faster, sometimes within 1-2 weeks when priced accurately. Homes needing significant updates or priced above market take 60-90+ days.

Is Trinity FL in Hillsborough or Pasco County?

Trinity is in Pasco County, not Hillsborough County. This is an important distinction for taxes, school district, and municipal services. Pasco County property tax rates are generally lower than Hillsborough County. Trinity homes are served by Pasco County Schools.

What is the best neighborhood to buy in Trinity FL?

It depends on your budget and priorities. Champions Club offers the golf lifestyle and larger homes for buyers in the $550,000+ range. Is Trinity FL good for families?

Pasco County Millage Rate

Trinity is an unincorporated community in Pasco County. There is no separate city or municipal tax. Total millage for unincorporated Pasco County typically runs 17.5 to 20.5 mills depending on the specific taxing districts at the property location. At 19 mills, a $475,000 home with a $50,000 homestead exemption (assessed value $425,000) generates approximately $8,075 in annual taxes, or about $673 per month. Investment properties without homestead exemption pay the full assessed value.

Save Our Homes Cap

Once you establish homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes amendment caps annual assessed value increases at 3% or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower. This is a meaningful long-term benefit in a market where property values have risen significantly. In the year of purchase, however, your assessed value starts at or near market value. The cap accumulates benefit over time, not in year one.

CDD Fees Are on the Tax Bill, Not the HOA Bill

In communities with a Community Development District (CDD), the annual assessment appears as a line item on the Pasco County property tax bill. It is NOT part of the monthly HOA fee. Starkey Ranch CDD assessments run approximately $2,000 to $3,500 per year depending on the specific sub-neighborhood. This amount is non-waivable and transfers to the next owner. You can look up CDD status for any parcel at pcpao.gov before making an offer. I recommend doing this for every Trinity purchase consideration.

Wind Mitigation Credits

A wind mitigation inspection (typically $125 to $175) documents construction features that can reduce your insurance premium by $300 to $1,200 per year. I recommend this inspection on any Trinity home built after 2002 that you plan to purchase. Homes in Starkey Ranch (built from 2014 onward) generally qualify for these credits.

Flood Insurance: Zone X Advantage

The vast majority of Trinity residential properties are FEMA Zone X, which means minimal flood risk and no lender-required flood insurance. This saves Trinity homeowners $1,500 to $5,000+ per year compared to coastal Pasco County flood zones. Water and sewer in Trinity is provided by Pasco County Utilities (pascocountyfl.net). Monthly bills typically run $45 to $90 for a household of two to four people, depending on irrigation usage. Homes with large yards and irrigation systems can see higher bills during dry season.

Spectrum is the dominant internet provider in Trinity. Spectrum Gig speeds are available in most Trinity neighborhoods. Heritage Springs has cable included in the HOA fee. In most other Trinity communities, expect $65 to $120 per month for internet. Frontier Fiber is available in select areas.

content:
Quick Answer

Trinity FL property taxes run approximately 17.5 to 20.5 mills total for unincorporated Pasco County. On a $490,000 home with homestead exemption, expect $7,500 to $9,000 per year in property taxes. CDD fees in newer communities add $2,000 to $3,500 per year on top of this, billed on the same property tax notice. For a property-specific estimate call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

Trinity FL Property Taxes: What to Budget in 2026

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 26, 2026

Property taxes in Trinity FL are collected by Pasco County and reflect a combination of county, school, and special district millage rates. Trinity is an unincorporated community, so there is no separate city or municipal millage layer, which keeps the total rate lower than incorporated cities in Pasco County.

The complexity in Trinity comes from Community Development District (CDD) fees that appear on the same notice as property taxes for newer communities. Many buyers also encounter a mismatch between the current seller tax bill and what they will pay in year one, because the previous owner had Save Our Homes cap protection that does not transfer. Understanding this reset is essential to accurate budgeting.

Note: Pasco County uses a Municipal Services Benefit Unit (MSBU) system where special service districts cover fire/EMS, library, and road/stormwater. Your specific millage total depends on which MSBUs your parcel falls within. The Pasco County Property Appraiser website (pcpao.gov) allows you to look up the exact millage breakdown for any parcel by address or parcel ID.

Sample Tax Calculations

Scenario 1: $430,000 Home, Trinity Oaks, Homestead Exemption

Just value: $430,000. Minus standard homestead exemption: $50,000. Assessed value: $380,000. At 19 mills: $380,000 x 0.019 = $7,220 per year, approximately $602 per month. No CDD for Trinity Oaks.

Scenario 2: $520,000 Home, Starkey Ranch, Homestead Exemption, with CDD

Just value: $520,000. Minus homestead exemption: $50,000. Assessed value: $470,000. At 19 mills: $470,000 x 0.019 = $8,930 per year. Plus CDD fee: $2,400 to $3,200 per year. Total annual tax notice: approximately $11,330 to $12,130, or $944 to $1,011 per month.

Scenario 3: $420,000 Home, Heritage Springs, Homestead Exemption

Just value: $420,000. Minus homestead exemption: $50,000. Assessed value: $370,000. At 19 mills: $370,000 x 0.019 = $7,030 per year. No CDD at Heritage Springs. Approximately $586 per month.

Scenario 4: $480,000 Investment Property, No Homestead

Just value: $480,000. No homestead exemption. At 19 mills: $480,000 x 0.019 = $9,120 per year, approximately $760 per month. Plus any applicable CDD. Investment properties pay full assessed value with no exemption discount and no Save Our Homes cap protection.

Homestead Exemption

Standard Exemption

Florida homestead exemption reduces the assessed value of your primary residence by $50,000 for most taxing authorities (the first $25,000 applies to all; the second $25,000 applies to non-school millage only). To receive the exemption, you must own the property on January 1, establish it as your primary residence, and file by March 1 of the tax year. The Pasco County Property Appraiser (pcpao.gov; 352-521-4338) handles homestead applications. Applications are accepted online at pcpao.gov.

Additional Exemptions

Additional exemptions are available for qualifying residents: a $500 disability exemption, a veteran disability exemption (partial or total depending on disability rating), a senior low-income exemption (for residents 65+ with income under the threshold), and a widow/widower exemption. These apply in addition to the standard homestead exemption. Application deadlines and income thresholds change annually; check pcpao.gov for current requirements.

Save Our Homes Cap

Once homestead is established, the Save Our Homes amendment limits annual assessed value increases to 3% or the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. In years of rapid appreciation, this creates a meaningful gap between assessed value and market value for long-term owners.

The practical implication for buyers: the seller tax bill you see on Zillow or the MLS reflects years of 3% cap protection. Your assessed value in year one resets to current market value (less the homestead exemption). Your first-year tax bill will likely be higher than what the seller paid. The gap can be significant in communities where values have risen substantially.

Portability

Florida portability allows you to transfer up to $500,000 of Save Our Homes accumulated benefit from your previous Florida homestead to your new one. If you are selling a homesteaded Florida property and buying in Trinity, applying for portability can significantly reduce your assessed value in year one. Apply for portability at the same time as homestead exemption, by March 1 of the year following your purchase. More information is available at pcpao.gov.

CDD Fees Explained

What Is a CDD?

A Community Development District is a special-purpose local government created under Florida law (Chapter 190, Florida Statutes) to finance and maintain infrastructure for a development. CDDs issue bonds to fund the infrastructure, and the bonds are repaid through annual assessments on properties within the district. When the bonds are fully repaid, only the maintenance assessment remains, and the fee drops.

How CDD Fees Appear on Your Tax Bill

CDD fees appear on your Pasco County property tax notice as separate line items under "Non-Ad Valorem Assessments." They are due at the same time as property taxes (by March 31 to avoid interest; early payment discounts apply in November through February). The fee is not reduced by homestead exemption. Every owner pays the full CDD assessment regardless of exemption status.

How to Look Up Property Taxes Before Buying

The Pasco County Property Appraiser website (pcpao.gov) allows free lookups by address or parcel number. The site shows just value, assessed value, exemptions, taxing authorities, and current year tax amounts. For new construction, the lot may show lower values until the home is assessed after completion. In Starkey Ranch and similar new construction communities, the builder can provide the estimated CDD fee for a specific lot. Request this in writing before signing a purchase contract.

The Pasco County Tax Collector (pascotaxes.com) processes payments. Pay early for discounts: 4% off in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February, face amount in March.

Frequently Asked Questions: Trinity FL Property Taxes

Why will my property taxes be higher than the seller's?

The seller tax bill reflects years of Save Our Homes cap protection, which limits assessed value increases to 3% per year for homesteaded properties. When you purchase, the assessed value resets to current market value (just value), less your new homestead exemption. The first-year bill can be significantly higher. Check pcpao.gov for the current year estimated tax at your purchase price.

Can I appeal my property tax assessment?

Yes. If you believe your just value does not reflect market value, you can file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board (VAB) by the deadline on your TRIM (Truth in Millage) notice, which typically arrives in mid-August to mid-September. Contact pcpao.gov or 352-521-4338 for the appeal process.

Are CDD fees negotiable with the seller?

No. CDD fees are a government assessment tied to the parcel, not the seller. They transfer to the buyer at closing. Some sellers offer closing cost credits to offset the fee, but the CDD obligation itself is not extinguishable. The fee can be paid off early in some districts by paying the outstanding bond balance directly. Check with the specific CDD management company for payoff options.

What is the homestead exemption filing deadline in Pasco County?

The deadline is March 1 of the tax year for which you want the exemption. If you close in August 2026, file for homestead exemption by March 1, 2027 to receive the exemption on your 2027 tax bill. File online at pcpao.gov.

Does Florida have an estate tax or inheritance tax?

No. Florida has no estate tax and no inheritance tax. Property transferred at death to heirs does not trigger a Florida tax. Federal estate tax may apply for large estates above the federal exemption threshold. Consult an estate attorney for planning specific to your situation.

New Construction in Trinity FL: Builders and Communities 2026

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 26, 2026

Trinity has limited supply of available land for new construction within its established core. The area built out significantly during the 1980s through the 2000s. The primary new construction activity in Trinity today is in Starkey Ranch, a master-planned development along Trinity Boulevard and Gunn Highway that has been developing since approximately 2016 and continues to add phases. Some scattered infill lots exist in other sections, but Starkey Ranch represents the majority of new home inventory.

I have represented buyers purchasing new construction homes across Pasco County for over 23 years, including dozens of transactions in Starkey Ranch. The builder on-site sales representative represents the builder's interests, not yours. This is the single most important thing to understand before walking into a model home and signing anything. Buyer representation in new construction typically comes at no cost to you because builder commissions are factored into the sales price regardless.

Where Is New Construction Available in Trinity FL?

Starkey Ranch

Starkey Ranch is a master-planned community managed by the Starkey Ranch Community Development District and its HOA. The community spans several thousand acres along the western edge of Trinity, bordering Jay B. Starkey Wilderness Preserve. Multiple neighborhoods within Starkey Ranch offer different builders, home sizes, and price points. Community features include a K-8 school (Starkey Ranch K-8), a community library branch, recreational trails, multiple pools, and a town center with a Publix. The community connects to the Suncoast Parkway via Trinity Boulevard, making Tampa accessible in approximately 35 to 45 minutes.

Infill and Scattered Sites

Outside of Starkey Ranch, new construction in Trinity is limited to occasional infill lots in established communities and very occasional teardown-rebuild situations. These are rare. Buyers seeking completely new homes in Trinity who do not want Starkey Ranch will find options limited. Most buyers seeking new construction in western Pasco County choose between Starkey Ranch in Trinity and new communities further east near Wesley Chapel or south near Land O Lakes.

What to Expect When Buying New Construction in Starkey Ranch

The Purchase Process

New construction purchases in Starkey Ranch follow a builder-specific process that differs from resale transactions. You select a lot and floor plan from available options in the current phase, then sign the builder purchase contract. The contract is typically the builder form, written in the builder's favor. Key terms include the deposit structure (often 3% to 10% of the purchase price paid in stages), the closing timeline (typically 6 to 12 months for a build), and change order procedures.

CDD Fees Are Permanent Until Bonds Are Paid Off

Every home in Starkey Ranch is subject to CDD fees. These appear on your Pasco County property tax bill as non-ad valorem assessments. Fees vary by sub-neighborhood within Starkey Ranch because different phases were funded by separate bond issuances. Typical range is $2,000 to $3,500 per year. Ask the builder sales agent for the specific CDD fee for the lot you are considering, and get it in writing. The fee is non-negotiable and transfers to all future owners until the bonds are retired.

Builder Upgrades and the Design Center

Builders in Starkey Ranch earn significant profit at the design center, where buyers select flooring, countertops, cabinetry, fixtures, and structural options. Standard-package homes are priced attractively; the final home often costs 15% to 30% more than the base price after upgrades. I advise buyers to establish a design center budget before going in and to compare some upgrades against the cost of installing them post-closing through independent contractors, which is sometimes significantly cheaper.

New Construction Inspections

Many buyers skip inspections on new construction, assuming the home is defect-free because it is new. This is a mistake. I recommend three inspections: a pre-drywall inspection (to check framing, rough-in plumbing, and electrical before walls are closed), a final walk-through inspection, and a one-year warranty inspection at the 11-month mark before the builder one-year warranty expires. New construction defects are common and are much easier to address before or during the warranty period.

Frequently Asked Questions: New Construction in Trinity FL

Do I need a buyer's agent for new construction in Trinity FL?

Yes, and it typically costs you nothing. Builders pay buyer agent commissions from the sales price regardless of whether you bring an agent. The builder on-site agent represents the builder. Having your own agent gives you contract representation and someone whose job is to protect your interests. Register your agent on your first visit to the model home or sales center. Most builders require agent registration on the initial visit to honor the co-op commission.

How long does it take to build a home in Starkey Ranch?

Build timelines typically run 6 to 12 months from contract execution to closing, depending on the builder, plan complexity, and current construction demand. Spec homes already under construction can close in 30 to 90 days. Get a specific timeline in writing from the builder and understand the contract provisions if closing is delayed.

Can I negotiate on a new construction home in Trinity FL?

Builders in Starkey Ranch rarely negotiate directly on the base price because it sets a precedent for other buyers in the same phase. However, builders do negotiate on closing costs, included upgrades, premium lot fees, and rate buydowns through their preferred lender. End of quarter and end of year are typically when builders are most willing to negotiate to hit sales targets.

What is Starkey Ranch K-8 school like?

Starkey Ranch K-8 is a public school within the Pasco County School District, physically located inside the Starkey Ranch community. It opened in 2016 and has maintained A-school status. It serves kindergarten through 8th grade. Students then attend J.W. Mitchell High School. The school's location within the community means many students can walk or bike. Enrollment is primarily for Starkey Ranch residents. Check pasco.k12.fl.us for current ratings and capacity.

What happens to my CDD fee when the bonds are paid off?

Once the CDD bonds are retired, the annual assessment drops significantly to cover only ongoing maintenance costs. The timeline for bond retirement depends on the specific phase and when the bonds were issued. Ask the builder to provide the CDD bond payoff schedule for the specific lot you are considering. This information should be publicly available through the CDD financial records.

Rental Market Analysis: Trinity FL 2026

Long-Term Rental (LTR) Demand

Long-term rental demand in Trinity is steady. The primary tenant base is families with school-age children who want the J.W. Mitchell or Longleaf school zone but are not yet ready to buy. Secondary demand comes from corporate relocations, households in transition, and Pasco County employees. Trinity rentals in the 3-bedroom, 2-bath range typically rent within 2 to 4 weeks when priced competitively.

Estimates based on 2025-2026 market conditions. Cap rates are gross and do not include operating expenses.
Property TypeApprox Purchase PriceMonthly LTR Rent (est)Annual Gross RentGross Cap Rate (est)
3BR/2BA, 1,600 to 1,900 sq ft, Trinity Oaks$360K to $420K$2,100 to $2,400/mo$25,200 to $28,8006.0% to 8.0%

Net Operating Income Reality

Gross cap rates look reasonable until you account for operating expenses. In Trinity, expect the following annual expenses on a typical investment property: property taxes (approximately $7,500 to $9,500 on a non-homesteaded property), homeowners insurance (approximately $2,200 to $4,000), HOA fees (approximately $400 to $1,800 depending on community), CDD fees (approximately $0 to $3,500 depending on community), property management (8% to 10% of gross rent if using a manager), maintenance reserve (1% of value annually), and vacancy allowance (5% to 8% for this market). These combined expenses typically run $16,000 to $25,000 per year on a $450K to $550K property, reducing the net cap rate to approximately 2.5% to 4.5%.

Short-Term Rentals in Trinity FL

HOA Restrictions Are the Core Issue

The fundamental challenge for STR investors in Trinity is HOA restrictions. The vast majority of Trinity HOAs prohibit rentals of less than 6 months or 12 months, making Airbnb and VRBO-style rentals effectively prohibited under the governing documents. Heritage Springs (55+) has strict rental restrictions tied to the age requirement. Starkey Ranch HOA restricts short-term rentals. Champions Club does the same. Violating HOA rental restrictions can result in fines, legal action, and an HOA lien against the property.

Pasco County does not have a county-wide short-term rental ban, and Florida Statute 509.032 broadly preempts local government STR restrictions. However, private HOA governing documents are not subject to this preemption. An HOA can legally restrict rentals within its community. Before purchasing any Trinity property for STR purposes, have a real estate attorney review the specific Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs) for the community.

Pasco County Tourist Development Tax

For the limited properties that are not subject to HOA rental restrictions, Pasco County collects Tourist Development Tax (TDT) on short-term rentals. As of 2025, the Pasco County TDT rate is 6%. Remittance is required to the Pasco County Tax Collector on a monthly basis. A Florida DBPR Vacation Rental license is also required for STR operations statewide.

ViVi Property Management for Trinity Rentals

ViVi Property Management serves investors in western Pasco County, including Trinity. Services include tenant screening, lease preparation, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and move-in/move-out inspections. For investors who do not want to self-manage, a professional property manager reduces vacancy risk and time investment. Contact ViVi through the property management page for rates and availability.

Is Trinity FL a Good Real Estate Investment?

The Case For Trinity Investment

  • Strong, stable LTR demand driven by school quality (J.W. Mitchell HS, Longleaf Elementary)
  • Low flood risk (Zone X) eliminates mandatory flood insurance as a cost
  • No city/municipal tax (unincorporated Pasco County) reduces carrying costs
  • Appreciation track record: Trinity values have risen significantly over the past decade
  • School-zone demand attracts family tenants who tend to stay longer

The Case Against Trinity Investment

  • Price points are high relative to rent, making leveraged returns thin at current rates
  • HOA restrictions eliminate STR as a strategy in most communities
  • CDD fees in Starkey Ranch reduce net returns by $167 to $292 per month compared to non-CDD properties
  • Heritage Springs is 55+ and restricts tenant age, significantly limiting the tenant pool
  • Pasco County rental market competes with active supply from Wesley Chapel and Land O Lakes

Investment Due Diligence Checklist for Trinity FL

  • Obtain the HOA CC&Rs and confirm rental permissibility and minimum lease term
  • Check pcpao.gov for CDD status and annual assessment amount for the specific parcel
  • Get current homeowners and flood insurance quotes before finalizing your offer
  • Verify school zone assignment at pasco.k12.fl.us (investment value depends on this)
  • Review HOA financial documents: budget, reserve study, reserve funding percentage
  • Confirm no pending HOA special assessments that would transfer to you at closing
  • Run a realistic pro forma with actual non-homesteaded property tax at current value

Frequently Asked Questions: Trinity FL Investment Property

Can I do short-term rentals (Airbnb/VRBO) in Trinity FL?

In most Trinity communities, no. HOA governing documents in virtually all Trinity communities prohibit rentals under 6 or 12 months, which effectively prohibits Airbnb and VRBO-style rentals. HOA restrictions are enforceable through fines and legal action. Before purchasing any Trinity property for STR, have a real estate attorney review the specific CC&Rs. Do not rely on verbal representations from sellers or listing agents.

What is the typical vacancy rate for long-term rentals in Trinity FL?

Well-priced Trinity LTR properties typically experience 4 to 8 weeks of vacancy between tenants in current market conditions. A property priced at market rate in good condition in the J.W. Mitchell school zone tends toward the lower end of this range. Pricing too high extends vacancy significantly.

Should I buy in Trinity or Wesley Chapel for investment?

Wesley Chapel generally offers more new construction options and active development, which can provide equity through appreciation in newer phases. Trinity offers more established communities with lower entry points in non-CDD areas and a proven school-driven rental market. Both are viable for long-term buy-and-hold. The choice depends on whether you want newer construction (Wesley Chapel) or established neighborhoods with larger lots and no CDD (older Trinity). Call Barrett for a comparison specific to your budget and investment criteria.

Does Heritage Springs allow long-term rentals?

Heritage Springs is a 55+ active adult community. Rentals are subject to the age restriction: at least one occupant per home must be 55 or older, and no occupants under 19 are permitted with limited exceptions. This significantly restricts the tenant pool to seniors or retirees. Before purchasing Heritage Springs for investment, confirm the specific rental rules with the HOA directly.

Quick Answer

New Port Richey FL (ZIPs 34652-34655, Pasco County) has a median sold price of approximately $265K-$290K through 2026. The downtown area is undergoing active revitalization. Canal and Cotee River properties command premiums. For a buyer consultation, call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

New Port Richey FL Homes for Sale: What Buyers Need to Know

New Port Richey is one of the more interesting markets in Pasco County right now. The city has a downtown revival underway, with Sims Park along the Cotee River serving as an anchor, and the Railroad Square Park reopening in May 2026 as part of the pedestrian-friendly redevelopment effort. At the same time, the city's housing stock spans a wide range, from affordable older ranch homes in the $200K range to canal-front properties approaching $600K+.

I work this market regularly. New Port Richey is larger and more developed than its neighbor Port Richey to the south, with a more defined city identity and a broader range of property types. Here is what buyers need to know before searching.

What Are Home Prices Like in New Port Richey FL?

Overall Market Data for 2026

According to multiple market data sources through mid-2026, the median sold price in New Port Richey ranges from approximately $265K to $290K depending on data source and measurement period. Zillow's estimated typical home value was $288,380 as of August 2026, down about 1.3% year-over-year. Closed-sale medians from transaction data put the figure closer to $265K. A reasonable working range for buyers is $265K-$290K for the city overall.

ZIP code 34652 (closest to downtown and the Gulf) tends to have lower medians because of more older and smaller housing. ZIPs 34653 and 34654 (moving east toward Seven Springs and River Ridge areas) carry higher prices due to newer construction and Trinity adjacency.

How New Port Richey Prices Compare to Nearby Markets

What Areas and Neighborhoods Does New Port Richey Offer?

Downtown New Port Richey

Downtown NPR centers on Main Street and Grand Boulevard, with Sims Park along the Cotee River as its green anchor. This area is in active revitalization. The Railroad Square Park project reopened in May 2026, adding pedestrian gathering space at Nebraska Avenue and Grand Boulevard. New restaurants, boutiques, and events have followed. Homes close to downtown are older bungalows and ranch styles but offer the most walkable environment in the city. Prices in this area range from $250K-$450K depending on condition and proximity to the river.

West Side of US-19

Neighborhoods west of US-19 have the highest flood risk in New Port Richey, per the city's own flood information. These areas typically have lower natural grade and higher Base Flood Elevation requirements. Canal-front properties on this side of town offer Gulf water access via the Cotee River but require more flood due diligence. Many properties here are in FEMA Zone AE.

East Side and Seven Springs Area (34654-34655)

Moving east toward the Seven Springs and River Ridge High School areas, the housing stock transitions to newer construction from the 1990s-2010s. This part of New Port Richey blends into Trinity and has more HOA communities, better school zone assignments for many buyers, and higher prices. River Ridge High School at 11646 Town Center Rd serves this area.

NPR Condos and Smaller Communities

New Port Richey has a number of older condominium complexes, particularly in ZIP 34652. Buyers considering condos should be aware of Florida's SB 4-D milestone inspection requirements. Any condo in a building three stories or taller that was built before 1990 requires a structural milestone inspection and reserve study. The status of these inspections affects financing (some lenders will not approve condos that are not compliant) and special assessment risk. Always ask for the condo association's milestone inspection status and reserve fund disclosure before making an offer.

What Should Buyers Know About Flood Risk in New Port Richey?

The City's Own Flood Disclosure

The City of New Port Richey is candid about flood risk. Per the city's official flood information page, the Cotee River and Gulf proximity create risk of storm surge, flash flooding, and prolonged inundation. The city states that neighborhoods west of US-19 typically have lower natural grade and a higher Base Flood Elevation, and have historically flooded more frequently than neighborhoods to the east. The city also notes a 26% chance of flooding over the life of a 30-year mortgage for properties in the Special Flood Hazard Area.

Flood insurance is required by lenders for any property in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally-backed loan. For more information on a specific address, the city building department is at (727) 853-1047, and the FEMA map service is at msc.fema.gov.

For waterfront or canal properties specifically, add seawall inspection, dock permit verification, and riparian rights review to the inspection checklist. These issues can affect value and insurability significantly.

Frequently Asked Questions About New Port Richey FL Homes

What is the median home price in New Port Richey FL?

The median sold price in New Port Richey was approximately $265K-$290K through mid-2026, based on multiple market data sources. Zillow estimated $288,380 as of August 2026. Canal-front and river properties run $320K-$700K+.

Is New Port Richey in a flood zone?

Many properties, particularly west of US-19 and along the Cotee River, are in FEMA Special Flood Hazard Areas (Zone AE). Verify any specific property at msc.fema.gov. The City of New Port Richey building department at (727) 853-1047 can also assist with flood zone questions.

What is the downtown New Port Richey revitalization about?

Downtown New Port Richey has been undergoing active revitalization for several years. Sims Park along the Cotee River is a central gathering space. The Railroad Square Park opened in May 2026, extending the pedestrian-friendly district. New businesses, restaurants, and housing have followed. The city continues pursuing additional redevelopment, including the Main and Bank Building RFP issued in June 2026.

Are there new construction homes in New Port Richey?

New construction in New Port Richey proper is limited primarily to infill lots and smaller projects, since most of the city is already developed. Buyers looking for new construction in the area are often directed to Trinity (34655) or the Seven Springs area. See the New Port Richey new construction guide for details.

Does New Port Richey have a downtown?

Yes. Downtown New Port Richey centers on Main Street and the Cotee River waterfront, including Sims Park. The area has restaurants, shops, and events. It is modest compared to downtown St. Petersburg but genuinely walkable within a few blocks. The Railroad Square Park project extended the pedestrian zone in 2026.

Quick Answer

New Port Richey FL to downtown Tampa is approximately 38-50 minutes under normal conditions and 55-75 minutes during peak rush hour. The Suncoast Pkwy (SR-589) via SR-54 is the fastest Tampa route. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for real estate questions.

New Port Richey FL Commute Times, Routes, and What to Expect

New Port Richey sits about 32-38 miles north of downtown Tampa depending on the specific neighborhood. The commute is manageable but not short, and the routing options matter significantly. Most buyers find the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) via SR-54 to be the preferred route for Tampa trips, while US-19 serves shorter trips within Pasco County and to Clearwater.

Here is what I tell buyers who are weighing a New Port Richey purchase against something closer to Tampa. The commute is workable if you are not in a downtown Tampa office five days a week at fixed hours. It becomes a meaningful quality-of-life factor if you are.

How Long Is the Commute from New Port Richey to Tampa?

Downtown Tampa38-50 min55-75 minSuncoast Pkwy (SR-589) via SR-54
Tampa International Airport (TPA)33-45 min48-65 minSuncoast Pkwy (SR-589)

These are estimates. Time varies by NPR neighborhood, time of day, and day of week. Check Google Maps or Waze at your target departure time before making any purchase decision based on commute time.

What Are the Main Routes from New Port Richey to Tampa?

Suncoast Parkway (SR-589): The Primary Tampa Route

The Suncoast Pkwy is a limited-access toll expressway that provides the fastest connection from New Port Richey to the Tampa metro. The main NPR on-ramp is accessible via SR-54. From there, the expressway runs south to Veterans Expressway (continuing as SR-589) and into Tampa. For Tampa, Westshore, or TPA, the Suncoast Pkwy saves 10-20 minutes versus US-19 during any significant traffic period.

Toll cost for a typical Tampa round-trip from NPR is approximately $2-$4 with a SunPass transponder. Without SunPass, tolls are higher. At 5 days per week over a year, SunPass tolls run roughly $500-$1,000 annually, which is a cost factor to include in the monthly budget comparison.

SR-54: Gateway to I-75 and the East

SR-54 is New Port Richey's main east-west corridor. It provides access to the Suncoast Pkwy on-ramp (west of I-75) and to I-75 at Wesley Chapel (to the east). For commutes to Lakeland, Polk County, or Orlando, SR-54 to I-75 is the primary route. From NPR to the SR-54/I-75 interchange is approximately 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

US-19: Local Trips and Clearwater Commutes

US-19 runs north-south through New Port Richey and is the main commercial corridor. For commutes to north Pinellas (Clearwater, Dunedin, Safety Harbor), US-19 south to CR-580 west is the most direct route. However, US-19's frequent traffic lights and commercial cross-traffic make it slow during rush hour. For Tampa trips, US-19 is consistently slower than the Suncoast Pkwy.

Is There Public Transit from New Port Richey to Tampa?

Pasco County Transit (PCPT)

PCPT operates bus service within Pasco County, including routes that serve the New Port Richey and US-19 corridor. However, there is no direct, practical bus route from New Port Richey to Tampa with reasonable travel times. Multi-transfer trips via PCPT and Pinellas Suncoast Transit can take 3-5 hours to reach Tampa, making them practical only for those without other options.

No Rail or Express Bus to Tampa

New Port Richey has no commuter rail service to Tampa. There is no cross-county express bus service that makes the NPR-to-Tampa trip feasible for daily commuters. The only practical commuting options are personal vehicle (via Suncoast Pkwy) or remote/hybrid work arrangements.

title: Is New Port Richey FL Good to Live In? (2026)
excerpt: Is New Port Richey FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Review, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

New Port Richey FL is a good fit for buyers who want an affordable Gulf Coast community with a revitalizing downtown, can navigate flood zone due diligence, and work remotely or in Pasco County. It is less suited to daily Tampa commuters or buyers expecting a polished master-planned suburb. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

Is New Port Richey Florida a Good Place to Live? An Honest 2026 Review

New Port Richey is a city in active transition. The downtown core along the Cotee River has been improving for several years, with Sims Park as the anchor and the Railroad Square Park addition in May 2026 extending the walkable district. Property values are relatively affordable compared to Pinellas County. But New Port Richey is also a city with real flood risk, an aging housing stock in many areas, and a Tampa commute that requires the Suncoast Pkwy to be reasonable.

I work with buyers considering New Port Richey regularly. Here is the honest picture.

What Are the Genuine Pros of Living in New Port Richey FL?

An Affordable Gulf Coast City With a Real Downtown

New Port Richey is one of the few affordable communities in the Tampa Bay area with a genuine (if modest) walkable downtown. Main Street and the Cotee River waterfront have restaurants, coffee shops, events, and Sims Park. The Railroad Square Park expansion in May 2026 added pedestrian space. For buyers who want community character rather than a generic suburban strip, NPR offers that at a median price of $265K-$290K.

Real Water Access

The Cotee River runs through New Port Richey and connects to the Gulf of Mexico. Canal-front properties throughout the city provide boat access to the Gulf. For buyers who prioritize boating, kayaking, or Gulf-side living without Pinellas County prices, NPR offers genuine water access at a fraction of Clearwater or Dunedin prices.

No Florida State Income Tax and Homestead Exemption

Florida has no state income tax. New Port Richey homeowners who establish homestead on their primary residence benefit from the $50,000 homestead exemption (reducing assessed value for tax purposes) and the Save Our Homes cap, which limits annual assessed value increases to 3% or CPI, whichever is less. For buyers relocating from high-tax states, Florida's tax structure is a meaningful financial advantage.

Proximity to Gulf Beaches

New Port Richey is 25-35 miles from the public beaches of Clearwater Beach, Honeymoon Island, and Caladesi Island State Park. While it is not a beachfront community itself, residents can reach some of Florida's best Gulf beaches in 30-45 minutes. For buyers who want beach access without paying beachfront prices, this proximity has real value.

Growing Downtown and Events Calendar

New Port Richey hosts regular community events including the Chasco Fiesta (an annual spring festival), weekend farmers markets, and events in Sims Park. The downtown's Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) continues to invest in improvements. For buyers who want a community with events and a social scene, NPR's downtown offers more than most comparable-priced markets in Pasco County.

What Are the Honest Cons of Living in New Port Richey FL?

Significant Flood Risk in Many Neighborhoods

The City of New Port Richey acknowledges on its official flood information pages that neighborhoods west of US-19 historically flood more frequently, have lower natural grade, and face higher Base Flood Elevation requirements. Approximately 44% of the city (by some city estimates) falls within a Special Flood Hazard Area. Flood insurance in Zone AE runs $1,200-$4,500+/year; waterfront properties can cost significantly more. This is not a minor cost or risk consideration.

US-19 Corridor: Commercial Character Not for Everyone

US-19 through New Port Richey is a heavily commercialized strip corridor with strip malls, fast food, and auto-oriented development. Residential streets off US-19 are typically quiet, but the main commercial corridor lacks the aesthetic and walkable character of more urban markets. Buyers who prioritize visual environment should tour the specific neighborhoods they are considering, not just the main road.

Older Housing Stock with Known Issues

Most of New Port Richey's housing was built between 1960 and 1995. Common inspection issues include aging flat roofs, Federal Pacific and Zinsco electrical panels that require replacement, galvanized plumbing in older homes, and HVAC systems nearing end of life. Insurance underwriters are increasingly strict about these issues. Budget for inspections and potential repair costs, particularly on homes built before 1985.

Tampa Commute Is Workable but Not Short

The commute to downtown Tampa is 38-50 minutes under normal conditions and 55-75 minutes during peak rush hour. For full-time Tampa office workers, this is 1.5-2.5 hours of daily driving plus toll costs. It is workable for many buyers but should be tested at the actual commute time before purchase.

School Quality Varies by Zone

School quality varies significantly within New Port Richey. Eastern NPR near Seven Springs/River Ridge High rates better on state metrics than western NPR near Gulf High. For buyers with school-age children, verifying the specific school zone for a property is essential before making an offer.

Frequently Asked Questions: Is New Port Richey FL a Good Place to Live?

Is New Port Richey FL safe?

Crime varies by neighborhood. Downtown NPR and the more established residential streets have typical suburban crime levels. As with any city, check the Pasco County Sheriff's Office crime map for specific street-level data for any property you are considering.

Is New Port Richey FL affordable?

Yes, by Tampa Bay metro standards. The median sold price is $265K-$290K. Combined with no Florida state income tax and homestead exemption savings, the cost of ownership is substantially lower than comparable lifestyle options in Pinellas County. Main cost watch items are flood insurance and homeowners insurance.

Is New Port Richey FL growing?

The downtown is actively growing and improving. The broader Pasco County area is one of the fastest-growing counties in Florida, though much of the new development is in Wesley Chapel and Trinity to the east. New Port Richey itself is mostly built-out, with growth driven by revitalization and infill rather than new subdivisions.

What is New Port Richey known for?

New Port Richey is known for its Cotee River waterfront, the Chasco Fiesta (one of Pasco County's largest annual events), downtown revitalization centered on Sims Park, and as an affordable Gulf Coast alternative to Pinellas County communities. It is also home to Gulf High School's magnet programs and the Seven Springs area with River Ridge High.

What are the best parts of New Port Richey?

The downtown/Sims Park area offers the most walkable character. The eastern NPR/Seven Springs corridor (ZIP 34654-34655) offers newer housing stock and River Ridge High School. Canal-front streets throughout the city offer waterfront access at lower price points than the Pinellas barrier islands.

New Port Richey FL Real Estate: Prices, Trends, and Buyer Strategy for 2026

New Port Richey's real estate market in 2026 is characterized by balanced supply and demand, modest year-over-year price declines of 1-2% depending on the data source, and a continued split between the affordable inland/older segments and the premium waterfront and canal segments. The downtown revitalization adds a third dimension that does not have a direct parallel in nearby markets.

I work this market year-round. Here is the picture buyers and sellers need to understand in 2026.

What Does the New Port Richey Real Estate Market Look Like in 2026?

Key Market Metrics

Based on market data through mid-to-late 2026, New Port Richey's overall market shows: a median sold price of approximately $265K-$290K (varying by data source and measurement period); a modest year-over-year decline of 1-2%; and a balanced supply-demand dynamic with roughly 4 months of supply, which neither strongly favors buyers nor sellers.

What Drives Value in New Port Richey Real Estate?

Waterfront Premium

Canal-front and Cotee River properties command the most significant premiums over comparable inland homes. A canal-front home with a boat lift typically sells for 20-50% more than an equivalent inland property in the same condition. Direct Cotee River frontage with Gulf access carries even higher premiums. This dynamic is consistent with Gulf Coast waterfront markets broadly, but NPR's premium is lower than Clearwater or Sarasota because of the flood insurance cost that comes with Zone AE designation.

Flood Zone Impact on Value

Properties in FEMA Zone AE face a structural cost disadvantage compared to Zone X properties: required flood insurance adds $1,200-$4,500+/year to carrying costs, affects the pool of buyers (some are unwilling to pay flood insurance), and can complicate financing. In practice, Zone AE properties in NPR often carry lower list prices than equivalent Zone X properties, which partially offsets the insurance cost. Buyers should model the full monthly cost including flood insurance for any Zone AE property before comparing to Zone X alternatives.

School Zone and Eastern vs Western NPR

Eastern NPR (ZIP 34654-34655 area, River Ridge High zone) commands a modest premium over western NPR (ZIP 34652, Gulf High zone) on a price-per-square-foot basis, partly due to newer housing stock and the perception of better schools. However, ZIP 34655 also includes Trinity, which skews the data upward. Within pure NPR boundaries, the eastern premium is real but moderate.

Downtown Revitalization Premium

Homes close to downtown NPR's Main Street and Sims Park have benefited from the revitalization effort. This premium is modest but real, and prices near downtown have held up better than some inland sections. As the CRA continues its investment, properties within walking distance of the downtown core are expected to hold a relative premium.

What Should Buyers Know About the 2026 New Port Richey Market?

Buyer Strategy in a Balanced Market

With roughly 4 months of supply and modest year-over-year price declines, buyers have more leverage than in the 2021-2022 seller's market. Key strategies for 2026 buyers in NPR include:

Don't skip seawall inspection on canal propertiesSeawall replacement in NPR can run $15,000-$60,000+

Seller Strategy for 2026

Sellers in New Port Richey's 2026 balanced market should price competitively from day one. Overpriced listings are sitting longer (60+ days) before needing price reductions. Sellers who address the most common buyer objections before listing, primarily roof age, panel type, and deferred maintenance, tend to see fewer inspection-period renegotiations. For waterfront properties, verifying that dock permits are current and seawall condition is documented can accelerate the sale.

What Types of Properties Are Available in New Port Richey?

Single-Family Homes

Single-family homes make up the majority of New Port Richey's housing inventory. Most were built between 1960 and 2000, with a mix of concrete block (CBS) construction and some frame. CBS construction is preferred by insurance underwriters. Lot sizes range from under 5,000 sq ft for infill properties to 15,000+ sq ft on canal-front streets. The most common sizes are 3-bedroom/2-bath homes in the 1,200-1,800 sq ft range.

Condominiums

New Port Richey has a number of older condo complexes, primarily in ZIP 34652. Buyers must request the milestone inspection status for any building three stories or taller built before 1990 under Florida's SB 4-D requirements. Non-compliant buildings may have difficulty obtaining financing through conventional lenders. Always ask for the HOA reserve fund study and check for any pending special assessments before making an offer.

Investment and Rental Properties

New Port Richey has an active long-term rental market. With median home prices around $265K-$290K and rental rates for 3BR/2BA SFH in the $1,800-$2,400/month range, gross yields of 7-9% are achievable on well-selected properties. Quick Answer

New Port Richey FL cost of living is below the Tampa Bay average for most categories. The key variables are housing (median ~$265K-$290K), homeowners and flood insurance (higher than the national average), and electricity ($150-$300/month depending on usage). No Florida state income tax. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

New Port Richey FL Cost of Living: Full Breakdown for 2026 Buyers

New Port Richey is generally more affordable than most Pinellas County communities on a sticker price basis. But the full cost of ownership in NPR includes some important line items that buyers underestimate: homeowners insurance, flood insurance (for Zone AE properties), and property taxes. This guide builds out the full monthly cost picture across three scenarios.

No Florida state income tax and the homestead exemption help considerably. The key numbers to model before buying are your specific insurance costs, since these vary more here than in most Florida markets depending on flood zone, home age, and construction type.

What Does It Cost to Buy and Own a Home in New Port Richey FL?

Three Monthly Cost Scenarios

The following table models the full monthly ownership cost for three buyer scenarios: an entry-level home in Zone X, a midrange home in Zone X, and a canal-front home in Zone AE (where flood insurance is required). All scenarios use a 20% down payment and a 7.0% mortgage rate as of late 2026.

What Are Property Taxes Like in New Port Richey?

Pasco County Property Tax Overview

New Port Richey is in Pasco County. Pasco County's total millage rate (the combined rate for all taxing authorities including county, city, school district, and special districts) varies by exact location but typically falls in the range of 16-21 mills depending on which taxing districts apply. For a simple estimate, multiply the assessed value (after homestead exemption) by 0.016-0.021.

Without homestead exemption: a $265K home assessed at full value at 18 mills = approximately $4,770/year or $397/month. With homestead exemption (first $25K off, second $25K off for school only): the effective tax is lower. Use the Pasco County Property Appraiser's calculator at pascopa.com for a precise estimate.

What Do Utilities Cost in New Port Richey FL?

Electricity: Duke Energy Florida

Most of New Port Richey is served by Duke Energy Florida. Duke Energy announced rate reductions beginning March 2026 following a rate case, with temporary increases in January-February 2026 related to storm cost recovery charges. For a typical household, electricity in NPR runs approximately $150-$300/month, with the higher end during July-September air conditioning season. According to user-submitted data, the average monthly electricity cost in New Port Richey is around $265/month, with an average rate of approximately 15 cents per kilowatt-hour. Summer bills in a 1,500 sq ft home commonly run $250-$350+ if the home is not well insulated.

Water and Sewer: City of New Port Richey

The City of New Port Richey operates its own municipal water and sewer system for in-city accounts. Rates use a tiered structure based on consumption. For a typical household, water and sewer combined runs approximately $60-$130/month. Contact the City of New Port Richey at cityofnewportrichey.org for current rate schedules.

Flood insurance is separate from homeowners insurance. What Other Cost of Living Factors Matter in New Port Richey?

No Florida State Income Tax

Florida has no state income tax. For a household earning $100,000, relocating from a state like California (13.3% top rate) or New York (10.9% top rate) can represent $8,000-$13,000/year in state tax savings. This makes Florida's higher insurance costs much easier to absorb for most relocating buyers.

Grocery and Daily Expenses

Groceries and daily expenses in New Port Richey are in line with the broader Florida Gulf Coast average. National chains including Publix, Walmart, Aldi, and Winn-Dixie serve the US-19 corridor. Restaurant options range from fast casual to full-service dining, with more variety in downtown NPR and along the US-19 commercial strip. For specialty groceries or broader dining options, Clearwater (30-40 minutes) and Trinity/Wesley Chapel (25-30 minutes) offer additional choices.

Healthcare

New Port Richey has healthcare access through Morton Plant North Bay Hospital (6600 Madison St, New Port Richey FL 34652) which serves the Pasco Gulf Coast area. title: New Port Richey FL Property Taxes: 2026 Rates, Exemptions Guide
excerpt: New Port Richey FL Property Taxes, Complete 2026 guide to Pasco County millage rates, homestead exemption, and sample calculations. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

New Port Richey property taxes are set by Pasco County. The total millage rate for city residents runs approximately 18 to 21 mills depending on location and special districts. A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 reduces taxable value, and Save Our Homes caps annual assessment increases at 3%. On a $290,000 home with full homestead, expect roughly $2,600 to $3,400/year in property taxes. Call Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 for a precise tax estimate on any property you are considering.

New Port Richey Property Tax Guide: Rates, Exemptions, and What to Expect in 2026

Property taxes in New Port Richey are among the more manageable in the Tampa Bay region, partly because Pasco County has lower assessed values than Hillsborough or Pinellas and partly because the homestead exemption and Save Our Homes cap provide meaningful relief for primary residents. Understanding how the system works before you buy, not after, is one of the best ways to avoid budget surprises.

I have helped buyers in New Port Richey, Port Richey, Trinity, and Holiday for years, and property tax confusion is one of the most common issues I see at closing. This guide covers the actual numbers, how to look up your specific property, and what the exemptions really save you.

How Are New Port Richey Property Taxes Calculated?

The Millage Rate Formula

Florida property taxes are calculated using a millage rate applied to your property's assessed value after exemptions. One mill equals $1 per $1,000 of taxable value. A property taxed at 20 mills with a $250,000 taxable value pays $5,000 in annual taxes. In practice, the taxable value after exemptions is lower than the market value, which is why the effective tax rate is lower than the nominal millage rate suggests.

The formula: (Assessed Value minus Exemptions) x Millage Rate / 1,000 = Annual Tax Bill

Who Sets the Rate

Pasco County sets the base millage each year in its budget process. If you live inside the incorporated City of New Port Richey limits, the city adds its own millage on top. Many parts of ZIP 34654 and 34655 are unincorporated Pasco County, which means no city millage applies, only county and special district levies. This distinction matters a lot to buyers comparing properties inside vs. outside city limits.

What Is the Pasco County Millage Rate for New Port Richey?

Millage Rate Breakdown (2025 Tax Roll, Approximate)

Taxing Authority Approx. Millage Notes
Pasco County General5.26County-wide base rate
Pasco County School Board (operational)4.25State required levy
Pasco County School Board (capital)1.50Facility bond levy
Southwest FL Water Mgmt District0.25SWFWMD regional levy

Pasco County Library0.25County library system
City of New Port Richey (in-city only)3.28City limits only
Total (in-city estimate)~17 to 21Varies by special district

Source: Pasco County Property Appraiser (pascopa.com). Rates rounded. Verify current year rates at pascopa.com or with Pasco County Tax Collector (pascotaxes.com).

Unincorporated vs. City of New Port Richey

Properties in unincorporated Pasco County (many ZIP 34654 and 34655 addresses) do not pay the 3.28-mill city levy, which can save $700 to $1,200 per year on a typical home. Always confirm whether a specific address falls inside or outside city limits using the Pasco County Property Appraiser site before you budget your taxes.

What Is the Florida Homestead Exemption and How Does It Apply?

The Two-Layer Exemption

Florida's homestead exemption has two layers. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities and reduces the assessed value directly. The second $25,000 (for assessed values between $50,000 and $75,000) applies to all levies except the school board. The combined effect saves most homeowners roughly $800 to $1,200 in taxes per year depending on the total millage rate.

How to Apply for Homestead Exemption

You must apply by March 1 of the tax year for which you want the exemption. Applications are filed with the Pasco County Property Appraiser at pascopa.com or in person at 14236 6th St, Dade City, FL 33523 (main office) or 4111 Land O Lakes Blvd Suite 214, Land O Lakes, FL 34638 (west office). You need to have purchased and occupied the home as your primary residence by January 1 of the application year.

Save Our Homes Cap: The Long-Term Tax Protection

Once you receive homestead exemption, Florida's Save Our Homes law limits annual increases in your assessed value to the lesser of 3% or the Consumer Price Index change. If home values in your neighborhood increase 15% in one year, your assessed value can only go up 3%. Over 5 to 10 years of ownership this creates a significant gap between market value and taxable value, which is why long-term homeowners in New Port Richey often pay far less in taxes than a new buyer purchasing the same house today.

Portability: Taking Your SOH Benefit When You Move

If you have accumulated a Save Our Homes benefit on a prior Florida homestead, you can transfer (port) that benefit to your new New Port Richey home. Portability is applied on your homestead application. You have two years from January 1 of the year you abandoned your prior homestead to file. This is a significant financial benefit for move-up or downsizing buyers already in the Florida market.

Additional Exemptions That Can Reduce Your Tax Bill

Senior Exemption

Pasco County offers an additional $25,000 exemption for homeowners age 65 or older whose household income does not exceed the Florida Department of Revenue's annual threshold (approximately $35,167 in recent years, adjusted annually). This is applied on top of the standard homestead exemption and can meaningfully reduce the tax bill for qualifying retirees.

Disability Exemptions

Florida provides an additional $500 exemption for totally and permanently disabled persons and a separate exemption for quadriplegics and those requiring use of a wheelchair for mobility. Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 10% or more receive an additional exemption up to $5,000. A 100% service-connected disabled veteran may qualify for a full exemption on the homestead property.

Widow/Widower Exemption

An additional $500 exemption applies to surviving spouses of permanent Florida residents. These exemptions stack with the standard homestead and senior exemptions, so qualifying seniors with a disability and prior military service can accumulate substantial tax relief.

Contact Barrett Call (813) 733-7907

When Are Property Taxes Due in Pasco County?

The Florida Early Payment Discount Schedule

Florida property taxes are billed in November and paid in arrears for the prior calendar year. Pasco County offers early payment discounts that incentivize paying before the deadline:

  • November: 4% discount
  • December: 3% discount
  • January: 2% discount
  • February: 1% discount
  • March 31: Full amount due (no discount)
  • After April 1: Delinquent; additional fees and interest apply

If your lender escrows your property taxes, they handle payment timing. If you pay directly, paying in November captures the full 4% discount. Pasco County Tax Collector: pascotaxes.com, (727) 847-8165.

Closing Day and the Proration Adjustment

At closing, property taxes are prorated based on the tax year. Since Florida taxes are paid in arrears, the seller typically owes a credit to the buyer for the portion of the year the seller owned the property. This credit is calculated at closing and reduces the buyer's net cash needed. Your closing disclosure will show this credit clearly. On a $4,000/year tax bill, if you close on June 1, the seller credits you roughly $2,000 for their half of the year.

Frequently Asked Questions: New Port Richey Property Taxes

What is the property tax rate in New Port Richey FL?

The total millage rate varies by location within New Port Richey. Properties inside the incorporated city limits pay approximately 18 to 21 mills total (Pasco County general, school board, fire rescue, city of NPR, and special districts). Properties in unincorporated Pasco County portions of the 34654/34655 ZIP codes pay less because the 3.28-mill city levy does not apply. Verify the exact rate for any specific address at pascopa.com.

How much are property taxes on a $300,000 home in New Port Richey?

On a $300,000 first-year homestead purchase in the city of New Port Richey, expect roughly $4,500 to $5,400 per year in total property taxes. After applying the $50,000 homestead exemption, taxable value drops to approximately $250,000. Taxed at a blended rate of around 18 to 22 mills, the annual bill works out to $4,500 to $5,500. Investment properties with no homestead pay more because exemptions do not apply.

How do I apply for the Florida homestead exemption in Pasco County?

Apply at the Pasco County Property Appraiser's website: pascopa.com. You can file online or visit their Land O Lakes office at 4111 Land O Lakes Blvd Suite 214, Land O Lakes, FL 34638. The deadline is March 1 of the year for which you want the exemption. You must have owned and occupied the home as your primary residence as of January 1 of that year. Phone: (727) 847-8151.

What is Save Our Homes and how does it benefit New Port Richey buyers?

Save Our Homes (SOH) is a Florida constitutional provision that limits annual increases in the assessed value of a homestead property to the lesser of 3% or the rate of inflation. Once you homestead a New Port Richey property and values rise, your tax bill grows slowly while the market increases faster. The result is a growing gap between market value and taxable value over time, which compounds into significant savings over 5 to 10 years of ownership.

Are New Port Richey property taxes included in my mortgage payment?

Most lenders require an escrow account for property taxes and insurance when the loan-to-value ratio is above 80%. Your monthly mortgage payment includes principal, interest, property taxes (1/12 of the annual estimate), and homeowner's insurance. On a $290,000 purchase with a ~$4,200 annual tax bill, the escrow portion is approximately $350/month. Work with your lender to get an accurate escrow estimate before budgeting your monthly housing cost. content:
Quick Answer

New construction in New Port Richey is limited compared to neighboring Pasco County communities like Land O' Lakes and Trinity because the city core is largely built out. Most active new construction near New Port Richey occurs in the unincorporated 34654/34655 corridor, communities like Longleaf, Magnolia Valley Road, and scattered infill developments. Prices start near $290,000 for a base 3-bedroom and can reach $450,000+ for larger homes. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to find out what is currently under construction and available.

New Construction Homes Near New Port Richey FL: What Buyers Need to Know in 2026

Buyers looking for new construction in the New Port Richey area face a different market than buyers in high-growth corridors like Wesley Chapel or Land O' Lakes. The incorporated city of New Port Richey is largely developed, which means true new construction happens primarily in unincorporated western Pasco County or in nearby communities accessible via the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589). Understanding where new product exists, what it costs, and how builder contracts work will help you navigate this market without overpaying or missing incentives.

I work with buyers purchasing new construction throughout western Pasco County. Builder sales offices work for the builder, not for you. Having an independent agent represent you costs nothing extra (the builder pays the buyer agent commission) and gives you someone whose job is to protect your interests rather than maximize the builder's margin.

Where Is New Construction Happening Near New Port Richey?

Unincorporated West Pasco (34654 and 34655)

The most active new construction near New Port Richey is in the 34654 ZIP code along the SR-52 corridor and in portions of 34655 near Seven Springs and Trinity. This area includes scattered subdivision developments, infill lots in established neighborhoods, and some new planned communities. Home sizes typically run 1,500 to 2,400 sq ft with 3 to 4 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, and 2-car garages.

Why New Port Richey Proper Has Limited New Construction

The incorporated city of New Port Richey was developed primarily from the 1950s through the 1980s. The grid-based neighborhoods around downtown, Jasmine Estates, Gulf Harbors, Meadow Pointe, have mature street layouts with few vacant lots. New construction within city limits tends to be single-lot infill where a builder purchases an older home, demolishes it, and builds a new spec home. These are often smaller projects from local builders and custom home contractors rather than national tract builders.

What Does New Construction Cost Near New Port Richey in 2026?

Understanding the True Cost: Base Price vs. Total Price

Builder advertised prices are almost always base prices on the most basic floor plan with minimal upgrades. By the time buyers add flooring upgrades, extended lanai, granite countertops, upgraded appliances, premium lot selection, and HOA initiation fees, the final contract price typically runs 10 to 20% above the base price. On a $320,000 base, that is $352,000 to $384,000 all-in before closing costs. Budget realistically from the start rather than planning to add upgrades you cannot afford.

What Are CDD Fees and Do They Apply Near New Port Richey?

Community Development District (CDD) Explained

A CDD (Community Development District) is a special taxing district that finances the construction of community infrastructure, roads, utilities, stormwater systems, amenity centers, through bonds repaid by homeowners via annual assessments. CDDs are common in master-planned communities throughout Pasco County. The CDD fee appears on your property tax bill as a separate line item and is not included in your HOA dues.

How CDD Fees Affect Your Monthly Budget

A CDD assessment of $1,800/year adds $150/month to your ownership cost on top of your mortgage, property taxes, and HOA dues. Many buyers are surprised by CDD fees because they are not prominently disclosed by builder sales staff. Always ask for the full CDD assessment, both the debt service portion (bond repayment) and the operations and maintenance portion, before signing a contract. The debt service portion decreases as bonds are paid off over 20 to 30 years; the O&M portion is ongoing.

How to Buy New Construction Near New Port Richey Without Overpaying

Register with a Buyer's Agent Before Visiting the Sales Office

Builder policies generally require that your buyer's agent accompany you on your first visit to the sales center or register you before your first visit. If you walk into a sales office alone, the builder's agent becomes your only representation. Once registered with the builder directly, most will not allow you to add an independent agent later. Since the builder pays the buyer agent commission, having independent representation costs you nothing, but you must set it up before you walk in.

Builder Incentives and When to Use Them

National builders regularly offer incentive packages worth $10,000 to $30,000 on unsold inventory and spec homes. These incentives typically come as closing cost credits, design center allowances, or mortgage rate buydowns through the builder's captive lender. The catch: the builder's lender is often not the most competitive option for your long-term rate. Compare the all-in cost of the builder's rate buydown incentive against shopping your own lender to make sure you are actually saving money, not just getting a better-looking monthly payment on a higher rate.

New Construction Inspections Are Not Optional

New does not mean perfect. Builder inspections by Pasco County are for code compliance, not consumer advocacy. Budget for three independent inspections: a pre-drywall inspection (to catch framing, plumbing, and electrical issues before they are hidden), a final inspection before closing, and an 11-month warranty inspection before your builder's one-year warranty expires. Each costs $300 to $500 and can surface issues that cost thousands to fix after closing.
