5 Things I Tell Every Hudson Buyer

1. Budget for insurance first, purchase price second. The combination of homeowners, flood, and wind insurance on a canal-front home can run $5,000 to $15,000 per year. This changes the effective affordability of any listing.

2. Canal access quality varies widely. Not all canals are equal. Some are direct, deep, and navigable. Others are shallow at low tide or require multiple cuts to reach open Gulf. Ask about the route, the depth at mean low water, and any bridge clearances.

3. Older construction requires extra diligence. Much of Hudson was built in the 1960s through 1980s. Polybutylene plumbing, galvanized pipes, aluminum wiring, and original septic systems are real concerns. Budget for a thorough inspection and potential remediation.

4. Pasco County has no city-level tax for Hudson. Hudson is unincorporated, so there is no City of Hudson municipal tax. Your bill reflects county, school district, and special district millage only.

5. The Suncoast Pkwy changes the commute math. The Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) toll road is accessible east of Hudson via SR-52. This cuts Tampa commutes by 15 to 25 minutes vs. US-19. Factor in toll costs of approximately $6 to $10 round trip to Tampa.

What is the average home price in Hudson FL?

Typical homes range from $230,000 for non-waterfront inland homes to $550,000 or more for canal-front homes with Gulf access. Gulf-front properties can exceed $700,000. Visit current Hudson listings for real-time pricing.

Is Hudson FL a good place to retire?

Yes. Hudson has a significant retirement population and amenities that suit retirees: Beacon Woods golf community, affordable cost of living, Gulf access, mild winters, and no Florida income tax. The main trade-offs are insurance costs and limited walkability. Read the Is Hudson FL a Good Place to Live guide for a full honest assessment.

Does Hudson FL have a beach?

Yes. Hudson Beach is a public beach at the end of Hudson Beach Rd with a free public boat ramp and fishing pier. Hudson Beach Park is maintained by Pasco County. Adjacent SunWest Park offers a Gulf-side swimming area and cable wakeboarding.

What flood zones are in Hudson FL?

Hudson has Zone VE (Gulf-front, highest risk), Zone AE (canal-front and some interior areas), and Zone X (lower-risk inland areas). Check any specific address on the FEMA Flood Map Service Center before making an offer.

How far is Hudson FL from Tampa?

Hudson to downtown Tampa is approximately 45 to 65 minutes depending on route and traffic. Via Suncoast Pkwy (SR-589) the drive is typically 45 to 55 minutes off-peak. See the full Hudson commute guide for destination-specific times.

title: Hudson FL Commute Guide: Times, Routes, and Transportation
excerpt: Hudson FL Commute Guide: Drive Times and Routes, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

Hudson is approximately 45 to 65 minutes from downtown Tampa via the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) and US-19. St. Petersburg is 65 to 85 minutes. Tampa International Airport (TPA) is 50 to 65 minutes via Suncoast Pkwy. There is no public transit serving Hudson. A car is required for all daily needs.

Hudson FL Commute Guide: Times, Routes, and Transportation

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson sits at the northern end of a Gulf Coast commute corridor that flows predominantly south toward Tampa and Pinellas County employment centers. The two main routes are US-19 (the direct but often congested arterial) and the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589, a toll expressway accessible from SR-52 east of Hudson). Understanding these two options, their trade-offs, and your specific destination is essential for any Hudson buyer who commutes.

I have represented buyers and sellers across western Pasco County for over 23 years. The commute question comes up in almost every buyer consultation for Hudson. The honest answer is that Hudson is a viable base for many workers, but the math only works with the right combination of job location, schedule flexibility, and willingness to pay tolls.

The Two Main Routes Out of Hudson

US-19: The Direct but Congested Route

US-19 is a four-lane divided arterial that runs north-south through the entire US Gulf Coast corridor. Through Hudson and into New Port Richey, US-19 passes through a dense commercial zone with numerous traffic signals. This creates significant congestion during morning and evening rush hours, particularly southbound in the morning and northbound in the evening. Off-peak, US-19 is a reasonable route for destinations in New Port Richey, Holiday, Dunedin, and Clearwater. For Tampa destinations, US-19 adds 15 to 25 minutes compared to the Suncoast Pkwy route.

Suncoast Parkway (SR-589): The Faster Paid Route

The Suncoast Pkwy (SR-589) is a limited-access toll expressway that connects to I-275 south of Tampa. From Hudson, drivers take SR-52 east from US-19 to reach the Suncoast Pkwy interchange at SR-52/Suncoast (approximately 8 to 12 miles east of Hudson). Once on the expressway, the drive to Tampa is largely unimpeded. The Suncoast Pkwy uses SunPass tolls electronically. Round-trip tolls to Tampa run approximately $6 to $10 per day depending on entry/exit points. Monthly toll cost for a five-day commuter is approximately $130 to $200.

The SR-52 approach road from Hudson to the Suncoast Pkwy itself has traffic lights and can back up during peak hours, especially near the commercial corridor. Plan for 10 to 20 minutes from central Hudson (US-19/SR-52 intersection) to the Suncoast Pkwy on-ramp in peak traffic.

There Is No Rail or Bus Transit from Hudson

Pasco County does not have a fixed-route public bus system. Pasco County Public Transportation (PCPT) operates paratransit services for eligible disabled residents but does not serve the general public for commuting purposes. PSTA (Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority) does not extend into Pasco County. There is no commuter rail. Every Hudson resident who commutes drives.

title: Is Hudson FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Assessment
excerpt: Is Hudson FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Review, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

Hudson FL is a good place to live for retirees, remote workers, and boaters who prioritize Gulf access, affordability, and a quiet pace. It is a harder fit for daily Tampa commuters, buyers seeking walkable urban amenities, or families who place school quality above all else. The honest assessment: Hudson delivers on lifestyle and value but not on convenience or commute.

Is Hudson FL a Good Place to Live? Honest Assessment

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson is an unincorporated coastal community in western Pasco County with a Gulf shoreline, canal neighborhoods, affordable housing, and a slow-paced lifestyle that attracts a specific kind of buyer. Whether it is a good place to live depends entirely on what you are looking for. This guide gives the honest picture: what Hudson does well, where it falls short, and which buyer profiles are the best fit.

I have sold real estate in Hudson and western Pasco for over 23 years. I have seen buyers thrive here and I have seen buyers regret the decision. The difference is almost always about alignment with what Hudson actually is versus what someone hoped it would be.

What Hudson FL Does Well

Gulf Coast Access at Affordable Prices

Hudson is one of the few remaining Gulf-adjacent communities in the Tampa Bay region where a buyer can own a canal-front home with Gulf access for under $500,000. The same property in Pinellas County would cost $800,000 or more, if you could find it at all. For buyers whose priority is boat access to the Gulf of Mexico, Hudson delivers at a price point that has largely disappeared from the Pinellas coastline.

Hudson Beach and SunWest Park

Hudson Beach Park is a free public Gulf-access beach with a boat ramp, a fishing pier, and picnic areas. SunWest Park, adjacent to the beach area, offers a Gulf-side swimming area and a cable wakeboarding and wakeskating facility that draws visitors from across the region. These are genuine recreational assets that give Hudson a beach community identity most inland Pasco communities lack.

Outdoor Recreation and Boating Culture

The canal neighborhoods (Sea Ranch Lakes, Leisure Beach, Hudson Beach area) host an active boating community. The Hudson Bayou provides Gulf access, and the community has several waterfront restaurants and marinas. Fishing is strong in the nearshore Gulf waters. Kayaking, paddleboarding, and birding in the coastal salt marsh areas are additional options. Hudson is not a resort beach destination, but it is a place where you can genuinely live an outdoor Gulf Coast life.

Affordable Cost of Living

Hudson's housing costs remain well below those of Pinellas County coastal communities, Sarasota, or even parts of Hillsborough. Property taxes in unincorporated Pasco County are moderate (no city tax layer). The absence of a high-end retail and dining district means day-to-day living costs are also relatively low. See the full Hudson cost of living breakdown for details.

Beacon Woods Golf Community

Beacon Woods Golf Club is a public course within the Beacon Woods planned community. It gives Hudson a recreational anchor that many similarly priced communities lack. The Beacon Woods community itself offers pools, tennis, and a clubhouse. For retirees or near-retirees who want community structure and golf without the price tag of a gated luxury community, Beacon Woods is a genuine value.

No State Income Tax and Moderate Property Taxes

Florida has no state income tax. Pasco County property taxes run approximately 1.5% to 2.0% of assessed value for homesteaded properties, which is lower than the national average. For retirees living on fixed or investment income, this combination significantly reduces the total tax burden compared to most northern states.

Where Hudson FL Falls Short

The Commute to Tampa Is Real

From Hudson to downtown Tampa is 45 to 80 minutes depending on route and traffic. For daily five-day-a-week commuters, this is 90 to 160 minutes of driving per day plus $130 to $200 per month in Suncoast Pkwy tolls if using the expressway. Many buyers underestimate the cumulative quality-of-life impact of this commute. See the full Hudson commute guide for destination-specific times.

Limited Walkability and Dining

Hudson has no walkable downtown. The primary commercial corridor is US-19, a four-lane arterial with strip malls, fast food, chain restaurants, and service businesses. Dining options are limited relative to urban Tampa Bay communities. The nearest grocery stores are on US-19 in Hudson and New Port Richey. For buyers who value walkable restaurants, coffee shops, and boutique retail, Hudson will feel sparse.

Aging Infrastructure and Housing Stock

Much of Hudson's residential housing stock dates from the 1960s through 1980s. Older homes can have deferred maintenance, aging mechanical systems, polybutylene plumbing, and construction characteristics that increase insurance costs or require remediation. Buyers need to budget for thorough inspections and potential updating, particularly on canal-front homes that have been exposed to Florida weather and salt air for decades.

High Insurance Costs for Waterfront Properties

Flood insurance in Zone AE and VE can run $2,000 to $20,000+ per year for waterfront homes in Hudson. Homeowners insurance on older coastal Florida homes can add another $3,000 to $8,000. The total combined insurance cost on a canal-front home can easily reach $8,000 to $15,000 per year and significantly increases the effective ownership cost versus the purchase price alone.

School Quality Is Mid-Tier

Pasco County schools are mid-tier by Florida standards. Hudson High School and the area elementary schools have improved in recent years but are not the primary draw for families relocating specifically for school quality. Families who place schools as a top priority often look at Pinellas County communities or the Hillsborough County corridor. See the Hudson schools guide for a full breakdown.

Hurricane and Flood Risk Is Genuine

Hudson's Gulf Coast location makes it subject to hurricane risk and storm surge flooding. The community sits in Pasco County Hurricane Evacuation Zone A (the highest-risk zone) for the westernmost Gulf-front properties. Canal-front properties are in Zone B or C. During a major hurricane, evacuation is not optional for Zone A properties. Flood insurance, wind-hardening, and hurricane shutters are not optional expenses for Hudson waterfront homeowners. They are the cost of living on the Gulf.

Frequently Asked Questions: Is Hudson FL a Good Place to Live?

Is Hudson FL safe?

Hudson is generally a safe community. Pasco County crime statistics are available through the Pasco County Sheriff's Office (pascosheriff.com). Like most communities, crime rates vary by specific neighborhood. The canal communities and Beacon Woods tend to be quieter and lower-crime. The commercial US-19 corridor has the highest incident concentration, as is typical for commercial arterials anywhere.

Is Hudson FL a good place to raise a family?

Hudson can work for families who value outdoor recreation, affordability, and Gulf access more than walkability or top-ranked schools. Families who prioritize school quality as the primary criterion typically look at Pinellas County or eastern Hillsborough instead. Hudson offers good recreational options and a safe community feel in most neighborhoods.

What is the weather like in Hudson FL?

Hudson has a subtropical climate with hot, humid summers (June to September) and mild, dry winters. Average summer highs are in the low 90s with high humidity. Winter highs are typically in the low to mid 70s with occasional cold fronts bringing overnight lows into the 40s or 50s. Gulf breeze moderates summer temperatures somewhat. Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30, with peak activity in August through October.

Does Hudson FL flood often?

Properties in Zone AE and VE flood zones can experience flooding during significant storm events. Tropical systems and even strong frontal storms with surge can affect canal-front properties. Hudson experienced notable flooding during several tropical events in the 2020s. Zone X properties (inland) have significantly lower flood frequency. Flood insurance and seawall maintenance are essential for waterfront property owners.

What is the population of Hudson FL?

Hudson is an unincorporated census-designated place. The 34667 and 34669 ZIP codes together cover a population of approximately 60,000 to 70,000 people. The Hudson CDP itself (the core census area) is smaller. The population is predominantly older, with a significant retiree and near-retiree presence, though younger families and remote workers are a growing segment.

Pricing Strategy

Accurate pricing from day one produces better outcomes than aspirational pricing followed by reductions.

Pre-Listing Preparation

For canal-front and waterfront properties: complete any deferred seawall maintenance, repair dock boards and lift hardware, and ensure the dock permit is current. For all properties: address visible deferred maintenance, deep clean, and consider a pre-listing inspection to identify items buyers will discover and use as negotiating points. Florida disclosure requirements are extensive.

Insurance Documentation

Providing the current elevation certificate, insurance declarations page, and any existing wind mitigation or 4-point inspection reports upfront accelerates the transaction. Buyers in Hudson are insurance-aware. Having documentation ready reduces negotiation friction over insurance costs.

Buying a Home in Hudson FL: Market Strategy

Off-Season Timing Advantage

Hudson's market, like most Florida coastal markets, softens seasonally in summer (June to August) when northern buyers are less active. Contingency Strategy for Waterfront Purchases

For canal-front purchases, build your offer to include a home inspection contingency, a flood insurance review period, and, if the seawall condition is unclear, a specific seawall inspection contingency. By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

The total monthly cost of ownership includes mortgage, insurance (homeowners, flood, and wind), property taxes, HOA fees if applicable, and utilities. I have worked with buyers across every Hudson price tier for more than 23 years. The buyers who end up unhappy are almost always the ones who did not fully account for insurance and ongoing maintenance costs. The buyers who thrive here understand the full picture and buy accordingly.

Insurance: The Biggest Variable in Hudson

Homeowners Insurance

Homeowners insurance in coastal Pasco County reflects Florida's difficult insurance market. Many national carriers have reduced or exited the Florida market, and Citizens Property Insurance (the state insurer of last resort) and smaller carriers serve much of Hudson. Annual premiums for a typical 1,500 to 2,000 square foot SFH in Hudson run approximately $2,200 to $6,000 depending on age, construction type, roof age, wind mitigation features, and proximity to water. Older homes (pre-1990) with flat or older roofs pay significantly more.

Flood Insurance

Flood insurance in Zone AE is mandatory for federally-backed mortgages and is priced under FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or private carriers. Since FEMA implemented Risk Rating 2.0 in 2021-2022, premiums are calculated based on individual property characteristics rather than just flood zone. An elevation certificate ($350 to $600 from a licensed surveyor) that shows your home is above the Base Flood Elevation can significantly reduce your premium. Get quotes before making an offer.

Wind Insurance

In Pasco County, wind coverage is typically included in your standard homeowners policy (unlike in some South Florida counties). However, the wind mitigation features of your specific home (hip roof, hurricane straps, impact windows or shutters, roof covering age) significantly affect the premium. A wind mitigation inspection ($150 to $200) is worth getting on any older home. Resulting credits can reduce homeowners premiums by 20% to 50%.

Property Tax Cost in Hudson FL

Hudson is in unincorporated Pasco County, so there is no city-level municipal tax. The total millage rate runs approximately 17 to 20 mills depending on fire district and other special assessments in your specific location. For a $350,000 homesteaded property, the effective tax bill runs approximately $4,500 to $6,000 per year after the $50,000 homestead exemption. See the full Hudson property tax guide for millage breakdowns and calculation examples.

Utilities in Hudson FL

Electric: Duke Energy Florida

Duke Energy Florida serves most of Hudson. The average residential electric bill for a 1,500 to 2,000 square foot Florida home runs approximately $120 to $200 per month in summer (when A/C runs continuously) and $80 to $130 per month in winter. Homes with electric water heaters and older HVAC systems will trend toward the high end. Duke Energy customer service: duke-energy.com or 800-700-8744.

Water and Sewer

Water and sewer service in Hudson is provided by Pasco County Utilities (PCU) for most developed areas in 34667. Some portions of 34669 east of US-19 may be on well and septic, particularly on older lots. PCU monthly water/sewer bills average approximately $60 to $100 for typical residential use. For properties on well and septic, there is no monthly utility bill but there are maintenance and testing responsibilities. Verify the utility connection status for any specific property before purchase.

Internet and Cable: Spectrum and Frontier

Spectrum (cable internet) is the primary provider across most of Hudson with speeds up to 1 Gbps available. Frontier offers fiber internet in select areas of Pasco County; availability in specific Hudson neighborhoods varies. Standard Spectrum internet plans run $50 to $80 per month. Frontier fiber, where available, is competitive. Starlink satellite is an option for properties in rural parts of 34669 that lack fiber or cable coverage.

Grocery and Daily Living Costs in Hudson

Hudson has several grocery options on or near US-19, including Walmart, Publix, and Winn-Dixie locations within a 5 to 10 minute drive of most neighborhoods. Dining out on the waterfront (Hudson Beach Bar, Inn on the Gulf, Catches Waterfront Grille) ranges from casual to moderately priced. There are no upscale dining destinations within Hudson itself; New Port Richey and the broader US-19 corridor provide more options within 15 to 20 minutes.

Transportation Costs

Every Hudson resident drives. There is no public transit. Gasoline, vehicle maintenance, and Suncoast Pkwy tolls (for Tampa commuters, $130 to $200 per month for a five-day commuter) are real costs. A typical two-car household in Hudson spends approximately $600 to $1,200 per month on transportation including insurance, fuel, and tolls.

content:
Quick Answer

Hudson FL property taxes are assessed by Pasco County with a total millage rate of approximately 17 to 20 mills depending on location within the county. There is no city-level tax since Hudson is unincorporated. A $350,000 home with a $50,000 homestead exemption pays approximately $4,500 to $6,000 per year. The Pasco County Property Appraiser is at PascoPA.net; the Tax Collector is at pascotaxes.com.

Hudson FL Property Taxes: Pasco County Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson is located in unincorporated Pasco County, Florida. Property taxes are administered by two Pasco County offices: the Pasco County Property Appraiser (PCPA), which determines the assessed value of each property, and the Pasco County Tax Collector, which collects the taxes. Because Hudson has no city government, there is no municipal millage layer on top of county, school, and special district taxes.

Understanding your property tax bill in Florida requires understanding assessed value, just value, the homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes 3% cap, and the individual millage components that make up your total rate. This guide walks through all of it with specific examples for Hudson properties.

Hudson FL Resources

Pasco County Millage Rate Breakdown

The total millage rate for a Hudson property is the sum of several individual millages levied by different taxing authorities. The rates below are approximate based on recent Pasco County tax rolls. Individual rates change each year based on budget cycles.

Millage rates change annually. For current official millage, visit PascoPA.net or pascotaxes.com.
Taxing AuthorityApproximate MillageNotes
Pasco County General Fund~6.50 to 7.25 millsCounty government operations
Pasco County School District~6.80 to 7.30 millsRequired local school effort + discretionary
Pasco County EMS~0.50 to 0.75 millsEmergency medical services
Pasco County Library~0.40 to 0.60 millsCounty library system
Fire MSTU (varies by district)~1.50 to 3.00 millsVaries significantly by fire district
Southwest Florida Water Mgmt District (SWFWMD)~0.25 to 0.35 millsRegional water management
Pasco County Mosquito Control~0.15 to 0.25 millsMosquito and pest control district
Total (approximate)~17.0 to 20.0 millsVaries by specific fire district and special assessments

How Florida Property Taxes Are Calculated

Step 1: Just Value vs. Assessed Value

Just Value is the Pasco County Property Appraiser's estimate of your property's market value as of January 1 each year. For homesteaded properties, Assessed Value is limited to increase no more than 3% per year or the CPI change (whichever is less) under Florida's Save Our Homes cap. For non-homesteaded properties, Assessed Value is limited to a 10% annual increase. For new buyers, the Assessed Value resets to market value at the time of sale.

Step 2: Apply Exemptions to Get Taxable Value

Florida's homestead exemption reduces your Taxable Value by $50,000 ($25,000 off the first $50,000 of Assessed Value, and another $25,000 off the assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000 for non-school millage). To receive the homestead exemption you must apply to the Pasco County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year you want the exemption to take effect. You must own and occupy the property as your primary residence as of January 1.

Step 3: Multiply Taxable Value by Millage Rate

Taxable Value is divided by 1,000 and multiplied by the total millage rate. Example: a $350,000 assessed value home with a $50,000 homestead exemption has a $300,000 taxable value. At 19 mills: $300,000 / 1,000 x 19 = $5,700 per year in taxes.

Sample Tax Calculations for Hudson FL Properties

Sample calculations. Actual taxes vary by specific millage rate at the property address. Use pascotaxes.com to look up actual bills.

Mid-range SFH, homesteaded$350,000$50,000$300,000$5,400/yr$6,000/yr
Canal-front home, homesteaded$480,000$50,000$430,000$7,740/yr$8,600/yr

The Save Our Homes 3% Cap

Florida's Save Our Homes (SOH) amendment caps the annual increase in Assessed Value for homesteaded properties at 3% or the CPI change, whichever is less. Over time, this creates a "SOH differential" where long-time homeowners pay taxes on a much lower assessed value than the current market value. This benefit is lost when a property is sold, and the new owner's Assessed Value resets to market value at the time of purchase.

If you are buying from a long-time owner, do not rely on the seller's current tax bill to estimate your future tax bill. Calculate using the current market value (your purchase price) minus the homestead exemption, multiplied by the current millage rate. Your first full-year tax bill will typically be higher than the seller's last bill.

Portability: Transferring Your SOH Benefit

If you already own a Florida homesteaded property and are moving to Hudson, you can transfer ("port") up to $500,000 of your accumulated SOH benefit to your new home. You must apply for portability when you apply for your new homestead exemption (by March 1). The portability amount reduces your new home's Assessed Value by up to the amount of your SOH differential, subject to limits. Visit PascoPA.net for the portability application and calculation worksheet.

Additional Pasco County Exemptions

Senior Exemption

Pasco County offers an additional low-income senior exemption for homeowners age 65 or older with total household income below a Florida-set threshold (check PascoPA.net for current income limit). This exemption, when approved by local taxing authorities, can exempt an additional $25,000 or more from taxable value.

Disability and Veterans Exemptions

Florida offers additional exemptions for disabled veterans, first responders disabled in the line of duty, and total disability recipients. These can significantly reduce or eliminate property taxes. Visit PascoPA.net for current exemption schedules and application requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions: Hudson FL Property Taxes

What is the property tax rate in Hudson FL?

Total millage in unincorporated Hudson runs approximately 17 to 20 mills depending on which fire district covers your specific address. For precise rates on a specific parcel, look up the property at PascoPA.net.

How do I apply for homestead exemption in Pasco County?

Apply to the Pasco County Property Appraiser (PascoPA.net or 727-847-8151) by March 1 of the year you want the exemption. You must own and occupy the property as your primary Florida residence as of January 1 of that year. Late applications are generally not accepted for the current year.

Does Hudson FL have a city property tax?

No. Hudson is unincorporated Pasco County. There is no City of Hudson and therefore no municipal millage on top of county and school district taxes. This is a meaningful distinction compared to incorporated cities like New Port Richey or Tarpon Springs, which have additional city millage layers.

Will my tax bill match the seller's current bill?

Almost certainly not if the seller has owned the property for several years. Save Our Homes caps their assessed value increase at 3% annually. When you buy, the assessed value resets to approximately the current market value (your purchase price). Your first full-year tax bill will typically be higher than the seller's. Calculate using the purchase price minus the homestead exemption multiplied by the millage rate.

What is the homestead exemption deadline in Pasco County?

March 1 of the year for which you want the exemption. If you close before January 1 and establish Florida residency on that property, you can apply for the exemption by March 1 of the following year (effective that tax year). Apply at PascoPA.net or the Property Appraiser office.

Quick Answer

Hudson FL has limited new construction within the core coastal area due to lack of vacant land. New construction activity is concentrated in eastern Hudson (34669), the SR-52 corridor, and adjacent areas of Pasco County. For a true Gulf-access new build, buyers typically need to do a teardown/rebuild on an existing canal lot. New construction subdivisions near Hudson offer more options but without waterfront access.

Hudson FL New Construction: What Buyers Need to Know

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson is primarily a resale market. The western Gulf-side neighborhoods (Sea Ranch Lakes, Leisure Beach, Hudson Beach area) were largely built out in the 1960s through 1980s. Vacant canal-front or Gulf-front lots are extremely rare. The eastern portions of Hudson and the SR-52/US-19 corridor in ZIP 34669 have more development activity, though without waterfront access. For buyers specifically seeking brand-new construction in the Hudson area, this guide lays out the realistic options.

Understanding the distinction between new construction in the core Gulf-side Hudson area versus new construction in eastern Pasco County communities is important. They serve different buyers with different priorities.

Where Is New Construction Activity in the Hudson Area?

Eastern Hudson (34669) and the SR-52 Corridor

The eastern portions of Hudson and the SR-52 corridor heading toward Land O Lakes and Zephyrhills have had scattered new residential development. These areas offer larger lots, lower flood risk (Zone X in many areas), and proximity to the Suncoast Pkwy for Tampa commuters. However, they are 8 to 15 miles from Hudson Beach and the Gulf, which changes the character significantly.

Nearby Pasco County Master-Planned Communities

The broader Wesley Chapel, Land O Lakes, and Zephyrhills areas have significant active new construction from regional and national builders. These communities are 25 to 45 miles from the Gulf but offer new homes with modern amenities, newer schools, and better commute access to Tampa. Buyers who want new construction AND proximity to Hudson's Gulf lifestyle need to accept they will likely be choosing one or the other at the high end, or buying resale on the waterfront side and new construction inland.

Teardown/Rebuild on Canal Lots in Hudson

For buyers who specifically want a new home on a Hudson canal lot with Gulf access, the realistic path is to find an existing older home on a canal lot, demolish it, and build new. This is the primary route to brand-new construction in the established Gulf-side Hudson neighborhoods.

Finding a Tear-Down Candidate

Canal-front tear-down candidates in Hudson run approximately $200,000 to $380,000 for the lot with an existing structure. These are typically 1960s or 1970s concrete block homes in poor condition or with significant flood damage history. The lot value is the driver; the structure is often a demolition cost rather than an asset.

Demolition and Site Preparation Costs

Residential demolition in Pasco County runs approximately $10,000 to $25,000 for a typical 1,000 to 1,800 square foot structure, including debris removal and permit fees. Abatement for asbestos or lead paint in pre-1980 homes adds $2,000 to $8,000. Permit fees for demolition are paid to Pasco County Building Services (pascocountyfl.net/BuildingConstruction). Environmental assessment may be required if fuel tanks or contamination are suspected.

Flood Zone Building Requirements

Canal-front lots in Zone AE must have the lowest floor elevated to at least the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) plus any required freeboard. Zone VE lots (Gulf-front) require open pile or open lattice foundation construction to allow floodwaters to flow beneath the structure. These requirements add significant cost and must be designed by a licensed engineer and permitted through Pasco County. Expect elevation and foundation requirements to add $20,000 to $80,000 to construction cost depending on lot elevation and required BFE.

Frequently Asked Questions: Hudson FL New Construction

Are there new homes for sale in Hudson FL?

Limited new construction exists in eastern Hudson (34669) and adjacent Pasco County communities. The established Gulf-side neighborhoods of Hudson are effectively built out. For new homes near Hudson's Gulf lifestyle, the primary option is a canal-lot teardown/rebuild. Browse current Hudson listings for available inventory.

Who are the builders active near Hudson FL?

National builders (DR Horton, Lennar, Pulte, Maronda, LGI) are active in broader western Pasco County new construction communities but not typically in the established coastal Hudson neighborhoods. Canal-front new construction is typically done by local custom builders. Ask me for current builder referrals in the area.

Can I build a new home on a canal lot in Hudson FL?

Yes, via the teardown/rebuild process. You acquire an existing lot with structure, demolish the structure, and construct new. All-in costs typically run $550,000 to $985,000 depending on lot price and build specification. Canal-front lots in Hudson run $200,000 to $380,000 before construction. Permit times run 8 to 16 weeks; total project timeline is 12 to 24 months.

What flood zone requirements apply to new construction in Hudson?

Zone AE construction must be elevated to Base Flood Elevation (BFE) plus any county-required freeboard. Zone VE (Gulf-front) requires open pile or lattice foundation construction to allow water to flow under the structure. FEMA's requirements are enforced through the Pasco County Building Department. An elevation certificate is required upon completion.

Is new construction insured differently in Hudson FL?

New construction built to current Florida Building Code standards (2017 FBC or later) typically qualifies for significant wind mitigation discounts on homeowners insurance, including credits for hip roofs, hurricane clips, and impact-rated openings. These can reduce annual homeowners premiums by 20% to 50% compared to older pre-code homes. Flood insurance premiums on new construction depend on the finished floor elevation relative to BFE.

Quick Answer

Hudson FL investment property offers long-term rental (LTR) income potential in the $1,200 to $2,400 per month range for non-waterfront SFH and $1,800 to $3,500 for canal-front homes. Short-term rental (STR) regulations in unincorporated Pasco County are governed by Florida state law and Pasco County ordinance. HOA restrictions can prohibit STRs entirely. Cap rates in Hudson are typically low (2% to 4%) for waterfront properties and moderate (4% to 6%) for non-waterfront inland homes at current price levels.

Hudson FL Investment Property Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson attracts real estate investors for two primary reasons: affordable entry prices relative to Pinellas County coastal markets, and consistent tenant demand from retirees, seasonal residents, and Gulf-area workers. The investment thesis is different for waterfront vs. non-waterfront properties. Understanding both, and the regulatory environment, is essential before committing capital.

I have helped investors purchase and manage property in Hudson and western Pasco County for over 23 years. This guide covers LTR vs. STR strategy, cap rate analysis, HOA restrictions, Pasco County regulations, and property management options including ViVi Property Management.

Long-Term Rental (LTR) Strategy in Hudson FL

Tenant Demand Profile

Hudson's LTR market is driven by retirees and seniors who want to live in the coastal community without buying, Gulf Coast workers employed at Bayonet Point/Hudson Medical Center or along the US-19 corridor, and remote workers who want Gulf access without a long-term commitment. Vacancy rates for well-maintained properties at market rents are typically low (under 5% annually) based on western Pasco demand patterns.

LTR Financial Analysis

For a non-waterfront 3BR/2BA SFH purchased at $270,000 with 20% down ($54,000), the math works out as follows at current rates. Mortgage at 7% on $216,000 is approximately $1,438 per month. Taxes at 1.8% of $270,000 (before homestead, since investor purchase) is $4,860 per year or $405 per month. Homeowners insurance approximately $3,000 per year or $250 per month. Maintenance budget 1% of value per year = $2,700 per year or $225 per month. Total expenses: approximately $2,318 per month. At $1,600 per month gross rent, the property cash flows negative before property management fees. This illustrates why Hudson LTR works better as a long-term equity play than a current cash flow vehicle at today's prices and rates.

Where LTR Cash Flow Is More Achievable

The most favorable LTR cash flow scenarios in Hudson involve cash purchases (no mortgage), significantly below-market acquisition (distressed/estate sales), or value-add properties where renovation increases rents substantially. Buyers financing at current rates (above 6%) in Hudson will typically find that LTR alone does not cover carrying costs without a substantial down payment.

Short-Term Rental (STR) Strategy in Hudson FL

Pasco County STR Regulations

Pasco County applies Florida's vacation rental preemption law (Florida Statute 509.032), which limits how counties and municipalities can regulate short-term rentals. As of current law, Pasco County cannot ban STRs outright in unincorporated areas, but it does require Florida DBPR (Department of Business and Professional Regulation) vacation rental licensing for properties rented for periods under 30 days if rented more than three times per year. The DBPR license is obtained at myfloridalicense.com.

HOA Restrictions Override State Law

For any property within an HOA, the HOA's Declaration of Covenants governs STR eligibility. Many Hudson HOAs, particularly Beacon Woods and similar planned communities, explicitly prohibit or severely restrict short-term rentals. Violations of HOA covenants can result in fines and legal action by the HOA. Always review the full HOA declaration and rules before planning an STR investment. Properties outside of HOA coverage (no-HOA single-family in canal areas) have more STR flexibility.

Pasco County Tourist Development Tax

STR operators in Pasco County must collect and remit Pasco County Tourist Development Tax (TDT) on taxable rentals. The Pasco County TDT rate is 5% on total rental charges for periods of 6 months or less. TDT is collected by the Pasco County Clerk of Court's office. Failure to remit TDT is a significant compliance risk. Verify current rate and remittance requirements at pascoclerk.com or contact the Pasco County TDT office.

STR Market Realities for Hudson

Hudson Beach, SunWest Park, and the Gulf-access canal neighborhoods create genuine STR appeal. Boating visitors, fishing charters, and Gulf Coast recreation demand drive weekend and weekly rental traffic. However, Hudson is not a resort destination with the brand recognition of Clearwater Beach or Siesta Key, which limits nightly rates. Successful Hudson STRs are typically well-marketed with accurate descriptions of the Gulf access opportunity and waterfront lifestyle. Platforms including Airbnb and VRBO are the primary booking channels.

Property Management for Hudson Investment Properties

Managing a rental property in Hudson from out of state or while managing multiple properties requires either hands-on local management or a professional property management company. ViVi Property Management provides full-service property management for Hudson and the western Pasco County area, including tenant placement, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and lease administration. Professional management typically costs 8% to 12% of gross rent for LTR and 20% to 30% of gross revenue for STR.

Investment Property Due Diligence in Hudson FL

Insurance Quotes Before Committing

Investment properties in Hudson do not qualify for homestead exemption (and thus the $50,000 reduction in taxable value). They also typically pay higher insurance rates than owner-occupied homes. Get flood, homeowners, and wind insurance quotes for the specific property before finalizing your purchase decision. The insurance cost differential between an investor and owner-occupant can run $1,500 to $3,000 per year more.

Canal and Waterfront Due Diligence

For any canal-front investment property: hire a marine contractor or engineer to inspect the seawall and dock condition. Seawall replacement runs $500 to $900 per linear foot. A 60-foot seawall needing replacement costs $30,000 to $54,000. This is a capital cost that can materially affect your investment return if undetected at purchase.

Verify No Rental Restrictions

Before purchasing any HOA-governed property as an investment, read the full Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs) for rental policies. Some HOAs restrict rentals to leases of 6 months or longer, prohibit consecutive short leases, require HOA approval of tenants, or limit the number of investment-owned homes in the community. Get this information in writing before closing.

Frequently Asked Questions: Hudson FL Investment Property

Is Hudson FL a good place to invest in real estate?

Hudson offers affordable entry prices, consistent rental demand from retirees and Gulf area workers, and long-term appreciation potential supported by Pasco County population growth. At current prices and interest rates, cash-on-cash returns for leveraged investors are modest. The strongest case for Hudson investment is long-term appreciation and portfolio diversification rather than immediate cash flow.

Can I do short-term rentals in Hudson FL?

If the property is not in an HOA that prohibits STRs, yes. Unincorporated Pasco County follows Florida state law on STR preemption. You need a Florida DBPR vacation rental license and must collect and remit Pasco County Tourist Development Tax (TDT) at 5%. HOA restrictions, where they exist, override state preemption law within the HOA-governed community.

What is the cap rate for Hudson FL rental properties?

Gross cap rates typically run 2% to 4% for canal-front waterfront homes and 4% to 6% for non-waterfront inland homes at current market prices. Net cap rates after insurance, taxes, maintenance, and management are typically 1 to 3 points lower. These are not strong cash flow numbers; Hudson investment works best as an appreciation and lifestyle play.

Who manages rental properties in Hudson FL?

ViVi Property Management provides full-service property management in Hudson and western Pasco County. Services include tenant placement, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and lease administration. Contact ViVi at the link above for current rates and availability.

What taxes apply to Hudson FL investment properties?

Investment properties are subject to Pasco County property taxes at the full millage rate with no homestead exemption (approximately $4,500 to $9,000+ per year depending on assessed value). STR income is subject to Pasco County TDT at 5% and Florida sales tax at 6% on short-term lodging. Federal and Florida income tax treatment depends on rental days, personal use, and individual tax situation. Consult a licensed CPA for investment property tax strategy.

title: Hudson FL Waterfront Homes: Canal and Gulf Access Guide
excerpt: Waterfront Homes in Hudson FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

Hudson FL waterfront homes with Gulf access run from approximately $290,000 for secondary canal properties to $700,000+ for large main-canal homes in premium locations. The Hudson canal system connects to the Gulf of Mexico through the Hudson Bayou. Flood insurance in Zone AE is mandatory and runs $1,800 to $7,000+ per year. Seawall condition is the single most important inspection item.

Hudson FL Waterfront Homes: Canal and Gulf Access Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 25, 2026

Hudson has one of the most affordable Gulf-access waterfront markets on Florida's west coast. The canal system in western Hudson connects residential properties to the Hudson Bayou and ultimately to the open Gulf of Mexico. This is the defining feature of Hudson's real estate identity: Gulf access at price points that disappeared from Pinellas County a decade ago.

I have sold waterfront homes in Hudson and western Pasco County for over 23 years. The waterfront market here has genuine depth and genuine complexity. Buyers who understand the canal system, the flood insurance math, the seawall lifecycle, and the dock permitting process make better decisions. This guide covers all of it.

Hudson FL Resources

Hudson FL Waterfront Property Types

Price ranges are approximate 2025-2026 estimates. Individual properties vary.
Property TypePrice RangeFlood ZoneTypical InsuranceNotes
Main canal front, direct Gulf route$420K to $700K+AE$3,000 to $7,000/yrShortest route to open Gulf
Secondary/side canal front$290K to $480KAE$2,000 to $5,000/yrGulf access but longer route
Gulf-front or bay-front$550K to $900K+VE or AE$7,000 to $25,000+/yrVery limited inventory
Interior lot with Gulf view$380K to $600KAE or XLower than direct waterfrontNo dock; access at community ramp
Intracoastal/bayou-adjacent$350K to $580KAE$2,500 to $6,000/yrSaltwater access; depth varies

The Hudson Canal System: What Buyers Need to Know

How the Canals Connect to the Gulf

The Hudson waterfront neighborhoods (Sea Ranch Lakes, Leisure Beach, Hudson Beach area) are served by a network of man-made canals that were originally dredged in the 1950s and 1960s to create waterfront lots. These canals connect through natural bayou channels to the Gulf of Mexico. The Hudson Bayou is the primary connector between the residential canal grid and the open Gulf. From most Hudson canal homes, the boat trip to open Gulf water runs approximately 1 to 3 miles depending on your canal's position in the network.

Canal Depth and Draft Limitations

Canal depth in the Hudson system varies by location and by tidal stage. Many canals have been subject to decades of sedimentation without dredging. Nominal canal depths in the dredged channels run 4 to 6 feet at mean low water in established sections. Shallower areas, particularly at the heads of side canals and near inlets, can drop to 2 to 3 feet at low tide. Before purchasing a waterfront home, ask the seller to disclose the mean low water depth at the dock and at the canal mouth. If the answer is unknown, get a depth sounding. Buyers with larger draft vessels (sailboats, trawlers, cabin cruisers over 24 feet) need to verify depths carefully.

Bridge Clearances

Several bridges cross Hudson's canal system. Fixed bridges limit vertical clearance for tall vessels. Most bridges in the Hudson canal system have approximately 10 to 14 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, which accommodates most outboard-powered center console and bay boats but not taller cabin cruisers or flybridge vessels. Verify bridge clearances on your specific route before purchasing if you plan to use a vessel with significant above-waterline height.

Waterfront Home Components: What to Inspect

Seawall Inspection

The seawall is the property's frontline protection against canal erosion, storm surge, and property loss. Hudson seawalls are typically concrete block, poured concrete panel, or vinyl sheet pile. Age, construction quality, and maintenance history vary widely. A professional seawall inspection by a licensed marine contractor runs $250 to $500 and covers visible cracking, tie-rod condition, bowing or leaning, voids behind the wall, and cap condition. Do not skip this inspection on any canal-front purchase.

Seawall repair costs range from minor patching ($2,000 to $5,000) for hairline cracks to full replacement ($500 to $900 per linear foot) for failed walls. A typical 50-foot seawall replacement costs $25,000 to $45,000. If the seawall is near end-of-life, negotiate a price reduction or credit equal to the anticipated replacement cost.

Dock Inspection

Wood docks in Florida's saltwater environment have a functional life of 15 to 25 years before major reconstruction or replacement. Aluminum docks last longer but require different maintenance. Inspect for: rotted or soft decking, damaged pilings, corroded hardware, missing or damaged cleats, and condition of the gangway/access ramp. A basic dock inspection runs $150 to $300. Dock replacement costs $15,000 to $40,000 for a typical residential aluminum dock with gangway.

Boatlift Inspection

Boatlifts are mechanical systems with motors, cables, bunks, and frame components that require periodic maintenance and are subject to corrosion in saltwater environments. Inspect the lift motor, cable condition, bunk condition, and structural frame. Lift motor replacement runs $800 to $2,500. Full lift replacement for a 10,000-pound capacity lift runs $5,000 to $12,000 installed.

Flood Zone and Elevation Certificate

All Hudson canal-front homes should be assumed to be in Zone AE unless you have verified otherwise on the FEMA Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov). For every waterfront purchase, obtain an elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor ($350 to $600). The certificate tells you the finished floor elevation relative to the Base Flood Elevation. If the home is above BFE, your flood insurance premium will be lower. If it is below BFE, the premium will be higher. This information is essential for budgeting and for deciding whether to proceed.

Flood Insurance for Hudson FL Waterfront Homes

Flood insurance costs are estimates. Get actual NFIP and private market quotes for every specific property.
ScenarioNFIP Annual Cost (approx.)Private Market (approx.)Notes

Zone AE, floor 1 ft above BFE$1,200 to $2,200/yr$1,000 to $2,000/yrPremium decreases as elevation increases
Zone AE, floor at BFE - 1 ft (below)$3,000 to $6,000/yr$2,500 to $5,000/yrPre-FIRM homes often below BFE
Zone VE, Gulf-front, open pile$8,000 to $20,000+/yr$6,000 to $18,000+/yrWave action zone; highest risk

Since FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 implementation in 2021-2022, flood insurance premiums are calculated using individual property characteristics (structure type, first floor height, distance from water, frequency of flooding, cost to rebuild) rather than just zone. Risk Rating 2.0 has increased premiums for many older, lower-elevation Gulf Coast properties. Legacy policyholders with grandfathered policies may have lower premiums than a new buyer would obtain; confirm whether a NFIP policy can be assumed by the buyer at the existing rate.

Dock Permitting in Hudson FL

Adding, replacing, or significantly modifying a dock in Hudson requires permits from multiple agencies. The regulatory stack typically includes:

Pasco County Building Services (pascocountyfl.net): structural permit for the dock structure.

Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD) (watermatters.org): Environmental Resource Permit for work in or over navigable waters and wetlands. Minor dock replacements may qualify for a "No-Notice" or simplified permit; new construction or major modifications require a full ERP.

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (usace.army.mil): Section 10/404 permit for work in navigable waters. Many standard residential dock replacements fall under Nationwide Permit 3 (Maintenance) or NWP 18 (Minor Discharges), which have simpler processes than individual permits.

Plan 3 to 6 months for permit processing on a new dock installation. Budget $2,000 to $5,000 for permit application fees and engineering drawings.

Buying Process for Waterfront Homes in Hudson FL

Inspection Contingency and Additional Inspections

Standard home inspection ($350 to $500) plus seawall inspection ($250 to $500) plus dock/lift inspection ($150 to $300) gives you a full picture of the above-water physical condition. For older homes, also commission a 4-point inspection ($150 to $200) covering the roof, electrical, HVAC, and plumbing systems. Insurance underwriters often require a 4-point for older Florida homes.

Flood Insurance Quotes Before Committing

Get actual flood insurance quotes (NFIP and at least one private carrier) during your inspection contingency period. Do not accept seller's current premium as your actual cost. If the policy cannot be assumed, you are starting fresh under Risk Rating 2.0 pricing.

Title Search and Riparian Rights

Ensure the title search confirms riparian rights (the right to access and use the adjacent water) are included with the property. Docking rights, seawall ownership responsibilities, and maintenance obligations should be clearly established in the title chain. Some older Hudson properties have shared seawall or canal access structures that require clarity.

Hudson FL Waterfront vs. Pinellas County Waterfront

Comparisons are generalizations. Individual properties vary substantially.

Property tax (homesteaded, approx.)$5,000 to $11,000/yr$9,000 to $40,000+/yr

Market liquidity (days on market)Moderate (35 to 75 days)Higher liquidity in most price segments

Frequently Asked Questions: Hudson FL Waterfront Homes

Do Hudson FL canal homes have Gulf access?

Yes. The canal neighborhoods in western Hudson (Sea Ranch Lakes, Leisure Beach, Hudson Beach area) connect through the Hudson Bayou system to the Gulf of Mexico. Most canal-front homes can reach open Gulf water by boat in 1 to 3 miles depending on canal position. Canal depth and bridge clearances vary by location.

How far is the Gulf from Hudson canal homes?

From most Hudson canal-front homes, the boat ride to open Gulf water is approximately 1 to 3 miles. Travel time by boat depends on speed, canal conditions, and which neighborhood you are in. Hudson Beach itself is at the Gulf shoreline. Canal-front homes in Sea Ranch Lakes are typically a 10 to 30 minute boat ride to open water depending on route.

What is the flood zone for Hudson FL waterfront homes?

Most Hudson canal-front homes are in FEMA Zone AE. Gulf-front properties may be in Zone VE. Some interior properties away from the canal are in Zone X. Check any specific address on the FEMA Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov. For AE and VE properties, flood insurance is mandatory for federally-backed mortgages.

What should I inspect on a Hudson FL canal-front home?

Prioritize the seawall condition (hire a marine contractor, $250 to $500), dock and boatlift condition ($150 to $300), flood zone and elevation certificate ($350 to $600), standard home inspection ($350 to $500), and 4-point inspection for older homes. Get actual flood insurance quotes during the inspection period.

Is Hudson FL waterfront affordable compared to Pinellas County?

Yes. Canal-front homes in Hudson with Gulf access run $290,000 to $700,000. Comparable Gulf-access properties in Pinellas County (Tarpon Springs, Clearwater, Dunedin) typically start at $700,000 to $1,000,000 and go much higher. Hudson offers genuine Gulf access at a fraction of Pinellas County prices, which is the primary driver of its waterfront buyer demand.

title: San Antonio FL Homes for Sale: Rural Acreage, Horse Properties and Land Guide
excerpt: San Antonio FL (ZIP 33576) near Saint Leo University offers rural acreage homes from $320K-$700K+, most with well and septic and no HOA. Full buyer guide from Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

What homes are for sale in San Antonio FL?

San Antonio FL (ZIP 33576) is a small rural Pasco County community near Saint Leo University with acreage homes, horse properties, and country estates. Most properties sit on 1-10+ acre lots with well and septic. Prices typically range from $320K-$700K+ depending on acreage, home size, and improvements. Active inventory is limited given the community's size. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for current listings.

What Types of Homes Are Available in San Antonio FL?

San Antonio is not a master-planned community with subdivisions and HOA ponds. It is a genuine rural community where parcels vary from small-lot country homes to large working homesteads. Here is what buyers typically find:

Country Homes on 1-5 Acres

The most common property type in San Antonio is a concrete block construction (CBS) or frame home on 1 to 5 acres of land. Many were built between 1980 and 2010. These homes offer well and septic, privacy, room for outbuildings or gardens, and no HOA restrictions. Prices typically range from $340K to $580K depending on the size of the home and land.

Horse Properties and Small Farms

San Antonio's agricultural character supports equestrian buyers. AR-1 and AR-2 zoning in Pasco County allows horses, other livestock, and farming operations on qualifying parcels. Horse properties with fencing, run-in sheds or barns, and pasture access are available. These properties typically run $500K-$900K+ depending on the level of improvements.

Older Character Homes Near Saint Leo University

The downtown area of San Antonio near SR-52 and the Saint Leo University campus has older Florida homes that sell below the rural acreage market. These smaller lots with 1950s-1990s vintage homes can be found in the $280K-$420K range, appealing to Saint Leo faculty, staff, or buyers who want proximity to the university.

Vacant Land

San Antonio has a meaningful market for vacant land buyers wanting to build custom. Parcels from 1 to 20+ acres are available, with prices ranging from $80K to $250K+ depending on road frontage, utilities access, and land quality. Buyers building custom need to account for well, septic, and permitting costs through Pasco County.

How to Find San Antonio FL Homes for Sale

The San Antonio FL market is too small for a simple Zillow or Realtor.com search to show you everything. Many rural properties sell privately, through network relationships, or with limited marketing because owners do not want strangers on their land during showings. I find properties through MLS, direct outreach, and relationships with landowners in the area. If you have a specific acreage or property type in mind, contact me directly and I will search on your behalf.

What to Expect When Buying in San Antonio FL

Well and Septic Inspection

Almost all San Antonio properties use private wells and septic systems. Before closing, you need a well water quality test (coliform bacteria, nitrates, and pH at minimum), a well pump flow rate test, and a septic inspection by a licensed Pasco County inspector. FHA and VA loans have specific requirements for water quality. Budget $400-$800 for testing, separate from your standard home inspection.

Zoning and Agricultural Use Verification

If you plan to keep animals, run a home business, build an accessory dwelling unit (ADU), or add agricultural buildings, verify what is allowed under the current zoning with the Pasco County Development Services department before you close. Zoning does not always align with what the seller tells you is possible.

Acreage Appraisal and Financing

Rural acreage properties are harder to appraise than typical subdivision homes because comparable sales are limited and property characteristics vary widely. FHA and VA loans have specific limitations on acreage and agricultural use. Conventional loans are generally more flexible for rural parcels. I work with lenders who specialize in rural Pasco County properties and can match you with the right financing option.

What is the average home price in San Antonio FL?

San Antonio FL does not have a large enough sales volume for precise average pricing. Horse properties and improved farms command $600K-$1M+. Check current MLS listings or call Barrett for current market data.

Are there new construction homes in San Antonio FL?

There is limited new construction directly in San Antonio proper. Most new construction in the area is available in nearby Zephyrhills (D.R. Horton, LGI Homes) and the Wesley Chapel corridor (many builders). Custom building on vacant land is an option in San Antonio for buyers willing to manage the construction process and permitting through Pasco County.

Do San Antonio FL homes have HOAs?

The majority of rural properties in San Antonio FL do not have homeowners associations. This is a draw for buyers who want to avoid HOA fees and restrictions. Some newer subdivisions near the edges of San Antonio toward Zephyrhills or Wesley Chapel may have HOAs. Ask specifically about HOA status for any property before making an offer.

San Antonio FL is small enough that neighborhood comparisons are not as meaningful as in larger cities. Properties along SR-52, CR-54, and the rural roads south and east of Saint Leo University are the most typical. Buyers wanting more land tend to look east toward Zephyrhills Road and north toward Dade City. Contact Barrett for specific area guidance based on your lifestyle needs.

How competitive is the San Antonio FL real estate market?

San Antonio is a small, niche market. Inventory is limited and properties do not come up as frequently as in Wesley Chapel or Zephyrhills. Well-priced rural homes with acreage can receive multiple offers, especially from buyers who have been searching for rural Pasco County properties for months. Move quickly when a good property matches your criteria.

content:
Quick Answer

What schools serve San Antonio FL?

San Antonio FL is served by Pasco County Schools. The elementary school serving the immediate San Antonio area is San Antonio Elementary School. Middle and high school assignments depend on the specific address within the 33576 ZIP code. Some addresses are assigned to Pasco High School or Zephyrhills High School. Verify your specific school zone with Pasco County Schools before purchasing if school assignment is a priority.

Pasco County Schools Overview

San Antonio FL is in the Pasco County School District, which serves the entirety of Pasco County including Wesley Chapel, New Port Richey, Dade City, Zephyrhills, and Zephyrhills. The district operates schools ranging from highly rated suburban A-grade schools in Wesley Chapel to smaller rural schools serving communities like San Antonio.

School grades (A through F) are assigned annually by the Florida Department of Education based on standardized test scores, graduation rates, and other metrics. Grades change from year to year. Always verify the current grade at the Florida DOE School Accountability reports before making a purchase decision based on school rating.

Elementary Schools Serving San Antonio FL

San Antonio Elementary School

San Antonio Elementary School is the primary elementary school serving the San Antonio community. It is a smaller rural school with a community-focused culture typical of Pasco County's rural attendance zones. Contact Pasco County Schools at pasco.k12.fl.us to confirm current school assignment for a specific address.

Boundary Verification Is Essential

Rural Pasco County attendance boundaries are drawn around geographic areas, not subdivisions. The same ZIP code (33576) can fall in different school attendance zones depending on road frontage, parcel location, or geographic features. Always call Pasco County Schools directly at (813) 794-2000 or use the school boundary finder at pasco.k12.fl.us to confirm where your specific parcel falls before purchasing.

Middle Schools in the San Antonio FL Area

Middle school assignments for San Antonio FL addresses vary by location within the 33576 boundary. The most likely middle school assignments include schools serving the Dade City and Zephyrhills corridors. Contact Pasco County Schools to verify the specific middle school for any parcel you are considering.

High Schools Serving San Antonio FL

Pasco High School

Pasco High School, located in Dade City, is one of the high schools that may serve San Antonio FL addresses. Pasco High has a long history in the county and serves the traditional rural north Pasco County communities. The school offers standard diploma tracks, vocational programs, and dual enrollment through Pasco-Hernando State College.

Zephyrhills High School

Zephyrhills High School in Zephyrhills FL is another possible high school assignment for San Antonio area students, particularly those on the eastern side of the community. Zephyrhills High offers academic and career/technical education (CTE) tracks.

Private School Options Near San Antonio FL

Saint Leo University

Saint Leo University (founded 1889) is directly in San Antonio. As a university, it does not serve K-12 students, but the Saint Leo community has historically had a relationship with Catholic education in the area. Saint Leo Abbey is located on campus.

Private Schools in Zephyrhills and Dade City

The nearest private school options are primarily in Zephyrhills and Dade City, with additional options in Wesley Chapel for families willing to commute 20-30 minutes. Contact individual schools for current enrollment and tuition details.

College Access from San Antonio FL

Saint Leo University

Having a four-year liberal arts university directly in the community is unusual for a rural Florida town. Saint Leo University offers bachelor's and master's degrees on campus and through its extensive online division. Local families whose children want to commute to college rather than dorm at a large state university have a genuine option next door.

Pasco-Hernando State College

Pasco-Hernando State College (PHSC) operates campuses in Dade City and Wesley Chapel, both within 20-30 minutes of San Antonio. PHSC offers associate degrees, bachelor's degrees, and vocational certificates at community college tuition rates.

What is the school rating for San Antonio FL schools?

Florida school grades change annually. As of recent ratings, Pasco County's rural schools including those near San Antonio have ranged from C to B. Wesley Chapel schools tend to rate higher due to demographics and newer facilities. For the most current grades, visit the Florida Department of Education's school accountability website or the Pasco County Schools district site.

Is Saint Leo University in San Antonio FL a good school?

Saint Leo University is a regionally accredited, private Catholic liberal arts university founded in 1889. Florida's school choice programs allow parents to apply for public school transfers, including to schools in Wesley Chapel, through Pasco County's open enrollment program, subject to capacity. Alternatively, some families choose private schools in Wesley Chapel and commute. Contact Pasco County Schools for current open enrollment policies and availability.

title: San Antonio FL Commute Guide: Drive Times to Tampa, Wesley Chapel and More

content:
Quick Answer

How far is San Antonio FL from Tampa?

San Antonio FL is approximately 40-45 miles from downtown Tampa via I-75 south, about 50-65 minutes off-peak and 70-90 minutes during morning rush hour. Wesley Chapel is 15-20 minutes away and serves as the closest employment and retail hub. A personal vehicle is required; there is no public transit connecting San Antonio to Tampa.

San Antonio FL to Tampa: Commute Time and Route Options

Most San Antonio residents commute south via SR-52 to I-75, then continue south toward Tampa. The Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) is another option for those heading to the Westchase or Citrus Park areas of northwest Tampa, reachable via CR-41 west from San Antonio.

Which Route Is Fastest from San Antonio to Tampa?

SR-52 to I-75 South (Most Common)

Head west on SR-52 from downtown San Antonio, then south on I-75 toward Tampa. This is the standard route for most commuters. Traffic builds on I-75 between the SR-54 interchange and I-4 during morning rush hours (7:00-9:00 AM) and evening rush hours (4:30-6:30 PM).

SR-52 to US-301 South (Alternative)

US-301 south through Zephyrhills and into Plant City avoids I-75 entirely but adds 10-15 minutes in distance. This route works well for those commuting to Brandon, Riverview, or east Tampa, bypassing the I-75 bottleneck near I-4.

CR-41 to Suncoast Parkway (Northwest Tampa)

Buyers commuting to Westchase, Citrus Park, or Odessa should consider heading west on SR-52 to US-41 (SR-45, also called the Suncoast Parkway toll road). This adds a toll cost of approximately $3-$7 per day depending on where you exit, but delivers significantly faster travel times to northwest Tampa.

Is San Antonio FL Worth the Commute?

I work with buyers from all over Pasco County. San Antonio comes up when a client wants acreage, privacy, and proximity to Saint Leo University without paying Wesley Chapel prices. The commute to Tampa is longer than from New Tampa or Land O Lakes, but buyers consistently tell me they find the trade-off worth it for the lifestyle and the price point.

Remote workers increasingly choose San Antonio. High-speed internet availability has improved in Pasco County, and with one or two office days per week, the commute burden drops significantly. If your company allows remote flexibility, San Antonio deserves a serious look.

Rush Hour Tips for San Antonio Commuters

Leave Early or Late

I-75 southbound between SR-54 and Bearss Avenue is the worst stretch during Tampa-bound rush hour. Leaving before 7:00 AM or after 9:00 AM shaves 20-30 minutes off the drive. Same principle applies heading north in the evening: leave before 4:00 PM or after 6:30 PM.

Use Waze or Google Maps in Real Time

I-75 incidents near the SR-54 and SR-56 interchanges in Wesley Chapel can back up traffic significantly. Real-time navigation apps often reroute through CR-41 or US-301 to avoid major backups.

Park and Ride Options

Pasco County and HART do not operate a direct express bus from the San Antonio area to Tampa as of 2026. Commuters who want to reduce driving can meet coworkers or rideshare groups near the Wesley Chapel area and carpool from there.

Frequently Asked Questions About San Antonio FL

How long is the commute from San Antonio FL to Tampa?

From San Antonio FL, the drive to downtown Tampa via I-75 takes approximately 50-65 minutes off-peak and 70-90 minutes during morning rush hour. Total one-way distance is about 43 miles. There is no public transit option.

Is there a toll road from San Antonio FL to Tampa?

Most routes from San Antonio to Tampa via I-75 and I-275 do not require tolls. If you take the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) to northwest Tampa, tolls apply, running $3-$7 one-way depending on your exit. The Veterans Expressway also charges tolls near Tampa.

Does San Antonio FL have public transportation?

No. San Antonio FL has no direct bus or rail service to Tampa or Wesley Chapel. All commutes require a personal vehicle. Pasco County's Pasco County Public Transportation (PCPT) operates limited local routes but does not serve San Antonio directly.

title: San Antonio FL Property Taxes: Pasco County Millage, Homestead Exemption and Ag Tax
excerpt: San Antonio FL is in Pasco County with property taxes typically lower than Hillsborough County. Homestead exemption saves up to $50,000 in taxable value. Full guide from Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

What are property taxes in San Antonio FL?

San Antonio FL is in Pasco County. Property taxes are calculated using the Pasco County aggregate millage rate applied to your assessed value minus exemptions. For a home assessed at $400,000 with the $50,000 homestead exemption, the taxable value is $350,000. At Pasco County's millage rate, annual property taxes typically run $4,500-$7,000 for homes in this range. Verify the exact current rate with the Pasco County Property Appraiser at pascopa.com.

How Property Taxes Are Calculated in San Antonio FL

Florida property taxes follow a consistent formula: (Assessed Value - Exemptions) x Millage Rate / 1,000 = Annual Tax. The Pasco County Property Appraiser sets the assessed value based on market data. The Pasco County Commission, School Board, and special taxing districts set the millage rates each fall. The Tax Collector issues the November bill and collects payment.

Pasco County Millage Rate Components

The total millage rate for unincorporated Pasco County addresses includes:

Taxing AuthorityNotes
Pasco County General FundCounty government operations
Pasco County School BoardPublic schools funding
Water Management DistrictSWFWMD millage

Community Development District (CDD)Only in CDD communities; most of San Antonio has none

Contact the Pasco County Property Appraiser (pascopa.com) or the Pasco County Tax Collector for the current year's exact aggregate millage rate for your specific parcel. Rates change annually with budget cycles.

Florida Homestead Exemption: Critical for San Antonio Buyers

What Is the Homestead Exemption?

Florida allows up to $50,000 in assessed value to be exempt from property taxes on a primary residence. The first $25,000 exemption applies to all taxing authorities. The second $25,000 exemption (applied to the $50K-$75K value band) applies to all authorities except the school board millage.

How to Apply

File your homestead exemption application with the Pasco County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year following your purchase. If you purchase in 2026, file by March 1, 2027. Applications are available online at pascopa.com. You will need your Florida driver's license or ID, vehicle registration, and Social Security number showing your San Antonio FL address.

Save Our Homes Cap

Once your home has a homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes amendment caps assessed value increases at 3% per year or the Consumer Price Index change, whichever is lower. In a market where values rise 10-15% in a year, your taxable value may rise only 3%. This protection compounds over years and is a major long-term benefit of Florida homeownership.

San Antonio FL vs. Hillsborough County Property Taxes

Agricultural Property Tax Exemption in Pasco County

Rural San Antonio properties with agricultural operations may qualify for Florida's agricultural classification, which values the property based on its agricultural productivity rather than market value. This can dramatically reduce the assessed value and annual tax bill for working farms, nurseries, horse operations, or hay production. The Pasco County Property Appraiser reviews ag exemption applications by March 1 annually. Active use is required; you cannot receive the exemption on land that is not being farmed.

San Antonio FL is a small rural community without the large parcels available for master-planned community development. Production builders like D.R. Building a Custom Home in San Antonio FL

Step 1: Find and Secure the Right Parcel

Custom building starts with land. In San Antonio, lots vary from small rural parcels to large agricultural tracts. Before making an offer on land, verify zoning (AR-1, AR-2, or RSC are common), confirm that a perc test passes (required for septic approval), and understand road frontage requirements for Pasco County building permits.

Step 2: Perc Test and Septic Design Approval

Because San Antonio has no municipal sewer, the Florida Department of Health in Pasco County must approve your septic system design. This starts with a percolation (perc) test conducted by a licensed engineer. The soil absorption rate determines what type of septic system is required. Budget $500-$1,500 for the perc test.

Step 3: Well Permitting

Private wells require a water well permit from the Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD). A licensed well driller sinks the well to reach the Floridan Aquifer, typically 80-250 feet in this part of Pasco County. Well drilling costs $6,000-$18,000 depending on depth, casing, and pump size.

Step 4: Building Permit Through Pasco County

Pasco County Development Services processes residential building permits. Submit plans, pay the plan review fee, and wait for approval before breaking ground. Pasco County has improved permit turnaround times but expect 4-8 weeks minimum for new construction plan review.

Step 5: Construction and Inspections

Pasco County requires inspections at multiple phases: foundation, framing, rough electrical, rough plumbing, insulation, and final. Your contractor schedules inspections through the Pasco County permit portal. Final occupancy permit (CO) is issued after all inspections pass.

Is It Better to Buy Existing or Build New in San Antonio FL?

Buying an existing rural home in San Antonio is faster, simpler, and avoids construction management headaches. Building custom takes 12-24 months from land purchase to move-in. If you want a specific horse barn layout, a particular acreage configuration, or accessibility features not found in existing stock, custom may be worth the time and complexity.

Most rural San Antonio properties carry no HOA. This means you as the investor control what tenants can do with the property. Tenants with horses, boats, RVs, or multiple vehicles who cannot find HOA-free rentals in Wesley Chapel or Land O Lakes often pay a premium for no-HOA rural rentals.

Long-Term Tenant Base

Rural acreage renters tend to be stable, long-term tenants. Moving an acreage rental home is far more disruptive than moving from an apartment. Tenants with animals, gardens, outbuildings, or established equestrian operations stay for years. Lower turnover equals lower vacancy and lower maintenance costs.

Land Appreciation Potential

Pasco County has seen consistent population growth driven by Wesley Chapel's explosive development. San Antonio sits north of the Wesley Chapel growth corridor. As Wesley Chapel and Zephyrhills expand, acreage land in San Antonio may appreciate meaningfully over a 10-20 year holding period. This is speculative land banking, but the demographic trends support it.

Agricultural Tax Exemption

Qualifying agricultural operations in Pasco County can receive a significant reduction in assessed value for property tax purposes. Even a small commercial farming operation (bees, nursery plants, hay) may qualify. This reduces carrying costs substantially on larger parcels. Consult the Pasco County Property Appraiser and a Florida tax attorney for specifics.

Private wells and septic systems have maintenance costs that city-water rentals do not. A well pump failure costs $1,500-$4,000 to replace. Septic pumping runs $400-$700 every 3-5 years. Full septic replacement costs $10K-$25K if the drainfield fails. Budget for these as part of your cash flow analysis.
