Fully remodeled / premium$360,000 to $420,000+15-40 daysComplete renovation, new systems throughout, strong curb appeal

What Your Budget Gets in Kenneth City

The key pricing dynamic: condition drives value more than location in a city this small (0.9 sq mi). A $175,000 home in Kenneth City is not in a 'worse location' than a $380,000 home, it's in worse condition. This creates opportunity for buyers willing to take on updates, and it creates a clear ceiling for sellers who need to invest in their home before listing.

What Should Buyers Know About Kenneth City Home Inspections?

The 4-Point Insurance Inspection

Florida homeowners insurance carriers typically require a 4-point inspection for homes over 25 years old. Since virtually every home in Kenneth City qualifies, budget $150-$250 for a 4-point inspection in addition to a standard home inspection ($350-$500). The 4-point covers four systems specifically: roof, HVAC, plumbing, and electrical.

Electrical Panel Issues, The Biggest Risk in Kenneth City

This is the issue I see most frequently cause deal problems in Kenneth City. Many 1960s-1970s homes have Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok panels or Zinsco panels. These panels are widely considered fire hazards by home inspectors and are often refused by Florida homeowners insurance carriers. Budget $3,000-$6,000 for a panel replacement if you encounter one. Do not negotiate around it, address it.

Roof Type and Age, The Second Major Issue

Flat and low-slope roofs are common on 1960s Kenneth City construction. Florida homeowners insurance carriers are increasingly reluctant to insure flat roofs over 10 years old, and some carriers refuse them entirely or surcharge significantly. A pitched/sloped roof home in good condition is generally easier to insure. Always ask about roof age and type before making an offer.

Galvanized Steel Plumbing

Some older Kenneth City homes still have original galvanized steel plumbing. Galvanized pipes corrode from the inside over time, reducing water pressure and eventually failing. A re-pipe (typically done in CPVC or PEX) costs $5,000-$20,000+ depending on home size. Check plumbing during inspection and ask about permit history for any previous plumbing work.

What Are the Best Features of Kenneth City Real Estate?

No HOA, No CDD Fees

This is a major financial advantage over many Pinellas County communities. No HOA means no monthly dues, no rental restrictions (relevant for investors), no approval process for exterior changes, and no risk of special assessments beyond your property taxes. Kenneth City buyers typically save $200-$600/month versus comparable homes in HOA communities.

FEMA Zone X, Low Flood Risk

Most of Kenneth City sits in FEMA Zone X, which indicates low flood risk. Zone X properties are not required to carry flood insurance by most mortgage lenders (though it is available and optional). In a state where Zone AE flood insurance can cost $3,000-$8,000+/year, Zone X status translates to real monthly savings. Always verify specific address flood zone at msc.fema.gov.

Strong Rental Demand

Kenneth City's affordability and proximity to St. Pete employment centers creates strong rental demand. Zone X status, no HOA (no rental restrictions), and affordable purchase prices combine to produce gross cap rates of 7-9% for well-selected properties. This is competitive for Pinellas County, where waterfront and coastal properties often produce 4-6% gross cap rates at today's prices.

title: Kenneth City FL Property Taxes
excerpt: Kenneth City FL property taxes guide, Pinellas County millage rates, homestead exemption, Save Our Homes cap, portability, and how to verify taxes at pcpao.gov and taxcollect.com. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Kenneth City FL property taxes use Pinellas County millage rates plus a Kenneth City municipal millage, typically totaling 17-20 mills. A $280,000 home with Florida homestead exemption pays approximately $3,500-$4,800/year. Non-homestead investment properties pay approximately $4,800-$6,500/year for the same value. Kenneth City FL Property Taxes: Complete Buyer's Guide

Understanding property taxes before making an offer on a Kenneth City home is essential, the seller's current tax bill often significantly understates what you will pay, due to Save Our Homes caps that reset at sale. I walk every Kenneth City buyer through this math before they fall in love with a listing.

What Are Kenneth City FL Property Tax Rates?

How Florida Property Taxes Work

Florida uses a millage rate system. One mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable assessed value. Your taxable value is the market value minus applicable exemptions (primarily the homestead exemption). The total millage for Kenneth City addresses includes multiple components:

Millage ComponentApprox. RateNotes
Pinellas County General Fund~5.0-5.5 millsCounty-wide services
Pinellas County School Board~7.0-7.5 millsLargest single component
Kenneth City Municipal~3.0-4.0 millsSeparate incorporated city rate
SW Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD)~0.25-0.35 millsWater management
Pinellas County Emergency Management~0.5-1.0 millsCounty EMS
Other Special Districts~1.0-2.0 millsVaries by address
TOTAL~17-20 mills (approximate)Verify for specific address at pcpao.gov

Annual Tax Estimates by Home Price

Assessed Value (at Purchase)Homestead Estimated Annual TaxNon-Homestead Estimated Annual Tax
$175,000$2,100-$2,800/yr ($175-$235/mo)$3,000-$3,600/yr ($250-$300/mo)
$240,000$2,900-$3,800/yr ($240-$315/mo)$4,100-$5,000/yr ($340-$415/mo)
$300,000$3,600-$4,700/yr ($300-$390/mo)$5,100-$6,200/yr ($425-$515/mo)
$350,000$4,200-$5,500/yr ($350-$460/mo)$5,900-$7,200/yr ($490-$600/mo)
$400,000$4,800-$6,200/yr ($400-$515/mo)$6,800-$8,300/yr ($565-$690/mo)

These are estimates. Your actual tax depends on the final millage rates set in September of each year and your specific parcel's assessed value. Always look up the prior year's actual tax bill at taxcollect.com.

How Does Florida Homestead Exemption Work in Kenneth City?

The Two-Part Homestead Exemption

Florida's homestead exemption provides two layers of reduction on your assessed value:

Exemption TierAmountApplies Against
First exemption$25,000 off assessed valueAll millage (county, school, city, special districts)
Second exemption$25,000 additional off assessed valueAll millage EXCEPT school board millage
Total benefit (simplified)$50,000 reduction in taxable valueSaves approximately $700-$1,200/yr vs non-homestead

How to Apply for Homestead Exemption

To receive homestead exemption in Kenneth City: you must own the property and have it as your primary Florida residence as of January 1 of the tax year, and apply by March 1. Apply online at pcpao.gov or in person at the Pinellas County Property Appraiser's Office at 315 Court St., Clearwater, FL 33756. Phone: (727) 464-3207.

What Is the Save Our Homes Cap and How Does It Affect Buyers?

The SOH Cap Resets at Sale, This Is Critical

This is the most important tax concept for Kenneth City buyers. Florida's Save Our Homes amendment caps annual increases in a homesteaded property's assessed value at 3% or CPI (whichever is less). Over many years of ownership, a long-term owner's assessed value can be dramatically below market value, meaning their tax bill looks very low on paper.

When you buy that home, the assessed value resets to your purchase price. If the seller bought in 2005 and you buy in 2025, the difference can be enormous:

Seller's SituationYour Situation After Purchase
Purchase Price$120,000 (2005)$300,000 (2025)
Assessed Value (2025)~$160,000 (SOH capped)$300,000 (full market reset)
Homestead Exemption-$50,000-$50,000
Taxable Value$110,000$250,000
Est. Annual Tax (18 mills)~$1,980/yr~$4,500/yr
Difference+$2,520/yr more than seller paid

Never rely on a seller's current tax bill to estimate your future taxes. Always run the calculation based on the purchase price.

Can I Transfer My Homestead Exemption (Portability)?

Yes. Florida's Portability provision (Fla. Stat. 193.155) lets you transfer accumulated SOH benefit (up to $500,000) from a prior Florida homestead to a new Florida homestead within 3 years of selling the prior home. This can significantly reduce your assessed value on the new Kenneth City home. File Form DR-501T with the Pinellas County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year following your purchase.

2. Check assessed vs. market valuepcpao.gov property recordLarge gap = SOH cap; your taxes will be higher
3. View actual tax billtaxcollect.com → search by parcelSee exact prior year taxes paid
4. Estimate your taxesPurchase price × millage rate ÷ 1,000Use 18-20 mills as a conservative estimate
5. Verify millage for current yearpcpao.gov or Pinellas County budget officeFinal millage set each September

New Construction in Kenneth City FL: The Honest Answer

I get asked about new construction in Kenneth City regularly, and I give buyers the straight answer: there essentially isn't any. Kenneth City is a fully built-out incorporated city of approximately 0.9 square miles that reached development saturation decades ago. The housing stock is 1950s-1970s concrete block construction, and there simply is not land available for a ground-up subdivision. If new construction is a firm requirement for your purchase, Kenneth City is not the right market.

That said, I work with buyers who prefer new construction but end up choosing Kenneth City resale after running the numbers. The value gap between a $250,000 updated Kenneth City home and a comparable new construction home in Pasco County is often $150,000-$250,000, with a 30-50 minute longer commute attached. Understanding that trade-off is part of my job.

Why Is There No New Construction in Kenneth City FL?

The City is Fully Built Out

Kenneth City was incorporated in 1960 and developed rapidly through the 1960s and 1970s. The city's 0.9 square miles of land area is entirely filled with residential streets, small commercial strips, and parks. There is no remaining vacant land in sufficient quantity for a production homebuilder to operate. This is the fundamental reality of buying in a small, landlocked, historically developed city.

content:
Quick Answer

Kenneth City FL is a solid long-term rental investment market. Homes purchased at $200,000-$280,000 rent for $1,400-$2,000/month, producing gross cap rates of 7-9%. The market's advantages for investors: no HOA (no rental restrictions), Zone X flood status (no mandatory flood insurance), strong tenant demand from St. Pete and Pinellas Park employment centers, and affordable entry points relative to coastal Pinellas markets.

Investing in Kenneth City FL Real Estate: Rental Analysis and What to Know

Kenneth City is one of my go-to recommendations for entry-level Tampa Bay rental investors who want real Pinellas County exposure without the premium prices of St. Pete proper or the coastal markets. The cap rate math works. The tenant demand is steady. Zone X flood status keeps insurance costs down and eliminates mandatory flood insurance, a significant expense in much of Pinellas County.

The work is in the due diligence. Older homes require careful inspection, and the insurance marketplace for 1960s-70s construction requires understanding. I'll walk through both the upside and the things that can derail a deal.

Why Is Kenneth City a Strong Rental Market?

No HOA, No Rental Restrictions

Most Kenneth City SFH have no HOA, which means no rental restrictions, no approval requirements for tenants, and no monthly HOA fees that reduce NOI. This is a meaningful advantage over Pinellas communities where HOAs restrict rentals, require tenant approvals, or limit lease terms.

Tenant Demand Profile

Kenneth City's tenants are primarily working-class and middle-income households employed in St. Petersburg, Pinellas Park, and Tampa Bay's service and healthcare sectors. The combination of affordable rents relative to coastal Pinellas, proximity to major employment centers, and no HOA rental minimum (some HOAs restrict leases to 12 months, limiting flexibility) creates steady tenant demand.

Zone X Flood Status

Most Kenneth City addresses sit in FEMA Zone X, the lowest flood risk category. This means no mandatory flood insurance for tenants or owners (though optional flood coverage is available and inexpensive in Zone X). In a state where Zone AE flood insurance for a rental property can add $3,000-$8,000+/year to operating costs, Zone X status materially improves net cash flow.

What Are the Risks for Kenneth City Investors?

4-Point Inspection Issues, The Primary Deal Killer

The most common deal problem I see with Kenneth City investment properties is insurance placement after the 4-point inspection. Florida insurers require 4-point inspections on homes over 25 years old (virtually all Kenneth City homes qualify). Federal Pacific or Zinsco electrical panels, flat roofs over 10 years, and HVAC systems over 15 years old can cause carriers to refuse coverage or charge excessive premiums. Budget for potential panel replacement ($3,000-$6,000) and roof condition assessment before finalizing your purchase price.

Rental Comps Vary by Condition

A $200K home in original condition does not command the same rent as a $280K fully updated home. Overestimating rent potential on a lower-condition property is a common investor mistake. Verify actual rent comps from a property manager who actively manages Kenneth City properties before writing your pro forma.

Not a Short-Term Rental Market

Kenneth City does not have the beach proximity or tourist infrastructure to support meaningful short-term rental (Airbnb/VRBO) income. Investors seeking STR yields should look at Treasure Island, St. Pete Beach, Madeira Beach, or Anna Maria Island, but at dramatically higher purchase prices. Kenneth City is a long-term residential rental market, full stop.

Property Management for Kenneth City Rentals

Managing rental properties in Kenneth City from out of state, or even just across Tampa Bay, is possible but time-consuming. ViVi Property Management serves the Pinellas County area with professional tenant screening, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and regulatory compliance. Typical management costs run 8-12% of gross monthly rent plus one-time leasing fees. For investors with one or more properties, professional management typically pays for itself in reduced vacancy and tenant quality.

title: Longboat Key Homes for Sale: Complete Buyer Guide
excerpt: Longboat Key Homes for Sale: Complete Buyer Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Longboat Key homes for sale range from $450,000 condos to $15M+ Gulf-front estates. The island spans Manatee and Sarasota counties, with most properties in FEMA Zone AE or VE. Expect combined insurance costs of $8,000 to $40,000+ per year depending on location and property type. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for a current market analysis.

Longboat Key Homes for Sale: Complete Buyer Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key is a 12-mile barrier island split between Manatee County (north end) and Sarasota County (south end), with the Gulf of Mexico on the west and Sarasota Bay on the east. It is consistently ranked among Florida's most desirable and expensive coastal markets. Year-round residents number around 7,000 to 8,000, and the island's full-time population swells significantly from November through April. If you are seriously considering buying here, there are things to know before you look at a single listing.

Browse Longboat Key homes for sale for current active listings. Check the Longboat Key housing market page for recent sales data. Use the mortgage calculator to estimate monthly carrying costs including taxes, insurance, and any HOA or CDD fees.

What Are Home Prices Like on Longboat Key?

Longboat Key is a true luxury market. The floor for a habitable single-family home starts around $700,000 on the interior, non-waterfront streets. Prices climb sharply from there based on water exposure and view quality. Condominiums offer a lower entry point, but even those in older complexes can require significant reserve contributions under Florida's SB 4-D legislation passed in 2022.

Longboat Key price ranges are approximate. Market conditions change. Contact Barrett for current comparables.

Gulf-Front vs. Bay-Side: What Changes

Gulf-front properties sit in FEMA Zone VE on the western shore, meaning wave action is factored into flood risk calculations. This drives NFIP or private flood insurance premiums to $8,000 to $25,000+ per year on top of windstorm coverage. Bay-side properties along Sarasota Bay are typically Zone AE, with lower but still substantial flood insurance requirements. Interior streets are also often Zone AE, but with lower base flood elevations that can make insurance more manageable.

Manatee County vs. Sarasota County: Does It Matter?

Yes. The island is split roughly at the Sarasota-Manatee county line, which runs through the mid-island area near the Longboat Key Club. Properties north of the line are in Manatee County, assessed by the Manatee County Property Appraiser, and assigned to Manatee County schools. Properties south of the line are in Sarasota County. Tax rates, school assignments, and even utility billing can differ. I always confirm county assignment for any property my buyer clients consider here.

What Are the Main Communities on Longboat Key?

Longboat Key does not have a traditional neighborhood grid. The island is organized more by position (north, mid, south key) and by type of community. Several gated and private communities dominate the southern half of the island.

Bay Isles

Bay Isles is a private, gated community in the south key. It encompasses several distinct enclaves including Harbourside (condo towers on Sarasota Bay), Bayou Louise (single-family bay-front homes), Winding Oaks (interior estate lots), and access to the Bay Isles Beach Club (private Gulf beach). Properties here carry Bay Isles master HOA fees in addition to any sub-association fees. Access is controlled at the gate on Bay Isles Road.

Longboat Key Club Residences

The Longboat Key Club spans the southern tip of the island, encompassing two 18-hole golf courses, a racquet club, spa, marina, and multiple dining outlets. Club Residences and resort-managed condominiums are available for purchase and some units can participate in rental programs. Buyers should review the club membership requirements and fee structure before making an offer on a club-adjacent property.

Cedars East and Mid-Key Communities

The mid-key area includes Cedars East (a tennis community on the bay side), Longboat Harbour (condo complex with marina), and a mix of Gulf-front towers and bay-side single-family homes. North key properties are more varied, with smaller condos, bay-front homes, and older Gulf-front structures that sometimes represent teardown opportunities for buyers who want to build new.

What Insurance Costs Should Buyers Budget On Longboat Key?

Insurance is the number-one cost that surprises buyers who are new to Florida barrier island real estate. Every lender will require homeowners, flood, and windstorm coverage. On Longboat Key, wind mitigation credits help somewhat, but the island's location directly on the Gulf Coast means carriers price risk accordingly.

NFIP vs. Private Flood Insurance

The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) caps building coverage at $250,000, which is often insufficient for Longboat Key homes. Most buyers here will either layer private flood insurance on top or replace NFIP coverage entirely with a private policy that can cover full replacement value. Risk Rating 2.0, implemented by FEMA in 2021, eliminated older subsidized rates and now prices each property based on its individual risk profile. An elevation certificate ($400 to $800 from a licensed surveyor) can help establish your property's actual flood exposure and may lower your premium.

What Should Buyers Check Before Making an Offer?

Longboat Key has a high concentration of older condominium buildings that may face significant special assessments due to SB 4-D compliance requirements. Florida law now requires structural milestone inspections for any condo building three stories or taller that is 30 years old (or 25 years for Gulf-front and coastal structures), along with funded reserve accounts. Buildings that deferred maintenance for years are now issuing large special assessments to unit owners. I always review the most recent meeting minutes, the current budget, and the structural inspection report before advising any condo buyer on Longboat Key.

Five Things to Verify Before a Longboat Key Offer

  • Flood zone and elevation certificate Verify FEMA zone assignment at the FEMA Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov) and request an elevation certificate from the seller or order a new one.
  • Insurance quotes in writing Do not rely on estimates. Get actual quotes for homeowners, flood, and windstorm before your inspection period expires.
  • Permit history Confirm all work was permitted and closed. The permit history guide walks through how to verify this in Florida counties. For Longboat Key, check through the Town of Longboat Key Building Department and the applicable county (Manatee or Sarasota).
  • HOA and CDD fees Read the CDD fee guide and obtain a full accounting of all fees, assessments, and upcoming capital expenditures. For condos, review the current reserve study.
  • Rental restrictions If you plan to rent the property, confirm whether the HOA, condo declaration, or Town ordinances permit short-term rentals. Longboat Key has adopted regulations affecting vacation rental activity.

Ready to Buy or Sell on Longboat Key?

Contact BarrettCall (813) 733-7907

How Does the Buying Process Work on Longboat Key?

The Florida real estate contract (FR/Bar AS-IS or standard) governs most transactions here. Buyers typically have a 10 to 15-day inspection period during which they can cancel for any reason. Given the complexity of barrier island purchases, I recommend using all of that time. A general home inspection is necessary but not sufficient here: you will want a separate roof certification, a licensed structural inspector for older homes, a seawall inspection for waterfront properties, and an independent insurance consultation before you waive contingencies.

Typical Closing Costs on Longboat Key

In Sarasota and Manatee counties, sellers traditionally pay the owner's title insurance and documentary stamp tax. Confirm with your agent and closing attorney.

Is Longboat Key Right for You?

Longboat Key is the right fit for buyers who want luxury coastal living, Gulf beach access, and a relatively low-density, quiet environment. The year-round community is older, affluent, and values privacy. If you want a vibrant nightlife scene, easy walkability to restaurants and shops, or a fast-paced urban environment, Longboat Key is probably not your answer. Sarasota proper or the St. Armands Circle area might suit you better. If you want a more casual island vibe at a lower price point, consider Anna Maria Island to the north.

Read Is Longboat Key a Good Place to Live? for a full breakdown of the pros and cons, including comparisons to nearby markets. For waterfront-specific guidance, see Longboat Key Waterfront Homes. Cost details are in the Cost of Living guide.

Frequently Asked Questions About Longboat Key Homes for Sale

What is the average home price on Longboat Key?

The median sale price on Longboat Key typically falls between $900,000 and $1.4M depending on the mix of condos and single-family homes in a given period. Gulf-front single-family homes routinely exceed $3M. Entry-level condos can start around $300,000 to $450,000 in older, non-Gulf-front buildings, but those often carry elevated HOA fees and may face upcoming assessments for SB 4-D compliance. Contact Barrett for a current market snapshot and specific comparable sales in the area or property type you are targeting.

Are there any condos available under $500,000 on Longboat Key?

Yes, occasionally, primarily in older buildings on the north key and mid-key areas that do not have direct Gulf-front access. Buyers in this range should be especially careful about the building's financial health, reserve funding, any pending or recently issued special assessments, and the results of any structural milestone inspection. Some of these buildings face very large per-unit assessments that can erode the value of a seemingly affordable purchase within months of closing.

Can I rent out a Longboat Key property on Airbnb or VRBO?

It depends on the property type and location. The Town of Longboat Key has adopted vacation rental regulations that restrict short-term rentals in certain single-family residential zones. Many condo associations explicitly prohibit short-term rentals in their declarations. Before purchasing any Longboat Key property with rental income as part of your investment thesis, verify the town ordinance, the HOA or condo declaration, and obtain Florida DBPR vacation rental license requirements. Do not rely on a listing agent's assurance that rentals are "allowed" without reading the governing documents yourself.

What is the property tax rate on Longboat Key?

It depends on which county your property falls in. Sarasota County properties carry a combined millage of roughly 13 to 16 mills, while Manatee County properties are in the 14 to 18 mill range, depending on the applicable special districts. With Florida's homestead exemption ($50,000) and Save Our Homes cap (3% annual increase limit), primary residences receive meaningful tax savings over time. A $1M home assessed at just under market value with homestead might pay $10,000 to $15,000 per year in property taxes. See the Longboat Key Property Taxes guide for full detail.

How long does it take to buy a home on Longboat Key?

A cash transaction can close in 2 to 3 weeks if the parties are motivated and all documents are in order. A financed purchase typically takes 30 to 45 days from accepted contract to closing. In practice, the inspection period alone on a complex coastal property often takes the full 10 to 15 days as buyers work through insurance quotes, structural assessments, seawall inspections, and HOA document review. Do not rush this process on Longboat Key. The costs of buying the wrong property here are very high.

Quick Answer

Longboat Key is split between Sarasota County Schools and Manatee County Schools depending on where your property sits. Sarasota County students attend Longboat Key Elementary, then Booker Middle, then Riverview High or Sarasota High. Manatee County students from the north key attend Anna Maria Elementary, then Martha B. King Middle, then Bayshore High School or Manatee High School. Pine View School (gifted, grades 2-12) in Sarasota is a notable public school option. Most Longboat Key families use the Sarasota County public system or private schools.

Longboat Key FL Schools Guide: Ratings and Zones

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

School assignment on Longboat Key depends on which county your property is in. The island is divided at the Sarasota-Manatee county line, which runs through approximately the mid-island area near the Longboat Key Club. Properties south of the county line are in Sarasota County and assigned to Sarasota County Schools. Properties north of the line are in Manatee County and assigned to Manatee County Schools. Before purchasing if schools matter to your decision, confirm the county assignment for any specific property you are considering. Note: Longboat Key's permanent population skews heavily toward retirees and adults without school-age children. The island has one public elementary school and no public middle or high school.

What Schools Serve Sarasota County Properties on Longboat Key?

Longboat Key Elementary School

Longboat Key Elementary is the only public school physically located on the island. It serves kindergarten through 5th grade students in the Sarasota County portion of Longboat Key. The school is small, with a tight-knit community character reflecting the island's demographics. Confirm current enrollment boundaries and academic ratings through Sarasota County Schools at sarasotacountyschools.net or by calling the district at (941) 927-9000.

Booker Middle School (Sarasota County)

After Longboat Key Elementary, Sarasota County students from the island typically attend Booker Middle School in Sarasota for grades 6 through 8. Booker Middle is a magnet school offering fine and performing arts. Students commute from Longboat Key to the mainland for middle school (25 to 40 minutes each way). Confirm current boundary assignments with Sarasota County Schools, as magnet program participation involves an application process.

Riverview High School / Sarasota High School (Sarasota County)

For grades 9 through 12, Sarasota County students from Longboat Key are typically zoned to Riverview High School or Sarasota High School depending on the specific boundary. Both schools offer IB, AP, and dual enrollment programs. Sarasota High School is the historic downtown Sarasota high school with strong arts and performing arts programs. Riverview High School in southeastern Sarasota offers a wide range of academic and extracurricular programs. Commute from mid-key to these schools is approximately 30 to 45 minutes each way.

What Schools Serve Manatee County Properties on Longboat Key?

Anna Maria Elementary (Manatee County)

Students from the Manatee County (north key) portion of Longboat Key attend Anna Maria Elementary School, located on Anna Maria Island, for K-5. Anna Maria Elementary is a small school reflecting the barrier island community it serves. Confirm current enrollment data and boundary assignments with Manatee County Schools at manateeschools.net or (941) 708-8770.

Martha B. King Middle School (Manatee County)

Manatee County students from the island attend Martha B. King Middle School in Bradenton for grades 6 through 8. The school is located at 600 Dr. MLK Jr. Way, Bradenton, approximately 35 to 55 minutes from the north end of Longboat Key. Confirm current assignments with the district.

Bayshore High School or Manatee High School (Manatee County)

For grades 9 through 12, Manatee County north key students are typically assigned to Bayshore High School or Manatee High School. Both are in the Bradenton area. Manatee High School is the older downtown Bradenton high school with strong athletic traditions. Bayshore High School offers a range of academic programs. Confirm current boundary assignments with Manatee County Schools.

Pine View School (Sarasota County Gifted)

Pine View School at 1 Python Path, Osprey, FL is a public school serving academically gifted students in grades 2 through 12 from across Sarasota County. Admission requires qualification through the Sarasota County gifted education identification process. Families who qualify their children for Pine View often cite it as a primary reason they choose the Sarasota County side of the island. Transportation from Longboat Key to Pine View in Osprey is approximately 35 to 50 minutes. Confirm current gifted qualification process at sarasotacountyschools.net.

IB Programs in Sarasota County

Sarasota County offers International Baccalaureate (IB) programs at the middle and high school levels. Riverview High School and other Sarasota County high schools participate in the IB program, providing a rigorous pre-university curriculum. For families with academically motivated high school students, the IB option within Sarasota County public schools is a meaningful academic resource.

Is Longboat Key a Good Place for Families with School-Age Children?

This depends heavily on your school priorities and tolerance for commute. The one public elementary school on the island (Longboat Key Elementary) serves early grades for Sarasota County residents. Middle and high school requires commuting off the island daily, typically 25 to 45 minutes each way. For families who use private schools in Sarasota, the calculus is similar: daily driving to the mainland is unavoidable.

Many families who are willing to make the daily school commute find that the lifestyle benefits of living on Longboat Key, beaches, water activities, quiet streets, and a safe environment, are worth the driving. Others find the daily transport burden to be too much and choose to live closer to their chosen school in Sarasota or Bradenton. For families with teens who drive themselves, the concern diminishes somewhat once children can manage their own transportation. The school situation is one more factor to evaluate honestly rather than assume will resolve itself.

If schools are your primary household priority, consider living closer to school in Sarasota (near Pine View or the Sarasota city schools) or in Bradenton (near the Manatee County magnet and IB programs). You can still visit and enjoy Longboat Key's beaches without the daily school commute burden.

Frequently Asked Questions About Longboat Key Schools

How do I find out which school district my Longboat Key property is in?

The simplest approach is to check the property's county through the applicable county property appraiser website. Sarasota County properties are at sc-pa.com; Manatee County properties are at mcpafl.org. The county assignment determines the school district. Once you know the county, use the district's school locator tool to confirm specific school assignments. Sarasota County uses a school locator at sarasotacountyschools.net. Manatee County uses a similar tool at manateeschools.net. Do not rely on the listing agent's statement about school assignment; verify it yourself through the district.

Can I apply for school choice to a different school on Longboat Key?

Both Sarasota County and Manatee County offer open enrollment / school choice programs that allow students to apply to schools outside their assigned attendance zone, subject to available capacity. Magnet programs (like Booker Middle's fine arts program in Sarasota County) have their own application processes. Private school choice is available through Florida's education scholarship programs for qualifying students. The Florida Department of Education oversees several scholarship programs that provide state funding for private school tuition for eligible students. Details change annually; check fldoe.org for current program availability.

How good are the public schools assigned to Longboat Key?

School quality in the Sarasota area is generally above the Florida average. Sarasota County Schools has been recognized as one of Florida's stronger school districts. Within the county, there is variation by school, and Longboat Key's small elementary school has a community character that many parents find appealing. Pine View School (accessible to qualifying Sarasota County students) is one of Florida's highest-rated public schools. Manatee County Schools serves the north key; the district is generally solid but not uniformly top-rated across all schools. For current Florida School Grades (A-F ratings) and detailed school data, visit the Florida Department of Education's school performance reports at fldoe.org.

Is IMG Academy near Longboat Key?

IMG Academy is in Bradenton, approximately 35 to 50 minutes from Longboat Key. IMG is a private boarding school known for its elite athletic training programs combined with college-preparatory academics. It primarily serves boarding students from around the world who are training in their sport (tennis, soccer, golf, baseball, football, basketball, track and field, lacrosse). Families who have children attending IMG sometimes choose to live in the Bradenton or Longboat Key area to be close to campus during the school year.

What college or university options are near Longboat Key?

The Sarasota-Manatee area has several higher education options within commuting distance. New College of Florida (a public liberal arts honors college, one of only about a dozen in the US) is in Sarasota. Ringling College of Art and Design is a highly-regarded private arts college in Sarasota. State College of Florida (Manatee-Sarasota) has campuses in Bradenton and Sarasota with associate and bachelor's degree programs. The University of South Florida has a Sarasota-Manatee campus offering upper-division and graduate programs. For a full four-year research university, USF's main campus in Tampa is 80 to 95 minutes away.

title: Longboat Key FL Commute and Location Guide
excerpt: Longboat Key FL Commute and Location Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Longboat Key is 20 to 30 minutes from downtown Sarasota and 35 to 50 minutes from downtown Bradenton. Tampa is 70 to 95 minutes on a good day. SRQ (Sarasota-Bradenton Airport) is 25 to 35 minutes. There is no public transit. A car is required. Longboat Key is an excellent base for professionals working in Sarasota or Bradenton, but a challenging daily commute to Tampa or points north.

Longboat Key FL Commute and Location Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key is a barrier island, which means there is only one road on and off: Gulf of Mexico Drive (SR 789), which runs the length of the island and connects at the north end via the Longboat Key Bridge to St. Armands Circle and Lido Key, then to downtown Sarasota, and at the south end via the Longboat Key Bridge (a different bridge) to Sarasota's southern neighborhoods and the mainland. There is no shortcut, no back road, and no bypass. For residents commuting daily to employment centers, this geography is both the attraction and the constraint.

What Are the Congestion Patterns on Longboat Key?

On-Island Traffic

Gulf of Mexico Drive is a two-lane road for most of its length. During peak season (November through April), traffic builds around the grocery stores and restaurants in the mid-key area and at access points to the bridges at both ends. During the winter season peak, the 15-minute mid-island-to-bridge drive can extend to 20 to 30 minutes on particularly busy days. During the summer, traffic on the island is very light. The bridges at each end of the island are the primary congestion points during high season.

Off-Island Congestion

Sarasota traffic has grown significantly as the area's population has expanded. The major arterials (US-41, Fruitville Road, Bee Ridge Road, Clark Road) see meaningful congestion during morning and afternoon rush hours. Sarasota's road network has not kept pace with growth, and the lack of a true freeway through the core of the city creates bottlenecks that extend commute times. Residents commuting to the Sarasota medical corridor, downtown, or to employers along Cattlemen Road and Fruitville should expect 35 to 55 minutes total door-to-door during morning rush.

Is There Public Transit from Longboat Key?

No. The Sarasota County Area Transit (SCAT) system does not provide service to Longboat Key. Manatee County's Public Transit bus routes do not extend to the island. There are no commuter rail options. Rideshare (Uber and Lyft) operates on the island, but during slow periods of the day, wait times can exceed 15 to 20 minutes, and during peak season surge pricing applies. For any regular commute, a personal vehicle is the only practical option.

Airport Access from Longboat Key

Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport (SRQ)

SRQ is the most convenient airport for Longboat Key residents. Located at 6000 Airport Circle, Sarasota, it is approximately 25 to 35 minutes from the north end of the island. SRQ offers direct service to major hubs (Atlanta, Charlotte, New York, Chicago, Boston, Dallas, Philadelphia) and select leisure destinations. The airport is manageable in size, with short security lines compared to TPA. For residents who travel frequently, SRQ's convenience is a genuine quality-of-life advantage of living in the Sarasota area. The airport has expanded service significantly since 2020. Check current routes at srq-airport.com.

Tampa International Airport (TPA)

TPA is approximately 80 to 100 minutes from Longboat Key under normal conditions. It offers significantly more routes and airline options than SRQ. For residents who need specific routes or find SRQ fares to be higher, TPA is the backup. The drive is straightforward: north on I-75, then I-275 northwest to the airport. Parking at TPA is straightforward with both garage and economy options.

Remote Work and Longboat Key

Remote work has meaningfully increased the appeal of Longboat Key for buyers who previously might have been constrained by commute distances. Many Longboat Key properties have excellent broadband internet (Spectrum and Xfinity both serve the island with 400 Mbps to 1 Gbps service), making video conferencing and cloud-based work practical. For remote workers with occasional business travel, SRQ's direct connections to major hubs reduce the friction of the island location. The lifestyle trade-off of longer occasional drives versus daily luxury living on the Gulf is a favorable one for many remote workers.

Frequently Asked Questions About the Longboat Key Commute

Can I commute to Tampa from Longboat Key?

Technically yes, practically no as a daily commute. The drive is 75 to 95 minutes under normal conditions, which means 2.5 to 3+ hours daily in a car. Some executives with flexible schedules do make this work, but it is an outlier case. Most people who commute to Tampa daily choose to live significantly closer. If Tampa is your employment center, a better base might be Bradenton (30 to 45 minutes to Tampa) or North Hillsborough County communities rather than Longboat Key.

What is the traffic like leaving Longboat Key on weekends?

During peak season (January through April), weekend afternoons can see bridge backups of 15 to 30 minutes at both ends of the island, particularly at the north bridge. The congestion is seasonal and weather-dependent. A sunny Saturday in January will generate more bridge backup than a rainy Tuesday in August. Year-round residents describe the traffic as manageable once you know the patterns and adjust timing accordingly. Leaving the island before 10 AM or after 4 PM on peak weekend days generally avoids the worst congestion.

Is there a ferry or water taxi from Longboat Key?

No scheduled ferry or water taxi service operates from Longboat Key as of September 2026. Marina-to-marina boat trips to Sarasota are certainly possible for boaters, but this is not a practical daily commute option for most residents. The island is exclusively car-accessed for all practical transportation purposes.

How do deliveries work on Longboat Key?

Amazon, UPS, FedEx, and USPS all deliver to Longboat Key addresses. Delivery times are comparable to other residential addresses in the Sarasota area. Grocery delivery services including Instacart and Amazon Fresh serve the island. Since there is no large supermarket on the island, many residents rely on delivery for major grocery shopping. Restaurant delivery apps also operate but with a more limited restaurant selection than Sarasota proper.

What is the best place to live on Longboat Key for the shortest Sarasota commute?

The north end of Longboat Key, closest to the north bridge connecting to St. Armands Circle and Lido Key, offers the shortest drive to downtown Sarasota. Properties near the Sarasota-Manatee county line (roughly the mid-key area and north) exit the island most directly toward Sarasota via the northern bridge. The south key exit goes through Longboat Key's southern bridge and then through Sarasota's southern neighborhoods before reaching the downtown core, adding time for Sarasota-bound commuters. For Bradenton-bound commuters, the north key is also advantageous, as Cortez Road (which connects to Bradenton Beach and Anna Maria Island, then to Bradenton) is accessible from the northern approach.

title: Is Longboat Key FL a Good Place to Live?
excerpt: Is Longboat Key FL a Good Place to Live?, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Longboat Key is an excellent place to live for buyers who want luxury Gulf Coast living, privacy, and natural beauty. It is not a fit for buyers who need urban walkability, affordable housing, or easy commute access to Tampa. Year-round residents enjoy world-class beaches, Gulf sunsets, and a quiet community. The tradeoffs are high property costs, significant insurance expenses, and limited everyday conveniences on the island itself.

Is Longboat Key FL a Good Place to Live?

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key is a 12-mile barrier island on the Gulf of Mexico, divided between Manatee County (north end) and Sarasota County (south end). The permanent population is roughly 7,000 to 8,000 residents. From November through April, snowbirds and seasonal residents roughly double that count. I have helped buyers from across the country evaluate whether Longboat Key fits their life, and the answer is genuinely different depending on the buyer. Here is the honest assessment.

What Makes Longboat Key a Good Place to Live?

Gulf Beaches and Natural Beauty

Longboat Key's Gulf beaches are consistently ranked among Florida's best. The sand is white and fine-grained, the water is warm from May through October, and the Gulf side has public beach access points spaced throughout the island. Longboat Key Beach (at the north end near the Sarasota Manatee county line) is publicly accessible. The south end features private beach access through Bay Isles Beach Club for Bay Isles residents. Dolphins, manatees, and shorebirds are regular visitors. Sunsets over the Gulf from the west-facing shores are genuinely spectacular.

Privacy and Low Density

Longboat Key is more private and less commercial than many Florida barrier islands. There is no Duval Street, no strip mall atmosphere, and no heavy party tourism. The Town of Longboat Key has aggressively regulated commercial development. The island has a handful of restaurants, a small grocery option, and a few boutiques. If you want quiet, this is genuine quiet. If you want convenience, you will drive to Sarasota or Bradenton for most of your shopping and dining.

Proximity to Sarasota's Cultural Scene

Downtown Sarasota is 20 to 30 minutes from the south key. Sarasota is home to the Ringling Museum, Van Wezel Performing Arts Hall, Sarasota Opera, the Sarasota Ballet, Florida Studio Theatre, and a restaurant scene that punches well above its population size. St. Armands Circle, a short drive from the north end of Longboat Key, offers outdoor dining, boutique shopping, and direct beach access at Lido Beach. Residents of Longboat Key who want cultural amenities have easy access to them without having to live in a dense urban environment.

Boating and Water Recreation

Sarasota Bay on the east side of the island provides protected water for sailing, kayaking, paddleboarding, and motorboating. Gulf access is available through New Pass (at the north end of the island, where it connects to Sarasota) and through Longboat Pass (at the south end). Several marinas serve the island, including at the Longboat Key Club and at Bayfront. Fishing in the bay and Gulf is productive year-round for snook, redfish, tarpon, grouper, and flounder. The bay's seagrass beds attract manatees and support a diverse fishery.

What Are the Drawbacks of Living on Longboat Key?

Cost

Longboat Key is expensive by any measure. Property values, insurance costs, HOA fees, and the general cost of island living all run significantly higher than comparable mainland properties. A buyer who stretches their budget to buy here may find the ongoing carrying costs uncomfortable within the first year. See the Longboat Key Cost of Living guide for a detailed breakdown of what to budget for a primary residence.

Limited On-Island Amenities

There is no Target, no Costco, no large grocery store, and no hospital on Longboat Key. The island has a small convenience-oriented market and a collection of restaurants, but any major shopping or medical care requires a drive to the mainland. Sarasota Memorial Hospital is the closest major facility, roughly 30 minutes from mid-key. If you value walkability and everyday convenience without a car, Longboat Key is the wrong choice.

Hurricane and Flood Risk

Longboat Key sits on a barrier island in a Gulf Coast hurricane zone. The island is designated Evacuation Zone A, meaning mandatory evacuation orders will apply in any significant storm threat. Flooding risk is real: the entire island is in FEMA flood zone AE or VE. Post-storm cleanup, insurance claims, and temporary displacement are not hypothetical for residents here. Buyers should read the actual flood maps, get genuine insurance quotes, and make peace with the storm risk before committing.

Commute Reality

Anyone commuting to Tampa from Longboat Key is looking at 70 to 90 minutes each way on a good day. The Sunshine Skyway Bridge toll route can add both cost and time to northbound commutes. The island is excellent for retirees, remote workers, and professionals whose work is in or near Sarasota/Bradenton. It is a challenging daily commute destination for anyone working in Tampa, St. Pete, or beyond. See the Longboat Key Commute Guide for full details.

Who Should Live on Longboat Key?

Based on my experience working with buyers here, the people who end up happiest on Longboat Key typically fit one or more of these profiles:

  • Retirees and semi-retirees who want a private, beautiful environment and have the time to enjoy the island's natural setting rather than needing quick access to employment centers.
  • Remote workers who can do their jobs from anywhere and value the lifestyle, provided they are realistic about internet reliability and the absence of coworking spaces on the island.
  • Part-time residents and seasonal buyers who want a Florida winter base and are comfortable with the carrying costs of a second home.
  • Sarasota/Bradenton-area professionals whose commute is 20 to 40 minutes, not 90 minutes. Doctors, attorneys, business owners with operations in the Sarasota corridor can live on Longboat Key without crushing daily commute times.
  • Buyers who value exclusivity and privacy in their daily life and are willing to pay the premium that comes with living on a well-regulated, low-density barrier island.

Frequently Asked Questions About Living on Longboat Key

Is Longboat Key safe?

Longboat Key has a very low crime rate by Florida and national standards. The Town of Longboat Key has its own police department. The small permanent population, gated community character of much of the south key, and the quiet nature of the island all contribute to a safe environment. Visitors unfamiliar with coastal Florida should note that the primary safety consideration on Longboat Key is hurricane preparedness and flood risk, not crime.

What are the best restaurants on Longboat Key?

Longboat Key has a modest but solid restaurant selection. The Longboat Key Club's dining outlets (Portofino and other venues) are well-regarded. Euphemia Haye is a long-established fine dining institution on the key. Mar-Vista Restaurant and Dockside Bar offer casual waterfront dining on the bay side. For a broader dining selection, St. Armands Circle (15 minutes north via Longboat Key bridge) and downtown Sarasota offer dozens of options across every price range and cuisine.

Does Longboat Key flood often?

Minor tidal flooding on low-lying streets occurs several times per year, particularly during king tide events in fall. Major flooding events are tied to named storms or tropical systems. The island was significantly affected by Hurricane Helene in 2024 and by Ian in 2022 in adjacent areas. Buyers should review FEMA flood maps, read recent news coverage of storm impacts, and have honest conversations with neighbors about what flooding looks like in their specific neighborhood.

Is there public transportation on Longboat Key?

No meaningful public transit serves Longboat Key. A car is required for all practical purposes. Rideshare services (Uber and Lyft) operate but with longer wait times than urban areas. Some residents use bicycles for local trips along the key. The island is not walkable for most daily errands. This is a car-dependent lifestyle choice and buyers should factor vehicle costs into their overall living expense calculation.

What is the vibe of the Longboat Key community?

The year-round community is primarily older adults and retirees who value privacy, nature, and a refined but low-key lifestyle. The seasonal influx from November through April brings a wealthier, more active demographic. Longboat Key is not a college-town vibe, not a young-families-with-strollers vibe, and not a bachelor-party-weekend vibe. It is an island for people who genuinely want to live quietly in a beautiful place. Most long-term residents describe it as exactly the right amount of everything.

title: Longboat Key FL Real Estate Guide
excerpt: Longboat Key FL Real Estate Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Longboat Key real estate is a top-tier luxury barrier island market with median sale prices typically between $900K and $1.4M, low inventory, and high carrying costs. The market is dominated by cash buyers, seasonal demand peaks in Q1, and days on market average 60 to 120 days for most price ranges. SB 4-D compliance in condo buildings is reshaping the sub-$600K condo segment significantly.

Longboat Key FL Real Estate Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key real estate sits at the intersection of coastal luxury and complex barrier island ownership realities. The island spans Manatee County (north) and Sarasota County (south), and operates under both county governments and its own Town of Longboat Key regulations. Understanding how this market works before you engage with it is essential. This guide covers market dynamics, inventory patterns, buyer profiles, and the factors that drive price on the key.

Longboat Key Resources

How Is the Longboat Key Real Estate Market Structured?

The Longboat Key market is roughly divided into two segments: single-family homes and condominiums. Condos represent the larger share of transactions by volume, given the concentration of mid-rise and high-rise condo buildings along both the Gulf and bay sides of the island. Single-family homes, particularly waterfront, transact at higher dollar amounts but in smaller numbers.

Segment shares vary by year and market conditions. Contact Barrett for current inventory breakdown.

Seasonal Demand Patterns

Longboat Key sees its peak buyer activity from January through April, when northern snowbirds are in residence and can physically tour properties. The summer months see lower activity but not as severe a drop as some Florida markets, because some national buyers prefer to visit off-peak when the island is quieter. Sellers who list in January through March typically see the most competition among buyers. Sellers who list in August and September may see fewer showings but also less competing inventory.

Cash Buyer Dominance

Longboat Key has one of the highest rates of cash transactions in the Florida coastal market. Cash buyers are drawn by the elimination of lender-required inspections, the ability to close quickly, and the negotiating leverage that cash brings in a seller's market. When interest rates are elevated, the cash advantage on Longboat Key is more pronounced than in starter-home markets, since the buyer pool is predominantly wealth-driven rather than income-driven. Financed buyers are competitive here but should expect some sellers to prefer cash offers, all else being equal.

What Drives Price on Longboat Key?

Water Exposure and View Quality

Water exposure is the primary price driver on Longboat Key. Direct Gulf-front properties command the highest premiums, with Gulf views adding $500,000 to several million dollars over comparable interior properties. Bay-front and bay-view properties sit in the middle. Direct bayfront with dock capability commands a premium over bay-view without dock access. Interior properties are priced on lot size, structure quality, and location within the key.

For Condos: Floor, View, and SB 4-D Status

In condo buildings, price is driven by floor (higher floors command premiums), view orientation (Gulf-facing vs. bay-facing vs. interior-facing), unit size, renovation quality, and most critically in the current market, the building's SB 4-D compliance status. Florida Senate Bill 4-D, passed after the Surfside collapse in 2021, requires structural milestone inspections and funded reserves for older multi-story condo buildings. Buildings that have completed inspections and have properly funded reserves are commanding price premiums. Buildings facing large special assessments are trading at discounts, sometimes significant ones.

What Is Inventory Like on Longboat Key?

Longboat Key is a built-out island. There is no vacant land being subdivided into new lots, and new construction is almost entirely teardown-rebuild activity. Total housing inventory on the island is finite and relatively stable. Active listing counts fluctuate seasonally, typically peaking in spring as snowbird owners decide whether to sell before heading north.

Months of supply on Longboat Key has ranged from 4 to 9 months in recent years depending on price tier. The luxury Gulf-front SFH segment ($3M+) carries the most months of supply, while well-priced mid-range condos in compliant buildings can move quickly during peak season. I track active inventory closely for my Longboat Key buyer clients. Contact me for a current inventory snapshot for the specific property type you are targeting.

What Are the Biggest Market Risks on Longboat Key Right Now?

SB 4-D Special Assessments in Older Condo Buildings

This is the most significant near-term risk factor for the Longboat Key condo market. Buildings that have deferred maintenance for years, and whose association boards elected not to fund reserves, are now being required by law to do structural inspections and fund reserves. The result in some buildings has been per-unit special assessments ranging from $20,000 to $200,000 or more. Buyers in the sub-$600K condo segment especially need to review building financials carefully before purchasing. I obtain all available HOA documents, meeting minutes, and inspection reports before advising any of my buyer clients in this segment.

Insurance Market Instability

Florida's property insurance market has been under severe pressure since Hurricane Ian in 2022. Multiple private carriers have exited the Florida coastal market or significantly restricted new policy issuance. This affects Longboat Key buyers in two ways: premiums have risen substantially, and in some cases buyers cannot secure adequate private coverage and must rely on Citizens Property Insurance, Florida's insurer of last resort, which has its own policy limits and may not cover full replacement value on high-end properties. Get insurance quotes early in your due diligence, not at the end.

Sea Level Rise and Long-Term Coastal Risk

Longboat Key sits at low elevation, with most developed areas between 3 and 8 feet above mean sea level. According to NOAA sea level rise projections, the Sarasota-Manatee coast is expected to see 0.5 to 1.5 feet of mean sea level rise by 2050 under intermediate scenarios. This does not mean the island is uninhabitable in the near term, but it does mean that buyers thinking about 20 to 30-year hold periods should factor in the trajectory of flood zone remapping, insurance availability, and financing conditions for coastal properties over that timeframe.

Frequently Asked Questions About Longboat Key Real Estate

Is now a good time to buy on Longboat Key?

I do not time markets for my clients, because no one can do that reliably. What I can say is that the fundamentals of the Longboat Key market are: finite supply, wealthy buyer pool, strong seasonal demand, and a location that cannot be replicated or expanded. Those fundamentals have historically supported prices through economic cycles better than more speculative markets. The key risk factors today are insurance cost escalation, SB 4-D assessment exposure in older condos, and broader Florida coastal market sentiment. Buyers who are buying for lifestyle and long-term hold are in a different position than buyers who are buying for short-term appreciation.

How do I find out if a condo building has passed its SB 4-D inspection?

Ask the listing agent for the most recent structural inspection report and the current reserve study. Florida law now requires that condo associations provide these documents to prospective buyers upon request. If the listing agent is unable to provide them, that itself is a red flag. I pull these documents for all of my condo buyer clients before we make an offer on any Longboat Key building.

What is the best neighborhood on Longboat Key to buy in?

There is no single "best" neighborhood, because the right choice depends entirely on your priorities. Bay Isles (south key, gated) is ideal for buyers who want maximum privacy and beach club access. The mid-key area offers the best balance of price and Gulf proximity for condos. North key offers the lowest price points but older inventory. The Longboat Key Club area is right for buyers who want resort amenities bundled into their residence. I help my buyer clients evaluate each area against their specific priorities rather than applying a one-size ranking.

Do I need a buyer's agent when buying on Longboat Key?

I am biased here because I am an agent, but the honest answer is: the complexity of barrier island real estate, the cost exposure from flood zones and condo assessments, and the negotiation dynamics of the luxury market make professional representation genuinely valuable. The listing agent represents the seller. If you work directly with a listing agent, you have no advocate for your interests in the transaction. On a property costing $1M or more, the cost of inadequate representation vastly exceeds the cost of having your own agent.

How long does inventory stay on the market on Longboat Key?

Average days on market varies significantly by segment. Well-priced condos in compliant buildings can move in 30 to 60 days during peak season. Luxury Gulf-front single-family homes at $5M+ may sit 6 to 18 months even when properly priced. Properties with known issues (SB 4-D concerns, deferred maintenance, high special assessments) can sit indefinitely if not priced to reflect the liability. title: Cost of Living in Longboat Key FL
excerpt: Cost of Living in Longboat Key FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

The cost of living on Longboat Key is high. A primary residence purchased at $1M will carry $15,000 to $35,000 per year in property taxes and insurance alone, before HOA fees, utilities, or maintenance. Budget an additional $12,000 to $30,000+ per year in insurance depending on your property type and flood zone. There is no on-island grocery store, no hospital, and limited public transportation, meaning a car (or two) is an unavoidable expense.

Cost of Living in Longboat Key FL

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key is one of the most expensive places to own real estate on Florida's Gulf Coast. This guide breaks down the actual ongoing ownership costs for primary residents, with honest numbers for insurance, property taxes, HOA fees, utilities, and everyday expenses. I have worked with buyers who underestimated Longboat Key carrying costs by $20,000 to $40,000 per year because they only looked at the mortgage payment.

What Are the Monthly Carrying Costs on Longboat Key?

Below is a cost model for three typical Longboat Key property types at representative purchase prices. These are estimates intended to illustrate the order of magnitude of costs. Your actual costs will vary based on your specific property, financing, and insurance quotes.

Estimates use Sep 2026 rate assumptions. Mortgage rate assumed at 6.75%. Tax assumes homestead exemption. Insurance is estimated, not quoted.

What Does Insurance Cost on Longboat Key?

Insurance is the line item that most surprises buyers new to Florida coastal real estate. On Longboat Key, every property requires at minimum homeowners insurance and flood insurance. Most lenders will also require windstorm coverage, though in Florida this is often included in a homeowners policy or purchased as a separate wind-only policy through Citizens Property Insurance.

Florida Power and Light (FPL) Electric Rates

Longboat Key is served by Florida Power and Light (FPL). Residential electric rates are based on a tiered consumption structure. A 1,500 sq ft condo with central air will typically see summer electric bills of $120 to $200 per month. A 3,000 sq ft Gulf-front home running heavy air conditioning from May through October may see bills of $300 to $600 per month. FPL's fuel adjustment charge fluctuates quarterly based on natural gas prices. Confirm rates at fpl.com or call FPL customer service to get a consumption-based estimate for a specific property.

Town of Longboat Key Water and Sewer

Water and sewer on the island is provided by the Town of Longboat Key Public Works Department. Rates are tiered by consumption. Typical residential water and sewer bills run $80 to $250 per month depending on lot irrigation, pool water top-off, and household size. Waterfront properties with irrigation systems can run significantly higher during dry season. Confirm current rates at the Town of Longboat Key website or Public Works office.

Internet and Cable

Spectrum (Charter Communications) and Xfinity (Comcast) are the primary internet and cable providers on Longboat Key. Fiber service is available in parts of the island. Standard broadband internet plans run $60 to $100 per month for 400 Mbps to 1 Gbps service. Many condo buildings include internet and cable in the HOA fee, so confirm with the building before signing up for redundant service.

What Are HOA Fees Like on Longboat Key?

HOA and condo association fees vary enormously by building and community. This is one of the most important due diligence items on any Longboat Key purchase. Condo fees in older Gulf-front high-rises can run $1,500 to $4,000+ per month for units that include amenities (pool, fitness center, 24-hour security, cable, water) and are actively funding reserves for upcoming capital projects. Newer or smaller buildings may run $600 to $1,200 per month. Single-family homes in Bay Isles or other master-planned communities carry HOA fees of $200 to $800 per month for gate security, common area maintenance, and community amenities.

Fee ranges are approximate. Always obtain the actual association budget and recent meeting minutes before purchase.

What Does Everyday Life Cost on Longboat Key?

Groceries and Dining

There is no large supermarket on Longboat Key. The island has a small convenience-style market, and some residents use Instacart or Amazon Fresh delivery for regular grocery orders. Most residents drive to Publix, Whole Foods, or Trader Joe's in Sarasota (15 to 25 minutes from mid or south key) or Bradenton for weekly grocery shopping. Dining on the island ranges from casual waterfront spots at $20 to $40 per person to fine dining at Euphemia Haye and the LBK Club where a dinner for two can easily exceed $150. St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota expand the dining options enormously without a long drive.

Healthcare

There is no hospital on Longboat Key. Sarasota Memorial Hospital (SMH) is the closest major facility, roughly 25 to 35 minutes from the south and mid-key areas. SMH is a well-regarded regional medical center with cardiovascular, oncology, and orthopedic programs. For emergencies, the town has a fire station with ALS capability, and air transport to Tampa's Level I trauma centers (Tampa General, St. Joseph's) is available for the most serious cases. Residents who require frequent specialist care or dialysis will want to plan carefully for the 30 to 45-minute round trip to Sarasota medical facilities.

Transportation Costs

A car is required on Longboat Key. There is no public transit and rideshare wait times can be long, especially during peak season when demand is high. Budget one to two vehicles plus insurance (typically $1,500 to $4,000/yr per vehicle in Florida depending on driver profile), fuel, and maintenance. For residents who commute to Sarasota or Bradenton daily, fuel costs are modest. For anyone commuting north toward Tampa, the Sunshine Skyway toll ($4.25 per crossing as of 2026) adds up quickly.

Frequently Asked Questions About Longboat Key Cost of Living

What income do I need to live comfortably on Longboat Key?

This depends heavily on your mortgage situation and property type. A retired couple owning a $700K mid-key condo free and clear might need $80,000 to $120,000 per year in income to cover association fees, insurance, property taxes, utilities, transportation, and lifestyle expenses comfortably. A family with a $2M financed Gulf-front home might need $350,000+ in annual income to keep housing costs below 40% of gross income. The general rule: do not buy on Longboat Key if the combined mortgage, insurance, and taxes will exceed 35% of your gross monthly income.

Are property taxes higher in Manatee County or Sarasota County?

Manatee County millage rates are typically slightly higher than Sarasota County's, resulting in marginally higher tax bills for comparable assessed values. The difference is not dramatic, on the order of $500 to $2,000 per year for mid-range properties, but it is a real factor to consider when comparing two similar properties on opposite sides of the county line. See the Longboat Key Property Taxes guide for detailed millage breakdowns and sample calculations.

Does the homestead exemption apply on Longboat Key?

Yes. Florida's homestead exemption applies to any property that is your primary residence as of January 1 of the tax year. The exemption reduces your assessed value by $50,000 (the first $25,000 applies to all taxes; the second $25,000 applies to non-school taxes). You must file by March 1 with the applicable county property appraiser: Manatee County Property Appraiser (mcpafl.org) for north key properties or Sarasota County Property Appraiser (sc-pa.com) for south key properties. The Save Our Homes cap (3% annual increase limit on assessed value) also kicks in after your first year with homestead, providing significant long-term tax protection for primary residents.

What is the biggest overlooked cost for new Longboat Key owners?

In my experience, the two most consistently underestimated cost categories are: (1) insurance, which continues to escalate and can increase $2,000 to $8,000 per year on renewal in the current market, and (2) condo special assessments, particularly in older buildings that are now required to fund structural inspections and reserves under SB 4-D. I have seen buyers walk into a condo purchase expecting $800/month HOA and then receive a special assessment notice for $50,000 within the first year of ownership. Due diligence on building finances is not optional on Longboat Key.

Are there any cost of living advantages to Longboat Key?

Florida has no state income tax, which is a meaningful benefit for high earners relocating from states like New York, California, or Illinois. Property taxes, while high in dollar terms, are applied at moderate mill rates. Florida's homestead protections are strong once established. Compared to comparable luxury coastal markets in the Northeast or California, the overall tax burden in Florida remains competitive even with high insurance costs factored in.

title: Longboat Key FL Property Taxes
excerpt: Longboat Key FL Property Taxes, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Longboat Key property taxes depend on which county your property is in. Sarasota County properties carry roughly 13 to 16 mills total. Manatee County properties run approximately 14 to 18 mills. A $1M home with Florida homestead exemption pays approximately $9,500 to $14,000 per year. Investment properties and seasonal homes pay more because the $50,000 homestead exemption does not apply.

Longboat Key FL Property Taxes: Complete Guide

By Barrett Henry, Broker Associate, REMAX Collective • Updated September 23, 2026

Longboat Key spans two Florida counties, which means property taxes work differently depending on where exactly your property sits. North key properties are assessed by the Manatee County Property Appraiser. South key properties are assessed by the Sarasota County Property Appraiser. Both counties offer Florida's homestead exemption and Save Our Homes protections to primary residents. This guide breaks down how the tax system works on Longboat Key and what you should expect to pay.

How Are Longboat Key Property Taxes Calculated?

Florida property taxes are calculated by multiplying the taxable assessed value of your property by the combined millage rate for your taxing district. One mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. Your taxable assessed value is your market value minus any applicable exemptions (homestead, senior, disability, etc.).

Formula: Taxable Value x (Total Millage / 1,000) = Annual Property Tax

How Does the Florida Homestead Exemption Work on Longboat Key?

Florida's homestead exemption is available to any property owner who uses the property as their primary residence as of January 1 of the tax year. The exemption works as follows:

  • First $25,000 of assessed value: Exempt from all property taxes including school taxes.
  • Second $25,000 of assessed value (between $50,000 and $75,000): Exempt from all taxes except school district taxes.
  • Net effect: Up to $50,000 reduction in assessed value, with the school tax saving applying only to the first $25,000 reduction.

The filing deadline is March 1 of the tax year for which you want the exemption. You cannot file retroactively. If you close on a Longboat Key property in January, you must file by March 1 of that same year to get the exemption for that year's taxes. File with the applicable county:

  • Sarasota County Property Appraiser: sc-pa.com | 2001 Adams Lane, Sarasota, FL 34237 | (941) 861-8200
  • Manatee County Property Appraiser: mcpafl.org | 915 4th Ave W, Bradenton, FL 34205 | (941) 748-8208

Save Our Homes Cap

Once you have homestead status, Florida's Save Our Homes provision limits the annual increase in your property's assessed value to 3% or the rate of inflation (CPI), whichever is less. In a rising real estate market, this protection is extremely valuable. A homestead property bought in 2015 at $500,000 that is now worth $1.2M may still be assessed at $650,000 or $700,000 if the owner has held it with homestead continuously. This creates a significant tax advantage for long-term primary residents vs. recent buyers at current market prices.

Portability

Florida's portability provision allows homestead property owners to transfer their accumulated Save Our Homes benefit (the difference between market value and assessed value) to a new homestead property in Florida. This is significant for buyers who are selling a long-held Florida primary residence and purchasing on Longboat Key. The transferred benefit can reduce the new property's assessed value by up to $500,000. Portability must be applied for when you file your homestead exemption on the new property. Do not miss this filing deadline.

Portability transfers the accumulated SOH benefit. Maximum portable benefit is $500,000.

How Do I Look Up Property Taxes for a Specific Longboat Key Property?

The fastest way to see what a specific property is currently paying in taxes:

  • Sarasota County: Go to sarasotataxcollector.com, click Property Taxes, and search by address or parcel number. The current and prior year tax bills are available online.
  • Manatee County: Go to taxcollector.com, search by address or parcel number. Tax bills and payment history are available online.

Important: the current owner's tax bill reflects their exemption status and their assessed value (which may be significantly below market due to Save Our Homes). Your tax bill as a new buyer will be based on a new assessment close to your purchase price, not the prior owner's assessed value. Always calculate what you will pay, not what the seller pays.

Frequently Asked Questions About Longboat Key Property Taxes

When are Longboat Key property taxes due?

Florida property tax bills are mailed in November and are due in full by March 31 of the following year. Florida offers early payment discounts: 4% if paid in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, and 1% in February. Taxes become delinquent after April 1. If you have a mortgage, your lender typically collects monthly escrow and pays the annual bill on your behalf, usually in November to capture the 4% discount.

Is there a senior exemption on Longboat Key?

Yes. Both Sarasota and Manatee counties offer additional senior exemptions for homestead property owners age 65 or older who meet income requirements. The senior exemption can provide an additional $25,000 to $50,000 reduction in assessed value on top of the standard homestead exemption. Income limits and specific amounts vary by county and are adjusted periodically. Contact the applicable county property appraiser's office for current income thresholds and application requirements.

How much will my taxes increase after I buy?

When a property is sold in Florida, the county property appraiser reassesses it to just value (market value) in the year after the sale. If the prior owner held the property with homestead for many years and Save Our Homes capped their assessed value well below market, your first-year tax bill can be significantly higher than the prior owner's. On a $1.5M purchase where the prior owner's assessed value was $700,000, your first-year bill could be 70% to 100% higher than theirs. Budget for your actual cost, not the prior bill on the listing sheet.

Are there any tax advantages to buying on Longboat Key vs. nearby mainland?

Not specifically from a millage rate perspective. Town of Longboat Key millage adds to the county rate for all properties on the island. In some cases, properties in the unincorporated Sarasota or Manatee county areas adjacent to the island carry lower total millage because they are not in a municipality. The homestead exemption, Save Our Homes cap, and portability protections apply equally across the island and the mainland, so the long-term tax advantages are the same for primary residents wherever they buy in Florida.

Does a condo HOA fee include property taxes?

No. HOA or condo association fees cover operating costs, reserves, and common area maintenance, but they do not include your individual property tax liability. You pay property taxes separately, either through your mortgage escrow account or directly to the county tax collector. Some residents confuse the association fee with an all-in payment, but taxes are always billed individually to each property owner.
