title: Englewood FL Property Taxes
excerpt: Englewood FL Property Taxes, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

How much are property taxes in Englewood FL?

Property taxes in Englewood depend on which county your home is in. Both Charlotte County and Sarasota County have combined millage rates resulting in effective tax rates of approximately 1.0-1.2% of assessed value for homesteaded properties. On a $400,000 home with homestead exemption applied, annual taxes are typically $3,500-$4,400. Apply for homestead exemption by March 1 of the year following your purchase. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for property-specific guidance.

Which County Handles Property Taxes for Englewood FL?

Englewood spans two counties and your property tax bill is issued by whichever county your property is in. Charlotte County properties are assessed by the Charlotte County Property Appraiser at ccpao.com. Sarasota County properties are assessed by the Sarasota County Property Appraiser at sc-pa.com. Property tax bills are due by March 31 each year, with a 4% discount for payment in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, and 1% in February.

What Are the Millage Rates in Charlotte and Sarasota Counties?

Millage rates are the combined rates from the county general fund, school board, water management district, and any applicable special districts. They are set annually and can change. Always verify current millage rates with the county appraiser's office. The figures below represent approximate ranges based on recent tax years.

Taxing AuthorityCharlotte County (approx.)Sarasota County (approx.)
County general fund~5.5-6.5 mills~3.0-4.0 mills
School board~5.5-6.5 mills~5.5-6.5 mills
Water management district~0.2-0.5 mills~0.2-0.5 mills
Special districts (if any)Varies by areaVaries by area
Total approximate combined~17-20 mills~16-18 mills
Approximate effective rate (homesteaded)~1.0-1.2%~0.9-1.1%

Note: One mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. A $400,000 assessed value at 18 mills combined would have a gross tax bill of $7,200 before exemptions apply.

How Does the Florida Homestead Exemption Work?

The Florida homestead exemption is one of the most valuable tax benefits for primary-residence homeowners. It reduces the assessed value of your home by $50,000 for tax purposes: $25,000 applied to all taxing authorities, and an additional $25,000 applied to all except the school board millage.

Eligibility Requirements

  • The property must be your primary permanent residence as of January 1 of the tax year
  • You must apply by March 1 of the year in which you want the exemption to take effect
  • Charlotte County: apply at ccpao.com or in person at the Charlotte County Property Appraiser office
  • Sarasota County: apply at sc-pa.com or in person at the Sarasota County Property Appraiser office
  • Florida driver's license or ID with the property address is required
  • Vehicle registration must be updated to the property address
  • Missing the March 1 deadline means waiting until the following year

How Much Does Homestead Exemption Save?

On a property with a combined millage rate of 18 mills, the first $25,000 exemption saves approximately $450 per year and the second $25,000 (applied to all but the school board) saves an additional $300-$375 per year. Total typical savings: $700-$900 per year. The bigger benefit over time is the Save Our Homes assessment cap.

What Is Save Our Homes and Why Does It Matter?

Save Our Homes (SOH) is a Florida constitutional amendment limiting the annual increase in a homesteaded property's assessed value to 3% or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. Once you establish homestead exemption and the SOH cap takes effect (the year after your first full year of homestead), your assessed value cannot increase by more than 3% per year regardless of market value increases.

In a rapidly appreciating market like Florida experienced from 2020-2022, the SOH cap was extremely valuable. A homeowner who bought in 2018 at $300,000 and benefited from SOH might have had an assessed value of $325,000-$335,000 in 2022 while the market value reached $500,000+. Their tax bill reflected the capped assessed value, not the market value.

Portability for Sellers

When you sell a Florida home with homestead exemption and purchase another Florida home, you can "port" the accumulated SOH benefit to the new property (up to $500,000 in portable savings). If you have lived in your Englewood home for many years and have a large gap between assessed and market value, ask your accountant or real estate attorney about portability when you sell and buy again in Florida.

What Are Typical Property Tax Estimates in Englewood FL?

Market ValueEst. Taxable (after $50K exemption)Charlotte County (18 mills est.)Sarasota County (17 mills est.)
$250,000$200,000$3,600$3,400
$350,000$300,000$5,400$5,100
$450,000$400,000$7,200$6,800
$600,000$550,000$9,900$9,350
$900,000$850,000$15,300$14,450

These are estimates using approximate millage rates. Actual tax bills depend on your specific county, all applicable special district millages, and the property appraiser's assessed value. Verify with the county property appraiser before purchasing.

What About Non-Homestead Properties?

If you purchase in Englewood as a second home, investment property, or vacation residence (not your primary residence), you cannot claim homestead exemption or benefit from the Save Our Homes cap. Non-homestead properties are assessed at market value and can increase without the 3% annual cap. Florida does apply a 10% per year cap on assessed value increases for non-homestead properties, but this is far less protective than the homestead SOH cap. Many seasonal snowbird buyers are surprised that their second home does not qualify for homestead.

How Do I Appeal My Property Assessment?

If you believe your property's assessed value is too high, file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board (VAB) in your county. The deadline is typically 25 days after the TRIM Notice (Notice of Proposed Property Taxes) mails in August each year.

  • Charlotte County VAB: through the Charlotte County Clerk of Court
  • Sarasota County VAB: through the Sarasota County Clerk of Court
  • Gather comparable sales data supporting a lower value
  • A formal appraisal significantly strengthens your case
  • The filing fee is typically $15 per parcel
  • Many appeals succeed at the informal conference stage before a formal hearing

Frequently Asked Questions About Englewood FL Property Taxes

What are property taxes in Englewood FL?

Property taxes depend on your county (Charlotte or Sarasota) and the local millage rates. Effective rates for homesteaded properties are approximately 1.0-1.2% of assessed value. On a $400K assessed value after the homestead exemption ($350K taxable), annual taxes are roughly $3,400-$4,200 depending on county and special district overlays. Check current rates at ccpao.com (Charlotte) or sc-pa.com (Sarasota).

When is the homestead exemption application deadline in Florida?

March 1 of the tax year in which you want the exemption to apply. If you close on your Englewood home in January 2026, apply by March 1, 2026 for the 2026 tax year. If you miss the March 1 deadline, you must wait until the following year. Apply as soon as possible after closing.

Is Englewood FL property tax higher than Tampa?

Property tax rates in Englewood (Charlotte and Sarasota counties) are generally comparable to or slightly lower than Hillsborough County (Tampa area) effective rates, which typically run 1.1-1.3% for homesteaded properties. The most significant difference is often in how individual special districts affect the combined millage, which varies by exact address.

Can I get a property tax exemption as a veteran in Englewood FL?

Yes. Florida offers several veteran-related property tax exemptions. Veterans with a service-connected disability of 10% or more receive an additional $5,000 exemption. Veterans with a total service-connected disability (100%) may qualify for a full property tax exemption. Surviving spouses of qualifying veterans may also qualify. Apply at the county property appraiser's office with VA disability documentation.

What happens to my property taxes when I sell my Englewood home?

When you sell your homesteaded property, the Save Our Homes benefit stays with your assessed value history at that property. The new buyer's assessed value resets to market value in the year following their purchase, and they must apply for homestead exemption on their own. If you are buying another Florida property, portability allows you to transfer your accumulated SOH benefit to the new home.

excerpt: New Construction in Englewood FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Is there new construction in Englewood FL?

New construction in Englewood proper is very limited. The community is largely built out. Most new construction activity near Englewood is in Rotonda West (10-20 min), North Port (28-40 min), Wellen Park (30-45 min), and Port Charlotte (20-30 min). Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to navigate the new vs resale tradeoff in this market.

Why Is New Construction Limited in Englewood FL?

Englewood is a mature coastal community that developed primarily from the 1950s through the 1990s. Unlike rapidly growing areas of Pasco County, eastern Manatee County, or parts of Lee County, Englewood does not have large undeveloped parcels available for master-planned communities. The waterfront nature of much of the area, combined with Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve protections and dual-county boundaries, makes large-scale new residential development difficult.

What new construction exists in Englewood tends to be small in scale: infill construction on lots where older homes were demolished (particularly post-Hurricane Ian in flood-prone areas), occasional custom builds on scattered vacant lots, and small townhome or villa projects. If you are specifically seeking a brand-new home from a national production builder, you will need to look outside Englewood proper.

What New Construction Options Are Near Englewood FL?

Rotonda West (10-20 miles east of Englewood)

Rotonda West is a planned community in Charlotte County featuring golf courses, canal waterways, and residential development. While not as active as a decade ago, Rotonda West still has custom and semi-custom builder activity on remaining lots. Some areas of Rotonda have canal access via Rotonda River with Gulf boating potential. Custom builds in Rotonda typically run $350K-$650K for the structure on available lots. This is the closest new construction option to Englewood that maintains a similar coastal/canal community character.

North Port (28-40 miles northeast)

North Port in Sarasota County is one of the most active new construction markets in the state. D.R. Horton, Maronda Homes, Christopher Alan Homes, and other production builders are active throughout North Port's extensive parcel grid. North Port does not have natural Gulf access but provides Sarasota County school access and prices generally in the $290K-$450K range for production-built homes. It is the closest high-volume new construction option to Englewood.

Wellen Park (30-45 miles northeast)

Wellen Park (formerly West Villages) is a master-planned community at the North Port/Venice boundary. Multiple builders are active (Mattamy Homes, D.R. Horton, Lennar, Neal Communities, and others). Prices range from the high $300Ks to $700K+ depending on neighborhood and builder. Wellen Park has its own downtown district and CoolToday Park (Atlanta Braves spring training). Sarasota County schools apply. CDD fees apply to most Wellen Park homes, which add $1,500-$3,500+ per year to the tax bill.

Venice Area (18-25 miles north)

The Venice corridor has limited but active new construction primarily in Sarasota National, Venice Woodlands, and a few other communities. Neal Communities and Mattamy have been active in this area. Venice new construction typically runs $400K-$700K+. Sarasota County schools apply, which is a draw for families. Venice access to the Gulf via Venice Inlet is a lifestyle advantage.

Port Charlotte (13-20 miles east)

Port Charlotte has more active new construction than Englewood proper. National builders like D.R. Horton have active communities in Port Charlotte and neighboring areas in the $280K-$450K range. For buyers who want Charlotte County and a new home, Port Charlotte offers more options than Englewood. Direct Gulf access from Port Charlotte requires a boat trip via the Peace River and Charlotte Harbor, with the Gulf about 30-45 minutes by boat.

What Does New Construction in Coastal FL Actually Cost?

Wind Load Requirements

Building codes in coastal Florida require heavier structural standards than inland construction: reinforced roof attachments, impact-resistant windows and doors or storm shutters, and stronger concrete block wall construction. These requirements add $15,000-$40,000 to the build cost of a typical home compared to a similar structure in Central Florida. This is a real cost that shows up in builder base prices and in lot-to-completion custom build budgets.

Lot Premiums in Coastal Areas

In the rare cases where new construction is possible directly in Englewood, lot prices are a significant component. Waterfront or canal-access lots in Englewood command $150,000-$500,000+ for the raw land. Even inland infill lots in established neighborhoods run $60,000-$150,000 depending on location, services, and lot size.

Insurance Advantages of New Construction

New construction built to the current Florida Building Code will generally have lower homeowner's insurance costs than an equivalent older home. Current code requires hip roofs, reinforced roof-to-wall connections, and secondary water resistance measures that qualify for wind mitigation discounts. The insurance savings on a new construction home versus a pre-2000 older home can be $1,000-$3,000+ per year, which partially offsets the higher purchase price.

What Should I Know About Builder Contracts in Florida?

Builder Contracts Favor the Builder

Builder purchase agreements are drafted by the builder's attorneys and are not buyer-friendly by default. Watch for: large non-refundable earnest money deposits (often 10-20% once past the inspection period), price escalation clauses that allow the builder to raise price if material costs rise, and limited warranty terms. Have a Florida real estate attorney review any builder contract before signing.

Upgrades and Change Orders

Builders make significant margin on upgrades. The base price attracts buyers, but flooring, kitchen packages, bathroom fixtures, lot premiums, and structural options can add $30,000-$100,000+ to the final contract price. If the base specification meets your needs, resisting upgrades protects your budget. If you want a turnkey home, factor realistic upgrade costs into your comparison against resale options.

Use Your Own Agent

The onsite sales agent at a builder's model home works for the builder, not for you. Having Barrett represent you as your buyer's agent costs you nothing (the builder pays the commission) and gives you an advocate in contract negotiations and construction walk-throughs. Never walk into a builder's sales office without your agent registered first. Call (813) 733-7907 before visiting any model home in the area.

Quick Answer

Is Englewood FL a good place to invest in real estate?

Englewood FL offers investment opportunities in long-term rentals for inland properties and short-term rentals near Manasota Key and Englewood Beach. Gross yields on inland long-term rentals typically run 6-8%. STR revenue near the beach is higher but carries more risk (regulations, seasonal vacancy, coastal insurance costs). Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to evaluate a specific investment property.

What Investment Strategies Work in Englewood FL?

Englewood's investment market splits into two main strategies based on proximity to the beach: short-term rental (STR) near Manasota Key and Englewood Beach, and long-term rental for the inland market. A third strategy, buy-and-hold appreciation, is less reliable in a coastal community with hurricane exposure and insurance cost headwinds.

Long-Term Rental: Inland Englewood

Inland Englewood has a steady tenant base of year-round residents (healthcare workers, hospitality, retail, trades), retirees who prefer renting, and relocators in transition. Long-term rentals for 3BR/2BA inland homes in the $300K-$480K purchase price range typically generate $1,800-$2,500 per month depending on condition and location. This represents a gross yield of approximately 5.5-8% on purchase price. Net yield after taxes, insurance, and maintenance is typically 4-6%.

Short-Term Rental: Near Beach and Waterfront

Properties within a mile or two of Englewood Beach and Manasota Key have strong STR demand from November through April (peak winter season) and moderate demand in the fall. A well-managed two- or three-bedroom home near the beach can generate $35,000-$70,000+ per year in gross STR revenue depending on the platform, property quality, and management quality. However, STR management fees (20-30%), insurance, taxes, maintenance, and platform fees reduce net margin significantly. See the financial scenarios below.

Buy-and-Hold Appreciation

Englewood appreciated strongly from 2020 to 2022, as did virtually all Florida coastal markets. Since then, appreciation has been flat to slightly negative in many price segments. Betting on appreciation in a coastal community with hurricane exposure, elevated insurance costs, and broader coastal risk factors is not a conservative investment thesis. The stronger financial case is cash flow plus personal lifestyle use, not pure price appreciation.

Utilities (STR owner pays)-$3,600
Net Operating Income (NOI)~$7,700
Cap rate on $650K purchase~1.2%

STR gross revenue numbers look attractive but coastal insurance and management costs are substantial. A property generating $55K gross STR revenue in a strong year may net $7K-$15K after all operating expenses. At current coastal property prices, STR investing in Englewood is a lifestyle play, not a strong yield play at market prices. Distressed post-Ian properties acquired below market can improve the math but carry additional risk.

What Are the Key Risks for Englewood FL Real Estate Investors?

Coastal Insurance Cost Inflation

Florida homeowner's and flood insurance rates have increased significantly over the past five years and are not expected to reverse quickly. Several major carriers have reduced Florida exposure. Citizens Property Insurance has capacity limits and assessment risk. An investor's financial model must account for insurance costs that may increase meaningfully year over year. Running your numbers at today's insurance cost and assuming it stays flat is an optimistic underwriting assumption.

Hurricane Risk

Hurricane Ian (September 2022) demonstrated the catastrophic damage potential in this part of Florida. Any investment in coastal Englewood, Manasota Key, or canal-front properties carries real hurricane risk. Mandatory flood and wind coverage adds cost. Between-storm damage (roof leaks, storm surge from tropical storms, falling trees) is also a recurring operational cost for coastal properties that inland markets do not face to the same degree.

STR Regulation Risk

Charlotte County and Sarasota County both have the authority to regulate short-term rentals, including registration requirements, inspection requirements, and fee structures. While Florida state law limits counties from banning STRs outright (for properties that were operating before any ban), the regulatory environment can change. Research current STR regulations in the specific county before purchasing a property specifically for STR use.

Seasonal Vacancy

The Englewood STR market is highly seasonal. Peak occupancy is November through April. Summer months (June-September) are slower, and peak hurricane season (August-October) is the weakest booking period. Underwrite based on annual average occupancy (typically 50-65% for well-managed coastal properties in this area), not peak-season occupancy, for a realistic projection.

Englewood offers investment in long-term and short-term rentals, but gross yields at 2026 prices are modest after coastal insurance, taxes, and management costs. The best financial case is for buyers who also use the property personally, offsetting carrying costs with rental income while enjoying the lifestyle. Pure yield investors typically find better cap rates in inland Florida markets.

title: Waterfront Homes in Englewood FL
excerpt: Waterfront Homes in Englewood FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

What types of waterfront homes are available in Englewood FL?

Englewood offers five distinct waterfront categories: Gulf-front estates on Manasota Key ($1.5M to $5M+), bayfront homes on Manasota Key ($750K to $2M+), mainland Lemon Bay direct-access homes ($800K to $2.5M+), canal homes with Gulf access ($450K to $1.2M), and Lemon Bay view properties without water access ($350K to $650K). Hurricane Ian in September 2022 significantly impacted the inventory and pricing of Gulf-front and canal properties. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 749-4748 to tour available waterfront listings.

Englewood, Florida sits along Lemon Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, offering some of the most diverse waterfront real estate on Florida's Gulf Coast. The market ranges from modest canal homes to multi-million-dollar Gulf-front estates, with significant differences in flood risk, dock rights, and insurance costs depending on which water you front. This guide covers every waterfront category in the Englewood market with verified price ranges and practical buying considerations.

Barrett Henry is a Broker Associate with REMAX Collective and has helped buyers navigate Englewood's waterfront market. Call or text (813) 749-4748 for current listings.

What Types of Waterfront Are Available in Englewood FL?

Englewood waterfront falls into five categories, each with distinct characteristics, price ranges, and ownership considerations.

Gulf-Front Homes on Manasota Key

Manasota Key is a narrow barrier island accessible via two bridges, one from Englewood and one from Venice. Gulf-front properties on the west side of Manasota Key sit directly on the Gulf of Mexico with private beach access. These are the most valuable and most exposed properties in the Englewood area.

Gulf-front homes on Manasota Key carry FEMA Flood Zone VE designations, meaning they are in the coastal high-hazard area where wave action during storms is expected. Flood insurance for VE-designated properties typically runs $5,000 to $20,000 annually or more depending on elevation and structure type. After Hurricane Ian struck in September 2022, several Gulf-front properties on Manasota Key sustained major damage, and some lots were cleared entirely, creating both teardown opportunities and significantly elevated rebuild costs.

Waterfront TypePrice RangeFlood ZoneDock PermittedKey Consideration
Gulf-front (Manasota Key)$1.5M to $5M+Zone VETypically noWave action risk; VE flood insurance
Bayfront (Manasota Key)$750K to $2M+Zone AE or VESometimes, permits requiredLemon Bay Aquatic Preserve restrictions
Mainland Lemon Bay direct$800K to $2.5M+Zone AEOften yes, permits requiredWide bay views; boating access
Canal homes with Gulf access$450K to $1.2MZone AEYes, most have existing docksWater depth varies; check at low tide
Lemon Bay view (no water access)$350K to $650KZone X or AENoViews without flood exposure

Bayfront Homes on Manasota Key

The east side of Manasota Key faces Lemon Bay rather than the Gulf of Mexico. Bayfront properties offer protected water, calmer conditions, and generally lower flood insurance costs than Gulf-front homes, though many still carry Zone AE or Zone VE designations. Boating access from bayfront properties is subject to Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve regulations (discussed below), which affect dock permitting and seagrass disturbance rules.

Bayfront Manasota Key homes typically list between $750,000 and $2,000,000+ depending on lot size, dock situation, and condition. Properties with existing permitted docks command a premium over those without.

Mainland Lemon Bay Direct-Access Homes

Moving off Manasota Key to the Englewood mainland, Lemon Bay direct-access properties sit on the east shore of the bay in areas such as Englewood Isles and along Englewood Road. These homes offer wide bay views, boating access, and generally larger lot sizes than island properties. Many include existing docks or have grandfathered dock rights.

Mainland Lemon Bay homes typically range from $800,000 to $2,500,000 depending on lot size, dock condition, and proximity to the Intracoastal Waterway. Flood zones on the mainland bay side are generally Zone AE, which carries lower flood insurance premiums than Zone VE but still requires mandatory flood insurance with federally backed mortgages.

Canal Homes with Gulf Access

The most numerous waterfront properties in Englewood are canal homes, primarily located in communities such as Englewood Isles, Overbrook Gardens, and Oakland Hills. These homes sit on finger canals that connect to Lemon Bay and from there to the Gulf of Mexico via markers through the Intracoastal Waterway.

Canal homes are the entry point to Englewood boating waterfront, with prices ranging from approximately $450,000 to $1,200,000. Key due diligence items include water depth at the dock (especially at mean low water), bridge clearances between the canal and open water, and whether the existing dock is permitted. Canal lots typically allow dock construction subject to Charlotte County or Sarasota County permitting and Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve rules.

Lemon Bay View Properties

Not every property marketed as "waterfront" or "water view" in Englewood sits on the water. A significant number of listings offer Lemon Bay views from elevated positions or across public lands without direct water access or dock rights. These properties benefit from the scenery at lower prices and often lower flood risk, as many carry Zone X designations meaning they are outside the base flood elevation area.

View properties typically list between $350,000 and $650,000, significantly below true waterfront prices, and carry standard homeowner's insurance without mandatory flood insurance requirements in many cases. For buyers who want the water atmosphere without the insurance burden, view properties represent a practical middle ground.

What Is the Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve and Why Does It Matter?

Lemon Bay was designated an Outstanding Florida Water and an Aquatic Preserve by the State of Florida, which imposes specific restrictions on dock construction, boat mooring, and activities that could disturb seagrass beds. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) administers these restrictions alongside Charlotte County and Sarasota County permitting.

Buyers considering waterfront properties on Lemon Bay, including Manasota Key bayfront and mainland Englewood properties, should verify:

  • Whether an existing dock is permitted or was built without permits
  • Whether the dock extends into or over seagrass beds, which can trigger mandatory removal orders
  • The maximum dock length and width allowed for the specific parcel
  • Whether a mooring field or boat lift is allowed given the water depth and preserve rules
  • Whether any prior dock permits have expired or lapsed

Unpermitted docks or docks built over seagrass are a material risk in real estate transactions on Lemon Bay. Sellers are required to disclose known permit issues, but buyers should independently verify dock status through Charlotte County (ccpao.com) or Sarasota County (sc-pa.com) permit records. An inspection by a marine contractor familiar with Lemon Bay regulations is strongly recommended before closing on any property with an existing dock.

New dock construction on Lemon Bay typically requires a Joint Coastal Permit through FDEP and Charlotte or Sarasota County approval. Processing times can range from several months to over a year. Budget $15,000 to $60,000+ for new dock construction depending on length, materials, and permit complexity.

What Happened to Englewood Waterfront After Hurricane Ian?

Hurricane Ian made landfall near Fort Myers Beach on September 28, 2022, as a Category 4 storm. Although the primary landfall was south of Englewood, the storm surge and winds caused significant damage to waterfront properties throughout Charlotte County and Sarasota County, including Englewood, Manasota Key, and the surrounding area.

The impacts relevant to current waterfront buyers include:

  • Multiple Gulf-front structures on Manasota Key were destroyed or severely damaged, with some lots cleared entirely
  • Canal docks and seawalls throughout Englewood sustained damage, with many repaired by 2023 and 2024 but some still unresolved
  • Flood insurance claims from Ian triggered policy reassessments, and some private insurers exited the Florida market following the storm
  • FEMA flood map remapping discussions accelerated post-Ian, potentially changing zone designations for some Englewood properties
  • Construction costs for waterfront rebuilds remain elevated due to post-storm demand on contractors and materials

For buyers today, Hurricane Ian history is directly relevant to due diligence. Sellers of waterfront properties are required to disclose known storm damage. Buyers should order a wind mitigation inspection and review the property's claim history through the Florida Comprehensive Loss Underwriting Exchange (CLUE) report. Properties with major Ian damage repairs should have documentation showing permitted repairs and code compliance.

One practical benefit of post-Ian turnover is that some rebuilt properties now meet or exceed current Florida Building Code wind and flood standards, which can result in lower insurance premiums compared to older unrenovated structures. Ask the listing agent for documentation on any post-Ian repairs.

What Does a Dock Add to an Englewood Waterfront Home's Value?

A functional permitted dock adds measurable value to an Englewood waterfront property, with the premium depending on water depth, access to open water, dock features such as a lift or covered slip, and permit status.

Dock Value and Cost Ranges in Englewood

According to appraisers familiar with the Charlotte County and Sarasota County markets, a well-maintained permitted dock in Englewood adds roughly $30,000 to $80,000 in market value depending on size and features. A dock with a boat lift adds more than a fixed dock without one. Properties with Gulf-access deep-water docks command the highest premiums.

Dock FeatureTypical Added ValueNew Construction Cost
Basic fixed dock, no lift$20,000 to $40,000$15,000 to $30,000
Dock with single boat lift$40,000 to $65,000$30,000 to $50,000
Covered slip with lift$55,000 to $85,000$45,000 to $80,000
Deep-water Gulf-access dock$60,000 to $100,000+$50,000 to $100,000+
Unpermitted dock$0 to negativeLiability to remove or permit

What to Check Before Paying a Dock Premium

Before paying a premium for a dock, verify the following directly rather than relying on listing descriptions:

  • Pull the dock permit from Charlotte County or Sarasota County permit records
  • Confirm water depth at mean low water alongside the dock (not just at the dock face)
  • Measure the bridge clearance on the route to open water if you plan to keep a center console or sailboat
  • Inspect the dock decking, pilings, and any boat lift cables or bunks for post-hurricane or general wear
  • Confirm the lift capacity matches the size of boat you intend to keep

Canal lots without existing docks can usually build one subject to Lemon Bay Aquatic Preserve rules and county permitting. Factor dock construction cost and timeline into your offer price and closing timeline if building a new dock is part of your plan.

Where to Search for Englewood Waterfront Homes

Englewood waterfront listings are distributed across multiple communities. The highest concentration of canal homes is in Englewood Isles, Overbrook Gardens, and Oakland Hills, all within a few miles of Manasota Key. Gulf-front and bayfront properties are concentrated on Manasota Key itself, accessed via Beach Road (CR 775).

For broader context on the Englewood market, see the Englewood FL Real Estate Guide covering median prices, market trends, and neighborhood comparisons. Buyers focused on investment potential should review the Englewood FL Investment Property Guide. For flood zone information specific to your target property, see the Englewood FL Flood Zone Guide.

title: Englewood FL Flood Zones Guide
excerpt: Englewood FL Flood Zones Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

What flood zones exist in Englewood FL and what do they mean for buyers?

Englewood FL properties fall into three primary FEMA flood zone categories: Zone VE (coastal high-hazard, highest risk, mandatory flood insurance), Zone AE (100-year floodplain, mandatory flood insurance with federally backed mortgages), and Zone X (minimal flood risk, flood insurance optional). Hurricane Ian in September 2022 demonstrated that these designations reflect real risk. Check any specific property at msc.fema.gov using the address. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 749-4748 to discuss flood zone implications before making an offer.

Englewood, Florida spans parts of Charlotte County and Sarasota County, and both counties include significant areas within FEMA-designated flood zones. Understanding the flood zone designation for any specific property is one of the most important due diligence steps for buyers, because it determines mandatory flood insurance requirements, insurance costs, and long-term resale exposure. This guide explains the main flood zones in Englewood, what each means for buyers, and how to verify the designation for any property you are considering.

Barrett Henry is a Broker Associate with REMAX Collective. Call or text (813) 749-4748 for guidance on evaluating flood risk before buying in Englewood.

What Are the FEMA Flood Zones in Englewood FL?

FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) designates flood zones through its National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) using Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). The key zones applicable to Englewood properties are:

Flood ZoneRisk LevelFlood InsuranceWhere in EnglewoodTypical Annual Premium
Zone VECoastal high-hazard (wave action expected)Mandatory (federally backed loans)Gulf-front Manasota Key$5,000 to $20,000+
Zone AE100-year floodplain (1% annual chance)Mandatory (federally backed loans)Lemon Bay frontage, canal communities, low-lying mainland$2,000 to $8,000+
Zone X (shaded)0.2% annual chance flood (500-year)OptionalSlightly elevated inland areas$400 to $1,000
Zone X (unshaded)Minimal flood riskOptionalHigher inland areas$400 to $700
Zone DUndetermined riskRecommendedRare in EnglewoodVaries

Note: Premium ranges above are generalizations based on publicly available NFIP data. Actual premiums depend on the specific property's elevation certificate, building characteristics, and the coverage amount selected. Private flood insurance is also available and may be priced differently from NFIP policies. Consult a licensed Florida flood insurance specialist for quotes on any specific property.

What Is Zone VE and Why Is It the Highest Risk?

Zone VE stands for "coastal high-hazard area with wave velocity." Properties in Zone VE are in the highest FEMA risk category because these areas experience not only flooding but also breaking wave action during major storm events. In Englewood, Zone VE primarily applies to Gulf-front properties on Manasota Key.

The "V" designation means that FEMA has determined breaking waves of at least 3 feet in height are expected during a 100-year storm event. Structures in Zone VE must be built on open foundations (pilings or piers) rather than closed foundations, and they must be elevated so that the lowest floor is at or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) plus the wave height. These construction requirements affect both new builds and post-damage rebuilds.

Zone VE Flood Insurance Requirements

Flood insurance is mandatory for all federally backed mortgages (conventional conforming, FHA, VA) on properties in Zone VE. NFIP policies for Zone VE properties are typically the most expensive in the program, often ranging from $5,000 to $20,000+ annually for a residential structure. Private flood insurance is available for Zone VE properties and may offer competitive rates in some cases.

Properties in Zone VE that were built before FEMA flood maps were initially adopted for the area are classified as "pre-FIRM" structures. Pre-FIRM Zone VE properties often face higher NFIP premiums because their construction pre-dates modern elevation and foundation requirements.

Hurricane Ian and Zone VE Damage

Hurricane Ian's September 2022 landfall near Fort Myers Beach sent significant storm surge and wave action north into Charlotte County and Sarasota County coastal areas, including Manasota Key. Multiple Zone VE structures on Manasota Key sustained major damage or were destroyed, validating the zone designation as an accurate predictor of risk. Buyers considering Zone VE properties today should request documentation showing that any post-Ian construction or repair was permitted and meets current Florida Building Code requirements.

What Is Zone AE and Where Does It Appear in Englewood?

Zone AE is the most common high-risk flood zone in Englewood. It covers the 100-year floodplain, meaning there is a 1 percent annual probability of flooding reaching the Base Flood Elevation in any given year. Over a 30-year mortgage, a property in Zone AE has roughly a 26 percent chance of flooding at least once.

Zone AE appears throughout Englewood in the following types of areas:

  • Properties fronting Lemon Bay on the mainland side of Englewood
  • Canal communities including Englewood Isles, Overbrook Gardens, and similar finger-canal developments
  • Low-lying inland areas near drainage channels and wetlands
  • Properties near Gottfried Creek and other tidal waterways
  • Portions of Manasota Key not classified as Zone VE

Zone AE Flood Insurance Costs in Englewood

NFIP flood insurance for Zone AE properties in Englewood typically ranges from $2,000 to $8,000+ annually, depending on the elevation certificate, building type, coverage amount, and whether the property is pre-FIRM or post-FIRM. Properties with elevation certificates showing the lowest floor elevated above the BFE qualify for lower premiums. Each foot of elevation above BFE generally reduces the NFIP premium substantially.

FEMA introduced Risk Rating 2.0 in October 2021, replacing the old zone-based flat-rate system with individual property risk assessments. Under Risk Rating 2.0, properties with the same Zone AE designation can have significantly different premiums depending on distance from water, foundation type, and first-floor elevation relative to the property's specific flood frequency.

Elevation Certificates in Zone AE

An elevation certificate is a document prepared by a licensed surveyor, engineer, or architect that records the elevation of the lowest floor relative to the Base Flood Elevation. For Zone AE properties, having an elevation certificate can significantly reduce flood insurance costs if the structure is elevated above BFE. Sellers should provide existing elevation certificates; if none exists, buyers can order one during the inspection period for approximately $400 to $700 from a licensed Florida surveyor.

What Is the Difference Between Zone X and Zone AE in Englewood?

The practical difference between Zone X and Zone AE for an Englewood buyer is significant in terms of insurance requirements and costs.

FactorZone AEZone X (Shaded)Zone X (Unshaded)
Flood risk level100-year floodplain500-year floodplainMinimal flood risk
Flood insurance required?Yes (federally backed loans)No (recommended)No (optional)
Typical annual premium$2,000 to $8,000+$400 to $1,000$400 to $700
Elevation certificate needed?Recommended to lower premiumNot typically requiredNot required
Post-Ian risk demonstrated?Yes (canal and bay areas)Lower exposureLowest exposure
Common Englewood locationsLemon Bay frontage, canal homesSlightly elevated inland areasHigher inland neighborhoods

Many buyers ask whether they should purchase flood insurance for a Zone X property even though it is not required. According to FEMA, approximately 20 to 25 percent of all NFIP flood insurance claims come from properties outside high-risk flood zones. For a Zone X property in Englewood, the optional flood insurance cost of $400 to $700 annually may be worthwhile given Florida's storm history. This is a personal risk management decision.

How Did Hurricane Ian Demonstrate Englewood Flood Risk?

Hurricane Ian is the most significant real-world flood event to affect Englewood in recent history. The storm made landfall near Fort Myers Beach on September 28, 2022, as a Category 4 hurricane, producing a storm surge of 12 to 18 feet at the primary landfall location and sending water north and east into Charlotte County.

In the Englewood area, Hurricane Ian produced:

  • Storm surge flooding in canal communities and along Lemon Bay frontage (Zone AE areas)
  • Wave and surge damage on Manasota Key Gulf-front properties (Zone VE areas)
  • Flooding of some Zone X areas that had not historically flooded in prior storms
  • Wind damage to structures throughout the area regardless of flood zone
  • A significant volume of NFIP and private flood insurance claims from Charlotte and Sarasota Counties

The Hurricane Ian experience reinforced several lessons for Englewood buyers. First, storm surge does not respect Zone X boundaries when a major hurricane tracks close to the area. Second, elevation above BFE is protective but not absolute protection in extreme events. Third, flood insurance should be evaluated on the basis of probability and cost relative to potential loss, not merely whether it is legally required.

Post-Ian, some private insurers reduced their Florida exposure or raised premiums significantly. The Florida Citizens Property Insurance Corporation absorbed some of this market, and the state legislature passed reforms intended to stabilize the insurance market in 2022 and 2023. Flood insurance availability and cost in Englewood continue to evolve. Buyers should obtain current quotes from multiple sources during the due diligence period rather than relying on prior-year premium estimates.

How Do I Check the Flood Zone for an Englewood Property?

Checking the FEMA flood zone for any specific Englewood address is a four-step process:

  • Step 1: Go to msc.fema.gov. This is FEMA's official Map Service Center where all current Flood Insurance Rate Maps are publicly accessible.
  • Step 2: Enter the property address. Use the address search tool to locate the property on the interactive FIRM map.
  • Step 3: Identify the flood zone polygon. The map will display the flood zone designation for the specific parcel. Note whether the property is in Zone VE, Zone AE, Zone X shaded, or Zone X unshaded.
  • Step 4: Check the effective date of the FIRM panel. Charlotte County and Sarasota County FIRMs have been updated at different times. Confirm you are looking at the current effective map, not a preliminary or outdated panel.

Charlotte County vs Sarasota County Flood Maps

Englewood straddles the Charlotte County and Sarasota County line. Properties east of the county line are in Charlotte County; properties west (including much of Manasota Key) may be in Sarasota County. The two counties have separate FIRM panels and sometimes different map effective dates. When searching msc.fema.gov, confirm which county's map is displayed for the property you are researching.

For Charlotte County property assessments and permit records, visit ccpao.com. For Sarasota County, visit sc-pa.com. Permit records from both counties can help verify whether an existing home was built to the flood zone requirements in effect at the time of construction.

Should I Order an Elevation Certificate Before Closing?

For any property in Zone AE or Zone VE, ordering an elevation certificate before closing is strongly recommended. The elevation certificate tells you exactly how the structure's lowest floor compares to the Base Flood Elevation, which directly determines flood insurance cost under NFIP. If the seller has an existing elevation certificate, request it early in the transaction. If not, budget approximately $400 to $700 and allow one to two weeks for a licensed Florida surveyor to complete one during the inspection period.

title: Best Neighborhoods in Englewood FL
excerpt: Best Neighborhoods in Englewood FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

The best neighborhoods in Englewood FL depend entirely on your budget and lifestyle. Manasota Key delivers Gulf-front estate living from $800,000 to $5 million. Lemon Bay-front communities offer dock access from $500,000 to $1.5 million. Dearborn Street area neighborhoods give walkable access to Englewood's arts district. Inland subdivisions on the Charlotte County side offer the most affordable entry at $300,000 to $480,000.

Englewood's geographic split across two counties, its mix of Intracoastal access and Gulf-front barrier island, and its range from affordable inland subdivisions to multi-million-dollar estate properties mean there is no single "best" neighborhood. It depends on what you are buying for. I have helped buyers find the right fit across all of these areas.

Manasota Key: Gulf-Front Estate Living

Manasota Key is a narrow barrier island accessible from Englewood via Manasota Beach Road. The island is almost entirely residential, with properties on the Gulf side and on Lemon Bay to the east. Unlike many Florida barrier islands, Manasota Key has resisted intensive commercial development, giving it a quieter character than Siesta Key or Anna Maria Island.

FactorDetail
Price Range$800K-$5M+ depending on Gulf-front vs. bay-side and lot size
AccessSingle bridge from mainland; traffic can back up during peak season
Flood ZoneZone AE and VE; flood insurance mandatory and expensive
AmenitiesManasota Beach County Park; Stump Pass Beach State Park at southern tip
Who It SuitsEstate buyers; second-home buyers; buyers who want true waterfront privacy

Lemon Bay Front Communities

Lemon Bay is the protected estuary that separates Englewood from Manasota Key. Properties along Lemon Bay offer dock access to the Intracoastal Waterway, typically at lower prices than Manasota Key Gulf-front homes. Boat access to the Gulf is available through Stump Pass at the southern end of Manasota Key.

The Lemon Bay area includes a mix of older bungalows, mid-century homes, and some more contemporary construction. Many lots are narrow by modern standards. Flood risk is significant, and seawall inspection is an important part of due diligence on any Lemon Bay-front property.

FactorDetail
Price Range$500K-$1.5M for direct waterfront; $350K-$600K for water-view or near-water
Dock AccessMost lots have docks; verify permits and condition
Flood ZoneZone AE typical; flood insurance required with federally backed mortgages
Water DepthVerify depth for your vessel; some areas have limited draft at low tide

Dearborn Street Area: Walkable Englewood Core

Dearborn Street is Englewood's main arts and dining corridor, lined with galleries, restaurants, boutiques, and seasonal farmers markets. Properties within walking or biking distance of Dearborn Street offer the closest thing to walkability that Englewood has to offer. Homes in this area tend to be older, with a mix of Florida cottage-style and ranch-style construction.

This area appeals to buyers who want community character and the ability to walk to dinner or the weekly market without getting in a car. Prices here are typically mid-range for Englewood, roughly $350,000 to $550,000 for single-family homes depending on size and condition.

Inland Subdivisions: Charlotte County Side

The majority of Englewood's population lives in inland subdivisions on the Charlotte County side. These neighborhoods offer quiet residential character, established landscaping, and the most affordable pricing in the Englewood market. Many of these communities have no HOA or low-fee deed restrictions.

FactorDetail
Price Range$300K-$480K for 3BR/2BA homes in good condition
Build EraLargely 1970s-1990s; renovated kitchens and bathrooms common
Flood ZoneGenerally Zone X; lower flood insurance costs
HOAMinimal or none in many communities

excerpt: Moving to Englewood FL: What to Know, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Moving to Englewood FL means choosing Gulf Coast living in a quieter, retirement-oriented community spanning Charlotte and Sarasota counties. The strongest arguments for Englewood: beach access on Manasota Key, Lemon Bay boating, Dearborn Street arts scene, and prices noticeably below Sarasota. Key things to plan around: no major hospital in Englewood (nearest is 20-30 min), limited job market, high insurance costs for waterfront properties, and no Costco or Target within 20 miles.

Moving to Englewood is a lifestyle decision. Almost no one relocates here for a local job. The buyers who move here and stay are people who planned carefully around the trade-offs: they have healthcare sorted out, they enjoy outdoor recreation, and they are not surprised by the insurance costs. Here is what I consistently tell buyers thinking about this community.

Englewood FL Housing Overview

Property TypePrice RangeNotes

Updated 3-4BR SFR$400K-$600KPost-2000 builds; newer mechanicals
Lemon Bay-front$500K-$1.5MDock access; Zone AE; significant flood insurance costs
Manasota Key$800K-$5M+Gulf-front barrier island; highest premium and risk

Utilities in Englewood FL

Electric: Florida Power and Light (FPL) serves most of the Englewood area. Charlotte County Electric Cooperative serves some rural areas. Call before purchase to confirm provider and estimated costs.

Water and Sewer: Charlotte County Utilities provides water and sewer for most of the Charlotte County side of Englewood. Some older or more rural parcels have well and septic. Sarasota County utilities serve the Sarasota County portion. Verify water/sewer status on any specific property as part of your inspection process.

Internet: Spectrum cable internet is the primary provider. Frontier Fiber serves some areas. Starlink works well in Englewood and is a good backup or primary option for rural parcels.

Garbage: Charlotte County Waste and Recycling manages collection on the Charlotte side. Sarasota County handles the Sarasota side.

Healthcare Near Englewood FL

Englewood does not have a major hospital within city limits. The closest facilities are Fawcett Memorial Hospital (HCA Healthcare) in Port Charlotte, approximately 20 to 25 miles east, and Sarasota Memorial Hospital Venice campus, approximately 18 to 22 miles north. For complex procedures and specialty care, Sarasota Memorial Hospital main campus in Sarasota is about 35 to 40 miles north. Tampa Bay hospitals are 90-plus minutes away and typically the destination for higher-acuity specialty care.

If regular medical care is a priority, verify your specific specialist and primary care provider location before committing to Englewood. Most residents manage routine care locally but plan ahead for specialty visits.

Shopping and Everyday Life in Englewood FL

Publix is on Placida Road. Winn-Dixie and other options are available. The Dearborn Street corridor has independent restaurants, galleries, and seasonal specialty shops. For big-box stores including Costco, Target, Lowe's, and Home Depot, Port Charlotte is the primary destination at roughly 20 miles east.

Englewood has a farmers market and art festivals that are well-attended during the winter season (November through April). The community has a strong seasonal character: noticeably more active from November through April when snowbirds are present, quieter during summer.

Insurance: The Cost Most Buyers Underestimate

Homeowners insurance in coastal Florida requires careful budgeting. For Englewood, inland Zone X homes typically run $4,000 to $8,000 per year for homeowners insurance depending on construction type, roof age, and coverage level. Waterfront homes in Zone AE can run $8,000 to $20,000 or more annually when you add mandatory flood insurance on top of homeowners coverage.

Always request the seller's current insurance declarations page during your inspection period. For any coastal or Lemon Bay-adjacent property, get flood insurance quotes before submitting an offer. Insurance costs are non-negotiable obligations that directly affect your monthly carrying cost.

Who Moves to Englewood FL

The Englewood buyer profile is heavily weighted toward retirees and people planning retirement within a few years, second-home buyers seeking Gulf Coast access, remote workers who can work from anywhere and prioritize lifestyle over urban amenities, and buyers priced out of comparable Sarasota County properties who find Englewood delivers similar outdoor recreation at lower cost. Young families with school-age children are a smaller segment of the market.

title: Things to Do in Englewood FL
excerpt: Things to Do in Englewood FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Englewood FL offers Englewood Beach on Manasota Key, Lemon Bay kayaking and fishing, scalloping in Charlotte County waters, the Dearborn Street arts district, Stump Pass Beach State Park, Indian Mound Park, and easy day trips to Boca Grande and Venice. The outdoor recreation calendar is strongest October through April, with scalloping season adding July through September summer activity.

Englewood is fundamentally an outdoors community. The buyers who come here and stay are the ones who show up in August for scalloping, spend winter mornings kayaking Lemon Bay, and know which Dearborn Street restaurant opens for lunch on Tuesdays. Here is an honest inventory of what the community has to offer.

Englewood Beach and Manasota Key

Englewood Beach is on Manasota Key, accessible via Manasota Beach Road across the Lemon Bay bridge. The beach at Chadwick Park (the county park at the main beach access) has parking, restrooms, picnic areas, and a modest amount of food and beverage nearby. The Gulf here is typically calm compared to more exposed Gulf beaches, making it particularly good for swimming and paddleboarding.

Blind Pass Beach is on the northern end of Manasota Key near the Sarasota County line. Stump Pass Beach State Park anchors the southern end and is one of the best preserved stretches of undeveloped barrier island on Florida's Gulf Coast. Stump Pass State Park charges a day-use fee and offers shelling, swimming, nature trails, and kayak launch access.

Lemon Bay: Kayaking, Fishing, and Boating

Lemon Bay is a protected estuary and part of Florida's Intracoastal Waterway running between the Englewood mainland and Manasota Key. It is excellent for kayaking, paddleboarding, and shallow-draft fishing. The bay's grassy flats support redfish, snook, and sea trout. The protected water makes it accessible for beginners and families even when Gulf conditions are rough.

For powerboat access to the Gulf, Stump Pass at the southern end of Manasota Key is the primary inlet. Pass the bridge clearances carefully if trailering a larger vessel. Several boat ramps and marinas serve the Englewood area.

Scalloping Season in Charlotte County Waters

Charlotte County waters near Englewood and Gasparilla Island are open for recreational bay scallop harvesting during Florida's annual scallop season. The FWC typically opens Charlotte County waters for scalloping in July with the season running through September, but exact open dates are set annually. Verify the current season at myfwc.com before planning a trip.

To scallop, you need a valid Florida saltwater fishing license, a mask and snorkel, fins, and a mesh bag. The legal limit is two gallons of whole scallops or one pint of cleaned scallop meat per person, and 10 gallons whole or one half gallon cleaned per vessel. Scalloping is a family-friendly activity in shallow, calm bay waters.

Dearborn Street Arts and Dining

Dearborn Street is Englewood's main commercial corridor with a distinctly artsy character. The street hosts galleries, gift shops, restaurants, and the Englewood Farmers Market (Saturday mornings during season). The area is most vibrant from November through April when seasonal residents are in town.

Restaurants along Dearborn Street lean toward Florida casual, with seafood, sandwiches, and local favorites. The arts community has regular gallery walks and events. Dearborn Street is the social center of Englewood proper and worth visiting on a Saturday morning during season to get a feel for the community character.

Indian Mound Park and Nature Activities

Indian Mound Park in Englewood sits on Lemon Bay and provides a kayak launch, bay access, picnic areas, and the historic Paulson Indian Mound, a Calusa Indian mound dating back approximately 1,500 years. The park is a local favorite for kayakers, birders, and those wanting a quiet bay access point without the crowds of the main beach.

Birding is strong throughout the Lemon Bay area. Great blue herons, roseate spoonbills, ospreys, and various shorebird species are regularly visible from kayaks and along bay-front properties. Manatees are frequently spotted in Lemon Bay, particularly near seagrass beds and warmer water outflows.

Englewood is known for Englewood Beach on Manasota Key, Lemon Bay waterway access, the Dearborn Street arts district, scalloping season in Charlotte County waters, and proximity to Stump Pass Beach State Park. The area has a strong fishing, boating, and beach lifestyle culture.

Is there a beach in Englewood FL?

Yes. Englewood Beach is on Manasota Key accessible via Manasota Beach Road. There is also Blind Pass Beach and Stump Pass Beach State Park at the southern end of Manasota Key. Caspersen Beach in nearby Venice (15 miles north) is famous for shark tooth hunting.

Can you scallop in Englewood FL?

Yes, Charlotte County waters near Englewood are open for recreational scalloping during the annual Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) season. The season typically runs July through September with specific open dates set annually by FWC. Snorkeling equipment, a mesh bag, and a valid Florida saltwater fishing license are required. Check FWC for current season dates before heading out.

Dearborn Street is Englewood's historic commercial corridor and arts district. It features independent galleries, gift shops, restaurants, and seasonal events including the weekly farmers market. Dearborn Street is the social heart of Englewood, particularly active during the winter season from November through April.

How far is Boca Grande from Englewood FL?

Boca Grande on Gasparilla Island is approximately 20 to 25 miles south of Englewood. The drive via SR-775 and SR-771 takes 30 to 40 minutes. Boca Grande is famous for tarpon fishing, a preserved old-Florida downtown, and some of the best Gulf beaches in Southwest Florida. It is a popular day trip from Englewood.

excerpt: Osprey FL homes for sale guide: price ranges, neighborhoods (The Oaks, Casey Key), buyer checklist, and 2026 market data. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL is a small upscale Sarasota County community between Sarasota and Venice with a median listing price around $792,000 as of 2026. Homes range from $450K for inland single-family to $7M+ for Casey Key Gulf-front estates. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

What Are Home Prices Like in Osprey, FL?

The Osprey market skews luxury. According to Movoto and Redfin data, the median listing price in Osprey was approximately $792,000 in April 2026, with a median price per square foot of $335. That said, actual sale prices have run closer to $650,000 as sellers have made concessions in a softening market. Prices are down roughly 6-14% from the 2022-2023 peak, and homes are sitting an average of 85 days before going under contract.

The wide price range in Osprey reflects two very different market segments: the coastal luxury segment (Casey Key, The Oaks Bayside) where $2M-$7M+ is routine, and the inland/Intracoastal-adjacent segment where $450K-$900K buys a comfortable Sarasota County home.

Approximate 2026 figures. Always verify current data with a local agent.

What Neighborhoods Should Osprey Buyers Consider?

Osprey is an unincorporated Sarasota County community spanning roughly the 34229 ZIP code. Unlike a master-planned city with dozens of developments, Osprey has a handful of distinct communities worth knowing.

The Oaks, Osprey's Premier Country Club

The Oaks sits on approximately 1,000 acres of former Palmer family land overlooking Little Sarasota Bay on US-41. It is a private, gated golf and country club community with two championship golf courses, a large clubhouse, tennis, and resort amenities. Three distinct gated neighborhoods share the club:

  • Oaks Bayside: 133-197 home sites on 200 acres with direct Little Sarasota Bay frontage. Private docking facilities. Prices $1.5M-$7M+ on 0.33-1.5+ acre lots.
  • Oaks Clubside: Single-family homes adjacent to the golf courses, $850K-$2.5M. Larger lots, mature landscaping.
  • Oaks Preserve: A mix of condos, villas, and smaller single-family homes. More accessible price point at $500K-$1.2M. Maintenance-free options available.

Club membership is required for residents and is separate from HOA dues. Buyers should factor in both when evaluating total cost of ownership.

Casey Key, Gulf-Front Barrier Island

Casey Key Road runs north-south along a narrow barrier island off Osprey and Nokomis. It is one of Sarasota County's most private and sought-after addresses. Properties range from older Florida cottages to custom-built Gulf-to-Bay estates. With Gulf-front lots and direct water access, prices routinely exceed $3M-$10M+. There is no through traffic on Casey Key Road, which keeps the street quiet and residents private.

Edgewater at Hidden Bay

Edgewater at Hidden Bay is a boutique gated community built on 12 resort-style acres on the edge of Little Sarasota Bay in Osprey. Homes are newer construction with bay views, resort-style amenities, and a marina. Prices range from approximately $900K to $2.5M+. The community suits buyers who want new or near-new construction with waterfront access without the mandatory country club membership of The Oaks.

Other Osprey Communities

Beyond those three anchors, Osprey has established residential neighborhoods including Sorrento East, Country Club Estates, and Oakwood Manor, inland single-family communities from the 1970s-1990s where $450K-$750K buys a comfortable home on a larger lot. These neighborhoods are popular with buyers who value Sarasota County schools and location without the club fees of The Oaks.

What Should Osprey Buyers Know Before Making an Offer?

Flood Insurance Is a Real Factor

Osprey's coastal and bayfront properties often fall in FEMA flood zones AE or VE, requiring mandatory flood insurance for federally-backed mortgages. Even Zone X properties near Osprey Creek or Little Sarasota Bay may be re-mapped over time. Always pull the FEMA flood map at msc.fema.gov before making an offer, and request flood insurance quotes before removing contingencies. Annual flood premiums for coastal Sarasota County homes can run $3,000-$10,000+ for Zone AE properties.

HOA, CDD, and Club Membership Fees

Many Osprey communities carry HOA fees and some carry CDD (Community Development District) bonds, which appear as line items on the annual property tax bill. The Oaks communities also require a mandatory club membership with initiation and annual dues separate from HOA. Always request a complete fee disclosure before making an offer to understand your true total monthly cost.

Buyer Due Diligence Checklist for Osprey

  • Verify flood zone classification (FEMA MSC) and request current flood insurance quotes
  • Confirm HOA fees, CDD assessments, and any mandatory club membership dues
  • Check permit history with Sarasota County (SCC Property Appraiser website)
  • Inspect roof age and condition, hurricane windstorm insurance is significant in coastal Sarasota County
  • Confirm AC system age, coastal humidity accelerates wear
  • Order a 4-point inspection for homes over 30 years old (required by most insurers)
  • If waterfront: inspect seawall, dock permits, and water access rights
  • Verify school zone assignment directly with Sarasota County Schools

content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL is served by the Sarasota County School District, one of Florida's top-performing districts. Pine View School for the Gifted (A+, GS 10/10, #12 nationally) is physically located in Osprey but requires gifted identification for admission. Most Osprey students are zoned for Venice High School. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 if schools are a priority in your home search.

How Good Are Schools in Osprey, FL?

Osprey sits within the Sarasota County School District, which is consistently among Florida's highest-performing public school systems. According to PublicSchoolReview, the district's average testing ranking is 10/10, placing it in the top 10% of Florida public schools. District-wide math and reading proficiency averages 62%, versus 52% for Florida as a whole. For families relocating from Hillsborough, Pasco, or Pinellas County, Sarasota County's academic performance is a meaningful upgrade.

What Schools Serve Osprey Students?

Because Osprey is a small unincorporated community, the Sarasota County Schools attendance boundary matters more than the city name. Confirm your specific address zone at the Sarasota County Schools website before making a purchase decision.

Elementary and K-8 Options Near Osprey

Laurel Nokomis School serves students in the Osprey-Nokomis area as a PK-8 combination school, an increasingly common format in Sarasota County that keeps students with the same peer group through 8th grade. The campus is located on Laurel Road and serves families in both Nokomis and south Osprey areas.

Venice High School, The Primary Osprey High School

Most Osprey students in the 34229 ZIP code are zoned for Venice High School, a large comprehensive high school offering AP courses, International Baccalaureate (IB) pathway, dual enrollment through Sarasota County Technical College, fine arts programs, and competitive athletics. Venice High consistently earns solid Niche ratings from Sarasota County parents.

What Is Pine View School, and Can My Child Attend?

Pine View School for the Gifted is physically located in Osprey at 1 Python Path (34229) and is one of the nation's most extraordinary public schools. According to Niche, Pine View earns an A+ overall grade. GreatSchools rates it 10/10. U.S. News ranked it #12 among all high schools nationally. The school serves grades 2-12 with 1,674 students, a 16:1 student-teacher ratio, 100% graduation rate, average SAT of 1420, and average ACT of 32.

However, Pine View is not the automatic neighborhood school for Osprey residents. It is a county-wide gifted magnet school, admission requires identification as intellectually gifted through the Sarasota County Schools' formal evaluation process. Families with children who qualify often specifically choose Osprey for the convenience of living close to Pine View.

Osprey is an unincorporated Sarasota County community along the US-41 (Tamiami Trail) corridor, positioned between Sarasota to the north and Venice to the south. ZIP code 34229. The community sits on and around Little Sarasota Bay, with Casey Key just to the west providing Gulf of Mexico access. I-75 runs approximately 3-5 miles east of the US-41 corridor, accessible via Laurel Road (Exit 195) or Jacaranda Boulevard (Exit 193).

It has traffic signals, school zones, and commercial intersections that slow travel, but the distance is short enough that it remains the default for local trips. For Tampa, Fort Myers, or any destination more than 25 miles away, I-75 is the answer. title: Is Osprey FL a Good Place to Live? Honest 2026 Review
excerpt: Osprey FL pros and cons: Oscar Scherer State Park, Pine View School, bay and Gulf access. Trade-offs include high home prices and no city services. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL is a small, upscale Sarasota County community that consistently ranks as one of the better places to live in Southwest Florida. Top-rated schools, Oscar Scherer State Park, Little Sarasota Bay access, and a location between Sarasota and Venice make it an appealing choice. The main trade-offs are high home prices and limited public amenities compared to larger cities. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 if you want a candid take.

What Makes Osprey FL a Good Place to Live?

I work with buyers across Sarasota County, and Osprey regularly comes up as one of the more coveted addresses in the area, not because of name recognition, but because of what it actually delivers: a quiet coastal setting, Oscar Scherer State Park in the backyard, 13 minutes to Sarasota, 12 minutes to Venice, and Sarasota County's top-performing school district serving the community. It is the kind of place where people stay once they arrive.

What Are the Pros of Living in Osprey, FL?

1. Sarasota County Schools, Among Florida's Best

Osprey is served by the Sarasota County School District, which ranks in the top 10% of Florida public school districts with math and reading proficiency scores averaging 62% versus the 52% state average. Pine View School for the Gifted, ranked #12 nationally by U.S. News, is physically located in Osprey. For families with gifted-identified children, living close to Pine View is a significant draw.

2. Oscar Scherer State Park in Your Backyard

Oscar Scherer State Park is a 1,400-acre natural preserve within the community of Osprey. The park protects one of Florida's best remaining scrub habitat areas, home to the Florida scrub jay (a threatened species). It offers 15 miles of hiking and biking trails, two miles of Osprey Creek for kayaking and canoeing, freshwater swimming at Lake Osprey, camping, and a Nature Center. For nature-oriented residents, this is a rare amenity that other SW Florida communities don't have.

3. Location Between Sarasota and Venice

Osprey's between-city position is a genuine advantage. Sarasota's cultural district, downtown restaurants, Ringling Museum, and Whole Foods are 13 miles north (about 15 minutes on US-41). Venice's charming downtown, Venice Beach, and Brohard Paw Park are 8 miles south (about 12 minutes). Osprey residents routinely enjoy both cities without living in either one.

4. Little Sarasota Bay and Gulf Access

Osprey fronts Little Sarasota Bay along the Intracoastal Waterway. Waterfront communities like The Oaks Bayside and Edgewater at Hidden Bay offer direct bay access with private docking. Blackburn Point Park provides a kayak launch and fishing pier. Casey Key, the Gulf-front barrier island accessible via Blackburn Point Bridge, is within the Osprey community. Siesta Key Beach, routinely rated one of the nation's best beaches, is about 22-25 minutes north.

5. Quieter Lifestyle at Coastal Southwest Florida

Osprey does not have downtown bars, traffic-clogged commercial strips, or high-rise condos. It has a state park, a bay, gated neighborhoods, good schools, and two excellent nearby cities. For buyers who want the Sarasota lifestyle without the Sarasota density, Osprey is the answer.

What Are the Cons of Living in Osprey, FL?

1. High Home Prices

Osprey's median listing price of approximately $792,000 is well above the Florida statewide median. Buyers priced out of The Oaks or Casey Key will find fewer entry-level options than in Venice or North Port. The market has softened from the 2022 peak, but Osprey remains a premium-priced community.

2. No City Services or Downtown of Its Own

Osprey is unincorporated, there is no city hall, no city police department, and no downtown to walk to. All services come from Sarasota County. This is not a problem in practice (County services are excellent), but buyers accustomed to walkable downtown environments should plan to drive to Sarasota or Venice for dining, shopping, and entertainment.

3. Long Tampa Commute

At 69 miles, Tampa is a 70-90 minute drive from Osprey. This rules out Osprey as a practical daily-commute suburb for Tampa workers. MacDill AFB is 72 miles away, even further. Remote workers and those employed in Sarasota/Venice are better positioned.

4. Hurricane and Flood Zone Risk

Osprey's coastal position means meaningful hurricane and flood exposure. Casey Key and bayfront areas sit in FEMA flood zones that require costly flood insurance. Windstorm insurance premiums for all Sarasota County coastal properties have risen substantially since Hurricane Ian (2022) and Hurricane Idalia (2023). Buyers must factor insurance costs into their budget, not just mortgage P+I.

Osprey FL is an excellent place to live for buyers who prioritize coastal proximity, top-rated Sarasota County schools, natural beauty, and a quieter lifestyle close to Sarasota's arts and dining. The trade-off is a higher cost of living, limited walkability, and a long commute to Tampa.

Osprey is a small unincorporated Sarasota County community with an estimated population of approximately 6,000-7,000 residents. Its unincorporated status means there is no city government, Sarasota County provides all services.

Osprey is generally considered a safe, low-crime area. Its small size and suburban/rural character, combined with the gated community presence (The Oaks, Edgewater at Hidden Bay), contribute to low crime rates. Check the Sarasota County Sheriff's Office crime mapping tool for current data.

What is the weather like in Osprey FL?

Osprey has a subtropical climate with hot, humid summers (June-September, daily highs 90-93°F with frequent afternoon thunderstorms) and mild, dry winters (December-February, highs 70-76°F). Hurricane season runs June-November. The coastal location moderates temperatures slightly versus inland Sarasota County communities.

Is Osprey FL expensive to live in?

Yes, Osprey is an upscale community. The median home listing price is approximately $792,000 as of 2026. Cost of living beyond housing is comparable to the broader Sarasota-Venice area, lower than Miami or Naples, but higher than most of the Tampa Bay metro.

What Price Points Can Buyers Find in Osprey?

Entry Level: $450K-$700K

Inland single-family homes from the 1980s-2000s, CBS construction, 1,600-2,800 square feet, typically with a pool. Many in Sorrento East, Country Club Estates, and Oakwood Manor areas. No mandatory club membership. HOA fees may be low or nonexistent in older sections.

Mid Market: $700K-$1.2M

Newer builds, larger square footage, closer to the bay, or in The Oaks Preserve (condos/villas/smaller SFH). This tier captures much of the move-up buyer demand and remote worker relocations. Properties at this level typically have impact windows, updated kitchens, and pool/lanai.

Upper Market: $1.2M-$3M

The Oaks Clubside single-family homes with golf course frontage, or smaller Edgewater at Hidden Bay properties. At this level, buyers expect club amenities (The Oaks has two championship golf courses), gated security, and estate-level finishes.

Luxury: $3M-$10M+

The Oaks Bayside waterfront estates on Little Sarasota Bay and Casey Key Gulf-front properties. These are some of the most exclusive addresses in Sarasota County. Casey Key Gulf-to-Bay lots with 200+ feet of frontage on both the Gulf of Mexico and Intracoastal Waterway command $4M-$10M+.

Seller Flexibility Has Increased

With 85+ days on market as the average, many Osprey sellers have become more willing to negotiate. Motivated sellers may contribute to closing costs, accept offers below list price, or leave appliances and furnishings for a faster close. Get pre-approved and come in with a clear offer rather than lowballing, Osprey sellers tend to have holding power, but reasonable offers are being accepted.

Insurance Costs Are a Budget Factor

Sarasota County is a coastal market, and windstorm insurance premiums have risen sharply since Hurricanes Ian and Idalia. For a $650K-$800K home in Osprey, combined homeowner's + flood + windstorm coverage can run $8,000-$15,000+ annually depending on flood zone, roof age, and wind mitigation features. Get insurance quotes before removing contingencies, this is a meaningful monthly cost.

The Oaks Club Membership Is Non-Optional

Buyers purchasing in The Oaks (all three sections, Bayside, Clubside, Preserve) are required to join The Oaks Club. Membership includes initiation fees and annual dues on top of HOA fees. Request the complete membership fee schedule before making an offer, as total carrying costs in The Oaks are significantly higher than headline HOA fees suggest.

Selling a Home in Osprey FL

Pricing Accuracy Matters More Than Ever

In 2022, overpriced Osprey homes sold anyway. In 2026, overpriced listings sit and accumulate days-on-market stigma. The most successful Osprey sellers price accurately from day one, complete pre-listing inspections to remove buyer objections, and present the home well, fresh landscaping, clean pool, decluttered interiors.

Best Season for Osprey Sellers

February through May is the peak season when seasonal residents and winter visitors are actively purchasing. List in January for full February-April exposure. Summer closings are quieter but can still produce results with motivated buyers who are avoiding competition.

Utilities

Florida Power and Light (FPL) or Florida Public Utilities serves Osprey, depending on the specific address. Sarasota County summer electric bills for an air-conditioned home run $180-$280/month in peak cooling months (July-September), dropping to $100-$160 in the mild winter months (November-March). No State Income Tax

Florida has no state income tax, which is meaningful for high earners relocating from California, New York, New Jersey, or Illinois.
