title: Osprey FL Property Taxes: 2026 Guide & Estimates
excerpt: Osprey FL property tax guide: Sarasota County millage rates, homestead exemption, Save Our Homes cap, portability, and 2026 tax estimates by home value.
content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL properties in unincorporated Sarasota County pay a combined millage rate of approximately 14-15 mills. On a $700,000 home with Florida homestead exemption, estimated annual taxes are approximately $9,400-$9,750. Apply for homestead by March 1st. Contact Sarasota County Property Appraiser for specifics. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907.

How Are Property Taxes Calculated in Osprey, FL?

Osprey is in unincorporated Sarasota County, so property taxes are set by several overlapping taxing authorities: Sarasota County government, the Sarasota County School Board, and various special taxing districts (mosquito control, fire, etc.). The sum of all these rates is your total millage rate. Millage is expressed per $1,000 of taxable value, a 14.5 millage rate means $14.50 in tax per $1,000 of taxable value.

For most Osprey residential properties in the 34229 ZIP code, the combined millage rate falls in the range of approximately 14-15 mills. Some waterfront areas or special districts may differ slightly. Always verify the specific millage rate for any property you are considering by checking the Sarasota County Property Appraiser's website (sc-pa.com).

What Florida Tax Exemptions Apply in Osprey?

Homestead Exemption ($50,000)

Florida's homestead exemption reduces assessed value by $50,000 on your primary residence. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities. The second $25,000 applies to non-school taxes only. Apply by March 1st of the year in which you want the exemption to take effect. File at the Sarasota County Property Appraiser's office (sc-pa.com) or in person.

Save Our Homes Assessment Cap

Once you have a homestead exemption, the Save Our Homes cap limits annual increases to your assessed value to 3% or the Consumer Price Index (CPI), whichever is lower. During rapid appreciation periods (like 2021-2022), this cap provides substantial long-term tax savings. If you buy a home in Osprey where the previous owner had Save Our Homes benefits, your assessed value resets to market value, you don't inherit the cap until you establish your own homestead.

Portability

Florida homeowners who sell a homesteaded property and purchase another in Florida can port up to $500,000 of accumulated Save Our Homes savings to their new home. If you are selling a Tampa Bay area home to move to Osprey, portability could significantly reduce your assessed value in Osprey and save thousands annually in property taxes.

Additional Florida Exemptions

  • Senior Low-Income Exemption: Additional $25,000 exemption for homeowners 65+ meeting income limits (varies by county)
  • Disabled Veterans: Up to 100% exemption depending on disability rating from the VA
  • Surviving Spouse of First Responder: Full exemption for surviving spouses of first responders killed in the line of duty
  • Widow/Widower Exemption: Additional $500 exemption for widows and widowers

Upcoming Florida Homestead Exemption Expansion

The Florida legislature passed legislation to expand the homestead exemption significantly in future years. Homeowners who establish Florida homestead and file by December 31, 2026, qualify for the expanded exemption of $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, a significant potential tax reduction for Osprey homeowners. Consult a tax professional for current legislative status, as exemption laws can change.

Expect $700K+ for new construction. Buyers seeking production-builder new construction under $500K should consider Venice-Wellen Park (south) or Sarasota County's northern areas. Is New Construction Available in Osprey, FL?

Osprey is a largely built-out coastal community. Unlike Wesley Chapel, Lakeland, or the Wellen Park area near Venice, Osprey does not have large master-planned communities with dozens of new home models at production-builder price points. What you will find instead is: boutique gated communities with newer construction, custom infill on remaining lots along Casey Key and Little Sarasota Bay, and occasional resale of homes that were built in the last 5-10 years within The Oaks.

What New Construction Options Exist in Osprey?

Edgewater at Hidden Bay, Gated Boutique Community

Edgewater at Hidden Bay is a newer gated, resort-style community positioned on 12 acres on the water's edge of Little Sarasota Bay in Osprey. The community features a marina, resort amenities, and newer construction homes with bayfront access and views. Price range runs approximately $900,000-$2,500,000+. This is the closest thing Osprey has to a new-construction community with a resort lifestyle, though the scale is far smaller than developments like Epperson Ranch or Wellen Park.

Custom Infill and Casey Key Lots

Casey Key Road, Osprey's barrier island, sees occasional custom home builds on lots that come available. Gulf-to-Bay lots, those with frontage on both the Gulf of Mexico and the Intracoastal Waterway, are extraordinarily scarce. Vacant lots, when available, can command $2,000,000-$4,000,000+ before a single nail is driven. Custom builds on Casey Key typically range from $3,000,000 to $10,000,000+.

The Oaks, New Phases and Infill

Within The Oaks, occasional lots are available for custom builds, particularly in the Oaks Bayside section. The community's architectural review committee controls design standards. Buyers interested in building in The Oaks must become club members and work within the design guidelines. Contact The Oaks Club directly for current lot availability.

Taylor Morrison and Other Builders Near Osprey

Taylor Morrison has been active in the Sarasota-Venice corridor and has built within the broader Osprey area. However, production builder communities with homes in the $400K-$700K range are more prevalent in Venice, Nokomis, and the Sarasota North corridor than in core Osprey. If you want new construction at a lower entry price, the surrounding areas provide more options.

Custom Builder Due Diligence

Sarasota County building codes for new construction require impact-resistant windows, hurricane straps, and engineered roofing systems. These are actually advantages for buyers, new construction built to current code typically carries lower windstorm insurance premiums than older resale homes that predate these requirements. When comparing new construction to older resale in Osprey, factor in insurance savings, reduced immediate maintenance, and builder warranties.

Quick Answer

Osprey FL real estate investment is best approached as an appreciation and wealth-preservation play rather than a cash-flow investment. At median prices around $650K-$792K, gross yields are approximately 4-5% annually. Seasonal rentals in gated communities can command $4,000-$6,000+/month. Limited supply and strong Sarasota County market fundamentals support long-term value. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for an investment analysis.

What Makes Osprey FL an Investment Market?

Osprey sits in one of the most supply-constrained real estate markets in Southwest Florida. The community is largely built out, there is no large land bank available for mass development. Combined with Sarasota County's top-10% school district, Oscar Scherer State Park, Little Sarasota Bay frontage, and the established prestige of addresses like The Oaks and Casey Key, Osprey has strong long-term appreciation fundamentals.

That said, Osprey is not a cash-flow market at 2026 prices. Gross yields of 4-5% on $650K-$800K properties, before insurance, maintenance, management, and HOA expenses, produce modest net returns. Investors who do well in Osprey typically buy for long-term equity accumulation, seasonal rental income, or eventual owner-occupancy.

What Are Rental Rates in Osprey, FL?

Annual Rental Market

According to Zillow rental data, the average rent in the broader Sarasota, FL market is approximately $2,535/month. In the Osprey ZIP code (34229), annual rentals for single-family homes typically run $2,400-$3,500/month for 3BR homes and $3,000-$5,000/month for larger or waterfront properties. The Oaks communities command premium annual rents due to the included club amenities and gated environment.

Seasonal (Winter) Rental Market

The Osprey-Sarasota seasonal market is active from November through April, drawing Northern snowbirds. Furnished seasonal rentals in gated Osprey communities (The Oaks, Edgewater at Hidden Bay) can command $4,000-$6,000+/month for 3-4 month winter leases. Annual lease income from a seasonal property rented for the 5-month winter season might total $20,000-$30,000, with the property owner-occupied or rented during summer at lower rates.

Short-Term Rental (STR) Considerations

Short-term Airbnb/VRBO-style rentals in Osprey face HOA restrictions in most gated communities. The Oaks and similar communities prohibit STR. Older non-HOA properties in Osprey may allow STR, but Sarasota County has enacted STR regulations that require registration, safety inspections, and limit rentals in some residential zones. Verify STR eligibility with Sarasota County before purchasing any property with STR income in mind.

What Are the Risks of Investing in Osprey?

Insurance Cost Escalation

Post-Hurricane Ian (2022) and Idalia (2023), Florida property insurance, particularly windstorm and flood, has risen sharply. This can absorb 30-50% of annual gross rent income, dramatically compressing net yields.

HOA Rental Restrictions

Many Osprey communities restrict rental frequency and minimum lease terms. The Oaks requires all rentals to be approved through the HOA and has minimum lease duration requirements. These restrictions reduce the investment flexibility of community-governed properties. Older non-HOA Osprey properties offer more rental flexibility.

Luxury Market Volatility

Osprey's upper price tier (The Oaks Bayside, Casey Key) has seen more price volatility than the overall market, both faster appreciation during the 2020-2022 runup and deeper corrections in the 2024-2026 softening period. High-end luxury markets in coastal Florida can take longer to recover from downturns than broader mid-market communities.

Quick Answer

Osprey FL has three waterfront markets: Little Sarasota Bay (The Oaks Bayside, Edgewater at Hidden Bay), Gulf of Mexico via Casey Key, and canal-front homes. Bayfront homes range from $900K to $7M+. Casey Key Gulf-front estates run $2.5M-$10M+. All coastal waterfront properties require flood insurance. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for current waterfront listings.

What Waterfront Options Exist in Osprey, FL?

Osprey offers three distinct waterfront markets, each with different price points, lifestyle characteristics, and access types. Whether you want a bayfront estate with a private dock, a Gulf-front island retreat, or a bayview home in a gated resort community, Osprey has a waterfront product, at significant price premiums over inland alternatives.

The Oaks Bayside, Little Sarasota Bay Estates

The Oaks Bayside is the premier bayfront community in Osprey, located on approximately 200 acres with 133 to 197 home sites offering direct Little Sarasota Bay frontage. The community is gated within The Oaks Country Club development on former Palmer family land. Home sites range from 0.33 to 1.5+ acres, and properties come with private docking facilities on the bay.

Casey Key, Gulf-Front Barrier Island

Casey Key is a narrow barrier island off Osprey and Nokomis, accessible via Blackburn Point Road and the Blackburn Point Bridge. Casey Key Road runs north-south along the island, providing access to Gulf-front and bay-front properties. The island has no through traffic, it dead-ends, which creates an extraordinarily private atmosphere.

Properties on Casey Key range from vintage Florida cottages that occasionally come up at $1.5M-$3M for renovation, to newly built custom Gulf-to-Bay estates at $5M-$10M+. Gulf-to-Bay lots, those with frontage on both the Gulf of Mexico and the Intracoastal Waterway, are among the rarest and most valuable real estate in all of Sarasota County.

Edgewater at Hidden Bay, Resort-Style Bay Community

Unlike The Oaks, which is a large country club community with golf, Edgewater is a smaller, resort-style marina community. Amenities include a marina, resort pool, fitness center, and bay access. Prices typically run $900,000-$2,500,000+.

What Do Waterfront Buyers in Osprey Need to Know?

Flood Zone and Insurance

All Osprey waterfront properties, bay front, Gulf front, or canal front, carry meaningful flood risk. Most sit in FEMA flood zones AE or VE. Zone AE properties require mandatory flood insurance for any federally-backed mortgage. Zone VE (velocity zone, direct wave action) carries the highest rates. Annual flood insurance for a $1.5M-$3M Osprey waterfront home in Zone AE can run $5,000-$15,000+ depending on the property's base flood elevation and first-floor elevation relative to the flood map.

Seawall, Dock, and Riparian Rights

Bayfront and canal-front properties in Osprey may come with seawalls, docks, and boat lifts in various states of condition and permitting. Before purchasing any waterfront home, commission an independent inspection of the seawall (concrete and cap condition, erosion signs), verify all dock permits are current with Sarasota County, and confirm that any boatlift is properly permitted and structurally sound. Seawall repairs in Southwest Florida run $500-$1,500+ per linear foot, a substantial expense if deferred.

Riparian Rights and Dock Permitting

Waterfront homeowners in Florida have riparian rights, the right to access, use, and place structures on the adjacent waterway subject to state and county permits. Adding or modifying a dock on Little Sarasota Bay requires permits from Sarasota County, the Florida DEP, and potentially the Army Corps of Engineers. This process can take months and is not guaranteed. Buyers who want to add a dock should research permissibility before purchasing.

Hurricane and Storm Surge Exposure

Osprey's location on Little Sarasota Bay and Casey Key's position as a barrier island create storm surge exposure in major hurricane events. Hurricane Ian (2022) caused significant storm surge damage in Southwest Florida coastal communities. Buyers of waterfront Osprey homes should review the National Hurricane Center's storm surge risk maps for the property's specific location, and ensure homeowner's insurance includes adequate windstorm, flood, and storm surge coverage.

Casey Key properties with direct frontage may have private docks subject to Sarasota County permitting.

Is Casey Key in Osprey FL?

Yes, Casey Key is a barrier island accessible from Osprey via Blackburn Point Road and the Blackburn Point Bridge. It falls within the 34229 ZIP code and is considered part of the Osprey community. Gulf-to-Bay lots on Casey Key are among Sarasota County's most exclusive and expensive real estate.

What are the flood zones for waterfront homes in Osprey?

Most waterfront properties in Osprey (Casey Key, The Oaks Bayside, Edgewater at Hidden Bay) are in FEMA flood zones AE or VE, which require mandatory flood insurance for federally backed mortgages. Annual flood insurance premiums for high-value bayfront or Gulf-front properties can range from $3,000 to $10,000+ annually. Always check the FEMA Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov.

title: Osprey FL Flood Zones: What Buyers Need to Know (2026)
excerpt: Osprey flood zones explained: how to look up your property's flood zone, what flood insurance costs, and which neighborhoods carry the most risk. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Many Osprey properties near Little Sarasota Bay and the Intracoastal Waterway fall in FEMA Zone AE (high-risk flood zone) requiring mandatory flood insurance if you have a federally-backed mortgage. Inland Osprey is typically Zone X (minimal flood hazard). Always look up the specific address on the FEMA flood map before making an offer.

Why Flood Zones Matter in Osprey

Osprey sits along the Sarasota County coast in an area where elevation differences of just a few feet can mean the difference between a Zone X property with no mandatory flood insurance and a Zone AE property where lenders require an NFIP or private flood policy. For buyers, the flood zone designation directly affects your monthly carrying cost. According to FEMA, National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) premiums for Zone AE properties in coastal Florida can range from $1,500 to $8,000 or more per year depending on the structure's elevation relative to the base flood elevation (BFE).

I have worked with buyers across Osprey and Sarasota County for years, and flood zone due diligence is one of the first things I walk every client through. The FEMA map alone is not the full picture. An elevation certificate, the community rating system discount, and the condition of existing flood vents all affect what you actually pay.

FEMA Flood Zone Designations in Osprey

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps flood risk by designating zones on Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). Here are the zones you are most likely to see when researching Osprey properties:

ZoneRisk LevelFlood Insurance Required?What It Means
Zone XMinimalNo (not mandatory)Less than 0.2% annual chance of flooding. Most inland Osprey streets.
Zone AEHighYes (federally-backed loan)1% annual chance of flooding. Base flood elevation (BFE) is defined. Most bay-adjacent and canal properties.
Zone AHHighYesShallow ponding flood risk. BFE defined. Less common in Osprey but present in some low-lying inland areas.
Zone VEHighestYesCoastal areas with velocity wave action. Typically oceanfront and direct bayside properties. Highest insurance rates.
Zone X500ModerateNo (not mandatory)0.2%-1% annual chance. Between X and AE in risk level.

Which Osprey Areas Carry the Highest Flood Risk?

Waterfront and Bay-Adjacent Properties

Properties along Little Sarasota Bay, the Intracoastal Waterway, and direct coastal areas carry the highest flood risk. Sorrento Shores (a waterfront community on the Intracoastal) and properties along Bay Street are most likely to be in Zone AE or VE. The premium for waterfront in Osprey is real, but so is the flood insurance cost. On a waterfront property, plan for $3,000 to $10,000+ per year in flood insurance depending on structure elevation and coverage amount.

Canal-Connected Homes

Canal-adjacent and canal-access properties offer boat access but typically sit in Zone AE. The canal itself is a conduit for storm surge, meaning even properties a block or two from the bay can carry significant risk. Always ask for the elevation certificate and the current flood insurance policy on any canal-access home. An elevation certificate showing the finished floor at or above the BFE can dramatically reduce premiums.

Inland Osprey: Lower Risk

Communities built on higher inland ground typically land in Zone X. Rivendell (which borders Oscar Scherer State Park), and many homes along US-41 that are set back from the water, are often Zone X or Zone X500. Zone X means no mandatory flood insurance, though coverage is still available and advisable for peace of mind given Florida's hurricane exposure.

How to Look Up a Property's Flood Zone Before Buying

The process is straightforward. You do not need a real estate agent or specialist to check the basic zone designation:

Step 1: FEMA Map Service Center

Go to msc.fema.gov and enter the property address. The map will show the flood zone designation and which FIRM panel covers the property. This is a public, free tool. Write down the map panel number and the zone designation.

Step 2: Get the Elevation Certificate

If the property is in Zone AE, ask the seller for the current elevation certificate (EC). The EC shows the structure's lowest floor elevation compared to the base flood elevation. Properties with finished floors 1-2 feet above the BFE pay significantly less for flood insurance than those at or below the BFE. If no EC exists, a licensed surveyor can produce one for $300-$600.

Step 3: Get an Actual Flood Insurance Quote

Do not rely on estimates. Contact a licensed insurance agent for an actual NFIP or private flood quote based on the property address and EC. Private flood insurance is often cheaper than NFIP for newer homes or elevated structures, but NFIP has the advantage of being transferable (the existing policy can be assumed by the buyer in some cases).

Step 4: Review the Prior Claims History

Under Florida law, sellers must disclose known flooding history. You can also check FEMA's database for prior claims on a property by requesting a flood insurance claims report through FEMA or an insurance agent. A property with multiple prior flood claims is a red flag regardless of zone.

What Flood Insurance Costs in Osprey

NFIP premiums are calculated based on flood zone, structure type, year of construction, number of floors, foundation type, and the structure's elevation relative to the BFE. FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 methodology (implemented in 2021) calculates rates based on the actual risk profile of each property rather than just the zone designation. This has created more variation in rates within the same zone.

Property TypeEstimated Annual NFIP RangeKey Rate Factors
Zone X single-family home$400-$900/yr (preferred)Voluntary coverage, minimal risk
Zone AE, elevated structure$1,200-$3,500/yrFloor elevation vs. BFE is critical
Zone AE, at or near BFE$3,500-$8,000+/yrLower elevation = higher premium
Zone VE coastal/waterfront$5,000-$15,000+/yrWave action risk adds substantial cost

Private flood insurers are an increasingly competitive alternative to NFIP in Florida. For recently constructed homes with good elevation, private carriers sometimes offer better coverage with broader terms (loss of use, replacement cost) at lower prices. Always compare both options.

Sarasota County's Community Rating System (CRS) Discount

Sarasota County participates in FEMA's Community Rating System (CRS), a voluntary program that rewards communities for exceeding minimum floodplain management requirements. According to FEMA, CRS-participating communities can qualify their policyholders for discounts of 5% to 45% on NFIP premiums. Sarasota County's CRS class determines the discount available to property owners within participating areas. Ask your insurance agent to confirm the current CRS discount that applies to any Osprey property you are considering. This is a legitimate cost reduction that many buyers overlook.

Hurricane Ian's Impact on Sarasota County Flood Maps

Hurricane Ian made landfall in Lee County in September 2022, but the storm's storm surge reached into Sarasota County. Some areas that had not historically flooded received water during Ian. In the aftermath, FEMA conducted damage assessments and reviewed existing flood maps in affected counties. If you are buying in a coastal Sarasota County area, ask the seller whether the property experienced any flooding during Ian or any prior storms. This disclosure is required under Florida law and is one of the most important questions to ask.

Post-storm, some areas may be subject to FEMA advisory base flood elevations (ABFEs) or Letters of Map Change (LOMCs) that differ from the current effective FIRM. Your lender's flood zone determination service should account for current advisory maps. If you have any question about a specific property's status, the Sarasota County Floodplain Management office can provide guidance.

Should Flood Risk Stop You from Buying in Osprey?

No, but it should be part of your total cost calculation. Osprey waterfront properties command significant premiums for their location, views, and boat access. For the right buyer, the flood insurance cost is an acceptable trade-off. For a buyer on a tight budget, a Zone AE waterfront property's insurance cost could meaningfully affect affordability. The calculation changes completely for a Zone X inland property where flood insurance is optional and inexpensive.

My recommendation: always get the full insurance picture before you fall in love with a property. Know the zone, get the elevation certificate, get an actual flood insurance quote. Then decide with complete information. I help buyers work through this process regularly. Call me at (813) 733-7907 and I can refer you to licensed flood insurance specialists who work in the Osprey and Sarasota County market.

Contact BarrettCall (813) 733-7907

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Osprey have a lot of flood-prone properties?

It depends on location within Osprey. Properties near Little Sarasota Bay, the Intracoastal Waterway, and canals are typically in Zone AE (high risk). Inland Osprey neighborhoods like those near Oscar Scherer State Park and US-41 are more often in Zone X (minimal risk). The mix is roughly similar to other coastal Sarasota County communities.

Is flood insurance required in Osprey FL?

Flood insurance is required by federal law if your property is in a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA, which includes Zones AE, AH, AO, and VE) and you have a federally-backed mortgage (FHA, VA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac). If you are paying cash or the property is in Zone X, you are not legally required to carry it, though buying it is advisable given Florida's hurricane exposure.

How do I find Osprey's flood zone before making an offer?

Go to msc.fema.gov, enter the property address, and view the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for that parcel. This is a free public tool. For more detail, get the elevation certificate from the seller and ask a licensed insurance agent for an actual NFIP or private flood quote.

How much does flood insurance cost in Osprey FL?

Costs vary widely based on zone, structure elevation, and coverage amount. Zone X preferred policies can cost $400-$900/year. Zone AE properties can range from $1,200 to $8,000+ per year depending on how the structure's elevation compares to the base flood elevation (BFE). Getting an actual quote based on the elevation certificate is the only way to know the real number.

Did Hurricane Ian affect Osprey FL?

Ian made landfall in Lee County (Fort Myers area) in September 2022, but storm surge and wind impacts extended into Sarasota County including the Osprey area. Florida law requires sellers to disclose any known flooding history. Ask the seller directly whether the property flooded during Ian or any prior events. You can also check for prior NFIP claims on the property through an insurance agent.

title: Best Neighborhoods in Osprey FL: Where to Buy in 2026
excerpt: Osprey FL neighborhoods compared: Sorrento Shores, The Oaks Club, Rivendell, Bay Street Village, and Willowbend. Price ranges, school zones, and what each community actually offers.
content:
Quick Answer

The best neighborhoods in Osprey FL include Sorrento Shores (waterfront on the Intracoastal), The Oaks Club (private country club community), Rivendell (borders Oscar Scherer State Park), and Bay Street Village. Prices range from roughly $400K for inland non-waterfront to $1.5M+ for bay-front properties. All Osprey students attend Laurel Nokomis K-8 and Venice Senior High School.

Why Buyers Choose Osprey

Osprey is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County positioned between Sarasota (about 10 miles north) and Venice (about 7-8 miles south) along US-41/Tamiami Trail. That location is its primary appeal. You get access to Sarasota's restaurants, arts scene, and medical facilities without Sarasota's property prices, while Venice's beaches and walkable downtown are a short drive south.

Oscar Scherer State Park (1,384 acres) anchors the eastern side of Osprey, giving residents access to hiking, kayaking, swimming, and wildlife. The Legacy Trail, an 18.4-mile paved multi-use path from Sarasota to Venice, runs through Osprey and connects to both cities without touching US-41 traffic. These two amenities give Osprey an outdoor lifestyle that is genuinely hard to replicate at this price point in Sarasota County.

The tradeoff is that Osprey is not a city. There is no Osprey police department (Sarasota County Sheriff serves the area), and the local commercial strip is modest. Buyers who want the urban energy of Sarasota or the walkable downtown of Venice should look there instead. Osprey appeals to people who want a quieter base with easy access to both.

Sorrento Shores

What It Is

Sorrento Shores is a waterfront residential community on the Intracoastal Waterway/Little Sarasota Bay side of Osprey. Homes in Sorrento Shores sit on lots that back directly to the water or have nearby water access. The community has no mandatory HOA in most sections, which appeals to buyers who want waterfront without the governance layer. Streets are quiet, lots are generous, and the setting is genuinely scenic.

Price Range and Property Types

Direct waterfront homes in Sorrento Shores range from roughly $700K to $2M+ depending on lot size, home size, water frontage, and dock access. Non-waterfront homes within the community (typically a few blocks from the water) come in meaningfully lower, starting in the $500K-$700K range. Properties range from older 1960s-1970s Florida ranch homes on large lots to updated and newer-construction bayfront residences.

Key Considerations

Most Sorrento Shores bay-adjacent lots are in FEMA Zone AE. Flood insurance is a real cost here. Seawall condition and dock permits matter. If you are buying for boating, verify the dock permit is current and the seawall is sound. A seawall inspection ($300-$500) and dock inspection are worth the investment before closing. I walk Sorrento Shores buyers through all of this routinely.

The Oaks Club

What It Is

The Oaks Club is a private country club community in Osprey with two 18-hole golf courses, 12 har-tru clay tennis courts, croquet, and a full social program including dining. The residential side includes homes, villas, and condos priced from roughly $500K to $3M+. Community living at The Oaks comes with mandatory club membership, which means HOA fees and club dues are part of your carrying cost.

Price Range and Fees

Entry-level condos at The Oaks start around $400K-$600K. Single-family homes on the golf course range from $700K to $3M+. Club membership is required for all residents. Membership fees and the exact monthly/annual structure change periodically, so verify the current initiation fee and dues before contracting. The club and HOA fees together typically add $1,500-$3,000+ per month to ownership costs depending on the property type and membership tier chosen.

Who It's For

The Oaks suits buyers who actively want a private club lifestyle. If you play golf regularly, play tennis seriously, or want a built-in social community of similar-aged neighbors with resort-level amenities, The Oaks delivers. If you are a casual golfer or rarely use club amenities, the mandatory fees are hard to justify. Most buyers here are 55+, though the community is not age-restricted.

Rivendell

What It Is

Rivendell is a residential community in Osprey that directly borders Oscar Scherer State Park. Residents can access the park's trails, kayak launch, swimming area, and wildlife areas from the neighborhood perimeter. It is one of the more unusual community settings in Sarasota County, where your backyard fence can border a state-protected 1,384-acre natural area.

Price Range and Community

Rivendell homes are primarily single-family residences built in the late 1990s through 2000s. Prices typically range from $550K to $1.2M+ depending on size, lot, and upgrades. The community has an HOA. Most Rivendell homes are not in high-risk flood zones given the inland positioning away from the bay, which is an advantage for buyers who want Osprey without the flood insurance cost of waterfront areas.

Lifestyle Appeal

Rivendell attracts buyers who value the nature access over waterfront. The state park access, mature landscaping, and quiet streets are the primary draws. The Legacy Trail is accessible nearby, connecting Rivendell residents to Venice and Sarasota by bike or on foot. It is a lower-intensity lifestyle compared to a private club community but with a genuinely exceptional natural setting.

Bay Street Village and Other Osprey Communities

Bay Street Village

Bay Street Village is a more compact residential community in the Osprey area with a mix of single-family homes and townhomes. It is a more affordable entry point into the Osprey market. Properties here typically start below $500K. Verify school zoning and HOA details directly for any specific Bay Street Village property, as sections vary.

Willowbend

Willowbend is a gated community in Osprey offering single-family homes with a community pool and clubhouse. Homes typically range from $500K to $900K. The gated setting and amenities make it a middle ground between the private-club intensity of The Oaks and the no-HOA flexibility of areas like Sorrento Shores. Willowbend is inland enough that many properties carry lower flood risk than the bayfront neighborhoods.

Other Osprey-Area Communities

Several smaller and newer communities sit along the Osprey/Nokomis border. Prices and community features vary. For any community in this area, I recommend verifying the actual ZIP code and school zone assignment before contracting, as the Osprey/Nokomis boundary can affect where students are assigned even within short distances.

Osprey School Zone: What to Know

Sarasota County schools serve Osprey through the following assignment (always verify at the Sarasota County School District for any specific address):

Grade LevelSchoolNotes
Pre-K through 8thLaurel Nokomis SchoolK-8 combined campus in Nokomis, serves Osprey area
9th through 12thVenice Senior High School~7-8 miles south of Osprey on Nokomis Ave

Both schools are part of Sarasota County Schools. The K-8 model at Laurel Nokomis means students stay at one campus from kindergarten through 8th grade, which many families find preferable to a traditional elementary/middle split. Verify assignments at sarasotacountyschools.net for your specific address and the current school year.

Osprey vs. Nearby Communities: Price Comparison

AreaTypical Price RangeRelative CostKey Differentiator
Osprey (inland, no HOA)$400K-$700KMid-rangeOscar Scherer Park access, Legacy Trail
Osprey (waterfront)$700K-$2M+PremiumBay/Intracoastal frontage, boat access
Osprey (The Oaks Club)$400K-$3M+Premium (plus fees)Private golf and racquet club lifestyle
Nokomis (just north)$400K-$900KSimilarCasey Key proximity, beachier feel
Venice (south)$350K-$1.5M+Similar to slightly lowerWalkable downtown, direct beach access
South Sarasota$500K-$3M+HigherCloser to Sarasota amenities

Commute and Access from Osprey

US-41 (Tamiami Trail) is the primary arterial through Osprey. I-75 is accessible via Clark Road or Laurel Road interchange. Typical commute times:

  • Downtown Sarasota: 15-20 minutes via US-41 or I-75 north
  • Venice: 12-18 minutes via US-41 south
  • Siesta Key beach: 20-30 minutes
  • Sarasota Memorial Hospital: 15-20 minutes
  • Tampa (via I-75 north): 60-80 minutes
  • Fort Myers/Naples (via I-75 south): 60-90 minutes

Questions About Buying in This Area?

Contact BarrettCall (813) 733-7907

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the most desirable neighborhood in Osprey FL?

The Oaks Club and Sorrento Shores are the most well-known prestige communities. The Oaks is best for private club lifestyle buyers. Sorrento Shores is best for waterfront and boating buyers. Rivendell suits buyers who prioritize the natural setting and state park access. The "best" community depends entirely on your priorities and budget.

Are there affordable homes for sale in Osprey FL?

Affordable is relative in Sarasota County. The lowest entry points in Osprey are condos at The Oaks starting around $400K, townhomes in Bay Street Village type communities, and inland single-family homes in the $450K-$600K range. Osprey is not a bargain market by Florida standards, but it is less expensive than prime Sarasota neighborhoods.

Is Osprey FL a good place to retire?

Yes, for the right person. The Oaks Club specifically has an active 55+ demographic with an organized social calendar. Rivendell and Willowbend attract retirees who prioritize the outdoor lifestyle. Osprey's proximity to Sarasota Memorial Hospital and Venice Regional Bayfront Health is a practical advantage for retirees. The commute-based lifestyle stress is low compared to more urban areas.

What are property taxes like in Osprey?

Osprey is in unincorporated Sarasota County. Property taxes are based on Sarasota County's millage rates (county, school board, and any applicable special districts). Florida homestead exemption applies to primary residences. Sarasota County's effective property tax rate is generally competitive with other Florida counties. Verify the specific tax bill for any property you are considering through the Sarasota County Property Appraiser website (sarasotaproperty.net).

Does Osprey FL have its own downtown or shopping?

No. Osprey is an unincorporated community without a formal downtown. US-41 has some local businesses, restaurants, and services, but the commercial center is minimal. Most residents shop and dine in Venice (7-8 miles south) or Sarasota (10 miles north). The lack of walkable retail is a real trade-off that potential buyers should understand before committing to the area.

title: Moving to Osprey FL: 2026 Relocation Guide
excerpt: Planning to move to Osprey FL? Complete relocation guide: home prices, schools (Laurel Nokomis, Venice High), utilities, healthcare, commute, and honest trade-offs. Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL is an unincorporated Sarasota County community between Sarasota and Venice on the Gulf Coast. Expect home prices from $450K to $2M+ depending on waterfront vs. inland, quiet streets without a walkable downtown, Oscar Scherer State Park and the Legacy Trail as major lifestyle amenities, and Laurel Nokomis K-8 and Venice Senior High as the school assignments.

What Osprey FL Is (and Is Not)

Osprey is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County, not an incorporated city. That distinction matters for a few practical reasons. There is no city government, no city police department (Sarasota County Sheriff serves the area), and no city income or utility taxes. Services are county-provided. Zoning and permitting go through Sarasota County rather than a city hall. For most buyers, this is a non-issue. For buyers accustomed to tight city-neighborhood infrastructure, it can take an adjustment.

The community stretches along US-41 (Tamiami Trail South) in the 34229 ZIP code. The main landmarks are Oscar Scherer State Park on the east side and Little Sarasota Bay/Intracoastal Waterway on the west. The combination gives Osprey genuine outdoor amenity without the density of Sarasota proper.

Home Prices in Osprey: What to Budget

Osprey is not a budget market by Florida standards. Pricing breaks down roughly as follows:

Property TypePrice RangeKey Notes
Condos (community like The Oaks)$350K-$700KHOA fees and club membership add significant monthly cost
Inland single-family, no HOA$450K-$750KOlder 1970s-1990s construction on larger lots
HOA community (Rivendell, Willowbend)$550K-$1.2MNewer construction, 1990s-2010s, community amenities
Club community (The Oaks single-family)$700K-$3M+Golf course lots, private club membership required
Waterfront/bay-front$800K-$2.5M+Flood insurance adds $3,000-$10,000+/yr; seawall condition critical

Inventory in Osprey is typically limited. This is not a large community. It is not unusual for desirable properties to sell in days when priced correctly, or to sit for months if overpriced. Work with an agent who watches this micro-market regularly.

Schools in Osprey

Students in Osprey's 34229 ZIP code are served by Sarasota County Schools. The standard assignment for most Osprey addresses:

  • Elementary and Middle (Pre-K to 8th): Laurel Nokomis School (K-8 combined campus in Nokomis)
  • High School: Venice Senior High School

Laurel Nokomis School's K-8 model keeps students on one campus from kindergarten through 8th grade, eliminating the middle school transition. This is a meaningful feature for families relocating with children. Venice Senior High School is a large comprehensive high school with varied extracurricular programs. Both are Sarasota County public schools.

Private school options accessible from Osprey include several independent and faith-based schools in Sarasota and Venice. Verify current assignments at sarasotacountyschools.net before contracting on any property, as zone boundaries can change.

Utilities and Services in Osprey

Electric

Most Osprey properties are served by Florida Power & Light (FPL), the dominant electric utility in South Florida. FPL's residential rates are set by the Florida Public Service Commission. Budget for air conditioning costs that are significant from May through October in the Florida climate.

Water and Sewer

Utility service varies by location within Osprey. Some areas have Sarasota County water and sewer service. Others, particularly on larger lots and more rural sections, may rely on well water and septic systems. Ask specifically whether any property you are considering has county utilities or well/septic. A well and septic inspection is essential if the home is not connected to county systems.

Internet and Cable

Comcast/Xfinity serves most Osprey addresses with cable internet. Frontier fiber is available in some areas. Coverage and speeds vary by street. If you work from home and depend on reliable high-speed internet, verify your specific address before signing a purchase contract. Satellite internet (Starlink and others) is an increasingly viable backup for any gaps in service.

Trash and Recycling

Sarasota County provides waste collection and recycling pickup for Osprey. Collection frequency and details are through the county's Public Works and Utilities department.

Healthcare Near Osprey

Osprey is well-positioned for healthcare access relative to its size:

  • Sarasota Memorial Hospital (Sarasota, ~12-15 miles north): the major regional hospital for Sarasota County with Level II trauma center and comprehensive services
  • Venice Regional Bayfront Health (Venice, ~8-10 miles south): full-service community hospital serving the Venice/South Sarasota area
  • Physicians and Specialists: Both Sarasota and Venice have strong concentrations of primary care and specialist practices. Drive times are 15-25 minutes from most Osprey addresses.

For emergency care, both hospitals offer 24-hour emergency departments. The closest urgent care clinics are in Sarasota and Venice. This is an above-average healthcare access situation for a community of Osprey's size.

Shopping, Dining, and Daily Errands

Osprey itself has minimal commercial development. You will drive for most daily needs. The practical reality:

Grocery Shopping

Publix and other grocery stores are primarily in Venice and Nokomis within 10-15 minutes. There is no grocery store within walking distance of most Osprey addresses. Budget for a weekly drive rather than a daily walk.

Dining

There are a small number of restaurants along and near US-41 in the Osprey area. The primary dining scenes are in Venice (excellent walkable downtown restaurant concentration) and Sarasota (more upscale options). Most Osprey residents find themselves in Venice or Sarasota for dinner regularly. This is a feature of the lifestyle, not a flaw, but it means dining out always involves a drive.

Shopping and Services

Venice has a downtown with retail, personal services, and a walkable main street environment. Sarasota has larger retail concentration including mall options and specialty stores. Neither is more than 20-25 minutes from Osprey. For big-box retail (Home Depot, Target, Walmart), Venice and Sarasota both have options on US-41 or nearby.

Commute and Transportation from Osprey

Osprey does not have public transit in a meaningful sense. A car is essential. Typical commute times:

DestinationEst. Drive TimePrimary Route
Sarasota downtown20-30 minUS-41 north or I-75 north via Laurel Rd
Venice12-20 minUS-41 south
Siesta Key / Crescent Beach25-35 minUS-41 north then Stickney Point Rd
Venice Beach20-30 minUS-41 south into Venice
Sarasota Bradenton Airport25-35 minUS-41 north or I-75 to Airport Connector
Tampa International Airport65-80 minI-75 north to I-275
Fort Myers / RSW Airport70-90 minI-75 south

I-75 access from Osprey requires driving to either the Laurel Road interchange (north) or the Jacaranda Blvd interchange (south in Venice). US-41 is convenient for local travel but can get congested during season (November through April) when seasonal population swells.

Honest Trade-offs of Living in Osprey

Advantages

  • Direct access to Oscar Scherer State Park (hiking, kayaking, swimming)
  • The Legacy Trail connects to Venice and Sarasota without traffic
  • Quieter than either Sarasota or Venice proper
  • Between two strong lifestyle cities without committing to either
  • Good school assignment (Laurel Nokomis K-8, Venice Senior High)
  • Unincorporated = no city taxes or additional city regulations

Disadvantages

  • No walkable downtown or commercial center of its own
  • All grocery, dining, and major retail requires a drive
  • Limited new construction (mostly resale market)
  • Flood risk and flood insurance costs for waterfront/bay-adjacent properties
  • Seasonal traffic on US-41 (November through April)
  • Limited public transit

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Osprey FL a good place to live?

For the right person, yes. Osprey suits buyers who want a quiet, outdoor-oriented lifestyle between Sarasota and Venice, do not need a walkable urban environment, and can afford Sarasota County prices. It is not the right fit for people who want city walkability, easy public transit, or lower home prices.

What ZIP code is Osprey FL?

Osprey FL is in ZIP code 34229. This is the primary ZIP for the community. Some addresses near the Osprey/Nokomis border may use 34275 (Nokomis). Always verify school zone assignments and utility service area for any specific address rather than assuming by ZIP code.

What county is Osprey FL in?

Osprey is in Sarasota County, Florida. It is an unincorporated community, meaning it is served by county government rather than a city government. Property taxes, zoning, permitting, and public safety (Sheriff's Office) are all county-level services.

How far is Osprey from Siesta Key Beach?

Siesta Key is roughly 20-35 minutes from most Osprey addresses. You drive north on US-41 to Sarasota, then out Stickney Point Road or Siesta Drive to reach the island. Venice Beach is closer at 15-25 minutes south via US-41.

Is traffic bad in Osprey FL?

US-41 through Osprey can slow during season (November through April) when the regional population increases significantly. Morning and afternoon congestion at US-41 intersections is manageable compared to metro Tampa. I-75 provides a faster alternative for longer drives. Local residents generally find the traffic acceptable compared to larger metro areas.

title: Things to Do in Osprey FL: Parks, Trails, and Local Life
excerpt: Best things to do in Osprey FL: Oscar Scherer State Park, Legacy Trail, kayaking on the Intracoastal, Historic Spanish Point, and access to both Sarasota and Venice.
content:
Quick Answer

Osprey FL centers on outdoor activity: Oscar Scherer State Park (hiking, kayaking, scrub-jay viewing), the Legacy Trail (18.4-mile paved path to Venice and Sarasota), and water access to Little Sarasota Bay and the Intracoastal Waterway. Historic Spanish Point is a 30-acre historic and environmental site on the water. Most dining and nightlife is in Venice (south) or Sarasota (north) within 20-30 minutes.

Oscar Scherer State Park

Oscar Scherer State Park is the anchor of the Osprey outdoor experience. Located on the east side of US-41 in Osprey, the park covers 1,384 acres of Florida scrub, scrubby flatwoods, savannas, and the South Creek corridor. According to Florida State Parks, Oscar Scherer is one of the few remaining habitats for the threatened Florida scrub-jay, making it a destination for birdwatchers and nature photographers.

What to Do at Oscar Scherer

  • Kayaking and Canoeing: Kayak rentals are available at the park. You can paddle South Creek through the park's interior. The creek connects to Blackburn Bay and eventually to the Intracoastal Waterway. This is one of the more scenic paddling routes in Sarasota County.
  • Hiking: Over 15 miles of trails through scrub and flatwoods habitats. Trails range from easy to moderate. The scrub-jay trail gives you the best chance of seeing the Florida scrub-jay in its natural habitat.
  • Swimming: Lake Osprey inside the park is a designated freshwater swimming area. Lifeguards are not provided; swim at your own risk. A sandy beach area is available.
  • Camping: Oscar Scherer has campsites for tent and RV camping. Reservations at ReserveAmerica. A popular option for visitors who want to experience the area without committing to a hotel.
  • Picnicking: Covered pavilions and open picnic areas available. Reservations for pavilions at busy times of year.

Entrance fee applies (Florida State Parks standard day-use fee). Annual passes are a cost-effective option for Osprey residents who visit regularly. Dogs are allowed on leash on designated trails.

The Legacy Trail

The Legacy Trail is an 18.4-mile paved multi-use path running from Sarasota (near downtown) to Venice. The trail passes through Osprey and connects to both cities without using US-41. According to Sarasota County, the trail follows a former railroad corridor, giving it a flat, continuous alignment well-suited for cycling, running, and inline skating.

Using the Legacy Trail from Osprey

Multiple trailheads and access points exist along the Osprey section. Cyclists can reach Venice's downtown in 30-45 minutes. Reaching central Sarasota from Osprey takes roughly 60-80 minutes by bicycle at a moderate pace. The paved surface is well-maintained by Sarasota County. Restrooms are available at key trailheads.

The Legacy Trail is one of the most concrete benefits of living in Osprey. Residents cite the ability to bicycle to Venice for dinner or to reach the Sarasota Farmers Market on weekend mornings without touching US-41 traffic as a genuine quality-of-life advantage. For buyers who cycle regularly, this is a meaningful amenity worth factoring into your decision.

Water Activities: Kayaking, Boating, and Fishing

Kayaking and Paddleboarding

Beyond Oscar Scherer's South Creek, Osprey residents have access to Little Sarasota Bay and the Intracoastal Waterway. Several launch points exist along the bay side of the community. Paddlers can explore the mangrove-lined shores of the Intracoastal, access Casey Key on the Gulf side, and reach both Venice and Sarasota by water.

Boating

Waterfront homes in Osprey often include private docks with direct Intracoastal access. The Intracoastal Waterway south of Sarasota provides a protected route for motorboats through Venice and beyond. Venice Inlet provides Gulf access to the south. Several marinas operate in the Venice area for residents without private docks. Dock permits require coordination with the Army Corps of Engineers and Florida DEP; the permit status of any existing dock should be verified before purchasing a waterfront property.

Fishing

Sarasota Bay and the Intracoastal through Osprey offer year-round fishing for snook, redfish, trout, mangrove snapper, and tarpon. Oscar Scherer State Park's South Creek supports freshwater fishing for bass and bream (freshwater license required). Offshore fishing trips depart from Venice Inlet and Sarasota marinas.

Historic Spanish Point

Historic Spanish Point is a 30-acre historic and environmental site on Little Sarasota Bay in Osprey, operated by Gulf Coast Heritage Association. The site spans 5,000 years of history, from prehistoric Native American shell midden evidence through late-19th century pioneer homestead history associated with the Webb family, who settled the area in the 1860s.

What's at Spanish Point

  • Restored pioneer structures including a citrus packing house, chapel, and homestead buildings
  • Archaeological excavations showing prehistoric midden layers
  • Formal sunken garden and pergola structures
  • Bay views and a boat dock on Little Sarasota Bay
  • Walking trails through hammock and coastal plant communities
  • Guided tours available

Admission is charged. Spanish Point is open Tuesday through Sunday (verify current hours at historicspanishpoint.org). It is a genuinely interesting stop for history-oriented visitors and a point of local pride that distinguishes Osprey from other coastal communities without significant historical sites.

Golf and Racquet Sports

The Oaks Club in Osprey is a private country club with two 18-hole golf courses and 12 har-tru clay tennis courts. Membership is required and is only available to residents or those sponsored by existing members. The club also offers croquet and full dining and social programming. It is a significant draw for buyers who prioritize a private club lifestyle.

Public golf options within reasonable distance include courses in Venice, Sarasota, and the Englewood area. The Venice Golf and Country Club is a private option in Venice. Several public and semi-private courses are within 20-30 minutes of Osprey.

For racquet sports outside The Oaks, Venice has public tennis courts in several parks. Pickleball courts have expanded significantly in Sarasota and Venice in recent years. The Sarasota YMCA and private clubs in Sarasota offer fitness and racquet options for non-members of The Oaks.

Day Trips: Venice and Sarasota

Venice (15-20 Minutes South)

Venice has one of the more charming small-city downtowns on Florida's Gulf Coast. Venice Avenue is a walkable main street with independently owned restaurants, boutiques, and cafes. Venice Beach (main beach) and Caspersen Beach (known for shark teeth finding) are the primary beaches, with free parking easier to find than at Sarasota's beaches. The weekly Venice Farmers Market runs downtown. Osprey residents frequently treat Venice as their primary dining and weekend destination.

Sarasota (20-30 Minutes North)

Sarasota offers a substantially larger and more diverse amenity base. The Ringling Museum of Art (18th-century European paintings, contemporary gallery, circus history museum, and the Ca' d'Zan mansion on Sarasota Bay) is a genuine world-class attraction. The Sarasota Orchestra, Asolo Repertory Theatre, and Florida Studio Theatre give the city a performing arts density unusual for a metro its size. Siesta Key beach (white quartz sand) is a 35-40 minute drive from Osprey. St. Armands Circle on Lido Key has walkable retail and dining.

Dining Near Osprey

Osprey proper has a limited restaurant scene. Most dining destinations are in Venice or Sarasota. A few highlights accessible from Osprey:

Within Osprey / Very Close

There are several small restaurants and casual spots along US-41 in the Osprey area. The selection is modest. Chains and independent spots serve breakfast and casual lunch options. This is not a food-destination stretch of US-41.

In Venice (15-20 Minutes)

Venice Avenue and surrounding streets have a concentration of independently owned restaurants, pizza, Italian, seafood, and brunch spots. The city's scale keeps prices reasonable compared to Sarasota. Osprey residents regularly drive to Venice for dinner.

In Sarasota (20-30 Minutes)

Sarasota has a larger and more varied dining scene ranging from casual waterfront spots to upscale dining on Main Street downtown. St. Armands Circle on Lido Key is a walkable dining and retail destination for a full evening out. The drive from Osprey is manageable and most residents use both Venice and Sarasota depending on the occasion.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Osprey FL known for?

Oscar Scherer State Park and its Florida scrub-jay population, the Legacy Trail connecting to Venice and Sarasota, Historic Spanish Point on Little Sarasota Bay, and The Oaks Club private country club. Osprey has a strong outdoor recreation identity in a Gulf Coast community that is otherwise relatively quiet.

Is Oscar Scherer State Park worth visiting?

Yes, particularly if you kayak, hike, or birdwatch. The Florida scrub-jay viewing is rare and notable. The kayaking on South Creek through the park is one of the better inland paddling experiences in Sarasota County. The freshwater swimming lake is a good alternative to beach crowds. Entrance fee applies.

Are there beaches near Osprey FL?

Osprey does not have its own beach, but Venice Beach is 15-25 minutes south and Siesta Key beach (Sarasota) is 25-40 minutes north. Venice's Caspersen Beach, south of the main beach, is known for shark tooth finding and has a more natural, less crowded feel. Casey Key (between Osprey and Nokomis) has private beach access for property owners along the narrow barrier island.

Is there much nightlife in Osprey FL?

Very little. Osprey is a residential community without a bar or nightlife scene of its own. Venice and Sarasota have the nearest options. Sarasota's downtown and Rosemary District have bars, live music venues, and a more active evening scene. Venice is quieter but has a few spots on Venice Avenue. Most Osprey residents drive to whichever fits the occasion.

Can you kayak to Venice from Osprey?

Yes, via the Intracoastal Waterway and coastal waters. The route follows the protected Intracoastal south from the Osprey/Nokomis area to Venice Inlet. This is an experienced paddler's trip (several hours each way), not a casual outing. The South Creek paddle through Oscar Scherer State Park to Blackburn Bay is a more accessible shorter excursion for less experienced kayakers.

title: Nokomis Homes for Sale: Complete Buyer Guide
excerpt: Nokomis Homes for Sale: Complete Buyer Guide, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

What homes are for sale in Nokomis FL?

Nokomis FL is a small unincorporated Sarasota County community between Venice and Osprey with homes ranging from inland subdivisions in the $320K-$580K range to Casey Key Gulf-front estates above $3M. Waterfront properties on Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay run $600K-$2.5M. Inventory is tighter than Venice because Nokomis has limited new construction land. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 for current listings.

Nokomis sits in a pocket of Sarasota County that many buyers overlook because it lacks the name recognition of Venice or Siesta Key. That is a mistake. The community offers Gulf beach access at Nokomis Beach, direct Intracoastal Waterway frontage, and some of the most exclusive real estate in Florida along Casey Key. I have worked this market for years and I can tell you the inventory is narrow, the buyers are motivated, and the sellers often have strong price expectations.

Browse Nokomis homes for sale for current listings. Check the Nokomis housing market for recent sales. Use the mortgage calculator to model your payment.

What Types of Homes Are for Sale in Nokomis FL?

Nokomis has three distinct property tiers that serve very different buyer profiles. Understanding which tier fits your needs is the starting point for any search in this community.

Inland Single-Family Subdivisions ($320K-$580K)

The bulk of Nokomis real estate sits in established inland subdivisions built between the 1960s and 1990s. These are concrete block homes on quarter-acre or larger lots with no HOA in many cases, mature landscaping, and direct proximity to US-41 for easy access to Venice and Sarasota. Communities like Sorrento South, Sorrento East, and the streets around Laurel Road represent this tier. Homes range from 1,400 square feet in the low $300Ks to 2,400+ square feet in the upper $500Ks for updated properties.

Many of these homes were built before hurricane codes tightened in 2002, so buyers should pay close attention to roof age and hurricane strap documentation. A 4-point inspection is standard for insurance underwriting. The good news is that most sellers in Nokomis have owned for decades and know the property history.

Waterfront on Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay ($600K-$2.5M)

Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay are both part of the Intracoastal Waterway system in Sarasota County. Waterfront homes here have docks, boat lifts, and direct access to the Gulf through Stump Pass and New Pass. Most of the waterfront single-family stock was built in the 1970s-1990s, so buyers often have the option to renovate an existing structure or scrape and build new. Post-Hurricane Ian (September 2022) brought a wave of motivated sellers in this zone, and prices adjusted. Rebuilt or fully updated waterfront homes now start around $950K and can reach $2.5M+ for the best lots.

Flood insurance is mandatory and expensive on these properties. Zone AE designation from FEMA is common. Expect $4,000-$12,000 per year for flood insurance depending on the elevation certificate reading. Factor that into your monthly payment before making an offer.

Casey Key Gulf-Front and Bay-Front ($2M-$15M+)

Casey Key is a 9-mile barrier island accessed only from the north via Blackburn Point Road (with a swing bridge) or from the south near Osprey. There are no traffic lights, no commercial development, and strict deed restrictions on most parcels. Gulf-front properties can reach $15M+ for fully renovated large estates. Bay-front properties on the east side of the key run $2M-$6M. Both tiers are dominated by seasonal owners, and inventory turns over slowly. When a Casey Key property comes to market, serious buyers need to act within days.

What Should Buyers Know Before Making an Offer in Nokomis?

Verify the Flood Zone Before the Inspection

Nokomis has more flood-zone exposure than buyers sometimes expect. Even some inland streets see Zone AE designation because of the creek and bay drainage systems. Check any address at msc.fema.gov before writing an offer. Zone X properties exist in the higher inland areas and typically do not require flood insurance, which saves $3,000-$8,000 per year.

HOA Status Varies Widely

Many of the older Nokomis subdivisions have no HOA at all. Newer developments and planned communities do have associations. Ask for the HOA disclosure package if applicable and read the rules carefully, some Sarasota County communities have restrictions on short-term rentals, boat storage, and RVs.

Water and Sewer vs. Well and Septic

Parts of Nokomis are still on well water and septic systems, particularly older properties set back from the main roads. Sarasota County has been extending municipal water and sewer lines, but coverage is not universal. A well and septic inspection adds cost but is essential, Sarasota County requires septic inspection at the time of sale for systems installed before 1983.

Casey Key Has Limited Buyer Access Windows

The swing bridge at the north end of Casey Key operates on a schedule and can delay access during high boat traffic periods. More importantly, the island gets severe flooding during tropical storms. Hurricane Ian (2022) caused significant damage to Casey Key structures. Flood insurance on Casey Key is Zone VE (Velocity Exposure), the most expensive designation. Budget $15,000-$30,000 per year for flood insurance on Gulf-side properties.

Many older Nokomis neighborhoods have no HOA. Newer or waterfront communities may have deed restrictions or mandatory HOA fees. Always ask for the full HOA disclosure before making an offer.

Yes. Nokomis is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County, Florida. It has a 34275 ZIP code. Property taxes, permits, and public services are all administered through Sarasota County.

Nokomis Beach (a Sarasota County park) is directly accessible at the northern tip of Casey Key, just west of the US-41 bridge. It is one of the less crowded Gulf beaches in the county. Venice Beach is 5 miles south.

Are there new construction homes in Nokomis FL?

Very limited. Nokomis has little vacant land for subdivision development. Most new construction is custom infill on existing lots or complete rebuilds of older homes. Venice and Sarasota north of the Nokomis area have more new construction options.

title: Nokomis FL Schools Guide: Ratings and Zones
excerpt: Nokomis FL Schools Guide: Ratings and Zones, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

What schools serve Nokomis FL?

Nokomis FL is served by Sarasota County Schools. The primary K-8 school is Laurel Nokomis School on Laurel Road. Most Nokomis students attend Venice High School for grades 9-12. Pine View School (one of Florida's top gifted programs) is also in Sarasota County and accepts qualified students from Nokomis by application.

School zone is one of the most frequent questions I get from buyers looking in Nokomis. The short answer: Sarasota County Schools are generally well-regarded, and Nokomis benefits from having a well-rated K-8 school within the community itself. That said, the school zone picture has nuances depending on exactly where a property sits, and a few streets near the Nokomis-Osprey boundary can fall into different attendance zones.

Always verify a specific property's school assignment at sarasotacountyschools.net using the address search tool. School boundaries can shift when enrollment changes, and a sale listing's stated school zone may not be current.

Public Schools Serving Nokomis FL

Laurel Nokomis School (K-8, Public)

Laurel Nokomis School on Laurel Road is the primary elementary and middle school for most Nokomis-area students. The school serves grades K through 8, which means students stay in one building for nine years before transitioning to high school. This structure builds strong community ties and reduces the transition disruption that separate middle school formats can create. The school has received solid ratings from the Florida Department of Education. Check the current state report card at edudata.fldoe.org for the most recent grade.

Venice High School (Grades 9-12, Public)

Most Nokomis students feed into Venice High School for grades 9-12. Venice High is a traditional large comprehensive high school with a full range of AP courses, vocational programs, and athletics. It consistently earns a B or better on the Florida school grading system. The school is about 4-6 miles south of central Nokomis, depending on the student's address. Sarasota County provides bus service.

Pine View School (Grades 2-12, Gifted, Public)

Pine View School in Osprey is one of the most well-known public schools in Florida. It is a gifted magnet school serving Sarasota County students who qualify through standardized testing. If your child qualifies, Pine View is within close proximity to Nokomis, the school is on Laurel Road, effectively the same corridor as Laurel Nokomis School. Admission is by qualification, not address. Many Nokomis families consider Pine View a significant community asset. pineview.sarasotacountyschools.net has the qualifying test schedule.

Sarasota Online School (Sarasota County Virtual)

Sarasota County offers a fully online public school option for students who prefer virtual learning. This option is available to all county residents, including those in Nokomis. It follows the same Sarasota County curriculum and state standards.

Private School Options Near Nokomis FL

Venice Christian School

Venice Christian School is an independent Christian school about 5-6 miles south of central Nokomis in Venice. It serves preschool through 12th grade and is a common choice for Nokomis families seeking faith-based education. Tuition varies by grade level.

St. Thomas More Catholic School

St. Thomas More is a Catholic school in Sarasota serving K-8 and draws from across Sarasota County, including families in Nokomis. The school operates under the Diocese of Venice.

Out-of-Boundary and Magnet Options

Sarasota County Schools operates a controlled open enrollment system. Families can apply for out-of-boundary placements and magnet programs. Applications open in the fall for the following school year. Spots are limited and not guaranteed, but families in Nokomis have successfully placed students at highly-rated Sarasota schools including Phillippi Shores Elementary and Riverview High.

How School Zones Affect Nokomis Property Values

In my experience selling homes across Sarasota County, school zone is one of the top three factors buyers mention, behind price and location. Properties in the Laurel Nokomis School zone sell faster and at stronger prices than comparable properties just outside the zone. The Pine View proximity effect is real for families with academically accelerated children, even though Pine View admission is by qualification, being close to the school reduces daily commute burden.

Casey Key properties are in the same Sarasota County school district, but most Casey Key owners are seasonal residents without school-age children. School zone is less of a pricing driver on the island.

Venice High SchoolPublic9-12B~4-6 miles south

Tips for Buyers Prioritizing Schools in Nokomis

Use the County's Address-Based Zone Lookup

Do not rely on the listing agent or listing description for school zone confirmation. Sarasota County Schools has an official address-based lookup at sarasotacountyschools.net. Paste the property address and confirm the assigned school before you write an offer. Zone boundaries can shift.

Check Current State Report Card Grades

Florida assigns letter grades (A through F) to every public school annually based on standardized test performance, graduation rates, and learning gains. Grades change year to year. The Florida Department of Education publishes current grades at edudata.fldoe.org. Do not rely on ratings from three or four years ago.

Factor in the Pine View Testing Window

If your child may qualify for Pine View School, check the application timeline before closing. The qualifying test (the Cognitive Abilities Test, or CogAT) is administered at specific times. Missing the window means waiting a full year for the next opportunity. Pine View starts accepting students in Grade 2.

Most Nokomis students are zoned for Venice High School, located about 4-6 miles south on US-41 in Venice. Venice High earns consistent B ratings from the Florida Department of Education.

title: Nokomis FL Commute and Location Guide
excerpt: Nokomis FL Commute and Location Guide, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

How far is Nokomis FL from major cities?

Nokomis FL sits on US-41 between Venice (5 miles south) and Osprey (2 miles north) in Sarasota County. Sarasota downtown is 20-28 minutes north. Tampa is 65-80 minutes via I-75. Fort Myers is 65-80 minutes south. Bradenton is 30-40 minutes north. The area has no direct interstate access, commuters use US-41 or reach I-75 at either the Venice interchange or the Sarasota/Osprey interchange.

Nokomis is a quiet community, and that quiet comes partly from the fact that it is not a freeway town. US-41 (Tamiami Trail) is the main artery, and for short local trips it is perfectly adequate. For anyone commuting to Tampa or Fort Myers regularly, the distance to I-75 matters, the nearest northbound I-75 on-ramp is at Clark Road/Bee Ridge Road in Sarasota, about 10-15 minutes from central Nokomis. Southbound, the nearest ramp is in Venice at Jacaranda Boulevard, about 8-10 minutes.

I tell buyers who are commuting to Tampa: Nokomis is a lifestyle choice, not a commuter choice. If your job requires you in Tampa five days a week, you will spend 2+ hours daily in the car. If you are working locally or remotely, Nokomis puts you within easy reach of everything on the Gulf Coast.

Route Options from Nokomis FL

North to Sarasota: US-41 vs. I-75

For a trip to Sarasota downtown, US-41 is the practical route. The drive is 16 miles and takes 22-30 minutes in normal conditions. Taking I-75 north (accessed at Jacaranda/Venice or Clark Road/Sarasota) adds distance and does not save significant time for this destination. US-41 goes directly into downtown Sarasota on Main Street.

For trips to the Sarasota suburbs, Lakewood Ranch, University Town Center, I-75 corridor businesses, getting on I-75 at either the Venice or Bee Ridge interchange makes more sense. From Nokomis to University Town Center via I-75 is about 22-28 miles and 25-35 minutes.

North to Tampa: I-75 via Sarasota

Tampa is the long haul from Nokomis. Most drivers take US-41 north to I-75 at Clark Road or Bee Ridge Road, then I-75 north through Sarasota and Manatee County to Tampa. The I-275 split near St. Petersburg takes you directly into downtown Tampa. On a clear day with no accidents, the drive is 65-75 minutes. During morning rush, budget 85-100 minutes.

The I-75/Gandy Boulevard construction zones in northern Manatee and southern Hillsborough counties have been an ongoing issue in 2025-2026. Check Google Maps or Waze before leaving, particularly for Tampa departure times.

South to Venice and Port Charlotte: US-41

South to Venice is the shortest and easiest commute corridor from Nokomis. US-41 south takes you through Venice in about 10 minutes. Port Charlotte is 28 miles south and about 30-40 minutes via US-41 or I-75 south from Venice.

South to Fort Myers and Naples: I-75

For Fort Myers and Naples, take US-41 south to Venice, then I-75 south at Jacaranda. I-75 south to Fort Myers is about 50 miles from Venice, adding up to roughly 65-80 minutes total from Nokomis to Fort Myers downtown. Naples is an additional 25 miles and 25-35 minutes.

Public Transportation Options in Nokomis FL

Sarasota County Area Transit (SCAT) operates bus service in Sarasota County, including routes along US-41 that serve the Nokomis corridor. SCAT Route 15 runs along US-41 and connects to the Sarasota County SCAT transfer center. This is a practical option for trips to Venice or Sarasota without a car, but transit frequency and coverage are limited compared to urban markets. There is no commuter rail connecting Sarasota County to Tampa.

For Tampa commuters who use transit, the most practical option is to drive to the Sarasota Amtrak station (when Silver Meteor/Silver Star service applies) or to use Greyhound. Neither is a realistic daily commute option. Remote work has made Nokomis a more practical choice for Tampa-area workers in the past few years.

Quick Answer

Nokomis FL is a quiet, unincorporated Sarasota County community on Florida's Gulf Coast. It offers beach access at Nokomis Beach, smaller-town feel compared to Venice and Sarasota, and relatively affordable home prices. Strong fit for retirees, second-home buyers, and remote workers. Key trade-offs are limited walkability, coastal flood risk in lower-lying areas, and no major grocery within Nokomis proper. Home prices range from $350,000 for inland homes to $3 million or more on Casey Key.

Nokomis sits between Venice to the south and Osprey to the north along Sarasota County's Gulf Coast. It is an unincorporated community, which means no city government and generally lower overhead costs than incorporated cities. I have worked with buyers relocating here from the Northeast and Midwest who want beach proximity, outdoor recreation, and a noticeably slower pace than you get in Sarasota proper. Nokomis typically delivers that, with a few important caveats.

What Is Nokomis FL?

Nokomis is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County, centered around the 34275 ZIP code. The population is approximately 3,700 residents within the defined community area, though the surrounding Sarasota County unincorporated zones add thousands more nearby. Nokomis Beach (also called North Jetty Park) provides free Gulf access at the southern end of Albee Road. Casey Key, a narrow barrier island just offshore, is one of the most exclusive residential addresses in Sarasota County with a limited number of estate homes and beach cottages accessible via two drawbridges.

Sarasota County administers all services here: property taxes, roads, utilities coordination, and permitting. There are no city-specific fees or a city commission to deal with, which some buyers prefer. Zoning and planning go through Sarasota County, and land use is predominantly low-density residential with some commercial along US-41 (Tamiami Trail).

Why People Choose Nokomis Over Sarasota or Venice

The common thread I hear from buyers who specifically target Nokomis is value. Compared to Sarasota, you get similar beach proximity at a meaningfully lower price point, without the commercial density and traffic congestion of the US-41 corridor through downtown Sarasota. Compared to Venice, Nokomis tends to offer slightly quieter residential areas, though Venice has more walkable downtown dining and retail.

Who Nokomis Works Best For

Retirees seeking beach proximity at a lower cost than Osprey or Sarasota. Remote workers who can work from anywhere and want Gulf Coast weather and outdoor recreation. Second-home buyers looking for a beach base within 75 miles of Tampa. Long-term holders interested in Sarasota County appreciation trends without the premium of Sarasota zip codes.

Who Nokomis May Not Work For

Buyers who want walkability and daily errands on foot will be disappointed. Nokomis has no walkable downtown. Young families looking for the most highly rated schools may prefer areas with A-rated elementary and middle schools throughout. Buyers sensitive to flood risk need to carefully check FEMA flood maps before making any offer, particularly in lower-elevation areas near Dona Bay and the Intracoastal.

Flood Risk in Nokomis FL

Flood risk is the single most important thing to investigate before buying in Nokomis. Parts of the community lie in FEMA Zone AE, which is the high-risk flood designation that triggers mandatory flood insurance if you carry a federally backed mortgage. Lower-elevation areas near Dona Bay, Lyons Bay, and the Intracoastal Waterway carry the highest risk. Inland higher-ground areas are generally Zone X, which is the moderate-to-low risk designation. Casey Key is a barrier island with significant storm surge exposure.

Always verify the flood zone for any specific property using the FEMA Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov before making an offer. An elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor can determine whether you actually pay for mandatory flood insurance or qualify for a lower-risk rating. Florida Power and Light (FPL) is the primary electric utility for Nokomis. Water and sewer service is provided by Sarasota County Utilities for most of the community, though some older and more rural parcels still rely on private wells and septic systems.
