title: Nokomis FL Property Taxes
excerpt: Nokomis FL Property Taxes, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

What are property taxes in Nokomis FL?

Nokomis FL is in Sarasota County. The combined millage rate for unincorporated county areas runs approximately 17-20 mills, meaning you pay $1,700-$2,000 per $100,000 of assessed value. On a $400,000 assessed property, annual property taxes run approximately $7,000-$8,000 before the Florida homestead exemption. The $50,000 homestead exemption reduces taxable value and saves approximately $850-$1,000 per year. Check the Sarasota County Property Appraiser at sc-pa.com for any specific parcel.

Property taxes are one of the more confusing line items for buyers relocating to Florida from other states. In some northern states, property taxes are assessed at full market value but at low millage rates. Florida operates differently, the assessed value can diverge significantly from market value due to the Save Our Homes cap, and the rates vary by municipality. Understanding what you will actually pay as a new buyer is essential before you budget.

I walk every buyer through the property tax math before we make an offer. The Sarasota County Property Appraiser website at sc-pa.com lets you look up any parcel's current assessed value, homestead status, and most recent tax bill. It is one of the most useful buyer research tools in the county.

How Sarasota County Property Taxes Work

Assessed Value vs. Market Value

The Sarasota County Property Appraiser determines the assessed value, which is supposed to reflect market value but is constrained for homesteaded properties by the Save Our Homes (SOH) cap. The SOH cap limits annual increases in assessed value to 3% or the CPI, whichever is less, for primary residences. A homeowner who purchased in 2010 at $250K may have an assessed value well below the current $500K market value.

When you buy a property, the SOH cap resets. Your assessed value will be recalculated to market value in the year following your purchase. This means your property tax bill as a new buyer will typically be higher than what the seller was paying, sometimes significantly so.

Millage Rates in Nokomis / Unincorporated Sarasota County

The millage rate is expressed as dollars per $1,000 of taxable value. For unincorporated Sarasota County areas (which includes Nokomis), the combined millage rate includes the county general fund, the school board levy, and various special district levies. The total typically falls in the 17-20 mill range. One mill equals $1 per $1,000 of taxable value, so 18 mills on $350,000 taxable value is $6,300/year.

Tax Levying BodyApproximate Millage (2025)Notes
Sarasota County General~4.7 millsCounty services, roads, parks

TOTAL (approx.)~18-20 millsUnincorporated Nokomis typical

Exact millage rates are set annually by each governing body. The Sarasota County Tax Collector publishes the current year's rates at sarasotataxcollector.com.

Florida Homestead Exemption in Nokomis

The $50,000 Exemption

Florida's homestead exemption reduces the taxable value of a primary residence by $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities. The second $25,000 applies to all taxing authorities except the school board levy. This means the effective savings depend on the blended rate, but typically the homestead exemption saves $850-$1,100 per year in Sarasota County.

Additional Exemptions

Florida offers additional homestead exemptions for qualifying seniors (65+), veterans with disabilities, first responders with disabilities, and widows/widowers. A senior exemption can provide an additional $25,000-$50,000 reduction in assessed value. The Sarasota County Property Appraiser office at sc-pa.com has the current exemption applications.

How to Apply for Homestead Exemption

You must file for homestead exemption by March 1 of the year following your purchase. File online at sc-pa.com or in person at the Sarasota County Property Appraiser office. You will need your Florida driver's license or ID with the Nokomis address and the property deed. You must occupy the property as your primary residence on January 1 of the application year.

These are estimates based on approximately 18 mills total millage. Actual bills will vary. Note that the first year after purchase you may pay taxes based on the prior owner's assessment if you close late in the year. The following January the reset occurs.

Non-Ad Valorem Assessments in Nokomis

Some Nokomis properties carry non-ad valorem assessments, special charges that appear on the tax bill but are not based on property value. Common examples include stormwater utility fees and solid waste assessments. These appear as line items on the annual tax bill separate from the millage calculation. Review the specific parcel's tax bill at sarasotataxcollector.com to see all charges.

CDD Fees in Nokomis Area

Nokomis itself has limited CDD-governed communities. Adjacent areas like parts of Osprey and newer Venice-area developments sometimes carry CDD (Community Development District) fees that appear on top of regular property taxes. excerpt: New Construction in Nokomis FL, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

Is there new construction in Nokomis FL?

New construction in Nokomis FL is very limited. Nokomis is a fully built-out unincorporated community with almost no vacant land available for subdivision development. Most 'new construction' in Nokomis is custom infill, teardown and rebuild on an existing lot, or construction on a rare vacant parcel. Buyers seeking new construction near Nokomis should expand their search to Venice (5 miles south), North Port (20 miles south), or North Sarasota.

New construction is the number one question from buyers relocating from markets like Tampa, Orlando, or out-of-state where master-planned communities with new homes are abundant. Nokomis simply does not have that product. The community is surrounded by water on the west, conservation land and existing development to the north and south, and established neighborhoods to the east. There is no large tract of vacant, developable land waiting for a national builder.

That is not necessarily bad news. It means Nokomis retains its character, quiet, established, tree-canopy streets, mature landscaping. But buyers who need a new-construction warranty and the peace of mind that comes with it should understand they are looking at a different buying experience here.

New Construction Options in and Near Nokomis FL

Custom Infill in Nokomis

The most common form of new construction in Nokomis is a teardown-and-rebuild. An older home on a desirable lot, particularly a waterfront lot on Roberts Bay or Blackburn Bay, is purchased, demolished, and replaced with a custom-built home. These projects typically take 12-18 months from land acquisition to completion. Custom build costs in Sarasota County run $280-$400+ per square foot depending on finish level and lot conditions.

Buyers interested in this path need to buy the land first. Waterfront lots suitable for a custom build start around $400K-$700K on the bay and can exceed $1M for larger or better-positioned parcels. The combined land-plus-build cost typically runs $1.2M-$3M+ for a quality waterfront custom home.

Casey Key Custom Estates

Casey Key has its own active, quiet market for custom construction. The island attracts high-net-worth buyers who want a Gulf or bay-front estate built to their specifications. Finding a suitable lot on Casey Key is the hard part, existing estates rarely come to market as land-only sales. When they do, they go quickly.

Venice FL New Construction (5 Miles South)

Venice is the nearest market with meaningful new construction activity. Legacy Trail and the South Venice area have seen infill construction. The Venice Farms development and scattered builder projects in the greater Venice area offer new construction, primarily in the $450K-$750K range. National builders are less prevalent in Venice than in North Port or Sarasota north. Mattamy Homes, Neal Communities, and D.R. Horton have had presence in the Venice/Nokomis corridor at various points.

North Port FL New Construction (20 Miles South)

North Port has one of the most active new construction markets in Sarasota County. The city has large tracts of platted lots available, and national and regional builders including D.R. Horton, Maronda Homes, and local custom builders have active projects. Entry-level new construction in North Port starts around $290K-$350K. This is the right call for buyers who prioritize new construction and are flexible on location. North Port is 20-25 miles south of Nokomis on US-41 or I-75.

Sarasota North and Lakewood Ranch (15-25 Miles North)

North Sarasota and Lakewood Ranch (Manatee County but functionally Sarasota market) have active master-planned new construction. Lakewood Ranch is one of the most successful planned communities in the US and has phases that include homes from the $500Ks to several million dollars. Drive time from Nokomis to Lakewood Ranch is 25-40 minutes depending on traffic.

What Buyers Should Know About Infill Construction in Nokomis

Permit Requirements

All new construction in Nokomis requires Sarasota County building permits. The county's building department reviews plans for compliance with current Florida Building Code, including wind speed requirements, flood zone regulations, and energy efficiency standards. In Zone AE or Zone VE areas, freeboard requirements dictate how high the finished floor must be above base flood elevation. Getting the land and the permitting process right before breaking ground is critical.

FEMA Flood Zone Elevation Requirements

Any new construction in a flood zone in Nokomis must meet FEMA's minimum elevation standards plus any Sarasota County freeboard requirements. In Zone AE, the finished floor must be at or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE). Sarasota County may require additional freeboard (typically 1-2 feet above BFE). In Zone VE, requirements are more stringent, open foundations (pilings or columns) are required, and breakaway walls are standard. Building in Zone VE significantly increases construction cost.

Utility Connections

Any new home on an existing lot needs to verify utility availability. If the parcel has existing water/sewer connections, they can typically be reused. If the property is on well/septic and you want to connect to county utilities, you need to check availability and capacity with Sarasota County Utilities. Connection fees can run $5,000-$15,000+ depending on the situation.

title: Investing in Nokomis FL Real Estate
excerpt: Investing in Nokomis FL Real Estate, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

Is Nokomis FL a good place to invest in real estate?

Nokomis FL offers two distinct investment angles: long-term rental of inland homes (modest cash flow, appreciation play) and short-term vacation rentals near Nokomis Beach (stronger gross revenue, higher management cost). The combination of beach proximity, Sarasota County amenities, and limited inventory creates a floor under values. The main headwind is insurance cost, waterfront investment math requires careful modeling of $10,000-$25,000+ annual insurance against rental income.

Investment property in Nokomis is not for the first-time investor looking for an easy deal. The numbers here require careful underwriting because the same beach proximity and scarcity that make Nokomis attractive also mean purchase prices are high relative to achievable rents for long-term tenants. Where Nokomis shines is in the short-term vacation rental market, seasonal demand is strong and nightly rates near the beach are competitive.

I have worked with investors in Nokomis and the surrounding Sarasota County market. Let me break down what the numbers actually look like.

Long-Term Rental Investment in Nokomis FL

Market Rents

Long-term rental market rents in Nokomis in 2026: 2-bedroom home or villa $1,600-$2,100/month; 3-bedroom single-family home $1,900-$2,600/month; 4-bedroom home $2,400-$3,200/month. Vacancy rates are low because rental supply is tight. Most Nokomis rental units are owner-occupants who became accidental landlords or inherited the property.

Sample Long-Term Rental Math

Purchase price: $420,000. Down payment (25% investment): $105,000. Loan ($315K at 7.25%, 30-year): ~$2,148/month P&I. Property taxes: ~$625/month. Homeowner's insurance (Zone X): ~$450/month. HOA (if applicable): $0-$200/month. Maintenance reserve: $250/month. Total expenses: ~$3,473-$3,673/month.

Gross rental income at $2,200/month: $2,200/month. Net cash flow: negative $1,273-$1,473/month. This is typical for many Sarasota coastal markets, you are buying appreciation and principal paydown, not cash flow, in the long-term rental model. Cap rate for this scenario is approximately 3-4%, which is not attractive on its own but can be compelling if combined with 3-5% annual appreciation.

When Long-Term Rental Works in Nokomis

Long-term rental pencils better in Nokomis when: (1) you have a large down payment reducing the mortgage load, (2) you inherit or purchase a property with a lower basis, (3) you are buying for eventual personal use and renting in the interim, or (4) you pair the rental income with tax benefits including depreciation.

Short-Term Vacation Rental Investment in Nokomis FL

Nokomis Beach Demand

Nokomis Beach is a Sarasota County beach park at the northern end of Casey Key, accessible from US-41. It is less crowded than Siesta Key and Venice Beach, making it appealing to visitors who want a quieter Gulf beach experience. The beach attracts seasonal snowbirds (November-April) and families in summer. Vacation rental demand in the Nokomis vicinity tracks this seasonal pattern.

Short-Term Rental Revenue Estimates

A well-managed 3-bedroom home within 1-2 miles of Nokomis Beach can achieve gross short-term rental revenue in the range of $40,000-$65,000 annually in 2026, with peak months (January-April) generating $3,500-$6,000/month. Off-peak months (May-September, excluding July) may generate $1,500-$3,000/month. Occupancy rates of 60-75% are achievable with good management and pricing strategy.

Short-Term Rental Regulations in Sarasota County

Sarasota County regulates short-term rentals (rentals under 30 days). County Ordinance No. 2020-056 established a vacation rental registration and inspection program. Property owners must register with the county, pay annual fees, meet minimum safety standards (smoke detectors, pool barriers, fire extinguishers), and designate a local contact person reachable 24/7. Florida state law limits how much counties can restrict vacation rentals, but the registration and safety requirements are in place.

Some Nokomis HOA communities prohibit or limit short-term rentals. Casey Key has deed restrictions on some properties that restrict rental frequency. Verify the specific property's status before purchasing for short-term rental use.

Casey Key Investment Considerations

Casey Key is a different investment class entirely. Properties on Casey Key are trophy assets. The investment thesis is appreciation and exclusivity, not rental yield. Some Casey Key properties are deed-restricted against short-term rentals. Flood insurance costs (Zone VE) eliminate most yield even if rents are high. Buyers at this level are generally purchasing for lifestyle, second-home use, or estate planning, not cash flow.

Is Nokomis FL a cash-flow positive rental market?

Not typically for long-term rentals purchased at current prices with conventional financing. Cap rates are 3-4%. Short-term vacation rentals near the beach can achieve 5-7% cap rates under good management.

What are short-term rental regulations in Nokomis FL?

Sarasota County requires vacation rental registration, annual fees, safety inspections, and a 24/7 local contact person. HOA and deed restrictions may further limit short-term rentals. Verify before purchase.

A 3-bedroom single-family home within 1-2 miles of Nokomis Beach, in Zone X (no mandatory flood insurance), with no HOA short-term rental restrictions offers the best investment profile for vacation rental use.

title: Waterfront Homes in Nokomis FL
excerpt: Waterfront Homes in Nokomis FL, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

What waterfront homes are available in Nokomis FL?

Nokomis FL offers three tiers of waterfront real estate: Intracoastal Waterway and bay homes on Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay ($600K-$2.5M), bay-front estates on Casey Key ($2M-$6M), and Gulf-front estates on Casey Key ($2.5M-$15M+). All waterfront properties are in FEMA flood zones and carry significant mandatory flood insurance requirements. Dock access to the Gulf is available for most waterfront properties via Stump Pass or New Pass.

Waterfront real estate in Nokomis sits at the intersection of a very desirable location and very real flood risk. The same water that makes these properties beautiful is the water that came inland during Hurricane Ian in September 2022, causing significant damage to coastal Sarasota County properties. Buyers of waterfront homes in Nokomis need to understand the flood zone, the insurance cost, the elevation certificate, and the dock permitting process before they fall in love with a listing.

That said, for buyers who do their homework and underwrite correctly, Nokomis waterfront offers something you cannot get in most of the Tampa Bay market, direct Gulf access through two passes, some of the best fishing and boating on Florida's Gulf Coast, and the exclusivity of Casey Key, which has no commercial development and very few full-time residents.

Waterfront Areas in Nokomis FL

Roberts Bay (Intracoastal Waterway)

Roberts Bay is a protected bay that is part of the Intracoastal Waterway system, located between the Nokomis mainland and Casey Key. Homes on Roberts Bay have dock access to the ICW with boat access to the Gulf via New Pass (Venice Inlet) to the south or Venice Inlet / Stump Pass system. Roberts Bay homes typically feature concrete seawall, covered boat dock, and boat lift. Water depth varies, typically 4-7 feet at the dock, with the main channel deeper. The bay is protected from direct wave action, making it relatively calm for docking even in moderate weather.

Home prices on Roberts Bay range from approximately $700K for dated, smaller homes on modest lots to $2.5M+ for larger, updated homes with better water frontage and dock improvements. Post-Ian, some owners sold at distressed prices and buyers who purchased in 2023-2024 got favorable entry points.

Blackburn Bay (Intracoastal Waterway)

Blackburn Bay is north of Roberts Bay, on the ICW between Osprey and the northern end of Casey Key. The Blackburn Point Road area provides access to the bay and to the swing bridge at the north end of Casey Key. Waterfront homes on Blackburn Bay are similar in character to Roberts Bay properties, ICW frontage, dock access, and Gulf access through New Pass. Prices are comparable.

Casey Key Bay-Front (East Side of Island)

Casey Key's east side faces Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay. Bay-front properties here have private docks, calm water, and sweeping views of the Intracoastal. Homes range from modestly sized older structures in the $2M range to large custom estates on substantial frontage at $4M-$6M. The bay-front tier on Casey Key is more price-accessible than the Gulf side but still carries full Zone AE or Zone VE flood zone designations.

Casey Key Gulf-Front (West Side of Island)

The west side of Casey Key fronts directly on the Gulf of Mexico. This is one of the most exclusive stretches of barrier island real estate in Florida. There is no commercial development. Properties are primarily large single-family homes set back from the shoreline in compliance with setback requirements. Gulf-front homes run $2.5M on the low end for older, smaller structures to well above $15M for large, fully renovated estates with beach frontage. These properties are in FEMA Zone VE, the highest-risk coastal zone. Insurance costs, building restrictions, and setback rules are all significantly more onerous here than anywhere else in Nokomis.

Boating and Gulf Access from Nokomis Waterfront

Stump Pass and Englewood Beach Channel

Stump Pass is south of Nokomis, between Manasota Key (Englewood side) and the southern end of Casey Key. It provides a channel from the ICW to the Gulf. The pass is relatively shallow and unmarked in places, local knowledge of the tides and sand bar positions is essential. Many boaters prefer Venice Inlet (New Pass) to the south as the more reliable deepwater exit to the Gulf.

Venice Inlet (New Pass)

Venice Inlet, also called New Pass, is the primary deep-water channel from Roberts Bay and the ICW south of Nokomis to the Gulf of Mexico. The inlet is maintained and relatively reliable for vessels drawing up to 5-6 feet. It provides access to fishing grounds offshore, the Venice fishing pier area, and the Gulf Coast boating network. Most Nokomis bay homeowners use New Pass for Gulf access.

Dock Permitting and Regulations in Nokomis

Dock construction and replacement in Nokomis requires permits from Sarasota County and, for docks on the ICW, a permit from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and in some cases the Army Corps of Engineers. The permitting timeline can be 3-12 months depending on the complexity and environmental review required.

Roberts Bay is adjacent to state-designated Aquatic Preserves. Activities in or near aquatic preserve areas face additional scrutiny. Dock materials, size, and configuration are regulated. Seagrass surveys may be required.

Flood Insurance for Nokomis Waterfront Homes

Every federally backed mortgage on a property in FEMA Zone AE or Zone VE requires flood insurance. Nokomis waterfront properties fall into these zones. Flood insurance can be obtained through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or through private flood insurance carriers. NFIP coverage caps at $250,000 for the structure and $100,000 for contents. For higher-value waterfront homes, excess flood coverage through private carriers is essential.

Private flood insurance can cost $5,000-$18,000 per year for a waterfront Nokomis home depending on the elevation certificate, flood zone, and coverage amount. Get an elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor before purchase, it is the key document that determines your flood insurance rate.

What is the cheapest waterfront home in Nokomis FL?

Entry-level waterfront on Roberts Bay or Blackburn Bay starts around $600K-$700K for smaller, dated homes. These properties need updating and carry significant insurance costs but provide genuine Gulf boat access.

How is the boating from Nokomis FL waterfront homes?

Excellent. Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay both connect to the ICW. Gulf access is via Venice Inlet (New Pass), a reliable deep-water channel. Fishing and boating are primary reasons people buy waterfront in this area.

Is Casey Key accessible to visitors?

Casey Key has two access points, Blackburn Point Road with a swing bridge from the north, and a southern entrance near Osprey. There is no commercial activity on the island. Most of the island is private residential.

Bay homes on Roberts Bay and Blackburn Bay are typically Zone AE. Casey Key Gulf-front properties are Zone VE, the highest-risk coastal designation. Both require mandatory flood insurance with federally backed mortgages.

Annual dock maintenance including inspection, hardware replacement, and anti-fouling treatment runs $500-$2,000 depending on dock size and material. A complete dock replacement (wood, 40 ft pier with lift) can run $40,000-$80,000+ depending on permitting and scope.

title: Nokomis FL Flood Zones Guide
excerpt: Nokomis FL Flood Zones Guide, Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. Call (813) 733-7907.
content:
Quick Answer

What flood zones exist in Nokomis FL and what do they mean for buyers?

Nokomis FL properties fall into three primary FEMA flood zone categories: Zone VE (coastal high-hazard on Casey Key Gulf side, highest risk, mandatory flood insurance required), Zone AE (100-year floodplain covering most waterfront and low-lying areas, mandatory flood insurance with federally backed mortgages), and Zone X (minimal flood risk in inland elevated areas, flood insurance optional). Check any property at msc.fema.gov. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to discuss flood zone implications before making an offer.

Flood zone is one of the first things I tell buyers to check in Nokomis. It is not a formality. Hurricane Ian (September 2022) demonstrated exactly what FEMA's flood maps predict, surge water moved inland through the bays, the ICW, and the Gulf-front barrier islands in patterns that aligned closely with the flood zone boundaries. Properties in Zone AE and Zone VE were in the water. Properties in Zone X with good elevation were not.

The practical impact of flood zone for Nokomis buyers is: (1) whether flood insurance is required, (2) how much it costs, and (3) what elevation your new construction or addition must achieve. These are not abstractions, they directly affect your monthly payment and your ability to get a mortgage.

FEMA Flood Zone Categories in Nokomis FL

Zone VE, Coastal High-Hazard Area

Zone VE is the most severe FEMA flood zone designation. In Nokomis, Zone VE applies primarily to the Gulf-front side of Casey Key and portions of Nokomis Beach park area. The 'V' stands for Velocity, these areas receive not just flooding but wave action during major storm events. New construction in Zone VE must use open-foundation design (pilings or columns) with breakaway walls below the first floor. Finished floor elevations must be at or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) plus freeboard. Existing structures may not meet current standards and face challenges with insurance and resale.

Flood insurance in Zone VE is mandatory for federally backed mortgages and is the most expensive tier. Private flood insurance quotes for Zone VE properties in Nokomis commonly run $8,000-$20,000 per year for the structure alone. Cash buyers sometimes purchase without flood insurance but this is a significant risk given the real storm history.

Zone AE, High-Risk, 100-Year Floodplain

Zone AE is the most common flood zone designation for Nokomis waterfront properties outside of the Gulf-direct zones. Zone AE means the area has a 1% annual chance of flooding (the so-called "100-year flood") and the Base Flood Elevation has been determined by engineering study. Roberts Bay waterfront homes, Blackburn Bay properties, and bay-side Casey Key are predominantly Zone AE.

Flood insurance is mandatory in Zone AE for federally backed mortgages (FHA, Fannie, Freddie, USDA, VA). NFIP coverage up to $250,000 for structure, $100,000 for contents. Annual premiums for Nokomis Zone AE properties run approximately $3,500-$12,000 depending on the elevation certificate and NFIP risk rating 2.0 calculation. Homes with higher elevation relative to BFE pay lower premiums.

Zone X, Minimal Flood Risk

Zone X covers areas outside the 500-year floodplain, the lowest-risk designation. Most inland Nokomis subdivisions away from the bay and creek systems are Zone X. Flood insurance is not required for federally backed mortgages in Zone X, though it is available and optional. Zone X is often incorrectly described as "out of the flood zone", technically it means lower risk, not zero risk. Extreme rainfall events can cause localized flooding even in Zone X areas.

Zone X properties in Nokomis are clustered in the elevated inland areas east of US-41, particularly in the higher portions of Sorrento East, Sorrento South, and the Laurel Road corridor back from the bay system. Homeowners in these areas pay homeowner's insurance only (no mandatory flood premium), saving $4,000-$12,000 per year compared to AE zone neighbors.

Zone X500, Moderate Risk

Some Nokomis areas fall in Zone X500 (shaded X on flood maps), which is the 500-year floodplain, moderate risk. Flood insurance is not required but is recommended. Properties in shaded X are generally in better shape than AE but still face some flood exposure.

How to Check the Flood Zone for Any Nokomis Property

The official source for flood zone information is FEMA's Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov. Enter the property address and the site will show the applicable Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) with the flood zone designation. The map also shows the effective date of the FIRM, Nokomis maps are periodically updated as conditions and study data change.

For a more precise determination, a licensed surveyor can produce a Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) request if a property appears to be in a higher-risk zone but the actual grade elevation is above the BFE. A LOMA can remove a property from a mandatory purchase requirement if the lowest adjacent grade is at or above BFE.

Elevation Certificates and Flood Insurance Rates

An elevation certificate is a document prepared by a licensed surveyor that records the building's lowest floor elevation, lowest adjacent grade, and other measurements relative to the FIRM's base flood elevation. Insurance companies use the elevation certificate to price flood insurance, the higher your building is relative to BFE, the lower your premium.

For existing Nokomis homes, ask the seller for the elevation certificate if one exists. For waterfront properties, always commission a new elevation certificate from a licensed surveyor as part of your due diligence, cost is typically $300-$600. The savings in annual insurance premium can pay for the survey cost within weeks.

Flood Zone Impact on Nokomis Construction Requirements

ZoneFoundation RequirementMin. Floor ElevationBreakaway Walls?Insurance Req.
Zone XStandard slab OKNo BFE requirementNoNot required
Zone AESlab or elevated OKAt or above BFE (+freeboard)NoRequired (federally backed)
Zone VEOpen (pilings/columns)At or above BFE (+freeboard)RequiredRequired (federally backed)

Post-Hurricane Ian and Flood Zone Reality in Nokomis

Hurricane Ian made landfall on September 28, 2022, near Fort Myers. Even though the direct landfall was to the south, Ian's storm surge and wind impacts extended throughout Sarasota County. Nokomis waterfront properties on Roberts Bay and the ICW experienced flooding that aligned with AE zone predictions. Casey Key took wind damage and some surge impacts, though the island's Gulf-front properties fared better than many locations to the south due to the storm track.

Post-Ian, flood insurance costs increased substantially as NFIP updated its risk modeling under Risk Rating 2.0 (implemented October 2021 and phased in through 2022-2023). Properties that had legacy low flood insurance premiums saw significant increases. Some homeowners saw flood insurance jump from $2,000/year to $8,000-$15,000/year as Risk Rating 2.0 caught up with actual risk. This insurance shock contributed to waterfront price corrections in 2023.

My Recommendations for Nokomis Flood Zone Due Diligence

Here is what I tell every buyer looking at waterfront or potentially flood-exposed properties in Nokomis: First, check the FEMA flood map before making an offer. Second, get an elevation certificate. Third, get flood insurance quotes from at least two providers, NFIP through an agent and at least one private flood insurer. Fourth, factor the full annual insurance cost into your budget. Fifth, if you are buying in Zone AE or VE, make sure you understand what Ian-like surge would look like at that specific elevation based on the elevation certificate reading.

Frequently Asked Questions About Nokomis FL Flood Zones

Is Nokomis FL in a flood zone?

Parts of Nokomis are in flood zones and parts are not. Waterfront properties on Roberts Bay, Blackburn Bay, and Casey Key are in FEMA Zone AE or Zone VE. Inland elevated properties are generally in Zone X, the low-risk designation. Check msc.fema.gov with the specific address.

What does Zone AE mean in Nokomis FL?

Zone AE means the property is in the 100-year floodplain with a mapped Base Flood Elevation. Flood insurance is mandatory for federally backed mortgages. Annual premiums for Nokomis AE properties run $3,500-$12,000 depending on the elevation certificate.

What does Zone VE mean in Nokomis FL?

Zone VE is the coastal high-hazard zone covering Gulf-front portions of Casey Key. It includes velocity wave action risk. New construction requires open foundation (pilings). Insurance is mandatory and expensive, commonly $8,000-$20,000+ per year.

How do I check the flood zone for a Nokomis property?

Go to msc.fema.gov, enter the property address, and the Flood Insurance Rate Map will show the zone designation. For precision, have a licensed surveyor produce an elevation certificate.

Did Nokomis FL flood during Hurricane Ian?

Hurricane Ian (September 2022) caused flooding in Nokomis waterfront areas, particularly along Roberts Bay and the ICW, consistent with Zone AE designations. Casey Key experienced wind damage and some surge. Inland Zone X properties generally remained dry.

What is an elevation certificate and why do I need one?

An elevation certificate documents the building's floor elevation relative to the FEMA Base Flood Elevation. Insurance companies use it to price flood insurance. A higher elevation means lower premiums. Commissioning one for $300-$600 can save thousands per year in insurance.

title: Moving to Nokomis FL: What to Know in 2025 | Complete Guide
excerpt: Moving to Nokomis FL: unincorporated Sarasota County, 34275 ZIP, beach access, homes from $320K-$700K+. Schools, utilities, commute times, shopping, healthcare, everything buyers need before relocating.
content:
Quick Answer

Nokomis is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County (34275 ZIP code) positioned between Venice (5 miles south) and Osprey (3 miles north), with beach access via Nokomis Beach on Casey Key. Homes range from $320K for smaller inland properties to $700K+ for Casey Key Gulf-front. Daily grocery shopping requires driving to Venice or Osprey. The commute to Sarasota is 20 to 30 minutes and to Tampa is 65 to 80 minutes.

Nokomis attracts buyers who want proximity to the Gulf of Mexico without paying full Venice or South Sarasota prices, and who appreciate the quiet, unincorporated character of a community without a downtown commercial core of its own. I'm Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective with 23+ years of real estate experience. Here's what you actually need to know before moving to Nokomis.

What Is Nokomis FL?

Nokomis is an unincorporated community, not a city or town with its own government. It falls entirely within Sarasota County's jurisdiction. The 34275 ZIP code covers Nokomis and parts of the surrounding area including portions of Laurel. Nokomis sits between US-41 (Tamiami Trail) and the Gulf of Mexico, with the Intracoastal Waterway (Dona Bay and Roberts Bay) between the mainland and Casey Key.

Because Nokomis is unincorporated, property owners pay Sarasota County taxes and fees but do not pay a separate city tax. County services (sheriff, county roads, county utilities in some areas) are the primary governance layer. This is a meaningful distinction for buyers comparing Nokomis to incorporated Venice, which has its own city government and city millage rate.

Housing Costs in Nokomis FL

Property Type Typical Price Range Notes
Inland condo/villa $280K to $420K 55+ communities present, HOA fees vary
Inland SFR $380K to $620K Established subdivisions east of US-41

Casey Key Gulf-front $1.5M to $5M+ Barrier island, very limited inventory
Casey Key bay-side $700K to $2M+ Intracoastal frontage with boat dock

Schools in Nokomis FL

Nokomis is served by Sarasota County Schools. The primary school serving the area is distinctive:

  • Laurel Nokomis School: A K, 8 combined school serving both elementary and middle grades. The K, 8 model means students stay at one campus through 8th grade, which many families appreciate for continuity. Located on Laurel Road.
  • Venice Senior High School: The public high school serving the Nokomis area, in Venice approximately 5 miles south. Venice High consistently performs well in Sarasota County rankings.

According to the Sarasota County School District, always verify school assignments by specific address before purchasing, boundaries can change.

Utilities in Nokomis FL

Electric

Florida Power and Light (FPL) serves Nokomis for electric. For a 3-bedroom, 1,600-square-foot home, expect monthly FPL bills of $130 to $230 in summer (June, September) and $80 to $140 in cooler months. Sarasota County summers are hot and humid, AC is the dominant cost driver. Homes with newer HVAC systems and good insulation run at the lower end.

Water and Sewer

Sarasota County Utilities serves much of Nokomis with public water and sewer. Some areas of Nokomis, particularly older homes and more rural areas east of US-41, are on well and septic. Always verify which applies to any specific property. County water/sewer combined bills typically run $70 to $120/month for average residential use.

Internet

Comcast Xfinity and Frontier (in some areas) serve Nokomis for internet. Frontier has been expanding fiber availability in Sarasota County. Speeds and availability vary by location, verify at any specific address before purchasing if reliable high-speed internet is important to your lifestyle or work.

Shopping, Dining, and Daily Life in Nokomis

Nokomis itself does not have a major grocery store or significant commercial center as of 2025. Daily shopping requires driving:

  • Venice (5 mi south): Publix, Winn-Dixie, Aldi, Target, extensive restaurant scene on Venice Avenue, Venice Island beaches
  • Osprey (3 mi north): Publix on US-41, some restaurants along the corridor
  • Sarasota (15 to 20 mi north): Full metropolitan amenities including Whole Foods, Total Wine, specialty dining, performing arts, Sarasota Memorial Hospital

The Nokomis area has a small selection of restaurants, a hardware store, and community services along US-41. For buyers who want to walk to restaurants and shops from home, Nokomis is not the right fit, Venice's walkable downtown is a better match. For buyers who want quiet residential character and are comfortable driving 5 to 10 minutes for daily needs, Nokomis works well.

Healthcare Access from Nokomis

  • Venice Regional Bayfront Health: ~5 miles south in Venice. Full-service community hospital with emergency services.
  • Sarasota Memorial Hospital: ~20 miles north in Sarasota. One of Florida's highest-rated regional hospitals, with comprehensive specialty care.
  • UF Health Venice: Additional healthcare option in Venice.
  • Primary care and specialists: Available in both Venice (5 mi) and Osprey/Sarasota (10 to 20 mi) corridors.

Tampa downtown ~65 mi 65 to 80 min I-75 N

Flood Zones in Nokomis, Know Before You Buy

Nokomis has significant flood zone exposure, more so than many inland communities. Areas west of US-41 near Dona Bay, Roberts Bay, and particularly Casey Key carry FEMA AE or VE flood zone designations requiring mandatory flood insurance. Areas east of US-41 are more commonly in Zone X (lower risk) but not universally so. Check the FEMA Flood Map Service Center for any specific property. Flood insurance adds $600 to $8,000+/year depending on zone, elevation, and property type. Always get an elevation certificate and flood insurance quotes during your inspection period.

Is Nokomis FL a good place to live?

Nokomis is a good fit for buyers who want Gulf Coast proximity, quiet residential character, and slightly lower prices than Venice or South Sarasota, without the urban density of Sarasota proper. It is best suited for retirees, remote workers, or buyers who do not need to commute daily to a major employment center. If you want a walkable downtown with restaurants and shops within easy reach of your front door, Venice's walkable downtown is a better fit. For buyers who value quiet and nature access and are comfortable driving for daily needs, Nokomis is a strong choice.

What is the cost of living in Nokomis FL compared to Venice?

Housing costs in Nokomis are generally 5 to 15% lower than comparable properties in the City of Venice, partly because Venice city taxes add a city millage on top of Sarasota County millage. The trade-off is fewer services and amenities within walking or short driving distance. Property taxes in Nokomis (unincorporated Sarasota County) are typically Sarasota County millage plus Sarasota County School Board, no city layer. On a $500,000 home, the annual property tax savings from being outside Venice city limits can be $800 to $1,500/year.

How far is Nokomis beach from the main residential areas?

Nokomis Beach on Casey Key is approximately 2 to 5 miles west of most inland Nokomis residential areas, accessible via Albee Road or Laurel Road to Casey Key. The drive takes 8 to 15 minutes depending on your starting point. Nokomis Beach is a less crowded alternative to Venice Beach, it has a parking area, restrooms, and a small picnic area but fewer commercial amenities than Venice Beach. Sunset at Nokomis Beach is a popular local tradition, and the beach tends to be quieter on weekdays than weekend afternoons.

What school does Nokomis FL feed into?

Most of Nokomis (34275 ZIP) feeds into Laurel Nokomis School (K, 8) and Venice Senior High School. The K, 8 model at Laurel Nokomis means students attend the same campus from kindergarten through 8th grade, which many families find beneficial. Sarasota County also has a robust choice and magnet school program, some families use open enrollment to attend schools outside their assigned zone. Is there an HOA in most Nokomis neighborhoods?

It varies by community. Nokomis has a mix of HOA communities (particularly newer subdivisions and gated communities) and non-HOA neighborhoods (older subdivisions and more rural areas). The presence or absence of an HOA is a significant lifestyle and cost consideration, HOA fees in Nokomis range from $0 to $400+/month depending on the community and amenities. Communities near Casey Key and the Intracoastal tend to have higher HOA fees due to gated access and amenity infrastructure. Always confirm HOA status and fee schedule before making an offer.

title: Things to Do in Nokomis FL | Beaches, Trails, and Nearby Attractions
excerpt: Things to do in Nokomis FL: Nokomis Beach on Casey Key, Legacy Trail cycling, Oscar Scherer State Park, Venice Island day trips, shark teeth hunting at Caspersen Beach, paddling Dona Bay.
content:
Quick Answer

Nokomis offers Nokomis Beach (quieter Gulf beach on Casey Key), the Legacy Trail (18.4-mile paved cycling and walking trail), Dona Bay paddling, and quick access to Oscar Scherer State Park (3 miles north in Osprey) and Venice Island's walkable downtown and beaches (5 miles south). Nokomis itself is residential in character, most activity is within a 10-minute drive.

Nokomis is a quiet unincorporated community in Sarasota County positioned between the outdoor recreation of Oscar Scherer State Park to the north and the walkable charm of Venice Island to the south. I'm Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective with 23+ years of real estate experience corridor. Here's an honest look at what Nokomis and the immediately surrounding area offer for residents and visitors.

Nokomis Beach, Casey Key

Nokomis Beach sits on the Gulf side of Casey Key, a narrow barrier island that runs roughly parallel to the mainland between Venice and Osprey. The beach is accessed via Albee Road off US-41. Key details:

  • Character: Local, unpretentious, less crowded than Siesta Key or Venice Beach on most weekdays. Wide sand, good shelling and shark tooth hunting, Gulf swimming.
  • Facilities: Parking lots (paid, county managed), restrooms, picnic pavilions, a volleyball area.
  • Nearby on Casey Key: The north end of Casey Key has Nokomis Beach; the southern end reaches Venice Inlet. The island itself is mostly private residential, with North Jetty Park near the southern tip offering another beach access point and the famous "shark tooth beach" reputation for fossil hunting.
  • Sunset tradition: Nokomis Beach draws a nightly sunset crowd, a spontaneous community gathering that is one of the area's most authentic daily rituals.

Legacy Trail, Cycling and Walking

The Legacy Trail is a 18.4-mile paved multi-use trail that runs from Venice in the south to Sarasota in the north, generally following the old Seaboard Coast Line railroad corridor. Nokomis sits roughly midway along the trail. Key details:

  • Total length: 18.4 miles one way (Venice Freight Depot to Culverhouse Nature Park in Sarasota)
  • Surface: Paved asphalt, suitable for road bikes, hybrid bikes, e-bikes, and pedestrians
  • Nokomis trailhead access: Laurel Road area provides convenient on-ramp for Nokomis residents heading north or south
  • Connection points: Trail connects to Venice Island to the south and to Sarasota's urban trail network at the northern end
  • Practical use: Some Nokomis residents commute by bike to Venice for dining or errands via the trail, the 5-mile Venice-to-Nokomis section is flat and shaded in parts

Oscar Scherer State Park, 3 Miles North in Osprey

Oscar Scherer State Park is the most significant natural area immediately accessible from Nokomis, located on US-41 in Osprey approximately 3 miles north. According to the Florida State Parks system, the park covers 1,384 acres and is one of the most important remaining habitats for the Florida scrub-jay, a federally threatened species found only in Florida.

  • Admission: $5/vehicle (up to 8 people), $2 per pedestrian/cyclist
  • Kayaking: South Creek, which runs through the park, is a popular kayak and canoe route. Kayak rentals are available at the park concession.
  • Swimming: Lake Osprey is a freshwater swimming area within the park, a rare freshwater swim option on an otherwise saltwater-focused coastline.
  • Trails: 15+ miles of trails through Florida scrub, pine flatwoods, and hammock habitats. Mountain biking is permitted on designated trails.
  • Camping: 104 campsites including full-hookup RV sites, popular year-round.
  • Florida Scrub-Jay viewing: The park's scrub-jay population is habituated to humans, bird watching here is exceptional for this species.

Paddling Dona Bay and Roberts Bay

The Intracoastal Waterway around Nokomis includes Dona Bay and Roberts Bay, shallow estuarine systems between the mainland and Casey Key. These bays offer excellent kayaking and paddleboarding, with abundant bird life (ospreys, herons, roseate spoonbills, pelicans), dolphins, and manatees in season. Launch points include the public ramp on Albee Road near the Casey Key bridge and several county parks. The water is shallow and calm enough for beginners and suitable for fishing by kayak, spotted sea trout, redfish, and sheepshead are common catches in the grass flats.

Venice Island, 5 Miles South

Venice is Nokomis's nearest full-service town and is one of the Gulf Coast's most walkable and livable small cities. The 5-mile drive (10 to 15 minutes on US-41) makes Venice the default destination for dining, shopping, and entertainment for Nokomis residents. What Venice offers:

  • Venice Avenue downtown: A walkable street lined with independent restaurants, boutique shops, and cafes. More artsy-local character than a typical Florida strip mall corridor.
  • Venice Beach: The main public beach at the foot of Venice Avenue, with parking, restrooms, and beach chair rentals. Wide beach, clear Gulf water, and the Venice Fishing Pier.
  • Caspersen Beach: Located south of Venice Beach, Caspersen is Florida's best-known shark tooth hunting beach. The rough sand and exposed rock layers concentrate fossil shark teeth, a practical reason many Gulf Coast visitors prefer Caspersen to more manicured beaches.
  • Venice Theatre: One of the oldest and most active community theaters in Florida, staging professional-quality productions year-round.
  • Farmers market: Venice Farmers Market runs Saturday mornings in downtown Venice, produce, artisans, food trucks, and community gathering.

Historic Spanish Point, Osprey

Historic Spanish Point is a 30-acre archaeological and historical site in Osprey, approximately 4 miles north of Nokomis on Little Sarasota Bay. Operated by the Gulf Coast Heritage Association, the site spans 5,000 years of human habitation, from prehistoric shell midden deposits through the 19th-century Webb family pioneer homestead and the early 20th-century estate of Chicago socialite Bertha Palmer. Walking trails connect archaeological excavations, a restored chapel, pioneer homestead buildings, and formal gardens. Admission: $15 adults, $5 children (ages 6 to 12). Open Tuesday, Sunday.

Sarasota Day Trips, 20 Miles North

Nokomis is within easy reach of Sarasota's cultural and entertainment amenities:

  • The Ringling: The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art complex includes one of the most significant art museums in Florida, the Ringling's historic Ca' d'Zan mansion, and the Circus Museum. A full day can easily be spent here.
  • Siesta Key Beach: Consistently ranked among the best beaches in the United States, with 99% quartz sand that stays cool to the touch even in summer. Approximately 25 miles from Nokomis.
  • St. Armands Circle: A walkable shopping and dining circle on Lido Key, adjacent to Lido Beach. Upscale restaurants and boutiques in a pleasant outdoor setting.
  • Sarasota Opera and performing arts: The Van Wezel Performing Arts Hall and Florida Studio Theatre offer Broadway touring shows, opera, and resident company productions year-round.

Questions About Nokomis Real Estate?

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective. 23+ years of real estate experience.

Contact Barrett Call (813) 733-7907

Frequently Asked Questions, Things to Do in Nokomis FL

Is Nokomis Beach good for swimming?

Yes, Nokomis Beach on Casey Key has clear Gulf water suitable for swimming with a gradual sandy bottom. The beach is generally calm compared to Atlantic-facing beaches, with the Gulf's characteristic warmer and calmer water. Sarasota County posts water quality and red tide advisories at the beach and on the county website when conditions are not ideal for swimming. The beach has no lifeguards, swim with awareness. Most days, particularly in fall and winter, conditions are excellent.

Can you find shark teeth at Nokomis Beach?

Yes, but the best shark tooth hunting near Nokomis is at Caspersen Beach in Venice, approximately 5 miles south. Caspersen Beach has rougher, coarser sand that concentrates fossil shark teeth from the offshore phosphate deposits. Nokomis Beach does yield teeth as well, particularly near the Casey Key jetties where wave action concentrates material. A simple mesh scoop (called a "Florida snow shovel" by locals) makes hunting much more productive than searching dry sand by eye. Shark teeth in this area include modern shark species plus prehistoric sharks, megalodon teeth are found occasionally, though not commonly.

What is the Legacy Trail and how do Nokomis residents access it?

The Legacy Trail is an 18.4-mile paved multi-use trail connecting Venice to Sarasota along the former Seaboard Coast Line railroad corridor. Nokomis residents can access the trail from several points along Laurel Road and Sorrento Road. The trail is free to use and open sunrise to sunset. It is one of the primary recreational amenities that Nokomis residents cite as a reason for choosing the area, the flat, shaded corridor is suitable for year-round cycling and walking.

Are there restaurants in Nokomis FL?

Nokomis has a small selection of restaurants, a handful of casual dining spots along US-41 and near the beach area. The dining scene in Nokomis proper is limited. Most Nokomis residents drive to Venice (5 miles south) for the primary restaurant and dining experience, Venice Avenue downtown has dozens of independent restaurants. Osprey (3 miles north) also has a growing restaurant corridor along US-41. For more extensive dining variety, Sarasota (20 miles north) offers the Gulf Coast's broadest restaurant selection outside Tampa and Naples.

Is Nokomis FL good for fishing?

Yes, the Nokomis area is excellent for both inshore and near-shore fishing. Dona Bay and Roberts Bay hold spotted sea trout, redfish, snook, sheepshead, and flounder in the grass flats accessible by kayak or small skiff. The Venice Fishing Pier (5 miles south) offers free public pier fishing for a wide variety of species. Offshore charter boats operate from Fisherman's Wharf in Nokomis, a small marina on the Intracoastal near the Casey Key bridge offers charter and guide services for Gulf fishing. Snook season, redfish, and Spanish mackerel runs are seasonal highlights for area anglers.

The Siesta Drive bridge connects this end to Sarasota's US-41 corridor.

Crescent Beach (Middle)

The middle section of Siesta Key stretches along Crescent Beach, which is the longest stretch of the island's Gulf-facing shoreline. This area has a mix of older condo complexes, single-family homes on the interior streets, and some of the island's larger lot properties. The beach here is quieter than the Village area. Most buyers looking for a primary residence or long-term rental target Crescent Beach streets.

Turtle Beach (South End)

Turtle Beach is at the southern tip of the island via Midnight Pass Road. This end is more residential and less touristy. Turtle Beach has a public boat ramp, smaller pavilion, and a different character from the north. Single-family homes in this area often have more lot size and some have canal or bayfront access. The Stickney Point Road bridge connects this end to the mainland via Clark Road.

What Buyers Need to Know Before Closing on Siesta Key

Flood Insurance Is Not Optional

Nearly all of Siesta Key falls in FEMA Zone VE or Zone AE. Zone VE is the highest-risk velocity zone assigned to Gulf-front properties. Zone AE covers bayfront and canal properties. Flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or a private carrier is required by any lender for Zone AE and VE properties. For a Gulf-front home valued at $2M+, flood insurance alone can run $8,000-$20,000+ per year.

Wind Insurance Is Expensive on a Barrier Island

Wind coverage for a barrier island property in Sarasota County is among the highest in Florida. Citizens Property Insurance covers some properties, but many Siesta Key owners use private surplus lines carriers. Budget $8,000-$25,000+ per year for wind coverage depending on home age, construction type, and value. Newer construction with impact glass, hip roofs, and strong connections gets better rates. Ask for a wind mitigation inspection before buying any older home.

Review HOA Documents Carefully

Many condo complexes on Siesta Key have rental restrictions that limit short-term rentals to 7-day or 30-day minimums, or restrict rentals to a certain number per year. If you plan to use the property as a vacation rental, verify the HOA documents, rules, and rental policy before making an offer. Some HOAs also have significant deferred maintenance or underfunded reserves, which can lead to special assessments. Florida's condo safety law (SB-4D) now requires structural inspections and reserve studies for older multistory condos.

Get a Full Inspection Including Seawall and Roof

On Siesta Key, inspections should cover the standard items plus seawall condition (for waterfront homes), dock and boat lift structure, flat roof sections common on older buildings, HVAC age (salt air accelerates corrosion), and any evidence of past flooding. Hurricane Milton hit the Sarasota coast in October 2024. Ask sellers for disclosure and FEMA flood claim history.

What is the median home price on Siesta Key?

Yes. Some of the older residential streets in the Siesta Key Village area and the Crescent Beach section have no-HOA single-family homes. These offer more flexibility for rental use. Prices for no-HOA SFH on Siesta Key typically start at $1.5M-$2M given land values.

title: Siesta Key FL Schools: Ratings, Zones, and Private Options
excerpt: Siesta Key FL Schools: Ratings, Zones, and Private Options -- Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective, Sarasota County real estate.
content:
Quick Answer

Siesta Key residents are served by Sarasota County Schools. The assigned schools are Phillippi Shores Elementary, Brookside Middle, and Sarasota High School. Pine View School for the Gifted (#1 in Florida) is available county-wide to qualifying students.

Which Public Schools Serve Siesta Key Residents?

Siesta Key is an unincorporated community in Sarasota County. Students who attend public school use the Sarasota County School District. The assigned school zone for most of Siesta Key runs through Phillippi Shores Elementary, Brookside Middle, and Sarasota High School. Always verify the current zone for a specific address with the Sarasota County School District, as boundary lines can shift.

Phillippi Shores Elementary School

Phillippi Shores Elementary serves grades K-5 and is located on South Tamiami Trail on the mainland near Siesta Key. The school is generally regarded as one of the stronger elementary schools in Sarasota County. It participates in the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme (IB PYP), which provides structured inquiry-based learning. Parents looking for an academically focused public elementary school near Siesta Key consider Phillippi Shores a strong option.

Brookside Middle School

Brookside Middle School serves grades 6-8 and is located in south Sarasota. The school draws students from Siesta Key and surrounding mainland neighborhoods. Brookside offers IB Middle Years Programme, which aligns with the IB PYP at Phillippi Shores, giving families a consistent international curriculum through middle school. Check current Niche and FLDOE grades before purchasing, as school performance data updates annually.

Sarasota High School

Sarasota High School (SHS) serves grades 9-12 and is the primary public high school for Siesta Key residents. Sarasota High is one of the older public high schools in the county. According to U.S. News and World Report rankings, Sarasota High School has historically ranked lower than nearby Riverview High School but still performs above the Florida average in several metrics. It offers AP courses and vocational programs. For families prioritizing academics, Riverview High School (assigned to properties in east Sarasota) typically ranks higher.

What Is Pine View School for the Gifted?

Pine View School for the Gifted is a free public school in Sarasota County open to students in grades 2 through 12 who meet gifted eligibility criteria. It is one of the most academically acclaimed schools in the United States, consistently ranked #1 in Florida and highly nationally. Pine View is not assigned by address, meaning a student on Siesta Key can attend if they qualify. Transportation is the family's responsibility.

Qualification requires meeting Florida's gifted criteria: typically an IQ score of 130+ and demonstrated educational need. The application process includes teacher/parent nomination, psychological evaluation, and review by the district. Because Pine View accepts students county-wide on a gifted basis, it draws high-achieving families across Sarasota County and can be a significant factor in a family's decision to settle in the area.

Private School Options Near Siesta Key

Out-of-Door Academy

Out-of-Door Academy (ODA) is a private PK-12 school with two campuses in the Sarasota area, including one near Siesta Key's side of the island on Bird Road. ODA is known for its rigorous academics and smaller class sizes. Tuition ranges from approximately $14,000/yr for lower school to $22,000+/yr for upper school. ODA is a popular choice for families relocating from larger metro areas who want a private school option with a strong college prep track.

Cardinal Mooney Catholic High School

Cardinal Mooney is a Catholic co-educational high school in Sarasota serving grades 9-12. It offers AP courses and has a strong athletic program. Tuition is lower than independent private schools. It draws Catholic families from across Sarasota County and some from Siesta Key.

Sarasota Military Academy

Sarasota Military Academy is a public charter school serving grades 6-12 with a military structure and strong academics. It operates within the Sarasota County school system, so there is no tuition for Sarasota County residents. It is particularly popular with families who want structure, discipline, and college preparation in a public school setting.

School zoning plays a smaller role in Siesta Key purchasing decisions than in most residential markets. The majority of Siesta Key buyers are purchasing second homes, investment properties, or vacation rentals. For these buyers, school assignment has little or no bearing on the purchase.

For buyers purchasing a primary residence with school-age children, the Sarasota County school zone does matter. Phillippi Shores Elementary with its IB program is considered a positive by families with young children. title: Siesta Key FL Commute: Drive Times and Bridge Access Guide
excerpt: Siesta Key FL Commute: Drive Times and Bridge Access Guide -- Barrett Henry, REMAX Collective, Sarasota County real estate.
content:
Quick Answer

Siesta Key is accessible via two bridges: Siesta Drive (north, to US-41) and Stickney Point Road (south, to Clark Road). Drive time to Tampa: 65-80 min off-peak, 90-150 min in rush. Sarasota is 10-20 min. No public transit to the island. Call (813) 733-7907 to discuss commute-friendly locations on the island.

How Do You Get On and Off Siesta Key?

Siesta Key is a barrier island with exactly two road access points. There is no other way on or off. Understanding this before buying is essential, because during high season and major events, both bridges can create significant delays.

Siesta Drive Bridge (North Access)

The Siesta Drive bridge connects the north end of Siesta Key to US-41 (Tamiami Trail) on the Sarasota mainland. This bridge leads directly into the Siesta Key Village area. Coming from downtown Sarasota, US-41 South to Siesta Drive is the most direct route. During tourist season, the Village area and the bridge approach can back up significantly on Friday and Saturday afternoons as visitors arrive. The north bridge is the primary access point for most residents living in the Siesta Key Village and Crescent Beach sections.

Stickney Point Road Bridge (South Access)

The Stickney Point Road bridge connects the south end of Siesta Key to Clark Road (US-72) on the mainland. This access point serves residents in the Crescent Beach south and Turtle Beach sections. Stickney Point Road connects to I-75 via Clark Road, making it the more practical route for commutes to points east, south, or north via I-75. If you are driving to Tampa, exiting via Stickney Point and taking Clark Road to I-75 North is typically faster than going through downtown Sarasota on US-41.

Tourist Season Bridge Congestion

Sarasota's tourist season runs October through April, with peak congestion from late December through Easter. On winter weekends, both bridges can back up with day-trip visitors, and summer also sees Florida families visiting the beach. Allow extra time on Friday afternoons and Saturday mornings year-round. This is not a deal-breaker for residents but is something to factor into your lifestyle expectations.

Is There Public Transportation on Siesta Key?

Sarasota County Area Transit (SCAT) does not operate routes directly onto Siesta Key island. Bus service operates on US-41 on the mainland, including routes near the Siesta Drive bridge intersection, but does not cross the bridge. For those without a car, rideshare (Uber, Lyft) and taxi services cover Siesta Key, but wait times can be 15-30 minutes during peak season, and surge pricing is common on weekend evenings.

There is no commuter rail, light rail, or express bus to Tampa from Siesta Key. The lack of transit options means car ownership is essentially required for anyone living on the island who commutes to work outside the immediate Sarasota area.

Siesta Key for Remote Workers

Remote workers have found Siesta Key to be an ideal base. The combination of beach access, a walkable village with coffee shops and restaurants, and relatively stable high-speed internet makes day-to-day life comfortable without a daily commute. Many residents I work with are location-independent professionals who chose Siesta Key specifically to decouple their lifestyle from a commute.

For remote workers who travel for work, SRQ airport is 20-30 minutes away and serves an increasing number of direct routes including flights to Northeast cities, Chicago, and hub connections. The proximity of a smaller airport without the traffic complexity of Tampa International is a practical advantage.

Siesta Key is approximately 10-15 miles from Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport (SRQ). The drive takes 20-30 minutes off-peak. During tourist season, traffic on US-41 and airport approach roads can add 10-15 minutes. SRQ serves a growing number of direct routes to northeast cities and hubs.

title: Is Siesta Key FL a Good Place to Live?
excerpt: Is Siesta Key FL a Good Place to Live?, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Siesta Key FL is an excellent place to live if you can afford it and want a genuine beach-lifestyle community with world-class sand and a walkable village. It is not a good fit for buyers on a budget, families who want to walk to school, or daily Tampa commuters. Property prices start around $700,000 for basic single-family homes and go well into the millions for Gulf-front. Most properties carry flood insurance requirements. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to discuss whether Siesta Key fits your situation.

What Makes Siesta Key FL Distinctive

Siesta Key is a barrier island in Sarasota County, connected to the mainland by two bridges, Stickney Point Road bridge at the south end and Siesta Drive bridge at the north. The island is approximately 5.5 miles long and 0.5 miles wide at its widest point. It has no major commercial development beyond Siesta Key Village, a low-rise collection of restaurants, shops, and bars that gives the island its walkable social hub.

The beach is the reason people come to Siesta Key and the reason they stay. Siesta Beach has been repeatedly rated the number one beach in the United States by TripAdvisor and Dr. Beach based on sand quality, water clarity, and beach width. The sand is 99% quartz crystal, which means it stays cool to the touch even on Florida's hottest summer days and has a fine, powdery texture unlike any other beach on the Gulf Coast.

I have worked with buyers across the entire Sarasota-Tampa Bay corridor, and Siesta Key occupies a genuinely unique position. The combination of world-class beach, walkable village, manageable island size, and access to Sarasota's arts and cultural scene makes it a lifestyle destination with no direct equivalent in Florida at any price point.

Hurricane and Flood Risk on Siesta Key FL

Siesta Key sits on a Gulf barrier island. This creates the same risk profile as every barrier island in Florida: meaningful hurricane and storm surge vulnerability. The island is in Sarasota County Evacuation Zone A, which is the highest-priority mandatory evacuation zone for major storms. County emergency management issues evacuation orders for Zone A when a Category 1+ hurricane threatens the coast.

FEMA flood zones on Siesta Key range from Zone AE (most of the island) to Zone VE (Gulf-front properties facing direct wave action). Flood insurance is required on virtually all Siesta Key properties with federally backed mortgages. Budget $3,000-$8,000+ per year for flood insurance depending on zone, elevation, and structure type.

Hurricane Irma (2017) and Hurricane Ian (2022) produced storm surge damage in Sarasota County. Siesta Key's beach-facing properties are most exposed to surge. Properties on the bay side of the island generally experience less surge risk than Gulf-front, though they are still in evacuation zones. Elevation above base flood elevation and proper hurricane shutters or impact windows materially reduce risk and can reduce insurance premiums.

HOA fees in condo buildings cover insurance on the structure (not the contents or unit interior), common area maintenance, reserves, and amenities. Florida's SB-4D structural inspection law has added scrutiny to buildings 30+ years old with 3 stories or more, which covers many of Siesta Key's older condo buildings.

Single-Family Homes

Single-family homes on Siesta Key occupy the island's interior streets, bayfront lots, and the rare Gulf-front parcels. Most SFH were built between the 1950s and 1990s. content:
Quick Answer

Owning on Siesta Key costs significantly more than mainland Sarasota due to wind and flood insurance. A $1M home with a mortgage can easily exceed $8,000-$10,000/month all-in. STR rental income can offset costs significantly for investment-oriented buyers. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to model your specific scenario.

What Are the True Monthly Costs of Owning on Siesta Key?

Siesta Key ownership costs are meaningfully higher than comparable mainland properties because of insurance. Wind and flood premiums on a barrier island can add $15,000-$40,000+ per year to your annual cost compared to an inland home of similar value. When budgeting for a Siesta Key purchase, insurance should be modeled before you make an offer, not after.

Cost Item$500K Condo (Zone AE)$1M SFH (Zone AE)$2.5M SFH (Zone VE)

Note: These are estimates. Actual costs vary by specific property, insurance carrier, loan terms, and HOA. Get actual insurance quotes for any specific property before finalizing your budget. Non-homesteaded properties (second homes, investment) pay higher effective property tax rates.

Wind Insurance Costs on Siesta Key

Wind insurance is typically the largest surprise cost for buyers coming from inland or northern states. Siesta Key's barrier island location puts it in the highest-risk classification for wind coverage. Florida's Citizens Property Insurance covers some properties, but many Siesta Key homes do not qualify or choose surplus lines carriers for higher coverage limits.

Factors That Affect Wind Insurance Rates

Roof type matters significantly. Hip roofs (sloped on all four sides) receive better rates than gable roofs. Roof age: roofs under 10 years old typically qualify for better rates. Impact-rated windows and doors can reduce premiums 10-25%. Documented wind mitigation through a certified inspection is one of the most valuable documents a seller can provide, as it often transfers with the property and can save thousands per year on the buyer's policy. Construction year also matters: post-2002 construction in Florida was built to substantially stronger wind codes.

Flood Insurance Costs on Siesta Key

Zone AE Properties

Bayfront, canal-front, and interior island properties not on the Gulf face are typically in FEMA Zone AE. The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) covers AE properties up to $250,000 for the structure and $100,000 for contents. For higher-value properties, private flood insurance fills the gap. Zone AE flood coverage typically runs $2,000-$8,000 per year through NFIP, with private carriers sometimes offering competitive rates with higher coverage limits.

Zone VE Properties

Gulf-front properties on Siesta Key fall in Zone VE (velocity zone), which includes wave action risk in addition to flood inundation. NFIP covers Zone VE but the rates are substantially higher than Zone AE, and coverage limits may be insufficient for high-value properties. Private flood insurance is common for Gulf-front properties. Premiums in Zone VE for a $2M+ home can be $12,000-$25,000+ per year. The elevation of the structure above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) is the primary driver of NFIP rates.

Utilities and Other Monthly Costs

Florida Power and Light (FPL) provides electricity to Siesta Key. Monthly electric bills for year-round residents average $150-$300 for condos and $250-$500+ for larger single-family homes, driven heavily by air conditioning. Sarasota County provides water and sewer service. Monthly water and sewer bills for a single-family home typically run $60-$120.

Internet service is available through Comcast/Xfinity on the island. Cable, streaming, and phone costs are similar to mainland rates. There are no toll roads on Siesta Key itself, but using the downtown Sarasota area or I-75 routes involves the standard toll costs on Florida roads.

Can Rental Income Offset Ownership Costs?

For buyers purchasing on Siesta Key as a short-term rental investment, the income potential is substantial. Siesta Key is one of the most recognized beach destinations in the United States. Peak season weekly rates for beachfront condos can run $3,000-$8,000 per week. Gulf-front homes command $8,000-$25,000+ per week in peak season. Off-season rates drop substantially, but 12-month gross revenues for well-located, professionally managed properties can reach $80,000-$250,000+.

However, this comes with real expenses: property management (typically 20-25% of gross for STR), cleaning fees, STR platform fees, maintenance, insurance, and HOA fees. Before projecting STR income, verify that the specific condo or community allows short-term rentals. Some HOAs on Siesta Key restrict rentals to 30-day or longer minimums.

Total all-in monthly costs for a $1M property often exceed $8,000-$10,000/month.

Wind insurance on Siesta Key is among the most expensive in Florida because barrier islands receive the highest-risk classification from insurers. For a $1M SFH on Siesta Key, wind insurance typically runs $8,000-$20,000+ per year depending on construction age, roof type, and specific location. Gulf-front homes or Zone VE properties pay the highest rates. Newer construction with hip roofs, impact windows, and verified mitigation features can get better rates.

Is flood insurance required on Siesta Key?

If you are financing the purchase, flood insurance is required for any property in Zone AE or VE, which covers most of Siesta Key. Even for cash purchases, flood insurance is strongly advisable given the island's exposure. NFIP (federal) rates for Zone AE typically run $2,000-$8,000+/year. Zone VE (Gulf-front) can be $8,000-$20,000+/year through private carriers since NFIP caps have limits that are often insufficient for high-value properties.

What are typical HOA fees for condos on Siesta Key?

HOA fees for Siesta Key condo buildings vary considerably. Older buildings with limited amenities run $400-$700/month. Buildings with pools, beachfront access, covered parking, and maintenance staff typically run $800-$1,500/month. Newer luxury towers with concierge services, fitness centers, and covered garages can run $1,500-$3,000+/month. HOA fees for SFH communities are much lower, typically $50-$300/month if any HOA exists.

Can rental income help offset costs on Siesta Key?

Yes, significantly. Siesta Key is one of Florida's most active short-term rental markets. Gulf-front homes and beachfront condos can generate $5,000-$25,000+ per week during peak season (January-March). A well-managed STR property can generate $60,000-$250,000+ in annual gross revenue depending on property type, condition, and location. This income can substantially offset ownership costs, but it does not eliminate them. You need an HOA that permits STR, and you need to factor in management costs, cleaning, and off-season vacancy.

content:
Quick Answer

Siesta Key is in unincorporated Sarasota County with a combined millage rate of approximately 13.0-14.0 mills. A $1M home without homestead exemption pays approximately $13,000-$14,000/year in property taxes. Most Siesta Key owners do not qualify for homestead exemption since the majority of properties are second homes or investment properties. Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to discuss tax implications.

How Are Property Taxes Calculated on Siesta Key?

Florida property taxes are calculated by multiplying the assessed value by the applicable millage rate, then subtracting any exemptions. Siesta Key is unincorporated Sarasota County, so you pay the county millage rate (there is no additional city millage). The Sarasota County Property Appraiser determines the assessed value of your property based on market data. The Value Adjustment Board hears appeals.

Note: Florida's assessment value is typically set close to market value for non-homesteaded properties. The first-year assessment after purchase often reflects the sale price. These are estimates only.

Does the Homestead Exemption Apply on Siesta Key?

Most Siesta Key property owners do not qualify for Florida's homestead exemption because the property is not their primary residence. Homestead requires that the property be your permanent residence as of January 1 of the tax year, supported by Florida driver's license, voter registration (if registered), and a Declaration of Domicile filed with the Clerk of Courts.

If you do establish Siesta Key as your primary residence, the homestead exemption provides a $50,000 reduction in assessed value (first $25,000 applies to all tax rates; second $25,000 applies to non-school millage). At a combined rate of approximately 13.5 mills, this saves approximately $550-$600 per year (because the full exemption does not reduce school district taxes). The more significant benefit is the Save Our Homes cap.

Save Our Homes Cap and How It Works

Once you establish homestead, the Florida Save Our Homes (SOH) amendment limits your annual property tax assessment increase to 3% or the rate of CPI inflation, whichever is lower. Over 10-15 years in a rising market, this creates a substantial gap between your assessed value and market value, significantly reducing your tax bill relative to a new buyer.

Example: If you buy a Siesta Key home for $2M as your primary residence and establish homestead, your assessment is capped at 3% growth per year. After 10 years in a market where values grew 5-7% annually, your assessed value might be $2.5M while market value is $3.5M, saving you $13,500+ per year in taxes versus a new buyer assessed at market.

When you sell, the new buyer loses the SOH cap and is assessed at the new market value. SOH savings are transferable to a new Florida homestead via portability within three years.
