title: Ozona FL Schools: Palm Harbor Cluster Guide (2025)
excerpt: Ozona FL Schools Guide: Ratings and Zones, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona is served by Ozona Elementary, Palm Harbor Middle School, and Palm Harbor University High School (PHUH). All three are Pinellas County public schools. PHUH offers an International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme and consistently earns an A rating, making it one of the top public high schools in the Tampa Bay region. Always verify school zone at pcsb.org before closing.

Ozona, FL Schools: Complete Guide for Families

For families buying in Ozona, the Palm Harbor school cluster is a genuine selling point. Palm Harbor University High School is consistently ranked among Florida's best public high schools and offers a full International Baccalaureate program. This guide covers each school, magnet options, private alternatives, and what families must verify before finalizing a purchase.

Which Schools Serve Ozona, FL?

Ozona Elementary School

Ozona Elementary serves kindergarten through grade 5. It is located within the Ozona community, making it a short drive or walk for most residents. Performance ratings are published annually by the Florida Department of Education at the FDOE school report card site. Contact Pinellas County Schools at pcsb.org for current enrollment information and ratings.

Palm Harbor Middle School

Palm Harbor Middle serves grades 6 through 8 for students in the Palm Harbor zone, including Ozona. The school offers standard Pinellas County academic programs with elective options including music, art, and technology. Students who excel academically may be identified for advanced coursework that prepares them for IB candidacy at PHUH.

Palm Harbor University High School

Palm Harbor University High School (PHUH) serves grades 9 through 12 and consistently earns the highest rating from the Florida Department of Education. The school offers Advanced Placement courses, dual enrollment options, and a full International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme.

The IB Diploma Programme is a demanding two-year curriculum for 11th and 12th graders. IB completers can earn college credit at most major universities. Admission to the IB programme requires meeting academic prerequisites and submitting an application. It is not automatic for all PHUH students. Families who bought in Ozona specifically for the IB programme should contact PHUH directly to understand admission requirements for their student.

What Magnet and Choice Program Options Are Available?

IB Programmes in Pinellas County

Pinellas County Schools offers IB programmes at multiple campuses. The IB MYP (Middle Years Programme) and IB DP (Diploma Programme) are available at designated schools. Students outside the home zone may apply through the district's magnet/choice process if seats are available.

STEM and Specialized Programs

Pinellas County operates STEM academies, arts magnet programs, and CTE programs across the district. Application and availability are at pcsb.org under Magnet and Choice Programs. Deadlines typically fall in late winter for the following school year.

Dual Enrollment at St. Petersburg College

Pinellas County high school students can dual enroll at St. Petersburg College (SPC), taking college courses that count toward both the high school transcript and the college record. Information is at spcollege.edu/dualenrollment.

Verify School Zone with the Exact Address

Use the Pinellas County School Zoning tool at pcsb.org with the exact property address. School zone boundaries can change. Properties on the edge of Ozona may fall into adjacent clusters. Do not rely on Zillow school listings, which are often incorrect or outdated.

IB Admission Is Separate from School Attendance

Living in the Palm Harbor University High zone guarantees your student can attend PHUH, but not that they will be admitted to the IB Diploma Programme. IB has separate academic admission criteria. Families buying specifically for IB should contact the school directly.

Private School Waitlists

Desirable private schools in the Palm Harbor area often have waitlists. If private school is a priority, contact schools before or immediately after submitting a purchase offer to understand current enrollment and waitlist status.

What school district is Ozona FL in?

title: Ozona FL Commute Times: Complete 2025 Guide
excerpt: Ozona FL Commute and Location Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona is on the northwestern Pinellas County coast, served primarily by Alt-19 (Alternate US-19). Dunedin is 8 to 15 minutes south. Clearwater is 20 to 35 minutes. St. Petersburg is 45 to 60 minutes. Tampa downtown is 50 to 75 minutes via the Veterans Expressway. There are no express lanes from Ozona. US-19 corridor congestion is significant during peak hours. Remote workers find Ozona excellent. Daily Tampa commuters should evaluate carefully.

Commuting from Ozona, FL: What to Expect

Commute reality is one of the most underestimated factors when buying in northern Pinellas County. Ozona is a beautiful community, but it sits at the opposite end of Pinellas County from Tampa, and there is no express lane bypass. This guide covers actual route options, realistic time ranges, and an honest assessment of who this commute works for.

What Routes Lead Out of Ozona?

Alt-19 (Alternate US-19 / Bayshore Drive)

Alt-19 is the main north-south artery through Ozona and the primary route for most residents. Heading south, it runs through Crystal Beach, Palm Harbor, and Dunedin before connecting to Clearwater at US-19. Heading north, it connects to Tarpon Springs and then US-19. The Pinellas Trail runs parallel to Alt-19 through much of this corridor.

Orange Street (East-West Connector)

Orange Street runs east from Alt-19 toward US-19 and beyond, providing the main east-west connection from the waterfront to the regional road network. From Orange Street, drivers reach US-19, SR-580 (Curlew Road), and eventually the Veterans Expressway via SR-580 to the Suncoast Parkway interchange.

US-19 (Main Arterial)

US-19 is Pinellas County's primary north-south highway. From Ozona, accessing US-19 requires heading east via Orange Street or SR-586/Curlew Road. US-19 is notoriously congested through Palm Harbor, Dunedin, and Clearwater during peak hours.

How Does the Tampa Commute Work from Ozona?

Via Veterans Expressway (Fastest Route)

The most common Tampa-bound route: east on SR-586 (Curlew Road) to SR-580, east on SR-580 to the Suncoast Parkway (Veterans Expressway, SR-589) on-ramp, south on the Suncoast to I-275, south on I-275 to downtown Tampa or Westshore. Approximately 35 to 40 miles. Takes 50 to 65 minutes off-peak. Tolls run approximately $3 to $5 per one-way trip with SunPass.

Via US-19 and Howard Frankland Bridge

US-19 south to the Gandy Bridge or Howard Frankland Bridge connects to Tampa's east side. Generally slower than the Suncoast option due to US-19 congestion. Not recommended for daily commuters who prioritize time over tolls.

For full-time remote workers, Ozona is one of the most attractive communities in the Tampa Bay region. The combination of coastal character, no HOA, strong schools, and Gulf access is hard to replicate at comparable price points on the Gulf coast.

Frequently Asked Questions About the Ozona FL Commute

How long is the commute from Ozona FL to Tampa?

The commute from Ozona to downtown Tampa takes 50 to 75 minutes in normal traffic via SR-580 east to the Veterans Expressway (SR-589) and I-275 south. Morning rush hour (7:00 to 9:00 AM) is consistently the most congested. Driving via US-19 surface roads takes 60 to 80+ minutes.

Is there public transit from Ozona FL to Tampa?

What is the best route from Ozona to Clearwater?

Alt-19 south to US-19 south to Clearwater. Off-peak this takes about 20 to 30 minutes. During morning rush, SR-580 (Curlew Road) east to US-19 then south can sometimes be faster depending on the specific Clearwater destination.

Waterfront properties with dock access command significant premiums over interior lots. Flood insurance costs are a real factor in waterfront pricing. The market correlates with broader Pinellas County trends but is insulated by its supply constraints.

Ozona FL Real Estate: How the Market Actually Works

Understanding Ozona real estate requires setting aside metrics from growth markets like Wesley Chapel or Parrish. There are no new phases, no builder incentives, and no price reductions from inventory overhang. Every transaction is a one-off. What drives value is scarcity, location, condition, and the specific characteristics of each property.

What Drives Property Values in Ozona?

Water Access and Dock Position

Water access is the single biggest value driver. A home with a private dock on Sutherland Bayou with deepwater access can sell for $500K to $800K more than a comparable interior lot home. Within the waterfront category, water depth, dock condition, and clarity of Gulf access all affect value.

Condition and Roof Age

Florida homeowners insurance underwriters use roof age as a primary rating factor. A new roof can meaningfully increase both buyer pool and achievable sale price. Homes with roofs older than 15 years face restricted insurer options. Sellers considering whether to replace a roof before listing should discuss this with their agent; in many cases the investment returns more than its cost.

Flood Zone Designation

Zone X properties attract more buyers and more financing options than Zone AE properties. An interior Ozona home in Zone X may sell at only a modest discount from a similarly sized near-water home in Zone AE, but the buyer pool is significantly wider. Flood zone affects NFIP premium, lender requirements, and some buyers' willingness to purchase at all.

Palm Harbor University High School Cluster

The PHUH IB program attracts buyers who specifically want this school cluster. Some buyers move to Ozona precisely for PHUH. This creates a sustained demand source from school-motivated buyers that many less well-schooled coastal communities lack.

Buying Strategy for Ozona

Be Ready to Move Quickly

Good Ozona homes do not wait for buyers who need a week to decide. Have financing or proof of funds ready before you start looking. If a property comes available that meets your criteria, your offer needs to be submitted the same day or the next morning.

Understand Insurance Costs Before Making an Offer

Get preliminary flood and homeowners insurance quotes before submitting an offer. Insurance costs directly affect your monthly payment and can make an otherwise attractive property unworkable at your budget. Finding this out after going under contract is avoidable.

Use a Waterfront-Specific Inspection Team

For any waterfront Ozona property, your inspection team should include a licensed home inspector, a seawall inspector/marine contractor, and a pool/dock inspector if applicable. The additional inspections add $500 to $1,500 but can reveal $20,000 to $100,000+ in needed repairs.

Pricing Correctly in a Thin Market

Low inventory does not automatically justify overpricing. Overpriced listings in Ozona sit just as they do anywhere else. The best pricing strategy is to anchor at realistic current market value with a modest buffer, not to test the ceiling and reduce later. Price reductions signal to buyers that something is wrong.

Insurance Documentation Matters

Sellers who provide recent insurance documentation, including current premium statements for flood and homeowners insurance, seawall inspection reports, and elevation certificates, reduce friction and build buyer confidence. Providing this proactively speeds the process.

Is the Ozona FL real estate market a buyer's or seller's market?

What is the typical days on market in Ozona FL?

Because so few properties list at any given time, averages are not very meaningful in this micro-market.

Is Ozona FL a good place to flip houses?

In Ozona FL, expect total monthly housing costs of $3,200 to $6,500+ depending on your home price, flood zone, and insurance situation. Inland homes are more affordable to carry than waterfront properties where flood insurance alone can run $500 to $700 per month.

Ozona real estate is priced like the Pinellas County waterfront-adjacent market it is, not like an affordable first-time buyer market. But the cost of living here is shaped by more than just the purchase price. Direct Sutherland Bayou frontage is the top tier of the Ozona market. These properties have the highest flood insurance costs and the most complex maintenance requirements (seawall, dock, pilings), but also the strongest long-term appreciation profile due to scarcity on the Pinellas coast.

title: Ozona FL Property Taxes: Rates, Exemptions and Estimates
excerpt: Ozona FL Property Taxes, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona FL property owners pay unincorporated Pinellas County millage of approximately 19 to 21 mills total. On a $500,000 home with Florida homestead exemption, expect roughly $7,500 to $9,000 per year in property taxes. There is no city millage because Ozona is unincorporated.

Property taxes in Ozona are calculated by Pinellas County using the state's millage system. Because Ozona is an unincorporated community, buyers here pay county, school board, and special district millage rates, but no city millage layer. This is a meaningful advantage over incorporated cities like Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, or Clearwater where a city millage adds $1,000 to $2,000 per year to the tax bill at similar price points.

This guide explains how Pinellas County calculates property taxes for Ozona homes, what exemptions apply, and what you can expect to pay at different home price levels. For a full cost picture, also read the Ozona cost of living guide and browse current Ozona listings.

How Are Property Taxes Calculated in Ozona?

The Millage Rate System

Florida uses millage rates to calculate property taxes. One mill equals $1 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value. For a home assessed at $500,000 with no exemptions, a 20 mill rate produces a tax bill of $10,000. Exemptions reduce the assessed value before the millage is applied, which is why the homestead exemption matters so much.

What Makes Up the Ozona Millage Rate

The total Ozona millage rate combines several components: Pinellas County general fund, Pinellas County School Board, Pinellas County municipal service taxing unit (MSTU) for unincorporated areas, and several small special districts. The total typically runs between 19 and 21 mills for unincorporated Pinellas County. Pinellas County publishes the current year millage breakdown at pcgov.org. You can verify the exact rate for any Ozona parcel at the Pinellas County Property Appraiser website (pcpao.gov).

No City Millage in Ozona

Incorporated cities in Pinellas County add their own city millage on top of the county rate. Dunedin adds approximately 4 to 5 mills. Tarpon Springs adds a similar amount. Clearwater adds several mills. Because Ozona is unincorporated, none of those city taxes apply. At a $600,000 assessed value, this saves roughly $2,400 to $3,000 per year compared to buying in an incorporated city at the same price.

Property Tax Estimates for Ozona Homes

Assessed ValueLess Homestead ExemptionTaxable ValueAt 20 MillsAnnual Tax Estimate
$400,000$50,000$350,000$7,000~$7,000/yr
$500,000$50,000$450,000$9,000~$9,000/yr
$650,000$50,000$600,000$12,000~$12,000/yr
$900,000$50,000$850,000$17,000~$17,000/yr
$1,200,000$50,000$1,150,000$23,000~$23,000/yr

These are estimates using a 20-mill effective rate after homestead exemption. Actual millage varies by parcel's specific district assignments. Use pcpao.gov to look up the current tax bill on any property you are evaluating.

Florida Homestead Exemption in Ozona

First $25,000 Exemption

Florida law provides a $25,000 exemption off the assessed value of any homesteaded primary residence. This applies to all taxing authorities, including the school board. On a 20-mill combined rate, this saves $500 per year.

Second $25,000 Exemption

For properties assessed at more than $50,000, a second $25,000 exemption applies to the assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000. Importantly, this second exemption does not apply to the school board millage. Combined, the two exemptions reduce taxable assessed value by $50,000 for most non-school millage purposes. The practical total savings is roughly $850 to $1,000 per year on a Pinellas County home at current millage rates.

Save Our Homes Assessment Cap

Once you establish homestead in Florida, the Save Our Homes (SOH) cap limits annual increases in your assessed value to 3% or the rate of inflation (CPI), whichever is lower. In a rising market, this creates a growing gap between market value and taxable assessed value over time. Long-term Ozona residents often pay taxes on assessed values 20% to 40% below current market value because of this cap. When you buy, the SOH cap resets at your purchase price, so first-year taxes for a buyer are higher than what the previous owner was paying on an equivalent home.

How to Apply for Homestead Exemption in Pinellas County

File your Florida homestead exemption application with the Pinellas County Property Appraiser at pcpao.gov. You must have closed on your home and established it as your primary residence by January 1 of the tax year for which you are applying. The deadline to file is March 1. You will need a Florida driver's license or ID with the Ozona address, and your deed or closing disclosure as proof of ownership.

Ozona vs Other Pinellas Communities: Property Tax Comparison

Tarpon Springs~4-5 mills~24-26~$11,250Ozona saves ~$2,250/yr
Palm Harbor (uninc.)None~19-21~$9,000Same as Ozona

Millage figures are approximate. Verify current rates with pcpao.gov before relying on any estimate for budgeting. See the full Pinellas County real estate overview for additional tax context.

Can You Appeal Your Property Tax Assessment in Ozona?

Yes. Florida law allows you to challenge your property's assessed value by filing a petition with the Pinellas County Value Adjustment Board (VAB). The deadline is 25 days after the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes (TRIM notice) mails in August. If you believe the Pinellas County Property Appraiser has overassessed your home relative to comparable sales, a successful VAB challenge can reduce your tax bill. You can also contact the Property Appraiser's office informally before filing a formal VAB petition.

Frequently Asked Questions About Ozona FL Property Taxes

Does Ozona have a city property tax?

No. Ozona is unincorporated Pinellas County, so there is no city millage. You pay county, school board, and special district rates only. This saves $1,000 to $2,500 per year compared to incorporated Pinellas cities at similar home values.

How do I look up my exact property tax in Ozona?

Visit pcpao.gov (Pinellas County Property Appraiser) and search by address or parcel ID. You can see the current assessed value, taxable value, applied exemptions, and the year's tax bill broken down by taxing authority. This is the only reliable way to get precise figures for a specific property.

When do I apply for Florida homestead exemption?

You must close on your home and establish it as your primary Florida residence before January 1 of the tax year, then file your homestead application by March 1 of that year. Applications are submitted to pcpao.gov. If you miss the March 1 deadline, you wait until the following year.

What happens to property taxes when I buy a home in Ozona?

The assessed value resets to or near your purchase price in the year following the sale. If the previous owner had a Save Our Homes cap locking in a low assessed value, your first year's tax bill will be higher than theirs was. This is the "assessment reset" effect. Your lender's closing disclosure will show an escrow estimate, but verify with pcpao.gov after the assessment resets.

Are there senior exemptions available in Ozona?

Yes. Florida offers an additional senior exemption for qualifying Pinellas County residents who are 65 or older and whose household income is below a certain threshold (adjusted annually). Qualifying seniors may receive an additional exemption on top of the standard homestead exemption. Check with the Pinellas County Property Appraiser for current income limits and filing requirements.

title: New Construction in Ozona FL: The Honest Answer (2025)
excerpt: New Construction in Ozona FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

There is no new construction in Ozona, FL. The community is fully built out with no available lots, no builder pipeline, and no new phases. The only path to a new home in Ozona is buying an existing property (teardown or heavily remodeled) and doing a custom build on the existing lot. This guide explains why, what the custom build path looks like, and where to find new construction if that is what you need.

New Construction in Ozona, FL: Why It Does Not Exist and What to Do Instead

Every few months, a buyer calls asking about new construction in Ozona. The answer is always the same: it does not exist as a category. Ozona was platted and built out decades ago. There are no new communities opening, no spec home builders clearing lots, and no large parcels available for subdivision. If new construction is your primary requirement, Ozona is the wrong search area. This guide explains why, what the custom build path involves, and where the actual new construction options are near northern Pinellas County.

Why Is There No New Construction in Ozona?

Fully Platted Decades Ago

Ozona's residential lots were platted and developed primarily from the 1940s through the 1980s. There is no unplatted land remaining. Every parcel that can be built on already has a home or structure on it. This is common in coastal Pinellas communities that developed before the era of master-planned new construction.

No Available Vacant Lots

On rare occasions, a lot in Ozona becomes available when a structure is demolished or condemned. These are one-off events, not a pipeline. When vacant lots do appear, they sell quickly, often to custom home builders or individuals planning their own build. They are not marketed as new construction communities.

Environmental and Regulatory Constraints

Much of Ozona's waterfront is in FEMA AE flood zones. Florida and Pinellas County both have setback, environmental, and floodplain management requirements that make developing previously undeveloped coastal land extremely difficult. The combination of floodplain elevation requirements, SWFWMD wetland rules, and Pinellas County setback ordinances effectively prevents any meaningful new development on undeveloped coastal land.

Community Character Preservation

Ozona's value is tied to its character as a small, historic, low-density waterfront village. Large-scale new development would change the character that makes Ozona desirable. The community has no cityhood and no formal planning authority of its own, but Pinellas County zoning for this area does not accommodate large-scale new residential development.

The Teardown/Rebuild Path: What It Actually Involves

Step 1: Find a Teardown Candidate

A teardown in Ozona is typically a home that is in such poor condition, or is so small relative to the lot's potential, that the land value exceeds the improved value. Finding these properties requires working with a local agent who knows the community and can identify prospects before or shortly after they list. Asking prices for teardown-suitable properties in Ozona range from $350K to $700K+ depending on lot size and waterfront status.

Step 2: Demolition

Demolition of a single-family home in Pinellas County typically runs $12,000 to $30,000 depending on size, asbestos testing requirements, and disposal costs. Pinellas County requires a demolition permit. Any structure with asbestos-containing materials (common in pre-1980 construction) requires licensed abatement before demolition.

Step 3: Survey and Elevation Certificate

Before designing a new home, you need a current survey and elevation certificate for the lot. These establish setback boundaries, the flood zone, and the Base Flood Elevation, all of which constrain the new home's design. For Zone AE lots, the new structure must be built at or above BFE. In Zone VE, open-pile foundation construction may be required.

Step 4: Design, Permitting, and Construction

Custom home construction in Ozona requires architectural plans, Pinellas County Building Services permit review (8 to 16 weeks for plan review), and for waterfront lots, SWFWMD and potentially Army Corps permitting. Total permitting time for a waterfront custom build is realistically 12 to 24 months. Construction typically takes an additional 12 to 18 months. The full process from lot acquisition to move-in for a waterfront custom build in Ozona is 24 to 36 months.

Teardown/Custom Build Cost Estimate

Frequently Asked Questions About New Construction in Ozona FL

Is there new construction in Ozona FL?

No. Ozona is a fully built-out community with no new construction communities, no available lots for subdivision, and no builder pipeline. The only path to a new home in Ozona is buying a teardown and building a custom home on the existing lot. This is an expensive, time-consuming process, not a standard new construction purchase.

How much does it cost to build a custom home in Ozona FL?

A custom build in Ozona involves acquiring a teardown lot (typically $350K to $700K+ for the land and existing structure), demolition ($12,000 to $30,000), and construction. For a Zone AE lot near the water, elevated foundation construction adds $30,000 to $80,000+ to the foundation cost compared to standard slab construction. Total all-in cost for a custom Ozona build is typically $800,000 to $1.5M+ depending on the lot, elevation requirements, home size, and finishes.

What permits are required to build in Ozona FL?

Ozona is in unincorporated Pinellas County, so building permits are issued through Pinellas County Building Services (pcbuildingservices.com). The permitting process for new residential construction typically takes 8 to 16 weeks for plan review. For waterfront lots, additional permits from SWFWMD (Southwest Florida Water Management District), and potentially the Army Corps of Engineers and FDEP, are required. Permitting for waterfront new construction can take 12 to 24 months total.

Are there any new construction communities near Ozona FL?

Yes. The closest new construction communities to Ozona are in east Palm Harbor (some infill development), parts of Dunedin, and the SR-54/SR-56 corridor in Wesley Chapel (farther but larger volume). For buyers who specifically want northern Pinellas coastal proximity with new construction, the options within 30 minutes are limited. Buyers willing to drive 45 to 60 minutes east will find the most new construction options in Pasco County.

What is the substantial improvement rule and how does it affect Ozona?

The substantial improvement rule (FEMA) states that if a structure in a Special Flood Hazard Area is damaged or renovated to the point where the cost exceeds 50% of the structure's pre-improvement market value, the entire structure must be brought into compliance with current floodplain management standards. For older Ozona waterfront homes, this means that a major renovation (kitchen + bathrooms + roof, for example) could trigger a requirement to elevate the entire structure to current BFE standards, a cost that can run $50,000 to $150,000 or more.

title: Investing in Ozona FL Real Estate: What You Need to Know
excerpt: Investing in Ozona FL Real Estate, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona is a low-inventory, high-barrier-to-entry market that rewards patient long-term investors. It is not a strong market for short-term rentals or quick flips. The investment case rests on Pinellas waterfront scarcity and Palm Harbor school zone desirability, not rental yield.

Most buyers who come to me asking about Ozona investment properties are attracted by the same things that make Ozona desirable for primary residents: limited supply, waterfront access, no HOA, and a top school cluster. The investment fundamentals here are real, but they favor a specific type of investor. This guide covers what works, what does not, and how Ozona compares to other Pinellas investment markets.

Browse current Ozona listings or read the Ozona real estate guide for market structure overview. The Ozona market trends guide covers price history.

Why Is Ozona a Hard Market to Invest In?

Chronically Low Inventory

Ozona has very few homes available at any given time. The community is completely built-out, and turnover is low because many owners hold their properties for decades. When a home does come to market, it typically sells quickly, often with multiple interested buyers. This makes it hard to be selective as an investor. You either accept the asking price and whatever terms the seller wants, or you miss the opportunity. Patience and pre-qualification are essential.

No New Supply Pipeline

There are no new construction communities coming to Ozona. No lots are available for development. The only "new" product entering the market is teardown-rebuild custom homes, which are expensive to produce and typically aimed at owner-occupants, not investors. This supply constraint is a long-term positive for values but a short-term negative for investor deal flow. See the Ozona new construction guide for full context.

Owner-Occupant Competition

The buyers competing for Ozona homes are primarily families attracted by the Palm Harbor University High School IB program and the no-HOA lifestyle. These are emotional purchases made by highly motivated buyers who will pay fair market value or above. Investors looking for below-market distressed properties will rarely find them here.

What Investment Strategies Work in Ozona?

Long-Term Buy and Hold

The strongest investment case for Ozona is simply buying and holding. Pinellas County waterfront-adjacent inventory is permanently constrained. Palm Harbor school zones drive sustained demand from families. Homes held for 10 or more years in similar Pinellas communities have consistently appreciated, particularly for waterfront and near-waterfront properties. The key is accepting a low initial yield (cap rates in Ozona are low because prices are high relative to rents) in exchange for long-term capital appreciation.

Waterfront Appreciation Play

Canal-access and bayou-front homes in Ozona have a scarcity premium that inland homes do not fully share. Gulf-access waterfront on the Pinellas coast is a finite resource. Buyers looking for maximum long-term appreciation in a buy-and-hold strategy often focus on waterfront tiers despite the higher entry cost and flood insurance overhead. See the Ozona waterfront homes guide for due diligence requirements on canal and bayou properties.

Primary Residence with Future Rental Potential

Some buyers purchase in Ozona as a primary residence with the plan to rent the home when they move or upsize in the future. This avoids the short-term rental regulatory complexity and positions the property as a long-term rental in a market with strong school zone demand. Long-term rental demand from families relocating to Pinellas County for the PHUHS school zone is real.

What Does Not Work in Ozona

Short-Term Rentals (STR)

Pinellas County has regulations governing short-term rentals in unincorporated areas. Florida's 2011 preemption law limits local governments' ability to ban STRs outright, but registration requirements, inspection mandates, and enforcement have tightened. More importantly, Ozona's character as an owner-occupant residential community means STR operations face practical resistance from neighbors. The economics rarely pencil out given Ozona's high home prices and the management overhead of a vacation rental. The flood zone complications (AE zone insurance costs) further compress STR margins for waterfront properties.

Flips

Flipping in Ozona requires finding a distressed property at a below-market price, which happens rarely. When homes do sell below market, it is usually due to estate sales or deferred maintenance, not motivated investor-friendly situations. Renovation costs for older CBS homes in Pinellas County (permitting, flood mitigation, roofing) can erode margins quickly. Flip investors generally find better inventory in Brandon, Riverview, or Plant City where more distressed properties circulate.

Key Due Diligence for Ozona Investment Properties

Flood Zone and Insurance Cost

Before making an offer on any Ozona property, get a flood zone determination and an insurance quote. For AE zone waterfront properties, flood insurance can cost $3,000 to $8,000 or more annually. This directly affects your effective cap rate and cash-on-cash return. See the Ozona flood zone guide for details. Also read the flood insurance buyer guide for general Florida flood insurance strategy.

Seawall and Dock Condition

For waterfront properties, always commission a seawall inspection before closing. Seawall replacement in Pinellas County runs $15,000 to $60,000 or more depending on linear footage and materials. Dock replacement adds to that. These are material costs that can turn a moderately priced canal home into an expensive surprise for an investor who did not do proper due diligence. Read the full waterfront due diligence checklist.

Permit History

Older Ozona homes may have unpermitted additions, modifications, or HVAC replacements. Pinellas County permits are searchable online. Unpermitted work can create financing complications, insurance issues, and resale problems. Read the permit history guide for how to research this before making an offer.

Is Ozona FL a good investment?

For patient long-term investors focused on capital appreciation, Ozona has a strong case built on Pinellas waterfront scarcity and Palm Harbor school zone demand. For yield-focused investors, STR operators, or flippers, Ozona is not the right market. Read the Ozona real estate guide and market trends guide for supporting context.

Can I do short-term rentals in Ozona?

Short-term rentals in unincorporated Pinellas County are subject to county regulations including registration and inspection requirements. The economics are challenging given Ozona's high home prices, flood insurance overhead on waterfront properties, and the community's owner-occupant character. Most Ozona investors focus on long-term rentals or primary residence use.

What kind of rent can I get for an Ozona home?

Long-term rental rates for a 3-bedroom inland Ozona home typically run $2,500 to $3,500 per month depending on size and condition. Canal-front homes command higher rents but also have higher carrying costs. At a $600,000 purchase price and $3,000/month rent, the gross yield is only about 6% before taxes, insurance, and maintenance, which illustrates why Ozona is an appreciation play, not a yield play.

How often do investment properties come available in Ozona?

Very rarely. Ozona has low turnover, and when homes do sell, owner-occupant families typically buy them. Investment-oriented purchases happen opportunistically, usually on estate sales or when a long-term owner decides to cash out. The best approach is to have an agent on alert and be ready to move quickly when something comes available. Browse current Ozona listings for what is on the market now.

Does Ozona have strong home price appreciation?

Historically, Pinellas County waterfront-adjacent communities have appreciated well over long holding periods, driven by the permanent scarcity of gulf-access land. Ozona shares this characteristic. Short-term appreciation depends on interest rate cycles and buyer demand. Long-term, the structural supply constraint supports values. See the Ozona market trends guide for historical context.

Sutherland Bayou connects to St. Joseph Sound and the Gulf, providing genuine cruising access for vessels appropriate to the depth at the specific dock.

Buying Waterfront in Ozona, FL: Complete Due Diligence Guide

Buying a waterfront home in Ozona means buying into a real working coastal community. The properties here have had boats in the water for decades. What you are acquiring is genuine Gulf access, Old Florida character, and a community where neighbors know each other's vessels. Flood insurance costs, seawall condition, dock permitting, and water depth are not background details. They are central to the purchase.

Bayou front (deepwater, wide lot)$1.3M-$2M+Zone AE or VE$5,000-$10,000+/yrAll above + elevation certificate

Understanding Sutherland Bayou Access

Water Depth and Tidal Variation

Water depth at the dock is the most important specification for any boating buyer. The typical tidal variation on St. Joseph Sound is approximately 1.0 to 2.5 feet between mean low water (MLW) and mean high water. A dock that reads 4.5 feet at high tide may be 2.5 feet at low tide. Request the depth at MLW for any dock you are evaluating, and verify independently with a depth sounder if boating is a primary purchase motivation.

Canal Arm Properties

Canal properties that connect to the bayou via finger canals are common in Ozona. Check: (1) depth along the full route from dock to open bayou at MLW, (2) any bridge clearances if bridges cross your route, and (3) whether the canal is maintained by the county or private parties. Some canals have silted over time.

Gulf Access Route

From Sutherland Bayou, boaters access the Gulf via St. Joseph Sound and through Dunedin Pass (Honeymoon Island cut) or Clearwater Pass. The route adds 20 to 45 minutes of run time from many dock positions to open Gulf water, which is typical for Tampa Bay region coastal communities.

Seawall Due Diligence

Why Seawall Condition Matters

Seawalls in Ozona are typically cast concrete panel or poured concrete construction from the 1950s through the 1980s. A properly maintained seawall has a lifespan of 30 to 50 years. Many Ozona seawalls are at or past that age. Failure modes include panel cracking, loss of backfill behind the wall, tie-back rod failure, and cap deterioration.

Seawall Inspection Cost and Process

A qualified seawall inspection costs $250 to $500. The inspector will assess the full seawall length from both land side and water side, checking for cracks, probing for voids behind panels, assessing cap condition, and identifying any tie-back failure evidence.

Seawall Replacement Costs

Seawall replacement in Pinellas County runs $500 to $900 per linear foot for a standard concrete panel seawall. A 60-foot seawall replacement runs $30,000 to $54,000. Corner lots or irregular parcels may have 80 to 100+ linear feet of seawall, multiplying these figures. Factor any seawall capital need into your offer price.

Dock and Lift Inspection

Wood Dock Lifespan

Pressure-treated wood dock structures in salt water typically last 15 to 25 years. At inspection: check for rot in decking, cross-beams, and pilings; piling condition at the waterline; and hardware corrosion on cleats, ladders, and electrical conduit.

Boat Lift Inspection

Boat lifts should be inspected by the same marine contractor handling the seawall and dock. Assess motor condition, cable wear, cradle alignment, and structural integrity. A marginal lift may need $3,000 to $8,000 in repairs or full replacement within a few years.

How much do waterfront homes cost in Ozona FL?

title: Ozona FL Flood Zones: What Buyers Must Know (2025)
excerpt: Ozona FL Flood Zones Guide, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Much of coastal Ozona is in FEMA Zone AE, which requires mandatory flood insurance for any mortgaged property. Annual flood insurance for Ozona waterfront homes typically costs $3,000 to $8,000+ through the NFIP. Interior Ozona streets are more likely to be in Zone X with no mandatory insurance requirement. Check msc.fema.gov for any specific address before buying. An elevation certificate ($400-$800) can reveal whether the structure sits above or below the Base Flood Elevation and may reduce NFIP premiums.

Ozona FL Flood Zones: A Complete Buyer's Guide

Flood zone designation is not a background consideration in Ozona. For any waterfront or near-waterfront property along Sutherland Bayou or St. Joseph Sound, flood zone directly determines whether flood insurance is required, how much it costs, and what lenders will accept. This guide covers each zone designation you will encounter in Ozona, what they mean in practice, and the due diligence steps every buyer should complete before removing contingencies.

The full Pinellas County flood zones guide covers the county-wide picture. This guide focuses specifically on Ozona.

FEMA Flood Zone Designations in Ozona

FEMA ZoneRisk LevelFlood Insurance Required?Where in OzonaTypical Annual Cost
Zone AEHigh (1% annual chance flood)Yes, for mortgaged propertiesCoastal and near-water areas along bayou and canals$3,000-$8,000+ (NFIP)
Zone VEVery high (coastal wave action risk)Yes, for mortgaged propertiesSome exposed bayou-front positions$7,000-$15,000+ (NFIP)
Zone X (shaded)Moderate riskNo (voluntary only)Transition areas, some interior streets$500-$1,200 (voluntary)
Zone X (unshaded)Low riskNo (voluntary only)Interior Ozona streets farthest from water$300-$800 (voluntary)

FEMA Community Number for Pinellas County is 125096. Verify zone designation for any specific address at msc.fema.gov.

Zone AE: What It Means for Ozona Buyers

Mandatory Flood Insurance

If you are taking out a mortgage on a property in Zone AE, your lender is required by federal law to mandate flood insurance as a condition of the loan. This is not negotiable. If you stop paying flood insurance while your mortgage is active, the lender can force-place coverage (typically at higher cost) and add it to your mortgage payment.

Base Flood Elevation (BFE)

Every Zone AE designation has an associated Base Flood Elevation, which is the elevation at which FEMA estimates a 1% annual flood risk. The BFE is shown on the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map. Whether your structure's lowest finished floor is above or below BFE is the most important single factor in your NFIP premium. A property at or above BFE can cost $1,500 to $4,000 per year. A property below BFE can cost $4,000 to $8,000+ per year.

Risk Rating 2.0 Methodology

Since October 2021, the NFIP prices policies using Risk Rating 2.0, which rates each property individually based on specific risk factors: distance to water, structure elevation, foundation type, replacement cost, and historical flood frequency. The old zone-based flat rate system is no longer used for new policies. This means two adjacent homes in the same Zone AE can have significantly different premiums. An elevation certificate is the most reliable way to understand a specific property's rating inputs.

Zone VE: The Highest Risk Category

What VE Means

Zone VE is the coastal high hazard area designation, indicating properties subject to wave action during a 100-year flood event. In Ozona, Zone VE designations may apply to some exposed positions with direct Gulf or Sound exposure. Zone VE properties typically require open-pile foundation construction for any new building or substantial improvement (generally defined as a renovation exceeding 50% of the structure's pre-improvement value).

Insurance Costs in Zone VE

Zone VE properties are the most expensive to insure. NFIP premiums for Zone VE structures typically start at $7,000 per year and can exceed $15,000 for large or older structures. Private flood insurance may be available but can be difficult to obtain in the highest-risk coastal zones. Buyers considering Zone VE properties should obtain multiple insurance quotes before making an offer.

Zone X: Lower Risk, But Not Zero Risk

What Zone X Means in Practice

Zone X (both shaded and unshaded) designates areas outside the high-risk SFHA. Lenders do not require flood insurance for mortgaged Zone X properties under current federal law. However, Zone X is not the same as flood-proof. FEMA models have margins of error, and drainage flooding, stormwater events, or a storm that exceeds the model's parameters can affect Zone X properties.

Why Voluntary Zone X Coverage Makes Sense

Voluntary flood policies for Zone X properties are available through the NFIP Preferred Risk Policy and some private carriers at significantly lower cost than Zone AE policies. For a property near the Zone AE boundary, a voluntary Zone X policy provides meaningful protection at a fraction of the Zone AE cost.

Elevation Certificates: What They Are and Why They Matter

What an Elevation Certificate Documents

An elevation certificate (EC) is prepared by a licensed land surveyor or engineer. It documents the finished floor elevations of all levels of a structure, the foundation type, the flood zone and BFE from the current FIRM, and the property's specific flood zone boundary. For a Zone AE property, the EC is the document that tells the flood insurance underwriter exactly where your structure sits relative to BFE.

How an EC Can Save Money

If the EC shows your structure sits above BFE, your NFIP premium is substantially lower than if it sits at or below BFE. For an older Ozona home, the difference can be $2,000 to $5,000 per year in premium. An EC costs $400 to $800. If the seller does not have one, requesting the seller pay for an EC during due diligence is reasonable, especially for a Zone AE property where the result affects your ongoing annual costs.

NFIP vs. Private Flood Insurance for Ozona Properties

FactorNFIP (National Flood Insurance Program)Private Flood Insurance
Max building coverage$250,000 (structure only)Higher limits available
Max contents coverage$100,000Higher limits available
Policy cancellation riskLow (government-backed)Can be non-renewed; market has contracted
Price comparisonRequired benchmark; may be higher or lowerSometimes lower; get quotes both ways
Coverage for additional living expensesNot coveredSometimes available
Claims processEstablished federal processVaries by insurer
Availability in Zone VEYesDifficult to obtain; limited carriers

For Ozona waterfront properties, get quotes from both NFIP and private flood carriers during the due diligence period. Private flood has become more expensive and less available in coastal Pinellas County in recent years, but it is worth checking.

Buyer Due Diligence Checklist for Flood Zones in Ozona

StepAction
1Look up flood zone for the specific address at msc.fema.gov
2Ask seller for any existing elevation certificate
3If no EC exists, order one during due diligence period ($400-$800)
4Get NFIP flood insurance quote using elevation certificate data
5Get private flood insurance quote for comparison
6Request FEMA flood claim history for the property (ask your insurance agent)
7Look up Pinellas County Evacuation Zone for the property (Pinellas County Emergency Management)
8Factor annual flood insurance premium into monthly budget before making offer

Pinellas County Evacuation Zones and How They Relate to Flood Zones

Flood zone (FEMA FIRM designation) and evacuation zone (Pinellas County Emergency Management) are separate but related. Flood zone determines insurance requirements and costs. Evacuation zone determines when residents should leave during a hurricane. Ozona's waterfront sections are in Evacuation Zone A, the highest-priority evacuation tier. Zone A residents are asked to evacuate when a major hurricane threatens the area.

Check the Pinellas County evacuation zone for any specific address at pinellascounty.org. Knowing both your flood zone and your evacuation zone gives you the full picture of coastal risk for any Ozona property.

Frequently Asked Questions About Ozona FL Flood Zones

What flood zone is Ozona FL in?

Ozona has a mix of flood zones. Waterfront and near-waterfront properties along Sutherland Bayou and St. Joseph Sound are primarily in FEMA Zone AE, the high-risk Special Flood Hazard Area. Some exposed coastal positions may be in Zone VE. Interior Ozona streets are more likely to be in Zone X, which is a lower-risk designation with no mandatory flood insurance for mortgaged properties. Check the FEMA Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov for any specific address.

How much does flood insurance cost in Ozona FL?

Flood insurance for Ozona waterfront homes in Zone AE typically costs $3,000 to $8,000+ per year through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). Properties in Zone VE can exceed $10,000 per year. Interior Zone X properties do not require flood insurance for mortgaged purchases, though voluntary policies are available at lower cost. Private flood insurance is sometimes available at better rates than NFIP; compare both markets before buying.

What is FEMA Risk Rating 2.0 and how does it affect Ozona?

Risk Rating 2.0 is the current NFIP pricing methodology, implemented in 2021-2022. It prices each property individually based on its specific flood risk factors (distance to water, elevation relative to flood level, structure type, replacement cost) rather than the old zone-based flat rates. For many Ozona waterfront homeowners, Risk Rating 2.0 changed their NFIP premiums. Some saw decreases; others saw significant increases, particularly for older, lower-elevation structures.

What is an elevation certificate and do I need one for an Ozona property?

An elevation certificate (EC) is a document prepared by a licensed surveyor or engineer that measures the lowest finished floor elevation of a structure relative to the Base Flood Elevation (BFE). For a FEMA Zone AE property, the EC determines whether your structure is above or below BFE, which directly affects NFIP premium calculations. An EC typically costs $400 to $800. If the seller does not have one, getting one during due diligence can reveal premium reduction opportunities or flag costly issues.

Should I get flood insurance even if I am buying in Zone X?

It is worth considering, especially for properties near Zone AE boundaries. Zone X is defined as lower risk, not zero risk. FEMA flood map boundaries are not perfectly precise. Flooding from stormwater, drainage overflow, or near-miss storm surge can affect Zone X properties. Voluntary Zone X flood policies are available at much lower cost than Zone AE policies and provide coverage against events that are statistically less likely but not impossible.

title: Moving to Ozona FL: What to Know Before You Relocate
excerpt: Moving to Ozona FL: What to Know, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona is an unincorporated Pinellas County fishing village between Palm Harbor and Dunedin with no HOA, no CDD fees, old Florida character, and extremely limited home inventory. If you find a home here, move fast.

Ozona is one of the few communities left on the Pinellas County coast that has not been absorbed into a master-planned development. The area sits off Alt-19 between Dunedin and Palm Harbor, a few miles from the St. Joseph Sound. It has a built-out, resale-only market with homes that range from 1950s concrete block cottages to 1980s ranch styles to renovated waterfront properties on canals connected to Sutherland Bayou.

I have worked with buyers moving to the Pinellas coast for years. Ozona comes up when someone wants the feel of Old Florida without HOA rules or community fees. It is a legitimate option if your budget and timeline align, but you need to understand what you are getting into before you start your search. Browse Ozona homes for sale for current listings, or read the complete Ozona buyer guide for a full market breakdown.

What Kind of Place Is Ozona?

Ozona is not a neighborhood. It is a loose-knit unincorporated community that predates most of Pinellas County's suburbs. There are no big box stores in Ozona, no new construction communities, and no community pool or clubhouse. What there is: mature trees, a working waterfront feel near the bayou, proximity to Dunedin's downtown, and homes that sell quickly when they hit the market.

Unincorporated Means No City Taxes

Because Ozona is unincorporated, you pay Pinellas County taxes but no city millage on top. That saves roughly $1,000 to $1,500 per year compared to buying in an incorporated city like Dunedin or Tarpon Springs at a similar price point. The tradeoff is fewer city services, though Pinellas County still handles roads, water, and emergency services. See the Ozona property tax breakdown for full millage details.

No HOA and No CDD

The vast majority of Ozona homes carry no homeowners association. You are not paying monthly dues, following paint color approval requirements, or dealing with board governance. There are also no CDD (Community Development District) fees, which can add $1,500 to $4,000 per year in newer Pinellas and Pasco communities. Read more about how CDD fees work in Florida.

Old Florida Character

Homes in Ozona are not cookie-cutter. You will find concrete block CBS homes from the 1950s and 1960s sitting next to renovated 1970s ranches next to updated modern interiors behind vintage facades. The community has a history as a commercial fishing hub, and that independent, non-conformist character still shows in the streetscape.

What Are Homes Like in Ozona?

Non-Waterfront Inland Homes

Inland Ozona homes (not on a canal or the bayou) typically range from $400,000 to $650,000. These are mostly CBS construction from the 1950s through the 1980s, ranging from 1,000 to 1,800 square feet. Many have been updated over the decades. FEMA flood zone X applies to most inland Ozona properties, which means federal flood insurance is not required by a lender (though you can still purchase it). See the Ozona flood zone guide for the full zone breakdown.

Canal-Access Homes

Canal homes in Ozona connect to Sutherland Bayou and ultimately to St. Joseph Sound. Prices for canal-access properties typically start around $600,000 and run past $1.1 million depending on lot size, water frontage, dock condition, and renovation level. These are AE flood zone properties in most cases, so budget $3,000 to $8,000 or more annually for flood insurance. Read the Ozona waterfront homes guide for detailed due diligence steps.

Bayou-Front Homes

Direct Sutherland Bayou frontage is the premium tier in Ozona. These properties start near $900,000 and can exceed $2 million for renovated homes with deep water, a rebuilt dock, and significant square footage. Flood insurance and seawall maintenance are major budget considerations. A seawall inspection alone can run $15,000 to $60,000 if replacement is needed.

Schools That Serve Ozona

Ozona sits in the Palm Harbor school cluster of Pinellas County Public Schools. This is one of the most desirable school zones in Pinellas County. Read the full Ozona schools guide for detailed information on each school.

Ozona Elementary School

Ozona Elementary serves K-5 students within Ozona. It is a smaller neighborhood school with a community-oriented feel that matches the character of the surrounding area.

Palm Harbor Middle School

Middle school students from Ozona typically attend Palm Harbor Middle School, which feeds directly into Palm Harbor University High School.

Palm Harbor University High School

PHUHS is one of the top-rated high schools in Pinellas County and offers the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme. This school zone is a significant factor in Ozona property values. Buyers relocating with high school-age students specifically seek out the Palm Harbor school cluster.

What to Do Near Ozona

J.O. Douglas Park and Boat Ramp

Just off Alt-19, J.O. Douglas Park has a public boat ramp with access to St. Joseph Sound and the Gulf waters beyond. It is a practical amenity for residents who fish or kayak. See things to do in Ozona for a full recreation breakdown.

Dunedin Day Trips

Dunedin's downtown is about 3 miles south of Ozona. You get access to Honeymoon Island State Park (one of the best beaches in Pinellas County), downtown restaurants on Main Street, TD Ballpark (Blue Jays spring training), and the Pinellas Trail without living in Dunedin itself.

Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks

Tarpon Springs is about 5 miles north. The Sponge Docks area has Greek restaurants, sponge diving history, and an active waterfront. It rounds out the lifestyle options in the northern Pinellas corridor without a long drive.

Ozona is on the Pinellas peninsula, which means Tampa commutes are real. title: Things to Do in Ozona FL
excerpt: Things to Do in Ozona FL, Barrett Henry, REALTOR at REMAX Collective.
content:
Quick Answer

Ozona itself is small with no formal commercial district, but its location on the Pinellas County coast puts you 10 minutes from Dunedin's downtown, 15 minutes from Tarpon Springs, and within easy reach of Gulf beaches, the Pinellas Trail, and waterfront fishing. The lifestyle here is outdoor-driven and genuinely coastal.

What Ozona Offers

Ozona is not a destination town. It has no themed main street, no resort hotel, and no curated tourist district. What it has is access to real Florida coastal life: fishing from a public boat ramp, kayaking through Sutherland Bayou, cycling the Pinellas Trail, and being 10 minutes from Dunedin and 15 minutes from Tarpon Springs. Residents treat their daily access to the water and the surrounding Pinellas coast as their primary recreation resource.

On the Water in Ozona

J.O. Douglas Park and Public Boat Ramp

J.O. Douglas Park is the waterfront anchor of the Ozona community. It is a Pinellas County park providing a free public boat ramp, fishing access, picnic areas, and views of St. Joseph Sound. Locals use it daily for fishing, launching kayaks and small boats, watching sunsets, and letting kids and dogs run near the water. It is one of the few remaining genuinely unpretentious waterfront parks in Pinellas County and a primary reason people buy in Ozona even if they cannot afford a waterfront home.

Fishing

St. Joseph Sound and Sutherland Bayou are active fishing areas. Redfish, snook, trout, and sheepshead are among the species pursued by anglers fishing the grass flats and dock pilings throughout the Ozona area. Residents with private docks fish from home. Others use J.O. Douglas Park or launch kayaks and small skiffs to access the flats. This is genuine backcountry-style fishing within 30 minutes of Clearwater. For residents, it is part of daily life.

Kayaking and Paddleboarding

Sutherland Bayou and the interconnected waterways around Ozona offer calm, protected water for kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding. The mangrove-lined channels and grass flats are accessible from J.O. Douglas Park or from private docks for waterfront homeowners. On calm mornings, the water conditions here are among the best in Pinellas County for flat-water paddling.

The Pinellas Trail

The Pinellas Trail is one of the longest paved rail-trail systems in the eastern United States, running approximately 70 miles from Tarpon Springs to St. Pete Beach. The section near Ozona follows the Alt-19 corridor and is a primary recreational amenity for residents. Regular cyclists use it to commute to Dunedin or Tarpon Springs. Casual riders use it for weekend exercise and to reach Dunedin's waterfront and downtown without driving. Dogs are welcome and the trail surface is well-maintained in this section.

Day Trips from Ozona

Dunedin (10 Minutes South)

Dunedin is the most practical extension of the Ozona lifestyle. Its downtown on Main Street has independent restaurants, craft breweries including Dunedin Brewery (Florida's oldest craft brewery), boutique shops, and a walkable waterfront causeway. Honeymoon Island State Park is accessible from Dunedin by causeway and offers Gulf beach access and osprey nesting areas. Blue Jays spring training at TD Ballpark runs through February and March each year. Dunedin is genuinely worth exploring rather than just passing through.

Tarpon Springs (15 Minutes North)

Tarpon Springs is home to the Sponge Docks, a working waterfront district shaped by the Greek sponge-diving culture that has defined the city for over a century. The Sponge Docks have sponge shops, Greek bakeries and restaurants, and boat tours departing into the Gulf. The broader Tarpon Springs downtown on Tarpon Avenue has antique shops, cafes, and a growing arts scene. Anclote River Park provides beach and boat access on the north side of town. Tarpon Springs is easy and worthwhile from Ozona.

Clearwater and Clearwater Beach (25-30 Minutes South)

Clearwater Beach is consistently ranked among the top beaches in the United States. The wide white sand beach, Pier 60, and the waterfront restaurant strip make it a practical day trip or evening destination. Clearwater Marine Aquarium, home of the real Winter the dolphin of the Dolphin Tale films, is in downtown Clearwater on the island. From Ozona, Clearwater Beach is accessible via Alt-19 south to US-19 to SR-60 west, roughly 25 to 35 minutes depending on traffic.

Caladesi Island State Park

Caladesi Island is an undeveloped barrier island accessible only by ferry from Honeymoon Island State Park (near Dunedin) or by private boat. It consistently ranks among Florida's top beaches and has a 3-mile self-guided kayak trail through its mangrove system. Residents with boats can access Caladesi directly from Ozona waterfront homes, making it a practical weekend destination rather than an occasional trip.

Dining Near Ozona

Ozona itself has limited dining, but Dunedin and Tarpon Springs are both within 10 to 15 minutes with strong dining scenes. In Dunedin: The Hammock, Casa Tina, and the Main Street restaurant strip cover most dining needs. In Tarpon Springs: Hellas Restaurant and Bakery at the Sponge Docks is a landmark for Greek food. Closer to home, Dunedin's waterfront on St. Joseph Sound has a small number of casual waterfront establishments. For serious dining, Clearwater and St. Petersburg are within 30 to 50 minutes.

Is there a beach in Ozona FL?

Ozona does not have a traditional Gulf sand beach. J.O. Douglas Park has waterfront access on St. Joseph Sound but it is a park setting rather than a swim beach. Clearwater Beach is the closest major Gulf beach, roughly 25 to 30 minutes south. Caladesi Island State Park is accessible by private boat from Ozona waterfront homes.

Can I fish from shore in Ozona?

Yes. J.O. Douglas Park provides shore fishing access on St. Joseph Sound. Dock fishing from private docks is also common for waterfront homeowners. The local waters hold redfish, snook, trout, and sheepshead among other species year-round.

Is there a restaurant in Ozona FL?

Ozona has very limited dining within the community itself. Dunedin to the south (10 minutes) and Tarpon Springs to the north (15 minutes) have strong dining options. How far is Ozona from Honeymoon Island?

Honeymoon Island State Park is approximately 15 to 20 minutes from Ozona via Alt-19 south to Dunedin Causeway. It provides Gulf beach access and is the ferry departure point for Caladesi Island. Annual Pinellas County residents with boats can access Caladesi directly from Ozona waterfront homes.

Does Ozona have any community events?

Ozona's community events are modest and centered around the waterfront and park rather than a commercial district. Neighboring Dunedin has a robust events calendar including the Dunedin Celtic Festival, the Dunedin Craft Beer Festival, and seasonal waterfront events. Residents of Ozona access these easily. content:
Quick Answer

The Ozona housing market is defined by chronically low inventory, no new construction, and a buyer pool of retirees, boaters, and remote workers who specifically want coastal northern Pinellas character. Home prices have moderated from their 2021-2022 peak consistent with broader Pinellas County trends, but supply constraints prevent significant price declines. Waterfront homes remain the most competitive segment.

Ozona FL Housing Market: Trends, Data, and What to Expect

The Ozona housing market operates by different rules than growth markets in east Hillsborough or Pasco County. There are no new phases, no builder price cuts, and no inventory overhang. Understanding this market requires understanding its structural characteristics rather than looking at broad Tampa Bay market reports, which are dominated by suburban growth markets that have little in common with Ozona.

Pinellas County Market Context

Ozona sits within the Pinellas County market, which has been among the higher-priced county markets in the Tampa Bay region. According to Pinellas County Property Appraiser data, county-wide values appreciated significantly from 2020 through 2022, moderated through 2023 and 2024, and have been broadly stable in 2025 with price variation by property type and location. Ozona tracks this trend but with less volatility due to its thin market and supply constraints.

The Ozona housing market page tracks recent sold data and active listings. For Pinellas County median pricing, the Pinellas Realtor Organization publishes monthly market reports.

What Is Driving Ozona Home Prices in 2025?

Supply Constraints

Ozona's most durable price driver is supply constraint. There is simply no new construction to add inventory, and existing homeowners have limited motivation to sell unless driven by life events. This structural scarcity means price declines require a surge in distressed selling (death, divorce, financial stress) to overcome. In a low-distress environment, low inventory is the dominant force.

Sustained Demand from a Specific Buyer Profile

Ozona attracts buyers who specifically want what it offers: Old Florida character, Gulf access, no HOA, and the Palm Harbor University High school cluster. This is a motivated, specific buyer pool. These buyers are not interchangeable with buyers who would settle for a suburban Palm Harbor home with a bigger garage. When an Ozona home lists, it draws buyers who have been waiting for exactly this type of property.

Insurance Market Headwinds

Florida homeowners and flood insurance costs have increased significantly since 2020. For Ozona waterfront properties, total annual insurance costs can run $8,000 to $15,000+ between homeowners and flood policies. This raises the effective monthly ownership cost and narrows the buyer pool for higher-priced waterfront properties. Buyers who can absorb these costs (cash buyers, high-income buyers with smaller mortgages) are relatively less affected.

Interest Rate Sensitivity

Higher mortgage rates since 2022 have reduced buyer purchasing power market-wide. In Ozona, the impact is moderated by the elevated share of cash buyers (particularly for waterfront properties) and by the fact that Ozona buyers tend to be financially established relative to first-time buyer-heavy suburban markets. The market slowed in 2022-2024 but did not break.

These patterns are tendencies, not certainties. In a market as thin as Ozona, a single listing can dominate activity for weeks. Being ready year-round matters more than timing the season.

What Should Buyers and Sellers Expect in 2025?

For Buyers

Expect limited selection. Properties in the $450K to $700K range that are priced at market and in good condition will attract multiple buyers. Properties with deferred maintenance or insurance complications will sit longer and may negotiate. Get your pre-approval, insurance research, and agent relationship in place before a property comes available, not after.

For Sellers

Accurate pricing remains the most important factor. The 2021-2022 peaks are past; pricing to that era on a 2025 listing will create extended market time. A well-presented home priced at current market attracts the specific buyers who have been waiting for an Ozona opportunity. These buyers are real, motivated, and patient but not indefinitely.

Frequently Asked Questions About the Ozona FL Housing Market

Is the Ozona FL housing market up or down in 2025?

The Ozona market has moderated from its 2021-2022 peak, consistent with the broader Pinellas County and national trend of higher interest rates slowing activity. Prices have not collapsed. Low inventory insulates Ozona from significant price declines because there are few distressed sellers and few motivated sellers willing to accept below-market offers. Active properties are sitting longer than in 2021, but well-priced homes in good condition still sell.

How many homes sell in Ozona FL each year?

Ozona is a very small community. Annual sales volume is low, typically in the range of 20 to 50 transactions per year depending on market conditions. This low volume means that individual transactions can significantly affect reported median prices, and averages have limited statistical meaning. Each property in Ozona is effectively its own micro-market.

Are home prices in Ozona higher or lower than surrounding areas?

Ozona waterfront homes are priced comparably to Crystal Beach waterfront and lower than equivalent Dunedin waterfront, reflecting location, water access quality, and desirability differences.

Is Ozona FL a good investment?

Ozona has historically appreciated in line with or better than the broader Pinellas County market over multi-year periods, driven by supply constraints and sustained demand from a specific buyer profile. As an investment (rental property), Ozona is challenging because most properties have no HOA to enforce rental restrictions, but the buyer profile skews toward owner-occupants and long-term residents, limiting rental demand and affecting cap rates.

When is the best time to buy in Ozona FL?

There is no classic seasonal window in Ozona the way there is in larger markets. The market is so thin that buyer timing is less about season and more about being ready when the right property lists. What Public Schools Serve Redington Shores FL?

Redington Shores is served by the Pinellas County School Board (PCSB), which operates public schools across the county. PCSB is one of the larger school districts in Florida, with dozens of elementary, middle, and high schools plus a significant magnet and choice school program that allows families to apply for specialized schools outside their attendance zone.

School assignments for any specific Redington Shores address can be verified using the PCSB school locator at pcsb.org/choice. I always tell buyers with school-age children: verify the school assignment using the exact property address, not neighborhood name, because zone boundaries can fall mid-block and change periodically.

Gulf Beaches Elementary Magnet School

Elementary-age children in Redington Shores are typically zoned for Gulf Beaches Elementary Magnet School. The school is located at 200 120th Ave W, Treasure Island, FL 33706. The main office number is (727) 893-2139.

Gulf Beaches Elementary Magnet is part of PCSB's choice and magnet school program. Magnet schools offer specialized curriculum designed to attract students from across the district, not just the immediate neighborhood. Students in the school's attendance zone are guaranteed admission. Students from outside the zone can apply through PCSB's school choice process, which typically involves an application during the choice window (usually November through February for the following school year).

For current school grades, programs, and enrollment data, visit the PCSB school profile page at pcsb.org or the Florida Department of Education school report card at fldoe.org. School ratings can change year to year based on student performance data, always check the current year's data rather than relying on multi-year-old information.

Middle School Assignment for Redington Shores FL

Middle school assignments for Redington Shores vary by specific address and have historically included schools serving the Pinellas barrier island and Gulf Beaches area. Verify the current middle school assignment for any specific address at pcsb.org/choice or by calling PCSB Enrollment at (727) 588-6000.

PCSB also operates several middle school magnet programs that Redington Shores students can apply to through the school choice process. Middle school choice options allow students to attend specialized programs outside their assigned attendance zone if accepted through the lottery.

High School Assignment for Redington Shores FL

High school zoning for Redington Shores has historically included Boca Ciega High School (924 58th St S, Gulfport, FL 33707; (727) 893-2100) for portions of the southern Pinellas barrier island communities. Depending on specific address within Redington Shores, Seminole High School in Seminole may also be an assigned option.

As with all Pinellas school zone assignments: verify using the exact property address at pcsb.org/choice before making a purchase decision based on school access. High school zone boundaries in Pinellas have shifted in recent years as the district manages enrollment. Do not assume that a neighbor's high school assignment reflects yours.

PCSB also operates several magnet high school programs including Pinellas County Schools' Career Academies and International Baccalaureate (IB) programs. Applications for these programs are typically submitted in early spring for the following school year.

Pinellas County Schools Choice and Open Enrollment Process

One of the distinctive features of Pinellas County Schools is its robust school choice program. PCSB allows families to apply for schools outside their assigned attendance zone through an open enrollment and lottery process. This includes elementary, middle, and high school magnet programs, career and technical education programs, and Exceptional Student Education (ESE) programs.

The PCSB school choice window typically opens in November and closes in February for the following school year. Applications are submitted at pcsb.org/choice. Results are typically announced in the spring. Seats are allocated by lottery when applications exceed capacity, with preferences given to siblings of current students in the school and certain demographic criteria.

For Redington Shores families, the school choice process means that even if the assigned neighborhood school does not meet your preferences, there may be other PCSB schools available through the choice process. Working with a real estate agent who is familiar with local school options can help you understand what options are realistically available for a specific property.

Private School Options Near Redington Shores FL

Families who prefer private education have several options within a reasonable drive of Redington Shores. Private schools in Pinellas County range from small faith-based schools to larger college-preparatory schools. Drive times from Redington Shores to most Pinellas private schools run 15-35 minutes depending on traffic.

Private schools in the Seminole, St. Petersburg, and Clearwater areas are the most common choices for Redington Shores families. For a comprehensive list of accredited private schools in Pinellas County, visit the Florida Department of Education's school locator at fldoe.org or contact PCSB at (727) 588-6000.

I have worked with buyers who specifically relocated to Redington Shores while enrolling children in private schools in Seminole and St. Pete. The barrier island's proximity to Park Boulevard (SR 694) makes cross-causeway school commutes practical, though they add 20-35 minutes each way to the school day.

Practical School Transportation from Redington Shores FL

PCSB provides school bus transportation for eligible students. Eligibility is based on distance from school and whether the route qualifies under PCSB busing standards. Barrier island students are typically eligible for busing given the distance to mainland schools. Contact PCSB Transportation at (727) 588-6000 to verify bus service for a specific address and school assignment.

For families choosing to drive, the Park Boulevard (SR 694) causeway is the primary route to mainland schools. Rush-hour traffic on Park Blvd can be significant during school drop-off and pick-up times. Morning westbound traffic from the mainland to the beach is light, but eastbound traffic (off-island) during morning school hours can back up at the causeway.

Private school families should factor in both route planning and bridge/causeway crossing times when evaluating school commute logistics from Redington Shores. A 15-mile drive to a Seminole private school may take 20-25 minutes at 7:30 AM but only 15 minutes at 8:30 AM.

How Do You Get On and Off Redington Shores FL?

Redington Shores sits on a Gulf barrier island, which means every trip off the island requires crossing a causeway. The primary mainland access point is Park Boulevard (SR 694), which runs east from Gulf Boulevard across Boca Ciega Bay to Seminole and the broader Pinellas County mainland. This is the route most Redington Shores residents use for daily shopping, work commutes, and accessing major roads.

A second option heading south is to drive down Gulf Boulevard through North Redington Beach and Redington Beach to Madeira Beach, where Tom Stuart Causeway (connecting Madeira Beach to Treasure Island) and the Johns Pass corridor provide additional access to the Treasure Island causeway connecting to St. Pete. Most residents use this southbound route for access to Treasure Island, St. Pete Beach, or St. Petersburg, but Park Boulevard remains the primary daily commute route.

There are no bridges or causeways on the northern end of Redington Shores, heading north on Gulf Blvd leads through Indian Shores and Indian Rocks Beach, where the Indian Rocks Beach bridge provides a third access to the mainland at the Largo area. Clearwater Beach has its own causeway (Memorial Causeway / SR 60) further north.

Traffic Patterns on Park Boulevard and Gulf Boulevard

The causeway section itself rarely backs up severely, but the US-19 intersection at Seminole and connecting roads to St. Pete can see delays. Morning commute to downtown St. Pete: plan for 35-50 minutes from Redington Shores between 7:30-9:00 AM.

Park Boulevard, Afternoon Return: Westbound traffic (from mainland to the beach) peaks from 4:30-7:00 PM on weekdays and from approximately 10:00 AM-3:00 PM on weekends during tourist season. Friday afternoons are the heaviest regular period.

Gulf Boulevard (CR 699): During tourist season (roughly March through Labor Day), Gulf Blvd can experience slow north-south movement through Madeira Beach and other commercial sections. Redington Shores itself has lighter commercial activity, so Gulf Blvd through town is typically less congested than sections further south.

Major disruptions: Special events at beaches (Suncoast Jazz Festival, local art festivals), hurricanes or tropical storm preparations (evacuation traffic), and occasional bridge maintenance closures can significantly disrupt typical traffic patterns. Route 35 (Gulf Beach Trolley) runs along Gulf Blvd connecting barrier island communities. Service is available for local circulation within the beach communities and connections to other PSTA routes, but frequency and hours are not designed for regional employment commuting.

Using PSTA for daily employment commuting from Redington Shores to St. Petersburg or Tampa is not practical for most workers.
